# Decisions
- perf(cli): a session on a built-in model no longer waits for the endpoint's model listing (`GET /models`) before its first request (2026-11-17, local systems lane L3). `Host::start` and `Host::open` await `ModelClients::listed` only when no context window is configured and the model is not built in (`native_model`: a Claude model or a `Model::ALL` Codex model), so custom and unknown models still block on the listing as before. A listing that has arrived by the time the session is built still sets its window through `listing_windows` in the configure hook; a built-in model otherwise uses its own window. Why: on the local systems scorecard (gak-9, GPT-6.1 Sol through a per-attempt route proxy), headless startup (exec to first model request) was 69 ms warm vs fx's 36 ms and 301 ms cold vs 257 ms, and about 45 ms of nanocode's was the listing round trip before request 1. Measured with a local Responses stub (exec of `nanocode exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -t high`, fresh home per run, N=12 each, medians, interleaved builds of master 3d4e03de9 and this change): listing answered at once 16.4 vs 16.6 ms to the first POST; listing answered after 100 ms 119.6 vs 14.8 ms.
- perf(claude): a headless root session on a Claude Sonnet model (`claude-sonnet-` model ID prefix) skips the finish check by default, as a Claude Opus session does since 1adee5c97 (2026-11-17). `finish_check(true)`, `finish_retries` and the `finish_*` levers still run it, and `late_finish_check` or `finish_check_min_requests` run it unless `skip_finish_check(true)` is also set, the same rules as for Opus. Haiku and the other models keep the check by default. Why: in a local systems comparison against Claude Code 2.1.326 on claude-sonnet-5-5 with high effort (the 10 Python repository tasks of nanoeval-suites traps-ni with hidden tests, 3 runs each, one Apple M1 Max, both clients headless on the same Claude plan route), nanocode master 2b90366ef took 1.49 times Claude Code's wall time [1.30, 1.70] (task-clustered bootstrap, seed 1, 4000 draws). Each of its 30 runs continued after the model's first end_turn (2.5 more requests, 14.3 s and $0.049 per run on average), and Claude Code continued in none. All 60 runs passed. Measured (2026-11-17, same tasks, machine, route and settings, both arms built with scripts/build-cli.sh, runs interleaved in one shuffled list): with the change, wall time is 0.504 times master's [0.466, 0.544] (14.9 s against 29.7 s per run), cost per pass 0.543 times [0.501, 0.590], 3.6 requests per run against 6.2, and both arms pass 30 of 30. Limit: these tasks are easy (every arm passes all of them), so the run shows what the check costs, not what it buys on hard tasks. The Opus default rests on Terminal-Bench 2.1 rescue tasks and a trap suite; Sonnet on a hard set (hard-v1, 3 runs) is the open check. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `rustfmt --check` on the changed file, `git diff --check`, and the dist build of nanocode-cli.
- fix(code-mode,subagents): a Code Mode cell that ends (or fails) with nested calls still running keeps running them to their end before it settles, and `spawn_agent` without an output contract returns a plain string (2026-11-17, swarms lane L10: model-side tool errors). Why: stock DeepSeek v4.1 flash agents in swarms called `spawn_agent` with neither `output_contract` nor `output_schema` (`provide exactly one of output_contract or legacy output_schema`), and started `spawn_agent` calls in a cell without awaiting them, so the cell ended, the calls were reported abandoned with an unknown outcome, and the model retried them, risking duplicate agents. What: `RunningCell` now drains `pending_calls` in `settle_calls` before `CellTerminal::Completed` and `CellTerminal::ScriptFailed`, journaling kept results as before and not sending results to the finished worker; a terminated cell still abandons its calls. `spawn_agent`'s schema makes `output_contract` nullable (null or missing is `{"type":"string"}`), both harnesses share that one definition, and giving both fields names the fix. The exec description says started calls finish but their values never reach the script. Measured on a Mac with `nanocode exec --harness codex --codex-orchestration code-mode -m tempo/boundless/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, 20 prompts spawning 2 to 5 subagents per build: master a20bda181 6 `output_contract` errors in 3 of 20 runs; this change 0 errors and 0 abandoned calls (2 runs ended early on a provider response with a negative `usage.cost`, unrelated). Scripted probes: a `spawn_agent` without a contract fails on master and spawns here; 3 unawaited `spawn_agent` calls in a cell that returns, or throws, are abandoned with 0 agents on master and leave 3 running agents here. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-subagents`, natively and `+1.97.1 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-subagents -- -D warnings`.
- perf(python): a matplotlib chart in python.wasm holds about 18 MiB less, so the Cloudflare demo's charts fit its 48 MiB Python cap (2026-11-17, cfmem lane; Georgios: python3 only on python.wasm). Why: on the live durable-cloudflare demo, matplotlib scripts failed with exit 126 (held 48.5 to 49 MiB, past the 48.0 MiB maxMemoryBytes), and once the Durable Object isolate passed its 128 MB limit and was reset; numpy-only scripts were fine. Measured in Node (nanocode-ts Bash, the smallest maxMemoryBytes that passes, found by bisection in 0.25 MiB steps, plus the instance's linear memory after the run), before (nanocode-ts dist at 3aab39a) and after (master 4b6fa30e3 with these commits): import numpy 8 to 7 MiB; import matplotlib.pyplot 41.25 to 25.25 MiB (linear memory 80.1 to 61.8 MiB); a sine plot and savefig 51.5 to 34.5 (92.1 to 72.0); plot, savefig and plt.show() 48.75 to 32 (89.2 to 69.8); the demo's chart of viem's largest source files (barh at dpi 120, tight_layout, savefig) 60 to 41.75 (111.3 to 82.1). The 35 MiB memory image itself is not counted against the cap (held starts after it), so the cap stays 48 MiB. Where the memory went, measured with a held probe per module and per line: (1) every code unit had a 2-byte adaptive counter and an 8-byte pointer cache allocated on decode, which is 10 bytes per unit for every function a module defines, run or not. CodeUnits now allocates both on first write (one AtomicPtr; a read of a missing cache returns 0, the value the eager arrays started at), -4.9 MiB on import matplotlib.pyplot. (2) PyCode::location filled the code object's whole location table (16 bytes per instruction, kept for good) on the first lookup, and a module body that catches one exception (try/except ImportError) asks once. Now the first 8 lookups decode only the one location from the line table, and only after that is the table kept. (3) A pybind11 class's tp_dealloc lives on pybind11_object, and ready_type didn't inherit it as CPython's inherit_slots does, so RendererAgg and FT2Font never ran their C++ destructors. Each savefig leaked its 4.4 MiB Agg buffer (1200x960 at dpi 120). Types without their own tp_dealloc now take their base's. (4) A bound method of a C object parks its proxy, and parked proxies were rescanned only when their count doubled, so a dead renderer stayed alive for the rest of the run. The sweep now also rescans after 1 MiB of heap growth, and again while a scan frees proxies. (5) matplotlib imported a lot that a plain chart never uses: pyparsing (through _fontconfig_pattern at rc validation and mathtext), dateutil (category, dates, the version check), unittest (pyparsing.testing), fontTools (dviread), mpl_toolkits.mplot3d (projections), widgets (backend_bases' LockDraw, pyplot's Button and Slider), _afm, and all 182 builtin colormaps and their reversals. Each now loads on first use: a plain fontconfig pattern (families with escapes, constants, name=value) is parsed without pyparsing and gives the same dict, LockDraw moves to matplotlib._lockdraw, the colormap registry holds lazy entries that build on lookup, matplotlib.cm.<name> comes from a module __getattr__, matplotlib.dates loads when matplotlib.units first meets a date or datetime64, and the '3d' projection registers on first use. (6) pyplot.savefig redrew the figure on Agg after saving it, a second full draw kept only for GUI canvases (transparent=True), so now it redraws only with an interactive framework. FigureCanvasAgg also drops its old renderer before making one of a new size. Checked: nanocode-ts bench/python/score.ts on the baked build is unchanged at 8/18 packages, numpy 14/14, matplotlib 6/6, pillow 6/6, contourpy 2/2, kiwisolver 1/1, limits 4/4. A probe also passes: dates and datetime64 on an axis, mathtext titles, imshow with magma_r, cm.viridis, colormaps['grey'] and 'Grays_r' (182 names), plt.Slider and plt.Button, a 3d plot, matplotlib.projections.Axes3D, style.use('ggplot'), the fontconfig pattern 'DejaVu Sans-12:bold' (full parser), pyparsing.testing, savefig at another dpi and to SVG. cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -D warnings is clean for rustpython-compiler-core, rustpython-vm, nanocode-python-capi and nanocode-python, native and wasm32 (rustpython-vm's two wasm32 warnings were already there), and their cargo tests pass. Not changed: PDF output still fails on fontTools.subset, as before. The memory image JS keeps for a host (34.5 MB decompressed, on top of each instance's linear memory) is nanocode-ts's to shrink.
- fix(python): subprocess honors timeout= and sys.executable names python3 (2026-11-17, subproc lane). Why: nanocode-ts now runs python.wasm's child commands through the hosting shell, and scripts on the benchmark pass timeout= and spawn [sys.executable, '-c', ...]. Before this, timeout was accepted and ignored, and sys.executable was '' so that spawn failed with FileNotFoundError. What: run, call, check_call and check_output prefix the command with the shell's timeout command and raise TimeoutExpired when it reports 124. Under timeout, a program given by its /bin, /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin path (shell=True's /bin/sh, sys.executable) is named by its base name, because the shell resolves commands by name. The command's output up to the timeout is kept on the exception. sys.executable and sys._base_executable are '/usr/bin/python3', which the shell resolves to python3 by name. Unsupported: Popen(...).wait(timeout=) and communicate(timeout=) on their own (the child already ran to completion when Popen returned). Checked with nanocode-ts bench/python/subprocess.ts and a probe: run('sleep 3', shell=True, timeout=0.5) raises TimeoutExpired, and check_output([sys.executable, '-c', 'print(6*7)']) returns '42\n'.
- feat(code-mode): `image` takes an image file's path and shows it through the host's image reader, once per cell (2026-11-17, image-path lane). On the demo build of 76a97ad63, a cell that saved a chart and then called `image("/workspace/viem_largest_files.png")` failed with `Tool call failed: invalid image output. Pass a base64 data URI instead`, although the chart itself still showed as a file the cell's calls created; the exec description's `image(await tools.Read({ file_path }))` form was not what models wrote. native-behavior.json records `image` with strings only for `data:` URLs (kept, even `data:garbage`) and `https:` URLs (refused with the remote-URL message), and no path, so a path string is outside recorded native behavior, like the array form. The engine now receives the reader's field on its tool definition (`images::with_reader` adds `image_reader` to the catalog `CellTools::encode` sends), and `image` given a non-empty string that is not a `data:` or `http(s):` URL reads it with a synchronous call to that tool and shows what it returns; without a reader, and for URLs, nothing changes. The read is the same call the cell's auto-shown copy makes, so the explicit item's data URL has the same hash, `ImageFiles::shown` records it and `changed` does not show the file again. Making the call a no-op when the cell already showed the file was rejected: it would still fail for a file an earlier cell saved, which is how a run below showed its second chart. The description now says `image` also takes an image file's path, which it reads with that tool. Checked with `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-code-mode-engine`, the same with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib` for both crates and targets with `-D warnings`, and rustfmt (no new diffs). Measured with real Haiku turns in nanocode-ts f681166 built against master c2ff927a5 with and without the change (`node scripts/build.mjs`, the harness in output/img passing the shell `github` and `fetch` so `git clone` works): a scripted cell that writes x.py, runs it with python3 and calls `image('/workspace/x.png')` failed in 5 of 5 runs on the 76a97ad63 build and in 0 of 11 after, each showing exactly one image; "Clone wevm/viem and chart its largest source files with Python" failed a cell with the invalid image output error in 3 of 6 runs before (each a path `image` call) and in 0 of 6 after, where path calls in 2 runs showed their charts; one image per run in 5 of 6, and the sixth showed two different charts its script saved, once each, with one unrelated failed cell (`unsupported Bash option: stdin`).
- fix(code-mode): a chart a cell's Python run saves shows even when no tool input names its file, and an image already shown is not shown again in a later cell (2026-11-17, images-finish lane; Georgios: charts in Code Mode demos). After a9e83b2cc and 101176e2b a cell shows image files that paths in its nested calls' inputs name, but a run like `python3 plot.py` whose script picks the name at run time (a timestamp, a directory it creates) and prints it names no path, so nothing showed. `ImageFiles::settled` now reads a successful nested call's text output and structured result for image paths, and when there is exactly one, tracks it like a path an input names (joined with the call's `workdir`); more than one is taken for a listing and ignored. The paths still missing at the end of a cell and the hashes of images already shown carry to later cells in `images::Carried` (one `Atom` on the runtime, merged rather than replaced, so overlapping cells keep each other's state), hashed with a fixed `BuildHasherDefault<DefaultHasher>` so a hash from one cell matches the same image in the next. A replayed cell records its paths without the before read, whose state is gone, and shows what differs from the shown hashes. The exec description now says that an image file the cell's calls create or change is shown after its output, so the model should run its script itself and save the chart with `savefig` rather than `show`. The lane's staged change also marked the Claude exec tool `strict`; dropped, since Claude Code sends no `strict` on its tools, it would change every Claude request, and nothing here measured it. Measured with real `claude-haiku-4-5` turns through the nanocode-ts harness (output/charts/run.ts, nanocode-ts WASM built from 310049c84 without and with the change, same Pyodide python.wasm), images shown per run: `Plot a sine wave with numpy and matplotlib` 5/5 before (1 each) and 6/6 after (1 each); `Clone wevm/viem and chart its largest source files with Python` 5/5 before (1,1,1,1,2) and 5/5 after (1 each); `Plot a sine wave with numpy and matplotlib and save it under a file name that includes the current Unix timestamp` 1/6 before (the one run called `image()` itself) and 6/6 after with no `image()` call; no run showed the same image twice. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-backend-claude`, the same for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`, rustfmt.
- feat(code-mode): a nested call whose input runs Python (a string containing `python` or `.py`) also tracks `Figure_1.png` to `Figure_4.png` in its working directory, so a figure that python.wasm's `plt.show()` writes shows in the cell like any image file the cell creates or changes (2026-11-17). The same before/after rule applies: a figure already there and unchanged is not shown again, and the four extra reads happen only for calls that run Python. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -D warnings`, `cargo check` for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, rustfmt.
- feat(python): matplotlib, Pillow, contourpy and kiwisolver import in python.wasm with no Pyodide (2026-11-17). Their pure-Python packages and dependencies (cycler, dateutil, a minimal fontTools, packaging, pyparsing, mpl_toolkits, six, pylab) are frozen under `crates/core/python/site`, without tests, GUI backends or `matplotlib.testing`. `mpl-data` (matplotlibrc, stylelib, the TTF fonts and a prebuilt fontlist.json; no AFM or PDF core fonts) is DEFLATE-compressed into the module by build.rs and served read-only through `_host` stat/read/list under site-packages, so matplotlib finds it with its own path logic; `_Located` gives frozen matplotlib modules site-packages filenames for that. `_missing` counts a frozen top-level package as present, so a host routes these imports to RustPython. python3's default backend is `module://nanocode_matplotlib`: Agg, and `plt.show()` writes `Figure_<n>.png` to the working directory (named on stderr) so the host picks it up as a created image; `_start` calls its `_reset()` so a kept interpreter starts each run with no figures and default rcParams. Cost, `wasm-opt -Oz` and baked: 40,896,332 to 50,528,905 bytes raw, 16,272,048 to 24,794,036 with `gzip -9` (fonts about 3.9 MB of that gzipped; LastResortHE stays because font_manager loads it as the last fallback). Not covered: PDF output (needs `fontTools.subset` and `ttLib`, not frozen) and JPEG (Pillow is built without libjpeg); PNG and SVG work, and an Agg sine plot is pixel-identical to native.
- perf(wasm): serde, the Claude client's wire types, the image codec and the Code Mode host shrink the nanocode-ts Claude module (one family, no extensions) from 1,193,594 to 1,023,107 bytes with Brotli (quality 11, window 24, `wasm-opt -Oz`), 1,620,808 to 1,369,607 with `gzip -9` (2026-11-16, nanocode-ts module size, round 3). Each figure below is that module's Brotli size before and after the one change, so they overlap a little and carry about 2 KB of build noise (crate hashes move code). serde_derive: a struct with named fields gets no `visit_seq`, so it no longer reads from a JSON array (every `Serialize` writes it as a map), -15.3 KB; field visitors keep `visit_u64` and `visit_bytes` only where they collect other fields, -4.3 KB. serde_json, on wasm32 only (native keeps the code it had): `from_str` reads through `SliceRead`, -3.5 KB; `from_value` and `to_value` go through text (`to_vec`, then `from_slice`), so a type deserializes from one input type instead of from `Value` too, and `Error::unplaced` drops the text's position so errors read as before, -14.0 and -6.6 KB, and `to_value` first tries `value::simple::Simple`, which serializes a string, number, bool, char, unit or option of one directly and refuses the rest, +1.2 KB; `Map::from_iter` and `extend` insert in a loop; a float prints core's shortest `{:e}` digits in ryu's layout (`float_wasm.rs`), which drops the POW10 table and the nanocode-sys dependency on wasm32 (40M random f64 against the old formatter: 40,453 differ, each a tie between two equally short digit strings that parse to the same f64); with the CRC32 and inflate tables built on first use (`LazyLock`, nanocode-compression), -19.4 KB together. `json!` builds a literal leaf with `Value::from` (-1.4 KB), inserts a literal key through one `__private::insert` (-1.9 KB) and unwraps `to_value` inside `__private::to_value` instead of at every site (-3.1 KB). Wire types: `ContentBlock`, `ContentDelta`, `ToolResultContent` and `StreamEvent` (claude client, on wasm32; native keeps the derives) and `UserInput` and `ToolOutputContent` (types-core, `fields::Fields`, every target) deserialize by hand from a map instead of through serde's buffered `Content`, -18.7 and -5.2 KB; on 37 inputs, valid and invalid, `UserInput` and `ToolOutputContent` give the same values and error messages as before except for a JSON array, which is still refused with `invalid type: sequence` in place of `expected variant identifier`. `CheckpointPayload::decode` decodes a tree through `from_value` on wasm32, -7.6 KB, and `PagedSnapshot` and `PagedCursor` read `PagedConversation` separately instead of through `flatten`, -2.7 KB. Image: `Codec` gains `inspect` (the header `Decoder::new` reads) and `resize` (`Filter::Lanczos3`, `Filter::Thumbnail`), so an embedder that lends a codec links neither, -22.4 KB; `Builtin` answers both with the code that ran before. Tool host: `Tools::code_mode_host` sets a process flag, and `Tools` and `EmbeddedToolRuntime` read their host through it, so a process that never installs a Code Mode host links none of the host paths, -4.6 and -14.5 KB; a host is only ever installed through that method, so behavior is unchanged. Native speed: release builds of one benchmark against ed1900582 and this change, pinned to one core, three interleaved runs of 15 samples (wall time; the build host has no hardware counters). Before the wasm32 gates, `json!` with a 1 MB string took 81x as long, checkpoint decode 13x, `to_value` 12x, `from_value` 8x, float printing 4.2x, `StreamEvent` 2.9x and string-heavy `from_str` +46%. With them every row is within the run spread: 1 MB history `from_str`, `from_value`, `to_value` and `to_string` -3.4 to -0.2%, 5,235 `StreamEvent`s +2.5%, `json!` +3 to +7% (spread 6 to 24%), floats +2.0 and -2.5%, `UserInput` -9.9%, `ToolOutputContent` +0.1%, crc32 and inflate within 5%. On wasm32 `from_value` and `to_value` of objects still go through text, so large checkpoints and tool results decode slower there; an `f32` through `to_value` rounds to its shortest `f32` decimal there (no SDK type serializes one). The nanocode-ts Claude module is 995,394 bytes with Brotli after the gates. Checks: nanocode-ts `pnpm test --run` on the modules built from this tree; `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked --lib --workspace`; the same for the changed crates and `nanocode` with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/core/serde-derive/src/de/{identifier,struct_}.rs, crates/patches/serde_json/{Cargo.toml,src/de.rs,src/error.rs,src/float_wasm.rs,src/lib.rs,src/macros.rs,src/map.rs,src/value/mod.rs,src/value/simple.rs}, crates/core/compression/src/{checksum,inflate,lib}.rs, crates/core/compression/src/inflate/table.rs, crates/backends/claude/client/src/lib.rs, crates/core/types-core/src/{fields,lib}.rs, crates/core/types-core/src/tools/mod.rs, crates/core/agent/src/session/contract.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/durability/format.rs, crates/core/image/src/{codec,decode,lib,resample,thumbnail}.rs, crates/runtime/tool-host/src/{selection,embedded/runtime}.rs, crates/runtime/agent-config/src/configuration.rs.
- perf(wasm): image decoding and encoding go through an installed `nanocode_image::Codec`, so an embedder can link none of the SDK's decoders and encoders and lend its own (2026-11-16, nanocode-ts module size). `Codec` has `decode(Decoder)` and `encode(Encoding)`. `Builtin` holds the decoders `Decoder::decode` held and the PNG, JPEG and WebP encoders that `encode_image`, `encode_png`, `fit_data_url` and Claude's `Read` media path called directly. `install(&'static dyn Codec)` sets the process's codec once, and `encode(Encoding)` is the encoder entry point, with the JPEG `quality` Claude's media path steps down; that path now uses it, and `nanocode-backend-claude-tools` drops its `nanocode-jpeg` dependency. `RuntimeBuilder::build` installs `Builtin` unless `RuntimeDefaults::BUILTIN_CODEC` (default `true`) is `false`, and a native build falls back to `Builtin` when nothing is installed, so runners, hands and every embedder on `Defaults` behave as before. On wasm with no codec, `Decoder::decode` returns `DecodeError::Unsupported` and an encode fails, which every caller already turns into the image placeholder. `Decoder` gains `bytes`, `format`, `limits` (as passed to `new`) and `reserved`, which a codec outside the process needs to decode the same way. Why: the codecs were linked into every wasm module that could see an image. nanocode-ts now ships them as a separate module (`nanocode-image.wasm`, 154,473 bytes gzipped) that its session modules call synchronously through the host. Measured on nanocode-ts's modules (wasm32, fat LTO, `opt-level = "z"`, `wasm-opt -Oz`, gzip -9), together with nanocode-ts's own `RuntimeDefaults` that also leaves out the in-memory default store: Claude 1,717,129 to 1,620,808 bytes, Codex 1,831,520 to 1,735,952, both families with every extension 4,422,533 to 4,324,187. Output is unchanged: a GIF prompt image converted to PNG and a 3000x2 PNG resized for Claude come out of nanocode-ts byte for byte as `prepare_base64_images` at 42e37d2 produces them natively. Checks: nanocode-ts's integration suite; `cargo check --lib -p nanocode-image -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode` native and for wasm32. Files: `crates/core/image/src/{codec,decode,lib,metadata}.rs`, `crates/backends/claude/tools/{Cargo.toml,src/tools/media.rs}`, `crates/runtime/agent/src/runtime.rs`, `crates/runtime/agent-config/src/configuration.rs`.
- perf(wasm): an embedder can build a runtime that links no subagents, and a runtime of one harness family (2026-11-16, nanocode-ts module size). `RuntimeDefaults::SUBAGENTS` (default `true`) is a `const` that `RuntimeBuilder::build` reads: with `false` it never opens the subagent registry, so nothing reaches `nanocode_subagents` beyond its data types. Every internal use of the registry and its control (`deliver_completions`, `await_restored`, `activity` in `settle`, `persist_subagents`, the journal reservation, `shutdown`, the delegation tools and the remote children's spawn, respawn and restore) now goes through one `Arc<dyn Delegates>` that only the `SUBAGENTS` branch constructs, and the router keeps remote children as the `AgentFactory` they already implement. An embedder sets it in its own `RuntimeDefaults`, such as a wrapper that delegates every method to `Defaults` and sets the `const`, so `Defaults<C, A>` is unchanged. The facade adds `Absent<F>`, an uninhabited backend in place of the other family's harness, with `ClaudeDefaults` and `CodexDefaults`, and re-exports `AgentRuntime`, `CheckpointFormats`, `Runtime`, `RuntimeBackend`, `RuntimeBuilder`, `RuntimeDefaults` and `ToolsBuilder` for embedders that build their runtime per family. `without_subagents()` still turns them off at run time, and `subagents()` still returns the `SubagentControl`. Why: the linker can't drop code behind an `Option` read at run time, so a runtime built with `without_subagents()` still carried the registry, its tools, journals, restore and the schema validator its structured results use. Measured on nanocode-ts's Claude module (wasm32, fat LTO, `opt-level = "z"`, `wasm-opt -Oz`, gzip -9): 2,446,806 bytes with both families' defaults narrowed to Claude, 1,771,035 with `SUBAGENTS = false` (`nanocode_subagents` 354 KB and `nanocode_schema` 74 KB of gzipped code gone, `nanocode_sync` 115 to 52 KB, `nanocode_agent` 122 to 108 KB); the module with both families and subagents is unchanged at 4.42 MB. Checks: nanocode-ts's integration suite (451 tests) on modules built both ways; `cargo check --lib -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode-agent-host -p nanocode` for wasm32. Files: `crates/runtime/agent/src/{delegates,handoff,lib,remote,router,runtime,turn_inbox}.rs`, `crates/runtime/agent/src/runtime/turns.rs`, `crates/runtime/agent-config/src/configuration.rs`, `crates/nanocode/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}`.

- feat(code-mode): a cell shows the image files its own tool calls create or change (2026-11-16, demo annoyances swarm, images lane). Why: in the durable-cloudflare and durable-vercel demos the agent saved a matplotlib PNG and said it was shown above, but no image item was in the cell; the `exec` description's `image(await tools.Read({ file_path }))` sentence was followed in about 1 of 3 runs. What: `code_mode/images.rs` (`ImageFiles`). When the session's catalog has an image reader (`Read` with `file_path` or `view_image` with `path`, now one table, `code_mode_description::image_reader`, that the description also uses), each nested call other than the reader has the image paths named in its input (tokens ending in .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif or .webp, anywhere in its JSON strings) read through the reader before it runs. When the cell completes or fails, those paths are read again, and each image whose reader output differs from before and that the cell did not already pass to `image()` (same data URL) is sent as a content item of that cell after the cell's own output. The reader decides what is an image (by its bytes) and fits its size, so no new size limit is added; the number of paths a cell tracks is the cell guard's `calls_per_tool`. Paths named but still missing at the end of a cell (a script written in one cell and run in a later one) carry to the session's next cells in `CodeModeRuntime::images`. A cell that called only the reader or `image()` reads nothing, replayed calls are not tracked, and the reader calls are not logged as nested calls. Hosts change nothing. Measured with a local nanocode-ts host (`output/img2/run.ts` in an ignored directory: `AgentRuntime.instantiate` over `node:sqlite`, `Bash.create` with Pyodide `python3` and matplotlib, Claude provider with code mode, direct Messages API) on claude-haiku-5-5, built with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 npm run build` with this checkout as `../nanocodex`, counting image blocks in `exec` and `wait` results: `Plot a sine wave with matplotlib and save it as a PNG.` before (nanocode-ts 451aa6b build) 0 of 5 runs with an image, after 6 of 6, with no `image()` call from the model in any of them; a two-cell prompt (Write plot.py in one `exec`, `cd /workspace && python3 plot.py` in the next) 3 of 3; a prompt asking for `image()` of `tools.Read` 3 of 3, one image each (no duplicate). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode` (no new warnings), `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the new and changed hunks. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/images.rs, code_mode/mod.rs, code_mode/description.rs.
- fix(code-mode): image paths a nested call names, and the paths still pending from earlier cells, are also read against that call's `workdir` when its input has one (2026-11-17, demo annoyances swarm, Codex images lane). Why: after a9e83b2cc the Claude skins of the durable-cloudflare and durable-vercel demos show a cell's chart, but on the ChatGPT skins (gpt-6-luna through the Codex backend) the vercel run `Clone wevm/viem and chart its largest source files with Python` attached none in 2 of 2 benchmark runs. Captured from the live stream (playwright on /chatgpt): the model wrote `/workspace/viem/chart_largest_sources.py` with `apply_patch` (the script names `ROOT / "largest_source_files.png"`) and ran `python3 chart_largest_sources.py` through `exec_command` with `workdir` `/workspace/viem`; the relative name was read against the Hand's working directory, `/workspace`, so it never existed and no image was added. What: in `ImageFiles::before`, when the call's input has a non-empty string `workdir` (Codex `exec_command`), each relative path it names and each tracked path is also tracked joined onto that directory; absolute paths are unchanged and the relative entries stay tracked as before. Claude's tools take no `workdir`, so their sessions are unchanged. The cloudflare run (`Plot a sine wave with numpy and matplotlib`, written in `/workspace`) already had the image in its `exec` result on the deployed build; that skin's missing image is the nds ChatGPT clone's closed tools row, fixed in nds 5454fa8, which is not yet in an nds release (the demos pin build-85fc456). Measured with an ignored nanocode-ts harness (`output/codex/run.mjs`: the build-fa6e5fd release package's `AgentRuntime` and `Bash` over `node:sqlite` with Pyodide matplotlib, provider `codex` with a local Responses mock that replays the captured calls as `exec` cells), swapping only `nanocode_wasm.wasm` (the release's against one built by `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 node scripts/build.mjs` with this tree at a9e83b2cc as `../nanocodex`): the viem pattern (patch in one cell, run with `workdir` in the next) before 0 of 3 runs with an image, after 4 of 4, one `input_image` in the `exec` result and in the next model request; the sine pattern (heredoc and run in `/workspace`) 2 of 2 on both. Checks: `cargo check -j 2 --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy -j 2 --locked --lib --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode` (no findings in images.rs), `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on images.rs. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/images.rs.
- feat(code-mode): a cell that uses the default yield waits in place for its foreground commands instead of yielding while one is still running (2026-11-16, demo annoyances swarm, yield/wait lane). Why: a Bash call that outlives the default 10000 ms yield came back as `Script running with cell ID`, and the model spent a whole model call on `wait` for a command that ends on its own; in Code Mode a ~24 s `git clone` of two large repositories cost 2.5 `wait` calls a run. What: `CodeModeToolset::returns_within(name, input)` (default `None`; `ToolRuntime` asks its `CodeModeToolPolicy`s, and Claude's policy answers for a `Bash` call without `run_in_background` with its own `timeout`, defaulting to `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` and capped at `MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`, the limits Bash itself enforces). When an `exec` or `wait` that named no `yield_time_ms` reaches its yield deadline and every running nested call has such a bound, the observation moves its deadline once to the latest `started + bound`. When those calls have returned, the cell gets a fresh default yield window from that moment, so a script that goes on to other work still yields on the usual clock. The limit comes from the caller's timeout, not a new constant. A named `yield_time_ms`, a background job, any other pending nested call, a pending `setTimeout`, or a steer (preemption still cuts the wait short) keeps the old behavior, and nothing is replayed: the runtime only waits longer on calls it already dispatched. The `exec` description says a cell waiting only on foreground commands yields once they return or reach their timeout; the `exec_spec_yielding` rewrite still matches. Measured (nanocode-exec debug build, claude-haiku-4-5, `--hedge-cap-percent 0`, 4 ABAB pairs, model calls counted from `model.call` spans): one Bash `git clone --depth 1` of rust-lang/rust and microsoft/TypeScript (11 to 13 s each), before 7/10/8/8 model calls (mean 8.25) with 1/3/3/3 `wait`s, after 5/6/4/5 (mean 5.0) with 0 `wait`s; time outside the cells, mostly model time, mean 15.6 s before and 13.3 s after (total wall time is dominated by clone network variance, 24.7 to 96.6 s). A `sleep 10` (10.2 s) already completed under the old quiet hold (0 `wait`s on both sides), and `sleep 25` is blocked by Bash's sleep guard, so the model fell back to an in-cell `setTimeout`, which still yields as before. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude` (native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib` on the same crates with `-D warnings`.
- feat(code-mode-engine): `__nanocodeSyncTool`, a blocking host tool call for preludes, and synchronous `WebAssembly` exports (2026-11-16, demo annoyances swarm, WebAssembly lane). Why: models (Haiku 5.5, GPT Luna) call instance exports without `await` (`const r = instance.exports.add(2, 3)`), get a Promise, print `{}` or `[object Promise]`, and retry; on the `Run a WebAssembly add function` prompt that took 10-13 s and up to 10 cells. What: the prelude wrapper takes a third argument `callSync(name, input)`; it reaches host function `__nanocodeSyncTool` (`SYNC_TOOL`), which records the tool call like `__nanocodeTool` and answers `Reply::Block(id)`. The machine leaves that host call unanswered, sets `blocked`, and goes idle without timers or parking; `idle` delivers only the blocked call's result, resolving the host call with `{ ok, value }` and resuming; other results stay queued. `invokeToolSync` parses the value and throws `toolFailure` on failure. The Code Mode description now says exports return their results synchronously. A prelude that ignores `callSync` is unchanged. Measured with nanocode-ts `output/wasmprobe.ts` against a local nanocode-ts WebAssembly build (`cargo build --locked --offline --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --profile wasm` with this checkout as `../nanocodex`) and its prelude using `callSync`: a scripted naive `instance.exports.add(2, 3)` prints `5` and `number` (before: `[object Promise]` and an abandoned wasm call); 200 sequential sync calls take about 300 ms; a sync call beside a pending tool call and a timer keeps both. Real Haiku 5.5, 8 interleaved runs each of the default prompt: before 28 cells, 6 of 8 runs with a failed or Promise-valued cell, median 11.07 s (8.5-20.6 s); after 9 cells, 1 cell per run in 7 of 8, median 6.21 s (5.9-10.5 s), the two failing cells being a model-written bad byte and `WebAssembly.Module.exports`, which nanocode-ts now provides. Checks: `cargo check -j 2 --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode-engine`, `cargo clippy -j 2 --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -- -D warnings`.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeAgentBuilder::finish_tool_truth`, a default-off finish-check item (2026-11-16, benchmark precision lane). When a task names a tool whose output is the ground truth for a value (a measurement with stated flags), the finish check asks that the value come from running that tool on the final result, that a missing tool be installed (package index refreshed first) before a substitute is written, and that a missing curl or python not be read as no network; failing that, keep the value well inside its limit and say it was not checked. Motivation: failed attempts in a matched Terminal-Bench run computed a tool-defined value with a reimplementation after reading a missing python3 or curl as no network, and missed the stated limit by about 3 units; none of those attempts errored or refused. Turning it on turns the finish check on. The text names no task (unit-tested). Not yet measured on an eval.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::stall_nudge(every)`, opt-in (2026-11-16, K7 small-models lane, stall sub-lane). Each time a session's `exec`, `wait` and `Bash` calls have run for another `every` of wall time in all (measured around the handler with `nanocode_platform::unix_millis`, one shared `AtomicU64` per agent), the tool result that crossed the multiple carries a `<system-reminder>` with the minutes waited, the deadline's time left when one is set (`Deadline::remain_now`), and to stop a job that is not on course to finish and change approach instead of waiting on it again. Why: in deployed run 0f032a59 (nano-claude on claude-haiku-5-5, terminal-bench-2.1) both feal-linear-cryptanalysis attempts hit agent_timeout at 1800 s after starting a brute-force attack and then waiting on it: a00007 spent 1244 s of its 1800 s inside tools (`sleep 240; cat run.log`, `sleep 60`, a 110 s `setTimeout` loop), a00034 1860 s of tool time (a `wait` with `yield_time_ms` 900000, then an 8 x 110 s poll loop); no command repeated exactly (at most once each in the last 30% of wall time), so the signal is time spent waiting, not identical commands. The two make-doom-for-mips timeouts (a00015, a00042, 900 s) are not this: their model calls took 790 s and 888 s (10k to 45k output tokens a call) and tools 9 s and 20 s, so they need an effort or thinking lever instead. Unset, the handlers are not wrapped and sessions behave as before. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude`, again with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo clippy` on both crates with no new warnings. Not run: a session with it against a model.
- feat(scripts): `scripts/cell-stats.py`, a stdlib-only statistics tool for ABAB-interleaved A/B timings, with the launch cell verdict (2026-11-16, Nanocode 1.0 durability swarm, B6a.11). Why: the durability numbers so far (main to first root call 3.46 to 52.45 ms at 100K, kill to lease 95 to 367 ms) are N=3 to 5 with no paired intervals, so no cell can be called. What: it reads JSONL rows (`build` A or B, `rep`, `metric_ms`, `K`, `host`, `loadavg`, optional `metric`, `commit` and `cost`), groups them into cells by `metric` and `K`, and prints per build the median, p95 and mean with 95% percentile bootstrap intervals; paired by `rep`, the geometric mean of B/A, the ratio of medians and of p95s, and the median paired lead (A - B, positive when B is faster; `--higher-better` flips it), each with a paired bootstrap interval (pairs resampled together); with `--target`, B's p95 (or median) and its ratio to the target with an interval, MET when the interval is entirely within it. Verdict: WIN when the lead interval excludes 0 upward or the target is MET, LOSS when it excludes 0 downward, TIE otherwise (cheaper when the paired `cost` ratio interval is below 1.0x), and MISSING, with the verdict it would have had, when a cell has fewer than `--min-n` matched pairs (30 by default, as systems cells need) or fewer than 3, spans hosts, pairs runs from different hosts, mixes commits within a build, has a rep without both builds or runs whose A and B are not adjacent in the file. It exits 2 when any cell is MISSING. Seeded (`--seed`, default 1, `--boot` 10000). Usage: `python3 -I scripts/cell-stats.py runs.jsonl --target 5 --label 'pinned host, load X'` (`--json` for machine output). Validated on synthetic cells (generator in ignored output/cellstats): B 20% faster gives WIN with B/A 0.799x [0.778, 0.820]; B 25% slower LOSS; equal TIE, and TIE cheaper with a 0.75x cost; N=10, a swapped host, a dropped rep, A-then-B blocks and a mixed commit each give MISSING (would be WIN); N=2 MISSING; a heavy-tailed equal pair gives B p95 MISSED against 5 ms. Hosted Hand, unpinned, load 190 to 290: 10000 resamples of a 30-pair cell took 39 s there.
- fix(buildcache): a restore reads one resolved entry, and a workspace slot's pointer flip and sibling sweep run under a lock (2026-11-16, swarm build-cache concurrency lane). Why: `restore` joined every file it reads (`inputs`, `sources`, `identities`, `env`, `files/`) onto the slot path `workspace/<key>`, a symlink that `point` swaps by rename, so a store from another build between the input check and the copy could restore the files of a version whose inputs were never checked; and `point` read the slot back after its rename and swept every sibling version but that one, so two stores of the same key with different identities could each sweep the version the other had just pointed to, leaving the slot dangling until the next miss rebuilt it. Now `restore` starts with `fs::canonicalize(entry)`, so every read comes from the version it checked (a version swept during a restore makes it fail and the unit compile, as any miss does), and `point` holds an exclusive lock on `<dir>/.point.lock` from its rename through its sweep. Registry entries (`store`, a symlink created once and never replaced) and `eager_pack` (already locked per pack) are unchanged. The two lines matter only when builds share a cache slot concurrently: several target directories of one checkout, or several agents on one shared store; a single build is unaffected. Checks: the helper compiles as `scripts/buildcache` compiles it, `rustc --edition 2024 -C opt-level=2 -C strip=symbols -C target-feature=+crt-static -o h-new scripts/buildcache.rs` (rc 0, no warnings; 460 s on the hosted Hand at load ~210, not pinned host). Not run: the K = 1, 5, 10, 20, 50 concurrent `cargo build --release -p nanocode-cli` sweep (shared warm XDG against a fresh XDG per agent, builds per minute, p50/p95, `nanocode --version` of every binary, dangling slots); the hosted Hand stayed at load 150 to 340 with OOM kills, so the timed sweep is left for a pinned host.
- fix(tool-host): a root session's `ToolRuntime` marks its cell journals with `CellJournals::preempt_recovery`, so a steer, such as a batch of subagent completions, cuts the root's recovered `exec` or `wait` short (2026-11-16, Nanocode 1.0 durability swarm, standby6 lane). Why: since `d3ce4cdff` only a session that its embedder marked lets a steer preempt a recovered observation, and no SDK host marked any session. In scale-bench k100k-4 (res7, sb3) the root resumed its `wait` cell after the claim with its 30000 ms yield and received the first completion batch at +38.3 s, while the first child call ran at +3.7 s. A subagent keeps the unmarked behavior, so its resume note does not cut its recovered `exec` short. What: `ToolRuntime::with_tools` marks the session when `Tools::session` names a session whose `root_session_id` is its own. Sim: the `cell_calls` scenario checks `root_recovery_preemptible` (a root is marked, a child is not), and the mutation `root_recovery_unbound` (the host builds the runtime without `for_session`) is caught. Checks: see the commit message. Files: crates/runtime/tool-host/src/runtime/execution.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/src/cellcalls.rs.
- perf(claude): a steer returns once its Code Mode preemption is started, and a spawned task waits for the rest (2026-11-16, steer latency lane). Before, `steer_input`, `driver::route` and the bound `Steer` released the steering lock and then awaited every `code_turn_preempt` future before returning. With a remote Code Mode host each hook is a `RemoteOperation::Preempt` request, and the host issues it on every steer, whether or not a cell is running, so every accepted steer paid the Hand's round trip before `steer_with_id` returned, while the model call was already cut short and the steer already durable. Now `State::finish_code_preempt` hands the started futures to `nanocode_platform::spawn` (a local task on WebAssembly). The order the generation counter relies on is unchanged: `start_code_preempt` still builds and polls each hook once under the lock, so the preempt request is on the transport before `consume_steering` can send `settle_code_preempt`. Nothing is replayed or dropped: the steer is accepted and recorded before the call returns, as before, and the hooks' results were already discarded (`BackendFuture<()>`). Measured with output/steer-lat (a Claude agent with `steer_preempts_model`, a `DurableSession` over `MemoryStore` on its own thread, a loopback Messages mock that holds every response open, 200 identified 4 KB steers 3 ms after each request arrives; call is `steer_with_id` start to return, reach is call start to the resend's arrival), 6 interleaved rounds per binary under the bench lock at load 5, medians of per-run percentiles with bootstrap 95% CIs. A hook that sleeps 5 ms (the remote round trip): call p50 6.05 [5.97, 6.11] to 0.23 [0.20, 0.32] ms, call p99 8.45 [7.52, 11.0] to 1.77 [1.04, 2.63] ms, reach p50 1.26 [1.12, 1.47] to 0.92 [0.84, 1.44] ms, reach p99 5.38 [5.07, 10.5] to 4.81 [3.38, 6.26] ms. No hook: call p50 0.25 [0.18, 0.33] and 0.27 [0.23, 0.32] ms, p99 1.84 and 2.01 ms, reach p50 1.08 and 1.23 ms, within noise. The wait for the cell's next boundary after a command steer happens on the Hand and is not in this call. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 2000`. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, agent/assemble.rs, agent/driver.rs.

- feat(turnlog): `FileLog`, a turn log host with a fixed header, a seq index and tail-only load (2026-11-16, o1start1). Opt-in: a host constructs `nanocode_turnlog::FileLog::open(path, FileOptions { scope, sync })` in place of its own `LogHost`, and existing hosts do not change. The data file begins with two 72-byte header slots (magic `nctlog01`, generation, end, indexed, next seq, tail offset, snapshot seq, crc32). A commit appends its records (row, move for `extend`, drop range) after `end`, syncs, writes the slot `generation % 2`, then writes its index entries (offset and length per seq, 16 bytes at `seq * 16` in `<path>.index`) and a second slot with `indexed = end`. A torn slot falls back to the other one, and an index that lags the header is rebuilt from the records in `[indexed, end)`, which is at most one commit. `load` reads the header and only `[tail, end)`, where `tail` is the offset of the first record at or after the newest snapshot row, and rejects a header whose snapshot seq differs from the newest snapshot row in that tail. `scan` reads the index range and then the rows, coalescing adjacent records into one read. `FileLog` runs the blocking I/O on one owning thread behind a `nanocode_sync` channel. `Image` and `Medium` hold the format and build for wasm32, and only `FileLog` (std::fs and a thread) is native. The start path does no scan: `FileLog::open` reads 144 bytes and nothing else, and no owner, index or registry walk happens before the first root call. scale-bench restart on the converted k100k log (397,076,868 bytes, 150,763 rows, tail 28.3 MB), `/proc/self/io` and `FileLog::io`: log open read 1,825,653 bytes in total, which is the 1.8 MB root region, against 432,196,409 bytes for the JSONL host (full parse, open 378 ms after main against 6.3 ms). Turn log open read 28,850,049 log bytes in 24 preads, against the whole file. At 10K (34.4 MB) the same counts are 281,781 and 3,954,091 bytes in 16 preads. The first root call fires from the armed root region before the log opens in both formats (main to first root call 4.6 to 10.8 ms at 10K and 100K, unlocked count runs). Turn log open is still about 1.66 s at 100K in both formats, because it decodes the 28 MB root snapshot, which grows with the number of children. Sim: `--scenario turns --policy turnlog` replays every committed write into an in-memory `Image` and, at each crash, checks that the header-and-tail load equals the full replay and the stored rows from the newest snapshot. Mutation `snapshot_pointer_stale` rewrites the header with the previous snapshot pointer and is caught by 121 of seeds 0..200. `sweep.sh 0 1500` passes for `--policy turnlog`, `--policy reference`, `--policy turnlog --takeover` and `--scenario store`. Checks: `cargo clippy --release --no-deps -p nanocode-turnlog -p nanocode-sim --features nanocode-code-mode/local-cells -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked --lib -p nanocode-turnlog --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- feat(turnlog): `Follower::advance` warms each owner that a deferred `Record::Forget` names (`Fold::take_forgets`), and the follower keeps its `Stats` into `claim` (2026-11-16, nanocode 1.0 durability swarm, standby lane). Why: a forget that waits on an owner state left that owner cold until `Follower::finish`, so `claim` read the owner state on the takeover path. The `--takeover` sim now also asserts that the claimed log reads the same turns, open calls, states and cells as a cold `TurnLog::open` at the same commit. Checks: `sweep.sh 0 300 3 --scenario turns --policy turnlog --snapshot-rows 4 --takeover` passes plain, with `--retain 2` and with `--state-bytes 131072`, `--twice` passes 200 seeds, and the mutation `takeover_opens` is caught by 60 of seeds 0..100. Measured with the ignored scale-bench (`--mode run --kill-at 0.5 --lease 1` primary on cores 1-3, `--mode hot` standby on core 0 woken by inotify on the log directory, interleaved with a plain `--mode restart` of the same log, host load 3 to 17): kill to claim has a median of 27.2 ms (95% CI 13.7 to 33.5, n=4) at 10K agents and 154.5 ms (119.2 to 240.9, n=3) at 100K. Claim to writable log is 2.4 ms (1.3 to 41.1) at 10K and 35.9 ms (26.5 to 45.3) at 100K. Kill to first root call is 945 ms (530 to 5217) at 10K and 5.1 s (3.7 to 9.5) at 100K, against 1.06 s (0.58 to 9.26) from start to first root call for the plain restart at 10K. At 100K the plain baseline fails to open the cut `.plain` copy in 2 of 3 runs (an index root section reads 0 rows), so its number is n=1 (28.2 s).
`nanocode-sim` checks that a restart reruns no leaf of a remote coordinator (2026-11-16). The `runtime` scenario with `--children remote` reports `coordinator_leaf_rerun` when a leaf whose label names a coordinator (`r0.t0.c1.c0`) runs as a second remote child after the coordinator restarts, separately from `remote_child_respawned` for a root child. The mutation `coordinator-forgets-spawns` makes a recovering coordinator perform a `spawn_agent` step again instead of recording its outcome as unknown, which is what a coordinator does when its subagent journal does not survive the restart. The sweep `--seeds 0..40 --scenario runtime --children remote` catches it on 11 of 40 seeds and passes 40 of 40 without it. A 2K Durable Object shard (200 leaves under 4 coordinators) that made 400 leaf calls after a workerd restart traced to its mock provider, not to the SDK: each coordinator restored with the same session id and its journal, and the mock issued a new spawn cell. `TurnLogPolicy::whole` uses `is_multiple_of` and is a `const fn`, which clippy 1.100 requires under `-D warnings`. Checks: clippy `--no-deps -p nanocode-sim`, `cargo +1.97.1` wasm32 check of `nanocode`, sweeps `--seeds 0..200` of runtime remote (with and without `--twice`), runtime log and kv, and turns turnlog `--twice`, all 200 of 200.

- perf(launch): `scripts/nanocode` runs the release `nanocode` straight from a local store when the tree is clean, without starting cargo; `scripts/launch.rs` is its helper, compiled by `rustc` into the store on first use and rebuilt when its source changes (2026-11-16, launch lane). Why: with nothing to rebuild, `cargo build --release -p nanocode-cli` still takes 0.32 s and a fresh clone with a warm store 0.55 s, while the binary runs in 7 ms, so nothing that goes through cargo reaches 0.1 s. The key is every tracked file's index entry (mode, blob ID and path), checked against the file's stat as git does and rehashed when racy, plus `rustc -vV` (memoized on the toolchain files' times), OS, arch, the profile, every Cargo config and `rust-toolchain` file from the root's parents and `CARGO_HOME`, and the build-related environment. A dirty, unmerged, split-index or SHA-256 index, a `RUSTC` override or any read that fails goes through cargo. After a cargo build the helper records the pair it built (hardlinks, else copies) in the background, only if no tracked file or toolchain input changed after the build started. Measured on the 5-CPU hosted Hand, each run a fresh clone and target, N=10 interleaved (run launch-202611161500): a cached key 0.050 s median, p95 0.103 s, 95% bootstrap CI [0.039, 0.073] s; a miss with a warm store 0.491 s against cargo's 0.516 s (paired mean -0.012 s, CI [-0.051, +0.027] s); a miss with an empty store 34.1 s against 33.2 s (+2.8% of medians, paired mean -0.94 s, CI [-4.9, +1.7] s; the empty-store path took about 33 s for both in this window, against 2.95 s earlier that day). An edit to crates/core/sync rebuilds nanocode-sync and runs the new binary, before and after it is committed, and checking out the old commit again runs the old one. dash -n passes.
- The mapped root request dispatches before the turn log opens, and its region clears before the completion write (2026-11-16, image lane). `ClaudeClient::arm_root_region` checks the region (magic, length, checksum), decodes it and builds the auth headers, and returns an `ArmedRoot`; `ArmedRoot::fire` polls the post once inline with a no-op waker and spawns it only while it is pending, so the request is written before the caller continues to the log open, with no executor hop. `prefetch_root_region` is arm then fire. `root_region_checksum` reads the checksum from the 32-byte header, so a host that arms early can rearm when the file changed. The root request clears the region before it records the completion: a crash between the two now leaves no region, and the restart replays the call normally, where before it prefetched a call that the replay never makes. Sim: `whole` reports a mapped root call that the restored root never adopts or rejects (stop and turn cancel excluded); mutation `region-skips-clear` keeps the region after each completion and is caught (seed 7 of 0..50, `region-keeps-stale` seed 1). Sweeps 0..200 runtime log, kv, remote children and http wire: 800 passed, 0 failed.
- perf(buildcache): the helper hashes with SHA-NI when the CPU has it, and release builds compile the build scripts that generate the code-mode snapshot (and their build-time dependencies) optimized through `[profile.release.build-override]` entries (2026-11-16, warm2). Why: on a Hand whose local store is warm, a fresh clone's build is all cache hits, and hashing inputs plus re-running the snapshot build script were the largest parts left after the probe memo (9db1c1869). Matched A/B on the 5-CPU hosted Hand, separate warm stores per variant, fresh clone and target each run, N=10 interleaved (run warm2-202611161421): master median 0.820 s (0.781-0.951), patch 0.707 s (0.620-0.855), -13.8%, paired mean -0.126 s with 95% t-interval [-0.163, -0.090] s. An edit to crates/core/sync still rebuilds, relinks and runs, an offline warm build succeeds, and dash -n passes. Build-override changes only build scripts and proc-macros, so shipped binaries are unchanged; it does change those units' cache keys, so fresh clones compile them until the mirror republishes.
- fix(subagents): `Registry::persist_durably` flushes the subagent store after the journal write, so a `submit_result` receipt, a spawn receipt or a completion that waits on it is acknowledged only after the record is committed (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 swarm, exactlyonce lane). Why: on a turn-log host without `OneLog::settle_durably` (every in-object parent, natively and in nanocode-ts without `remoteSubagents`), subagent journal writes reach `OneLogStore::replace` or `commit` with `Settle::Durable`, which commit the lease only while recovering or with `durable_settles`. The journal writer then answered its waiters while the records sat in the lease buffer, and `submit_result` returned `"durable": true` for an acceptance that a kill could still drop, after the child had already been told to end its turn. What: `SubagentStore::flush` and `ChildJournalStore::flush` (provided, `Ok`), `SharedJournal::flush` calls `SharedStore::flush`, which reaches `OneLogStore::flush` (9708674f4 on master: it commits the lease at `Point::Progress` when it holds buffered records). A flush that finds nothing buffered writes no row, so concurrent persists of one journal cycle commit once. Measured on 2026-11-15 (5-CPU Hand, mock provider, exactly-once harness output/eo-flat with SIGKILL at 25, 50 and 75 percent of acknowledged children, then a final resume): 10K flat before and after this change both end with lost 0, rerun 0 and called_after_ack 0, so the harness does not reach the window at 10K (the lease commits about twice per child for other rows). The change is kept because the receipt promises durability: `submit_result` answered durable true before the record was committed. Sims on this series, base (this commit reverted) and fix: runtime kv 600/600 both, log 400/400 both, log local 400/400 both, kv remote 300/300 both. Exactly-once on restart for this series (2026-11-16, hosted Hand, mock provider): the 100K flat exactly-once run with SIGKILL at 25 and 50 percent ends with rerun 0 of 100,000, task_twice 0 and called_after_ack 0, and every acknowledged task is present (50,004 acknowledged, all among 50,049 tasks). The 2K workerd crash gate (remoteSubagents, 2,000 children, batch 100, rate 200) passes spawn and turn with lost 0 and 0 repeats, and twice with lost 0 and 0 repeats. done ends with lost 0 and 0 child calls after the restart, but one child repeated a model call before the restart, which the gate counts as a failure. With remoteCoordinators at 200 leaves under 4 coordinators, turn and twice repeat every leaf that was done before the kill, on master and on this series alike, so the sharded tree still needs its own restore fix. Sims: `child-respawns-fresh` caught in 22 of seeds 0..200; with no mutation runtime kv and log 1000 of 1000 each, kv remote 1000, log remote 500, log local 500, turns 1000, turns takeover 500, agents 500 and cell_calls 500 pass.
- feat(sim): `--children remote` turns queued spawns on for half the seeds, as nanocode-ts does, and the invariant `remote_child_respawned` fails when one child task runs under two remote sessions, with the mutation `child-respawns-fresh` (the host opens a restored child as a new object under a new key) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 durability swarm, remoterestore lane). The invariant is checked where the simulated host creates a child object: a task label that already ran under another session id means a running child was not reattached, or a completed child runs again. `child-respawns-fresh` is caught in 279 of seeds 0..1000 (sweep.sh, 3 jobs); with no mutation the same binary passes `--children remote` 0..5000 and local 0..2000. Limit: the simulated turn log saves a started child before any crash finds it unstarted, so the SDK before the fix also passes 0..1000 here; the shard harness and the workerd crash gate reach that state. With `set_max_concurrency` 1-2 added (not kept), the SDK before the fix fails 15 of 0..1000 on root settle and `close_all` timeouts with no respawn (seeds 8, 37, 64), a separate follow-up.
- fix(subagents): a restored remote child keeps its session id. A queued spawn that a restart finds unstarted is reopened through `RemoteChildren::respawn` (`ChildSpec::restored`, the same session id) and its first start adopts the turn `child_pending` reports, instead of a respawn under a new `uuid_v7` (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 durability swarm, remoterestore lane). Why: nanocode-ts turns queued spawns on. A queued spawn journals the child once as unstarted, and its attach and first turn reach the root journal only with a later deferred save, so a root killed while its remote coordinators ran restored them as unstarted. `Registry::unstarted` then reissued each one a fresh session id: the old child object and its log were orphaned and the whole subtree ran again (bet-shard2: 0 of 64 sessions reused, the pending resolver never called, every leaf done before the kill ran again; the 2K workerd crash gate failed spawn, turn and twice). What: `AgentFactory::respawn` (provided, `None`) and `AgentHandle::respawn_with_host_context`. `RoutedFactory::respawn` answers only when the spawn would go to the `ChildHost` (no provider, the parent's family), with the same route test as `spawn`. `build_unstarted` tries it for a restored unstarted child, and `Registry::reissue_unstarted` (the old reissue, moved out of `Registry::unstarted`) gives a new id only to an in-process child, whose partial session must not be reused. The unstarted branch of `restored_session` counts a resume attempt, so `Registry::pending_turn` asks the resolver at the first start, and the harness's initial `Start` adopts a pending turn by its request id without steering the assignment into it a second time (the pending turn is that assignment). Measured on the hosted Hand with bet-shard2's shard harness, the alias workaround removed (output/shard-bench, mock provider, rate 5000, 4 workers), killed at 50%: 10K leaves under 100 coordinators, four runs, and 100K leaves under 100 coordinators of 1,000: 0 coordinators under a new session (100 of 100 opened restored, 100 `child_pending` reads), every leaf reported completed by its coordinator (10,000 x4, 100,000), 0 repeated completions, 0 leaves done before the kill called again, 0 failed coordinators. Checks: `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-agent-core -p nanocode-subagents -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo +1.97.1 check -p nanocode-agent-core -p nanocode-subagents -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` pass.
- The build cache answers cargo's rustc probes from a memo (2026-11-16, local lane). Cargo runs `rustc -vV` and the `rustc - --crate-name ___ --print=...` target-info probe through the wrapper on every fresh `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`; each went through the rustup proxy to the real rustc (about 8 ms each, measured old helper 8-9 ms vs 1-2 ms memo hit). The helper now keys the answer by the rustc version, the toolchain path, the flags and the `RUST*`, `*_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` and `SDKROOT` environment, stores it under `rustc/probe-<hash>` and replays it; a target `.json`, a rustc outside a rustup toolchain, a failure or any stderr is never memoized. A second fresh clone on a Hand with a warm `~/.cache/nanocode` (same commit, fresh target, timed excluding the clone, 5 CPUs, interleaved, N=10 each): 0.954 s median (p95 0.995) before, 0.700 s (p95 0.790) after, -27%. Fresh XDG baseline in the same session 3.204 s (p95 3.435); the warm store with `NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_URL=off` 1.122 s, so the warm path is purely local; sccache as `RUSTC_WRAPPER` with a warm local dir 10.95 s (it cannot cache the bins' link). The clone itself costs more than the warm build: `git clone --depth 1` 5.02 s, `--filter=blob:none --depth 1` 9.90 s, `--sparse --depth 1` 4.71 s (median, N=10). Offline (`unshare -rn`) builds succeed and editing `crates/core/sync` relinks and runs.
- perf(claude): `api_body` already serializes only the tail past the kept body prefix (61c1d1bad, `WireCache::assemble`), checked byte-identical and measured (2026-11-16, body prep lane). Why: a downstream seq trace (pinned at 12ab430264, which predates 61c1d1bad) showed 406 µs p50 preparation per model call, with the whole transcript serialized into a fresh buffer each call. The ignored `output/body-prep` harness (Claude agent, MemoryStore durability, 20 tools, 40 KB system, 60 turns of 4 tool steps against a local mock, thinking switched every 7 turns, compaction every 13, 60k-token auto compaction, 1h cache breakpoints moving every call; counting global allocator) ran one build with the kept prefix and with it turned off by a temporary switch. All 164 bodies of a 40-turn run were byte-identical (`cmp`), across 3 compactions and the thinking changes, and the prefix was reused on 120 of 164 calls (misses: first call, compaction, thinking change). Four interleaved pairs of 240 calls: reuse saved 38 KB and 4.5 allocations per call (525.7 against 563.5 KB, 1017 against 1022 allocations per call over the whole process), and preparation p50 stayed within noise (85-143 µs against 87-142 µs). So on master the remaining preparation time is elsewhere than body serialization, and moving the pin past 61c1d1bad is what removes the per-call full serialization.
- feat(claude): mapped root request on restart, behind `ClaudeClient::with_root_region` (default off) (2026-11-16, mmaproot2). Each root request the client posts is stored through the host's `RootRegion` sink as one region: magic `NCROOT01`, endpoint, non-secret headers and the rendered body, checked with xxh64. A committed root completion clears it. On restart the host reads the region and calls `prefetch_root_region` before it opens the turn log: the client posts the body at once with fresh auth headers and parks the buffered response in a slot keyed by the body hash. The first root request of the restored session adopts that response only when its rendered body hash matches. Otherwise the client drops it, reports `mapped root request stale` and posts normally, so a mismatch costs one wasted call and never a second answer. The prefetch task holds its response until a request claims it and aborts when the slot is dropped, so no call stays open across a crash. scale-bench, 100K children, `--mode restart --until-root 1 --target 0`, one core, interleaved N=5 under bench2.lock (load 12.7-19.2): exec to the first root request at the mock went from 8.97 s median (p95 21.25 s, 6.31-22.81 s) to 93.9 ms median (p95 123.0 ms, 84.1-127.9 ms, mean 99.2 ms, 95% CI [77.1, 121.2]), paired difference 11.89 s, 95% CI [3.24, 20.54]. All 5 runs adopted the prefetched response. exec to main is 28.4 ms median and the region read plus prefetch start end at 40.1 ms; the rest waits for the prefetch task behind the synchronous turn log open on the one worker. Sim: `--scenario runtime` checks at each epoch that the stored region equals the region of the last root request, and mutation `region-keeps-stale` is caught by 21 of 50 seeds. 200-seed sweeps pass for `--store log`, `--store kv`, `--children remote` and `--wire http`. Checks: `cargo clippy -p nanocode-backend-claude-client -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-sim --features nanocode-code-mode/local-cells -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- fix(turnlog): `Lease::load_owners` marks each warmed owner's state read (`Fold::touch`), as `load_owner` already did through `warm_state` (2026-11-16, store calls lane). Why: a downstream A/B saw store calls per model request rise from 7.15 to 7.53 when the pin moved from 15107afa to 33819fb4. Bisected with an ignored `output/store-calls` harness (a counting `LogHost` over `MemoryLog`, the `nanocode::turnlog` runtime, snapshot_ratio 2, 30 turns of 4 tool steps against a local mock, 116 model requests measured after the first turn): 15107afa and b19220112 made 1.000 store calls per request with the session kept open, 36dd8652d (lazy index root, snapshots counted by rewritten bytes) 1.207, all of it 24 `scan`s. Snapshots now come due inside a session, each snapshot evicts pages nobody marked read since the last one, and `load_owners` warmed pages without marking them, so every snapshot dropped the pages the next step reloaded, one `scan` each. With the fix, master (257542188) goes from 1.207 to 1.000 per request (scan 24 to 0, append 112 and append_compacting 4 unchanged), in two interleaved runs. Reopening the log before every turn stays at 3.03-3.15 against 1.250 at 15107afa (about 7 scans and one load per open): that is 36dd8652d's intended lazy root and page loads on open, which replace replaying the whole log.
- fix(claude): the nested model requests of the WebSearch and WebFetch tools count in the turn usage (2026-11-16). `nested_web_search` (behind `nested_web_search`, `upstream_web` and the public `web_search_tool`) and `web::Side::ask` add each response's usage, with an estimated cost for the requested model, to a session-keyed `AtomMap` (`SPENT_ASIDE`, keyed by the invoking session ID, as `durability/format.rs` keeps its prefixes). `State::spent_aside` takes that entry together with the cache refresh usage in `State::refreshed` at the three places where `run_rounds` already took the refresh usage, so the main-loop accounting does not change otherwise. Why: these requests use the provider web search tool and are billed, but their usage was dropped after `collect_stream`. Cache keep-warm requests from `keep.rs` already counted through `State::refreshed` since c95cb6e6c. Neither kind emits `model.call.completed`, so a host that sums that event's usage still leaves both out. `Usage` has no server tool use field, so `web_search_requests` is not counted. Check (ignored `output/usage-acct`): one harness binary built against this tree and one against origin/master 4736c723c, each run against a local Messages mock that records each request's usage. The full case is a 310 s custom tool that triggers one keep-warm, then one WebSearch call, then a final message. On master the turn reports 3,909 input and 66 output tokens against 4,312 and 129 the mock returned (the search request's 403 and 63 are missing, the keep-warm's 903 input tokens are present). With this change it reports 4,312 and 129, and the cached and cache-write tokens (2,700 and 900) are equal in both builds. The estimated cost rises from 0.007596 to 0.010468 USD. A plain one-request turn reports the same usage in both builds, and all request bodies are equal except the per-run device and session IDs. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (only the existing `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT` warning), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`, `rustfmt --check` with no new findings in the changed files, `git diff --check`.
- feat(sim): the turns scenario under `--policy turnlog` checks `cell_calls_forgotten` at each cell `forget`: the cell's journal is gone and the open calls are the ones before minus the cell's `<origin>/` prefix (2026-11-16, stall20k1 lane). The mutation `forgets_other_cell` forgets cell+1 instead and is caught by 200 of seeds 0..200, and `sweep.sh 0 1500 3 --scenario turns --policy turnlog` passes. Why: 95291a918 replaced the `retain` in `Record::Forget` with a prefix range, and no invariant covered which calls a forget removes. The same scan also stalled live 100K runs, not only restarts: each child turn start (`CodeModeControl::begin_turn`) forgets finished cell journals under the exclusive log lease while the root cell keeps up to 100,000 spawn calls open. On 631e64286 a 100K scale-bench run (`--rate 1000 --workers 4`, load 12-16 on 4 CPUs) reached done 6,001 at 400 s and 10,763 at 1,190 s, with flat phases of up to 25 s at `in_flight` 0 in which gdb showed `Fold::apply` in `starts_with` on every busy thread. A 30 s flat phase stall-kills `--kill-at 0.5` runs, as at done 20,949. With the range the same run reached 20,192 at 400 s and 50,241 at 1,190 s, and `--kill-at 0.5 --stall 120` reached done 50,001 in 778 s. Flat phases of up to 30 s remain, in snapshot `index`/`sections` and root cell journal commits under the lease. Checks: `cargo clippy --release --no-deps -p nanocode-turnlog -p nanocode-sim --features nanocode-code-mode/local-cells -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked --lib -p nanocode-turnlog --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- One-request head and background prefetch for the workspace cache (2026-11-16, fast3). `buildcache publish` also writes `workspace-head-<cksum>-<os>-<arch>`, a gzip tar of the eager list, the raw index and the helper, so prefetch makes one small request instead of three (it falls back to the three files when a release has no head), and the bundle keeps its own connection: one HTTP/2 connection carrying both the head and the 23 MB bundle delayed the head to about 1.9 s, against 0.6 to 0.9 s on its own. The wrapper starts prefetch and the helper in the background at cargo's first probe (`rustc -vV`) under an exclusive flock on `remote.lock`, so probes run plain rustc at once and compiling calls wait on a shared flock, which overlaps the fetch with cargo's resolution (the prefetch starts about 0.25 s after cargo does, not 0.5 s). nanocode-exec stays in the eager bundle: `-p nanocode-cli` builds both bins. Measured on a hosted Hand against the experiment release buildcache-exp-fast3, published from a mirror-like master build, fresh clone, XDG_CACHE_HOME and target per run, N=10 interleaved, 1-min load < 1.0 at each start: master 2.993 3.346 3.282 2.576 2.691 2.854 4.521 3.240 2.493 3.078 s (median 3.036); patch 2.763 2.976 2.217 3.038 2.886 2.671 3.055 2.509 2.250 3.238 s (median 2.825, -7.0%). The 1.5 s goal is out of reach on this network: the 23 MB bundle alone took 0.9 to 2.2 s, and the build waits on it for its last hits and the link. An offline build with a warm cache succeeds (0.98 s), a cold offline build falls back to compiling, and an edit to crates/core/sync after a lazy build relinks and runs.
- perf(turnlog): `Record::Forget` removes the open calls of the forgotten cell with a prefix range on `Fold::calls` instead of a `retain` over every open call (2026-11-16, rootfirst2 lane). A 100K-child restart in scale-bench (`--mode restart --until-root 1`, one core) spent more than 20 minutes in `Fold::paged` under `writer::warm`, where each paged `Forget` scanned all open calls, and was killed before its first root call. With the range it reaches the first root call in 15.3 s (load 10-14, same log). Checks: nanocode-sim 200-seed sweeps of turns `--twice`, `--snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072`, `--owners 2000 --long 50`, `--calm --row-limit 1024` and runtime `--store log`/`kv`, clippy, wasm32 check.

- Warm standby takeover (2026-11-16, standby1). `TurnLog::follow` returns a `Follower` that folds the rows that `TurnLog::open` folds and keeps the fold, history and snapshot accounting between calls. `Follower::advance` scans the rows after the last folded row and folds them, holding back the last logical row until the next call, and skips section rows that `load` does not return. `Follower::claim` folds the held rows, opens the writer state that `open` builds, and commits one `writer` host row at the next sequence before it returns the log. `open` is now `follow` followed by the same finish. `OneLog::claim` and `nanocode::turnlog_claim` wrap it. Fencing comes from the append itself: a stale writer appends at a sequence the claim row already holds and gets `StoreError::Fenced`. The claim commit skips the snapshot check, because a snapshot evaluation at 100K children took 35 s of the takeover (gdb samples, 20 of 25). The poll cadence belongs to the host: the follower reads only when the host calls `advance`. Scale bench, hosted Hand, load 4 to 11, primary killed at 0.5 of the run, standby following the file with 1 ms polls: kill to lease 27 to 48 ms at 10K and 95 to 367 ms at 100K, with 0 rows left to fold at the claim in every run. Kill to an open log: 80 to 140 ms at 10K (plain open 180 to 310 ms), 3.2 s at 100K. Kill to the first root call: 1.36 to 1.46 s at 10K (plain restart from process start 1.0 to 2.1 s) and 60 s at 100K, so registry restore and the first root call after open, not the log, now set the takeover time. Checks: nanocode-sim `--takeover` asserts that a claimed log matches a cold open, keeps every acknowledged event, announces no event again and fences the stale writer (300 of 300 seeds pass), and the `takeover_opens` mutation, which takes over with a plain open, is caught in 92 of 100 seeds. `cargo clippy -D warnings` for the changed packages with `nanocode-code-mode/local-cells` and `cargo +1.97.1 check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` pass.

- feat(sim): `--scenario cell_calls` runs one async Code Mode cell per seed on the embedded djs host (2026-11-16, stall100k lane gcbarrier3). The cell awaits 1,000 to 30,000 tool calls in `Promise.all` batches of up to 500, with results padded by up to 64 bytes. The scenario checks that each call index reaches the host exactly once, that the cell sums every result once and that two runs of a seed give the same trace digest. Why: 83341910e fixed a minor collection that remembered an old Generator frame slot twice, which corrupted async cells (cm10k reported 17,500 calls instead of 10,300), and no simulator scenario covered async cells under collection. Seeds 0..40 issue 592,786 calls and pass plain and with `--twice`. The mutation `cross_results` (each result answers the previous call) is caught by 40 of 40 seeds. A build with 83341910e reverted (the clean-card scan and its `BUILT_BY`) fails 25 of 40 seeds with `index N reached the host twice`. Checks: `cargo clippy --release --no-deps -p nanocode-sim -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode-engine --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
