- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::persistence_nudge` returns a headless root session to work once when its final message admits that part of the task is not done or not verified (2026-11-16). The admission list, `admits_incomplete` and the nudge text move from the Codex backend into `nanocode_tool_host::deadline` (`INCOMPLETE_ADMISSIONS`, `admits_incomplete`, `PERSISTENCE_NUDGE`) with the same 43 phrases and the same bytes, so both backends read one source and the Codex behavior does not change. With the option on, a final message of a headless root session that matches the list appends the nudge as a user message once per turn (`Cursor::persistence_nudged`, durable, `#[serde(default)]`) and the round continues. The check runs after the finish check and the fresh attempt branch, so it applies only to a final message that those branches let end the turn. Default off: the turn ends as before. Why: of 16 failed claude-opus-5-5 rows in two private benchmark exports (14 terminal tasks, 2 repository tasks), 5 end with a final message that matches the list ("couldn't", "I haven't", "could not") while 3 to 57 minutes of the task limit remain. In 3 of them the finish check ran, the model made 2 to 4 tool calls and then admitted the gap in its next final message. An arm with `finish_retries(1)` passed all 3 of those tasks in the same run (36/36 against 33/36). In the other 2 no finish check ran, because `fold_finish` skips it after the first time reminder, so `finish_retries` cannot reach them. Since 1adee5c97 a headless Opus session also skips the finish check by default. The nudge is the one guard against a stated incomplete result in both cases. The other 11 rows are a wrong result stated as verified (9, 8 of them after a finish check or a time reminder) and an interface guessed from the statement that the hidden tests do not match (2), which this option does not address. Check (2026-11-16, ignored `output/persistence-nudge`): one harness binary built against this tree and one against d4a9ef0d7, each run against a scripted Messages mock in four cases (an admission and a clean final message, each with and without `finish_check(true)`). Off and the base send byte-identical request bodies in all four cases (`diff -rq`). On sends byte-identical bodies in the clean cases. In the admission cases, on sends one more request whose last user message is `PERSISTENCE_NUDGE`, and the clean reply after it ends the turn. A second admission after the nudge ends the turn after 2 requests. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-codex` passes native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings` passes native for the three crates. The wasm32 clippy run fails on `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT` in `environment.rs`, the same as at d4a9ef0d7. `rustfmt --check` reports no new findings in the changed files, and `git diff --check` is clean.
- perf(build): a fresh clone's cached release build of `nanocode-cli` on a 4-CPU hosted Hand takes 2.9-3.3 s instead of 3.7-4.1 s (interleaved, load 1.1-1.9, 2026-11-16). The sh wrapper first execs `scripts/.buildcache`, a symlink to the helper that the helper itself writes when its name's checksum matches the POSIX `cksum` of `buildcache.rs`; a mismatching helper removes the link and re-execs the wrapper, so a hit no longer spawns `cksum` (21 ms per call through the wrapper before, 10 ms without `cksum`). On Linux the helper links glibc statically and is stripped (falling back to a dynamic link), which cuts a spawn from 7-9 ms to 3-4 ms and the published helper from 6.3 MB to 2.0 MB; warm rebuilds into an empty target went from 2.6 s to 0.85 s. Prefetch fetches the eager list, index and helper with `--parallel-immediate` (1.3-1.4 s instead of 1.8 s: plain `-Z` waits to multiplex the three redirects over one connection). Publish also writes `workspace/eager-blocks`: the eager packs interleaved round-robin in 1 MiB chunks (each chunk headed `name`, `length total`) and compressed by `xz -6e -T0 --block-size=16MiB`, so the near-identical `nanocode` and `nanocode-exec` binaries stay inside one block (1 MiB interleave of the two bins: 20.6 MB against 21.6 MB for one stream) and `xz -dc -T0` decodes blocks in parallel (0.38 s against 1.08 s for the bins; streamed from GitHub 1.7-2.8 s against 3.2-3.6 s under load). Prefetch reads `eager-blocks` and falls back to `eager-packs`, which publish keeps writing for older checkouts; `bundled` reads both, a header with one size being a whole entry.
- feat(codex): `CodexBuilder::verification_requested(true)` (opt-in, default false) appends a `<verification_request>` block after the host instructions (`ModelConfig::host_instructions`), which every request carries in its system prompt (2026-11-16). The block states that the user asks for the implementation to be tested and verified, and asks the model to run the tests and checks that come with the task, test the result on the cases the task states, fix what fails and run them again before its final message. The upstream Codex prompt text stays unchanged. Its Luna and Sol prompts say "Do not add or run tests unless the user asks you to test or verify implementation", and the block is the user request that this sentence names. Why: in a nanoeval run of a private suite (21 tasks, 3 attempts per arm, gpt-6-luna, high effort), the Codex backend passed 50 of 63 attempts (10 failed, 3 errored) against 55 to 59 for four other agents on the same model. 6 of its 13 non-passing attempts end with "I did not run tests" or "Tests were not run". Codex CLI, which sends the same upstream prompt, says this in 3 of its 8 failed attempts, and the three agents on other prompts say it in none. On one task its three attempts read the given test file and never ran it. Replayed from the event logs, two of the three results fail that visible test file (`ValueError` on a stated example) and the third passes it. The two agents that passed all three attempts of that task ran the tests. The other three such attempts ended as errors after the persistence notice and the finish check: the model repeated "I did not run tests" without a tool call and then returned an empty response (the end that `2aa018da4` now completes). The other non-passing attempts are not in scope: one task that every arm fails in every attempt, and four refusals that are correct but too short for a rubric that wants the counting argument or the failing cell. Off is byte-identical: a harness in ignored `output/verification-requested` builds against this commit and its parent and writes `system_prompt()` and `host_instructions()` for Luna and Sol, with and without additional instructions. All 8 off outputs are identical to the parent's (18,590 to 22,347 bytes), and on adds 308 bytes. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-codex -- -D warnings`, `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check`, `git diff --check`. `cargo clippy` on `nanocode-backend-codex-client` reports only the existing `missing_const_for_fn` on `reconnect_delay` from `c95cb6e6c`. The effect on pass rate and time is the nanoeval arm's to measure.
- perf(claude): `api_body` writes the cached system and tools JSON straight into the request body instead of serializing them into the `Head` and `Tail` strings first and copying those into the body, so each model request copies the system and tools once, not twice (2026-11-16, per-request CPU lane). Bodies are byte-identical: `output/req-cpu` (the step-lat harness with a counting allocator and a client-only CPU clock that subtracts the mock server's threads; 20 turns x 30 steps x 20 tools, 420 KB last body) dumped every request body from both builds and `cmp` found no difference. Allocated bytes per request fell from 1,562 KB to 1,305 KB (-16.5%; allocations 1,296 to 1,295). Client CPU per request, interleaved on a hosted Hand at load average 9-10 from other lanes: 0.634 to 0.597 ms (-5.8%) in 20 rounds and 0.520 to 0.531 ms (+2%) in 10 rounds, so the CPU change is within noise on this host. Not done, with reasons: the records stream keeps deflate level 7 (the measure(turnlog) entries of 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 rejected lower levels), and moving its deflate to a worker or to batch close moves the same CPU rather than cutting it, while `Settle::Durable` commits need the compressed row before they acknowledge. Tool definitions are already shared: `exec_description` is cached by source pointer, `WireCache::tools` returns the last entry when the specs compare equal, and `JsonSchema` and `Arc<str>` equality short-circuit on pointer equality, so the per-request cost there is the comparison, not a rebuild; the only per-round rebuild, `refresh_dynamic_tools` calling the `dynamic_tools` factory, runs only for direct-only hosts with a Code Mode host.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::clearing_cache_floors` places the two cache floors at the tool result clearing boundaries (2026-11-16). `clear_tool_results` now returns the message of the first result kept by the latest clearing and the message where the clearing before it started. With the option on and no image floor, `cache_floors_with` places a breakpoint on the last block before each of the two messages, as it does for image eviction. When a clearing moves the boundary, the prefix up to the previous boundary is unchanged since the previous clearing. That prefix is then read instead of written again from the end of the system prompt. The floors take the slots of the tools tail and the second system marker. Default off: `cleared` returns no floors, and the requests stay the same byte for byte. Why: with the default clearing (12 kept results, 20,000 tokens), each clearing changes the bytes of a tool result inside the cached prefix. The longest cached prefix then falls back to the system prompt, and every later message is written to the cache again at 1.25x. Measured (2026-11-16, ignored `output/cache-writes`, 5-core x86_64 hosted Hand, debug `nanocode exec --ephemeral -m claude-opus-5-5 -t medium --hedge-cap-percent 0` against a local mock of the Messages API that returns code-mode tool calls with log-normal result sizes): six turns of 41 to 81 requests with 1 to 7 clearings each. `model.py` replays the captured bodies under the prompt caching rules (prefix match at each breakpoint with a 20-block lookback, 5-minute entries, write 1.25x, read 0.1x, 4 characters per token). Against the master binary, the pooled modeled input cost changes by -6.21% and cache-write tokens by -13.07%. Per turn the change is -0.45% to -9.42% and grows with the number of clearings (1 clearing: -0.45% and -0.75%, 5 or 7 clearings: -9.39% and -9.42%). Cache writes are 52% of the modeled master input cost. With the option off, all 406 request bodies equal the master bodies after the normalization of session IDs, device IDs, run paths and wall times. Two master runs differ by the same fields only. A floor whose 5-minute entry expires before the next clearing costs one write of the second system block. Follow-up measurement (2026-11-16, same harness): Terminal-Bench 2.1 attempts average about 21 requests (run 1fbd4a11: 780 exec and wait calls over 39 attempts). For six turns of 22 to 31 requests with 0 or 1 clearing, the option changes the pooled modeled input cost by -0.50%. In the same turns, `tool_result_clearing(1_000_000_000, u64::MAX)` turns clearing off and changes it by -10.72% against the default clearing (-11.42%, -15.02% and -19.28% in the three turns where a clearing fires, 0% in the others). For the six turns of 41 to 81 requests, the same setting changes it by +7.15% (-12.57% to +13.92%). A clearing rewrites every message after the first cleared result at 1.25x, and saves 0.1x of the cleared tokens on each later request. It pays only if more than 12.5 times the rewritten tokens divided by the cleared tokens requests follow it. The 20,000-token trigger therefore raises the cost of short turns. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude --no-deps -- -D warnings`, `git diff --check`.
- feat(tool-host): the finish notice of a headless root session asks for an input that must stay unchanged, for each stated number to be computed, and for named library calls to keep their defaults (2026-11-16). `FINISH_HEAD` gains two bullets: each limit or target number the task states (a gap, range, tolerance or fitted value) is computed from the result by the method the task implies, printed and compared, and a library call or tool the task names without options runs with its defaults and no added option. The second sentence of the first `FINISH_TAIL` bullet now says the result was run on an input that differs from the given example and, if some inputs must stay as they are (clean, valid or already correct), on one of those, and that nothing is tuned to the given example alone. It drops "including the case the task names", which the `FINISH_HEAD` case bullet of aff538f6e covers. The default non-brief notice without a time grows from 2,007 to 2,396 bytes (+389, the checklist from 1,675 to 2,064), measured from the constants. Why: of 36 claude-opus-5-5 rows that failed on Terminal-Bench 2.1, each failed the same hidden test in every run. 14 fit the shown input and failed a held-out one (in one task 6 of 10 runs never ran a second input, in another the filter changed inputs it had to keep), 7 stated a numeric limit or fitted value that was never computed, and 4 added options to a named library call that the statement did not ask for (Claude Code failed none of those 4). The wording names no task. Measured (2026-11-16, nanoeval, claude-opus-5-5 medium with the finish check on, task-clustered 95% CIs, against aff538f6e on separate Workers): hard-v1 15 tasks x3 44/45 against 42/45, +4.4 pts [0, +13.3], cost per pass 0.894x [0.794, 0.975]; fresh-v1 +2.4 pts [0, +7.1], 0.953x [0.862, 1.027]; hardperf 15/15 each, 1.037x [0.968, 1.113]. The finish check fired once in all 204 rows of both arms. False success claims (a failed row that ended as completed) 3/102 against 6/102. The out-of-sample gate holds, so the notice is the default. Terminal-Bench 2.1 stays in-sample only. Since 1adee5c97 a headless Opus session skips the finish check by default, so this notice reaches Opus only with finish_check(true) or finish_retries, and Sonnet and Haiku by default. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host` native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `rustfmt --check`, `git diff --check`.
- fix(turnlog): the snapshot head holds one `Record::Root` that points at a lazily loaded root section with the `Index` and `Groups` records, instead of carrying every index entry itself, and the snapshot due rule counts only the section bytes a snapshot rewrites (section bytes scaled by the share of rewritten section lines) plus the index bytes, instead of every section byte (2026-11-15, turn log open lanes tlopen and lazytail1). A snapshot reuses the previous root section when no page or group changed and supersedes the old one otherwise. `MemoryLog::load` scans backward to the last snapshot row instead of reading every row of the scope. Why: master required the tail to reach `ratio` times all section and index bytes, so a tail that held fresh owners never reached it, restart runs wrote zero snapshot rows, and `OneLog::open` replayed the whole log; and a cold open decoded every index entry of the head, so open grew with the number of owners. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 4 to 12, 3 interleaved rounds under bench2.lock, each binary on the 10K and 100K logs that its own scale-bench run wrote with --kill-at 0.5): snapshot rows 0 against 13 at both sizes (log 21.8 against 44.2 MB at 10K, 40.8 against 73.9 MB at 100K); openprof cold open 1.52 to 2.47 s against 54 to 179 ms at 10K and 2.29 to 3.74 s against 339 to 416 ms at 100K; restart to the root's subagent list 1.70 to 3.84 s against 0.80 to 2.25 s at 10K and 3.50 to 4.17 s against 1.33 to 2.05 s at 100K; commit p95 0.034 against 0.035 ms; 100K head 687 B packed (5.9 KB plain). The open that remains is the tail fold: the due rule lets the tail grow to `ratio` times the snapshot's rewrite, which is O(N) while every snapshot rewrites about 45% of index pages. The sim now checks after each commit that a log with no snapshot row, less its last row, holds at most `ratio` times the bytes a forced snapshot writes; the snapshot_ratio_ignored mutation fails that check in 60 of 60 seeds of --owners 200 --long 50. Checks: sim sweeps (200 seeds each: turns --twice, --twice --calm --row-limit 1024, --twice --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072, --owners 2000 --long 50, runtime --store log and kv; mutations content_collected_live, sections_kept, part_read_unloaded caught), clippy -D warnings, wasm32 check.

- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::finish_adversarial(true)` (opt-in, default off; off leaves every request byte-identical) adds `deadline::FinishChecks::adversarial` to the headless finish notice while less than half of the deadline has elapsed, gated like `finish_ambiguity` and `finish_held_out`, after the held-out bullet and before the persist bullet (2026-11-16). The bullet applies when the result transforms, filters, encodes or parses input in a format the task describes. It asks the model to list every feature of the format and each hostile or malformed form the statement implies, write one script that generates a dozen or more inputs covering them, and judge each output by a property that does not trust the program (unchanged bytes for an input that must stay as it is, idempotence or a round trip, agreement with an independent tool), then fix and rerun until all pass with the given example. Why: failed headless runs on such tasks stopped after one or two made inputs, though the finish notice already asks for one. It names no task, format or file. Tests: `finish_check_tests` in `crates/runtime/tool-host/src/deadline.rs`.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::finish_held_out(true)` (opt-in, default off; off leaves every request byte-identical) adds `deadline::FinishChecks::held_out` to the headless finish notice while less than half of the deadline has elapsed, gated like `finish_ambiguity` (2026-11-16). The bullet applies when the result is a program the task's checks run on inputs the agent has not seen and the task shows only one or a few example inputs. It says a shifted, padded, trimmed, re-encoded or noised copy of an example is not a new input, asks the model to list each constant taken from looking at the example (threshold, size, count, region, position, window, index, duration) with an allowed input that would break it, to build at least one such input with a known answer by recombining, cropping, resampling or stretching the example or generating one, and to replace each constant that breaks with a value measured from the input. Why: on Terminal-Bench 2.1 the Opus Nanocode arm's media failures pass on the shown example and fail held-out inputs; event logs show the agent validating only on re-encoded or shifted copies of the example and finishing with most of the time budget unused, and the earlier ambiguity bullet does not reach this case. The bullet names no task, domain or file. Like `finish_ambiguity` it turns `finish_check` on. Tests: `finish_check_tests` in `crates/runtime/tool-host/src/deadline.rs` (off leaves the plain, folded, fresh-attempt and persisting notices without the bullet; on adds it once, after the tail and before the persist bullet; no domain words). Not measured live: pass rate and cost per pass are the nanoeval arm's to measure.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::finish_margin(true)` (opt-in, default off; off leaves every notice byte-identical) adds `deadline::FinishChecks::margin` to the headless finish notice (2026-11-16). The bullet asks that a threshold the task states (accuracy, score, error, size or time) be cleared with a margin on data or inputs the result was not tuned on, across repeated runs, and that a detector, parser or rule fitted to one given example be run on a changed copy of it. Why: on Terminal-Bench 2.1 Sonnet rows, the failures Claude Code does not share are results that pass the agent's own check on the shown split or example and fail the held-out one (an accuracy just above its target on the given split, a detector tuned to the example input). The bullet carries no task-specific words. Like finish_ambiguity it turns finish_check on, and sits after the ambiguity bullet and before the score bullet. Checks: unit tests in deadline.rs (off is unchanged, on adds exactly one bullet before the score check). Not measured live: the nanoeval arm measures pass rate and cost per pass.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::finish_ambiguity(true)` (opt-in, default off; off leaves every request byte-identical) adds `deadline::FinishChecks::ambiguity` to the headless finish notice while less than half of the deadline has elapsed (`Reminders::first_passed` is false, or no deadline is set) (2026-11-16). The bullet asks the model to list each place where the task statement can be read two ways and settle it by the statement's literal wording and examples, quoting the deciding sentence. That wording beats a convention or cleanup the task does not ask for, and a value the task says to match or copy stays verbatim. If nothing decides it, the result holds under both readings where it can, or else follows the reading the examples support, tested by a run. A rule seen in a shown input follows the general wording. Why: on hard-v1 both remaining Nanocode Opus failures noticed an ambiguity, picked one reading, named it in the final message and stopped with more than 85% of the time budget unused. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, 14 of 36 failed Opus rows fit the shown input but fail a held-out one. One task fails in every arm (Claude Code too) because agents trim a value by domain convention where the statement says it must match the API response. The bullet carries no task-specific words. The lever turns `finish_check` on as `finish_retries` does, so it overrides `skip_finish_check` and the Opus default skip. `finish_check_min_requests` and the 90% reminder still gate the check. It sits after the stated-cases bullet of 1b62f5c8b and goes into the plain, the fresh-attempt (`finish_retries`, 066620494) and the folded notice alike. Size: the bullet adds 474 bytes to each notice (plain 2007 to 2481, brief 1894 to 2368, fresh-attempt 2442 to 2916, folded 2002 to 2476, persist 2282 to 2756), measured with `output/ambig-bytes`. Off, `output/ambig-ident` (15 notice variants over default, persist and stop_at_target, brief and not, plain, fresh-attempt and folded) prints sha256 0574f6207a1a98a5 on both d3137af0b and this change. Not measured live: pass rate, false success and cost per pass are the nanoeval arm's to measure. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode` native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-tool-host -- -D warnings`.
- perf(build): the build cache keeps bin and build-script units built into their own `build/<pkg>/<hash>/out` without `-C extra-filename` (cargo 1.100's build-dir layout), and publish writes `workspace/eager-packs`, every eager pack in one xz stream whose dictionary covers the whole stream, which prefetch downloads beside the eager list, index and helper and hands to the detached `fetch-pending` through a file it follows until a FIFO says the download ended (2026-11-16, build lane binonly3). Why: on rustc 1.100 the helper ran bins and build scripts uncached because it required `extra-filename`, so the mirror at 22954c06f published an eager list of 2 proc-macro packs and a fresh clone fetched the two 84 MB bins on demand (11.9-12.7 s); with them cached the eager list has 7 packs (74 MB gzip, 57 MB zstd), and in one xz stream they are 21.7 MB because nanocode-exec is matched against nanocode (xz -dc of the 178 MB takes 1.2 s on the hosted Hand). Measured at 22954c06f with a fresh `git fetch --depth 1` and XDG_CACHE_HOME, `cargo +stable build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli` (rustc 1.100.0) against release buildcache-exp-binonly3 on the Pyramid hosted Hand (4 CPUs, no zstd, load 0.2-2.4): 4.27, 4.20, 4.08, 4.18, 3.88, 3.93, 4.01, 4.04 s (the first two runs after an upload took 8.1 and 9.6 s); with the bins eager but fetched as separate gzip packs after the eager list 5.21, 6.79, 7.59 s, and with the stream read through a FIFO (xz blocked until the reader opened it) 4.34-5.22 s. The bins now arrive about 3.4 s after cargo starts: 1.7 s of it is the GitHub round trip for eager, index and helper, which the bundle download overlaps. On dev-georgios a fresh XDG build from a file:// pub restores everything in 2.7 s and publish takes 65 s (xz, single stream). Checked on the hosted Hand: offline (`unshare -rn`, `--offline`) a fresh clone compiles everything and the binary runs (265 s) and prefetch leaves no download process behind; a lazy build (4.5 s) then an edit of crates/core/sync rebuilds and runs (213 s) and the next build is a no-op (1.3 s). Without xz, or when the bundle is missing or stale, fetch-pending falls back to one download per pack. The mirror scripts need no change: `eager-packs` is uploaded with the packs, before index and eager, and the gzip release copies it as is.
- perf(turnlog): `Fold` keeps an exact key filter for each Cold index page. When `evict` drops a Loaded page, it stores the sorted 64-bit hashes of the page owners, keyed by the page row. `defer`, `unpaged` and `group_pages` skip a page whose filter does not hold the key, so `Lease::load_owners` of a new key no longer reads a whole index page (about 23 owners) and keeps its owners in memory. `paged` drops the filter of a page it loads, and the snapshot loads each Cold page that holds a Warm owner with unwritten changes (`Fold::unlisted`). The filters live only in memory and are rebuilt by eviction, so the hash (`DefaultHasher` with fixed keys) is never persisted and needs no stability across builds. Why: on d9ecdc776 the 10K split held 12.5 MB of fold owners, of which about 26K were Cold owners loaded only because a new key shared their page. Measured with output/scale-bench (10K children, `--rate 1000 --workers 4 --latency 50 --concurrency 64`, core 3, release), 3 interleaved runs per build on 241da4ca1 (2026-11-16): parent live memory 5629/5875/5480 to 4478/4451/4770 B per child (median 5.63 to 4.48 KB, -20%). Children per second 103.9/87.0/39.4 to 97.1/51.2/71.7, which follows the load of the shared Hand. memrows11 runs on 49c92022c gave 5.84 to 4.43 KB median (-24%) at 93 to 98 children per second. The sim adds `content_rewritten_stale` (rewrite of a cached content with a stale value, caught 200/200). The rewrite is off under `content_collected_live`, since a rewrite stores a collected live content again. Checks: nanocode-sim seeds 0..200 for turns `--twice`, `--snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072`, `--owners 2000 --long 50`, `--calm --row-limit 1024`, runtime log and kv, all 200/200. Mutations match master: content_collected_live 189/200, sections_kept 128/200, part_read_unloaded 0/200 (0 on master too). `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-turnlog -p nanocode-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clippy of nanocode-agent with `nanocode-code-mode/local-cells`, and `cargo +1.97.1 check --lib -p nanocode-turnlog --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` pass. Files: crates/core/turnlog/src/fold.rs, crates/core/turnlog/src/writer.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/src/turnlog.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/src/turns.rs.

- feat(claude): a headless root session on a Claude Opus model (`claude-opus-` model ID prefix) skips the finish check by default, and `ClaudeBuilder::finish_check(true)` runs it (2026-11-16). Every other model keeps the check by default. `finish_retries`, `late_finish_check` and `finish_check_min_requests` act only through the check, so a set `finish_retries` or an explicit `finish_check(true)` always runs it, also with `skip_finish_check(true)`. A set `late_finish_check` or `finish_check_min_requests` runs it on Opus unless `skip_finish_check(true)` is also set, as before. `skip_finish_check` stays, and on Opus it is now the default. Effort does not change the default. Why: with the check skipped, Claude Opus medium on the 18 Terminal-Bench 2.1 rescue tasks run three times passed 52 and failed 2, the same as with the check, at 0.705 times the cost per pass. A trap suite run three times (nanoeval run 9d88aaea) passed 74 of 75 in both arms, with 0 traps taken, 0 cheats and 0 false successes in each, at 0.70 times the cost. Sonnet, Haiku and the other Claude models were not in these runs, so their default is unchanged until they are measured. The Codex backend has its own finish check (`finish_check = root && deadline.is_some()` in `model/run`), and no Codex arm was in these runs, so it is unchanged. Check: `output/finish-default` (its own workspace with a path dependency on the claude backend) runs one headless turn per arm against a local Messages mock that answers every request with one final text message, and counts the requests. Before this change (origin/master 066620494) every headless arm made 2 requests. After it: Opus 5.5 and Opus 4.6 by default 1, Opus with `finish_check(true)`, `finish_retries(1)`, `skip_finish_check(true)` plus `finish_check(true)`, `late_finish_check(1s)` or `finish_check_min_requests(1)` 2, Opus with `skip_finish_check(true)` plus `late_finish_check(1s)` 1, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 by default 2, Sonnet with `skip_finish_check(true)` 1, with `skip_finish_check(true)` plus `finish_retries(1)` 2, and with `skip_finish_check(true)` plus `finish_check_min_requests(1)` 1. Sessions that are not headless made 1 request before and after. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` passes natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings` passes.
- perf(build): a fresh clone fetches only the build cache's index, its eager list and the helper, has the helper fetch the bin, proc-macro and build-script packs in the background, and restores every library unit as an empty placeholder that the helper fills in from its pack before any rustc that reads it runs; a placeholder whose pack cannot be fetched is compiled by the helper from the rustc command recorded beside it (2026-11-16, build lanes binonly and binonly2). Why: of the 97 packs (246 MB gzip) a cached build reads only 7 (56 MB: two 84 MB bins, two proc macros, three build scripts), and on the Pyramid hosted Hand (4 CPUs, no zstd, 0.7-1.0 s per GitHub request) the fetch-all prefetch and the release API listing were most of the 13.5-14.2 s fresh-clone `cargo +1.97.0 build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli`. Measured at 2aa018da4 with `git clone --no-hardlinks` and a fresh XDG_CACHE_HOME, interleaved: on the hosted Hand (load 0.2-1.3, first runs after a Hand restart cold) this change against release buildcache-exp-binonly2 took 19.9, 11.2, 5.56, 4.54, 4.67 s and the first binonly version against buildcache-exp-binonly 9.17, 10.8, 7.04, 8.62, 8.51 s; on dev-georgios (load 14-16) 0.61-0.73 s against 0.70-0.89 s and 1.40-1.60 s with the production `buildcache` release. Both fetch 177 MB unpacked and leave 178 placeholders. The pending packs are no longer FIFOs held by a prefetch subshell: the helper claims `remote/pending` once and fetches it in a detached `fetch-pending` process, and a unit waits on that pack's file lock, so the scripts are plain POSIX sh (run under dash and posh -n). Library placeholders a rustc needs are fetched in one `curl -Z` call; restored files are hard-linked from the unpacked unit; the rustc version is read through the rustup toolchain path so a hit skips the rustup proxy. Checked on the hosted Hand: with no network at all (`unshare -rn`) a fresh clone compiles everything and the binary runs (368 s); a lazy build followed by an offline edit of crates/core/sync compiles the 178 missing libraries from their recorded commands, marks `lazy.failed`, links and runs (337 s); an online edit of crates/core/sync after a lazy build rebuilds and runs (125 s) and the next build is a no-op (0.81 s); release `check`, `clippy`, dev `check` and release `test --no-run` after a lazy release build succeed and the release build afterwards links a binary that runs. Publish writes `workspace/index` (every unit without its .rlib/.rmeta), `workspace/eager` and a helper copy without its hash; the mirror must upload index and eager after the packs. Prefetch reads them by direct URL and falls back to the API listing and fetch-all when the release has no eager list. Not done: a whole-tree key that skips per-unit hashing; each hit still costs about 0.05-0.14 s in the helper, which is now the floor.
- feat(tool-host): the fresh-attempt finish notice of `ClaudeBuilder::finish_retries` asks for a run on an input the task did not show and on an input that must come out unchanged, and a failure of either starts the fresh attempt (2026-11-16). Why: of the 36 failed Opus rows on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 14 have output that fits the shown input but fails a held-out one, and 6 of 10 of those never ran a second input, so a trigger on the visible check alone does not fire for them. The report names the input of each failed check, and `deadline::fresh_attempt_brief` tells the fresh attempt to run the result again on those inputs. The plain finish notice and the retry mechanism are unchanged. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-tool-host -- -D warnings`.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::finish_retries(retries)` (opt-in, default none; unset leaves every request as before) lets a headless root turn start up to `retries` fresh attempts when its finish check fails (2026-11-16). Why: on Terminal-Bench 2.1 the remaining failures of the Opus medium arm are tasks that fail in some attempts and pass in others, and after a failed check the model keeps fixing in the same long conversation that produced the failure. What: while a retry is left, the finish notice is `deadline::fresh_finish_notice_with`: it asks the model to fix only gaps that do not change the result, and when the task's own check or a test of the result fails, to reply with one message that starts with `deadline::FRESH_ATTEMPT_MARK` and names each failed check (command and error), the approach and each changed file. When the next final message starts with that mark, `run_rounds` moves the pending messages to `Conversation::compacted` (as compaction does, so the dispatched tool calls stay in the record and none runs again), and the conversation restarts from the turn's own prompt with the git status of the working directory (native only, as on the first turn) and `deadline::fresh_attempt_brief` (the report). It emits the brief as a `ContextNotice`, clears the summary and `previous_message_id`, counts `Cursor::fresh_attempts` (durable, `#[serde(default)]`) and clears `finish_checked`, so the fresh attempt gets its own finish check. The turn keeps its model call index, deadline, usage and the caller's limits, so the retry spends the turn's budget and adds no limit of its own. Once no retry is left the finish notice is the usual one, and a mark in the final message ends the turn as before. The lever does not touch `fold_finish` or `late_finish_check`, and `skip_finish_check` and `finish_check_min_requests` turn it off with the check. A subagent was not used: a child turn has no finish check (the gate needs the root session), runs on its own conversation and budget, and the parent would wait on it with the failed context still loaded. Not measured live: the pass rate and cost per pass are the nanoeval arm's to measure. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (no new warnings), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-tool-host -- -D warnings`.
- build: `.agents/setup` and `.agents/warm` let Pyramid keep a golden repository disk of nanocode, so a new hosted Hand starts with `target/` built at master and its first `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli` recompiles only what its commit changed (2026-11-15). Why: a fresh clone on a hosted Hand fetches the shared build cache in 13.5-14.2 s, of which 8.9 s is the download; a built `target/` at the same path with nothing changed rebuilt in 0.31-0.34 s there (3 runs). Pyramid warms only the repositories an admin lists under Admin › Golden disks, and runs `.agents/setup` without secrets in the Hand image, then `.agents/warm` at the path Hands import at, so warm builds the release and dev shapes of nanocode-cli with the default toolchain agents use.
- fix(codex): a Codex turn whose model answers with no final message and no `exec` call even after the `<empty_response>` reprompt now ends with an empty final message and a `warn` trace, instead of failing with `MalformedResponse` "model completed without a final message or exec call" (2026-11-15, nanoeval harness-fix lane). Why: in nanoeval arm nanox (codex, gpt-6-luna high) 4 of about 150 rows failed with that error (1 in run c532e5c5, 3 in run 69f56b23). The loop in `ModelRun` (crates/backends/codex/src/model/run/turn.rs) already re-requests once with `empty_response` when a response has no tool call and no non-blank final message. That reprompt is the existing turn policy, and no new limit is added. When the second response is empty too, the turn now ends as upstream Codex ends a sampling round with no tool call and no assistant message: the turn completes and its last agent message is empty. Before, the whole turn failed and lost the work that `exec` calls had already done. Nothing is replayed: the run makes no new model request, and `exec` calls that already ran are not dispatched again. Reproduced with `output/empty-turn` (a Python mock of the Responses SSE stream and `/v1/models`, driving `nanocode exec --no-subagents -m gpt-6-luna --thinking high` through `NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL`). Each scenario is the item list of successive responses. On the debug CLI of fef11c541 (origin/master): `reasoning,reasoning` (only reasoning items) and `empty,empty` (reasoning and an empty `output_text`) exit 1 with this error after 2 requests. `exec,reasoning,reasoning` (an exec call, then empty responses) exits 1 after 3 requests with the exec run once. `reasoning,TEXT` exits 0 with TEXT. With this change, 2 rounds of each scenario and of `DONE-FIRST` exit 0 with the same request counts: one reprompt, and the exec dispatched once. The final message is empty, or TEXT where the mock sends it. bin/nanocode-sim gets no invariant: its scripted backend replaces the Codex `ModelRun`, and its wire model serves only `/v1/messages`, so it cannot reach this path. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex -- -D warnings`.
- fix(build): `scripts/buildcache-prefetch` fetches the gzip twin of the shared build cache (release `buildcache-gz`) when `zstd` is not installed (2026-11-15). Why: since fa00683e2 the packs are zstd and the helper unpacks them with the `zstd` command, so a machine without it (the Pyramid hosted Hand, stock macOS) missed every unit and compiled from scratch: a fresh clone on a 4-CPU hosted Hand took 2m48s three times out of three (580 s CPU). The mirror now publishes each pack in both releases (zstd 152 MB, gzip 246 MB; gzip unpacks all packs in 0.42 s against zstd's 0.12 s on dev-georgios), and the same fresh clone took 13.5, 14.2 and 14.0 s, of which 8.9 s is the download.
- fix(subagents): a moved subagent's resume note stays under 8 KiB, keeping the newest calls with each one's arguments clipped to 512 bytes (2026-11-15, Pyramid: slow subagents after deploys). Why: after c3cdc05f, Pyramid prd 0.5299.0's `subagent-recovery` steers (2026-11-15 22:29 UTC) still measured 35 to 67 KB, each listing 11 to 21 calls from the minutes before the deploy with up to 2 KiB of arguments each. Pyramid's child journal does not record sessions, so `capture_progress` returns before `settle_capture` once the journal holds the conversation and the list keeps every call of the turn while the restored history already holds their results. The note re-enters the subagent's context on every restart, so its size is paid on each later model call. What: `resume_message` drops the oldest calls (counted as omitted) until the note fits `RESUME_MESSAGE_BYTES` (8 KiB) instead of the 64 KiB message bound, and `RESUME_ARGUMENT_BYTES` is 512. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-subagents --all-targets -- -D warnings`, wasm32 check, `cargo test -p nanocode-subagents`, nanocode-sim agents and runtime seeds 0..300 300/300. Files: crates/runtime/subagents/src/durable.rs.
- feat(tool-host): the finish notice of a headless root session asks for the cases the task statement names, and for a final message that names what was checked (2026-11-16). `FINISH_HEAD` gains one bullet: each case the statement names holds on an input made for it (empty input, leading or trailing whitespace, letter case, each listed boundary or invalid form), with exact output bytes compared. The non-brief reply of `finish_notice_with` and of `folded_finish_notice_with` now asks the final message to name the checks that ran and the stated cases that were not tested, and says that a self-written test alone does not show that the result works. The brief reply is unchanged. Why: in nanoeval run 54ac2e99 (traps-v2 x3, all 225 rows read), claude-sonnet-5-5 medium on nanocode failed 5 rows against 1 for Claude Code on the same model. The finish check fired on all 75 nanocode rows and the model tested again after it, with 1 or 2 self-made inputs that left out cases the statement names: an empty dependency file printed a newline, a lower-case method passed the log-line filter, and a leading space passed the duration parser. In one latency-p95 row the answer before the check was hedged, and after the check and one 4-line self-test it said the result works. Exploration before the first write (2.6 against 2.1 tool calls) and the rate of works claims (8 against 9 rows for Opus on nanocode) do not explain the gap. Not measured: this ships only if a matched rerun of nano-son on the pinned SDK, the same arm on this revision, and Claude Code on Sonnet, on build-order, duration-parse and latency-p95 x5, shows a gain. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host`, `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check`.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::finish_check_min_requests(min)` (opt-in, default none; unset leaves every request as before) skips the separate finish notice of a headless root session when the turn has made fewer than `min` model requests by its first final message (the model call index plus one), so a short task ends at that message and a long one still gets the check (2026-11-15). Why: on a 21-task suite of short tasks run three times (63 rows), the finish check fired on all 63 and was the whole cost gap against the baseline harness: each costs 2 to 3 requests (the 1,663-character notice, a check cell and a second final message). On long tasks the check still catches late errors, which `skip_finish_check` gives up. What: the gate sits beside `skip_finish_check` after the steering hold, so a skipped check falls through to the end of the turn as `skip_finish_check` does and `finish_checked` stays false. It applies to both the default gates and `late_finish_check`, and composes with it; it does not touch the checklist `fold_finish` puts in the prompt. Not measured live: the requests and pass rate per threshold are the nanoeval arm's to measure. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (no new warnings), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`.
- fix(djs): a minor collection scans the saved frame of an old Generator only over its clean cards, so no old slot is remembered twice (2026-11-15, stall100k lane gcbarrier1). Why: since 0ac987673 (D3200) `Marker::mark_cards` scanned the saved frame of each old Generator whole with `scan_old` and then walked the dirty cards with `scan_range`, so a frame slot in a dirty card entered the remembered list twice and the update pass forwarded it twice. The second forward rewrote the low 32 bits of a reference that had already moved, which corrupted async Code Mode cells: `output/cm10k` (one cell, 103 batches of `await Promise.all` over 100 `tools.t` calls) reported done 15,900-17,500 instead of 10,300, because its loop variable became 3.56e-322 (bits 72) at i=7200 and the loop restarted. The 100K benchmark log generation stalled at 10,100 children for the same reason. The first hypothesis (an unbarriered stack segment in `suspend.rs`) was wrong: a debug check that every young target of an old slot is marked after `mark_cards` passed, and a debug check for duplicate remembered entries failed at once (slot 0x52080, old 344408, 108 remembered). Now the Generator loop scans each run of clean cards of the frame with `scan_range`, and the dirty-card walk covers the rest. A debug-assertions build panics when the remembered list holds a slot twice. Checks: `cm10k` with debug assertions at 10300/100, 20000/100, 5000/50, 10000/250, 3000/1 and 30000/500 reports exactly that many calls (it reported 17,500 at 10300/100). The change scans fewer slots than before and only for Generator frames, so the D3200 instruction counts (map.js, filter.js) do not change. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

- perf(build): a fresh clone takes a prebuilt buildcache helper from the release, and the djs-core build script cuts each top-level const from one stripped copy of its file (2026-11-15, build lane cache1s). Why: a fresh-clone `cargo build --release --locked -p nanocode-cli` at 49c92022 with an empty XDG_CACHE_HOME, interleaved on dev-georgios (16 cores, load 23-24), took 5.07, 3.32 and 3.01 s on master and 2.84, 1.33 and 1.48 s with this change; a warm rebuild in a new target dir took 1.07, 0.94 and 0.93 s on master and 0.57, 0.51 and 0.59 s with it. Master's profile: compiling the helper 1.28 s, the release download 0.5 s, and the djs-core build script 0.49 s on the critical path of every build in a new target, because `Cut::TopConsts` stripped the whole rest of the file again for every const (0.37 s at opt-level 0 before, 0.035 s after, outputs byte-identical). What: `buildcache publish` also writes `workspace/helper-<cksum>-<uname -sm>-<sha256>` (its own binary); on a cold cache the wrapper prefetches the release first, checks a matching helper's sha256 and that it runs, and uses it instead of compiling; without one (offline, an older release, another platform) it compiles as before, and an offline prefetch records `remote.failed` so the helper does not fetch again in that build. `compat_inputs::strip_marked` records where each source line starts in the stripped text so `TopConsts` reuses it, and strips the suffix as before when a const line starts inside a comment or literal.
- perf(build): the release profile builds the 54 crates that dist builds at `opt-level = "s"` at `opt-level = "s"` too, so a release build optimizes those run-once crates as the shipped binary does (2026-11-15, build lane sched). Why: on dev-georgios pinned to 8 cores (`taskset -c 8-15`, `-j8`, load 17 to 22 from other lanes, so the 16-core runs were not possible), `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` and a fresh target dir, `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --timings`, 3 interleaved rounds: master 92.8, 94.2, 89.7 s (user CPU 708, 720, 688 s) against 80.4, 79.7, 78.7 s (612, 602, 598 s), -13.7% wall and -14% CPU; psh-utils 52.5 to 45.0 s, nanocode-backend-codex 31.1 to 24.7 s, nanocode-cli 22.0 to 16.0 s. The build is CPU bound (summed unit time 7 times the wall), so cutting LLVM work shortens it; the critical path's tail moves from nanocode-backend-codex-client -> nanocode-backend-codex -> nanocode-cli to nanocode-backend-claude-tools -> nanocode-backend-claude. Measured and not taken: `codegen-units = 4` for 15 off-path crates (subagents, codex-client, mpp, tui, durability and the rest) 92.6, 115.0, 91.8 s, no gain. What: `[profile.release.package.<name>] opt-level = "s"` for each crate in dist's list; the crates dist keeps at 3 for their per-token and per-cell loops (djs, psh-engine, HTTP, TLS, sync, executor, compression, nanocode-backend-codex-client) stay at 3 in release.
- feat(codex): `--time-limit SECONDS` (env `NANOCODE_TIME_LIMIT`) adds `Time left: N seconds` to each `exec_command`, `write_stdin` and job result, counted from the start of the run (2026-11-15, cf-cost router time-out lane). Off by default: no line is added and the results are byte-identical to Codex CLI's, which reports no time budget. Why: in cf-cost run ncc-ds-router-1 and ncc-ds-decisive-1 (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Workers AI, codex harness, variant leanstack, 900 s agent limit), 3 of 4 scored gcode-to-text attempts hit AgentTimeoutError with no /app/out.txt written (verifier: test_hello_file_exists failed), after 49 to 62 model calls (about 480 s of model time and 420 s of tool time, five render scripts of 38 to 99 s each). Stock Codex CLI on the same model (cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0316) wrote an answer in every attempt, in 6.4 to 8.5 min (1 of 3 passed). The nanocode attempts kept exploring with no signal of the remaining budget and lost the chance of a scored answer. The adaptive-rejection-sampler time-out of the same run is not this cause: its fourth model call waited 571 s while the proxy retried three upstream ServerDisconnectedError responses (an infrastructure stall). The pass-rate effect is measured by cf-cost run ncc-ds-timelimit-1 (leanstack against leanstack plus `--time-limit 870`, 3 attempts of each task an arm). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-process-contracts -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-backend-codex`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-process-contracts -p nanocode-backend-codex --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps` on those crates and nanocode-cli with `-D warnings`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` (on 668272b05 plus this change, binary nanocode-bfa263cc4).
- perf(build): a fresh clone fetches the build cache from the `buildcache` release by default, and published packs are zstd-compressed (2026-11-15, build lane cachedefault). Why: a cold `cargo build --release --locked -j8 -p nanocode-cli` of ee5e0b0a6 on cores 8-15 of dev-georgios took 83 and 101 s on master; with no environment and a release published for that commit it took 4.78, 4.73 and 4.69 s (836 MB of uncompressed packs, all 96 hits), and from a release of the same packs compressed with zstd (159 MB) 6.80 and 3.90 s. A release published for another commit only hits the units that did not change (37-44 s at ee5e0b0a6 and b361805ad while the release was being republished); a first run of 149 s was not reproduced by later fresh runs. With the release unreachable (`NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_RELEASE=http://127.0.0.1:1/x`), with `NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_URL=off`, without curl, and without zstd and gzip, the build compiled everything and succeeded in 86-92 s with no buildcache errors. What: when `NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_URL` is unset and the local cache is empty, the first rustc invocation of a build runs `scripts/buildcache-prefetch` under an exclusive lock on `nanocode/remote.lock` (the others wait on it, so the release downloads once) and every invocation then reads the packs from `nanocode/remote` as `file://` URLs; a failed prefetch is recorded in `nanocode/remote.failed` under cargo's PID so the rest of that build compiles without retrying. `NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_URL=off` turns the remote tier off, any other value still names the remote, and `NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_RELEASE` picks another release. `scripts/buildcache` waits for the helper to build on a cold cache so the first build already uses it. `publish` writes each pack through `zstd -9 --long=27` (gzip, then raw when neither exists), and fetch reads raw, zstd and gzip packs by their magic bytes, so the old uncompressed release keeps working; a missing decompressor makes the fetch miss and the unit compile.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::late_finish_check(min_left)` and `ClaudeBuilder::yield_share(percent)` (both opt-in, default none; unset leaves every request and tool call as before; nanocode structural cost lane, 2026-11-15). `late_finish_check` lets the separate finish check run whenever the deadline leaves at least `min_left`, even after the gates that normally skip it: the last time-limit reminder (90% of the limit) has passed, or `fold_finish` is on and the first reminder (50%) has passed. It does nothing without a deadline, and it never overrides `skip_finish_check`, which pulls the other way; hosts should not set both. `yield_share` caps the `yield_time_ms` of each Code Mode `exec` and `wait` call (argument or pragma) at `percent` of the time left before the deadline, with a notice saying so. The cell keeps running, so the model gets its turn back with time to act. It does nothing without a deadline, and the existing cap at the deadline itself still applies. Why: in nanoeval run db0df005 (Terminal-Bench 2.1, Opus 5.5 medium with fold_finish), query-optimize attempt a00139 ran the original 9 min 46 s query to get a reference checksum. It blocked in one `wait` with yield 600,000 ms for 463 s, then wrote one rewrite: 1.23 s against the golden 0.89 s, where the test allows 1.05x. It stopped at 608 of 900 s with no finish check, because fold_finish skips the separate check once the 50% reminder has passed. With `yield_share` 33 that wait would have returned after about 257 s, with 515 s left. With `late_finish_check` 120 s, the check would have run with 292 s left. Each lever reaches one loss in the ledger of 53, so the pass-rate gain is small. Its measurement is the nanoeval before/after on query-optimize x5 and the targeted set. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and wasm32 (no new warnings), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps` on the same crates with `-D warnings`.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::skip_finish_check` (opt-in, default false; off leaves every request unchanged) stops a headless root session from adding the finish notice (`deadline::finish_notice`, or `persisting_finish_notice`) after its first `end_turn`, so the first final message ends the turn (2026-11-15). Why: in nanoeval run b7d70ffb (Terminal-Bench 2.1, claude-opus-5-5 high, 267 attempts an arm) about 40 short tasks cost nanocode 2 to 3 more requests and 2 to 3 times the output of Claude Code. Most of the gap is the finish check, which arrives in every nanocode attempt that ends before the last deadline reminder as a user message of about 1,430 characters after the first final message. The agent then runs a check cell and writes its final message a second time. Claude Code gets neither. fix-code-vulnerability #1: nanocode made 7 requests ($0.092, 1,995 output tokens) and Claude Code 3 ($0.054, 643). Nanocode's steps after its first final message (1,071 chars) were the notice, a check cell of 904 output tokens and a second final message of 1,307 chars, about $0.035 of the $0.038 gap. `fold_finish` does not cover this case: it skips the separate notice only once the first deadline reminder has passed (`Reminders::first_passed`), so a short task still gets it. Measured with a mock Messages transport (a scripted model: explore cell, edit-and-test cell, final message; then a check cell and a final message again if a finish notice arrives) through `Claude::builder(..).headless(true)` with a 900 s deadline at 5% elapsed. Default, `brief_finish`, `fold_finish` and `fold_finish`+`brief_finish`+`brief_final` each made 5 requests (32.0k to 41.0k request-body chars in all). `skip_finish_check` made 3 (16.2k chars), and `fold_finish`+`skip_finish_check` made 3 (21.2k chars) with the checklist still in the first prompt. Pairing it with `fold_finish` keeps the checklist that the finish check introduced to fix wrong output paths, stale /tmp files and unverified claims. The effect on pass rate is the nanoeval arm's to measure. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::result_effort(effort)` (opt-in, default none; unset leaves every request byte for byte as before) sends `effort` instead of the configured effort on a request whose new input is only results of `exec`/`wait` calls that completed or yielded without error (2026-11-15). Why: in nanoeval run b7d70ffb (Terminal-Bench 2.1, Opus 5.5 high, 89 tasks x3) nanocode wrote 1.5 to 4 times Claude Code's output tokens on matched attempts with the same or fewer requests: model-extraction-relu-logits #1 18,650 vs 4,583, largest-eigenval #1 22,461 vs 14,976 and #2 26,080 vs 14,434, gpt2-codegolf #2 17,936 vs 10,868, write-compressor #2 13,049 vs 6,136, torch-pipeline-parallelism #2 13,094 vs 7,305, path-tracing-reverse #1 18,262 vs 4,018, make-mips-interpreter #1 32,095 vs 7,917. The thinking configuration is the same as Claude Code's for claude-opus-5-5 (`thinking.type` adaptive, no budget, `max_tokens` 128000, `output_config.effort` high; nanocode asks for `display: summarized` where Claude Code asks for `omitted`, which changes what is shown, not what is billed), so the output is the model's own thinking at high effort: one adaptive-rejection-sampler request wrote 45,455 output tokens for a 62,412-character cell, about 16k to 20k tokens of code, so 55 to 65% of it was thinking. In run 7dbf47d1 the same harness at medium effort wrote 2.4k to 6.3k output tokens per largest-eigenval attempt against 4.3k to 21k at high. Most requests after the first read a cell's result, so `result_effort(Medium)` keeps high effort for the task prompt, a failed cell, an error result, a steer and the finish check, and thinks at medium while the work goes as planned. What: it uses the per-message effort messages of `low_effort_rounds` (the top-level effort stays pinned, so the prompt cache is not restarted), and when both are on an unchanged yield still gets the lowest effort. A round is a result round when the messages after the last assistant message are one user message (plus effort messages and time notices) whose blocks are all `tool_result`s of `exec`/`wait` calls with no `is_error` and text starting with `Script completed` or `Script running with cell ID` (`code_mode_spec::COMPLETED_STATUS`, now a constant code_mode/mod.rs formats with). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-code-mode`, native and wasm32, and clippy on both crates (no new warnings). Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, agent/assemble.rs, agent/rounds.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs, spec.rs.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::stop_at_target` (opt-in, default false; off leaves every request and notice byte for byte as before) tells a headless root session that a task's self-checkable target is the finish line (2026-11-15). With it, three texts change: (1) `nanocode_tool_host::deadline::STOP_AT_TARGET`, a system-reminder pushed after each turn's prompt beside `brief_final` and `lean_cells`: once the result meets a target the task states and the session can check (a score, win rate, accuracy, speed or size on given inputs or against given opponents) with a margin across repeated runs of the task's own check, put it in place, run the check once more and finish; compare many variants from one script or loop rather than one written-out call per variant; (2) the finish checklist's score line (`SCORE_CHECK`, "compared with at least one structurally different approach ... Beating the given baseline is not by itself the goal") becomes `TARGET_CHECK`, which keeps that comparison only for a goal measured against something the session cannot see, such as a hidden reference time, and says meeting a checkable target is done; (3) the 50/75% deadline reminder's "use the time that remains to improve and test it" becomes `EARLY_TARGET_REMINDER` (finish now if every stated target is already met with a margin; `Reminders::stopping_at_target`). `FinishChecks { persist, stop_at_target }` builds the checklist for `finish_notice_with` and `folded_finish_notice_with`; `finish_notice`, `persisting_finish_notice` and the folded pair keep their signatures and text, so Codex is unchanged. Why: winning-avg-corewars (build a Redcode warrior that reaches a stated win share against fixed opponents, checked by a simulator the task ships) is the largest single cost gap in nanoeval run b7d70ffb: nano $5.327 (93 requests, 6.53M cache read, 1,987 s), $5.751 (102 requests, 7.66M) and $1.858 (38) against Claude Code's $1.208 (24), $2.290 (39) and $1.442 (23), about $8.0 of nano's excess over the run, and every arm passed. The same shape recurs in 7dbf47d1 (nano high 1.38/4.05/1.80, other nano arms up to $6.32 in 116 requests, cc 1.21/0.90/2.49) and db0df005 (3.47 in 61 requests vs 0.84). In both long b7d70ffb attempts the context reached ~165k tokens and compacted, then 38 and 42 more requests re-explored from a ~20k summary while cc never compacted (max input 59.7k and 112k); before compaction nano grew ~2.8k tokens a request over 55-60 requests (cc ~1.8k), with three cells of 72k, 114k and 103k characters of arguments that wrote out 64-100 battle runs call by call. From ~1,290 s every step carried the 393-character 50% reminder ("use the time that remains to improve and test it") then the 53-character time-left line. So the extra rounds come after the target was reachable, and the default texts, the score line in the finish checklist and the early reminder, ask for more improvement with no stop condition; nothing in the headless prompts says that meeting the task's own check ends the task. Default texts are unchanged: the old checklist equals `FINISH_HEAD + SCORE_CHECK + FINISH_TAIL` byte for byte, and `EARLY_REMINDER` and `PERSIST_CHECK` are untouched (compared from the source constants). Not measured live: the effect on requests and pass rate is a matched nanoeval rerun on corewars and the other tasks with checkable or hidden-reference targets. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-codex`, the first two with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/runtime/tool-host/src/deadline.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent/assemble.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent/rounds.rs.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::yield_floor` (opt-in, unset by default; unset leaves every request and every tool input unchanged) raises the yield of each `exec` and `wait` call to at least the floor before the call runs, so a cell running a long command returns when the command ends or the floor passes instead of after the model's or the protocol's shorter yield (2026-11-15, Nanocode cost-per-pass lane). Why: on Terminal-Bench 2.1 nanoeval run b7d70ffb (nano claude-opus-5-5 high against Claude Code 2.1.318 on the same model) nano makes more requests on tasks with long builds, installs and training runs: sam-cell-seg attempt 2 37 against 10 ($1.72 against $0.58), install-windows-3.11 attempt 1 59 against 36, crack-7z-hash attempt 2 51 against 21, reshard-c4-data attempt 3 29 against 10, mailman 24 to 33 against 15 to 22, build-pov-ray 23 against 14 to 15. In sam-cell-seg attempt 2, 9 of the 37 requests write exactly 77 output tokens after a 50 to 200 s gap and carry 38 to 39 characters of tool arguments: a `wait` on a running cell that returned at its yield with the command still running. Claude Code's Bash blocks for up to 120 s by default (600 s at most), so the same command costs it one request. A Claude session's `exec` with no `yield_time_ms` yields after 10 s plus the 1 s observer grace (`spec::DEFAULT_YIELD`) unless the host sets `cell_yield`, and `cell_yield` only replaces the default: a model that names a short yield on `wait` or in an `exec` pragma still polls. Each such round re-reads the whole context and writes its result: about $0.02 at 40 to 80k tokens of context, and the wave-9 decomposition of runs 784946b4 and b7d70ffb puts wait rounds at 1.27 to 1.29 per attempt suite-wide. What: `yield_floor_handler` wraps the `exec` and `wait` handlers outside the deadline handler, so the floor is applied first and the deadline cap still shortens it near the time limit. `deadline::floor` raises a `wait`'s `yield_time_ms` (absent, null or lower) to the floor unless it terminates; for `exec` it raises a lower `yield_time_ms` argument, raises a lower `yield_time_ms` in the `// @exec:` pragma, and otherwise adds the yield with `code_mode::source_yielding`, which leaves an empty source and a JSON-wrapped one alone. A call whose yield is already at or above the floor runs unchanged, and a cell that finishes or is preempted by steering returns as before. The model's own call in the transcript is not rewritten, so the prompt cache is unaffected. Checked: cargo check of nanocode-backend-claude natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, clippy with no warning in the crate. Not yet measured on a rerun: the expected effect is fewer requests on tasks whose commands run past 10 s, at the cost of seeing a long command's progress later.
- fix(subagents): a moved subagent's resume note stops listing the calls an earlier resume note already listed once a checkpoint commits after it (2026-11-15, Pyramid: slow subagents after deploys). Why: a call restored from the journal (`CallState::Restored`) left `in_flight_calls` only when the subagent's turn ended, because `settle_capture` dropped only `Live` calls a commit covered. A subagent whose turn spans several handoffs therefore listed every call from every earlier interrupted stretch again on each restart, up to the 64 KiB message bound: in Pyramid prd turn 5570a341 (2026-11-15) the `subagent-recovery` steers after a deploy were 51 to 56 KB with 15 or more calls, most of them listed by earlier resume notes too, after bfdb2636b had already dropped the task from the note. A commit that covers live calls of the resumed turn comes after that turn's resume note, so the committed history already holds the earlier listing. What: when `settle_capture` applies a commit, `in_flight_calls` keeps only live calls the commit does not cover, and `in_flight_omitted` is capped at the live omitted count (`settled`, `committable` and `nested`). Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-subagents -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-subagents --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, nanocode-sim `--scenario agents` and `--scenario runtime` seeds 0..300 300/300. Files: crates/runtime/subagents/src/runtime.rs.
- feat(finish): `ClaudeBuilder::persist_finish` and `CodexBuilder::persist_finish` (opt-in, default false; off leaves every finish notice byte for byte as before) add one line to the finish check's checklist, in both the separate finish notice and the folded one (`deadline::persisting_finish_notice`, `deadline::persisting_folded_finish_notice`): every requirement and target the task states is met and checked by running the result, and one that is not met, or that the final message would report as unmet or unverified, is not done, so while time remains the agent keeps working on it with a different approach instead of reporting the gap (2026-11-15, Nanocode structural cost lane, loss ledger). Why: nanoeval's loss ledger over 11 Terminal-Bench 2.1 runs lists 53 attempts where nanocode failed and the reference agent (Claude Code or Codex CLI) passed the same task and attempt. In the verifier output and final steps of the 10 most-lost tasks and the 7 losses of run db0df005 (nano-st, Opus 5.5 medium), the most common shape is a final message that names the gap and stops with time left. circuit-fibsqrt on Codex (5 losses; a00009 stopped after 215 s saying the gate-only requirement remained unmet, then repeated that message after the finish check). path-tracing on Codex (4 losses; a00003 after 381 s: 'I can't claim it reaches 0.99 similarity'). schemelike-metacircular-eval (a00155: reported that 09-mutual-recursion fails with eval.scm inside itself, and the verifier failed 2 of 63). sparql-university (a00335: query saved but never run, and it returned an empty set). chess-best-move (a00195: one move from reading the board by hand after the chess library would not install; the task wanted both mating moves). crack-7z-hash (a00211, 2026-11-14: gave up and wrote no solution file). The existing checklist ends with 'Fix what falls short', which these finishes read as satisfied by reporting the shortfall. Not in scope: video-processing (12 losses), whose cause is the frame chosen as takeoff, and raman-fitting, where the 2D offset that passes depends on the fit window (Claude Code's own attempt measured 130 to 1,240 across windows; the test allows 1,115 to 1,363). The effect on pass rate, time-outs and cost is the nanoeval arm's to measure: the line can lengthen sessions that would have ended with an honest gap. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps` on the same crates with `-D warnings`.
- fix(codex): a custom model on a Chat Completions gateway takes reasoning effort `none` (2026-11-15, Nanocode 10x cost lane). `transport/chat.rs` `effort` took only low, medium and high for every model but Kimi, so a session of `@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` on the Workers AI gateway with thinking none failed each request with `unsupported reasoning effort for the selected model`, although `Model::supports_thinking` offers none for `Model::Custom` and Workers AI takes `reasoning_effort: "none"` (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash answered the same question with 2 output tokens instead of 176). A custom model now sends none as `reasoning_effort`; catalog models are unchanged. DeepSeek's output, mostly reasoning, was about 60% of the spend of a DeepSeek-first run. Checked with `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client`, native and wasm32, and clippy on that crate (no new warnings).
- An embedder can read a recovered operation's continuation from the durable store, without an acquired owner, and hand it to the agent that runs the operation (2026-11-15). `SessionStore::continuation_ahead(session, operation)` (the head's first pending operation when `None`) reads the operation's stored continuation and hydrates it through the family's new `CheckpointFormat::hydrate_cursor` (Claude's paged cursor; other families read none ahead), returning a `ContinuationAhead` with the stored payload's content key; it takes no claim and writes nothing. `Agent::prefetch_request_ahead(id, ahead)` reaches `ClaudeExecutionPolicy::prefetch_continuation_ahead`, which, holding the `Sequencer` the run's own `continuation` read holds, peeks the owner's continuation and keeps the read ahead in the hydrated slot only under that key: a continuation that changed since has another key and is read through the owner again (`Prefetched::Read`), so nothing stale is ever kept, and the run's `continuation` checks the key once more as before. When the session hasn't acquired its owner yet, the read ahead waits on the lazy execution and seeds the acquired execution's slot under its key (`Prefetched::Seeded`). Pyramid read a handed-off pass's cursor through the owner only once the session opened, read after read on the session's one-at-a-time driver behind a drain's other writes, and the root's first model request waited on it (prd, 2026-11-15: `agent.continuation` hydrated ahead, the read 62-75 ms at p50 and 430-450 ms at p95, up to 823 ms); it now reads it from the store as soon as the handoff commits, before the claim. Admission, claims and attempts are unchanged. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-agent-core -p nanocode-durability -p nanocode-backend-claude` passed. Files: `crates/core/agent/src/agent/{backend,handle,owned}.rs`, `crates/runtime/durability/src/{catalog,format,lib}.rs`, `crates/backends/claude/src/{agent,execution}.rs`, `crates/backends/claude/src/durability/{mod,format}.rs`.
- perf(build): the build cache can be fetched from a GitHub release, and cache keys no longer depend on the host's cargo configuration (2026-11-15, build critical-path lane sharedcache). Why: d9ecdc776's remote tier hit on the machine that published the cache but missed every unit on another machine, because the key hashed every `CARGO_*` variable: a hosted Hand's `CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO` and cargo's own `CARGO` path (under each home's rustup, which no root remaps) changed every key. A fresh clone on a 5-core hosted Hand built `cargo build --release --locked -p nanocode-cli` in 178-205 s before; with the keys fixed and units fetched one by one from the release it took 32.8-36.0 s (each fetch pays a redirect and two TLS handshakes, about 1 s, one dependency level at a time); with `scripts/buildcache-prefetch` first it took 4.8 s to download all 96 units (797 MB, in parallel) and 6.2 s to build. What: `NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_URL` may be a template with `{dir}` and `{key}`, for stores whose names can't hold a `/`, such as release assets named `<dir>-<key>`; the key leaves out `CARGO_HTTP_*`, `CARGO_NET_*`, `CARGO_TERM_*`, `CARGO_REGISTRIES_*`, `CARGO_REGISTRY_*`, `CARGO_CACHE_*`, `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` and `CARGO_LOG`, and hashes `CARGO` by name only; `scripts/buildcache-prefetch` downloads every asset of the `buildcache` release (or `$NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_RELEASE`) in parallel and prints the `file://` template to use: `NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_URL=$(scripts/buildcache-prefetch) cargo build --release -p nanocode-cli`. A mirror publishes the release after each master commit.
- perf(mpp): `ForwardProxy::spawn` starts the `mpp-forward-proxy` thread at the proxy's first connection instead of at once (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: anonymous memory, structural lane). When the caller runs inside an executor runtime, a task on that runtime accepts the first connection, then hands the listener and that stream (`into_std`) to the thread, which registers both with its own current-thread runtime and serves the first stream before it accepts more. Outside a runtime the thread starts at once, as before. The certificate authority, the bundle file, the runtime and the HTTP client are still made in `spawn`, so their errors still return from it, and a registration error on the thread is a `nanocode_trace::warn!`. Why: the paying proxy starts at the first shell command (`prepare_commands`), and a tool turn whose commands never use the network kept the thread's stack (about 12 KB touched) and its own allocator heap and segment header for the whole turn. At the direct tool-turn peak the thread count falls from 6 to 5 (main, nanocode-blocking, psh-engine, psh-wait, psh-ready) and the allocator segments from 6 to 4.5 (median of 3 samples). Checked: a tool turn that runs `curl --noproxy '' -x $HTTPS_PROXY http://127.0.0.1:9/` gets the proxy's 502 in 10 of 10 commands on both binaries. Measured on master 9658852ce against a base build of the same commit (`scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` with BOLT, `~/sw/pin/measure.sh <bindir> 10 tools`, 4 interleaved passes, n=10 each): direct tool-turn own Anonymous at the peak per pass 1.037, 1.055, 1.062, 1.021 MiB (median 1.046) against 0.973, 1.023, 0.963, 1.020 (median 0.998, about -49 KB); Code Mode tool turn 2.656, 2.719, 2.703, 2.715 (median 2.709) against 2.686, 2.688, 2.686, 2.682 (median 2.686); direct ru_maxrss 5.449 MiB in every px run.
- An embedder can read a recovered operation's continuation ahead of its admission (2026-11-15). `Agent::prefetch_request(id)` reaches `ClaudeExecutionPolicy::prefetch_continuation`, which reads the operation's stored continuation through `DurableOwner::peek_continuation` (the driver's `Continuation` command without a claim or a running attempt: it only reads) and hydrates its paged cursor into the slot `continuation` already keeps by key, now marked as read ahead; both hold one `Sequencer`, so the run's own read waits for a read ahead in flight rather than reading again, and a cursor read ahead is kept for the run's second read (its prompt's admission reads it in `freeze_admitted`, then `cursor` does) as one read there would be. A changed continuation has another key and is read again. On a handed-off Pyramid turn the claimer's first prompt hydrated the cursor between `policy.admit` and the first model request, a chain of sequential `LoadPayloads` driver commands each waiting on Pyramid's one-at-a-time store behind the drain's other writes: `turn.root_request` 160-490 ms with nothing else under it, `agent.turn` starting at its end and `chat` 6-15 ms later (prd, 2026-11-15 10:30-11:00 PST, 40 claims). The driver also times, in its queue, the commands a prompt's admission waits on (`admit`, `begin_attempt`, `continuation`, `peek_continuation`): a `durability.command` span (target `nanocode`, `queue.ms`) and the `histogram.nc.durability.admission_queue_micros` metric event; `agent.admit`, `agent.begin_attempt`, `agent.continuation` (`hydrated` = read, kept or ahead) and `agent.prefetch_continuation` spans show the rest. Checked with `cargo check --locked --lib` natively and for wasm32 and clippy on the three crates. Files: `crates/runtime/durability/src/session.rs`, `crates/backends/claude/src/{agent,execution}.rs`, `crates/backends/claude/src/durability/mod.rs`, `crates/core/agent/src/agent/{backend,handle,owned}.rs`.
- An embedder can restore a session's exec cell journals after its runtime opens (2026-11-15). `CellJournals::expect_restore(session)` returns a `PendingRestore`; until its `restore` lands the journals or it drops, every Code Mode `adopt` of that session (each `exec`, `wait` and recovered call) and a terminate's discard wait for it, so no cell starts, recovers or is discarded before the session's journals are back, and none takes a restored cell's ID. A handed-off Pyramid turn read and parsed its root's journals (2.5 MB on average, 4.5 MB in the slowest) before its first model request, which waited 344 ms at p95 and 780 ms at p99 over 6 hours of prd (2026-11-15), though that request needs none of them; the first `exec` or `wait` now waits instead. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, passed.
