- An embedder can defer restoring a root's subagent journal until something needs it (2026-11-15). `SubagentControl::set_deferred_restore(true)` makes `adopt_journal` register the root's restoration gate (Loading) without spawning the restore; it starts on `SubagentControl::start_restore(root)` or on the first `await_restored` for that root, which every subagent tool (`list_agents`, `wait_agent`, `spawn_agent`'s admission and the rest), `deferred_resume`, `resume_restored` and `discard_restored` reach, so nothing that reads subagents runs before they are restored and nothing waits on a restore nobody started. Pyramid's turns run every durable operation of a root, its journal and its subagents' sessions through one store whose operations run one at a time (`StagedStore` has no pipeline handle), and a handed-off turn that moved 3 to 8 subagents restored them at the session's open, beside its first prompt: the root's admission queued behind the journal's reads and its first model request went out when the restore ended (prd, 2026-11-15 09:47-09:51 PST, 105 handoffs: decode to `agent.turn` p95 636 ms, `agent.turn` starting within 25 ms of the restore's end in the slowest). Pyramid now starts the restore once the root's first prompt is admitted. Default off: nothing changes unless an embedder asks. Not built on this Hand; Pyramid's CI builds it (tempoxyz/pyramid). Files: `crates/runtime/subagents/src/runtime.rs`.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::tool_result_tokens(limit)` (opt-in, default none; without it `exec` and `wait` results keep the 12,000-token bound) bounds the text of each Code Mode `exec` and `wait` result put into history at `limit` tokens, with the same middle cut and `…N tokens truncated…` marker as the default bound. Direct tools and `Read` are unchanged, and so is the `exec` description, which still states the default bound (2026-11-15, Nanocode structural cost lane). Why: the nanoeval run 7dbf47d1 records (30 tasks x3, 90 matched attempts an arm, read with an extractor over each attempt's model-requests.jsonl and trajectory.json) put the Opus 5.5 medium arm at 34.5 tool observations an attempt, 80,504 characters, quantiles p50 454, p90 8,147, p99 17,335 and max 48,029 characters. Each observation is written once and then read on every later request, so the characters above a cap cost (chars/3.5) x ($6.25 + $0.50 x later requests) per million at a 6.25 write and 0.50 read (Opus 5.5's rates in `nanocode_agent_types::pricing` are 5 and 0.20, which lowers each figure by about a third): $0.093 an attempt above 8,000 characters (about 2,000 tokens), $0.013 above 16,000 and $0.002 above 32,000, against $0.761 an attempt at the same rates (12%, 1.7% and 0.3%). The same records rule out the prompt-cache levers: 5-minute writes of 28.9k tokens an attempt are almost all new context, the first request writes 508 tokens (the tools and system prefix is already read across attempts), the last writes 1,304, misses after a gap over 5 minutes are 0 and prefix misses 958 tokens ($0.006 an attempt), where Claude Code's arm loses $0.056 an attempt to 0.43 cache expiries. The pass-rate cost of losing the middle of long outputs is the nanoeval arm's to measure. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::tool_result_clearing(keep, at_least_tokens)` (opt-in, default none; without it history clearing keeps Claude Code's 12 results and 20,000-token batch) replaces the two values of `clearing::clear_tool_results`: the most recent `keep` clearable results stay whole, and older ones become the cleared stub once at least `at_least_tokens` of them are pending. Both values are caller policy (2026-11-16, Nanocode input-token lane). Why: a mock Anthropic server (`output/` harness, one recorded `/v1/messages` body a call) replayed 24 Opus 5.5 medium sessions shaped by the nanoeval 7dbf47d1 records (lognormal 4 to 31 tool calls, median 14, 2.1 observations a call drawn from the measured quantiles p50 454 to max 48,029 characters, a 300-word thinking block a turn). Over 398 calls the prefix is already fully cached: the breakpoints on `system[0]`, `system[1]`, the last tool and the top-level automatic breakpoint leave 0 uncached input tokens, so moving breakpoints changes nothing. Input cost is 9.38M cache-read and 0.94M cache-write tokens, 0.94M against 1.18M input-price units, so writes are 56% of it. Tokens read split as recent tool results 35%, tools 31%, thinking 17%, system 7% and results older than the last 12 7%. A replay of the clearing rule over the same bodies (it matched the binary's requests for 62 of 62 calls at (2, 10,000)) priced at read 0.1x and write 1.25x of input, with `block_binding` dropping thinking after a changed prefix, puts the default at 2,026,573 units and (2, 10,000) at -14.6%, (2, 5,000) -17.4%, (4, 10,000) -8.1%, (8, 20,000) -3.0%. Without the thinking drop the same policies give -4.0%, +2.7%, +0.6% and -2.3%, because each clear rewrites the suffix at 1.25x. With the lever unset, 62 of 62 request bodies across 6 sessions equal those of d2253c609 apart from the per-run working directory and session ID. The pass-rate cost of losing older tool output is the nanoeval arm's to measure. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`.
- perf(alloc): `alloc_zeroed` of a small block skips the zero fill when the block comes from the bump region of a page whose slices were clean when the page was made (`Page::zero`, set in `make_page` from the segment's dirty bits, `Page::take_filled`), because a fresh mapping or a `MADV_DONTNEED` purge already reads as zero and an unwritten block stays non-resident (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: anonymous memory, structural lane). Why: at the direct tool-turn peak about 100 to 130 KB of resident anonymous pages held only zeros, 36 KB of them in the psh engine thread's heap, from `vec![0u8; 16 * 1024]` pump and read buffers (`psh-engine` `fd.rs` `Pump::new`, `read_to_end`) that `alloc_zeroed` wrote in full before a short command output used a few bytes. Apple targets keep the fill (`os::PURGE_ZEROES` is false there, since `MADV_FREE_REUSABLE` keeps old contents), and a block from a free list is always filled. `Page` grows from 88 to 96 bytes, so a segment header is 6,200 bytes and still touches two 4 KB pages. Measured on master 9658852ce against a base build of the same commit, both `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` with BOLT, `~/sw/pin/measure.sh <bindir> 10 tools`, 4 interleaved passes (n=10 each): direct tool-turn own Anonymous at the peak per pass 1.059, 1.041, 1.051, 1.047 MiB (median 1.049) against 1.035, 1.018, 1.033, 1.043 (median 1.034, about -15 KB, lower in every pass); Code Mode tool turn 2.725, 2.695, 2.697, 2.715 (median 2.706) against 2.697, 2.697, 2.695, 2.691 (median 2.696). nanocode-sim's alloc scenario now requests half of its allocations zeroed through the new `Local::allocate_zeroed` and checks that each reads as zero: seeds 0..4000 pass, and the `drop_zero` mutation (a zeroed request served by `allocate`) is caught by 50 of 50 seeds.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::escalate(Escalation { model, trigger })` (opt-in, default none; without it every request is unchanged) moves a root session to `model` for the rest of the session once `trigger` is due after a round's tool results: `EscalationTrigger::ToolErrors(n)` after n tool results in a row with `is_error`, `ContextTokens(t)` once `active_context_tokens` reaches t, or `Either`. The switch sets the round cursor's model and `Conversation::escalated`, which the turn template reads at each later turn start (before the refusal fallback latch), so a resumed session stays escalated; subagents keep their model (2026-11-15, Nanocode structural cost lane). Why: the 0.4x Claude Code USD-a-pass goal is out of reach on Opus 5.5 at medium effort (nanoeval A/B 7dbf47d1, 30 tasks x3, 86 matched attempts: $0.546 a pass, 0.68x), and that arm's $0.504 an attempt at the run's Opus 5.5 prices (4/0.20/5/20 USD per million input, cache read, 5-minute write and output tokens) is $0.105 of cache reads (524k tokens), $0.145 of 5-minute writes (28.9k) and $0.254 of output (12.7k). Sonnet 5.5's rates in `nanocode_agent_types::pricing` (`ClaudeModel::rates`, not fast) are 2/0.10/2.5/10, exactly 0.5x Opus 5.5's on every component, so the same tokens cost $0.252 an attempt, and a Sonnet session costs $0.252 x k with k its tokens over Opus's: about 0.33x Claude Code's USD a pass on that run at equal tokens and passes (medium was 0.661x), before escalation. The switch restarts the prompt cache, since a cache belongs to one model: one write of the context at the Opus price ($0.20 at 40k tokens) plus Opus prices for the rest, which is why the triggers are early signals and host policy rather than a finish-time check. The cross-model history (Sonnet thinking blocks sent to Opus) takes the path the refusal fallback latch already takes. Not checked with a mock; the effect on cost and pass rate is the nanoeval arm. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and wasm32 (no new warnings), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`.
- perf(build): read-through remote tier for the build cache (2026-11-15, build critical-path lane remotecache). Why: on dev-georgios (shared, load 21-30), a fresh clone at another path with an empty XDG_CACHE_HOME and a fresh target dir built `cargo build --release --locked -p nanocode-cli` from a `python3 -m http.server` on 127.0.0.1 serving the published cache (737 MB, 95 units) in 2.46 s and 2.59 s with the helper bootstrapped in the build (about 1.3 s of it is compiling the helper), 1.15 s and 1.70 s with the helper already built, against 85.9 s for the same cold build with the remote answering 404 (8 cores) and 226 s for plain rustc (8 cores, load 30); a remote 404 or a refused connection falls back to compiling with no error. Restored files keep their mode, since a build script restored without its execute bit fails with EACCES. What: on a local miss, scripts/buildcache.rs fetches `$NANOCODE_BUILDCACHE_URL/{workspace,units}/<key>` (http:// over a std TcpStream with HTTP/1.1 GET, https through curl, file:// or a plain path read directly), unpacks it into a staging directory and renames it into the cache under the same key and version names as a local store, then restores as before; `scripts/buildcache publish <dir>` lays the local cache out as those static files (one pack per key: name, size and mode, then bytes); the wrapper builds the helper in the foreground when the remote is set, so the first build already uses it. Local keys and the local layout are unchanged.
- perf(turnlog): `Fold::evict` returns an index page to `Page::Cold` and drops its owner entries once every owner in it is cold with no pending records, and an evicted stored key also leaves the dead map, whose values the key's own sections now carry (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 lane memrows9, on 6e33a93c8). Why: after 6e33a93c8 each stored key is its own owner, and an evicted owner stayed in `Fold::owners` as `Owner::Cold` with its section list: at 10K children 138K owner entries held 44 MB (4.4 KB per child), and 9.7K unreached content values held 7.7 MB in `dead` for the life of the process. A cold page reloads on demand through the existing open path (`defer` returns `Owner::Waiting`, `page` reads the index page), and `delta_records` and `owner_records` read `Fold::stored`, which falls back to `dead`, so a dead key keeps its value in its sections before eviction drops it from memory. Measured with output/scale-bench at 10K (--rate 1000 --workers 4 --latency 50 --concurrency 64, taskset -c 3, interleaved under bench2.lock, 4 runs each): live per child 9.5-10.1 KB to 5.9-6.3 KB, peak per child 13.9-14.5 KB to 9.4-10.9 KB; owner entries 138K to 35K, dead entries 9.7K to 17; children/s 96-123 vs 89-132 (noisy, a sim sweep shared the machine). Sims: turns --twice 200/200, --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072 200/200, --owners 2000 --long 50 100/100, --calm --row-limit 1024 200/200, runtime --store log 200/200; mutations content_collected_live 189/200 and sections_kept 128/200 caught.

- fix(code-mode): a steer cuts a recovered `exec` or `wait` short only for a session its embedder marked with `CellJournals::preempt_recovery` (2026-11-15, Pyramid handoff lane). Why: the entry below made every recovered observation preemptible, but a moved subagent's runtime steers it with its resume note as soon as its interrupted turn replays, and in Pyramid's prd turn e917aa81 (2026-11-14) sleepers whose recovered `exec` that note cut short gave up on 9-minute commands that were still running; Pyramid's test `a_steer_waits_for_the_recovered_cell_of_a_moved_subagent` failed with the entry below. Only a root wants a member's message to cut a recovered wait loop. What: `CellJournals` keeps the marked sessions (`preempt_recovery`, `preempts_recovery`); `recover_with_updates` builds its `Preemption` only for one. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode`, again with `--features local-cells`; `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode -- -D warnings` reports only the existing `type_complexity` on `Journals::pending`; Pyramid's subagent and root cell replay tests. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/{mod,replay}.rs.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::lean_cells` (opt-in, default false; off leaves every request unchanged) appends `nanocode_tool_host::deadline::LEAN_CELLS` (a system-reminder: code cells hold only the commands the step needs, without comments or progress prints; print only the needed lines of a file or command output; do not read an unchanged file again) after the prompt of each turn of a headless root session, beside `brief_final` (2026-11-15, Nanocode cost-per-pass lane, output-token lane OT). Why: lane OT's decomposition of nanoeval run b7d70ffb (71 tasks, 213 attempts an arm) puts the Code Mode wrapper at +792 output tokens an attempt over Claude Code, and lists three cuts it estimates at $0.016 an attempt together at $25 per million output tokens (terse cells, bounded echo of file and command output, no re-read of unchanged files). They are one switch because each is under the per-task noise of a 90-row arm alone. Nanoeval A/B 7dbf47d1 (30 tasks x3, 86 matched attempts an arm) has medium effort at 0.68x Claude Code's USD a pass with 82 against 81 passes, so this switch is measured on top of medium. Not checked with a mock: the block is pushed by the same code path as `brief_final`'s; the effect on output and pass rate is the nanoeval A/B. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-tool-host -- -D warnings`.
- perf(codex): a resumed session keeps the `ResponseHistory` that `load_snapshot_with_keys` decoded, so its request reuses the stored JSON of each loaded item and `sync_history` adopts the seeded `SequenceLog` instead of encoding and hashing the whole history again (2026-11-15, resume8 lane). Why: the head `HistorySegment` with stored payload JSON (patch a) gave no win alone (r30 median 16.35M vs 16.26M), because `SessionSnapshot` restore flattened the history to a `Vec` and `ManagedSessionState::resume` committed a new segment without stored JSON. A temporary counter showed 0 stored-JSON encodes and `shared_prefix_len` 0 on every `sync_history`. `ModelCheckpoint::resume` now passes the loaded history to `ManagedSessionState::resume_loaded`, and `ContextManager::resume` adopts it when no item got a new id, was filtered or was truncated (`truncate_tool_output` reports a change). With it the counter showed every loaded item (69 of 69) spliced from stored JSON, with `rewritten()` `None` for each, and the seeded log adopted at full length. Measured with `~/sw/resume8/r30.py` (30 resumes, interleaved, two runs each, base b8b69f3f0): median 16.29/16.27M to 14.10/14.10M (-13.4%), last resume 23.1M to 19.2M, growth 0.463M to 0.350M a turn, request bodies identical (5b6f8220cf76e49a). Checked with `cargo clippy --lib` (no warnings in the changed files) and `cargo check --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for the codex client, codex backend and durability crates.

- fix(subagents): `harness_turn_finished` counts a turn as delivered when it ends without a submit and keeps the previous result (`follow_up_output`), the child's previous completion already settled (`settled_revision` is set) and no completion is pending (2026-11-15, o1restart lane). Why: a peer message queued while the child ran starts a follow-up turn on the completed child, which settles a new revision with the same output, so `delivered` was false and the parent received the same completion a second time (nanocode-sim runtime scenario with the snapshot-header lane's `completion_announced_once` invariant, `--store kv --wide 24 --concurrency 4`: about 8% of seeds before). Validation: `nanocode-sim --scenario runtime --store kv --seeds 0..1000` passes 1000 of 1000 on master f417d3594 with this change; clippy and wasm32 check of nanocode-subagents pass.

- perf(turnlog): each stored key is its own section owner behind a two-level owner index, and a changed owner appends a delta section until its sections reach `snapshot_ratio` times its last full write (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 lane partsnap2, on 11363e57b). Why: after 11363e57b the head still listed every owner of every section group (13,215 `Record::Section` records, 5.5 MB plain at 100K children), so open grew with N, the first read of a state scanned every section of the state and of its content owner (`root:subagents` holds every registry page), and a changed state rewrote all its keys and cells at every snapshot: over the 100K kill run, 3.24 GB of section plain text was written, 1.75 GB of it `root:subagents` registry pages and 0.67 GB the root session's spawning cell. What: (1) `owner_of` maps a `Stored` key that holds a newline to the key itself, so every registry page and every `b3:` content record is an owner. A state owner holds its checkpoint and cells. (2) The head holds one `Record::Index { first, row, rows }` per index page and one `Record::Groups` table of `(row, rows, references)` per section group. An index page is a `p` row of `Record::Owner { checkpoint, full, legacy, owner, sections, written }` entries for the owners in `[first, next first)`, packed until the 32 KiB deflate window. `Fold` creates owner entries only when a page loads: a record of an owner on an unloaded page waits as `Owner::Waiting` and applies after the page. (3) `Owner` is `Cold { entry, pending }`, `Waiting { pending }` or `Warm { delta, entry }`. A snapshot writes the pending records of a cold owner and the changed keys, checkpoint and cell records of a warm owner as a delta section, and writes a warm owner whole when `written + delta >= snapshot_ratio * full`, so the bytes an owner keeps stay within `snapshot_ratio` times its size at the last full write. A full write decrements the references of the owner's old groups, and a group at zero references is dropped in the same append (`Compaction.superseded`), as is the old row of every rewritten index page. (4) `TurnLog::read_owners` and `Lease::load_owners` load exactly the listed owners (a state, or a full `<state>\\n<key>`), loading the index page and then only the groups that hold them. `OneLogStore` uses them for `read_record`, `read_records`, `peek`, `acquire`, `replace`, `commit`, `put_records`, cell journals and the code-mode stored blob. `TurnLog::load_owner` and `read_owner` keep their meaning (the state and all its keys), and `TurnLog::load_index` loads every page for `list_states`. (5) Garbage collection only considers states whose checkpoint, keys and index pages are all loaded, since an unloaded holder can reference a loaded key. (6) A snapshot is due when the tail passes `snapshot_ratio` times the head and the tail is at least `snapshot_ratio` times the packed bytes of the sections and index pages it writes. Compatibility: a log written by 11363e57b opens with its `Record::Section` owners marked legacy. A legacy owner (a state, or a `<state>\\n` content owner) is converted on its first read: the index pages of its key range load first, then its sections, and each key it holds that has no owner of its own becomes one, written at the next snapshot. The flag persists in `Record::Owner` until then. A binary without this change rejects `Record::Index`, `Record::Groups` and `Record::Owner` instead of opening without its sections. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, `taskset -c 1`, 2026-11-15, master 1982e3a71 binaries against this change, interleaved, load 2.6 to 7.6 from other lanes): output/openprof on the 100K-child kill-run log (k100k-base.jsonl, 87 MB, written by master): migration snapshot 439.6 ms (944 rows, 7.4 MB) against master 992.1 ms (292 rows, 22.4 MB); turn-log open 9.0, 17.7 and 8.6 ms against master 111.3, 106.2 and 141.2 ms; `load_all` 41.3 s (102,417 section loads, 483 index loads) against master 168.4 s. scale-bench `--agents 10000 --rate 1000 --workers 4 --kill-at 0.5 --limit 3000`: 11,944 rows and 21.2 MB at 5,018 done children against master 14,198 rows and 59.0 MB at 5,008. Collection: every content key that a reopen drops (92 at 10K, 1,075 at 100K, one second provider-state blob per session) is in the set of `b3:` keys unreachable from any loaded checkpoint, and so are the 1,075 keys an earlier build dropped. nanocode-sim (`bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh`): turns/turnlog `--twice` 200/200, `--calm --row-limit 1024` 200/200, `--snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` 200/200, `--owners 2000 --long 50` 100/100, runtime log and kv 200/200 each; mutation `sections_kept` (a full write keeps the owner's old sections) is caught on 128 of 200 seeds with `--twice --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072`, `part_read_unloaded` on 120 of 200 and `content_collected_live` on 189 of 200.

- feat(claude): `RefusalFallbackScope::Off` keeps a refused request on its own model: the classifier-category fallback (f85fd5a04) and its latch are skipped, and the existing same-model retry and continuations still apply (2026-11-15, Pyramid nanocode bump). Why: the fallback has no off switch, so a host with its own refusal handling (Pyramid's admin-configured fallback, its refusal metric and the notice it posts in the thread) never saw these refusals, and with `ReturnOnce` a second refusal latched the older model into the durable session while the host still showed the main model. What: `refused` leaves the latch as it is under `Off`, and the fallback branch in `rounds.rs` is skipped when the scope is `Off`. The default stays `ReturnOnce`. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent/rounds.rs.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::brief_final` (opt-in, default false; off leaves every request unchanged) appends `nanocode_tool_host::deadline::BRIEF_FINAL` ("Keep your final message to at most three lines: the result and where it is." in a system-reminder) as a text block after the prompt of each turn of a headless root session, at the point where `fold_finish` appends its checklist (2026-11-15, Nanocode cost-per-pass lane, output-token lane OT). Why: lane OT's decomposition of nanoeval run b7d70ffb merged with its rerun (71 tasks both arms passed 3 of 3 without fallback, 213 attempts an arm) puts nano's output at 10,758 tokens an attempt against Claude Code's 8,127 (1.32x): thinking +1,236, the Code Mode wrapper +792, the final answer written again after the finish check +595 (which `brief_finish` and `fold_finish` aim at), and the first final answer 624 against 665. `brief_final` aims at the first final answer, which Terminal-Bench does not grade (estimate $0.012 an attempt realistic, $0.016 upper bound, at $25 per million output tokens). Not checked with a mock: the block is pushed by the same code path as `fold_finish`'s, which the output/cost-levers harness checked; the effect on output and pass rate is the nanoeval A/B. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-tool-host -- -D warnings`.
- perf(build): scripts/buildcache shares compiled crates across checkouts, target directories and cache locations, so a cache can be copied, synced or served remotely (2026-11-15, build cache lane: path-free keys). Before, a clone at another path with another CARGO_TARGET_DIR and the cache copied to another XDG_CACHE_HOME recompiled every unit. Three things tied a unit to its paths. (1) Cargo hashes the absolute path of `rustc-workspace-wrapper` (scripts/rustc-parallel-frontend, resolved from the checkout) into every workspace unit's `-C metadata`, so symbols, file names and rmeta differed per checkout: `cargo rustc -p nanocode-sys` in two checkouts gave metadata 24a47f8ed4f19345 and 7f2d1cf9c85126a6, and e2f2a041f732a3c3 in both when both named one wrapper path. .cargo/config.toml no longer sets it; the helper puts the frontend in front of rustc itself for workspace units (all 86 packages are members, so the same set; clippy units keep clippy-driver alone, as before), and scripts/buildcache does the same while the helper is not built yet. A build with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` now runs plain rustc, without `-Zthreads=0` and share-generics. (2) The key hashed the workspace root, and CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, CARGO_MANIFEST_PATH, OUT_DIR, `-L native`, the manifest paths in inputs, dep-info sources and env-dep values were absolute. The workspace root, CARGO_HOME, the cache directory and the unit's out dir are now placeholders in the key, inputs, sources, recorded env-deps, the stored dep-info and the replayed stderr, and are put back on restore; rustc still gets real paths, plus `--remap-path-prefix` for the workspace root (`.`), CARGO_HOME (`/cargo`) and the cache (`/nanocode-build`), placed before the caller's flags so a RUSTFLAGS remap still wins. With the remap a test crate built in two checkouts gives identical rlib and rmeta, without it different ones. A stored unit whose outputs still contain one of those absolute paths (an `env!` value kept as data, a string a proc macro generated) records them and is restored only where they are the same. djs-core's `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), ...))` was the last miss: its env-dep held the cache's absolute path, and its rebuild cascaded to 17 dependents because rustc's rmeta is not reproducible across rebuilds (90 bytes of djs-core's differ, with no path among them). (3) Cache entries were absolute symlinks; they are relative now. Keys move to nanocode-rustc-cache-6 and nanocode-workspace-cache-2. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, rustc 1.100.0, load 2 to 15 from other agents): clean `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli -j8`, 96 rustc calls counted by a logging RUSTC, the helper built into the cache beforehand instead of a warm-up build, B at another path with another target dir and the cache copied to another XDG_CACHE_HOME. Before: fill at A 246.6 s; B 212.6 s, 689.6 s user CPU, 96 of 96 compiled (A's cache kept, so the symlinks resolved). After: fill at A 188.4 s; a warm rerun at A 4.8 s, 5 compiled; B 4.1 s, 3.8 s user CPU, 5 compiled (A's cache deleted after the copy). The 5 are the same in both: cargo's probe, three build scripts and the nanocode binary. Dev profile, after: fill at A 79.6 s, 92 calls; B 5.1 s, 5 compiled. No artifact in B's release target (183 rlib, rmeta, so and the binary) contains a path under either checkout, target or cache, and `nanocode --version` prints `nanocode 0.7.0`. Not covered: the toolchain's rust-src path (rustc names it in place of `/rustc/<hash>` where rust-src is installed; the output check then keeps such units to one machine), and the C object cache, which still keys on cwd. Files: scripts/buildcache, scripts/buildcache.rs, .cargo/config.toml.
- fix(subagents): a restored subagent's resume message no longer repeats its delegated task, and each in-flight call it lists quotes at most 2 KiB of its arguments (`RESUME_ARGUMENT_BYTES`), not only when the whole message would pass 64 KiB (2026-11-15, Pyramid: slow subagents across deploys). Why: a host that moves a running turn at every deploy restores every live subagent each time, and each restore steered the child with `RESUME_MESSAGE` plus its whole task plus whole call arguments, which stays in the child's history. In one 21-hour Pyramid turn with 65 subagents (Claude, 156 handoffs, as its deploys shipped every main commit), each restore added 30k to 36k input tokens to each live child (`instruction_bytes` 65,589 to 66,939 per `subagent-recovery` steer), against a median of about 2k per ordinary step; children climbed to 950k to 980k tokens and compacted, and time to first token rose from 2.0 s under 100k to 3.8 s over 900k. The task is already at the start of the child's history, and it was `descriptor.task`, the task the child was spawned with, so a child reused through a `delegate` message was handed its old task again. What a restore sends now: the notice and, per in-flight call, its tool, call ID, state and 2 KiB of arguments, then the oldest calls count as omitted while it passes `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`. Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-subagents`, again for wasm32-unknown-unknown; `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-subagents -- -D warnings`; `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 300 8 --scenario agents` and `--scenario runtime`: SWEEP passed=300 failed=0, panics=0 each. Files: crates/runtime/subagents/src/durable.rs, crates/runtime/subagents/src/runtime.rs.
- fix(code-mode): `recover_with_updates` observes the recovered cell with the session's preemption, as `wait` does, so a steer cuts a recovered `exec` or `wait` short instead of waiting out the cell's own yield (2026-11-15, Pyramid handoff lane). Why: a host that moves a turn to another process recovers the call that was observing a running cell, but the recovery passed `ObservationMode::YieldAfter(yield, yield, None)`, so a member's message sent meanwhile waited for the whole yield. Pyramid works around it by capping a recovered observation at 15 s (`MOVED_OBSERVATION_MS`, after a message waited nearly 13 minutes behind a recovered subagent loop on 2026-11-14), which wakes the root model about 15 s after every handoff with nothing new; in its prd trace of turn 702864ed on 2026-11-15, a root blocked in a `wait_agent` loop was woken after each of 20 handoffs in an hour and once terminated and rewrote its loop. What: `recover_with_updates` builds a `Preemption` from `preempt`, `current_turn` and `preempt_consumed`, the way `wait_inner` does, and passes it to `observe_cell`. A steer that arrived before the recovery and was not consumed preempts it at once. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode`, again with `--features local-cells` and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs.
- feat(tool-host): `FINISH_CHECKLIST` gets one bullet after the task's own check: if the task states a speed, size or score goal, the result was compared with at least one structurally different approach under repeated measurements, and the best one is kept, and beating the given baseline is not by itself the goal (2026-11-15, Nanocode cost-per-pass lane). Why: in nanoeval run b7d70ffb and its rerun 6294482a (Terminal-Bench 2, claude-opus-5-5), two failed rows of one optimization task wrote a result much faster than the slow given baseline, timed it only against that baseline and stopped, at 1.10x and 1.12x of the hidden reference time where the limit was 1.05x. The passing rows of nano and Claude Code used a structurally different approach. The bullet is general and names no task. It reaches the headless finish check (`finish_notice`, Claude and Codex) and the checklist that `fold_finish` appends to each prompt (`folded_finish_notice`). The rest of the text is byte-identical. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-codex` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-tool-host -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/runtime/tool-host/src/deadline.rs.
- fix(nc): `--codex-orchestration code-mode` now gives every Codex model Code Mode's `exec` and `wait`, custom endpoint models included; the default (direct) is unchanged (2026-11-15, DeepSeek cost lane, code-mode bet). Why: `Host` passed `direct_tools_for(codex_direct || !native_model(model))`, so the explicit flag was silently ignored for a model outside `Model::ALL`: a Terminal-Bench 2.1 trial of `@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` through the cf-cost proxy with the flag (nanocode 668272b05, log-summary-date-ranges) sent exec_command, write_stdin, view_image, job_start, job_wait and job_kill and no `exec`. Custom models keep direct tools by default (the 2026-11-12 entry below), so only a request for Code Mode reaches them. What: the predicate is `codex_direct` alone. Checks: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode --no-deps -- -D warnings`. Files: bin/nanocode/src/host.rs.
- perf(process): an `exec_command` script that names programs is run by the psh embedded in the nanocode process, which starts each program directly (`posix_spawn`), instead of being handed to a warm psh shell process (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: child processes out of the tool-turn peak). What: `psh::embed::contained` now accepts any program with a literal name; it still refuses `exec`, `kill` and `suspend`, a builtin or shell (`bash`, `sh`) that runs code the classifier cannot see (`source`, `eval` of a non-literal, `bash -c "$s"`), a `LongRunning` command, anything in the background and anything that reads `$$` or `$PPID`; those still go to the warm shell, a PTY run (`tty`) or a requested shell too. The embedded run keeps the programs it leaves running (`Leftovers::Keep`, as a shell process does), inherits the ignored signals (`inherit_ignored`), sets `login_shell` for a login command (`Command::login`, `-O login_shell`), and `Running::interrupt` also sends INT to every live program group of the run (`RunKiller::interrupt`). Each program leads a session of its own (`Placement::Session`), so stopping the run kills its groups as before. Parity: the 53-command exec_command sample of 90e7a930c (empty HOME and a HOME whose `.bash_profile` sources the skeleton `.bashrc`, exports a function, uses arrays and sets umask), base 5be7df421 against this change, gives the same bytes apart from chunk ids and wall times for 50 of 53 commands in both homes; the other three now match `/bin/bash -lc` (bash 5.2.21) where the warm shell did not: `shopt login_shell` prints `on` and exits 0 (was `off`, 1), `python3 -c 'print(os.getpgrp()==os.getpid(), os.getsid(0)==os.getpid())'` prints `True True` as under `setsid bash -c` (was `False False`), and a program's stdout and stderr keep their write order (the warm shell interleaved `o1 e1 o2` as `o1 o2 e1` in one of four base runs). Memory: `~/sw/pin/measure.sh <dir> 10 tools` (bench/cli, pinned to one core, ASLR off, 1 warm-up round, n=10 each, median [min-max]) on dist builds of 5be7df421 and of this change: direct tool turn own peak RSS 6.06 [5.82-6.40] -> 5.81 [5.63-5.99] MB, tree peak 7.40 [6.40-7.52] -> 7.35 [5.65-7.45] MB, CPU 0.89 -> 0.80 ms a step; Code Mode tool turn own peak 8.58 [8.51-9.15] -> 8.58 [8.52-8.81] MB, tree peak 10.16 [8.52-10.32] -> 9.37 [8.55-10.28] MB, tree PSS 6.83 -> 6.48 MB, CPU 1.25 -> 1.16 ms a step. An earlier n=2 pass on the bench/cli harness with profile-bearing turns gave direct tree 16.49 -> 7.74 MB and helpers 3 -> 1. Rebased on 759f81902, whose warm-shell start now serves only the scripts `contained` refuses. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-psh-embedded` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-psh-embedded -p psh -p psh-os -- -D warnings`, `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode`. Files: crates/integrations/process/src/{embedded,foreground,lib}.rs, crates/integrations/psh-embedded/src/lib.rs, crates/patches/psh/crates/psh-os/src/unix/{mod,spawn}.rs, crates/patches/psh/crates/psh/src/embed.rs.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::low_effort_rounds` and `ClaudeBuilder::fold_finish` (both opt-in, default false; with both off every request is unchanged) (2026-11-15, Nanocode cost-per-pass lane, wave 9). Why: in nanoeval runs 784946b4 and b7d70ffb the headless finish check added 2.24 to 2.40 agent steps after the first end_turn ($0.041 to $0.054 per attempt) and Code Mode wait rounds added 1.27 to 1.29 rounds per attempt ($0.025 to $0.029). Cache key: a change of the top-level `output_config.effort` renders into the prompt and starts the prompt cache over (c25b588fd), so `low_effort_rounds` never changes it. It uses the per-message effort of c25b588fd instead: the top-level effort stays pinned at the conversation's first request, and an effort-only system message (`{"role":"system","content":[],"output_config":{"effort":...}}`, beta mid-conversation-output-config-2026-07-01) is appended after the last user message, so every request extends the one before it. Where per-message effort is not available (subscription wire, thinking disabled, a model without `supports_effort_updates`) the option does nothing and the effort stays constant. What `low_effort_rounds` does: before each model request of a turn it sends the lowest effort the model accepts (low for Opus 5.5) when the request is low-information, and the configured effort otherwise, and appends an effort message only when the level in effect changes. A request is low-information when the messages after the last assistant message are one user message and, at most, effort messages and repeated `Time limit: ... remain.` notices, and the user message is either the finish-check notice (`nanocode_tool_host::deadline::is_finish_notice`) or only `exec`/`wait` results of a running cell that printed nothing and returned no nested call since the last yield, whose running nested calls show no output or the same output as the cell's previous result (`nanocode_code_mode::code_mode_spec::unchanged_yield`; the strings it matches are now constants in code_mode_spec.rs that code_mode/mod.rs formats with). What `fold_finish` does: in a headless root session it appends the finish checklist (`folded_finish_notice`: the same bullets, asked for before the final message) as a text block after the prompt of each turn, and the separate finish check then runs only when the first final message comes before the first deadline reminder (50%); without a deadline it does not run. Harness: output/cost-levers (a native Claude agent on claude-opus-5-5 at high effort, Code Mode with a 1 s cell yield and a `build_step` tool that sleeps, against mock.py, a scripted Messages server that logs every request; run.sh runs nine arms and analyze.py compares them). Default against every option set to false: all 8 requests identical after normalizing wall times. `low_effort_rounds`: 8 requests, the same as default; the top-level `output_config` stays `high` on all of them; request 2 (a wait result with nothing new) appends effort low, request 3 (the same) appends nothing, request 4 (the cell completed) appends high, request 5 (an exec yield that printed nothing) low, request 6 high, and request 7 (the finish check) low; the first yield, which printed `compiling`, stays high; every request's system, tools, output_config and thinking equal the previous request's and its messages extend the previous request's messages. `fold_finish` with the deadline at 0%: the checklist block on request 0, and the finish check still runs (8 requests); with 60% of the deadline gone: 7 requests, no finish check, where default with 60% gone sends 8. With 60% gone the repeated time notices do not stop `low_effort_rounds`. Not checked against the live API: how much output a low-effort wait or finish-check round saves, and whether the model's choices on those rounds change; that is the nanoeval A/B. Also: removed a redundant clone in claude_tools.rs that `cargo clippy -D warnings` reported. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-code-mode` native and wasm32, and `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps` on the same crates with `-D warnings`.

Why: a cost decomposition of the recorded request streams of nanoeval runs 784946b4 (W7D build, 233 attempt pairs that both arms passed) and b7d70ffb (W7F build with 205edb3d5, 188 pairs at 428 of 534 ended rows), priced at $4 input, $0.20 cache read, $5 and $8 cache writes and $20 output for Opus 5.5 ($5/$0.50/$6.25/$10/$25 for the Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 refusal fallbacks), puts nano at $0.4071 against Claude Code 2.1.318 at $0.4028 an attempt on W7D and $0.4430 against $0.3776 on W7F. By class, nano against cc, W7F: output $0.2301 against $0.1823, 5 minute writes $0.1137 against $0.1184, cache reads $0.0991 against $0.0768, refusal fallback models $0.0588 against $0.0616 (inside the classes), keep-warm refreshes 0.28 a attempt at $0.0022 against 0.12 at $0.0018, 13.89 against 10.86 requests, first request 13.7k against 17.1k tokens. The 5 minute TTL did its part: on the 169 keys that both arms passed in both runs, nano's cache writes fell from $0.1475 to $0.1054 an attempt and its total from $0.4060 to $0.4034, while cc's total fell from $0.4050 to $0.3472 on the same keys; without winning-avg-corewars (nano $5.33 and $5.75 on two W7F attempts against $1.21 and $2.29 for cc) the nano/cc ratio is 1.030 on W7D and 1.028 on W7F, so the W7F regression is task variance, not the build. Nano's own extra rounds are the finish check (2.24 and 2.40 agent steps after the first end_turn, $0.041 and $0.054 an attempt, 79 to 82% of them run commands that change files, so the check stays) and `wait` rounds after an `exec` yield (1.27 and 1.29 an attempt, $0.025 and $0.029). The finish check's last step repeats the final message: 541 and 606 output tokens, 1,378 and 1,540 characters of text, after a first final message of 716 tokens. Replay estimate: cutting that last message's text to one line (text tokens = characters / 4, less 10, at $20/M, thinking unchanged) saves $0.0065 and $0.0074 an attempt, 1.6% and 1.7%. The same replay prices the existing `cell_yield` option (nanocode-ts `cell_yield_ms`) at 120 s, which drops each `wait` round of a cell whose recorded wall time ends within ceil(T/120 s) - 1 rounds plus that round's later reads and writes, at -$0.0221 and -$0.0236 (5.4% and 5.3%); 60 s gives 4.7% and 4.6%, 30 s 3.4% and 3.7%. - perf(djs): minor collections promote their survivors and trace only dirty cards of the old region (2026-11-15, djs generational GC lane). Why: a minor collection walked every slot of the old region for young references (`mark_old`: 9.50M of map.js's 86.57M callgrind instructions, 17.4M of them memset) and never raised `Roots::OLD_END`, so survivors were re-marked and slid at every minor. What: `Heap::promote` sets `OLD_END` to the arena's end after every minor collection and after every full collection of a heap that has an old region (`seal` and `collect_canonical` too), so no young cell survives a collection. The arena keeps a card table (`Cards`, one byte per 512-byte card of the old region, not part of the image): `Arena::barrier` and `Arena::wrote` compare the offset with `low`, the larger of the tracked prefix's end and the card table's end, and a write below it marks its cards in `Arena::noted` (out of line), so a write above both costs the one compare the tracked prefix already had. `barrier_end` replaces `tracked_end` in run_hot's capture stores and each_fused's accumulator and result stores. Raw writes that bypass the barrier are covered by tracing their cells whole: the value stack and an active stack segment get their cards marked after every collection, and the minor collection traces the saved frame of every old Generator (a stack segment or `run_tier1` writes it in place; `tracked_end` keeps its meaning for tier1). `ic_write` marks its template's card, and the card walk empties the offset caches of templates over dirty cards; an insertion into a Map or Set writes its `LIVE` slot, so the walk finds collections with young keys there. The cell starts per card, the old ephemeron count and the Generator list are filled lazily by the next minor collection for the cells promoted since; a restored or rebuilt arena, or one truncated below the table, drops the table and its next minor collection walks the old region as before. Debug builds check before each card walk that every young reference in the old region lies in a dirty card or a Generator frame. Measured on 590b2a41b (instructions:u, best of 3, output/djsrun): map 68.76M to 61.08M (-11.2%), filter 71.12M to 63.44M (-10.8%), err -1.5%, loop/gen/find/some/forEach/reduce within +0.14%, gennext +1.6% (old Generator frames traced whole each minor), empty +29K (+3.3%: scan_old no longer inlined into the fallback walk). Callgrind map.js: collect_auto 11.18M to 3.43M. cellbench (instructions per cell): loop 169.19M to 164.80M (-2.6%), empty/text/tool1/seq16/par16/agent +0.1% to +0.7%. Tried and dropped: folding the card end into `tracked_end` (tier1 declines old Generator frames: gennext +213%); an eager cell-start walk at promotion (empty +17%); a clean card table on image load plus an inline single-card store (Code Mode cells +5%). Gates: test262 subset 2,535 passing, result file identical; fuel harness identical; gc_stress harness (output/gcstress: base image VM, `seal`, `gc_stress`, debug card check) clean.
- feat(claude): a Bash call can be given the directory it starts in through `ToolContext::with_directory`, which a host that serves several directories sets instead of putting `cd <dir> &&` in front of the command (2026-11-15, Pyramid: cell calls that waited on `sleep 30`). Why: Pyramid's broker started each Bash call in the thread's directory by prefixing `cd -- '<dir>' || exit 1` to the command, so `leading_sleep`, which reads the command's first word, saw `cd` and let a Code Mode cell's `sleep 30; echo hi` block for 30 s on production Hands, and Pyramid's turn reviews flagged agents waiting minutes on such commands. A context directory keeps the command as the model wrote it. What: `ToolContext` carries an optional directory (`with_directory`, `directory`), `ClaudeBash::execute_call_in` puts it on `BashRequest::directory`, and `LocalBash` starts the command there: a cell call or background command in it instead of the workspace, and a direct call in it instead of the tracked shell directory, which such a call neither reads nor moves (no `pwd -P` marker, no reset note), so the host owns where calls start. Without a directory nothing changes. Measured with output/bash-dir (`hand_tools_with` on a root, the Bash tool called with a `ToolContext`): cell `pwd` with a directory prints it and without one the root; direct `pwd` with a directory prints it with no reset note (before the marker skip: `Shell cwd was reset to <root>`); cell `sleep 30; echo slept` with a directory is refused at once with the `Blocked: sleep 30` text; a background `pwd > bg.txt` writes bg.txt in the given directory. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-tool-contracts`, the same with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo run` in output/bash-dir. Files: crates/core/tool-contracts/src/lib.rs, crates/backends/claude/tools/src/tools/bash.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/claude_bash.rs.
- fix(process): a psh command with no warm shell free starts one and hands it the script on stdin, instead of running `psh -c SCRIPT` (2026-11-15, Pyramid: agents' `pgrep -f` loops on hosted Hands). Why: the cold path put the whole script in the shell's own command line, so a command that looks for a process by its command line (`pgrep -f cargo && echo RUNNING`, `pkill -f scripts/prototype.ts`) found, or killed, the shell running it. A Pyramid agent's loop printed RUNNING for 24 minutes after its tests had ended, and a `pkill -f` ended the agent's own command before the next step ran. A warm shell's command line is `psh --warm`, whatever it runs, and the warm path already serves most commands; it is now the only path for psh. The cold shell is launched on a blocking worker (`Lane::launch`) and is not counted in the lane, since it is taken at once. Measured with output/psh-cold (path dependencies on this tree; `nanocode_process::NativeForeground` with psh as the chosen shell runs `if pgrep -f '<marker>' >/dev/null; then echo matched-itself; else echo clean; fi; tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$$/cmdline` four times in a fresh process, the first with an empty pool), 10 fresh processes per build, interleaved, on a Pyramid hosted Hand: before, the first command matched itself 10 of 10 times (`... psh-shell -c if pgrep -f 'psh-cold-marker-1' ...`); after, 0 of 10 (`... psh-shell --warm`); the first command took 23.8 ms on average in both. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-process`, `cargo build --release` in output/psh-cold. Files: crates/integrations/process/src/warm.rs.
- docs(decisions): file-page release schedules after the power-of-two drops, clean writable segments and a per-process fault-around switch measured and not shipped (2026-11-15, CLI file pages wave 3). Schedules (an `NC_FPDROP` experiment build of 4032b375f that runs `release_file_pages` at chosen `ModelCallStarted`, `ToolCall` and `ToolResult` counts; bench/cli `tools,oneshot` under `PIN_WARMUP=1` and `~/sw/pin/measure.sh`, four interleaved passes of 3 runs, n=12 each, direct tool turn ru_maxrss median): drops at power-of-two model calls 5.605 MB (the shipped schedule); also at every model call 5.605 MB with 2,446 instead of 1,978 minor faults; also at the first tool result 5.605 MB; also at the first tool call 5.441 MB (-0.16 MB, 2,017 faults, CPU per step 1.275 to 1.230 ms within spread); first drop at the second model call with the first tool call 5.441 MB, with the first tool result 6.531 MB. The peak is set inside the first tool call, after its `ToolCall` event and before its `ToolResult`, so no event-boundary schedule reaches the 0.5 MB goal, and -0.16 MB was not shipped. Clean writable data: the agent's writable `PT_LOAD`s are 0x5b00 and 0x10fe8 bytes (92 KB of address space, RELRO included), so dropping their clean file pages cannot lower the peak by 0.5 MB. Fault-around: registering the read-only mappings with userfaultfd in `UFFDIO_REGISTER_MODE_WP` and `UFFD_FEATURE_WP_ASYNC` sets `VM_UFFD_WP`, which turns off fault-around for that mapping only, but `userfaultfd(UFFD_USER_MODE_ONLY)` returns ENOSYS on the 6.18.56 bench kernel (`CONFIG_USERFAULTFD` off), so it was not measured. `MADV_PAGEOUT` was not tried: it evicts the binary from the page cache for every process and turns later touches into major faults.
- perf(cli): a headless session (`nanocode exec`) starts its MCP servers and loads the Tempo and Boundless model listing on demand instead of at startup (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track, startup network lane). Why: the one-shot with `--gateway vercel` and a local base URL resolved gateway.tempo-dev.workers.dev twice, api.inference.boundless.network and mercator.sh before its first request. `Tempo::offer` spawned the listing load, which feeds only `list_models` and `spawn_agent` routing, and `Mcp` connected the gateway and mercator servers, whose tools are deferred and absent from the first request. The interactive terminal keeps the eager start and listing. Limit: in a headless Code Mode session, the cell metadata includes MCP tools only after `tool_search` or a call has started the servers. Measured (`scripts/build-cli.sh` dist+BOLT of f94d79461 against this change, the fixture one-shot under a netns with a logging DNS server): DNS queries 8 to 0, and the first request is byte-identical except the time-based message, session, thread and turn IDs. `perf stat`, 5 interleaved passes of 12: user instructions 3.44M to 3.03M, kernel 3.01M to 2.68M (pass medians 3.00-3.13M against 2.65-2.73M), page faults 360 to 343.5. bench/cli tools (measure.sh, 5 runs, base, new, base, new): direct own RSS 5.50 and 5.63 MB to 5.39 and 5.41 MB, Code Mode 8.19 and 8.18 MB to 8.34 and 8.00 MB, within the spread. The kernel target of 1.1M is not reachable from this lane: the rest is execve and page faults, and `--no-tempo-tools` on the base moved kernel instructions by only about 0.03M.
