Measured: dist+BOLT `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` of 777b22b3b and the change, 8 interleaved passes of bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc --rounds=2` (Code Mode turn), `smaps_rollup` sampled every 0.3 ms, n=80 each: peak RSS median 7,780 to 8,188 KB, anonymous at the RSS peak 1,552 to 1,572 KB, maximum anonymous 1,640 [1,612-1,644] to 1,684 [1,668-1,696] KB. So the expected -300 KB does not appear and anonymous memory grows by about 44 KB. Cause: `segment::large_free` (crates/core/sys/src/alloc/segment.rs) keeps a freed large block below 4 MiB in `LARGE_CACHE` (16 slots, 8 MiB) without purging its pages, so the derivation's 329 KB heap buffer, freed after the runs are taken, stays resident, and the runs and their `Vec`s are added on top. The RSS change includes the layout of two BOLT builds, as the direct turn of earlier pairs moved by up to 0.5 MB with no Code Mode code in it. For the change to pay, the derivation's buffer must be reused or returned: hand it to the first `Instance` (no second allocation), or purge cached large blocks above some size in `large_free`. The remaining gap is then the instance arena's own image copy (about 380 KB resident). Also not shipped: (1) tool definitions per cell on the static image, which removes the derived image entirely, cost about 740K instructions per cell (djs `Object.defineProperty` is about 270 fuel per call); (2) releasing the static image's pages after the derivation (21c410f01) measured nothing after b5e824777 drops read-only file pages at model calls; (3) a copy-on-write instance arena over the base image's file pages (`MAP_PRIVATE` of the executable over the page-aligned interior of the arena buffer, so untouched pages stay file-backed and a write copies one page): `Arena` is a `Vec<u8>` that the global allocator owns and grows by `realloc`, so a private file mapping would live on in memory the allocator frees, caches, moves or purges (after `MADV_DONTNEED` such a page reads back the file, not zeros), every growth and drop would have to remap it anonymous first, a read page still counts as file RSS so only never-read pages are saved, and wasm32 has no equivalent; a software lazy map does not fit either, because the interpreter reads the arena through slices (`Arena::bytes`, `hot_bytes`) on every path. Harnesses: ~/sw/cmanon (deleted after this entry); the patch is kept at ~/sw/cmanon-derive-over.patch.
- perf(djs): `json::parse::scan_one` decodes an escaped one-byte string into a buffer that only grows, with one bounds-checked 8-byte store a word and the special byte decoded in place through a 256-entry `UNESCAPE` table, and a string that turns two-byte continues in the cold `scan_wide`, which only counts (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 8). Typical-cell suite (output/cellbench, `--vary`, perf `instructions:u`, best of 3, base 29b3e7945): 6,168,073 -> 6,095,030 (-1.2%), seq 884,510 -> 851,061 (-3.8%), json 1,327,852 -> 1,308,157 (-1.5%), edit 962,373 -> 949,223 (-1.4%), sh 1,401,376 -> 1,394,640, agent and the empty cell unchanged within 15 instructions. Outputs byte-identical for all six cells, test262 subset 2,535 and the fuel harness identical (it includes the JSON error-position cases), `scripts/base.sh --check` passes, and the 10 djs benches move by -0.001% to +0.001%. Cause, measured with callgrind on the seq cell (315 escapes in a 4.2 KB tool result): each word extended `dec` (a capacity check and a length update) and then truncated it, and each escape paid a `len` counter beside `dec`, a second end check and an 8-way match before `dec.push`. `dec[..len]` is now the decoded text, `len` is the write position, and `string_value` copies `dec[..nbytes]`. Where the cells go now (perf with call graphs, after this change): compile is 13.5% of the agent cell and 19.7% of the json cell, of which `resolve::finish` is 5.7% and 9.8% (`emit_function` 4.8% and 8.3%), so a single-emit compile of capture-free functions saves at most about 5% of the suite; JSON parse is 16.7% of the json cell; on the sh cell a `split(/\s+/)` pays about 650 instructions for the literal's `regexp::create`, 470 for `pristine` and 630 for `Simple::of` before `split_now`.
- perf(djs): each_fused's filter keeps a chunk of 8 int32 elements with one tag test and a branchless append (2026-11-15). `scan::<KEEP, OP>` with a constant operand tested each element's tag, compared it and set a mask bit, then appended the kept ones in a second loop with a branch per element; it now ORs the 8 words against the int tag once, and if all are int32 writes each element to the next output slot and advances the count by the comparison. Holes, non-int elements and the per-index form (`q` from the index) take the existing loop, so results and fuel are unchanged. Measured (output/djsrun, user instructions, best of 3, interleaved, against 614ad2d9f): filter.js 71.54M to 70.80M (-1.0%), find and some -0.14% (layout), map, forEach, reduce, loop, gen, gennext, err and empty within 0.06%. Measured and left out: computing MAP_TO's range test and its tagged results in one pass over the chunk (map.js +2.4%). Where map.js's 68.48M goes on 614ad2d9f, by exact counts (callgrind, which also counts `rep stosb` per byte, so memset is left out): the MAP_TO scan 22.0M (about 11 user instructions an element, scalar), minor collections 10.9M (mark_old 9.2M: about 340,000 instructions a minor over the old region, 27 minors; sampled profiles put it at 2%, it is 13%), run_hot's own loop (`s += a.map(...).length`, a closure per iteration) about 11M, each_fused's setup in decline_plain about 7.5M, the result's allocation about 5.9M and plain_species 2.7M (two own-property searches per call while builtins are not frozen); filter.js is the same with the KEEP scan at 25.6M. The fused path already writes results by index into a store reserved to the source length, so create_element_fast and dense_put no longer run in either benchmark. 33M for map.js needs the collections and the per-call cost (about 2,300 instructions outside the scan for 100 elements), not the per-element store. Checks: the test262 subset passes 2,535 with identical output, the fuel harness (408 runs) is identical, a filter edge script (each comparison, int32 limits, a double, a string, a hole, undefined) and a map/filter edge script print the same, `scripts/base.sh --check` and `scripts/bgen.sh --check` pass, `cargo check --lib -p djs-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes, clippy reports nothing in the changed file.
- feat(code-mode): `CellJournals::live_journals` snapshots a session's live cells as they stand, held or not, skipping cells that are unsupported, past the journal's limit or still replaying; `journals` keeps snapshotting only once every cell is held (`CellRecord::snapshot_when`) (2026-11-15, Pyramid handoff prestage lane). Pyramid's draining backend writes a turn's cell journals' content-addressed chunks ahead of its handoff, but cells are held only when the handoff begins, so `journals` gave the write-ahead nothing and each handoff wrote 0.9 to 3.7 MB of chunks while the turn waited (Pyramid prd drains 07:01 and 07:03 PST: `Prestaged ... 0 KB of cells` on 43 of 45 turns; claim gap p95 1.3 to 2.4 s for turns sending at least 500 KB, against about 200 ms for the rest). A live snapshot is never restored: it differs from the held journal only in what the cell did since, so the handoff sends only those chunks. Shipped first on hotfix/live-cell-journals-63951c4 (f0a9f9be), which Pyramid pins (tempoxyz/pyramid#4079); checked by Pyramid CI's `prestage_live_tests`.

- perf(turnlog): a snapshot evicts every warm owner that no load read since the previous snapshot back to its sections, so a finished child's state and content leave the live fold (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 lanes memrows5 and memrows6, measured on 90e7a930c, landed on 29b3e7945). Why: the lazy turn log (11363e57b) keeps cold owners out of the fold only after an open. In a live process every owner it ever wrote stays warm, so each finished child kept its checkpoint, named records, cells and content records for the life of the parent. What: `Fold::touch` records each owner that `warm_state` loads (`TurnLog::load_owner`, `TurnLog::read_owner`, `Lease::load_owner`). After `Fold::sectioned`, `Fold::evict` turns each warm owner that is not in that set into `Owner::Cold` with the same sections and drops its records from the fold. A state owner is evicted only together with its content owner `<state>\n` (or when that owner is already cold), so collection never sees content whose checkpoint left the fold. A later read loads the owner from its sections as after an open, and a later write waits in its pending list as for a cold owner. `OneLog::cells` loads the tool catalog and the session in one lease, since an eviction between two separate loads can drop the catalog. No record kind and no head change: the head lists the same sections before and after an eviction. nanocode-sim: after every commit the turnlog policy reads `<scope>:part` through `TurnLog::read_owner` and checks the last part revision. Mutation `part_read_unloaded` reads it from the fold without a load and is caught on 120 of 200 seeds with `--snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072`. Measured with output/scale-bench `--agents 10000 --rate 1000 --workers 4 --latency 50 --concurrency 64` on one core (`taskset -c 3`), 3 runs of each build interleaved on the hosted Hand at load 12-13, all 10000 children done in every run. Parent live bytes per child: base 18623, 18902 and 16703 (median 18.6 KB), eviction 8778, 9588 and 7621 (median 8.8 KB). Peak bytes per child: base 56979, 57260 and 55062, eviction 18371, 19179 and 17211. Wall: base 151.7, 389.6 and 145.6 s, eviction 160.6, 238.3 and 101.1 s, inside the load noise of the shared Hand. Sims on the 90e7a930c tree, the same for both builds: turns 200/200, turns with `--snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` 200/200, runtime with the log store 100/100 and the kv store 100/100. `sections_pruned` is caught on 155 of 200 `--twice` seeds and `content_collected_live` on 195 of 200 for both builds. Checks: cargo clippy -D warnings (turnlog, sim, agent with local-cells) and cargo +1.97.1 check wasm32 (turnlog, agent) pass. What stays: the root registry state is read every cycle, so it stays warm (about 3.7 KB per child of content and named pages), and the dead map keeps about 0.8 KB per child.

- perf(djs): `Heap::alloc_latin1_range` copies a substring of a one-byte slice straight from the slice's parent, and `Simple` reads its first-set bitmap once per split and skips the class test when that bitmap is the class (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 7). Typical-cell suite (output/cellbench, `--vary`, perf `instructions:u`, best of 3, base 30a9d3a21): 6,270,053 -> 6,167,997 (-1.6%), sh 1,503,424 -> 1,401,358 (-6.8%), seq, json, edit, agent and the empty cell unchanged within 20 instructions. Outputs byte-identical for all six cells, test262 subset 2,535 and the fuel harness identical, `scripts/base.sh --check` passes, and the 10 djs benches move by +0.00% to +0.004% (layout). Cause, measured with callgrind on the sh cell: `l.split(/\s+/)` on a line of a split stdout cuts pieces from a `Slice`, which `alloc_latin1_range` refused (Str8 only) and `substring_slice` refused (a piece under `SLICE_MIN_LEN` of a string under `SLICE_PARENT_MIN_LEN`), so every piece went through `string::join` and `alloc_latin1_pieces`: about 375 instructions a piece, 588 pieces a cell. A slice's parent is a flat one-byte cell, so the copy reads `parent + off + a` directly (v1: sh -92,132). `Simple::search` (222 instructions a call) loaded the 8-word first-set bitmap from the program on every call and ran `in_ranges` on the first unit and on every unit of a `+` run. `Simple::of` now loads the bitmap once and compares it with the body's own bitmap below 256 (a CHAR or the CLASS ranges, word masks per range), and `exact` skips `matches` for one-byte input (v2: sh -9,934). Where the rest of the cell goes (callgrind, per sh cell after v2): `split_now` about 3.9k a split, `Simple::search` about 220 and `substring` about 217 a piece (`alloc_cell` 55 of it), regexp literal creation and the `@@split` pristine checks about 1.5k a split, and compile about 155k. Not changed: `json::parse::scan_one` (21% of the seq cell, 38k a tool result) already scans 8 bytes at a time and pays about 40 instructions an escape on stdout with an escape every 5 to 25 bytes, and `concat_int`/`concat` in the agent cell write through `Arena::split_mut` and its write barrier, which the GC lane owns.
- perf(cli): `scripts/build-cli.sh` reserves the original `.text` when non-lite BOLT reports `original .text too small` on the static agent. It reads the shortfall from BOLT's log (`<needed> bytes needed, have <have>`, rounded up to the reported alignment), relinks with `scripts/static-cli.py` and a fourth argument that adds a NOP-filled `.text.reserve` section (flag `R`, so `--gc-sections` keeps it) at the end of `.text`, and runs the same non-lite BOLT again. The `-lite` fallback stays for a shortfall that remains (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: code and rodata layout lane). Why: at 9452a7af3 the static link was 96,058 bytes short (322,810 with `-lite=0`), so the agent fell back to `-lite`, which keeps a `.bolt.org.text` copy of every function and leaves part of it hot (about 408 KB resident in 8 windows, mostly the ordered libc block with every ifunc variant and std). With the reserve (323,584 bytes) BOLT fits without a warning: the agent is 38,217,352 bytes instead of 44,879,560, with no `.bolt.org.text`. Measured on the hosted Hand with bench/cli (c7b57372d) under tools/localfs.sh and tools/netguard.sh, binaries interleaved, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh, per-section residency from /proc/<pid>/smaps: direct tool turn maxrss 5.41 to 5.31 MB (separate passes, n=9 and 6) and 5.51 to 5.46 MB (interleaved, n=6 and 3); tree PSS 7.82 to 7.47 and 7.70 to 7.56 MB; code-mode maxrss 8.46 to 8.37 and 8.43 to 8.41 MB. Resident direct-turn code: `.text` 1976 + `.bolt.org.text` 456 + `.text.cold` 472 KB before, `.text` 2028 + `.text.cold` 772 KB after. Refuted: `-align-functions=32` raised the requirement to 28,251,761 bytes. Not done: compressing cold rodata moves bytes into anonymous heap that `release_file_pages` never drops, so per-interval RSS cannot fall for data every request reads, and only cold objects gain, which ordering already moves away. Size-ascending rodata order inside the hot group and exec-shared before TUI-only groups in the order files are not measured. Only scripts changed, so no Rust or WebAssembly check applies. The end-to-end `build-cli.sh` run with the reserve step was not repeated after the manual reserve, BOLT and measurement runs.
- feat(tool-host): the last deadline reminder and the headless finish notice keep what the task's program built or set up, and the finish notice and the earlier reminders ask for a test on an input that differs from the given example (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench headline run 784946b4, claude-opus-5-5 high, wave 7f). Why: Nano scored 255/267 against Claude Code's 241/267, and 3 of Nano's 12 failed rows came from cleanup that the old texts asked for. Claude Code has no such text and passed these tasks 3/3. mcmc-sampling-stan #2 and #3 ended with `rm -f /app/hierarchical_model.rds`, the rstan `auto_write` cache of the compiled model that the analysis made, so the verifier compiled the Stan model from scratch inside its 180 s timeout and failed with "Timeout while validating Stan model structure" while every other test passed. configure-git-webserver #2 ran `rm -rf /var/www/site/*`, deleted refs/heads/master of the bare repository and ran gc to leave a clean state, and the verifier's push got HTTP 404. 6 rows failed on inputs the agent had not seen, after it tested only the given example: video-processing #1 and #3 (takeoff frame 227 and 241 on the hidden video against 219 to 223), train-fasttext #2 (0.635 on its own split, 0.567 on the verifier's data against 0.62), raman-fitting #2 (2D peak offset 1433 against 1239, with no robustness check of the fit window), filter-js-from-html #1 (66 attacks tested, one clean document, and the filter changed 3 of 12 clean files) and cancel-async-tasks #1 (the agent tested with a terminal, the verifier pipes stdout and sends SIGINT, so buffered output was lost and `test_tasks_cancel_above_max_concurrent` read ''). Not targeted: protein-assembly x2 and crack-7z-hash x1 (refusal fallback models, tasks that nanoeval's oracle marks unsound). What changed, in `nanocode-tool-host::deadline` only (shared by the Claude and Codex backends): `EARLY_REMINDER` adds "Test it on an input you made that differs from the given example, because the task's checks use inputs you have not seen." `LAST_REMINDER` is now "Finish now. Make sure every output the task asks for is in its final location. Delete only the scratch files and test output you made where the task's program or its checks write, read or wait for files, such as a file in /tmp. Keep what the task's program built or set up: caches and compiled artifacts (such as a compiled model or a build directory), installed packages, and the state the task asked for (repositories and their branches, served files, databases, services). Never reset or empty that state to make it clean. Stop background processes you started, unless the task asked to keep them running. Do not start a command or a wait that cannot finish in the time that remains." In `finish_notice`, the two cleanup points become three, and one point about unseen inputs comes before them: "The task's checks use inputs you have not seen (other files, data, sizes or seeds) and run the program as a script does: stdout piped, not a terminal, and signals such as SIGINT. The result holds on at least one input you made that differs from the given example, including the case the task names, and with stdout piped when output matters.", "The scratch files and test output you made where the task's program or its checks write, read or wait for files, such as a file in /tmp, are deleted, and nothing else is.", "What the task's program built or set up is kept: caches and compiled artifacts (such as a compiled model or a build directory), installed packages, and the state the task asked for (repositories and their branches, served files, databases, services). None of that state is reset or emptied to make it clean." and "Background processes you started are stopped, unless the task asked to keep them running." The /tmp example of the earlier stale-output fix stays, so the make-mips-interpreter and make-doom-for-mips checkers still get no old /tmp/frame.bmp. No other behavior changes. Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host`, again with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-tool-host -- -D warnings` pass. The effect on scores is not measured yet: the nanoeval lane measures it as wave 7f.
- docs(decisions): the pinned measurement of bench/cli's memory rows, and where the 5.61 to 7.13 MB spread between lanes comes from (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16). Nothing in the build changes. Binary: master 9452a7af3 from `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` (static glibc, BOLT, front sha256 2e90c5ed2d18b10f, agent a436e19504de6566). Harness: bench/cli at 00a297e98 on cli-bench, which adds the command's own `smaps_rollup` at its own sampled RSS peak (`own_peak_*`) beside the tree peak, since the tree peak of a tool turn also sums the shells it spawns (13.7 MiB direct). Method (`~/sw/pin/measure.sh <binary>` on the shared Hand): take a build-queue ticket and hold all four `~/sw/buildq.sh` slots, run `tools/localfs.sh tools/netguard.sh node harness/suite.mjs --parts=tools,oneshot --only=nc --steps=10` under `taskset -c 4` and `setarch -R`, 1 warm-up round dropped, 10 rounds kept, page cache warm. Canonical numbers, `ru_maxrss` in MiB, median (min to max, p90): direct 10-step tool turn 5.953 (5.891 to 6.016, 6.016), Code Mode tool turn 8.793 (8.699 to 8.949, 8.824), one-shot 4.605 (4.605 to 4.605, 4.605). Minor faults: 1,915 (1,903 to 1,923), 2,805 (2,796 to 2,819), 382 (378 to 383). Own smaps at the sampled peak, direct: Rss 5.56, Pss 5.55, anonymous 0.94, file 4.67 MiB; Code Mode: Rss 8.19, anonymous 2.68, file 5.51 MiB. Run to run, `ru_maxrss` spreads at most 0.25 MiB in every configuration, so one build under one method is stable and the lanes' 1.5 MB spread is between builds, harness copies and CPU sets. What moves it: the CPU set. The same binary on all 5 cores gives direct 5.578 (ASLR off) and 5.641 (ASLR on), Code Mode 8.574 and 8.637, so pinning to one core adds 0.31 to 0.38 MiB to direct and about 0.2 to Code Mode, and ASLR moves the median about 0.06 MiB. The sampled `own_peak_*` fields spread up to 0.97 MiB because a 2 ms sampler misses the short peak of a 10 ms one-shot; use `ru_maxrss` for comparisons and the smaps fields only for the split between anonymous and file pages. Compare builds only with the same method and CPU set, interleaved in one held window.
- perf(claude): a steer starts the Code Mode preemption under the steering lock and waits for it after releasing the lock (2026-11-15, steer tail latency lane). Before, `turn::accept_steer` awaited every `code_turn_preempt` hook while `steer_input` (and `driver::route` and the bound `Steer`) held `State::steering`. With a remote Code Mode host the hook is a `RemoteOperation::Preempt` request round trip, and `steer_preempts_model` bumps the model preempt watch before the hooks run, so the run loop aborted the model call at once and then waited in `consume_steering` for the lock until the hook's round trip came back: every steer that cut a model call short paid the host's round trip before its resend. Now `accept_steer` returns whether it queued the steer (`Result<bool>`, false for a repeated receipt or a durable duplicate, which did not preempt before either), and `State::start_code_preempt` builds each hook's future and polls it once while the lock is held, so a local host's preempt and a remote host's request are issued before `consume_steering` can run `settle_code_preempt` (the order the code-mode generation counter relies on stays as it was), then the caller drops the lock and awaits the rest. The steer call still returns after the hooks finish; only the lock is released earlier. Measured with output/steer-lat (a Claude agent with `steer_preempts_model`, a durable `DurableSession` over `MemoryStore` on its own store thread, a loopback mock Messages endpoint that holds every response open, 300 identified steers of 4 KB each 3 ms after each request arrives, a `code_turn_preempt` hook that sleeps for the simulated host round trip; reach is steer call start to the resend's arrival at the mock), on this 5-core shared hosted Hand at load 10 to 13, binaries interleaved per round, medians of per-run percentiles: 5 ms round trip (6 rounds) reach p50 9.49 to 3.68 ms, p99 40.3 to 29.0 ms, steer call p50 5.5 to 6.2 ms (unchanged: it still waits for the hook); 20 ms round trip (6 rounds) reach p50 26.0 to 4.6 ms, p99 59.2 to 34.0 ms; no hook (10 rounds, three-way with a variant that awaited the hooks after the lock without polling first) reach p50 2.79 / 2.98 / 2.87 ms and p99 31.8 / 32.3 / 32.2 ms, call p50 0.25 ms in all three, within noise. Also measured and left alone: the steering lock wait is about 2 us, the transcript clone in the preempt branch and `defer_cursor` take 10 to 60 us, and with `MemoryStore`'s driver on the caller's `block_on` thread (`spawn_local`) a commit costs about 1 ms, a harness artifact the store thread removes. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, agent/turn.rs, agent/driver.rs, agent/assemble.rs.
- docs(decisions): where a typical Code Mode cell's instructions go, measured with unthrottled sampling, and `CONCAT` taking Int32 parts measured and not shipped (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 6). Sampling: the dev host's `kernel.perf_event_max_sample_rate` was 2,750, so `perf record -c 50000` of 2,200 cells (about 4G instructions a second) kept about 4% of its samples, as `-c 2000` did before; with the rate at 100,000 and `kernel.perf_cpu_time_max_percent=0` (sudo sysctl) the per-cell sum of samples ((2,200 - 200 cells) x 50,000 / 2,000) matches `perf stat` within 0.5% (sh 1,498,725 against 1,503,473). Self instructions per cell by symbol group (output/cellbench, `--vary`, release, base 34d04947b; compile is every `compiler`, `lexer` and `bytecode` symbol): sh 1.50M (heap 339k, `run_hot` 280k, regexp 229k, the rest of the interpreter 210k, builtins 121k, compile 107k, json 44k, host 11k), agent 1.58M (`run_hot` 730k, heap 323k, interpreter 191k, compile 182k), json 1.32M (`run_hot` 302k, heap 234k, compile 222k, json 184k, interpreter 178k), edit 0.96M (json 141k, regexp 138k, compile 126k, `run_hot` 111k, heap 104k), the empty cell 82.8k (interpreter 26k, `run_hot` 14.5k, compile 12.7k, heap 9.7k, `memmove` 6.7k, host 5.4k). So compile is about 13% of the typical suite (sh, seq, json, edit and agent: 6,270,341 instructions): a compiler with no cost at all leaves about 5.5M, and the 4.0M goal needs the interpreter and the heap as well. Under perf the compile hot spots are `CodeBuf::encode` (13k to 31k per cell), `Parser::parse_lhs` (10k to 15k), `stack::walk` (8k to 19k), `resolve::emit_function` (8k to 16k) and `peephole::simplify` (5k to 12k): the per-instruction work of the two emits (phase 1, then the re-emit in `resolve::finish`), the peephole pass and the stack check, not the lexer (`next_token` 4k to 11k). Callgrind's 170k for the sh cell's compile counts `memcpy` and `memset` per byte. The compiler has no AST (the parser emits phase-1 code), so arena-allocated AST nodes do not apply; the structural bet left is one emit for a function whose names all resolve without captures. Not shipped: `Heap::concat_values`, a `CONCAT` (hot path and `Op::Concat`) that writes Int32 parts as digits in place instead of through `to_string`. Typical suite 6,270,341 -> 6,272,254 (agent 1,591,925 -> 1,593,972), outputs byte-identical. A template literal emits `ToString` after each substitution (compiler/expr.rs, template parsing), so `CONCAT` never receives an Int32. A `CONCAT` that converts its own parts would call an object's `toString` after later substitutions, which is observable.
- perf(claude): the token estimate after a tool round reads the new message's cached JSON instead of serializing it separately, so the next request's body reuses that JSON (2026-11-15, per-step cost lane). `run_rounds` estimated `active_context_tokens` from `serde_json::to_string` of the appended tool-results message, and `api_body` then serialized the same message again through `HistoryMessage::json`; `HistoryMessage::json` is now `pub(super)` and the estimate goes through it (same text, so the same estimate). Request bodies are byte-identical (output/step-lat DUMP, 90 requests, same sha256 as before the previous entry). Interleaved pairs against the previous entry on the hosted Hand (load 10 to 12, so latency is noise): instructions per request 1.516M -> 1.485M (6 turns x 30 steps, 10 pairs) and 1.593M -> 1.565M (3 x 100, 6 pairs), about -2%; step gap p50 0.570 -> 0.524 and 0.540 -> 0.574 ms, p90 1.564 -> 0.942 and 0.783 -> 0.811, p99 5.9 -> 9.5 and 10.4 -> 9.1. Measured and not changed (callgrind on output/step-lat after both entries, 239M instructions for 120 requests): `JournalState::checkpoint_payload` re-escapes every retained operation's inline payloads on each commit (6.5%, `serialize_within` through `collect_str`; 1.1% of server CPU in the production-shaped seq profile), `api_body` copies the cached system and tools raw values into each body (4.4%), and `cache_system_tail_with` rebuilds the system block array with its cache marker per request (2.8%). The Claude tool catalog (`dynamic_catalog`, 0.1%) and `SseState::decode` (about 1%) are too small in that profile to be worth a change. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent/{history,rounds}.rs.
- perf(durability): a sealed head carries a membership index of its sealed operation IDs (state format 10), so a resumed session accepts a new operation without loading its sealed receipt pages, and `AgentRuntime::open` reads only the head (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: session resume lane, wave 4). Before: `Driver::acquire`, `SessionStore::load` and `revised_summary` each loaded every sealed receipt page, because `Transition::OperationAccepted` refused any operation while a sealed receipt was unloaded, and `load` also read the input of every turn for `StoredSession::turns`. Now: `SealedReceipts.index` is a chain of Bloom filters written as base64 strings in the head. Filter i holds the IDs at sealed positions 16(2^i - 1) up to 16(2^(i+1) - 1), so the chain grows by doubling and the head holds about 2 to 4 bytes per sealed operation. Each ID sets 16 bits per ID with 11 probes (the probe count that minimizes false positives at 16 bits per ID, about 0.05% per filter), placed by double hashing of the BLAKE3 hash of the ID. The index only answers "absent": `JournalState::receipts_exclude` is true when every receipt is loaded or the index excludes the ID. The session driver loads every page before a command whose operation is neither in memory nor excluded, and before the commands that read all operations (`State`, `SteerReceipt`, `IdentifiedSteerAccepted`, `PruneReceipts`, `DiscardUnused`, `Abandonable`), so a repeated ID is refused exactly as before and a false positive costs the old full load. Receipts sealed while the pages are unloaded stay resident in the archive, and a later full load skips them by count (`resident`) and fails if the counts disagree. The session preview walks from the first page of the highest level down to the oldest receipt (one read per level) instead of loading every page, and the driver keeps it for the life of the acquisition. A driver with a terminal receipt limit, or with a write format below 10, still loads every page at acquisition. Format rules (as for formats 5 and 9): a head with the index is format 10, a head without it loads as before and gains the index at its first seal after a full load, `write_format` accepts 8 to 10 and drops the index below 10, and binaries without this change reject format 10 heads (`unknown field index` or `unsupported state format 10`) instead of reading them. `SessionStore::load_resumable(id)` returns a `ResumableSession` (record, latest checkpoint, unsettled turns) from the head without loading receipts or settled turns, and `prepare_resume_resumable` prepares it. `AgentRuntime::open` uses them, and `load`, `open_loaded` and `StoredSession` are unchanged. Measured with nc-lite `fast` builds (`CARGO_PROFILE_FAST_INCREMENTAL=false CARGO_PROFILE_FAST_STRIP=none`) of 64a264f22 and of this change, the bench fake Responses server and `perf stat -e instructions:u` per resume, one run per binary: 30 resumes of a fresh session, median 20.93M to 19.28M (first 10.21M to 10.00M, 30th 31.47M to 28.31M). With the index alone and `load` unchanged the median was 20.29M and the 30th 30.23M. 12 resumes of a `cp -a` copy of a 1,000-session store written by the old binary (format 9 heads, from /tmp/cli-bench-ws), rounds 3 to 12, median 15.99M to 15.26M, which also exercises the fallback load and the first index build. A 200-call `exec_command` session (`h=ncdirect`, 400 files in the workspace, 2.5 MB home), 5 resumes, median 186.92M to 183.53M. Growth per turn fell from 0.73M to 0.63M. What still grows with history at the 30th resume (perf record, samples with children): the JSONL journal parse in `Journal::open` (`refresh_index`, `consume`) 10%, record reads 9%, the zstd archive rewrite at exit 7% and the Codex history in `load_sequence` 6%. The flat targets need a store-level change (open the journal from a snapshot plus tail, as TurnLog does since 11363e57b) and history reuse, not more receipt work. Not done: handing the catalog's loaded state to the driver (plan item 2) is moot once neither loads receipts, and seeding `ContinuationCache` from `load_sequence` (item 3) was not attempted in this wave. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-durability-core, nanocode-durability and nanocode-agent, the first two also for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-durability-core -p nanocode-durability -p nanocode-agent -- -D warnings`, and 30 consecutive resumes plus the old-store resumes above without a failure. Files: crates/core/durability/src/{lib.rs,state.rs}, crates/runtime/durability/src/{branch.rs,catalog.rs,lib.rs,session.rs,state.rs}, crates/runtime/agent/src/runtime.rs.
- fix(sys): `send_descriptor` and `receive_descriptor` convert socket control lengths with a generic `fitted` helper, so `cargo clippy -p nanocode-sys -- -D warnings` passes on glibc and musl (2026-11-15). `msghdr::msg_controllen` and `cmsghdr::cmsg_len` are `usize` in glibc's libc bindings and `u32` in musl's, so each `try_into`/`usize::try_from` was an identity conversion on one of the two and clippy's `useless_conversion` failed the build on glibc (3 errors in `unix/mod.rs`, noted by the session resume lane, wave 3). `fitted::<T, U>` is generic in both types, so no call site converts a type to itself on either libc, and a length that does not fit its field still panics. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-sys -- -D warnings` and `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/core/sys/src/unix/mod.rs.
- perf(claude): an old tool result's cleared copy is kept on the message, so each request reuses its encoded JSON and digests instead of rebuilding them (2026-11-15, per-step cost lane). `clearing::clear_tool_results` clears old tool results on the request's copy of the history with `HistoryMessage::make_mut`, which gives the message a fresh entry every time: once a session passed the clearing threshold (more than 12 results and 20,000 cleared tokens), every request re-serialized every cleared message and recomputed its `MessageDigests` (blake3) in `api_body`, so per-request cost grew with the history. A message whose clearable results are all cleared now takes `HistoryMessage::cleared`, a copy built once and kept in the original entry's `cleared` slot (reset by `make_mut`), so its JSON, digests and wire id stay put across requests; a message cleared only in part (the one at the cutoff) is still copied per request. Callgrind on output/step-lat (a durable Claude agent with 20 function tools, a 50 KB system prompt and 3.3 KB tool outputs against a local SSE mock; 4 turns of 30 steps) put `HistoryMessage::digests` at 10.3% of instructions with 4,589 `MessageDigests::of` calls for 120 requests, every call a miss. Request bodies are byte-identical before and after (DUMP of 90 requests, 21,393,840 bytes, same sha256). Interleaved pairs on the hosted Hand (load 4 to 6), medians, step gap = mock's response end to the next request's arrival: 6 turns x 30 steps (10 pairs) p50 0.577 -> 0.466 ms, p90 0.690 -> 0.585, p99 0.857 -> 0.810, instructions per request 2.095M -> 1.514M (-28%); 3 turns x 100 steps (6 pairs) p50 0.646 -> 0.514, p90 0.847 -> 0.633, p99 1.088 -> 0.852, instructions 2.719M -> 1.593M (-41%). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude`, output/step-lat `perf stat -e instructions:u`. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent/{clearing,history}.rs.
- perf(cli), measured and not shipped: stacks and threads at the direct tool-turn peak, with boxing the exec root future's command futures, a lookup thread that exits after its job and releasing the unused stack at model calls (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: anonymous memory wave 2, stacks and threads). Method: static dist+BOLT `scripts/build-cli.sh` builds, bench/cli c7b57372d `suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --toolrounds=2` under tools/localfs.sh and tools/netguard.sh, 3 interleaved passes (n=6 per binary and mode), a wrapper around NC_BIN that polls the agent's /proc/pid/smaps_rollup every 0.3 ms and at the RSS peak reads smaps, each thread's stack pointer and VmHWM (the process alone; its children held 0 KB anonymous at every peak), plus a perf `page-faults -c 1 -d` profile (with `--call-graph=dwarf,65528` for chains) to attribute first-touch stack pages. On 988526ff7 (worker runtime): direct turn Anonymous at the peak 1,120 KB median (maxanon 1,266 KB), of which the private copies of the static binary's writable data are 40 KB (104 KB with PIE and shared libc before), `[heap]` 20 KB, main stack 72 KB, worker stack 104 to 108 KB, the rest allocator segments; threads at the peak main, worker, blocking, lookup, mpp-forward-proxy, psh-engine and sometimes psh-ready. The main stack was `run_with` (24,088-byte frame), `Runtime::block_on` (20,536, it pins the root future) and `run_with::{closure#4}` (20,376), because the root `async` block holds every command's future in one union. The worker's deepest point came once, during agent construction (`nanocode_cli::exec` 14,120, `Host::build` 11,464, `CodexHarness::build::{closure#3}` 42,184, `spawn_agent_driver` 12,968, `prepare_tools`), and each step reached 77 to 84 KB through `AgentDriver::run::{closure#0}` 26,656, `ModelRun::drive_session` 9,608, `execute_task` 6,872 and `ShellSessions::execute` 10,552. Tried on 988526ff7, all three together: `Box::pin` of each command arm in the `block_on` root (frames `run_with` 9,160, `block_on` 3,176, `closure#4` 11,416), a zero keep-alive for the lookup pool, and `release_unused_stack` (`MADV_DONTNEED` from the low end of the current thread's stack to one page below the caller, from `pthread_getattr_np`) after `release_file_pages` at model calls 1, 2, 4, 8: direct Anonymous at the peak 1,120 to 1,022 KB, maxanon 1,266 to 1,168 KB, VmHWM 5,876 to 5,648 KB, main stack 72 to 32 KB in all 24 samples, no lookup thread at the peak; Code Mode Anonymous 2,732 to 2,644 KB. Not shipped, because master moved under it: 08a782ec0 runs exec on a current-thread runtime (no worker thread; the whole agent runs on the main stack), 34a3ba226 removed the lookup pool, and b1bc87b72 boxed the mpp, durability and login futures. Rebuilt on 34d04947b with the boxing and the stack release (at `model_call_started`, now on the main thread): direct Anonymous at the peak 872 to 874 KB, maxanon 1,082 to 1,066 KB, VmHWM 5,446 to 6,048 KB, Code Mode Anonymous 2,566 to 2,532 KB and VmHWM 8,432 to 9,308 KB, threads at the peak 4 to 5 (main, blocking, mpp-forward-proxy, psh-engine, psh-ready). The main stack is 116 to 128 KB on both (29 to 31 first-touch pages against 27 to 30), its page faults doubled with the release (53 to 56 against 100 to 117, every step refaults the released depth), and the release cannot reach the frames still live under `block_on`, so neither change is worth its cost on current master. Also measured and not changed: the 197 KB `psh_utils::WITHOUT_GIT::wrap` and 52 KB `run_external_with` frames exist only in the release build; in the dist build (`opt-level = "s"`, fat LTO) no `wrap` frame reaches 4 KB, `run_external_with::{closure#0}` is 4,440 bytes and the psh-engine stack is about 28 KB; the blocking thread at the peak runs the process warm-up and the MPP proxy start (lane 109's), and a shorter keep-alive for the shared blocking pool would start a thread per blocking call. Current state: direct Anonymous at the peak 872 KB median against the 0.8 MB target; the next cut is the main-stack chain of agent construction and the step loop (`CodexHarness::build::{closure#3}` 42 KB from by-value moves of the agent builder, `AgentDriver::run::{closure#0}` 26.6 KB from the inline body of the driver loop), which needs those functions split, not boxed callees. Harness: ~/sw/anonstk (peak.py, pf.sh, pfstack.py, cg.py, frames.py), removed after this entry.
- docs(decisions): the paying proxy's per-process certificate authority measured in tool turns, and a table-free P-256 base multiplication measured and not shipped (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track). Method: static dist builds from scripts/build-cli.sh of 9f4f5c77b (base) and of base with graviola's secret `base_multiply` computing `k*G` through the runtime w5 window (`multiply_w5` over `public_precomp_w5` of the generator, 1.5 KB on the stack) instead of constant-time selects over the 151 KB `CURVE_GENERATOR_PRECOMP_W7` table. bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=tools --toolrounds=2` under tools/localfs.sh and netguard, 5 interleaved passes of 4 lanes (each build with the proxy, and without it through `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/dev/null`, which `OWN_PROXY_SETTINGS` treats as a session's own CA bundle), the nanocode process sampled every 0.3 ms from smaps_rollup with VmHWM and pagemap residency per ELF section at the sampled peak. Medians of VmHWM, proxy on and off: base direct 10.89 and 11.15 MB, base code-mode 14.58 and 14.48 MB, w5 direct 11.52 and 11.75 MB, w5 code-mode 14.93 and 15.22 MB. The proxy costs no measurable peak (-0.26 to +0.10 MB, inside the pass-to-pass spread) because it starts at the first `exec_command`, after the process has passed its peak: in the direct lane no sampled peak has the `mpp-forward-proxy` thread, and in the code-mode lane the thread is present with 28 to 44 KB of stack and no section moves by more than the noise. The 7.13 against 6.69 MB of the earlier note no longer reproduces on master. The w5 build moved every lane by +0.4 to +0.7 MB with or without the proxy (`.text.cold` resident 2.75 to 3.27 MB at the direct peak): that is the relink's layout, not the change, so the table-free path saves nothing at the peak and costs CPU: P-256 key generation 7.0 to 29.2 us (3,000 keys, results byte-identical to graviola 0.4.1 for random scalars, 1 and n-1, signatures verified by 0.4.1), about +22 us for every ECDSA signature the proxy makes per TLS handshake. Not shipped. Also not done, since the proxy is off the peak: Ed25519 for the CA (curl with GnuTLS and older clients refuse Ed25519 server certificates, and graviola has no Ed25519 signing), a bundle that references the system file instead of copying it (`std::io::copy` from file to file is `copy_file_range` on Linux and puts no bytes in the process), and a smaller proxy thread stack (only touched pages count). The startup MCP connections share no key-share code with the CA: they offer X25519MLKEM768 and X25519, and touch the P-256 table only when they verify an ECDSA P-256 signature (its public lookups read 37 entries in 37 separate 4 KB rows, so fault-around maps most of the table); under netguard no startup connection uses TLS.
- perf(process): the login environment probe of a bash login shell runs in psh inside the nanocode process instead of in `bash -lc` (`login::in_process`, `embedded::output`) (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: child processes out of the tool-turn peak). What: psh runs `shopt -s login_shell`, then sources `/etc/profile` and the first of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login` and `~/.profile` that exists (bash's own order for a non-posix login shell), then prints the mark and `command env -0`. Programs those files name are started directly by psh (posix_spawn), so no shell process starts. The bash probe still runs, as before, when the login shell is not named bash, when the launch environment holds a `PSH_` variable (psh takes those for itself), when `BASH_ENV` or `POSIXLY_CORRECT` is set after the profiles (bash would source `BASH_ENV` or skip the profiles), when psh writes anything to stderr, ends with a status other than 0 or prints no mark, or when no psh is embedded. Why: on master `exec_command` runs only through Code Mode, and every 10-step tool turn started `bash -lc`, which on this Hand started `locale-check`, `cat`, `tr` and `/usr/bin/env` (4 helpers at once); with localfs counting their libc and binary pages they added 6.7 MB to the tree peak. Parity: a 53-command exec_command sample (bench `ls`, ls -la, env | sort, env -0 digest, type of an exported function, $0, shopt login_shell, umask, exit codes, missing files, pipelines, externals such as uname, git, locale and python3, cd, ulimit) gives the same bytes from both builds apart from chunk ids and wall times, with an empty HOME and with a HOME whose `.bash_profile` sources the skeleton `.bashrc`, exports a function, uses arrays, `[[`, `$(...)` and `shopt -q login_shell`, and sets umask. psh serializes an exported function's body with its own layout, as it already did for every command, so the commands see the same value. Measured on the hosted Hand with bench/cli at c7b57372d, `tools/localfs.sh tools/netguard.sh node harness/suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --toolrounds=2 --only=nc`, `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` builds of 9f4f5c77b and of this change, 3 passes interleaved by build under ~/sw/buildq.sh (n=6 each, medians), base -> new: Code Mode tool turn tree RSS 21.34 -> 14.94 MB (nanocode's own peak 14.59 -> 14.62), PSS 13.99 -> 12.61, anonymous 4.88 -> 4.58, file-backed 16.46 -> 10.53, helpers 4 -> 1, CPU 2.01 -> 1.54 ms a step; the direct row, where `exec_command` is refused without Code Mode and starts nothing, is 11.34 -> 11.03 MB tree. The one helper left is `locale-check`. Refuted or left: running every profile through psh unconditionally (a profile psh cannot run would change the environment silently, so any stderr output or failure keeps bash); starting the probe at process start (a one-shot that never runs a command would then pay for a child); the 4.8 MB tree target, since nanocode's own peak in this turn is 14.6 MB.
- fix(psh): psh-os starts its `psh-wait` and `psh-kill` helper threads with the system's default stack instead of 64 KiB (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: child processes out of the tool-turn peak). Why: with the login environment probe in-process (the entry above), the first external a nanocode process starts from its own psh run (`/usr/bin/locale-check` from Ubuntu's `/etc/profile.d/01-locale-fix.sh`) starts a `psh-wait` thread in nanocode itself, and the BOLT-instrumented binary that `scripts/build-cli.sh` trains overflowed that 64 KiB stack in `waiter` (SIGSEGV on a stack probe 0x228 bytes below the stack, in all of 3 runs of `train-cli.py instrumented tools`), so the release build failed. The uninstrumented dist build fit, so the margin depends on code layout and no measurement backs 64 KiB. The default stack is reserved address space: only the pages a waiter touches are resident, and the bench rows below include it.
- perf(turnlog, code-mode, tool-runtime, agent): a Hand request's ledger row commits in the same transaction as the turn log's deferred settle (2026-11-15, per-step cost lane). `OneLog::barrier` returns a `RemoteBarrier` and turns on deferral: with `settle_durably`, a `Settle::Durable` state commit outside recovery buffers its rows and marks them owed instead of committing. Whatever leaves the brain next pays the debt first: a Hand dispatch (`RemoteCodeModeHost::barrier`, `RemoteTransport::request_after`/`call_after`, `RemoteLedger::sent_after`, `HandRequests::sent_after`) hands its ledger statement to `RemoteBarrier::carry`, which commits the owed turn-log rows and the statement in one SQL transaction (`LogHost::carry`, `TurnLog` `Lease::commit_carrying`, `SqlLog`'s `turn_log_carry`). That happens only when both use the same `Sql` host (compared by pointer); otherwise the debt is committed alone first, then the ledger row. Every default trait method pays the debt before it sends (`settle`, then the plain call), so a transport, ledger or host that knows nothing of the barrier stays correct. Direct tool calls settle in `effects::gated` (`EffectGate::settle`) before they run, and External ones already commit their `Call` row. `ToolRuntime` settles before every exec and wait unless its host carries the barrier (`CodeModeHost::carries_barrier`). A turn's end settles through `EventLog::flush` and `OneLog::settle_deferred`, which an embedder calls once a turn is done (the agent backend's flush does not reach the log). Crash semantics: the step's rows and the ledger row are durable together or not at all, so a dispatched request always has both its step and its row, and a lost step was never dispatched, so its model call runs again with nothing orphaned. A carried `extend` that finds itself fenced has already committed the ledger row: that row names a call the new owner's log never had, so it is never looked up and goes at the session's settle. nanocode-sim's hands scenario now runs a real `OneLog` over a host that holds both the log rows and the ledger in one store. Each call first commits its step durably, deferred, and then dispatches with `call_after`. The new invariant `folded` says the Hand never receives a request before its step is durable and its request is recorded. Restarts reopen the log, and a call whose step was lost is asked again, so the existing `once` check catches a silent replay. Mutations: `carry_drops_log` (carry commits only the ledger row), `carry_drops_request` (only the log rows) and `dispatch_unsettled` (dispatch without the barrier) are each caught by 1,996 of seeds 0..2000. Seeds 0..20000 pass with --twice, the existing five mutations are still caught, and turns 0..500 and store 0..300 pass. Measured in a production-shaped seq run (same pyramid2 server, before = master 6d4953bbb, after = this change, dev-georgios, PYRAMID2_SLOW_MS=0): durable transactions in the seq phase drop from 5,368 turn_log_append plus 3,288 hand_request_sent to 3,248 turn_log_carry plus 1,600 turn_log_append plus 40 hand_request_sent. Per-step span sum p50 drops from 1,625 to 1,474 us: model reply to tool call 368 to 86 us, and the call to the Bash call 517 to 654 us, since the carried transaction takes 200 us p50 against 137 for the ledger row alone. Plain interleaved seq runs at host load 10 to 20 (4 pairs) did not resolve the 0.15 ms: step gap p50 before 1.59, 2.19, 1.68, 2.32 ms, after 1.73, 2.22, 1.59, 2.22 ms. A first build had missed the turn-end settle, which left each turn's last state unsaved until the next dispatch. The SLOW run showed it (turn_log_append fell to 40), and it is fixed here.
- perf(djs): `decline_fast`'s `+` of a string and a primitive concatenates two strings directly and writes a string plus an Int32 (either order) as one flat one-byte string with the digits in place (`Heap::concat_int`), and tests for objects and symbols with tag checks instead of `Value::kind` (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 5). Why: in the agent cell, `'src/f' + i + '.rs'` (200 times) went through `conv::to_string` for both sides, which allocated a string cell for `i`, then `Heap::concat` (`resolve_str`, `str_len` and `str_is_two_byte` for each side, `write_leaves`), and `plain` called the out-of-line `Value::kind` twice: about 81k callgrind instructions in `to_string` and 14k in `kind` per cell. What: `concat_int` applies when the string is a flat `Str8` cell and the result is shorter than `ROPE_MIN_LEN` (the length below which `concat` copies too), so the result equals `concat(s, to_string(i))`; otherwise, and for every other primitive, the general path runs as before. Instructions per cell (output/cellbench, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, (1,200 - 200 cells)/1,000, best of 3, `--vary`, with the `try_has_finally` entry below, base the previous entry): agent 1,680,135 -> 1,593,473 (-5.2%), json 1,332,903 -> 1,328,861; djs bench err 653,202,116 -> 579,969,972 (-11.2%), the other nine within 0.02% or lower. Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/interp/run/hot.rs, crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/heap/string.rs.
- perf(djs): `try_has_finally` returns false at once when the source after the try block's `{` does not contain the bytes `finally` (`Lexer::rest`, `find_latin1`) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 5). Why: the parser asks before each try block whether it has a `finally` clause (D1080), and the scan tokenized the whole try block and catch clause a second time: about 20k callgrind instructions per sh cell (122 tokens through `Scanner::next`). A `finally` token needs those literal bytes, since an escaped reserved word is an identifier (`scan_ident_general`), so the answer is the same. Instructions per cell (as above): sh 1,521,652 -> 1,504,845 (-1.1%), seq 895,366 -> 884,323 (-1.2%), edit 963,320 -> 963,164; with the entry above the typical suite (sh, seq, json, edit, agent) 6,393,376 -> 6,274,666 (-1.9%), and 6,564,603 -> 6,274,666 (-4.4%) from 1c1bc9532. Rebased on 9452a7af3 (after the each_fused and tier1 for-of commits), both entries and the one-byte regexp entry below: sh 1,595,731 -> 1,503,496, seq 910,960 -> 885,000, json 1,336,078 -> 1,327,903, edit 1,037,330 -> 962,063, agent 1,679,571 -> 1,591,914, the suite 6,559,670 -> 6,270,376 (-4.4%); djs benches within 0.002% of 9452a7af3 except err (-11.2%); the test262 subset and fuel harness identical to 9452a7af3; scripts/base.sh --check passes. Each cellbench cell's printed output is byte-identical. Checked: test262 subset 2,535 passing, identical pass set; the fuel harness identical; djs-prelude's base remade with scripts/base.sh; `cargo clippy -p djs-core` natively and for wasm32 reports only the nine lints that master has (handlers.rs, Arena, Input, Caps). Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/compiler/scan.rs, crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/lexer/mod.rs, crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-prelude/base/base.rs.
- perf(djs): `Simple::search` on one-byte input scans with the first set's Latin-1 bitmap (`scan_latin1`), `star_settle` takes a lazy one-character loop over one-byte input in one byte loop (`star_settle_latin1`), and `split_now` and the one-byte path of `String.prototype.split` push their cuts and pieces inline into a preallocated list (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 5). Why: in the sh cell, `l.split(/\s+/)` over 100 `ls -la` lines spent about 110k callgrind instructions in `Simple::search`, which called `in_first` (a bounds-checked word read per byte) and then `in_ranges` (a binary search over the ranges of `\s`) for each character, and `split_now` grew its cut list from empty through the out-of-line `push_out` (about 38k perf-sampled per cell). In the edit cell, `/print\((.*?)\)/g` settled each lazy `.*?` one character at a time through `star_follows` and `single` (`next_char`, the follow-set binary search, the body match), about 130k callgrind with `Machine::run`. What: `scan_latin1` copies the 8 bitmap words once per search and tests each byte against them; a byte the bitmap rejects cannot match the body, since the first set holds every character that starts a match, so the `\s+` run only calls `matches` for a byte the bitmap accepts. `star_settle_latin1` runs when the input is one-byte, the `STAR` is lazy, forward and has a follow set (`F_CHECK`), and its body has no `F_ICASE`: it stops at the first byte in the follow set (or at the end with `F_END`) and fails where `single` would fail or at `max`, so its result and position equal the general loop's, which then finds the follow set at once. Neither path changes fuel accounting: `star_settle` charged no fuel per character before either. Instructions per cell (output/cellbench on the code-mode-engine native host, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, (1,200 - 200 cells)/1,000, best of 3, `--vary`, base 1c1bc9532): sh 1,597,952 -> 1,521,652 (-4.8%), edit 1,038,185 -> 963,320 (-7.2%), seq 910,453 -> 895,366 (-1.7%), json 1,336,862 -> 1,332,903, agent 1,681,151 -> 1,680,135; the typical suite (sh, seq, json, edit, agent) 6,564,603 -> 6,393,376 (-2.6%). Each cellbench cell's printed output is byte-identical. djs benches (djsrun, best of 5, loop, gen, gennext, find, forEach, some, filter, map, reduce, err) all equal or lower (filter -0.02%, map -0.01%). Checked: test262 subset 2,535 passing, identical pass set; the fuel harness (ten fuel/slice pairs over eleven scripts, including the split differentials) identical; djs-prelude's base remade with scripts/base.sh. Measured and set aside: under callgrind `__memset_avx2_unaligned_erms` is about 108k per cell (Arena::zero_ahead, mega_fill, intern), but `perf` counts its `rep stosb` as one instruction, so it is not a lever for this metric. - docs(decisions): per-step file pages after the power-of-two drops measured, and a steady-step text and rodata order measured and not shipped (2026-11-15, CLI file pages wave 2). Method: `perf record -e page-faults -c 1 -d -k mono` on the dist+BOLT agent of b5e824777 for a bench/cli 10-step direct tool turn (bench env, fixture server, netguard), with the drop points taken from the fixture's request arrival times; with fault-around each read fault on the binary maps one 64 KB window, so faults per section count the windows a step maps. Per interval the binary maps: startup to call 1, 68 windows (25 hot `.text`, 22 original rodata, 11 original text, 5 `.text.cold`); call 1 to 2, 84 windows plus about 3 MB of first-touch anonymous memory (the first tool call, the interval that sets ru_maxrss); calls 2 to 4 and 4 to 8, 71 to 72 windows each (31 of the 47 hot `.text` windows, 19 original rodata, 11 to 12 `.text.cold`, 7 original text: libc memmove, memset, writev and the drop's own dl_iterate_phdr and getauxval); 8 to exit, 73. The steady step is deterministic across runs and costs about 4.5 MB of file pages. The cold fragments a step runs in the bench and not in training come from environment differences (std env vars_os, Redactor::add, psh Vars::adopt, read_dir and run_compound cold blocks). Tried: train-cli.py `step` and `codestep` modes (one-step turns) and a steady-cli.py that takes every function whose instrumented count grows from the one-step to the ten-step turn (2,485 functions, 1.21 MB of hot text), with the training env given USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, TMPDIR, XDG_* and a second provider key. (a) steady functions first in the BOLT function order and steady rodata first in rodata-cli.py: the steady hot text became one 1.25 MB run and steady intervals fell from 71 to 58 windows (hot `.text` 31 to 21, `.text.cold` 12 to 8, rodata 19 to 18), but startup grew from 68 to 82 windows; bench/cli tools under localfs, three interleaved passes of 3 rounds against the TUI-drop build (n=9 each): direct ru_maxrss 5.84 to 6.00 MB, Code Mode 8.63 to 8.19 MB, CPU per step 1.75 to 1.56 ms direct and 1.95 to 2.02 ms Code Mode. (b) layered order (startup-only, startup and steady, steady-only, tools, Code Mode) with steady rodata after the startup rodata: direct 5.60 to 5.92 MB, Code Mode 8.31 to 8.25 MB (n=9 each). Neither lowers the direct turn's peak, because the peak is the first-call interval, where first-call-only code (lazy tool, shell and Code Mode setup) and the anonymous growth dominate and the steady order does not shrink it. Not shipped; scripts are unchanged. Next: shrink the call-1 interval (lazy work of lane 109, anonymous memory of lane 104), then reconsider the steady order, which saves about 0.8 MB per later step.
- perf(cli): the interactive terminal drops the binary's read-only file pages at the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 8th ... `ModelCallStarted` of the process, as `nanocode exec` does since b5e824777: `App::agent_event` and `stream_turn` share one `model_call_started` with the process-wide power-of-two counter (2026-11-15, CLI file pages wave 2). Measured (scripts/build-cli.sh dist+BOLT of b5e824777 against this change, a 10-step tool turn typed into the terminal through bench/cli harness/tui.py against the fixture server under tools/localfs.sh and tools/netguard.sh, three interleaved passes of 2 rounds per lane, medians, n=6 and 6): direct turn nanocode process ru_maxrss 9.43 to 7.98 MB, tree PSS 11.35 to 9.34 MB, file-backed 13.7 to 12.1 MB, anonymous 2.97 to 2.99 MB; Code Mode turn 15.34 to 13.66 MB, PSS 17.3 to 15.5 MB, file-backed 17.6 to 15.2 MB. CPU per step 2.16 to 2.34 ms direct and 3.2 to 3.4 ms Code Mode, within the spread of the shared host. `nanocode exec` is unchanged. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-cli` native and wasm32 and `cargo clippy -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` pass.
- perf(cli): the terminal interface starts the Tempo paying proxy the first time a shell command asks for its environment (`nanocode_process::prepare_commands`), as `nanocode exec` has since the 2026-11-14 one-shot entry, instead of on the `nanocode-paying-proxy` thread after its first frame (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: unneeded startup work lane). Why: `tempo::apart` ran `ForwardProxy::spawn` in every interactive process, which generates two P-256 keys and signs the proxy CA (graviola's 152 KB `CURVE_GENERATOR_PRECOMP_W7` table and the P-256 and x509 code become resident), copies the system bundle into the certificate file and starts the `mpp-forward-proxy` thread with its own runtime, whether or not the session runs a command. When a command runs, the proxy, its environment and its bundle are the same as before; the first command waits for the CA, about a millisecond. `tempo::apart` remains for non-Unix targets, where `prepare_commands` is not used. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 1 to 5 from other lanes), `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` at c34a38198 against the same tree with this change and the deferral below, bench/cli (c7b57372d) under tools/localfs.sh and tools/netguard.sh, binaries interleaved as lanes, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh. `--parts=firstframe --rounds=8`, RSS one second after the first frame: median 5.14 to 4.72 MB (range 5.03 to 5.19 against 4.68 to 4.79), PSS 5.13 to 4.71 MB, anonymous 1.28 to 1.18 MB. `--parts=tools --steps=10` (4 rounds, nanocode-agent peak RSS from a /proc pagemap and smaps_rollup sampler): the direct and Code Mode turns run a shell command, so the proxy starts in both builds and the rows do not move beyond the spread (direct 6.62 and 6.82 MB, Code Mode 9.78 and 9.75 MB). Measured and not shipped: (1) in the same build, `ForwardProxy::spawn` still generated the CA and wrote the bundle, but its thread waited in a blocking `accept` and built the proxy and registered the listener with its runtime only on the first connection; the direct tool turn moved anonymous memory 1.20 to 1.13 MB while file pages moved more with the changed layout, so the change showed no gain and was dropped. (2) A ceiling for the tool turn: the base binary with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` set, which disables the proxy entirely, gave direct 7.13 to 6.69 MB (file 5.88 to 5.60, anonymous 1.17 to 1.08) over 4 rounds, so about 0.44 MB of the direct tool turn is the proxy's CA, bundle and thread. The CA must be in the bundle before a child starts, since Node.js reads `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` at startup and OpenSSL clients load the bundle before a `NO_PROXY` connection, so deferring the CA to the first proxied connection would change behaviour. Without the proxy the generator table was still resident (139 KB median), from TLS key shares of the MCP connections at startup, and most other resident code the symbolized pagemap names (psh git and awk builtins, the PDF helper threads, gimli) is the 64 KB fault-around neighbourhood of executed code, not executed itself: no panic or backtrace runs in the turn (gdb breakpoints on `rust_panic` and `_Unwind_RaiseException` were never hit). Checks: `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli -p nanocode-mpp --no-deps -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-mpp -p nanocode-process --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, the bench tool turns exit 0 with 11 requests. Files: bin/nanocode/src/lib.rs.

Input tokens 29.9M against 32.0M. Same passes at lower cost, since requests after a served refusal go back to the main model's price. - feat(codex): the Codex backend takes a task deadline (`CodexHarness::deadline`, `CodexBuilder::deadline`) and acts on it like the Claude backend: reminders at 50, 75 and 90% of the limit with the same texts, sent as a user message after each tool round once 50% passed; `yield_time_ms` of a top-level `exec` pragma, `wait`, `exec_command`, `write_stdin` and `job_wait` capped to the time left with the same notice, or the call refused once the limit is reached; and one headless finish check with the Claude notice text when the root agent ends its turn before the 90% reminder. `Deadline`, `Reminders`, `Cap` and `finish_notice` moved from `nanocode-backend-claude` to `nanocode-tool-host::deadline`, and `nanocode_backend_claude::Deadline` and `nanocode_backend_codex::Deadline` re-export the one type (2026-11-15). Why: in Terminal-Bench run 908873c9 (gpt-6-luna high) Nano Codex scored 44/102 against the stock Codex CLI's 50/103, and its turns ended at 160 to 223 s with an admission of failure while most of the limit remained (circuit-fibsqrt 0/3 against 2/3, schemelike-metacircular-eval stopped at 223 s where the CLI passed at 500 s). The Codex backend read no deadline. Differences from Claude: the Codex finish check runs only when a deadline is set, so a session without one sends the same requests as before, and its once-per-turn flag lives in the turn loop beside the persistence nudge, not in a durable cursor. Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib` for nanocode-backend-claude and nanocode-backend-codex, and again with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for those, nanocode-tool-host and nanocode; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --no-deps -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-codex -- -D warnings` passes; for nanocode-backend-claude it reports one `redundant_clone` at `claude_tools.rs:710`, a file this change does not touch (Rust 1.100); `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli`. Harness `output/deadline-harness` against a mock Responses server (`mock.py`) that delays the first response 3.5 s and returns a custom `exec` call with `yield_time_ms` 60000, then a final message for every later request: with a 6 s deadline the turn sends 3 requests, the second carries the cap notice in the exec output (60000 ms ran as 2468 ms) and the 50% reminder, the third carries one finish check, and the turn ends after it; with a 3.8 s deadline the second request carries the 90% `Finish now` reminder and no finish check follows (2 requests); without a deadline both request bodies equal those of the same harness built at 777b22b3b byte for byte once UUIDs and the cell wall time are masked. The score effect on Terminal-Bench is not measured yet.
- perf(build): cut the serde code nanocode-code-mode instantiates (2026-11-15, release build-time lane djsllvm). (1) `ToolDefinition` (nanocode-types-core) derives with `remote = "Self"` and its `Deserialize` buffers into a `serde_json::Value` and decodes it in one non-generic `decode_definition`, so the internally tagged enum's content-buffering code is compiled once in types-core instead of again in every crate that deserializes it. (2) `RemoteFrame`'s fallback for frames whose `type` is not the first key re-serializes the collected fields with `type` first and decodes them through the same `from_str` path as every other frame (with the inner error's position stripped, so errors read as before), so `body` and every frame type are no longer instantiated a second time for the `Value` deserializer. `cargo llvm-lines --release -p nanocode-code-mode`: 722,605 lines before, 688,540 after (2), 668,673 after both (-7.5%); nanocode-backend-claude unchanged (1,145,684 vs 1,145,883). Interleaved release builds on a shared 5-core hosted Hand (load 3.5 to 6, -j8): code-mode `--timings` duration 10.78/9.05/8.14 s before and 9.61/8.39/8.06 s after; CPU time of a touched code-mode rebuild 24.1/22.1/24.7/23.4/23.3/24.6 s before and 24.3/21.9/22.2/22.3/23.3/21.2 s after (mean 23.7 to 22.5, -5%). Valid `ToolDefinition` input decodes identically (output/tooldef-check: values, field errors and messages compared with the old derive); on invalid input a duplicate key now takes the last value instead of failing with `duplicate field`, and tag errors (`unknown variant`, missing `type`) report the object's end position. Measured and not shipped: moving `Exec::call_intrinsic` out of djs-core's `interp::run` codegen unit (every `impl Exec` method lands in one CGU, the largest at about 3.1 s of 21 s LLVM time quiet) gave no measurable change on 5 cores and risks interpreter inlining; factoring `Atom::update`'s compare-and-swap into a T-only fn saved 1.7K lines (0.25%). djs-core has no generic hot spots (661,490 lines over 10,279 mostly single-copy functions).
- perf(psh): cut the LLVM work of psh-utils by keeping psh-engine's large async bodies out of it and by de-monomorphizing jq's iterator helpers and `UtilCtx::run_blocking` (2026-11-15, nanocode-cli cold release build lane pshllvm). An async fn's coroutine is codegened in each crate and CGU that awaits it, so psh-utils compiled about 67K LLVM lines of psh-engine (`run_external_with`, `nested::shell`, `run_chunk`, `run_text`, `spawn_program`, ...) through `UtilCtx::run_program`, `spawn`, `spawn_shell`, `search_path` and the blocking runner. Each of these public async fns now awaits a `#[inline(never)]` fn that returns the body as a `LocalBoxFuture`, so the body is coerced to `dyn Future` and codegened once, in psh-engine; the signatures stay the same and each call costs one more allocation. `run_blocking::<T>` boxes `f(ctx, arg)` as a `FnOnce` and runs one non-generic body instead of five instantiations, and jq's `map_with`, `flat_map_with` and `flat_map_then` box their closure only on the multi-item path, so the `Map`/`FlatMap` adapters are instantiated per item type rather than per closure. `cargo llvm-lines --release -p psh-utils`: 2,027,207 lines (31,576 copies) at b35581144, 1,895,506 (29,425) after (-6.5%); psh-engine lines inside psh-utils 67,335 to 14,859. psh-utils alone (`touch` lib.rs, `cargo build --release -j8 --timings`, 5-core shared hosted Hand, interleaved): base 27.94 s and 27.40 s, after 27.22 s and 25.51 s (mean -4.7%); rustc user CPU 65.1/64.1 s to 61.0/59.3 s (-6.5%). psh-engine: base 10.54/10.89 s, after 10.44/11.94 s (within noise). Measured and not shipped: placing each utility's `Box::pin` in its own module spreads the async bodies (all of them land in one CGU, the one that does the `dyn Future` coercion, which is the 12-18 s tail of psh-utils codegen) but every CGU then gets its own copy of the shared async helpers: serial LLVM time rose from 68.5 s to 109.1 s and the slowest CGU did not shrink (12.6 s to 14.9 s).
- perf(claude): the heaviest async bodies of nanocode-backend-claude are compiled once, in their own codegen unit, instead of copied into the codegen unit of every caller (2026-11-15, build speed lane backllvm). Why: rustc treats every closure and `async` body as cross-crate inlinable (`cross_crate_inlinable` returns true for `DefKind::Closure`), so a release build places a copy of each async body in every codegen unit whose roots reach it, and a method lands in the module of its self type; the `agent` codegen unit (rooted at `ClaudeBuilder`, `Driver` and `ClaudeNativeFactory`, all defined in agent.rs) pulled in most of the crate's async graph and held 396k of the 2.31M LLVM IR lines across the 16 units, 2.5 times the next one, so it alone set the end of LLVM (self-profile: its optimize plus emit took 16 to 21% of all LLVM time, against 1/16 for an even split). What changed: `ClaudeBuilder::build` moved verbatim to `agent::assemble::build`; the bodies of `Driver::{compact, submit, shutdown, route, cancel}` and `ClaudeNativeFactory::{spawn, fork, restore}` moved to free functions in `agent::driver` and `agent::factory`; `State::{run_rounds, request_response, call_tool, summarize_locked, accept_steer, append_developer_notice}` call free functions in `agent::{rounds, request, turn, context}` that return `AgentFuture` (`Box::pin(async move { .. })` of the unchanged body); `web::Side::{ask, search, fetch}` and `durability::format::{PagedConversation::restore, hydrate_snapshot}` return `AgentFuture` the same way; `AgentFuture` is `pub(crate)`. Each boxed future is a non-inlinable root, so its body is placed once, in its module's unit. Public APIs and behavior are unchanged; each of these calls allocates one box. Measured on this 5-core shared hosted Hand (load 4 to 8), -Csave-temps no-opt IR summed per codegen unit, master b35581144 against the change: total 2,306,147 to 2,206,653 lines (-4.3%), copies of inlined items 610,970 to 508,736, largest unit 396,256 to 238,772 (-40%, now 1.3 times the next, 177,680); `cargo llvm-lines` (one unit) 1,145,684 to 1,147,303. Self-profile of the crate, interleaved: largest unit's LLVM time / sum of all units' 8.6/44.8 and 21.7/102.3 and 19.7/93.0 and 7.1/40.2 before, 7.5/74.9 and 7.1/64.4 and 6.7/38.8 after (about 19% of the LLVM work in one unit before, about 11% after), which on 16 cores bounds the LLVM phase by the largest unit before and by about sum/16 after. `cargo build --release -p nanocode-backend-claude -j8 --timings` after touching it, interleaved base/new, crate duration: 23.2/13.9, 26.8/18.1, 16.1/20.9, 16.1/23.5 s, too noisy on 5 shared cores to show a difference, where the build is bound by total CPU rather than by the largest unit. Not done: upstream async bodies instantiated here (323k lines, for example `ClaudeClient::post_admitted` 3 copies of 7k, durability's `EncodedPayload` and session bodies) can be boxed where they are defined the same way, which would also take them out of nanocode-cli.
