What changed: the bodies of `Registry::{restore_missing, rehydrate, restore_inner, warm, thaw, await_restored}`, `{write_journal, journal_snapshot, fill_with, record_children, persist_durably, save_scope}`, `{attach_started, harness_turn_finished, launch_initial_turn, wake, stop_and_close, close_batch, close, hibernated, evict}` and `{deliver_message, observe_completions, publish_message_state, dispatch_parent, dispatch_parent_batch, route_completions}` moved verbatim to `#[inline(never)]` free functions in `runtime::{restore, journal, lifecycle, delivery}` that return `RegistryFuture` (`Box::pin(async move { .. })`, `BoxFuture` native and `LocalBoxFuture` on wasm), and the methods keep their signatures and await them; `Harness::{accept_delivery, start_turn}` the same in `harness::turns`; the public `SubagentControl::{send_user_message, interrupt, close, set_budget, budgets, agents, agents_page, session_id}` and its `active` and `lease_side_question` the same in `runtime::focus::control` (`send_user_message` converts `body` with `into` before it awaits), and `SubagentControl::{close_all, deferred_resume, resume_restored, discard_restored, cancel_all}` in `runtime::lifecycle`, because nanocode-cli instantiated about 106k IR lines of `SubagentControl` coroutines (clillvm lane); the private free fns `tools::{spawn_parent, start_child, build_unstarted, start_unstarted}`, `runtime::{journal_writer, continue_root}` and `durable::{read_leaves, load_leaves, load_cold, verified}` return the boxed future in place; in nanocode-agent-core `Agent::{resume_turn, resume_interrupted, resume_turns, claim_seed, claim_request, admit, abandon_created}` and `AgentHandle::{spawn_with_host_context, restore_runtime}` call boxed bodies in `agent::handle::resume` (`HandleFuture`). Public APIs and behavior are unchanged; each of these calls allocates one box. `Sequencer::enter` (nanocode-sync, 3 copies of 1.2k) is not boxed: its fast path takes no allocation today. Measured on this 5-core shared hosted Hand, master cc4f9a403 against the change: -Csave-temps no-opt IR summed over the 16 units 2,220,052 to 1,969,756 lines (-11.3%), largest unit 284,750 to 154,140 (-46%, now 1.01 times the next, 152,591) before boxing `SubagentControl`, and with it 2,029,738 total (-8.6%) and 155,656 largest (-45%), the extra lines being the `SubagentControl` bodies now compiled here once instead of in nanocode-cli; `cargo llvm-lines --release -p nanocode-subagents` (one unit) 1,067,737 to 1,065,587; `cargo build --release -p nanocode-subagents -j8 --timings` after touching agent-core and subagents, 5 interleaved base/new pairs at load 2.4 to 4.1, nanocode-subagents duration 17.8/15.1, 15.6/12.9, 16.0/13.1, 15.2/13.4, 16.5/14.4 s (median 16.0 to 13.4 s, -2.6 s, -16%), nanocode-agent-core 1.4 to 2.3 s either way. Checked: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-subagents -p nanocode-agent-core -p nanocode-cli` (native; no wasm target on the Hand).
- perf(cli): `nanocode exec` runs on a current-thread runtime, so the one-shot's tasks, store drivers and reactor run on the main thread inside `block_on` and no `nanocode-worker` thread starts; the terminal interface and the other commands keep the one-worker runtime (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: one-shot kernel instructions, wave 4). Why: exec's main thread only waited in `block_on` for `on_worker(exec(...))`, while the worker did all the work, so the worker cost a clone, a 2 MB stack, an 8 MB allocator segment mapping with two munmaps, its own partly used allocator pages per size class, and cross-thread wakes at the end. Checked with the change: the bench tools part (10 tool steps, 11 requests, exit 0, twice) and the one-shot; `exec` without `--ephemeral` and then `exec --continue` resume the same session id. Result: 1 thread instead of 2 until exit, 205 strace lines instead of 225, page faults 339 to 311. Measured with the entries above, 8 interleaved passes of 12: kernel instructions pass medians 2.29M to 2.32M before, 2.16M to 2.19M after (every pass lower), user instructions 3.39M to 3.35M. Cumulative for the three wave 4 entries on the static dist build: 2.63M to 2.18M kernel instructions (target 2.4M), 357 to 311 page faults. Left: when `block_on` returns, `Reactor::exit_driver` starts the `nanocode-reactor` fallback thread because no driver is left, just before `exit_group`. Measured and not shipped in this wave: `madvise(MADV_POPULATE_READ)` over the hot text or the first read-only segment, replayed offline with the one-shot's 82 file fault addresses on the static binary (a C harness that maps the binary's segments at their addresses and touches each address, median of 5): 0.82M kernel instructions with plain fault-around, 1.30M with the whole hot `.text` populated, 1.04M with its first half, 2.13M with the first read-only segment, because populate maps pages the one-shot never touches. The kernel has no transparent huge pages here, so huge-page aligned text has no effect.
- perf(process): `ShellSessions` finds the login shell (`nanocode_home::shell::login_shell`: the passwd entry's shell, else the first of /bin/bash, /usr/bin/bash, /bin/zsh, /bin/sh that exists) at the first command that asks for a login environment, not when the sessions are built (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: one-shot kernel instructions, wave 4). Why: every agent start read /etc/passwd (about 63k kernel instructions on the hosted Hand's virtiofs root) and stat()ed /bin/bash twice, also in a one-shot that runs no command. A command that asks for a login shell gets the same answer as before, once per process. Result on the bench one-shot: no /etc/passwd read and no /bin/bash stat, 225 strace lines instead of 255. Measured with the entry above, 8 interleaved passes of 12: kernel instructions pass medians 2.38M to 2.42M before, 2.29M to 2.32M after (every pass lower), user instructions 3.41M to 3.39M.
- perf(executor): a Linux name lookup reads /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf on the calling thread (`dns::System::load`), and reuses the last parsed copy while both files keep the same device, inode, size, modification time and change time (one statx each); the `nanocode-lookup` blocking pool and the `System::request` ticket are gone (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: one-shot kernel instructions, wave 4). Why: on the hosted Hand /etc is on virtiofs, where an open, fstat, read and close of /etc/hosts costs about 47k kernel instructions and a stat about 2.8k (microbenchmark, `perf stat -e instructions:k`, 100 iterations), and a thread start and join about 38k. The bench one-shot read both files twice (two of its four startup lookups started after the first read) and ran the pool thread (clone, 2 MB stack, allocator segment, exit) for that. The stamp check is the freshness rule glibc applies to resolv.conf: a lookup never uses a copy of a file that changed after it was read. LOCALDOMAIN and RES_OPTIONS are read with the files, so a change to them alone is seen at the next file change. Result: 2 threads instead of 3, one read of each file and 6 statx, 255 strace lines instead of 262. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 2 to 4 from other lanes) with `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` (dist, static glibc, BOLT) of 1c1bc9532 and of each change, bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=oneshot --only=nc` under tools/netguard.sh with `NC_BIN` wrapped in `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults` (~/sw/k3/ab.sh), 8 interleaved passes of 12 of the four builds, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh: kernel instructions pass medians 2.61M to 2.66M before, 2.38M to 2.42M after (every pass lower), page faults 357 to 341, user instructions 3.30M to 3.41M.
- perf(code-mode), measured and not shipped: releasing the embedded bootstrap image's pages with `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` right after the per-tool-set snapshot is derived, and where the bimodal Code Mode peak and the remaining anonymous gap come from (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: Code Mode tool-turn memory, wave 2). The change: a `nanocode_sys::unix::release_static(&'static [u8])` that advises the page-aligned interior of a static byte range away, called in `build` (crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/cell.rs) after `Snapshot::derive` when the image loaded with `Snapshot::from_static`. Why it was tried: `derive` copies the 318 KB build-time image into an instance and nothing reads the image again, but its `.rodata` pages stayed resident. On 2a533981c (static glibc) it worked as intended: dist+BOLT builds of 2a533981c and the change in one target directory (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 LLVM_BOLT=/usr/lib/llvm-23/bin/llvm-bolt scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode`), 10 interleaved passes of bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc --toolrounds=4` on the Code Mode harness (bench/cli b7396a9431) and the direct harness (benchd), each pass also with two smaps-sampled runs per row (peak of `/proc/pid/smaps_rollup`, sampled every 0.3 ms): Code Mode peak RSS median 10.00 [9.62-10.38] to 9.73 [9.29-10.04] MB (n=40), direct 7.57 to 7.59 MB; at the Code Mode peak (n=20) file PSS 8,519 to 8,178 KB (-341 KB, the image) and anonymous 1,960 to 1,964 KB. After b5e824777 (exec drops every read-only `PT_LOAD` at model calls 1, 2, 4 and 8) the image's pages go away at the next such call anyway, and the same A/B on 11363e57b against the change rebased on it measures nothing: Code Mode 7.93 [7.69-8.23] to 7.91 [7.64-8.39] MB, direct 5.61 to 6.11 MB (the direct turn runs no Code Mode code, so its +0.5 MB is this pair's BOLT layout), file PSS at the Code Mode peak 6,095 to 6,389 KB against 4,658 to 5,113 KB on the direct turn. So it was not shipped. The bimodal Code Mode peak (about 11 against 22 MB in earlier runs) is the harness's process-tree metric, not the RSS of nanocode: in the ~/sw/heapprof and ~/sw/struct results the rows with `tree_max_rss_mb` about twice `max_rss_mb` are exactly the rows where the sampler saw a child (`helpers_max` 1 or 5), because `/proc/<child>/statm` counts a child that still shares the parent's memory before `execve` at the parent's full RSS; `max_rss_mb` was 11.1 to 11.6 MB in both modes. In every Code Mode run of this lane (10 and 50 steps; 1, 2 and 5 CPUs; on 9f4f5c77b, 2a533981c and 11363e57b; more than 200 turns) the turn starts no child (`helpers_max` 0) and `tree_max_rss_mb` equals `max_rss_mb` within 0.2 MB, so no high mode is left in nanocode. Pinning to 1 or 2 CPUs moves the Code Mode peak by 0.5 MB at most (11.67 MB on 5 CPUs, 11.12 on 1, 11.18 on 2, on 9f4f5c77b), and 50 steps add 0.8 MB; both stay unimodal. Transparent huge pages were a candidate for a 2 MB-step mode on other machines, but the kernel of the hosted Hand has none (`/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage` is absent), so this was not measured; the allocator's 4 MiB-aligned segments are eligible on a kernel with `enabled=always`. The remaining anonymous gap at the peak (1,703 against 1,104 KB on 11363e57b) is the two heap copies that only Code Mode has: the `Vec` of the derived image (452 KiB mapped, 344 KB resident) and the instance arena (900 KiB mapped, 380 KB resident: the image and the cell's allocations); the allocator segments, stacks and threads (4 at the peak) match the direct turn. The derived copy goes away only if the tool definitions run per cell on the static image, which costs about 740K instructions per cell while `Object.defineProperty` of djs (a TypeScript builtin in crates/patches/djs/builtins/object.ts whose `ToPropertyDescriptor` does six `HasProperty`/`Get` walks and builds a descriptor record) costs about 270 fuel per call.
- perf(claude): a root, fork or side conversation on the subscription wire writes the prompt cache with the 5 minute TTL, and the 1 hour TTL stays for a session built with `cache_one_hour` or one whose cache outlived 5 minutes (`outlived_cache`) (2026-11-15, Nanocode cost-per-pass lane). Why: d03201ef7 made every subscription root write 1 hour caches, which Opus 5.5 bills at 2x input ($8/M) against 1.25x ($5/M), before 6f49aa8cf added the max_tokens 0 refresh that keeps a 5 minute cache alive across a tool wait or an idle pause (a root refreshes while idle and in a tool call, at most `cache_refreshes` = 25 times, at 0.05x each). Claude Code 2.1.318 on the same subscription route in nanoeval run 9091940d wrote only 5 minute caches (its stream usage: 3,089,109 `ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`, 0 `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` over 32 attempts; 2.1.325's `rNe` returns `live_5m_cache` while the last main-thread request is under 5 minutes old). Measured offline by replaying every recorded request of the 32 nano attempts of 9091940d (agent/model-requests.jsonl, 722 requests) through a pricing calculator at nanocode's own Opus 5.5 rates ($4 input, $0.20 cache read, $5 and $8 cache write, $20 output; Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 fallbacks at $5/$0.50/$6.25/$10/$25): before (1 hour writes) $27.73, which reproduces the attempts' reported `estimated_cost` to $0.0001 ($25.1141 against $25.1142 over the 29 costed attempts); after, with a refresh before each of the 14 waits of more than 300 s (14 refreshes, no lapse) $23.79, $0.895 to $0.767 a pass (-14.2%); after, with no refresh at all (every such wait rewrites the prefix at 1.25x and `outlived_cache` turns the session to 1 hour) $27.14, -2.1%. Every attempt costs less in the refresh case (a00007 2.707 to 2.174, a00009 2.873 to 2.404). The same replay on wave 7b c1a0e7a4 gives $0.530 to $0.464 a pass and on wave 6 1fbd4a11 $0.503 to $0.434. Requests, prompts and outputs are unchanged, so the pass rate is too: only `cache_control.ttl` and the refresh requests differ. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (one existing dead_code warning in environment.rs). Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs.
- feat(codex): `--lean-tool-arguments` (opt-in, `ModelConfig::lean_custom_tool_arguments`) offers a custom model `exec_command` with only `cmd`, `workdir` and `yield_time_ms`, and `write_stdin` without `max_output_tokens` (2026-11-15, DS output lane). Why: in the live Workers AI run cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0316, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on nc-codex (24 trials, 8 tasks) filled `justification`, `login`, `max_output_tokens`, `prefix_rule`, `sandbox_permissions`, `shell` and `tty` with their defaults in 501 of 714 `exec_command` calls. The served shell removes `justification`, `prefix_rule` and `sandbox_permissions` before it runs a command, and the tool output limit caps `max_output_tokens`. A one-call, low-reasoning turn with these arguments emits a median 300 output tokens (n=111), against 162 without them (n=58), at the same command length. A least-squares fit over 558 turns gives 87 output tokens for the seven fields and 30 for each of `workdir`, `yield_time_ms` and `max_output_tokens`. Stock Codex CLI shows the same pattern (287 against 170). Replay estimate: about 60k of 558k output tokens, 6% of output dollars, and about 8% of $/pass with the replayed arguments as uncached input. Reasoning is 73% of output characters, assistant text 2%, rewrites of a written file 0.1%, repeated reasoning sentences 0%, and no call reaches the 65,536-token proxy cap (max 25,838). `reasoning_effort: minimal` on Workers AI returns no reasoning, the same as `none`. Without the flag, the tool definitions are unchanged. Checked with `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` (native and wasm32), `cargo clippy --no-deps -D warnings` on nanocode-backend-codex and nanocode-cli, and `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Analysis scripts: hosted Hand `~/hill/analysis/dsout/`.
- perf(digest): BLAKE3 compresses each single block with SSE4.1 row vectors on x86_64, and measurements of the nc-lite `--continue` path that refute four other ideas (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: session resume lane, wave 3). Before: `ChunkState::compress_block` and `Output` ran the scalar `compress` for every 64-byte block, and records shorter than one 1024-byte chunk never reached the multi-lane `Blake3Instructions` paths, so the payload key checks of a resume spent most of their time there (13% self time of a 30-turn resume). Now: `nanocode_sys::blake3::compress` holds the four state rows in SSE4.1 registers (message permutation by shuffles and blends, diagonal rounds by lane rotation) and `nanocode_digest`'s `compress` calls it when `is_x86_feature_detected!("sse4.1")` holds, else the scalar code runs (wasm32, aarch64 and older x86_64 parts). Digests are unchanged: `output/b3check` hashed 2,113 inputs of 0 to 69,999 bytes and all matched the Python `blake3` 1.0.11 package; on 20,000 hashes of 64 to 963 bytes, `instructions:u` fell from 295.40M to 100.22M (three runs each, spread under 0.01%). nc-lite `fast` builds (`CARGO_PROFILE_FAST_INCREMENTAL=false CARGO_PROFILE_FAST_STRIP=none`) of b35581144 and of this change, the bench fake Responses server, `perf stat -e instructions:u` per resume, one session per binary: 30 resumes of a fresh session, median 23.67M to 21.86M (first 11.04M to 10.69M, 30th 34.80M to 32.03M); 12 resumes of a `cp -a` copy of the 1,000-session harness store, rounds 3 to 12, median 17.77M to 16.93M; a 200-call `exec_command` session (1.70 MB request), 5 resumes, median 137.65M to 132.78M. Request bytes were equal in every pair. Measured and not shipped: (1) A process-wide map from payload key to a `Weak` of verified content in `EncodedPayload::load_records`, so a second load of the same record skips `key_matches`: 30 resumes, median 23.48M to 23.94M (+2%). Each loader drops its payloads before the next one runs, so the weak entries never upgrade, and `strace` of one resume counts 225 record reads for 162 records, so the loaders read nearly disjoint records and duplicate hashing is not the cost. (2) Record collection at archive: in a 30-turn journal (247 KB, 128 lines) all 162 records are reachable from the head through `latest_checkpoint` and the sealed receipt levels, so collection frees nothing. The superseded part is the 1 to 1.8 KB payload rewritten twice per turn (about 110 KB). `superseded()` compares it with all live records (137 KB) and never compacts, and compacting at every archive costs about what the next replay saves, since the archive rewrites the journal anyway. (3) The journal growth is legitimate data: each turn adds a receipt page, a checkpoint head and three history items, and `Driver::acquire` and `SessionStore::load` hydrate every sealed receipt because `Transition::OperationAccepted` requires `unloaded == 0` to refuse a repeated operation id. A flat resume cost needs that check answered without loading every receipt (for example an operation id index in the head), which is a durable format change. (4) Benchmark setup: the fake server's `steps` mode finds no tool for `h=nclite` because nc-lite sends its tools inside `additional_tools`, and the request then fails with "connection closed before message completed", so 200-call sessions use `h=ncdirect`; the harness store resumes only from its own workspace (`/tmp/cli-bench-ws`), and the first resume of a `cp -a` copy rebuilds the brief index (192M). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-sys and nanocode-digest natively, for wasm32-unknown-unknown and for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu; `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-digest -- -D warnings` stops at three `useless_conversion` errors in sys/src/unix/mod.rs that this change does not touch. Files: crates/core/sys/src/blake3.rs, crates/core/digest/src/blake3.rs.
- perf(turnlog): a snapshot writes each state's records as its own section rows before the head row, and `TurnLog::open` reads only the head and the tail; a state's sections load when it is first read (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 lane partsnap). Why: open inflated, parsed and applied the whole snapshot, so it grew with the number of children (measured with an openprof harness over `MemoryLog`, one core, kill-at-50% scale-bench logs: at 10K 4,659 rows, 123 MB plain, inflate 216 to 359 ms, record parse 537 to 751 ms, open 466 to 596 ms; at 100K 47,066 rows, 1.15 GB plain, inflate 2.0 to 2.6 s, parse 4.2 to 5.2 s, open 4.70 to 5.61 s; stored 66%, checkpoints 26%, cells 7%, open calls 0.5%, all of them per child or per registry page). Each record has an owner: a Checkpoint and a Stored key without a `b3:` content name belong to the state, a Cell or Forget to its session, and a `b3:` content record to the state's content owner (`<state>\\n`). A snapshot commit packs the changed owners into section rows (tag `p`, one deflate stream per group, a group closes once it reaches the 32 KB deflate window) at the seqs before its head row, and the head carries one `Record::Section` per group with its row range and its owners. `host.load` starts at the last `s` row, so the sections are never in the open path. A binary without this change rejects `Record::Section` as an unknown record instead of opening a log without its sections, and an old log opens as before and writes sections at its next snapshot. State owners are rewritten when they change, and the groups nobody references any more are dropped in the same append (`Compaction.superseded`). Content owners only append, since a content key never changes value. A record for a state that is not loaded waits in that owner's pending list and applies after its sections. `TurnLog::load_owner`, `TurnLog::read_owner` and `Lease::load_owner` scan a state's groups and also load every other unloaded owner whose only section is in a scanned group. `OneLogStore` loads the state before every read and write, `list_states` lists unloaded states from the head, and the code-mode stored blob moves to `<session>\\n$nanocode_stored` (the old key is still read) so it stays in its session's section. A snapshot is due when the tail passes `snapshot_ratio` times the head, the part open reads, and `snapshot_ratio` times the tail is at least the packed size of the state owners it rewrites, so rewriting a large state (the root session's cells) costs at most `snapshot_ratio` times the tail it replaces. Measured (same harness, one forced snapshot of the base log, then three opens per run, two runs each): open at 10K 21.8 to 41.6 ms (head 1 row, 337 KB, 3.5 MB plain: 15,022 open calls and 1,680 section records) and at 100K 121 to 152 ms (head 2.1 MB, 9.4 MB plain: 50,028 open calls 6.3 MB and 16,679 section records 3.1 MB). Loading every state after that took 766 to 864 ms at 10K, about the old open. What is left in the head is the open calls and the owner index. End to end (scale-bench restart from a kill-at-50% log, one core, `--workers 1`): at 10K on ba3deec20 the turn log opened in 34 to 52 ms against 628 to 801 ms and the first provider call came 0.83 to 1.13 s after open against 1.12 to 1.38 s (three interleaved runs each); at 100K on 1c1bc9532 with lazy registry restore the turn log opened in 406 to 494 ms and the first provider call came 4.34 to 4.54 s after open, the first root call 5.7 to 6.9 s after start (three runs), where ba3deec20 took 6.67 s to open and 12.45 s to the first call after open. Cost: the 100K kill run wrote 146,980 rows by 50,011 finished children against 117,216 rows on ba3deec20 (+25%, section rows), in 1,128 s against 1,281 s on the shared Hand. nanocode-sim: the turnlog policy writes `<scope>:part` at revisions 3, 9, 27 and so on in the same commit as the scope checkpoint, and after each restart it must read the value of the last such revision at or below the restored one; mutation `sections_pruned` (the host drops every section row below a new head that the head does not supersede) is caught on 319 of 400 `--twice` seeds.

- perf(cli): `nanocode exec` drops the binary's read-only file pages from the process's page tables (`nanocode_sys::entry::release_file_pages`: `madvise(MADV_DONTNEED)` over every non-writable `PT_LOAD` of each loaded object from `dl_iterate_phdr`, skipping the vDSO and any object with text relocations) at the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 8th ... `ModelCallStarted` of the process, which lowers the 10-step direct tool turn's peak RSS from 8.11 to 6.14 MB and the Code Mode turn's from 11.30 to 9.47 MB (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: tool-turn peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, file-pages lane). Why: after startup most of the resident set is clean private file pages (text, `.text.cold`, rodata, static libc) that startup or an earlier step touched, or fault-around mapped beside them. DONTNEED on a clean private file mapping only unmaps the pages, the page cache keeps them, and the next touch is a minor fault, so RSS then holds only what runs between two drops. The kernel records `hiwater_rss` before it zaps, so `ru_maxrss` still counts what ran before each drop. The gain is that startup-only code and earlier steps' cold pages do not add to later steps. Schedule: dropping before every model call gave the lowest peak but cost about 900 extra page faults and 12 to 14M kernel instructions per 10-step turn (shim measurement below). Dropping only at the first call kept 75% of the gain at almost no cost. Powers of two (calls 1, 2, 4, 8, so log2 of the calls) kept about 90% of the gain at a third of the faults, so a long session pays a logarithmic number of refault rounds. Skipping BOLT's hot `.text` in the drop saved a third of the faults but kept 0.3 MB more. Measured (bench/cli at cli-bench 3e70e983e under tools/netguard.sh, static-glibc dist+BOLT `build-cli.sh` of 2a533981c and of this change, six interleaved passes alternating lane order, each `--parts=firstframe,oneshot,tools --steps=10 --rounds=4 --toolrounds=3`, medians): direct tool turn ru_maxrss 8.11 to 6.14 MB, tree peak 12.72 to 10.94 MB, CPU per step 1.96 to 2.07 ms (n=18). Code Mode ru_maxrss 11.30 to 9.47 MB, tree 15.64 to 14.31 MB, CPU per step 2.21 to 2.34 ms, one-shot 5.86 to 5.49 MB (n=24), first frame 5.61 and 5.30 MB (the TUI does not call it). A smaps_rollup sampler at 0.2 ms on the agent pid of the direct turn (n=16 and 18, its peak sample): Rss 11.41 to 7.55 MB, Pss 11.40 to 7.54, file 8.36 to 5.43, anonymous 3.01 to 2.06. Schedule choice, prototyped as an LD_PRELOAD shim on the dynamic dist+BOLT binary of c7c42d5e5 that drops at each HTTP `POST` write (~/sw/fpage/shim.c), direct turn ru_maxrss / page faults / kernel instructions per turn under perf stat: none 8.82 MB / 2024 / 56.6M, every call 6.97 / 2921 / 68.5M, first call only 7.44 / 2082 / 60.6M, powers of two 7.17 / 2356 / 62.9M, every call without hot text 7.24 / 2613 / 67.6M. Measured and not shipped: `MADV_PAGEOUT`/`MADV_COLD` (they evict page-cache pages the process maps alone, so a refault reads the disk), and a timer thread dropping every 50 or 200 ms (a 10-step turn takes 40 to 80 ms, so it never fires inside one). Writable segments, RELRO and `.data` are 31 KB in all and are never dropped. Not done here: the interactive terminal interface does not call it yet.
- fix(claude-client): `MessageAccumulator::finish` again treats a finished message with no content blocks as `ClaudeError::IncompleteStream` only when it has no stop_reason; an empty end_turn message goes to the agent, whose one `NO_VISIBLE_OUTPUT` nudge (9a9e5d038) asks for a visible reply and ends the turn if the next reply is empty too (2026-11-15, reverts the end_turn half of 4421fca3d). Why: an empty end_turn is a valid reply when the model already wrote its answer and its last tool call needs no follow-up. 4421fca3d sent that same request again, which came back empty in under a second on each of the 11 attempts, so the turn failed with `Messages stream ended before message_stop` after about 184 s even though its answer was already written. Sending the identical request again cannot change a deterministic empty reply; the nudge changes the request, so it covers the case 4421fca3d targeted (an empty reply right after a tool result, with no answer yet) as well. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client` (native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
- docs(decisions): fresh CLI sessions keep the no-hedge-before-estimate rule of c95cb6e6c, measured against the 1.5 s floor hedge and Codex CLI 0.166.0 and not shipped (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 latency SLA: GPT p99 lane). What: three interleaved lanes on dev-georgios through `bench/sla/run.ts --live --turns=3 --settle=3000`, 100 three-turn sessions per lane per model in 10 chunks of 10 per model, alternating models, every chunk at load below 60 (max 42.7): (A) master 5d2ab874d, (B) the same commit with `Hedging::race_when` hedging at `deadline()` (the 1.5 s floor before 10 first bytes) and the window cap `hedged < ceil(window * cap / 100)` restored, the behaviour before c95cb6e6c, (C) Codex CLI. Per-turn e2e ms, p50 / p95 / p99 / max, A then B then C: gpt-6-luna turn 1 1185/1973/2592/3287, 1193/2009/2522/2907, 1657/2646/3472/3860; turn 2 1259/1910/2455/2859, 1164/1894/2700/3210, 1450/2716/3499/3499; turn 3 1203/1908/2083/2409, 1289/2265/2518/2968, 1366/2250/2531/2723; gpt-6.1-terra turn 1 1317/2107/2304/3053, 1350/2116/2828/2903, 1712/2735/3905/5682; turn 2 1252/2111/2392/4760, 1250/2057/2347/2645, 1267/2263/4355/5157; turn 3 1279/2188/3059/3448, 1296/2175/2744/2778, 1362/2487/3988/4267. B beats A on p99 in 3 of 6 cells and loses pooled luna p99 (2700 against 2455 over 300 turns), wins pooled terra p99 (2744 against 3053) and max. Hedges in B (otel `hedge.status` on `responses.attempt`): luna 47 sent of 300 calls, 4 won by the hedge, terra 70 of 300, 3 won. The replayed input equals 15.7% (luna) and 23.3% (terra) of the lane's input tokens (10.9% and 23.4% of uncached input), over the 10% `cap_percent`, because a fresh process admits up to 10 hedges before its window holds any sample. A sent no hedge (600 calls `unestimated`). Both nanocode lanes beat Codex CLI on p99 in all 6 cells and on p50 in 5 of 6. Decision: the GPT p99 losses to Codex at n=30 (5d2ab874d) do not reproduce at n=100, and floor hedges win about 6% while costing more than the cap, so fresh sessions stay unhedged. Raw data: dev-georgios `~/sla/out11/hf-*.jsonl`, analysis `~/sla/hfab-analyze.py`, report `~/sla/hfab-report.txt`, lane B patch `~/sla/hedge-fresh.patch`. Code is unchanged, so no sim sweep or cargo check was run.
- perf(cli): the dist profile builds 36 run-once crates at `opt-level = "s"`: the agent, config and host crates, both backends' agent crates and the Claude client and tools, nanocode-cli, the durability, store, subagent, MCP, MPP, Tempo, tool, schema, observability and image crates, psh-utils and unicode-normalization (2026-11-15, CLI binary size wave 2, aimed at resident file pages). Kept at 3: djs, psh-engine, serde_json, the HTTP, TLS, sync, executor, zstd and compression crates and nanocode-backend-codex-client, which hold the per-token and per-cell loops. Why: after 2a533981c the tool-turn peak is mostly file pages of code a turn runs once (startup, tool registration, session setup), and per-crate `opt-level` applies to each function under fat LTO, as the RustPython entry below showed. Measured on the thread's hosted Hand (5 cores, shared), base 2a533981c against the same tree with this change, both from scripts/build-cli.sh, bench/cli `--parts=tools --steps=10` under tools/netguard.sh with both binaries as interleaved lanes, 4 rounds, plus a pagemap and smaps_rollup sampler at each process's largest RSS: nanocode-agent 48,445,640 to 45,781,992 bytes (-2.66 MB); direct tool turn peak RSS median 7.52 to 7.07 MB, Pss 7.86 to 7.29 MB (Pss_File 6.46 to 5.92 MB, Pss_Anon 1.34 to 1.36 MB); Code Mode tool turn 11.23 to 10.54 MB, Pss 11.53 to 10.82 MB (Pss_File 8.43 to 7.71 MB). Resident text at the direct peak (hot `.text`, `.text.cold` and the original text) 4.43 to 3.81 MB; rodata 1.64 to 1.85 MB. The smaller original `.text` no longer holds BOLT's rewritten code (28,082,280 bytes needed, 27,944,792 available), so build-cli.sh takes its existing `-lite` fallback; rerunning BOLT with `-lite=0` and without `-use-old-text` on the earlier tree (37b42b7f5-era base, dynamic glibc) gave the same direction: direct 8.36 to 7.25 MB, Code Mode 11.55 to 11.27 MB, so the gain is the code size and not the lite layout. Cost, `perf stat -e instructions:u` over scripts/train-cli.py's modes, 3 interleaved runs: tools (three 10-step turns) 56.2M to 59.1M (+5.2%), codemode 97.8M to 101.7M (+4.0%), oneshot 4.5M to 4.7M; `perf record` puts most of it in serde_json's string escaping (`format_escaped_str_contents`) instantiated in the size-optimized crates, about 0.1M instructions per tool step. Measured and not changed: the CLI links 32 third-party crates and none twice (`cargo tree -d` is empty); the largest resident rodata objects in a direct turn are the merged strings (175 KB), graviola's P-256 generator table (151 KB, read because the MPP paying proxy generates a P-256 CA key and certificate in every process), the five Codex-family prompts (96 KB, one used) and the session zstd dictionary (42 KB); cua_driver.mjs (193 KB) is referenced by an executed function but only about 60 KB of it is resident through neighbouring windows, so compressing it would save little. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-store-jsonl --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes; the change touches only the dist profile. Files: Cargo.toml.
- bench(cli): memory rows are measured with virtiofs files bind-mounted from ext4 copies, and every row reports PSS, anonymous and file-backed memory beside peak RSS (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: honest memory bench). Why: on the hosted Hand `/` is virtiofs with DAX, so file pages of libc.so.6, ld-linux-x86-64.so.2, node and the other system files a CLI maps often count as 0 in smaps, statm and rusage; whether they count changes from run to run (libc.so.6 in a fresh `sleep` read 24 kB, 24 kB and 1,344 kB in three runs, node's own binary 31.5 MB against 41.3 MB from an ext4 copy), so dynamic CLIs and the shell children of a tool turn read low and noisy. What, on the cli-bench branch (c7b57372d): `tools/localfs.sh` collects each lane binary, node, sh, bash, ls, libnss_* and their ldd closure, copies those on a virtiofs mount to work/localfs and bind-mounts them over their real paths in a mount namespace (unprivileged user namespace mapped back to the caller, else sudo unshare and setpriv), and `harness/run.sh` runs every step under it (LOCALFS=0 turns it off; on a host without virtiofs it runs the command as it is). `tools/runstat-linux.c` reads the tree's smaps_rollup at each new statm RSS peak and writes PSS, anonymous and file-backed at that peak; `harness/tui.py` adds file-backed and the PSS split one second after the first frame and waits for that sample before it ends the session (opencode draws its first frame after the 2 s window and had no memory row before). `tools/install.sh` takes FX_VERSION: fx 0.0.17 retries "Offline" forever against the fixture, so the run pins 0.0.16. Measured: `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` at 2a533981c (static front and static agent) against fx 0.0.16, pi 1.5.2, opencode 1.19.5, Claude Code 2.1.325 and Codex 0.169.0, three passes interleaved by lane (startup 100 rounds, oneshot 3, firstframe 3, 10-step tool turn 2 per pass) under localfs and netguard, then one LOCALFS=0 pass, all under ~/sw/buildq.sh at load 2 to 5 (bench/cli/results/2026-11-15-hosted-localfs). Peak RSS, nc against fx, localfs (LOCALFS=0 in parentheses): --version 0.26 against 1.40 MB (0.29, 1.40), one-shot 5.37 against 7.32 MB (5.29, 7.26), first frame 5.16 against 8.85 MB (5.19, 8.72), RSS one second after the first frame 5.16 against 8.59 MB (5.19, 8.58), direct tool turn 14.9 against 18.2 MB (11.8, 16.4), Code Mode tool turn 17.7 MB (16.4). nc's own process maps no shared library, so its single-process rows do not move; the tool-turn rows grow by about 3 MB because the dash and ls children now count their libc and binary pages. After the first frame nc is 1.24 MB anonymous and 3.92 MB file-backed, fx 1.17 and 7.43 MB, so the remaining gap to fx's anonymous memory is 0.07 MB and nc's lead is its smaller mapped text. Other lanes after the first frame: codex 157 MB, Claude Code 206 MB, pi 121 MB (90 MB PSS, split with the harness's own node processes), opencode 759 MB.
- perf(cli): `Host::build` builds the runtime with `build` on the caller in `nanocode exec` too, so no path of the CLI uses `build_async` and its `nanocode-runtime-construction` thread (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: one-shot kernel instructions, wave 3). Why: the 2026-11-14 earlydraw entry moved the terminal interface to `build` and kept `build_async` for exec because exec's prepare runs on a runtime worker; the construction is about 0.2 ms of work, while the thread costs a clone, a 2 MB stack, an 8 MB allocator segment mapping and an exit per one-shot. Blocking exec's one worker for that time delays only the MCP and gateway connections that start at the same time. The durability store is always given (`config.store` or a `MemoryStore`), so `build_async`'s default-store path was not used here. Result with the four entries above: the bench one-shot runs 3 threads (main, worker, nanocode-lookup) instead of 5 and makes 270 syscall lines instead of 800. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 3 to 5 from other lanes) with release builds of f1cc5300c and of each change, bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=oneshot --only=nc` under tools/netguard.sh with `NC_BIN` wrapped in `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults` (~/sw/k3/ab.sh), binaries interleaved per pass, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh; syscall counts from `strace -f` of one one-shot. 6 interleaved passes of 12 against the entry above: page faults 799 to 781, user instructions 4.80M to 4.71M. Cumulative, f1cc5300c against this change, 8 interleaved passes of 12 (96 one-shots each): kernel instructions median 10.73M to 9.09M (p25 10.16M to 8.25M, every pass median lower), page faults 817 to 780, user instructions 5.08M to 4.71M (pass medians 4.71M to 4.94M). Refuted in this pass: the `nanocode-reactor` fallback thread that one strace showed at exit is a shutdown race (the worker leaves as the last reactor driver while main exits), absent in 5 of 5 runs of every build under lighter tracing, so it was left alone. fx 0.0.16 in the same harness, interleaved with this build (4 passes of 12): fx kernel instructions pass medians 5.93M to 6.05M, page faults 422, user 4.05M; nanocode 9.23M to 12.11M, page faults 775 to 790, user 4.72M to 4.94M, so the gap to fx is about 3.3M kernel instructions and 355 page faults on a release build.
- perf(durability,cli): `nanocode_durability::drive_on(handle)` (native) sets the runtime that `spawn_driver` uses for store drivers (`MemoryStore`, `SharedStore`, `SharedReader`); it succeeds only before the first driver starts and returns the handle back otherwise, after which the existing `nanocode-durability-store` thread and its runtime are used as before. `nanocode exec` calls it with its one-worker runtime right after building it (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: one-shot kernel instructions, wave 3). Why: the store thread cost each one-shot a clone, a 2 MB stack, an allocator segment (an 8 MB mmap and two munmaps) and its exit, about 0.14M kernel instructions in the wave 2 profile, and a one-shot's store operations still crossed threads (the 2026-11-14 MemoryStore entry moved the memory driver onto that thread so the session's worker woke the store thread and back). With exec's drivers on its only worker every store operation is a local wake on that worker. The exec runtime lives until the process exits, so the drivers do not outlive it; the terminal interface, `hand`, the swarm and SDK hosts do not call `drive_on` and keep the store thread. Checked: `nanocode exec` without `--ephemeral` writes its session, and `exec --continue` resumes the same session id; a 10-step tool turn (bench/cli tools part) completes with 11 requests. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 3 to 5 from other lanes) with release builds of f1cc5300c and of each change, bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=oneshot --only=nc` under tools/netguard.sh with `NC_BIN` wrapped in `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults` (~/sw/k3/ab.sh), binaries interleaved per pass, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh; syscall counts from `strace -f` of one one-shot. 6 interleaved passes of 12 against the build with the three entries above: page faults 822 to 799, user instructions 5.00M to 4.80M; kernel instructions within the load noise (medians 9.68M and 9.88M of 72 each); syscall lines 511 to 335.
- perf(cli): `arguments::hide` (Linux, a prompt on the command line) reads the argument area, argc and the whole argv array with one `read_exact_at` each and writes the rewritten array and the cleared area with one `write_all_at` each on /proc/self/mem (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: one-shot kernel instructions, wave 3). Before, each argv slot took an lseek and a read to check it and an lseek and a write to replace it: 37 seek, read and write calls on /proc/self/mem for the bench one-shot's 12 arguments, each an access to the process's own memory through the kernel's remote-VM path. The checks are unchanged (argc against the area, every slot pointing at its argument, skipped loader arguments), and slots are written only after every slot passed. Result: lseek 28 to 1, 511 syscall lines instead of 539. Measured with the DNS entry above.
- perf(computer-repl): `ComputerConfig::detect` returns "computer use needs a graphical session: DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY are unset" without searching for cua-driver when `NANOCODE_CUA` and `CUA_DRIVER_PATH` are unset and, on Linux, DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY are both unset or empty (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: one-shot kernel instructions, wave 3). Why: the Linux computer-use backend needs a desktop session (crates/integrations/computer/src/linux: AT-SPI bus and DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY), but every agent start stat()ed each PATH entry and `CUA_DRIVER_SEARCH` for cua-driver on the worker (12 to 15 statx on the bench one-shot, about 0.25M kernel instructions in the wave 2 profile) only to report it missing. The notice on stderr now names the missing display instead of the missing driver. `NANOCODE_CUA=cua-driver` or `CUA_DRIVER_PATH` keeps the search (an explicit request), macOS is unchanged, and `nanocode cua install`/status call `ComputerConfig::cua_driver` directly, which still searches. Result: statx 38 to 26 and 539 syscall lines instead of 544 on the bench one-shot. Measured with the entry above.
- perf(executor): a Linux name lookup records a name server whose UDP socket fails to open (`Wire::open` of the `Sockets` wire: socket, bind, connect, nonblocking, reactor registration), skips it in later attempts and later search candidates of the same lookup, and returns that error at once when every configured name server is recorded (a list that `lookup` keeps and passes to `query` and `exchange` in crates/core/executor/src/dns.rs, outside the `Wire` trait that nanocode-sim implements) (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: one-shot kernel instructions, wave 3). Why: these are local errors (ENETUNREACH, EADDRNOTAVAIL, EAFNOSUPPORT) that the next attempt repeats without any packet sent, and with the hosted Hand's resolv.conf (two name servers, four search domains, ndots 1) each of the four startup lookups (MCP and gateway hosts) under tools/netguard.sh made 5 candidates x 2 attempts x 2 servers = 20 failed socket, bind, connect and close sets, 80 per one-shot, the largest syscall group of the trace. A name server that opens and then times out, answers SERVFAIL or truncates is retried as before; TCP mode is unchanged. Result: 8 sockets per one-shot instead of 80, 544 syscall lines instead of 800. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 3 to 5 from other lanes) with release builds of f1cc5300c and of each change, bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=oneshot --only=nc` under tools/netguard.sh with `NC_BIN` wrapped in `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults` (~/sw/k3/ab.sh), binaries interleaved per pass, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh; syscall counts from `strace -f` of one one-shot. Combined with the next two entries (computer-use probe, argument hiding), 8 interleaved passes of 15 (120 one-shots each): kernel instructions median 11.00M to 10.33M (p25 10.81M to 10.03M, 7 of 8 pass medians lower), user 5.09M to 5.01M.
