Why: these are local errors (ENETUNREACH, EADDRNOTAVAIL, EAFNOSUPPORT) that the next attempt repeats without any packet sent, and with the hosted Hand's resolv.conf (two name servers, four search domains, ndots 1) each of the four startup lookups (MCP and gateway hosts) under tools/netguard.sh made 5 candidates x 2 attempts x 2 servers = 20 failed socket, bind, connect and close sets, 80 per one-shot, the largest syscall group of the trace. A name server that opens and then times out, answers SERVFAIL or truncates is retried as before; TCP mode is unchanged. Result: 8 sockets per one-shot instead of 80, 544 syscall lines instead of 800. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 3 to 5 from other lanes) with release builds of f1cc5300c and of each change, bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=oneshot --only=nc` under tools/netguard.sh with `NC_BIN` wrapped in `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults` (~/sw/k3/ab.sh), binaries interleaved per pass, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh; syscall counts from `strace -f` of one one-shot. Combined with the next two entries (computer-use probe, argument hiding), 8 interleaved passes of 15 (120 one-shots each): kernel instructions median 11.00M to 10.33M (p25 10.81M to 10.03M, 7 of 8 pass medians lower), user 5.09M to 5.01M.
- perf(djs): JSON.parse decodes an escaped one-byte string in its scan (`scan_one`), into a reused host buffer (`Scratch::dec`), and `string_value` copies that buffer into the new string, so `write_escaped_latin1` and `plain_run` are gone (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 4). Why: a 4.4 KB tool result with about 300 escapes cost about 53k instructions to parse, in two passes over the string: `scan_rest` (byte loop, then `plain_run` out of line after each escape) and `write_escaped_latin1` (word copy, then a byte loop per escape). What: `scan_string` of Latin-1 or UTF-8 input calls `scan_one` at the first escape or multi-byte sequence. `scan_one` reads 8 bytes at a time while `escape_mask8` (and, for UTF-8, the high bits) flags no byte, appends each word to `dec` (a partial word is appended whole and truncated, not copied by length), and decodes each escape or UTF-8 sequence in place. It reports the same errors at the same offsets as `scan_rest` did. A decoded unit above 0xFF sets `two_byte`, `dec` stops there, and `string_value` uses `write_string` as before. Two-byte input keeps `scan_rest`. Instructions per cell (output/cellbench on the code-mode-engine native host, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, (1,200 - 200 cells)/1,000, best of 3, base 2a533981c): seq 965,429 -> 906,619 (-6.1%), json 1,372,969 -> 1,334,725 (-2.8%), edit 1,062,077 -> 1,036,678 (-2.4%), sh 1,609,514 -> 1,596,837 (-0.8%), agent 1,678,964 -> 1,679,003; the typical suite (sh, seq, json, edit, agent) 6,688,953 -> 6,553,862 (-2.0%), and with `--vary` 6,704,326 -> 6,564,611; empty 83,736 -> 83,764. Each cellbench cell's printed output is byte-identical. djs benches (djsrun, best of 5, loop, gen, gennext, find, forEach, some, filter, map, reduce, err) within 0.001% of base. Checked: test262 subset 2,535 passing, identical pass set; the fuel harness (ten fuel/slice pairs over eleven scripts, including the JSON differential of 6,000 random strings with every escape, control characters, Latin-1, two-byte and surrogate text) identical; `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -p djs-prelude -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; djs-prelude's base remade with scripts/base.sh. Measured and corrected for the next wave: `prepareCell` in bootstrap.js runs once, when the snapshot is built (the bootstrap module's `runCell` export is its result), not per cell. Per cell, an empty cell (82.6k) is mostly the `AsyncFunction` compile of the wrapper source (`compile_function`, about 21k callgrind instructions per cell), `reset_written`'s image restore (about 21k callgrind, most of it a memcpy that `perf` counts as one `rep movsb`), and the promise, pump and host-call steps of `runCell`. `--vary` changes a cell by about 1k to 12k instructions, so no compiled-source cache exists. A cache keyed by cell source would remove compile only for repeated identical cells, so it was not built. Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/json/parse.rs.
- perf(tool-runtime, code-mode): an acceptor's runtime link reports the Hand's `caches_local_tools`, the client keeps the key of the last brain tool set it sent, and a Hand reply's ledger record and its ack run behind the reply instead of before it (2026-11-15, per-step cost lane). Why: `accept::registry`'s `Shared` link implemented neither `caches_local_tools` nor anything but send, receive, close, frame size and resumes, so the default `false` held for every accepted Hand and each Execute carried every brain tool's definition: in a production-shaped seq run (replayed production turns on 20 threads, a brain with its own server-side tools) each step's Execute was 105 KB, which the brain encoded twice (once for `local_tools_key`'s blake3, once for the frame) and the Hand decoded and stored again, though the Hand advertises the cache in its catalog. Now `Shared` carries the flag of the catalog the runtime attached with (a resumed socket is the same runtime), so a step's Execute carries the key and the Hand reuses its copy; a Hand that lacks the key on a new connection answers `LOCAL_TOOLS_UNKNOWN` and the client resends the full set, as before. `Client::local_tools_key` compares the definitions with the last set it hashed (their descriptions and schemas are `Arc`s, so equal sets compare by pointer) and hashes only a changed set. `settle_reply_behind` spawns `settle_reply` (ledger `replied`, then the `Ack` when the link resumes), so the reply reaches the cell without waiting for that commit: the Hand keeps an unacked reply and resends it after a crash or a redial, so the reply is never lost, and the ack still waits for the record (the hands scenario's `ack_after_store` invariant). Measured: bpftrace on the Hands' socket reads (16384 + 88528 bytes per step before, about 1 KB after); interleaved seq runs of a server built on this tree against the same server on 0a36b56c5, production-shaped host (server pinned to 10 cores, ParadeDB 18 on its own NVMe, load 19 to 23): step gap (model reply to the next model request, Hand time included) p50 2.93, 2.75, 2.88 ms before, 1.72, 1.62, 1.58 after; replayed-turn overhead p50 10.7, 10.4, 11.0 before, 7.0, 6.3, 6.5 after, p99 72, 71, 79 before, 48, 41, 56 after; server CPU per phase 10.2, 9.5, 10.0 s before, 7.8, 7.2, 7.5 after. `nanocode-sim --scenario hands`: seeds 0..300 pass, and ack_before_store, skip_record, forget_pending, cross_replies and mangle_runtime are each caught within 100 seeds.
- measure(turnlog): the records stream and snapshots keep their deflate levels on a Postgres host (2026-11-15, per-step cost lane). The turn log's deflate was 11% of a production-shaped server's user CPU in a seq run (`longest_match` 5.9%, `insert_string` 2.7%, `deflate_slow` 0.8%, `deflate_medium` 0.5%), so three level pairs were built and run interleaved: stream 1 and snapshots 1, stream 0 and snapshots 0 (stored blocks), and stream 7 with snapshots 1. Step gap p50: levels 1/1 3.68 and 2.53 ms against 2.24 and 1.88 at 7/6 in the same batches, 0/0 2.62 and 3.95; stream 7 with snapshots 1 1.43 ms against 1.54 at 7/6 in a quiet pair and within noise in loaded ones. Bigger rows reach the snapshot threshold sooner, and each snapshot re-serializes the whole fold, so less compression costs more CPU than it saves. The stream is already incremental (one deflate stream per log, sync-flushed per commit).
- feat(claude): the direct catalog of a headless root Claude session on a hand serves Claude Code 2.1.325's Monitor and ScheduleWakeup, with their upstream definitions vendored (2026-11-15, Georgios: nanoeval claude-direct catalog parity lane). Before: in nanoeval's claude-direct arm Claude Code 2.1.318 -p called Monitor and ScheduleWakeup 22 times to wait on background jobs (compile-compcert, crack-7z, train-fasttext, make-doom), while nano direct had neither and once called wait_agent on a Bash job ("unknown agent_id 1"); prompts/upstream.json vendored only Bash, Edit, Read, TaskStop, WebFetch, WebSearch, Write and the Task* tools. Capture: Claude Code 2.1.325 `-p --output-format stream-json --verbose --dangerously-skip-permissions --model claude-opus-5-5`, IS_SANDBOX=1, an empty HOME, a local Messages stub and a dummy key (output/default-print, ignored), with the official linux-x64 executable (sha256 0dc4f4a9a165fc60746d7ae8489712e5fc352f1e7ad4eb22e7141bd0812eb0cf) and the darwin-arm64 2.1.325 install (sha256 84590fefe6338be9087f5814b61f9a54c5f21524163a4c127cb5a808e31009f2), identical on both: the request carries Agent, Bash, Edit, ListAgents, Read, ReportFindings, ScheduleWakeup, Skill, ToolSearch, Workflow and Write inline and defers CronCreate, CronDelete, CronList, EnterWorktree, ExitWorktree, Monitor, NotebookEdit, SendMessage, TaskStop, WebFetch and WebSearch; with ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false all 21 are inline, and the init event lists the same 21 plus ToolSearch. The default set has no BashOutput or TaskOutput. `scripts/verify-claude-upstream.py --capture --write` with Monitor and ScheduleWakeup taken from the full profile adds their definitions to tools/src/tools/upstream.json, byte for byte the definitions of the stream-json capture; the system blocks and bash-first.json are unchanged. What: `claude_tools::install` gives the session that gets the hand job hold (headless, a Code Mode host, the root) a `Watches` state, and its direct catalog adds Monitor and ScheduleWakeup when the hand offers Bash. Monitor starts the hand's Bash with `run_in_background` and `timeout` set to `timeout_ms` (the upstream schema's default, 300000, when absent), at most 600000 ms (the cap upstream's description states), and answers with upstream's start text. On each Notices round of the hold (the session's cell yield, 10 s by default) a foreground hand Bash reads each monitor's output file from its last offset (`tail -c +N | head -c MAX_STREAM_BYTES`), and the complete non-empty lines are steered in as one `<task-notification>` with upstream's `Monitor event: "<description>"` summary and `<event>` tag, ahead of the job's own completion notice. A monitor whose job notice arrives at or after its timeout gets upstream's `[Monitor expired after ...]` event in place of the Bash time-limit notice. TaskStop stops a monitor as any hand job, and a `ws` source is refused. ScheduleWakeup clamps `delaySeconds` to [60, 3600] as upstream does, keeps one pending wakeup (the next call replaces it, `stop: true` cancels it), and answers with upstream's texts (without the CronDelete sentence, since no cron tool is offered). The hold then waits for the wakeup, bounded by the deadline as before, and steers its `prompt` in as the next user message. `bash::exited_line`, `KILLED_LINE` and `closes_output` hold the output file's closing line, which the reader drops. Subagent tools stay: Claude Code -p offers Agent, ListAgents, SendMessage and TaskStop, so the root's spawn_agent, wait_agent, list_agents, send_agent_message, close_agent and interrupt_agent keep their place. Not matched: events reach the model only from the turn hold, at the Notices cadence and not upstream's 200 ms batches; event lines include stderr, since the hand's output file holds both streams; no per-event truncation or rate suppression; monitors and wakeups are not in the durable checkpoint; the wakeup time is UTC in the wasm module. Measured with nanocode-ts output/catalog/run.ts (from output/wave7c/run.ts: a scripted Messages SSE mock, a `nanocode hand` and the wasm module built from this tree, direct orchestration, headless, one run each, gak-9): tools `Bash,Edit,Read,TaskStop,WebSearch,Write,Monitor,ScheduleWakeup` (with subagents also close_agent, interrupt_agent, list_agents, send_agent_message, spawn_agent, submit_result, wait_agent); a monitor of 8 ticks 3 s apart with timeout_ms 60000 gave events "tick 1..4" at 10.1 s and "tick 5..7" at 20.1 s, then "tick 8, READY" and the completion notice at 24.2 s, then the finish check; `sleep 30` with timeout_ms 4000 gave "[Monitor expired after 4s with no events delivered. ...]" at 4.1 s; a ws source was refused; delaySeconds 5 was clamped to 60 and the prompt arrived at 60.1 s; a wakeup then `stop: true` cancelled 1 and the turn ended at once; a 90 s wakeup under a 20 s deadline reached the finish check at 20.0 s. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -- -D warnings` (wasm32 clippy stops only at the existing unused `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT`), `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Not run: a nanoeval rerun. Files: crates/backends/claude/{prompts/upstream.json,src/claude_tools.rs,src/claude_bash.rs,tools/src/tools/bash.rs,tools/src/tools/upstream.json}.
- perf(cli): scripts/build-cli.sh links nanocode-agent for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu statically against glibc and runs BOLT on the static link (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, static-glibc lane 3). Why: without ld.so and libc.so a start costs 45% fewer kernel instructions, and on a disk-backed libc every memory row falls 0.4 to 1.7 MB. What: after training, scripts/static-cli.py relinks the build's own objects from nanocode.link with `-static -nostartfiles`, crt1.o, crti.o and crtbegin.o (not crtbeginT.o, whose frame registration walks the whole .eh_frame) before them and crtend.o and crtn.o after them, `-lc -lgcc -lgcc_eh` in one group and the dynamic-only libraries dropped. It uses rodata-cli.py's linker script with libc.a, libgcc_eh.a and libgcc.a .rodata placed right after the profile-ordered Rust .rodata (before: spread over the catch-all), and `--symbol-ordering-file` scripts/cli-libc.order. Then it starts the FDEs of `__restore_rt` and `_dl_tlsdesc_undefweak` at their symbols (glibc's CFI starts 1 and 7 bytes early, which BOLT rejects) and sets the int3 run that lld puts before each function after glibc's own padding to nop (229,070 bytes, which BOLT otherwise rejects as non-empty padding). BOLT then runs outside `-lite` on that binary with the build's profile and layout and `-function-order` cli-libc.order followed by startup.order. cli-libc.order is the first-call order of the 312 libc functions that startup, the first frame, one-shot and both tool turns run (gdb breakpoints on all 1,301 libc functions of the static link at c7c42d5e5, under bench/cli with a pseudo-terminal), each traced string function followed by its other ifunc variants, since glibc picks the variant per CPU. Function names that a toolchain does not have are ignored (`--no-warn-symbol-ordering`). The static binary links no NSS or resolver code (no getaddrinfo, getpwnam_r, getpwuid_r or `__nss_*`). Measured with bench/cli (cli-bench fb6e53fc0) under tools/netguard.sh on the 5-core hosted Hand, the dynamic dist+BOLT agent of c7c42d5e5 against the static agent from this build-cli.sh, three interleaved passes of `suite.mjs --parts=firstframe,oneshot,tools --steps=10 --rounds=4 --toolrounds=3` and `--rounds=3` oneshot and firstframe under `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k`, page cache of both binaries dropped before each pass, load 2 to 4. Two conditions, because / on this Hand is virtiofs with DAX, whose mappings of libc.so.6 and ld.so do not count in RSS (smaps shows libc's 1,572 kB text at Rss 0 kB), while on a disk filesystem they do. With libc.so.6 and ld.so bind-mounted from ext4 copies (as on a normal install), dynamic then static, medians: RSS 1 s after the first frame 6.54 and 5.35 MB, first-frame peak 6.35 and 5.12 MB, one-shot peak 6.85 and 5.16 MB, 10-step direct tool turn peak 8.77 and 7.11 MB, Code Mode 12.33 and 10.95 MB, one-shot CPU 2.88 and 2.35 ms, one-shot instructions user 3.81M and 3.59M, kernel 4.88M and 4.55M, first frame user 4.64M and 4.43M, kernel 6.31M and 5.78M. With the Hand's own virtiofs libc: RSS after the first frame 4.68 and 5.31 MB (the dynamic row leaves out libc.so and ld.so), first-frame peak 6.01 and 5.05 MB, one-shot peak 6.45 and 5.02 MB, direct tool turn 7.85 and 6.96 MB, Code Mode 11.37 and 10.92 MB, one-shot CPU 4.79 and 2.83 ms, one-shot kernel instructions 9.16M and 4.48M, first frame kernel 10.99M and 5.81M (DAX faults on libc.so are slow). Where the static binary's after-first-frame pages go (pagemap 1.1 s after start, sections against windows of 64 KB): libc-only pages are 140 KB of .text, 92 KB of .text.cold and 84 KB of .rodata (C-ctype tables), the rest is Rust code in 3 to 6 more windows than the dynamic layout. Resident pages are not touched pages: on kernel 6.18 a fault maps the whole large folio around it, so windows of strtod, tzfile and tunables code that no breakpoint hit are resident. The .eh_frame walk of the earlier static lanes is gone with crtbegin.o (64 KB resident, as dynamic). .data, .bss and .data.rel.ro together are 80 KB, TLS and IRELATIVE relocations dirty no extra page in the rows. The libc .rodata grouping was not measured on its own. Checks: `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` end to end (agent `file`: statically linked, `nanocode --version`), every bench part above with no errors, static-cli.py's output byte-identical to the hand-run relink, FDE fix and padding fix. No Rust crate changes, so no cargo or wasm32 build applies. Files: scripts/build-cli.sh, scripts/static-cli.py, scripts/cli-libc.order.
- perf(subagents): a v10 subagent journal writes a per-leaf summary (`LeafPending`: queued unstarted ids and pending completion revisions) next to each leaf stub in `AgentPage`, and stubs full leaves whose agents are settled, queued unstarted (Pending with `unstarted`, no turn, no calls) or root children with an unconsumed completion; `Registry::restore` keeps those leaves cold from the stub instead of decoding every record and profile (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 lazyrestore lane). Restore enqueues the summary's unstarted ids, `build_unstarted` warms the leaf before `Registry::unstarted`, `activity()`, `root_active`, `needs_root_watch`, the fold's quiescence and `listed` count cold queued children and cold completions, `cancel_all`/`close_all` and a cancelled spawning turn warm them first, `load_leaves` checks `cancelled_turns` for the stub's spawning-turn context, and cold completions are announced after Ready by a task that warms one leaf at a time, so the restored root's in-flight request is re-sent unchanged before them. Stubs stay immutable identity (the queued child's `context` only), a thawed leaf is not cooled again while its summary is stale, and v9 journals still open and keep writing v9. Measured (native scale-bench, kill at 50% then restart pinned to one core with `--workers 1`, each binary restarting from a log it wrote, base ba3deec20, interleaved, 3 pairs, hosted Hand at load 6 to 15): 10K restore to Ready 493, 462, 252 ms to 92, 47, 94 ms (hot agents 7,313 to 465); 100K 12.9, 5.6, 4.8 s to 5.4, 4.8, 5.3 s (hot agents 76,241 to 24,161: leaves changed by deltas since the last fold still load hot); first root call after restart at 100K 59.2, 43.7, 39.4 s to 21.2, 15.3, 16.0 s. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-subagents -p nanocode-sim -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked --lib -p nanocode-subagents --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, nanocode-sim runtime kv 0..400 400/400.

- fix(subagents): a completion retry delivers the agent's current pending revision when it is not older than the revision that scheduled the retry (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 durability swarm, remoteclose lane). Why: `completion_retries` holds one retry per agent, so `retry_completion` for a newer revision returns early while an older revision's retry waits. The waiting retry then checked `completion.awaits(old)`, found the newer revision and did nothing, so the newer completion stayed Pending and the root never settled. runtime --store log --children remote --wire http, seed 7707 (stop=Cancel): root turn-1 failed while completions of agent 2 revisions 1 and 2 were steered into it, both came back Unread, and revision 2 stayed pending with no pending turns. The existing runtime settle invariant ("did not settle") catches it. Measured 2026-11-15 with nanocode-sim (--scenario runtime --store log --children remote --wire http): seed 7707 fails on master b9b0116d7 and passes with this change. Seeds 0..10000 with both changes: 9997 pass; 7407 also fails on master, 5186 and 5889 are under investigation.

- fix(code-mode): the native tool runtime's `begin_turn` forgets the finished Code Mode cells of its sessions, as the remote hosts' `begin_turn` already does (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 lane leafbytes: parent memory per finished child). Why: a local session's finished cell stayed in `CellJournals::finished` (an `Arc<CellRecord>` with its journal, script and tool catalog) and in the turn log fold (its cell updates and its open journaled calls, which only a `Forget` clears) until that session ran another `exec`. A finished subagent never runs one, so every finished child kept its cell for the life of the parent: on the native 10K flat scale-bench (memrows located records, counting allocator) fold cells were 2,342 B/child (child cells 1,445, the root's spawn cell 752) and open calls 559 B/child (10,000 spawn_agent + 10,000 submit_result). What: `CodeModeRuntime::remove_and_join` records the session of each finished journaled cell in `CellRegistry::finished`; the new `CodeModeControl::begin_turn` drains it and spawns `CellJournals::forget_finished` per session; `NativeToolRuntimeControl::begin_turn` (reached from the Claude backend's turn cleanup after every turn) calls it before the remote hosts. Forgetting at turn end matches the existing contract: a turn's cells are forgotten before its session's next turn starts. Measurement (2026-11-15, hosted Hand, one run each, native scale-bench --rate 1000 --workers 4 --latency 50 --concurrency 64, counting allocator, binary built on the memrows2 bench base with this change and a dense TaskTree table that adds about 25 to 40 B/child): live bytes per child at the end of the run fell from 16,523 to 9,968 at 10K agents (fold 9,352 to 6,833 B/child) and from 20,146 to 12,145 at 2K. The root's live spawn cell, the largest sampled site at 14,227 B/child, is released once the root starts its next acknowledgement turn.

- perf(tools): the remaining tool schemas are static or lazy, and the Claude client sends `JsonSchema` (2026-11-15, static tool schemas lane). Before, a Claude session parsed `upstream.json` into `Value`s twice (`tool_value` and `tool_definitions`), `BashTool`, `TaskStopTool`, the file and host tools rebuilt their `Value` schemas on every `definition()` call, `bridge_shared` and the direct catalog called `JsonSchema::shared()` (a parse per static schema), `claude_output` built output schemas that only Code Mode reads, `FunctionTool` deep-cloned its `Value` parameters per call, and the subagent tools, `job_wait`, the computer tool, the web search commands and image generation built `Value`s at first use. What: `nanocode_backend_claude_tools::upstream::tools()` compacts `upstream.json` at compile time with `compact_json` and keeps each tool's `input_schema` as a borrowed `RawValue` in a `StaticSchema`. `ToolDefinition::input_schema` in the Claude client is a `JsonSchema` (it serializes through `RawValue`, `is_object` reads the first byte), and `FunctionTool` keeps a `JsonSchema`. A new `LazySchema` (`lazy_json_schema!`) holds a schema that interpolates constants: it builds the `Value` once, keeps only its compact JSON for requests, and parses a `Value` only on `as_value`. `same_metadata` compares `JsonSchema`s by pointer before value. Literal schemas use `json_schema!`. Measured on a direct 10-step tool turn (local fixture under netguard, with Claude direct mode through `NANOCODE_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` with an unlisted model, as the CLI offers Claude models Code Mode only) at origin/master c8974f2bd: request bodies are byte-identical in both modes after ids, chunk ids, wall times and device id are masked (11 Responses and 12 Messages requests). Live heap peak (heapprof tracer, release with line tables): codex 479,170 to 472,997 bytes, Claude 709,624 to 552,858 bytes. Tool-definition heap at the peak: codex 17,401 to 10,593 bytes, Claude 130,965 to 19,993 bytes, and what is left is names, descriptions and grammars (`Box<str>`/`Arc<str>`), no schema `Value`. Peak RSS (dist+BOLT, ru_maxrss, 7 interleaved runs, median): codex 11.30 to 11.28 MB, Claude 17.76 to 17.85 MB, both within run spread (11.13 to 11.41 and 17.25 to 18.07 MB): the freed heap stays in allocator segments. Native and wasm32 `cargo check` pass for the changed crates. JSON key order is the source order, so a build without `preserve_order` (where `json!` sorted keys) now sends the source order. Next: tool descriptions as static `&str` would take the last 10 to 20 KB.
- docs(decisions): where nc-lite `--continue` spends its user instructions, measured on a 1,000-session store and on a 200-tool-call session, and one hasher change measured and not shipped (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: session resume lane, wave 2). Setup: nc-lite `fast` builds (`CARGO_PROFILE_FAST_INCREMENTAL=false CARGO_PROFILE_FAST_STRIP=none`) of 8131a9e31, the bench harness fake Responses server, `perf stat -e instructions:u` per run and `perf record --call-graph dwarf` at 5 kHz for attribution. (1) Harness store (`suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nclite --sessions=1000 --storerounds=10`, `BENCH_PERF=1`): store-resume median 16.48M, rising by about 0.8M with every round (12.86M at round 1, 19.36M at round 9) while each round adds about 1 KB of request. The cost grows with the session, not with the store. After 30 rounds one resume takes 32.5M: the session journal holds 63 `replace` lines (224 KB of 236 KB) for a 55 KB transcript, and opening it replays every line into the `RecordMap` (`Journal::consume` and `refresh_index`, about 14%), `SessionStore::load` and the typed hydrate take about 22%, `Sessions::archive` recompresses the whole journal at exit (about 12%, of which `Matcher::prime` for the dictionary is about 2M per call), and `content_hash`/`key_matches` hash every loaded payload record (about 16%, mostly the scalar `ChunkState::compress_block` because the records are shorter than one BLAKE3 chunk). Store open, tool building and psh start are a constant 4M to 5M. (2) A long session (one exec turn of 200 `exec_command` calls, 1.40 MB request, 203 shared records of about 6.7 KB in `records/`): resume median 151.65M. The same 1.37 MB is hashed three times: `Shared::load` checks each blob against its name (17.9M), `EncodedPayload::load_records` checks each payload against its key (15.7M), and `DurableExecution::pool_prefix` keys every prefix item again through `Layout::of` before `stage_tree` finds it known (part of the 21.2M in `prepare_cached_continuation`). Request encoding (`RequestInput::encode`, 14.8M) is the only part that the request bytes require. (3) Measured and not shipped: `RecordKey` hashed its `Blake` and `Chunk` digests with the first 8 bytes instead of SipHash over 32 bytes. Interleaved runs on copies of one 10-round store, 10 resumes each, two passes: 25.44M and 25.41M before, 25.56M and 25.56M after (+0.5%). The `RecordKey::new` samples are the per-record replay, not the hasher. (4) Next, by measured share: key the continuation cache from the payloads that `load_sequence` already keyed so that the first pool after a resume hashes nothing; let one layer verify a shared record (the payload key or the blob name, not both); append a frame for the new journal tail at archive instead of recompressing the restored journal; and replay a journal from its latest `replace` line forward with an index of record locations, so a resume reads the tail instead of every superseded state. Copying a store with `cp -a` changes the identities that `.index-v1` records, so the first two resumes of a copy rebuild the brief index (92.8M and 47.2M at 1,000 sessions): benchmarks of copied stores drop those runs.
- A direct tool call on a hand is bounded by its own run time, and a headless Claude root session on a hand waits for its background jobs before its turn ends (2026-11-15, Georgios: wave 7c, run 3d8f01a9). Before: (1) a direct Claude Bash call with a 300000 to 600000 ms timeout failed after exactly 30 s with "remote operation deadline elapsed; outcome unknown; no retry" (58 calls in 17 attempts of 3d8f01a9), since `requested_yield` read only `yield_time_ms` and a Call named none, so `Client::deadline` was the operation timeout alone (the Worker's `REMOTE_TIMEOUT_MS`, 30000). (2) In compile-compcert, train-fasttext and crack-7z the model ended its turn after a `run_in_background` Bash ("I'll be notified when it completes.") and the session ended with the job still running: a hand's jobs have no bound agent, so no `turn_hold` waited for them, and the finish check fired at that first end. Claude Code 2.1.325 in print mode holds for background shells (`holdForBackgroundShells` is `drain.inputClosed && !maxBudgetUsd && tengu_tidy_sloth`, default on, bounded by `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS`) and sends each `<task-notification>` as the next user message, read from ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.325. Now: `ToolContext::with_run_time` names how long a call may run before its tool answers, `RemoteOperation::Call` carries it as `run_time_ms` (old hands ignore the field), and the client's deadline is the operation timeout plus that run time. Claude's direct Bash sets it with `bash::direct_run_time`: 0 with `run_in_background` (the start answer only), else `timeout` or `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`, at most `MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`, the bounds the Bash tool itself applies. A hand advertises `job_notices` in its catalog and answers `RemoteOperation::Notices { session_id, yield_time_ms }` with `JobNotices { busy, notices }`: the session's ready notices, or after the first notice or the yield, whichever comes first, while a job still owes one (`CodeModeToolset::session_busy`, Claude's `Jobs::session_busy`). `claude_tools::install` with `headless` (the wasm harness passes it) gives a root session with a Code Mode host a `turn_hold` that polls with the session's cell yield (`DEFAULT_YIELD` without one) until a notice arrives, which it steers in with the held wrapper (`notification::reminder`), or no job owes one. Code Mode sessions get the same hold. `State::hold_turn` runs the holds bounded by the deadline's remaining time, and a headless root turn runs them before the finish check, so the finish check fires once, after the last notice. A brain that sees no `job_notices` sends no Notices. Measured with output/wave7c/run.ts in nanocode-ts (a `nanocode hand` built from this tree, the wasm module built from it, a scripted Messages endpoint, operation timeout 30000 ms, one run each): `sleep 40` with `timeout: 300000` returned "started
finished" after 40.7 s (3d8f01a9's arm failed these at 30.0 s); a background `sleep 6` then an end_turn gave 4 requests: the task notification at 6.1 s, then the finish check, then the end, both direct and through an exec cell; with a 20 s turn deadline a `sleep 11` was followed by "Time limit: 8 s of this task's 20 s remain." Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-code-mode, nanocode-tool-host, nanocode-tool-runtime and nanocode-backend-claude natively and the last three for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-tool-runtime -p nanocode-tool-contracts -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-sim`, `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Not passing and not from this change: wasm clippy of nanocode-backend-claude stops at the unused `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT` in environment.rs. Not run: a deployed Worker, and a hand released before this change behind this brain (it advertises no `job_notices`, so the hold is skipped). Files: crates/core/tool-contracts/src/lib.rs, crates/runtime/code-mode/src/{toolset.rs,embedded/{mod,types}.rs,remote/{client,executors,frame,hand,mod,queue}.rs}, crates/runtime/tool-host/src/{policy.rs,embedded/runtime.rs,runtime/{execution,registry}.rs}, crates/integrations/tool-runtime/src/remote/{native.rs,accept/registry.rs}, crates/backends/claude/src/{agent.rs,claude_bash.rs,claude_tools.rs,deadline.rs,defaults.rs,lib.rs,notification.rs,runtime.rs}, crates/backends/claude/tools/src/tools/bash.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/src/hands.rs.

- perf(code-mode): the bootstrap snapshot of a cell without a prelude is built at build time and embedded, and a tool set's definitions are applied by deriving a snapshot from it once per tool set, so the first cell of a process no longer compiles the 34 KB bootstrap (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: Code Mode tool turn peak RSS, build-time snapshot lane). `build.rs` of nanocode-code-mode-engine runs `setup::per_cell()` (crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/setup.rs, shared with the library through `#[path]`) with djs-embed as a build dependency and writes `Snapshot::to_bytes` to `OUT_DIR/code-mode.snap`; `cell.rs` embeds it with `include_bytes!` and loads it with the new `Snapshot::from_static` (djs-embed), which borrows the bytes (`Inner::image` is a `Cow<'static, [u8]>`), checks the frame, the setup hash and the image's `ImageDeps` against this build's `IMAGE_DEPS`, and does not copy or verify the image cell by cell, as djs-prelude's `BASE`. The per-cell setup has no `__nanocodeDefinitions` global: its bootstrap module exports `prepareCell(definitions)`, which runs the bootstrap's `prepareCell` and assigns the module's `let runCell`; the new `Snapshot::derive(key, limits, prepare)` instantiates the shared image, calls `prepareCell` with the tool set's definitions, and takes the image as `Builder::build` does (`move_interp_to_end`, `seal`, image), with the definitions hashed into its setup hash. A prelude still builds its snapshot at run time with the definitions baked in, as before; a build-time image that does not load falls back to compiling (and the `SnapshotStore`) with a warning. Why derive and not definitions per cell: running `prepareCell` in every cell measured +740K instructions per cell (cellbench `cb.sh` empty 81K to 823K), because djs's `Object.defineProperty` costs about 270 fuel (about 32K instructions) per call (15 globals 4,136 fuel, 150 calls 40,962, against 221 and 1,812 for plain assignment), and `prepareCell` calls it for every global and twice per tool; deriving runs it once per tool set, as setup did. Parity: `setup::per_cell().build()` run inside wasm32-wasip1 (node WASI) gives the host-built image byte for byte (318,416 bytes), and the derived image is identical on both (329,400 bytes, same FNV-1a), harness `~/sw/cmsnap/parity`. Gates: the Code Mode tool-call harness (`djscell2-cellconf-main.rs`, with a prelude, 76 lines), the same cells without a prelude plus stack, `console.trace`, `ALL_TOOLS`, `toolSchema`, global-leak and `store`/`load` cells (100 lines), and cellbench `--print` of 11 cell kinds give identical output on 69a43f758 and this change. Measured (hosted Hand under load, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh): cellbench (release) first cell, `tool1 1`, 9 interleaved runs, median: user instructions 14.20M to 2.73M, kernel 7.38M to 6.81M, page faults 581 to 388, process wall 7.9 ms to 3.3 ms; steady state per cell (`cb.sh`, best of 3): empty 81.3K/82.5K, tool1 155.5K/156.5K, seq16 627.5K/628.0K, agent 1.676M/1.677M. - perf(djs): `each_fused` (interp/run/each.rs, from run_hot's `fclosure` decline) runs `arr.f(x => leaf)` for forEach, map, filter, some, every, find, findIndex and reduce without the closure, the loop state or the callback's frame, and `scan` reads the source's dense store as one slice, with a branch-free test per 8 elements for some, every, find and findIndex against a constant (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, callback lane wave 2). What: (1) at `fclosure c; call1` or `fclosure c; push0..3 | push_i8 | push_i32; call2`, when the callee on the stack is a `@fast` each builtin (`each_mode`), the receiver is an Array whose dense store covers its length (map and filter: `plain_species`), and the child template's code is a leaf (`leaf_of`, the wave 1 patterns), the whole call runs in place: the elements go through `scan` and `leaf_eval`, map's and filter's results are written into a result reserved at the length, a capture's Box is written once at the end, and the call's result replaces F and this. It runs only if the fuel covers every element (`fclosure`, the push and the call, plus the body's cost and `CALL_FUEL` per element, leaving fuel above 0), so no yield point lies inside, and it declines with nothing observable changed for a hole, a non-number operand, a TDZ capture, `gc_stress` or a failed allocation (the general path then runs the call; an allocated result is garbage). The fuel charged is the sum the general path charges. (2) `scan` takes the source range and the output range as `[u8; 8]` chunks once instead of a bounds-checked arena read per element. UNTIL with a constant `q` maps the passing set to one range of the biased word (`x = (w ^ key) - lo`, failing iff `(x | x + (2^32 - span)) >> 32 != 0`; `key` is the int tag with the sign bit flipped, or `int(q)` for `===` with the excluded point at 0), OR-folded over 8 elements (about 10 instructions per element as a per-element loop, about 3 folded); KEEP, MAP_TO and FOLD (add, sub) test 8 elements before they write. The element where a scan stops goes through the leaf path as before. Origin: (1) is the wave 1 lane's unshipped `each_fused` with the `new_array_with_length_reserved` signature of 6c4ae4cf5; its SIMD-lane `scan` (fused plus lanes: find 44.9M) was not kept, since the per-element slice scan plus the folded range test measured lower. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, hosted Hand, djsrun on djs-embed, 690c37b3b -> this; QuickJS 2021-03-27 in brackets): find 90.78M -> 37.26M (-59.0%, QuickJS 748.4M: 20.1x faster), some 92.46M -> 38.56M (-58.3%, 1,048.4M: 27.2x), forEach 94.04M -> 66.87M (-28.9%, 1,114.6M: 16.7x), filter 145.76M -> 75.03M (-48.5%, 1,409.1M: 18.8x), map 160.90M -> 101.47M (-36.9%, 1,651.9M: 16.3x), reduce 92.52M -> 67.54M (-27.0%, 1,041.7M: 15.4x); loop 148.72M and empty 0.86M unchanged. Steps on find: fused with the old scan 65.7M, per-element slice scan 45.6M, range test per element 46.5M, folded range test 37.3M. Where find's 37.3M goes (callgrind, per call of 100 elements): `scan` about 600 (the folded test, the slice setup and the tail), `each_fused` itself about 450 (template, flags and capture lookups, `leaf_of` 80, the result), the outer loop body in run_hot (`get_method`, `s +=`, the counter, the decline into `decline_plain`) about 750. map and filter also pay about 870 per call in the allocator's clearing (memset) and collections of the 20,000 results; forEach's and reduce's FOLD still takes about 21 per element, since the 8-element range check of the i64 sum does not vectorize. Checked: test262 subset (3,090 files) 2,535 passing with identical pass sets; the fuel harness (`Instance::step` with `Limits { fuel, slice }`, fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited at slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000) gives the same result, yield count and `fuel_used` as 690c37b3b for the core, each, generator and regexp edge scripts, loop.js, gen.js, err.js, the six callback benches and a new fused edge script (every mode, constants push0..3, i8 and i32, index arguments, int32 overflow, -0, NaN, doubles, strings, BigInts, holes, an index on Array.prototype, a longer length, a named property, a getter, an Array subclass, a species constructor, a Proxy, an array-like, an own method, a replaced Array.prototype.find, a non-callable, thisArg, frozen arrays, empty arrays, 3,000 and 20,000 elements, a capture in its TDZ, a string capture); that script prints the same as 690c37b3b. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. - feat(claude): the refusal fallback model stays the session's model across turns, as Claude Code 2.1.325 keeps it, and `ClaudeBuilder::refusal_fallback_scope(RefusalFallbackScope::ReturnOnce)` instead returns to the main model on the request after the one the fallback served, and goes back to the fallback for the rest of the session when the main model refuses again (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 refusal-return lane: in all 24 nano rows of crack-7z-hash, dna-assembly, dna-insert and protein-assembly in runs 1fbd4a11 and 5f48d05d, the second or third call to claude-opus-5-5 ended with stop_reason refusal and every later call went to the fallback, claude-opus-5 for the biology tasks and claude-opus-4-8 for crack-7z-hash; 13 passed and 11 failed, a third of nano's 33 failed rows). Upstream, read from the pinned executable (claude-code-linux-x64 2.1.325, sha256 0dc4f4a9a165fc60746d7ae8489712e5fc352f1e7ad4eb22e7141bd0812eb0cf, the one `prompts/upstream.json` names): on a `fallback_request` in the main thread, the query loop sets its loop override (`ho=B.fallbackModel`) and `options.mainLoopModel`, and `moveTo(fallback,{kind:"refusal"})` writes the app state's `mainLoopModel` and calls `replaceRefusalFallbackModelLatch` with the previous model. The latch is cleared only by `unlatchRefusalFallbackModel("session_transition")` (a new session, such as /clear or a fork, which `ht()` restores to the previous override, telemetry `tengu_refusal_fallback_latch_reset`) or `("model_pick")` (the user picks a model), and a resumed session latches again (`tengu_refusal_fallback_resume_latch` `model_latch_only`). A subagent's loop keeps the fallback only for that loop. So Claude Code is sticky for the session. Nanocode kept it only for the turn: `Cursor::template.model` took the fallback, and the next turn's cursor was built from `State::model`. What: `Conversation::fallback_latch` (serde default `Main`, skipped when `Main`, so older checkpoints read unchanged) is one of `Main`, `Serving { fallback, main }`, `Returned` and `Latched(model)`. A refusal that `refusal_fallback` maps moves it to `Latched` under `Session` (the default), and under `ReturnOnce` to `Serving` from `Main`, to `Latched` from `Returned` or `Latched`, and keeps `Serving` with the new fallback from `Serving`. The first response that is not a refusal while `Serving` sets `Returned` and puts the main model back into the cursor's template. A new turn's template takes the latch's model when the agent is at lineage depth 0, and a subagent (depth above 0) resets the latch at each turn, as upstream's per-loop override. A fork, a side conversation and a rewind into a new session reset it, as upstream's session transition does. `RefusalFallbackScope` is exported from nanocode-backend-claude (`nanocode::claude::RefusalFallbackScope`), so nanocode-ts can set it in its `harness.configure` closure, and subagents inherit it through the builder recipe. nanocode-ts is unchanged. Not matched: upstream subagents spawned after the main thread latched inherit `mainLoopModel`, the fallback, while nanocode's spawn still takes `State::model`. Measured with output/refusal-return (ignored): a harness that builds `Claude::builder(client, "claude-opus-5-5").headless(true)` with one Bash tool and runs two turns against server.py, a Messages SSE mock that answers tool_use until three tool results follow the turn's PROMPT, then end_turn, and stop_reason refusal with `stop_details.category` bio at the request indexes given. Each turn ends with the headless finish check request. M is claude-opus-5-5, F is claude-opus-5, and `|` separates the turns. Master 690c37b3b: refuse at 1, `M M F F F F | M M M M M`. Refuse at 1 and 3, `M M F F F F F | M M M M M` (request 3 is the fallback's own refusal, answered by the resend recovery). This change, default and `Session`: `M M F F F F | F F F F F` and `M M F F F F F | F F F F F`. `ReturnOnce`: refuse at 1, `M M F M M M | M M M M M`. Refuse at 1 and 3, `M M F M F F F | F F F F F`. Every turn ended ok. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (wasm32 reports only the existing unused `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT`), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`, `cd output/refusal-return && cargo build && ./run.sh`, and `./run.sh <base binary> base` for master. Not run: a Terminal-Bench rerun with `ReturnOnce`. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/{agent.rs,agent/durable.rs,lib.rs}.
- perf(platform, executor): `spawn_task`, `spawn_joined`, `spawn_on` and both `spawn`s box the future through a private `Pinned::pinned` (a non-inline default trait method) before anything generic sees it and are `#[inline]`; `Handle::block_on` and `Runtime::block_on` pin the future as `Pin<&mut dyn Future>` and run one non-generic-in-F `block_on_pinned`; mpp's proxy hands `server::serve` boxed handler futures, and nanocode-cli awaits its seven `Box::pin(..)` futures through `FutureExt::boxed` (2026-11-15, cold release build tail, nanocode-cli unit). Why: rustc makes every closure and coroutine body a local copy in each codegen unit that reaches it, and places an instance of an upstream generic (`Driven<F>::poll`, `spawn_task::<F>`, `park_on::<F>`, `Pin<Box<F>>::poll`, `Pin<&mut F>::poll`) in a unit named after that generic's module, so every spawned or blocked-on future tree was copied into the executor, platform and core::pin units of every downstream crate: in nanocode-cli 1.27M of 3.03M pre-optimization IR lines were cross-unit copies, and the three largest units held 1.26M. A dyn coercion inside `pinned` (placed by the future's own type, so in the module that defines the async block) or inside the inlined caller leaves one copy per tree, in its own module's unit. No behavior change: the same futures are polled through a vtable, with one more allocation per spawn (two on the host path, whose `spawn_with` boxes again). Measured on nanocode-cli's lib (cold `cargo rustc --release -p nanocode-cli --lib -Zself-profile`, 5-core hosted Hand, base 498e20459 / new / base / new, load 1.8): LLVM time 43.0 and 43.7 s before, 37.4 and 37.9 s after; largest unit 7.43 and 7.49 s before, 3.95 and 4.08 s after; IR 3.03M to 2.59M lines (cross-unit copies 1.27M to 0.90M); frontend (to the first codegen_module) 7.37 and 7.24 s before, 6.81 and 6.93 s after. Modeled on 16 cores (frontend, then the serial codegen_module feed, then each unit's LLVM time on 16 workers): 15.74 and 15.09 s before, 11.13 and 11.40 s after (-27%); the codegen part 8.37 and 7.85 s to 4.32 and 4.46 s (-46%), so the unit is now mostly frontend (type check 1.2 s, borrow check 1.8 s, MIR for metadata and the mono collector 3.4 s). On dev-georgios that is about 13.8 to 10 s at the end of the critical path (est., not measured there). What stays: mpp's `Flow<Wallet>`, `Proxy<Wallet>` and durability's `SessionStore` coroutines are still compiled in the cli (mpp 235k, durability and durability-core 250k IR lines with copies); a non-closure boxed entry point on the store's async API would move them upstream. Gate on 498e20459: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, wasm32 checks of nanocode-platform, nanocode-executor, nanocode-mpp and nanocode-cli, nanocode-sim release build, `sweep.sh 0 2000 4` (2000 passed) and `--tidy` clean; on 690c37b3b nanocode-sim does not build without this change either (`nanocode_executor::dns::Wire` is private). Files: crates/core/platform/src/native.rs, crates/core/executor/src/runtime.rs, crates/integrations/mpp/src/proxy.rs, bin/nanocode/src/lib.rs.

- perf(djs): `split_now` finds the separator of a one-`CHAR` or one-`CLASS` RegExp, alone or under a greedy `+`, with `regexp::Simple` instead of `exec_in`, and `string::substring` copies a range of a flat one-byte string with `Heap::alloc_latin1_range` instead of joining one piece (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 3; the matcher is the wave 2 sub-lane's ~/sw/djscell2rx-split.patch, validated and landed here). Why: `split(/\s+/)` ran the backtracking matcher once per field; in the `sh` cell regex split was about 1.36M of 2.27M instructions. What: `Simple::of` accepts a program with no `u`/`v` mode, one capture (the match), no anchor mode and a first set, whose anchored code is `SAVE 0`, one `CHAR` or `CLASS` (or a `STAR` of 1..inf greedy last over it) and `SAVE 1 MATCH`; `search` scans for the first position of the first set (`in_first`, now shared with `Machine`), returns `None` (fall back to `exec_in`) if the run does not start there, and charges exactly the fuel `exec_in` charges for the same match (scan length, plus 4 for one unit or 6 plus the run length under `+`), and only when that fuel is below what is left, so a match that would run out goes to `exec_in` and suspends as before. `split_now` reads captures beyond the match from the state only on the `exec_in` path. `alloc_latin1_range` (heap/string.rs) copies `s[a..b)` of a `Str8` cell within the arena when `substring_slice` declines (short pieces). Instructions per cell (cellbench as above, base a06bce803 plus the previous entry's change): sh 2,021,122 -> 1,597,182 (-21.0%), seq 969,319 -> 969,164, json 1,370,423 -> 1,370,358, edit 1,063,020 -> 1,063,323, agent 1,675,453 -> 1,675,413; from a06bce803 the typical suite (sh, seq, json, edit, agent) is 7,371,767 -> 6,675,440 (-9.4%). djs benches within 0.07% (all lower or equal). Checked: two split differentials against `exec_in` (base) give identical hashes: 3,000 random strings over Latin-1 and two-byte whitespace, digits, word characters and separators with 24 patterns and limits, and 4,000 strings with 37 patterns (including `u`, `v`, `y`, `g`, `m`, `s`, captures, lazy and counted quantifiers, anchors, `\b`, surrogates) and lengths to 17,000 code units (past the 16,384-step fast-entry cap) with limits up to 2^32+2; the fuel harness (ten fuel/slice pairs over eleven scripts including both differentials and a split benchmark) identical; test262 subset 2,535, identical pass set; the 17-cell tool-call harness identical; each cellbench cell's output byte-identical; clippy as above, native and wasm32; djs-prelude's base remade. - perf(djs): `regexp::pristine` caches its realm checks against the tracked image prefix, and `write_escaped_latin1` copies an escaped JSON string 8 bytes at a time (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 3). Why: `pristine` (builtins/regexp.rs) read %RegExp.prototype%'s `exec`, @@match, nine flag getters and `constructor` and %RegExp%[@@species] on every call, about 2,700 instructions, and the String fast paths read one more method after it; the `sh` cell calls `split(/\s+/)` 100 times, 271k of its 2.27M. There was no write counter for value writes to those objects (`proto_epoch` counts key additions and prototype changes only). What: the arena's `Tracked` prefix (D2065-style page tracking that `Arena::restore` relies on, debug-asserted to see every write below `end`) gets a `stamp`, bumped by every `note` and by `restore`, and a `kept` value; `Arena::keep_prefix` remembers the stamp and `Arena::prefix_kept` says no write below `end` happened since. `pristine` still checks the receiver itself (class, prototype, own keys, `lastIndex`) every time; when `prefix_kept` holds it skips the realm part, otherwise it runs it and, if it passes, the four String-facing methods (@@replace, @@search, @@split, @@matchAll) are also the originals and every cell it read (the realm cell, its installed-intrinsics array, %RegExp.prototype%, %RegExp% and the constructors object with their property blocks and accessor pairs: `Heap::storage_below`) lies below the tracked `end`, it calls `keep_prefix`. Any later write to one of them is below `end`, so it bumps the stamp; a new `track` (each restore of an image) starts with nothing kept; without the `embed` feature there is no tracking and nothing is cached. `symbol_method` (builtins/fast.rs) skips its `original_method` read when `prefix_kept` holds. `write_escaped_latin1` (json/parse.rs) used `find_byte` and `copy_from_slice` per run between escapes; it now copies whole words into the exactly-sized destination while no byte of the word is a backslash (the lowest flag of the zero test is exact), then decodes the escape. Instructions per cell (output/cellbench on the code-mode-engine native host, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, (1,200 - 200 cells)/1,000, best of 3, base a06bce803): sh 2,267,196 -> 2,021,111 (-10.9%), seq 983,402 -> 969,345 (-1.4%), json 1,378,838 -> 1,370,469 (-0.6%), edit 1,067,089 -> 1,063,018, agent 1,675,242 -> 1,675,466, empty, tool1, seq16 and par16 within 0.2%; each cell's printed output is byte-identical. djs benches (djsrun, best of 5): find, forEach, some, filter, map and reduce -0.03% to -0.06%, loop, gen, gennext and err within 0.001%. Checked: a RegExp patch cell (output of `cellbench pristine.js 2 --print`: each of @@split, @@replace, @@search, @@match, @@matchAll, `exec`, the ten flag getters, %RegExp%[@@species] and `constructor` replaced and restored, an added key, `setPrototypeOf(RegExp.prototype, null)`, an accessor @@split, a non-number `lastIndex`, an own `exec`, across two cells of one host) is identical to base; a JSON differential (6,000 random strings with every escape, control characters, Latin-1, two-byte and surrogate text, lengths to 400, parsed back and compared) has no mismatch and the same hash; test262 subset 2,535 passing, identical pass set; the fuel harness (fuelrun, ten fuel/slice pairs over eleven scripts including the JSON differential) identical; the 17-cell tool-call harness (output/cellconf) identical; `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -p djs-embed -p djs-prelude -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; djs-prelude's base remade with scripts/base.sh. Considered and not done: keeping JSON.parse's per-depth shape hints across parses (about 1k per parse here, and the hints are arena offsets a collection or an image restore would leave stale) and serializing tool input on the host (about 2.3k of `stringify_fast_at` and 1.8k of `Ser::finish` per call, measured with callgrind on seq16). A call with no job or no task file returns nothing, so the running line stays as a06bce803 prints it. The same clippy on wasm32 stops at `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT` in environment.rs, a dead constant on that target that this change does not touch.
- perf(executor): on Linux, name lookups run their DNS exchange on the reactor with nonblocking UDP sockets (and `TcpStream::connect_one` for truncated replies), and only the read of /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf runs on one `nanocode-lookup` blocking-pool thread (pool of one, the pool's 10 s keep-alive); a read serves every lookup requested before it started (`dns::System::request` ticket against the `covers` count it read at start), so no lookup uses files read before it was requested. glibc processes cap malloc arenas at one (`mallopt(M_ARENA_MAX, 1)` in `nanocode_sys::entry::prepare`) (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: kernel instructions against fx 0.0.16, kernel-work lane wave 2). Why: `perf record -g -e instructions:k` of the bench one-shot (master 69a43f758 dist+BOLT under tools/netguard.sh, 4 runs, symbols from /proc/kallsyms) put 26% of kernel instructions on the four `nanocode-lookup` threads that start for the MCP and gateway hosts (gateway.tempo-dev.workers.dev twice, api.inference.boundless.network, mercator.sh): each thread is a clone, a 2 MB stack, a 128 MB glibc arena reservation (mmap, two munmaps, mprotect, from the first glibc malloc in `pthread_getattr_np`), an allocator segment, and two opens and closes on the virtiofs root (`fuse_flush`/`fuse_release`). After: 5 threads instead of 8, the lookup thread 0.30M kernel instructions instead of 0.59M, and three reads instead of four (the hosts are requested at different times, so the ticket shares the files only between overlapping requests). Measured on the hosted Hand at load 3 to 30 from other lanes, `NC_BIN` = `build-cli.sh`'s front and agent of 69a43f758 and of this change, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh and tools/netguard.sh: `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults` of one-shots alternating the builds, 5 batches of 30 each, medians base then this: kernel 11.48M/10.32M, 8.81M/8.15M, 9.03M/8.35M, 10.05M/9.61M, 11.07M/10.63M (every batch lower, 4 to 10%), page faults 520/488, 516/486, 519/486, 528/488, 519/491, user 3.72M to 3.89M in both; 5 interleaved passes (8 one-shots and 2 first frames per build per pass, then bench/cli rows), medians of passes: one-shot kernel 12.26M to 10.90M, page faults 522 to 486.5, user 3.76M and 3.81M; first frame kernel 15.63M to 11.83M, page faults 581 to 519, user 4.73M to 4.68M; peak RSS one-shot 6.79 and 6.82 MB, first frame 8.57 and 8.31 MB, tool turn (10 steps) 11.48 and 11.62 MB, `--version` 0.30 MB in both (all within spread). Kernel instructions vary 30% between passes with the Hand's load, page faults do not. Checked: strace of a networked one-shot shows the AAAA and A queries sent and answered on the worker thread and the HTTPS connects that follow; `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-executor`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Not done in this change, measured: the `cua-driver` search (15 statx on the worker, about 11k kernel instructions each on this Hand, 0.17M) cannot move to the first computer-use call without offering the computer tools to the model before the probe says the driver is installed; the `nanocode-durability-store` thread (0.14M, MemoryStore's driver) runs on its own thread since 30ac1a33f for the 25,000-subagent groups; `MADV_RANDOM` and `MADV_COLD` leave fault-around on (`should_fault_around` reads only `fault_around_bytes` and the userfaultfd flags), so cold text needs a layout change, not an madvise. Commands: `sh ab.sh 30` and `sh passes.sh` (one.sh, ff.sh, rss.sh) in the lane's scratch directory, `perf record -g -e instructions:k -c 2000` with a kallsyms categorizer. Files: crates/core/executor/src/dns.rs, crates/core/executor/src/net.rs, crates/core/sys/src/entry.rs, crates/core/sys/src/libc/linux_gnu.rs.
- A yield or a result with nothing printed lists every nested call that returned since the last yield with its exit code and duration, and every call still running with its description, its running time and, when the toolset can give it, the latest output of that call (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1, Nano Claude arm on Opus 5.5). In 39 attempts of that arm, 79 of 83 Code Mode yields said only that the script printed nothing while nested Bash commands ran (3,439 s of cell time); train-fasttext a00523 ran three or four trainings one after another in one cell (cells of 901 s and 746 s) and saw no result before the whole batch ended, so it could not stop at a model that was good enough; and 25 cells ended with nested output but no text, which returned an empty result. Before, a yield with no text gave the count of calls that returned since the last yield, the tail of the latest only, and the running calls as counts by name (`Nested calls still running: 2 Bash.`); a result with no text gave nothing. Now each returned call adds one line (`- Bash exit code 3 after 2.0 s`; `returned` or `failed` for a call whose structured result has no `exit_code`), the latest call's tail stays, and each running call is one line with the `description` of its input and its running time (`- Bash (loop b), running for 4.0 s`). A completed cell that printed nothing and has calls that returned since the last yield gets the same summary, which opens with `The script printed nothing.` when the cell never yielded. `CodeModeToolset` gains `running_output(call_id)`, by default nothing; when it answers, the running call's line ends with `, its latest output:` and that output, or `, nothing printed yet`. No new bound: the list of returned calls and each running output go through `output_tail` (`TERMINATED_OUTPUT_BYTES`, the bound the latest call's tail already has), and `max_output_tokens` cuts the whole text as before. A yield or result with printed text is unchanged. The text is nanocode's own Code Mode text, not upstream Codex or Claude Code text. Checked with output/yield-tail (gak-9, macOS arm64, debug `nanocode exec --harness claude --model claude-opus-5-5 --thinking high --ephemeral --no-tempo-tools` against mock.py, a local Messages SSE mock that sends one exec and then a wait for every yield and records each tool result), before at 6ecd42e3e and after with this change: `pair` (two nested Bash loops that echo once a second for 4 and 6 s, `yield_time_ms` 1500) yielded `Nested calls still running: 2 Bash.` at 1.5 s and returned an empty result at 6.1 s, and now yields both calls with their descriptions at 1.5 s, `- Bash exit code 0 after 4.0 s` with loop a's tail at 4.1 s, and ends with `- Bash exit code 0 after 6.0 s` and b1 to b6; `batch` (three 2 s Bash calls in a row, the second exits 3, `yield_time_ms` 2500) now shows `- Bash exit code 3 after 2.0 s` at 5.0 s and the third result at the end, where the result was empty; `printing` (a cell that calls `text` after each call) returns `step 1` and `step 2` byte for byte as before. The running output needs a toolset that answers `running_output`: Claude's Bash keeps each command's output in its task file, which only claude_bash.rs can find by call ID, so the policy that reads it (the last `STALL_TAIL_BYTES` of the file of the running job whose `call_id` matches) and the forwarding through `CodeModeToolPolicy` and `ToolRegistry` are not in this change (output/yield-tail/provider.patch, 69 lines in tool-host and claude_bash.rs). With that patch applied, `pair` shows `- Bash (loop a), running for 1.5 s, its latest output:` with a1 and a2, the same for loop b with b1 and b2, and loop b's b1 to b5 at 4.1 s; `batch` shows `nothing printed yet` for a training 0.5 s in. Not run: a model, so the effect on how soon a model stops a batch is not measured. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode`, again with `--features local-cells --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode -- -D warnings` both ways, and `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-backend-codex -p nanocode-tool-runtime`. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/{toolset.rs,code_mode/mod.rs}.
- perf(durability): an `EncodedPayload` built by `encode` or by the new `EncodedPayload::from_record` keeps its inline record (`=` and the JSON) as one `Arc<str>` and reads the JSON as the slice after the `=`, so `stage_tree` stages that same allocation as the `StoreRecord` value instead of copying `=` plus the content (2026-11-15, heap lane: one live copy per history item). The codex request encoder's shared prefix (`SharedPrefix`, responses/request.rs) now holds each prefix item in that record form and writes the slice after the `=` into the request, and `shared_prefix_json` becomes `shared_prefix_records` (doc-hidden; its only caller is `ContinuationCache::sync_prefix`, which builds payloads with `from_record`), so the pooled prefix record, the durable payload and the request piece are one allocation. `from_json` and `keyed` still take bare JSON and copy at staging as before. Stored formats and keys are unchanged: the record bytes are the same `=`-prefixed text, and payloads read back from a store still hold bare JSON. Measured with the GlobalAlloc tracer (~/sw/heapprof/tracer.patch, release with line tables), base c8974f2bd against this change, 3 interleaved traced runs each of `~/sw/heapprof/run.sh` (bench/cli suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc, h=ncdirect, netguard): global live peak 464,701 / 464,862 / 464,973 B to 452,232 / 451,929 / 452,403 B (-12.5 KB); the durability theme 87.8 KB to 75.2 KB live; the 24 `=` copies of stage_tree (payload.rs, 14.8 KB live) are gone and the encoder's prefix site holds 34.7 KB (instructions item 18.0 KB, tools item 8.3 KB shared with its record, the namespaced tools item the request sends 8.2 KB) where it held 26.5 KB plus 8.2 KB. Request bodies: 11 requests per run, lengths equal (first 29,007, last 32,540) and bytes equal after normalizing UUIDs, exec chunk IDs and wall times, the same normalization under which two base runs are equal. Plain release (same profile, peak.py sampler, 5 interleaved runs): anonymous RSS median 1,600 KB both; total RSS 31,584 to 32,860 KB, all in file-backed pages (29,976 to 31,260 KB) of these non-BOLT binaries, whose layout differs per build. Not done, measured on this change's profile: the developer instructions item (18 KB) is past `INLINE_BYTES`, so durability stores it as three content-defined chunks (18.4 KB live) that are copies of slices of the encoder's record; sharing them needs `StoreRecord::value` to hold a slice of a shared string, which changes its type for every store and reader again. Keeping instructions inline instead would change their key and fail `verify_record` in earlier builds. The other largest sites at the peak are the instructions item's own text (build_request_prefix, 18.0 KB), the HTTP read buffer (wire.rs `fill`, 16 KB), the psh engine (66 KB, mostly a 13 KB `spawn_with_id` future and variable tables per shell start), std's 8 KB stdin buffer from `piped_prompt`'s `fill_buf`, the 8 KB `BufWriter` of `stream_turn`, the 12 KB epoll event buffer, and 16 `OnceLock` encodings per `HistorySegment` (4.6 KB over 10 segments), so the ~350 KB peak needs several unrelated changes. Checks: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p nanocode-durability-core -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-codex`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps` on those crates (no new warnings), `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 200 2` 200/200 passed, 0 panics. Files: crates/core/durability/src/payload.rs, crates/backends/codex/client/src/responses/{request,mod}.rs, crates/backends/codex/src/durability/context.rs.
- perf(durability): `StoreRecord::value` is an `Arc<str>`, so a record's content is one allocation shared by everything that holds it: the commit path (`Pool::ensure` keeps `added`, `SharedStore::commit` and `MemoryStore::commit` take `to_vec` of the borrowed records) clones only the reference, `MemoryStore`'s `Tables::records` keeps the `Arc` it receives, and `Pool::hold`, `RecordCache` and `StagedState::unstored` take the same `Arc` instead of copying the text into a new one (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 heap-site lane: MemoryStore and Pool copies). Why: the 10-step direct tool turn profile of 9c49d6f98 (~/sw/heapprof) showed each pooled prefix record held twice at the heap peak, once as the `String` the memory store cloned from the commit (store.rs:122, 32.9 KB live) and once as the `Arc<str>` `Pool::hold` copied from it (pool.rs:288, 26.8 KB live), with 386 copy calls per turn. `StateCommit` keeps its borrowed shape: with shared values a borrowed commit costs a reference count per record, and the payload copy it still makes is the one state payload the store must own. Readers that return `String` (`read_records`, `OneLog`, the JSONL shared-record loader) copy at the read as before, and the JSONL and SQL row formats are unchanged (serde writes `Arc<str>` as a string). Measured with the GlobalAlloc tracer (~/sw/heapprof/tracer.patch, release with line tables, `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=line-tables-only`, -j1), base 7d91ed29c against this change, 3 interleaved traced runs of `~/sw/heapprof/run.sh` each (bench/cli suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc, h=ncdirect, netguard), sites summed over durability/src: live at the global peak 98.7-103.3 KB to 72.3 KB (store.rs clone 32.9 KB and pool.rs 26.8 KB gone, payload.rs stage_tree now owns the one shared copy, 67.6 KB), durability allocations per turn 270-281 KB to 183 KB; global heap peak 646.2 KB (2 of 3 runs; 620.1 KB in one) to 619.7-619.8 KB (all 3). Request bytes identical in all runs (first 28,999, last 32,532, 11 requests). Peak RSS of plain release builds (same profile, 5 interleaved runs each, peak.py sampler): median 32,064 KB to 31,848 KB and anonymous 1,828 KB to 1,768 KB, within the run-to-run spread of these non-BOLT binaries. Checks: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p nanocode-durability-core -p nanocode-durability -p nanocode-agent`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps` on the changed crates (no new warnings), `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 200 2` 200/200 passed, 0 panics. Files: crates/core/durability/src/{store,payload,staged,row,sql,kv}.rs, crates/runtime/durability/src/{memory,pool,record_cache}.rs, crates/runtime/durability/src/catalog/store/transfer.rs, crates/runtime/agent/src/one_log.rs, crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/{lib,migrate,shared}.rs, crates/integrations/agent-host/src/cell_journals.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/src/{model,workload}.rs.
- feat(claude): a headless Claude agent (`ClaudeHarness::headless(true)`, which the Claude runtime now passes to `ClaudeBuilder::headless` on native and WebAssembly) checks its work once before it finishes a turn: the first time in a turn that a root session ends with `end_turn` and no tool calls, the agent adds a user message with nanocode's own `<system-reminder>` text (`crates/backends/claude/src/finish_check.rs`) and continues, and the next end is the turn's end (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 lane finish-check). Why: of the 13 nano verifier failures in run 1fbd4a11, dna-assembly a00397 claimed `**primers.fasta written**` for /root/primers.fasta while the cwd was /app, make-mips-interpreter a00269 and a00447 left a late-run /tmp/frame.bmp that the checker reads (Claude Code removed it in every attempt), mteb-retrieve a00281 ended with `Decision for you: ...` instead of a choice, and dna-insert and protein-assembly claimed success that their checks refused. The text says nobody will reply and asks for four checks: every output the task names at that exact path (a relative path against the working directory), the task's own check or a direct test run again, scratch files removed where outputs or checks may read them, and an open choice made and written; it names no task. It is modelled on the Codex `<persistence>` guard, but fires on every first end, not only on a message that admits incomplete work, because the failures above claimed success. Rules: once per turn (`Cursor::finish_checked`, serde default, so earlier checkpoints load), only when `headless` is set (the arm is unchanged without it), only in the root session (`lineage.root_session_id == session_id`; a subagent's result goes to its parent), and not once the deadline module's last reminder point has passed (`Reminders::last_passed`: all of `REMINDER_PERCENTS` elapsed, 90% today), so a turn that is almost out of time ends without the extra call. It runs before the `Stop` lifecycle event, so a Stop hook sees only the real end and keeps its own once-only `stop_hook_active` continuation. Checked with output/finish-check-agent (a `Claude::builder` against a local Messages SSE mock that answers a prompt with one `Bash` call and anything else with `end_turn` text, run.sh, 2026-11-15), model calls per run and notices in the final request: interactive 2 and 0; headless 3 and 1; headless with two turns in one session 6 and 2 (one per turn); headless with a deadline at 50% 3 and 1; headless with a deadline at 95% 2 and 0; interactive with a Stop hook that blocks once 3 and 0 (hook called with `stop_hook_active` false, then true); headless with that hook 4 and 1 (finish check, then the hook's two calls). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (one existing `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT` dead-code warning on wasm), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`. Hosts: nanocode exec already passes `config.headless` to `ClaudeHarness::headless`; nanocode-ts's `claude_harness` does not call `ClaudeHarness::headless` yet, and nanoeval's `App.create` does not set `headless`, so the Terminal-Bench nano arm takes this only after both do.

Every djs-core, djs-libm or prelude change must rerun base.sh; nanocode-sim --tidy and the const assert both catch a stale image.
- perf(cli), measured and not shipped: a static glibc link of the Linux CLI with non-lite BOLT, now that NSS is gone (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, static-glibc lane 2). Nothing in the build changes. Build: master 21c76f9e7 with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 LLVM_BOLT=/usr/lib/llvm-23/bin/llvm-bolt scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` (the dynamic dist+BOLT baseline, `__hot_end` 0xd98444, 46,932,744 bytes), then the same objects and rodata order relinked `-static -nostartfiles` with crt1.o, crti.o, crtbegin.o ... crtend.o, crtn.o (~/sw/static/relink.py staticnr). What links: the LTO object no longer references getaddrinfo, getpwnam_r, getpwuid_r or any resolver code, and `nm` of the static binary shows no `__res_context_query`, `getaddrinfo`, `getpwnam_r`, `getpwuid_r` or `__nss_*`. dlopen, `_dl_open` and `__libc_dlopen_mode` still link, because std's weak lookups call `dlsym` and libc.a's dlsym.o pulls in the static dl support. gdb breakpoints on all 1,301 libc functions over startup, first frame, one-shot and both tool turns hit `_dl_sym` and `_dl_catch_error`, never `_dl_open`, `__libc_dlopen_mode` or `_dl_map_object`. BOLT outside `-lite` now runs on the static binary with three fixes: (1) `__restore_rt`'s and `_dl_tlsdesc_undefweak`'s FDEs start at their symbols (~/sw/static/fde-cli.py), (2) handle_amd's PIC jump table is handled by BOLT itself (it forces `-jump-tables=move`), so neither `-skip-funcs` nor an order was needed, (3) lld fills gaps between libc's input sections with int3 after glibc's own NOP padding, which BOLT rejects as bad padding (`__strncpy_sse2_unaligned`: "cannot ignore non-empty function in current mode"), so the trailing run of 0xcc before each function symbol is rewritten to 0x90 (228,361 bytes in 28,074 gaps). The libc order comes from a fresh gdb trace of the static binary (first call per function across the bench parts, 308 functions) with every ifunc variant of each traced string function placed beside it, since glibc picks the variant per CPU (this Hand picks the AVX-512 memcpy, the 37b42b7f5-era order named other variants and no posix_spawn path). BOLT then runs with the build's layout and `-reorder-functions=user`, that order first and the build's startup.order after it: 5,793 functions pinned, all 334 traced libc functions in hot text, `__hot_end` 0xda9514, binary 47,931,144 bytes. Measured with bench/cli (cli-bench 3e70e983e) under tools/netguard.sh, both binaries in the same run (`BENCH_NC_VARIANTS=ncstatic=...`, rounds rotated), three passes of `suite.mjs --parts=firstframe,oneshot,tools --steps=10 --rounds=4 --toolrounds=3 --only=nc,ncstatic`, then oneshot and firstframe with `--rounds=3` under `/usr/lib/linux-tools/6.8.0-149-generic/perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k`, hosted Hand at load 2 to 4. Medians, dynamic then static: RSS 1 s after the first frame 4.74 and 6.03 MB (n=12, ranges 4.41 to 4.97 and 5.95 to 6.69), one-shot peak 6.61 and 6.45 MB (n=12), first-frame peak 6.09 and 5.76 MB, 10-step direct tool turn peak 7.79 and 8.51 MB (n=9), Code Mode 11.32 and 11.75 MB (n=9), CPU per step direct 1.81 and 1.78 ms, Code Mode 2.43 and 2.29 ms, one-shot CPU 4.3 and 2.7 ms. Instructions (n=9): one-shot user 4.12M and 3.69M, kernel 8.18M and 4.74M, first frame user 4.70M and 4.48M, kernel 9.84M and 5.86M. Why it is not shipped: no dynamic loader saves 40% of kernel instructions and 5 to 10% of user instructions on every start, but resident memory goes up 1.3 MB after the first frame and 0.4 to 0.7 MB in the tool turns, which are the rows this track optimizes. A probe that maps the TUI's residency per section (pagemap) 2.5 s after start shows where the static binary touches more than the dynamic binary and libc.so together: the original `.rodata` 2,536 against 2,356 KB (libc's tables and strings are placed by the linker without an order), `.eh_frame` 112 against 44 KB, `.data`, `.bss` and `.data.rel.ro` 84 against 40 KB, and 80 to 500 KB more `.text` and `.text.cold`. Next, if static is retried: order libc's rodata and data next to the hot rodata (rodata-cli.py sees only the Rust objects), find which startup code walks `.eh_frame`, and check the anonymous rows under the harness. Scripts are on the hosted Hand in ~/sw/static2 (static.sh, gapfix.py, libtrace.py, order.py, bench.sh, analyze.py) for the lane's duration.

Instructions are unchanged within noise.
- perf(types-core): `JsonSchema` holds a tool schema either as a `Value` or as static JSON that `json_schema!` compacts and validates at compile time, and the codex standard tools, job_start and job_kill, runners, the MCP tool search and hands use it (2026-11-15, structural lane). Before, each of these schemas was a `serde_json::Value` tree that `json!` built on the first `definition()` call (and `RunnerManagement::definition` built it again on every call), although a request only serializes the schema and `unified_exec_output_schema` is never sent. `json_schema!` stringifies its tokens, removes whitespace outside strings in a `const fn`, and checks the result against the JSON grammar in a second `const fn`, so a non-JSON token, a Rust-only escape or a trailing comma fails the build. The bytes go into a `static StaticSchema`. `Serialize` writes them through `RawValue` with no `Value`, and `as_value()` or `shared()` parses them once into a `OnceLock` only when a caller reads the tree (claude input schemas, code-mode descriptions, routed tools that add `workdir`). `PartialEq` compares two static schemas by address first, so the prompt-cache and request-prefix checks stay cheap. With `preserve_order` on (the CLI build) the compact text has the same key order as the old `json!` output: the request dumps of one direct 10-step tool turn (`DUMP=` on the fake model, 11 requests, base and new traced builds of d9d958224) have equal lengths, an equal `tools` array, and differ only in the random message ids. Heap, one direct 10-step tool turn under `~/sw/heapprof` (tracer.patch, release with line tables, `run.sh BIN OUT TRACE`, `tr.py`): on master ebfe46d58, which already has 2546bcb80 and a7f2b9b46, the live peak goes from 551,450 to 491,478 bytes (-59,972, -10.9%) and from 3,075 to 2,512 blocks, and the tool-definition theme from 77,648 to 17,401 bytes live (149,861 to 61,184 allocated). On d9d958224, where `RoutedTool::definition` still cloned every schema and so parsed the static text, the peak goes from 646,359 to 615,753 bytes. The 17 KB left are description `Arc<str>` copies, the `ToolSearch` description and the routed `workdir` clones.
