- feat(hand): a direct tool call on a hand (a `RemoteOperation::Call` whose call id has no `/code-`) returns the session's background job notices after its output, and a Bash job that such a call starts says "You will be notified when it completes." as Claude Code does (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 claude-direct lane). Why: on a hand the Claude jobs have no bound agent, so `Jobs::watch` answered `Watch::Reported` ("an exec or wait call ... reports it"), and the notice waited for a Code Mode cell that a direct session never runs. What: `ToolRuntime::session_notices` reads the policies' notices as Code Mode cells do, `NativeSession::call` appends them as text blocks to the output of a direct call, and `Jobs::watch` keeps `Reported` for calls from cells and for calls without an id. Checked with nanocode-ts output/claude-direct/run.ts and a debug `nanocode hand` from this tree: the background Bash answers with the upstream line, and the next Bash, 4 s later, returns `y` and then the `<task-notification>` (completed, exit code 0, `Output:` bgdone). A Code Mode run of the same jobs (`codemode-bg`) keeps the exec-or-wait text and still delivers the notice in the cell. - feat(claude): a `ClaudeHarness` with `direct_tools_for` offers Claude Code's tools directly in a WebAssembly session whose tools run on a hand (a Code Mode host), in place of only `exec` and `wait` (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 claude-direct lane). Why: direct tools beat Code Mode by 6.4 points on the Codex pair (entry of the Codex default below), and nanocode-ts could not run the same test for Claude. `ClaudeHarness::build` set `code_only(... || remote)`, and the wasm `claude_tools` never set `ToolExposure::DirectOnly`, so a Claude session on a hand always got exec and wait. Code Mode overhead in the 39 nano attempts of run 1fbd4a11 kept in ~/nc-live/miss89 on dev-georgios (13 tasks, 3 attempts each, claude-opus-5-5 high): 700 exec and 80 wait calls carried 1,449 nested calls. 11 cells failed: 4 TypeError, 2 SyntaxError, 2 thrown tool errors and 3 sleep-guard refusals, which only cells get. 83 cells yielded and 79 of those yields had no output (3,439 s of cell wall time, and 405 s of model calls that only sent the next wait). 25 cells finished with nested output but printed nothing, and 8 cells were cancelled. What: on wasm, `direct` now holds with a Code Mode host (native keeps `direct && !remote`), `code_only` is `!direct && (native || remote)`, and `claude_tools` builds the selected tools with `DirectOnly`. The session's tools are built before a hand attaches, so a static catalog held only WebSearch. A direct session on a Code Mode host now registers its whole catalog as a `dynamic_tools` factory that reads `ToolRuntime::model_specs` for each request, so the hand's tools appear once it attaches, in `sort_definitions` order, which is Claude Code's name order. Bash takes the upstream 2.1.318 description from `nanocode_backend_claude_tools::upstream::tool_value`, because the hand advertises its exec-cell variant and a direct call (no `/code-` in its id) gets upstream behavior. Checked with nanocode-ts output/claude-direct/run.ts on gak-9: a Node host of the nanocode-ts module built against this tree (`claude_orchestration: "direct"`, `hands: true`), a debug `nanocode hand` from this tree, and a scripted Messages endpoint that calls Bash, Write, Read, Edit, a background Bash and a foreground Bash. The first request offers Bash, Edit, Read, TaskStop, WebSearch and Write, each equal in description and input schema to `crates/backends/claude/upstream/request.json`, with no Code Mode system block, and every call runs on the hand. Without the option the same harness still offers exec and wait. Why it was tried: on the first cell the worker thread compiles the bootstrap (code-tools.mjs, code-values.mjs, bootstrap.js, 34 KB, and the tool definitions) with no native SnapshotStore set; a heap trace of the Code Mode turn (heapprof tracer on 9c49d6f98) puts the global live peak there, 2.29 MB, with the builder arena (`Arena::reserve`, 896 KiB) and compiler `FuncState`/`Spare` pools about 0.5 MB, and freed slices stay dirty in the worker's segments (up to `DIRTY_SLICES_MAX` 64 slices). The two large mappings outside the segments are the Snapshot image Vec (452 KiB mapped, 348 KB resident) and the instance arena (`image_buffer`, 900 KiB mapped, 376 KB resident, reused from the large cache). Build: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 LLVM_BOLT=/usr/lib/llvm-23/bin/llvm-bolt scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` for master 9368892d9 and the change on it (dist, BOLT). Peak RSS, n=28 each: Code Mode 11.28 MB base (10.98 to 11.42) against 11.19 MB (10.50 to 11.61), P(base > change) = 0.56; direct 8.02 against 8.04. smaps at the peak (n=3) shows the worker segment 1,044 to 1,100 KB resident on base and 688 to 932 KB with the change, so the thread frees 150 to 350 KB of segment pages, but the peak moves inside the run's noise. What the peak is made of: about 11.3 MB RSS with 2.3 to 2.6 MB anonymous, so about 9 MB is file-backed against about 6 MB on the direct turn; the Code Mode gap to the direct turn (3.3 MB) is about 3 MB of binary pages (djs VM builtin setup, the bootstrap compile and the interpreter) and about 0.7 MB anonymous. The next lever is therefore not the heap but not running VM setup and the bootstrap compile in the CLI at all: an image made at build time and restored per process, with the tool definitions given per cell instead of baked in at setup.
- perf(cli): `scripts/build-cli.sh` builds the release layout on Linux x86_64: the BOLT-optimized binary goes to `nanocode-agent` and the 8 KB static front (`bin/nanocode-front`) to `nanocode` beside it, so `target/cli/<triple>/nanocode` is what `install` puts on PATH; `scripts/release-cli.sh` copies both from that directory instead of building the front in a second container run. In `nanocode exec`, a non-terminal stdin that `poll` reports readable and whose first read is empty (`/dev/null`, a closed pipe) returns the empty piped prompt without starting the `nanocode-stdin` thread; a pipe with data or no data yet keeps the thread and its wait (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: kernel instructions against fx 0.0.16, kernel-work lane). Why: bench/cli measures `NC_BIN` = `build-cli.sh`'s output (or the release's `nanocode-<triple>` asset through tools/install.sh), and neither was the front, so the 1.91 MB `--version` row in 9368892d9 was the full dynamic binary; the front from 3e574d49a only reached users through `install`. The stdin thread cost a clone, a 2 MB stack mapping, a glibc arena reservation and an allocator segment for a read that returns EOF at once. Profile (master 9368892d9 dist+BOLT, `perf record -e instructions:k -g` under tools/netguard.sh, symbols from /proc/kallsyms): kernel time of the one-shot is page faults (~35%, mostly `filemap_map_pages` fault-around on the binary) and syscalls on the virtiofs root (`fuse_release`/`fuse_flush` on every close of an /etc or /lib file, `statx` path walks for the `cua-driver` PATH search); the NSS part of that profile is gone since the in-process resolver (`crates/core/executor/src/dns.rs`). Measured (bench/cli cli-bench 3e70e983e, hosted Hand at load 12 to 30, every run under ~/sw/buildq.sh): `--version` peak RSS through the suite's startup part, front 0.32/0.34/0.26 MB against the agent binary run directly 1.04/1.01/1.01 MB (3 interleaved passes of 4 rounds); one-shot and first frame with `NC_BIN` wrapped in `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults` (5 rounds, 2 passes): front then agent, one-shot kernel 8.66M/9.28M against 8.92M/8.78M, first frame 12.23M/10.88M against 10.06M/10.61M, user instructions 4.11M and 4.70M in both (the extra execve is within the spread); stdin shortcut, one-shot kernel instructions, 5 interleaved passes of 6 to 8 rounds, master then this: 8.76M/7.93M, 9.06M/7.80M, 9.86M/9.43M, 9.53M/8.79M, 8.88M/9.29M (median of passes 9.06M to 8.79M), user instructions unchanged (3.90M to 4.11M bimodal in both), strace -f shows 7 threads instead of 8. Checked: `nanocode exec` with stdin from /dev/null, an empty pipe, a pipe with the prompt, and a pipe that writes after 1 s (the thread path) against the bench fixture; `nanocode --version` from the built front prints the workspace version. fx stays ahead on one-shot kernel instructions (fx 3.9M on this Hand with a warm home): next are the binary's fault-around, the PATH `statx` walk for `cua-driver` on every start, and the four `nanocode-lookup` threads for MCP hosts.
- fix(claude): a Claude session whose Code Mode cells run on a hand renders its `# Environment` section from that hand at the session's first request: the hand's working directory, whether it is in a git repository, its platform, shell and OS version, in Claude Code 2.1.318's bullet form (` - Primary working directory: /app`, ` - Is a git repository: false`, ` - Platform: linux`, ` - Shell: bash`, ` - OS Version: Linux …`), before the untrusted-download line and the date (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 run 1fbd4a11: dna-assembly a00397 wrote /root/primers.fasta while its cwd was /app and failed on `File /app/primers.fasta does not exist`). nanoeval opens Claude sessions with `workspace: false` and `hands: 'always'`, so nanocode-ts passes a `ClaudeEnvironment` that holds only the placement instructions; the builder rendered it at build time, `resolve_context` used that text and never asked the hand, and the section had no directory, host or git line (the workspace resolver of the 2026-11-14 entry reaches only `environment_section`, the path without a `ClaudeEnvironment`). Now `State` keeps the `ClaudeEnvironment` unrendered and renders it in `resolve_context`, where the hand's facts (`ClaudeBuilder::hand_environment`, which the Claude runtime sets beside the workspace resolver when its tools have a Code Mode host) replace the configured machine fields, keeping the configured date and instructions; without a configured environment the hand's facts replace `environment_section`, and the direct path's `upstream_environment` takes them too. The facts come from `Tools::hand_environment(session_id)`, which asks `CodeModeHost::environment` of the hand the session's placement resolves to, as `hand_working_directory` asks `working_directory`. `HandEnvironment` gains `git_repository` (optional on the wire, so older hands and brains interoperate), which the native hand computes for its workspace as `is_git_repository` does; a hand without it gets no git line. `ClaudeEnvironment::render` and `environment_section` now prefix each fact with ` - `, as upstream's `R_` does (extracted from the claude-code-darwin-arm64 2.1.318 binary: `euo` builds `Primary working directory`, the worktree lines, `Is a git repository`, `Platform`, `Shell`, `OS Version`, the scratchpad and untrusted-download lines, and `R_` maps each to ` - ` + line). The untrusted-download line stays: the 2026-11-15 refusal entry measured the host lines alone at 15/16 refusals and the host lines with that line at 0/16. Checked with output/cwd-prompt (a native hand from `nanocode::hand::listen` on a directory, a brain built as nanocode-ts builds it: `CodeModeExecutors` with that hand as default executor, `ClaudeEnvironment::new().project_instructions(..)`, workspace `/`, and a mock Messages endpoint that saves each request): on ba3deec20 the first request's section is the heading and `Today's date` only; with this change it names `/private/tmp/cwd-prompt-app`, `Is a git repository: false`, `darwin`, `fish`, `Darwin 25.3.0`, and for a directory inside a checkout `Is a git repository: true`. `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-code-mode, nanocode-tool-host, nanocode-tool-runtime and nanocode-backend-claude, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, passed; clippy reports nothing in those crates (with `-D warnings` it stops at the existing `missing_const_for_fn` in nanocode-sync). Not run: a nanoeval rerun. - perf(code-mode): a tool call's promise is made and settled by the host, and a successful result is parsed into the heap without a trip through the bootstrap's pump (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane wave 2). `callTool` (crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/bootstrap.js) built a `new Promise` with an executor closure per call and kept its resolve and reject functions in `pendingTools`, and every result went through the pump: the host resolved `__nanocodeNext` with an `{id, ok, value}` object, the pump's `await` resumed, `JSON.parse` read the copied string and the settler resolved the promise. Now `__nanocodeTool` stays a sync host function (its journal entry, its `ToolCall` event and a sync `TypeError` for bad input are as before) but answers with a new pending promise: `HostCall::reply_promise` (djs-embed) calls `Vm::promise_host_call`, which opens an async host call (marked reported) whose promise is the call's value, and `ExecutionState` keeps the tool id -> `CallId`. A successful result is applied with `Instance::resolve_json` (`Vm::resolve_host_call_json`: the text becomes a heap string and `json::parse` runs on it with the realm's prototypes, as `JSON.parse` does, and the value goes into the host inbox, so `HostCallSettle` adopts it the way a resolve function would). A failed result, or text that is not JSON, still goes to the pump, now as `{id, ok, value, name}`: the pump builds the same value (`toolFailure`, or the `SyntaxError` of `jsonParse`) and passes it to the new sync `__nanocodeSettle`, which rejects the promise through `HostCall::settle_with_arg`; for a call made through `tools` the promise is marked handled first (`Vm::reject_host_call_handled` sets `[[PromiseIsHandled]]`), which replaces the `catch(ignore)` the old `reject` chained, so a prelude call's unobserved rejection is still reported and a `tools` call's is not. Out of memory while parsing a result ends the cell with the usual "ran out of memory" error. A first version parsed the result with `json::parse_utf8` straight from the host bytes and made the cells with a 7 KB result slower (seq +6%, json +2.6%), since the heap-string parse makes long strings slices of the text and `parse_utf8` copies each one; parsing the copied heap string is what landed. Instructions per cell (output/cellbench on the code-mode-engine native host, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, (1,200 - 200 cells)/1,000, best of 3, base 9f4f5c77b): empty 82,383 -> 82,251, tool1 193,557 -> 159,029 (-17.8%), seq16 1,074,669 -> 671,334 (-37.5%), par16 1,190,425 -> 824,442 (-30.7%), sh 2,353,725 -> 2,299,425 (-2.3%), seq 1,143,143 -> 1,009,904 (-11.7%), json 1,508,285 -> 1,424,618 (-5.5%), edit 1,142,788 -> 1,083,898 (-5.2%), agent 1,914,638 -> 1,784,480 (-6.8%); each cell's printed output is byte-identical. djs benches (djsrun, best of 5, base -> this): loop, gen, gennext, find, forEach, some, filter, map, reduce and err all within 0.001%. Checked: test262 subset 2,535 passing, identical pass set; the fuel harness (fuelrun, six fuel/slice pairs over seven scripts) prints identical results; a tool-call harness of 17 cells (output/cellconf: success, `ok: false` with the error's message, code, tool, detail and stack, a non-JSON result, an ignored rejected `tools` call, text/tool-call event order, `Promise.allSettled` over mixed results, a function as input, an uncaught tool failure, an ignored prelude `call` rejection reported as unhandled, prelude call success and failure, a timer beside a call, reaction order, non-ASCII results, `Object.prototype.then` adoption, a missing tool, failures in a loop) prints the same events for base and this, except that base hangs in the `Object.prototype.then` cell (the pump's `{id, ok, value}` event object is itself a thenable there, so `await nativeNext()` never resumes) and this one prints 42 as a resolve function would, since a successful result no longer passes through an event object; `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -p djs-embed -p nanocode-code-mode-engine -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. djs-prelude's base snapshot (crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-prelude/base/) is remade with scripts/base.sh, since djs-core's build hash changed. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode-engine/src/{bootstrap.js,cell.rs,host.rs}, crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-embed/src/instance.rs, crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/{vm/mod.rs,interp/run.rs}.
- feat(claude): an optional host deadline, `Deadline::new(at_unix_ms, limit)` set with `ClaudeHarness::deadline` or `ClaudeBuilder::deadline` (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench lane deadline). With a deadline the Claude agent (1) adds a system message after the tool results of the first round that ends past 50%, 75% and 90% of the limit, saying how much of the limit remains, that only what is on disk counts when it ends, that every required output must exist in its final location before it is improved, and not to start a command or wait that cannot finish in time; a round that passes several points sends one message; (2) runs a top-level `Bash` whose `timeout`, or an `exec` (argument or `// @exec:` pragma) or `wait` whose `yield_time_ms`, is longer than the time remaining with that value set to the time remaining, and appends to its result a line that names the requested and the used value; at 0 ms remaining such a call does not run and returns an error that says so. The text is nanocode's own (`crates/backends/claude/src/deadline.rs`), not Claude Code's, and goes through the existing round-notice system message, so upstream prompt and tool text are unchanged. Without a deadline nothing changes: no handler is wrapped and no message is added (checked below). Nested tool calls inside an exec cell run on the hand and are not capped: the cell still yields at its capped `yield_time_ms`, so control returns to the model before the limit whatever a nested `timeout` is. `EXEC_PRAGMA_PREFIX` is now `pub` in code-mode's spec so the pragma has one definition. Why: in nanoeval run 1fbd4a11 the model had no idea of its limit. Fractions from the failed attempts (trajectories under dev-georgios ~/nc-live/miss89, times from the first step): train-fasttext a00345 (3600 s) had a 0.638/0.620 model at 999 s (28%) and a 0.640/0.623 one at 2808 s (78%), was then in a 900 s wait, and never wrote /app/model.bin; a00523 had a passing model 13 to 18 min before its kill; extract-moves a00403 (1800 s) had its full transcript at 1466 s (81%) and never wrote /app/solution.txt; make-doom (900 s) a00445 started a 300 s wait at 647 s (72%) and a00089 a `timeout 300` run with a 400 s wait at 682 s (76%), and both were cancelled in them. 50% lands after the first fasttext candidate and before any trajectory starts its last long step; 75% lands before both make-doom final runs could fit (225 s left) and inside the fasttext and extract-moves windows; 90% is the last point at which a long step can still be cut short (90 s of a 900 s limit). Fewer points miss one of these windows, more points repeat the message within a few rounds. Checked with output/deadline-agent (a `Claude::builder` agent with `Bash` and `exec` handlers against a local Messages SSE mock that asks for `Bash` with `timeout` 600000, then `exec` with pragma `yield_time_ms` 900000): without a deadline the handlers got 600000 and 900000 and the requests carried no added text; with 300 s left of 600 s the handlers got 299996 and pragma 299994, each result ended with the cap line, and one system message ("Time limit: 4 min 59 s of this task's 10 min remain. ...") followed the first tool result only; with the deadline passed, both calls returned the error and did not run. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -p nanocode-code-mode -- -D warnings`, and rustfmt on the changed files (no new differences) pass.

- fix(agent): `OneLogStore` implements `StateStore::flush`: it commits the turn log lease (`Point::Progress`) when rows are buffered, so `SessionStore::flush` and `Runtime::shutdown` make every earlier `Settle::Durable` commit durable; nanocode-sim acknowledges a root turn only after `Agent::flush` and `SessionStore::flush`, and checks `acked_turn_lost` (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 durability push, lane flushdurable, dst-sweep classes A and B). Why: `OneLogStore::commit` and `replace` buffer a `Settle::Durable` write unless the fold is recovering or `OneLog::settle_durably` is set, because in nanocode-ts every write of a turn rides the commit of `OneLog::finish` (`TurnInbox`). `StateStore::flush` kept the trait default (nothing), so the store had no barrier: a host on `nanocode::turnlog` without `TurnInbox` (the sim's `runtime --store log --children local`) acknowledged turns whose rows and logged prompt were only in memory, and a restart found the turn Pending (class A) or lost its prompt (class B). In nanocode-ts no turn is acknowledged that way (turns are admitted by `OneLog::submit` and closed by `OneLog::finish`/`cancel`, which commit), but `Command::Settings` and `Command::Compact` answer while their rows wait for the next turn commit, and `TurnInbox::shutdown` reached `Runtime::shutdown`'s `store.flush()` that wrote nothing. What: `flush` writes nothing when `lease.buffered()` is 0. Nothing calls `StateStore::flush` per turn (only `Runtime::shutdown` and `SessionStore::flush`), so the in-object path writes the same rows per turn: `turns --policy turnlog --twice` keeps `cell_rows` (exact rows per crash-free turn) passing. The sim's `acknowledge` also flushes the store before it records a cancelled turn. Invariant `acked_turn_lost`: after each restart (`run_root` at epoch > 0 and `verify`), every acknowledged root turn reads `TurnStatus::Completed` from the store. Mutation `acks-unflushed` (acknowledge after `Agent::flush` alone, the old wiring) fails 231 of seeds 0..2000 of `--scenario runtime --store log`; of the printed first violations 71 of 72 are `acked_turn_lost`. Numbers (`bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 10000 3`, hosted Hand, one release build of 118dee1b3 plus this change): `--scenario runtime --store log` 10,000 of 10,000 (dst-sweep at 35ba28283: 256 failing), `--calm` 10,000 of 10,000 (219), `--wire http` 10,000 of 10,000 (255); seeds 512, 7495, 6, 13 and 148 pass. Checks: release build of nanocode-sim with this change (cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-sim) succeeds; clippy and wasm32 check results are in the lane log (queued behind build.lock).

- fix(code-mode,claude): an `exec` that starts while a session notice is pending yields at once with that notice, and a background Bash start message on a hand always states its time limit and the background maximum (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 run 1fbd4a11, nano on hand nanocode-cli-455d4e7, long-jobs lane). Why: compile-compcert a00025 failed at its 2400 s cap. At +1316 s the model started `make` with `run_in_background` and no `timeout`, so the job had the background default of 600000 ms and was stopped at about +1916 s while the build was nearly done. Its notice was pending when the next cell started, and `observe_updates` dropped the wake-up for `ObservationMode::Started` (the 2026-11-13 rule: an `exec` does not yield for a notice that was already there, because its own result or first yield carries it). That cell slept for 483 s, so the notice arrived only with its result, and the attempt was cancelled. The start message for an explicit `run_in_background` said nothing about a limit, and the Code Mode addition to the `timeout` sentence ended with "a `timeout` above the maximum counts as the maximum", which reads as if no `timeout` past 600000 has effect. In the same run Claude Code 2.1.318 made 18 `run_in_background` calls, all with a `timeout` (12 of them at 1 h or more), and nano made 1 and used `nohup` 8 times. crack-7z-hash and train-fasttext also lost time at the 600 s limits. Change: in `observe_updates`, a `Started` observation whose session notice is already ready sets `preempt_remaining` to the updates already queued, the same as a notice that arrives later, so the `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID N` with the notice and the model continues the cell with `wait`. The cost is one extra `wait` for a short cell that starts while a notice is pending. In `claude_bash.rs`, `started` takes the deadline that the job was armed with (the call's `timeout` for `run_in_background`, `DEFAULT_BACKGROUND_TIMEOUT_MS` for a command moved at its timeout). `Watch::Reported` (hand and runner tools, which the eval's Code Mode arm uses) now always says `If it is still running after <limit> in the background, it will be stopped, which is reported the same way.`, and, when the limit is below `MAX_BACKGROUND_TIMEOUT_MS`, `A command that needs longer must be started with `run_in_background` and a `timeout` of up to 7200000 ms (2h).` A limit that is not whole minutes prints in ms. `Watch::Notified` keeps Claude Code's text: in the 2.1.318 binary (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64@2.1.318`, the start-message function with `wakesItsOwner`) only a moved command gets the `If it is still running after ... it will be stopped and you will be notified.` sentence, and its duration now comes from the armed limit, which is the same value. `NESTED_TIMEOUT` (only with Code Mode, inserted after upstream's `max 600000 for a foreground command.`) now limits the cap sentence to a foreground `timeout` and adds that with `run_in_background` the `timeout` goes up to the background maximum in the next sentence (upstream's `(default 600000, max 7200000)`, unchanged and the same in 2.1.318), that a command without one is stopped at the background default, and that a long build or job needs a `timeout` that covers all of it. No default or maximum changed. Checked: output/notice-at-start (a `CodeModeToolset` with no tools whose `session_notice` is ready and whose `session_notices` returns one `<task-notification>` once; a cell with `yield_time_ms` 60000 that waits on an 8 s timer, and a cell that only calls `text`). On master (ba3deec20) the 8 s cell returned after 8.03 s with the notice attached to its result. With this change it returned after 0.00 s as `Script running with cell ID 1` with the notice, and the `wait` returned `slept 8 s` at 8.02 s. The short cell yielded at 0.00 s with the notice, and its `wait` completed at 0.03 s. Without a pending notice, both cells were identical on both builds (8.02 to 8.05 s and 0.02 s). output/bash-text runs `hand_tools` Bash with nested call IDs: the description shows the new sentence, and `run_in_background` with no `timeout`, 2500, 3600000 and 7200000 says `after 10m`, `after 2500 ms`, `after 1h` and `after 2h`, with the maximum sentence on all but the last. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-backend-claude`, again with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`; `cargo fmt --check` reports nothing in the changed lines. Not run: nanocode-sim, whose toolsets never have a notice ready, and a model. Hands serve this text, so it reaches an eval slot with the next nanocode-cli release that nanoeval pins. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/claude_bash.rs.

- perf(agent): `OneLog::journals` returns `CellJournals::with_sink` without restoring every session's Code Mode cell journals at open; each session's cells are decoded when that session resumes, through `CellJournalSink::load` (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 durability lane restart100: lazy restore). Why: `journals()` ran `cells(None)`, which parses every Cell record in the fold into `CellJournals.restored` before the runtime opens. In the 10K DO snapshot (snap-base-10k at 50% done) that is 15,632 records and 15.8 MB, 15,029 of them from 5,056 child sessions, so the step grows with child count (the restart lane measured it at about 90 ms native at 10K after its catalog fix, about 0.9 s by extrapolation at 100K). The eager map was never read on its own: `CodeMode::adopt` and the terminate path call `journals.load(session)` first, which reads that session's cells from the fold with `cells(Some(session))` and replaces the entry, and agent-host's `CellJournals::with_sink` path already restored only this way. The nanocode-sim cells world checks recovery through `sink.load`. Measured (restart101 lane, native scale-bench restart pinned to one core with `--workers 1`, base d9d958224 against this change, both with temporary eprintln timing around `OneLog::open` and `journals()`, each restarting from the same kill-at-50% log written by the base binary, interleaved, hosted Hand at load 4 to 10): the journals step after open went from 309, 192 and 237 ms to 8, 0.4 and 0.3 ms at 10K (7,377 hot agents), and from 434 and 675 ms to 0.3 and 0.3 ms at 100K (75,281 hot agents). Time to the first provider call after open stayed inside the run-to-run spread (10K 1.92, 1.20, 1.56 s base against 1.93, 1.64, 0.95 s; 100K 9.4, 13.1 s against 16.0, 11.8 s), which TurnLog open (0.6 to 1.2 s at 10K, 4.5 to 8.7 s at 100K) and Registry restore (0.24 to 0.62 s at 10K, 4.4 to 7.3 s at 100K) dominate. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode-subagents --features nanocode-code-mode/local-cells -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked --lib -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode-subagents --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 500 4 --scenario turns --policy turnlog --twice` 500/500, `--snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` 0..300 300/300, and `--mutation open_drops_journals` still caught by 143 of 400 seeds.

- fix(subagents): a child turn that resumes after a runtime restart and ends without an accepted `submit_result` is prompted once more in the same turn with `completion_reminder()`, and a turn whose `submit_result` was accepted ends `Completed` with that output even when its last model call fails (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 swarm, missingresult lane). Why: scale2's 100K kill/restart (box pyramid-prd-rootbytes-a3f1, master 30221fc) ended with 7 children `Failed` with `MissingResult`. With an eprintln at `durable::restored_session` (100K at add287497, 5 and 16 lost children in two runs), the journal of each lost child held no `accepted_output` and no tracked nested `submit_result` call. Its exec cell, whose script called `tools.submit_result`, was still running at the kill and had no cell journal. After the restart its first request carried the exec result "Tool execution interrupted by a host crash; outcome unknown" and the resume message, the model ended the turn, and `complete_session` failed the child. In this case no durable receipt exists, so the restore has no output to adopt. What: `harness_turn_started` marks a turn `resumed` when the session has `resume_attempts > 0`. When such a turn ends `Ok` in `TurnStage::Working` and holds no follow-up output, `Harness::turn_finished` calls `Registry::remind_resumed_turn`. That call clears the mark, records the usage and returns the turn revision. The harness then prompts the same agent with `completion_reminder()` at that revision and keeps the turn capacity, so a `submit_result` from that prompt is accepted for the same turn. A child whose acceptance is in the journal is still restored `Completed` with no model call. A turn is reminded at most once for each resume, and a turn that ends again without a result fails as before. The second path came from the new sim invariant on the http wire (seeds 32 and 195, on master and on the first fix): a child whose `submit_result` was accepted and whose final model call then failed with "Messages protocol: invalid UTF-8 SSE line" ended `Failed`, and the accepted output was lost. `harness_turn_finished` now completes such a turn with the accepted output. Cancellation and stop still end `Interrupted`. Sim: invariant `receipted_child_lost` (`whole::settled`) requires that a child whose model request carried an accepted receipt ends `Completed` with `"<label> done"` (stop Never, no cancelled root turn). Mutation `power_loss_drops_acceptance` (`--scenario runtime --store kv`) reverts each `state/*:subagents` head at a power loss to its value before the newest save that wrote an `accepted_output` patch, and the sim model holds its answer to a fresh receipt until the crash. The child's receipt row survives and the journal's acceptance does not. The sim model also calls `submit_result` again when the last user message is a bare completion reminder. Measured: sim `--scenario runtime --store kv --mutation power_loss_drops_acceptance` seeds 0..400 with the sim change only: 68 of 400 seeds caught by `receipted_child_lost`, each a child that ended `Failed` with `MissingResult`. With this fix: 1399 of 1400 seeds pass (0..1400). Seed 452 fails before and after the fix, because the reverted head also drops a later journal record that marks a completion as delivered, and the root waits for that completion. Without the mutation, with this fix: runtime kv 1000/1000, kv http 400/400 (399/400 before, seed 32), kv remote 400/400, kv --twice 300/300, agents 400/400, runtime log 967/1000 (the same 33 seeds fail on add287497, the settle_durably classes of the dst-sweep lane). `cargo clippy --no-deps --all-targets -- -D warnings` on nanocode-subagents and nanocode-sim, `cargo +1.97.1 check --lib -p nanocode-subagents --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and rustfmt on the changed lines pass. scale-bench 100K kill at 50% and restart (box pyramid-prd-nanoeval-s3-ee11, 48 cores shared with other lanes, mock provider, rate 1000/s, concurrency 64): 5 of 5 runs completed 100,000 of 100,000 children with 0 lost (kill at 50,000 to 50,033 done, restart 324 to 372 s, 7 to 84 children made more than 2 model calls in the restart). Before the fix the same harness lost 5 and 16 children in two runs.

- feat(codex): opt-in `custom_tool_output_tokens` (`CodexBuilder::custom_tool_output_tokens`, CLI `--tool-output-token-limit TOKENS`) sets the per-call tool output budget of a custom model, in place of the 2,500 tokens (Codex 0.162.1's 10,000-byte unknown-model policy) (2026-11-15, cost lane C12). exec_command and write_stdin cut their output to TOKENS x 4 bytes, head and tail around the marker, and the history keeps TOKENS x 1.2, as Codex CLI's `tool_output_token_limit` config does for a bytes-mode model. The default is unchanged, and built-in models keep their own budgets. Measured by a replay of 48 nc-codex trials (cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0316, cf-all-kimi-qwen-1115-0317 and the ncc-* A/B runs): each `last-request.json` function_call_output was mapped to the call that first sent it and the calls that read it again, priced with that trial's `calls.jsonl` cached share (DS 0.30/0.006, GLM 0.15/0.03, Kimi 0.95/0.19, Qwen 0.45/0.45 $/M). Tool outputs are 27 to 34% of input tokens on DS, GLM and Kimi (12% on Qwen), and 16% (DS), 29% (GLM), 19% (Kimi) and 8% (Qwen) of trial cost. A cut to 1,000 tokens saves 5.2% (DS), 4.0% (GLM), 6.1% (Kimi) and 0.2% (Qwen) of $/trial; a cut to 500 tokens saves 8.6%, 8.0%, 9.8% and 2.0%. DS saves mostly on the first, uncached send, GLM and Kimi on later re-reads. The risk is calls that read the cut part again: at 500 tokens, 1.2 (DS) and 1.1 (GLM) outputs per trial of file or test content (not apt, pip or build noise) had words from the cut middle in the next three calls, which at one extra call each leaves about 2% (DS) and 6% (GLM) net; Kimi's cut outputs were all package-install noise. A mock Responses server whose first reply runs `seq 1 6000` returned a 10,209-byte output by default and a 2,209-byte output with `--tool-output-token-limit 500`. `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-backend-codex-client and nanocode-backend-codex, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --no-deps -D warnings` of nanocode-backend-codex and nanocode-cli, and `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` pass (clippy 1.99 flags the existing `reconnect_delay` in nanocode-backend-codex-client as `missing_const_for_fn`). Files: bin/nanocode/src/{cli,host,lib}.rs, crates/backends/codex/client/src/openai/config.rs, crates/backends/codex/src/agent/builder.rs, crates/backends/codex/src/model/run/tool_calls.rs.
- perf(build): djs-prelude has no build script: its base snapshot is checked in (crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-prelude/base/base.img, 205,728 B, and base.rs with BASE_END and BUILT_BY), made by the new djs-base crate (`crates/patches/djs/scripts/base.sh`, `--check`), so nothing above djs-prelude waits for djs-core's code generation, only its metadata (2026-11-15, build speed lane "snapshot"; thread's hosted Hand, 5 cores, load 7 to 13 from other lanes). Why: the build script linked djs-core to make the image, so djs-embed, code-mode-engine, code-mode, tool-host, tool-runtime, agent-host, nanocode and the cli all started after djs-core's full build (16.9 s at 16 cores, its frontend about 45% of that). Same bytes: the checked-in image is byte-identical to the build script's on d9d958224 (cmp), and the image is target-independent as before (the host made it for cross builds). Staleness can't slip through: djs-prelude's existing const assert compares BUILT_BY with djs-core's BUILD_HASH (every non-test source of djs-core and djs-libm, the prelude and the features), so a djs-core change fails to compile until base.sh is run (checked with a probe edit), and `nanocode-sim --tidy` regenerates the image and fails on any byte difference (checked by flipping one byte). The release, fast, dist, lite and wasm `package.djs-core`/`djs-libm` overrides, which only existed to share the build-dependency's unit, are removed; each equalled its profile's own value. Measured: cold `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --timings`, private target, under the bench lock: djs-embed starts 2.9 s after djs-core's metadata instead of after its full build (djs-core rmeta→end gap removed: 54.1 and 56.3 s in the two base runs on the loaded 5 cores); critical path modeled with unlimited cores from the timings and `--unit-graph`: 213.4 s before (head: djs-core → djs-prelude build script → djs chain) to 139.7 s after (head: psh-utils), and the base run's own durations with the build-script edge cut give 163.6 s; walls 420.8 and 580.8 s base against 307.5 s after, at different loads. Expected at 16 cores: the djs chain starts about 9 s earlier; the next bound is the psh-utils chain.
- feat(codex): `--min-wait-ms MS` (env `NANOCODE_MIN_WAIT_MS`) raises the wait of `exec_command` and of empty `write_stdin` polls to at least MS, so a call returns when the process exits or MS passes, as Claude Code's Bash blocks up to its 120000 ms timeout (2026-11-15, cost lane GLM nc-claude vs nc-codex). Off by default: the waits stay Codex CLI 0.162.1's (exec_command 250-30000 ms, polls 5000-300000 ms at the requested value), byte-identical. Why: on Workers AI GLM-5.3-flash, nc-codex cost $0.178/pass against nc-claude's $0.032 in run cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0316 (11 vs 11 scored trials, 4 tasks, 9 vs 7 passes). The per-call request is not larger in the codex harness (fixed prefix about 5k tokens in both, tool outputs capped at about 10k characters, median 300-4,400 characters, against claude's 250-800). The difference is calls x context: 60 calls/trial against 17 (circuit-fibsqrt 115 and 249 calls against 42), 97% of input cached, one tool call per model call in both harnesses (GLM sends no parallel calls). 78 of 663 GLM codex calls (12%) and 27 of 199 DS calls are empty `write_stdin` polls that GLM sends with yield_time_ms 1000-30000 while apt-get, builds or simulators run, each one a full context. Replay of the recorded requests (each call's input minus the tokens of removed poll steps, the polled output kept, tokens per character fitted per trial, cache hit rate per call kept): MS=120000 cuts GLM nc-codex $1.599 -> $1.448 (-9.5%), DS $0.547 -> $0.493 (-9.9%), Qwen (cf-all-kimi-qwen-1115-0317) $0.214 -> $0.197 (-8.2%); with `--no-reasoning-replay` as well GLM is $1.030 (-35.6%) and DS $0.453 (-17.2%). MS=300000 gives GLM -10.6%, DS -14.9%. Only one trial (circuit-fibsqrt a1) ran a command that never exited without a poll, which would add 110 s of wall time at MS=120000. Pass rate is not measured: run a cf-cost A/B (`--min-wait-ms 120000` vs base) before making it a default for any model. Checks: cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-process (native and wasm32-unknown-unknown), cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-process and -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode -D warnings, cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode.
- feat(tool-runtime): `Acceptor::admitting(options, requests, authorize, admit)` takes a check `(key, &RemoteCatalog) -> Result<(), String>` that runs on every socket's catalog before it attaches (2026-11-15). A refused catalog never attaches: the acceptor sends a policy close (1008) whose reason is the check's error, and the socket ends with `hand <key> refused: <reason>`. Why: a host whose brain and hands are built from different nanocode revisions (a hand released on its own schedule) needs to refuse a hand that lacks what it relies on, such as a resumable runtime, call cancellation or a tool its sessions offer, at attach and with the reason, rather than fail later inside a session. A hand built on nanocode's `Hand` treats a 1008 close as a fence: it logs the reason and redials as a new runtime at its longest backoff, so a hand updated in place is admitted on its next dial. `Acceptor::new` is `admitting` with a check that admits every catalog, so existing hosts are unchanged. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-runtime` and `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p nanocode-tool-runtime -- -D warnings`.
- feat(claude): `SubscriptionIdentity::session_digest` and `ClaudeClient::session_digest` name how a request's device id derives from its session id, as `SessionDigest { prefix, suffix }` with the device id equal to the hex SHA-256 of `prefix + session + suffix`, and `None` when an install id fixes the device id (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 cold-start lane d: speculative first dispatch). `device_id` now builds its input from the same `device_digest`, so the bytes are unchanged (`omp-claude-device-id-v1:{install}` without an account UUID, `omp-claude-device-id-v2\0{install}\0{account}` with one). Why: a host that builds a fresh session's first request from another session's prepared bytes (nanocode-ts `Speculation.template`) must replace every value that derives from the session id; the session id itself appears verbatim, but the device id in `metadata.user_id` is a digest, and only the SDK knows its input. The host gets the derivation from the SDK instead of a copy of the format string, so a change here changes both sides. Measured with nanocode-ts `Speculation` in local workerd: the first requests of two sessions differ only in `metadata.user_id` (`session_id` and `device_id`), and a template filled with this digest gives the bytes the session sends (byte-equal SHA-256 at adoption).

- perf(djs): a plain generator's frame runs in its own value array (a stack segment) when the tier-0 loop resumes it from the main value stack, so `gen_enter_hot` and `gen_yield_hot` switch `Exec::stack` instead of copying the frame both ways (gen 2,061.6M -> 1,985.6M instructions natively, -3.7%; gennext 4,380.7M -> 4,306.7M, -1.7%) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs structural-bet lane, bet C). What: `generator_start` allocates the saved frame with room for the whole frame (`hp - bp + HEADER + LOCALS + STACK`, at least `len + 2`). `gen_enter_hot` (for-of `iter_next_loc` and `it.next()`) enters in place when no segment is active, the array is above the arena's tracked prefix and has that room: the frame keeps index 0 of the array, the array's `LEN` becomes its capacity, `Exec::seg_base` holds the main stack's top below it and `Exec::stack` becomes the array, which `run_hot`'s `switch_frame!` now reloads into `vals`. Calls from the generator body push their frames in the segment, and `grow_stack` grows the segment (the stack limit counts `seg_base`). The segment frame (bp 0 in a segment) leaves the segment in `gen_yield_hot` and `suspend_into` (no copy, `LEN` = frame length, `FRAME` = the current array), in `pop_frame` and in `throw_value` (sp = `seg_base`). `Interp::SEGMENT` and `Interp::SEGMENT_BASE` (new fields) hold the segment between runs: `flush` writes them and `Exec::new` reads them, so the GC traces and moves the array, and `safepoint_collect`, `Vm::abort` and `tidy_stack` clear the main stack above `seg_base` and the segment's dead slots. Stack traces and `prepare_stack_trace` follow the frame chain from the segment back to the main stack. Nested resumes inside a segment, generators in the tracked prefix and the `step` paths (`resume_hit`, `generator_resume`) copy as before; the saved format is the same either way. Fuel: each switch still charges `len / 8`, so totals, yields and stop points do not change. Why only -3.7%: callgrind on gen with 2 rounds (200,000 iterations, base 210.6M) shows the two frame copies at about 100 of 1,053 instructions per iteration (`memcpy` 46, `Arena::copy_within` 22, the rest their setup), not the 643 that 7d91ed29c's entry attributed to them: its own breakdown gives resume 313 and yield 330, each about 40 of them the copy. The rest of each switch is the generator slot reads, the template entry and the header writes, which a segment still needs; a first version that kept the segment in `Interp` on every switch (`state::set_segment`, a tracked write) cost 36 instructions per call and gave gen +6.8%, so the segment lives in `Exec` and reaches `Interp` only at `flush`. gen <= 691M needs about 345 instructions per iteration in all: the remaining lever is a loop that runs both bodies and the switch without `run_hot`'s dispatch (tier 1 over `iter_next_loc`/`yield`), not frame storage. Measured on the hosted Hand, base origin/master 8b3968951 against this change (output/djsrun, output/genfuel, output/t262, ~/bench-djs), natively `perf stat -e instructions:u` best of 5: loop 262,154,839 -> 262,122,230, gen 2,061,646,466 -> 1,985,643,952, gennext 4,380,673,473 -> 4,306,683,278, find 91,279,355 -> 90,817,715, forEach 94,559,524 -> 94,097,887, some 92,966,218 -> 92,504,550, filter 146,252,008 -> 145,811,966, map 161,391,695 -> 160,951,935, reduce 93,024,043 -> 92,562,312, err 660,399,210 -> 653,201,526. Wasm was not measured (the Hand ran at load 25-35 under a build lock). - feat(codex): opt-in `omit_custom_model_reasoning` (`ModelBuilder::omit_custom_model_reasoning`, CLI `--no-reasoning-replay`) leaves every earlier `reasoning` item out of the request input sent to a custom model (2026-11-15, cost lane C11). The default is unchanged and matches Codex 0.162.1, which replays every reasoning item. Measured on cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0316 nc-codex (Workers AI through cfproxy, which turns reasoning items into assistant `reasoning_content`): Workers AI bills replayed reasoning as prompt tokens, since the input growth between consecutive calls was never below the previous call's output tokens (0 of 424 steps), and on the 85 steps whose reasoning exceeded their tool output the growth less the output was 0.93x the estimated tool output. A replay of each trial's `last-request.json` with its `calls.jsonl` usage, prices from prices.json (cached input at 0.006 DS and 0.03 GLM $/M), and a prefix-match cache (64-token DS and 256-token GLM blocks, real misses kept) reproduces the billed baseline within 3% and gives, against it: never replay reasoning -12.1% DS (11 trials, $0.0410 to $0.0360 a pass) and -12.6% GLM (8 append-only trials, $0.0550 to $0.0481); reasoning of the last call only +15.5% DS and -4.6% GLM; the last 2 calls +41.7% and +4.0%; dropping all older reasoning every 8 calls +13.0% and -2.6%. Any window that later drops an item it already sent breaks the cached prefix after that item, and on DeepSeek the re-read of uncached tail costs more than the cached reasoning it removes, so only never sending reasoning keeps the history append-only and saves on both. The filter runs in `perform_model_call` after image eviction, only for `Model::Custom`, and resets the incremental start, which custom models never use because they send the full history over HTTPS. Risk, not measured here: DeepSeek's own API rejects thinking-mode tool histories without `reasoning_content` and GLM recommends preserved thinking for agents, so the saving holds only if pass rate and output tokens stay level, which needs a paired live run. Checked with a mock Responses server that returns a reasoning item and a call twice, then a message (`~/wt/C11-mock.py`, `nanocode exec --model @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash --harness codex`): without the flag request 3 carries REASONING-1 and REASONING-2, with it request 3 carries only the two function calls and outputs and extends request 2 byte for byte. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex`, native and wasm32-unknown-unknown, `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-codex -- -D warnings` and `cargo build -p nanocode-cli` pass.
- perf(alloc), measured and not shipped: one-slice pages for size classes of 5 KB and up, a 1 KB mini-page slice for the first page of each class of 1 KB and less, and purge thresholds 0, 1 and 8 (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: tool-turn peak RSS, allocator page-structure lane). Nothing in the build changes. Method: one dist+BOLT experiment build of 9f4f5c77b (`LLVM_BOLT=/usr/lib/llvm-23/bin/llvm-bolt scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode`, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1) whose heap read its policy from environment variables at the first heap start, each policy run through a wrapper that `exec`s the binary, bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc` under tools/netguard.sh, direct row (h=ncdirect) and Code Mode row, 4 interleaved passes of 3 rounds, 5-core hosted Hand at load 5 to 30; segment structure read at the peak RSS sample from /proc/pid/mem (each 4 MB segment header) and /proc/pid/pagemap; instructions and faults with perf stat (linux-tools 6.8 perf) around each process. Results, mean peak RSS MB direct / Code Mode: policy of 9f4f5c77b (64 dirty slices, 8-block pages) 10.96 / 13.87; dirty 4 alone 10.98 / 14.02; one-slice pages alone (a page holds at least one block, so classes of 5 KB to 64 KB take one 64 KB slice, larger classes the fewest slices for one block) 10.91 / 14.00; one-slice pages with dirty 4 10.77 / 13.73; with dirty 1 10.79 / 13.55; with dirty 0 10.73 / 13.58; with dirty 8 10.95 / 13.93; two-block pages with dirty 4 11.21 / 13.92; one-block pages only from 16 KB with dirty 4 10.78 / 13.67. At the peak the direct row's worker segment fell from 1.58-1.64 MB resident (a 65,536-byte class page of 8 slices with 4 blocks bumped and 1 live, 248 KB resident; a 40,960-byte page with 3 of 5 live) to 1.44-1.51 MB, and the overflow segment the worker opened (216 KB) was no longer needed. Purging every retired page (dirty 0) or at 1 dirty slice costs kernel work: direct turn 13.17M to 15.10M kernel instructions and 838 to 1165 page faults, one-shot 11.21M to 12.26M kernel instructions and 702 to 797 faults, so those were dropped; dirty 4 with one-slice pages measured one-shot 11.30M kernel instructions and 710 faults (within noise). The mini-page slice (one slice per segment cut into 64 units of 1 KB with their own page table entries, a class's first page taking 4 blocks' worth of units, the deallocation path reading the mini slice index from the segment header) made both rows worse: 11.51 / 14.34 MB with classes up to 1 KB and 11.56 / 14.50 MB up to 4 KB, because a class that outgrows its mini page still takes a full slice and the small threads touch the second header page either way; the short-lived threads' segments (durability 192-208 KB for about 105 KB live, main thread 144 KB for 49 KB live) are not where the gap is. Not shipped because master gained 3f730c21f (retire empty head pages, purge past 4 dirty slices) during the lane, which these runs did not include, and the dist+BOLT A/B of one-slice pages on top of it could not finish on the shared Hand (two builds lost to a full disk and an OOM kill at load 34). Next: build master with `slices_of(bytes) = bytes.div_ceil(SLICE_BYTES).max(1)` (PAGE_BLOCKS_MIN removed) against master and measure both rows and one-shot/first-frame instructions; the expected gain on top of 3f730c21f is 0.1-0.3 MB. Harnesses: ~/sw/allocpg (peak2.py segment reader, abk.sh interleaved A/B, perfab.sh), removed after this entry.
- feat(codex): `nanocode exec --compact-instructions` (env `NANOCODE_COMPACT_INSTRUCTIONS`, off unless set) sends a model nanocode does not know, such as one on a custom endpoint, nanocode's own 1,952 B base instructions (`crates/backends/codex/client/prompts/compact.md`, a subset of the unknown-model prompt's task, validation, shell and final-message rules) in place of Codex 0.162.1's 17,119 B `codex-unknown-model.md`, through the new `CodexAgentBuilder::compact_instructions` (2026-11-15, cost lane C3-short-prompt). The upstream prompt stays byte-identical and stays the default. Measured on a local mock Responses endpoint (`nanocode exec --model bench-model --harness codex`): the first developer message drops from 17,690 B to 2,117 B, and the permissions message, environment context and tools do not change. Why: in the live Workers AI run cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0316 / cf-all-kimi-qwen-1115-0317 (nc-codex, 12 DS, 11 GLM, 5 Kimi, 5 Qwen scored trials), the static prefix is about 5.3k-5.7k tokens per call (developer prompt 4.5k-4.9k, three tools 0.6k-0.8k). It is cached from the first call (the prefix is shared across sessions, so the first call's share of the saving is 5-12%), but it is read again on every call at the cached rate. A replay of each call's usage with 15,573 B (3.4k-4.3k tokens at each trial's measured tokens per byte) removed from the cached part gives a $/pass change of -1.2% on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ($0.0418 to $0.0413, output is 63% of cost), -5.7% on GLM-5.3 Flash ($0.178 to $0.168), -9.1% on Kimi and -31% on Qwen (no cached-input discount), at equal pass rate. The text changes model behavior (no preamble or formatting rules), so pass rate needs a same-task live A/B before the flag becomes a default. Commands: `python3 ~/hill/analysis/c3/static_prefix.py`, `python3 ~/hill/analysis/c3/replay_compact.py 15573`; checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` (native and wasm32-unknown-unknown), `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-backend-codex -p nanocode-cli` (no new warnings), `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`.

- fix(http): Transfer-Encoding's final coding skips empty list elements, so `chunked,` or `gzip, chunked` followed by an empty `Transfer-Encoding` line still frames the body as chunked (crates/core/http/src/wire.rs, `chunked`) (2026-11-15, HTTP/TLS bugs lane: fuzzing). Why: `chunked` took the text after the last comma of the last Transfer-Encoding line, so a trailing comma or an empty line made the final coding "" and the message not chunked: a request was rejected and a response was read to connection close with its chunk framing left in the body. RFC 9110 5.6.1 says a recipient MUST accept and ignore empty list elements, and 5.3 makes several lines of a field one list. What: the last non-empty element of the last line that has one decides; a Transfer-Encoding with no codings at all, or one that is not visible ASCII, is still not chunked. Checked: output/http-fuzz target `framing` failed on `Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked` + `Transfer-Encoding: chunked,` (an error, expected Chunked); after the fix 3,948,139 inputs in 121 s without a divergence; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-http` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-http` with no warnings in the crate.
- fix(http): a request with both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length is rejected by `request_framing` (crates/core/http/src/wire.rs) instead of being read as chunked (2026-11-15, HTTP/TLS bugs lane: fuzzing). Why: RFC 9112 6.3 says such a request "might indicate an attempt to perform request smuggling" and lets a server reject it or follow Transfer-Encoding only if it then closes the connection after responding; `nanocode_http::server` followed Transfer-Encoding and kept the connection alive, so a front end that framed the message by Content-Length and nanocode disagreed on where the next request began. Rejecting is the smaller change: the server answers the parse error and closes, as for any other invalid head, and `server::length` and the simulator's httpd see no length for it. Responses are unchanged (Transfer-Encoding overrides, as 6.3 says for a user agent). Checked: output/http-fuzz target `framing` (request_framing and response_framing on fuzzer-built Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding and other header lists against an RFC 9112 6.3 reference) failed on `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` + `Content-Length: 5` (Chunked, expected an error) and passes it after; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-http` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-http` with no warnings in the crate.
- fix(http): the 16 KiB limits on a chunk size line and on a chunked body's trailers hold whatever the reads deliver, counting each line with its CRLF, in `BodyReader::line` (crates/core/http/src/wire.rs) (2026-11-15, HTTP/TLS bugs lane: fuzzing). Why: `line` returned any line whose CRLF was already buffered and checked the limit only when none was, so whether a long line passed depended on how the peer's bytes were split: a chunk size line of 20,000 bytes delivered in one read was accepted, the same line read 1 byte at a time was rejected after 16,385 bytes, and a 16,384-byte line followed by CRLF passed or failed by where the CR landed. What: a found line is rejected when it and its CRLF exceed the limit, an unfinished one once the buffer holds the limit's worth of bytes (its CRLF cannot fit any more), so a line passes exactly when its bytes and CRLF fit; the trailer check after each line goes, since `line(TRAILER_BYTES_MAX - read)` now keeps the total within the limit. Checked: output/http-fuzz target `chunked` on `1;` + 16,382 bytes + CRLF, `1;` + 20,000 bytes + CRLF and a 16,384-byte trailer section, each read whole, 1 byte at a time and in seeded splits against the reference decoder: all three modes disagreed with it before (accepted a line over the limit in one read) and agree after; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-http` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-http` with no warnings in the crate.
- fix(http): a chunk size line or trailer line that holds a control byte other than HTAB (a bare LF or CR, NUL, DEL) is now an invalid chunked body, in `BodyReader::chunked` (crates/core/http/src/wire.rs, `has_control`) (2026-11-15, HTTP/TLS bugs lane: fuzzing). Why: the decoder ended a chunk line only at CRLF and read anything before it as chunk extensions or a trailer, so `1 ;zzz\nA\r\n0\r\n\x12\n` was accepted as one chunk holding `A`, while a peer that ends lines at a bare LF (which RFC 9112 2.2 allows for start and field lines) frames the same bytes differently. RFC 9112 7.1.1 limits chunk-ext to tokens, quoted strings and BWS, and 7.1.2 makes trailers field lines, so none of them holds a CTL other than HTAB. What: the size line and every trailer line are checked once their CRLF is found and rejected with `WireError::Parse`. Checked: libFuzzer target `chunked` in output/http-fuzz (the real `BodyReader` over an in-memory reader fed whole, 1 byte at a time and in fuzzer-chosen splits, against an RFC 9112 7.1 reference decoder) found the input above in 30 s; after the fix it ran 400,314 inputs in 91 s with no divergence; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-http` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-http` with no warnings in the crate.
- perf(djs): a tier-1 loop (interp/run/tier1.rs, `Exec::run_tier1`) runs a hot loop body of local, constant, number and jump instructions in its own small interpreter after `run_hot` returns for its backward-jump budget (loop 301.4M -> 262.2M instructions natively, -13.0%, under the 265M target; wasm -20%) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs structural-bet lane, bet A). Why: the two plateau entries (6f039f26f, 7d91ed29c) showed that every edit inside `run_hot` moves the other benches by 2 to 4% through register allocation, so this change leaves `run_hot` as it is (only `word` and the three `G_*` group constants become `pub(super)`) and puts the loop in a second function. What: the run loop calls `run_tier1` after each `run_hot` return with fuel left, and again while it returns true (its own budget, for V8's tier-up). It scans the instructions from `pc` to the first backward jump: each must be one of the 63 opcodes it runs, the jump must go to `pc` (so `pc` is a loop head), and the sum of their fuel is the most one pass can charge. A pass starts only with more fuel than that sum, so fuel never reaches 0 inside a pass. It leaves to `run_hot` at an instruction it declines (each decline leaves the state as before the instruction), at a jump out of the body, or at the head with too little fuel for a pass, always with fuel > 0, where `run_hot` continues exactly as if it had run the pass. Each instruction charges the same fuel as in `run_hot` (the arms are copies, with the `add_loc8`, `inc_lt` and `inc_lt_loc` group charges), it makes no heap call and it does not start with a collection wanted, so stop points, safepoints, yields and `fuel_used` do not change. A first copy of the arms gave loop 287.5M (-4.6%): callgrind showed 143 instructions per iteration, about what `run_hot` spends, so register allocation was not the main cost for loop. Two changes that `run_hot` cannot take without moving the others brought it to 262.2M: the body-end test only after a jump instead of at every instruction, the fuel and pass tests merged at the backward jump (269.7M), and `add_loc8` reusing the int32 decode of each operand on its f64 path (262.2M, about 131 instructions per iteration). Measured on the hosted Hand, base origin/master d9d958224 against this change (output/djsrun, output/fuelrun, output/t262 and the output/wasmrun cdylib with djs-core `unsafe-heap` under node, ~/bench-djs): natively `perf stat -e instructions:u` best of 5: loop 301,398,116 -> 262,155,022, gen 2,061.63M -> 2,061.65M, gennext 4,380.64M -> 4,380.67M, find 91.276M -> 91.279M, forEach 94.556M -> 94.560M, some 92.963M -> 92.966M, filter 146.229M -> 146.232M, map 160.489M -> 160.491M, reduce 93.021M -> 93.024M, err 660.40M -> 660.40M (all others +0.004% or less). Wasm, (13 runs - 3 runs) / 10 per run, best and median of 7: loop 318.0M / 321.5M -> 253.8M / 267.5M, gen 2,456.1M / 2,459.3M -> 2,454.3M / 2,462.7M, gennext 4,673.3M / 4,681.0M -> 4,672.2M / 4,679.6M, find 97.8M / 106.5M -> 93.5M / 109.2M, forEach 105.6M / 112.6M -> 105.4M / 113.5M, some 101.0M / 101.7M -> 96.5M / 108.9M, filter 159.2M / 170.1M -> 159.0M / 171.8M, map 182.9M / 187.0M -> 185.0M / 191.8M, reduce 106.8M / 110.9M -> 107.8M / 113.0M, err 723.9M / 733.4M -> 730.9M / 736.0M; outside loop every difference is inside the V8 tier-up spread already recorded (6% between identical modules). Not covered: gen and gennext, whose bodies contain `iter_next_loc` and `yield` (the scan rejects them and the cost per budget period is one scan). Their cost is the frame copy of each switch (about 643 of 1,030 instructions per gen iteration, 7d91ed29c), which a second interpreter does not remove: the stack-segment design (bet C, a generator frame that runs in its own value array) is the remaining lever for gen <= 691M. Bet B (cold arms out of `run_hot`) was not built: the tier-1 profile shows that the per-instruction work, not the size of `run_hot`, sets the loop cost. Checks: test262 subset (~/t262.list) 2,535 passing with identical pass sets; the fuel harness (`Instance::step` with `Limits { fuel, slice }`) prints the same result, yields and `fuel_used` on base and new for a tier-1 edge script (int and f64 sums, a break, a decline to a string, nested loops, a while loop, bitwise ops, a conditional inside the body, a local bound, a 2,147,483-iteration loop past int32), ~/core-work/edge.js, gen.js, gennext.js and loop.js at slices 1, 2, 7, 1,000, 65,537, 1,000,003 and unlimited, and fuel 5,000, 123,457 and 3,000,017 (50 runs, `cmp` identical); `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` pass. Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/interp/{run.rs,run/hot.rs,run/tier1.rs}.
- perf(nc-lite): bin/nc-lite/build.rs links the binary non-PIE (`-no-pie`) on Linux glibc, as bin/nanocode/build.rs does, so a plain `cargo build` gets the no-relocation start that scripts/build-cli.sh already gets from `-Crelocation-model=static` (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: nc-lite `--continue` user instructions at 1,000 sessions). Why: a perf profile of `--continue` on the PIE `fast` build spent 16% of its user samples in `_dl_relocate_object` before `main`. Measured as in the typed-preload entry below, on top of that change: store-resume user instructions 18.04M -> 16.90M (-6.3%), request bytes identical. Both changes together on master 12ab43026, interleaved runs of 10 rounds each: 19.28M and 19.23M -> 16.95M and 16.94M (-12.1%).
- perf(durability, codex): `SessionStore::load` keeps the typed checkpoint that a format hydrated, and `--continue` takes it instead of deserializing the hydrated `Value` again (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: nc-lite `--continue` user instructions at 1,000 sessions). Why: the Codex format hydrated the stored snapshot into a `SessionSnapshot`, serialized it to a `Value` for `StoredSession::checkpoint`, and `context::preloaded_snapshot` then deserialized that `Value` back into a `SessionSnapshot`. The second pass buffered every `ResponseItem` (an internally tagged enum) and the tool definitions of the request prefix through serde `Content`, about 12% of the user instructions in a perf profile of `--continue`. What: `CheckpointFormat::hydrate_typed` (a provided method that returns no typed value) returns the hydrated `Value` with an optional `Hydrated`, a type-erased `Arc` that `Hydrated::take` downcasts. `SessionStore::load` calls it for the latest checkpoint and keeps the result beside the payload, `prepare_resume_loaded` passes it to the preload, and `DurableSession::take_checkpoint_preload_hydrated` returns it. The Codex format implements `hydrate_typed`, and `preloaded_snapshot` uses the typed snapshot when it is present, else deserializes the `Value` as before. `StoredSession::checkpoint` and the existing public functions are unchanged. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, shared with other lanes) with nc-lite `fast` builds (`CARGO_PROFILE_FAST_INCREMENTAL=false CARGO_PROFILE_FAST_STRIP=none cargo build --locked --profile fast -p nc-lite`) of bc858a347 and of this change, `node harness/suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nclite --sessions=1000 --storerounds=10` under `BENCH_PERF=1` on copies of one 1,000-session store, medians of 10: store-resume user instructions 19.31M -> 18.00M (-6.8%), 0 errors, and the request bytes of all 10 rounds are identical (25,855 to 34,610). `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-durability -p nanocode-backend-codex --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes.
- feat(codex): `--lenient-patches` (`NANOCODE_LENIENT_PATCHES`, `apply_patch::set_lenient_matching`) lets apply_patch locate a hunk after Codex CLI's matcher fails: first from the start of the file (hunks out of file order), then with lines compared by whitespace-separated words, and it accepts a deleted file added again in the same patch. Off by default, so the tool keeps Codex CLI 0.162.1 behavior and error text. A lenient match that overlaps another hunk returns the stock error. Also, an end-of-file hunk is searched from `max(len - pattern, start)`, as stock seek_sequence does (2026-11-15). Why: GLM-5.3 Flash under the codex harness in cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0316 (10 nc-codex trials, 8 passes, $0.7267, $0.0908/pass, build 1d9243eb1) made 104 apply_patch calls and 15 failed: 14 "Failed to find expected lines" and 1 "multiple operations target" (Delete File then Add File of one path). None was a heredoc or "command not found" form. In older GLM trials in ~/hill/harbor/jobs, 6 such failures (glmmini nc-codex) are fixed on master by a162ab6eb, 88e95c06e and 1d9243eb1, and 6 are model format errors that stock rejects too (3 invalid hunk headers, 3 without a final End Patch line). The parser, seek_sequence fuzz (exact, trim_end, trim, Unicode punctuation), sequential chunk search and the duplicate-target check equal stock (codex-rs/apply-patch at rust-v0.162.1), so nanocode was not stricter than stock. A trajectory replay (files rebuilt from Add File and successful patches) gave 4 live and 1 older context failure that apply only out of order, 2 live failures that differ only in a whitespace run inside a line, and 1 live delete then add. The replay harness output/patch-lenient runs these 7 real patches through `apply_patch::apply`: all 7 fail with lenient off (stock text) and apply with it on, and the 5 rebuilt files equal the Python reference result. The cost of the calls from each such failure up to the next patch of the same file is $0.0380 of $0.7267 (out of order 2.46%, whitespace 1.88%, delete then add 0.87%), so with the flag $/pass is about 0.0861 (-5.2%) at equal pass rate. This is 2 of 10 trials, and the other 9 live context failures are stale or unknown context that no matcher fixes. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy --no-deps -- -D warnings` on nanocode-backend-codex and nanocode-cli, `cargo check -p nanocode-cli`.
- feat(executor): on Linux, nanocode resolves host names itself and reads the user database from /etc/passwd and /etc/group, so the CLI calls no glibc NSS function (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: NSS-removal lane for the static-glibc link). What: (1) `nanocode_executor::dns` answers `lookup_host` on the existing lookup thread instead of std's `to_socket_addrs` (getaddrinfo). It reads /etc/hosts first, maps `localhost` and `*.localhost` to loopback (RFC 6761), then reads /etc/resolv.conf (`nameserver` up to glibc's MAXNS of 3, `search` and `domain`, `options ndots timeout attempts use-vc no-aaaa` with glibc's limits of 15, 30 and 5) plus `LOCALDOMAIN`, `RES_OPTIONS` and the host name's domain as glibc does. It tries the names in glibc's ndots order, sends AAAA and A together on one connected UDP socket per server, retries a truncated answer over TCP, follows CNAME chains, matches the ID and the question, rejects forward compression pointers and loops, and uses glibc's per-round wait (`timeout << round / servers`). Addresses come AAAA first unless the AAAA family has no route (a UDP connect probe, as glibc's RFC 3484 sort does), then happy eyeballs takes over. macOS, Windows and Android keep getaddrinfo, since their resolvers carry scoped and VPN DNS that no file shows. (2) `nanocode_sys::unix::user_entry` parses /etc/passwd on Linux (new `user_entry_named` and `group_name` parse /etc/passwd and /etc/group), which feeds `Account::current` and `user_shell_path`, and psh-os's `user_name`, `user_shell`, `group_name` and `~user` expansion. psh-utils' gitconfig lookup and nanocode-mpp's store path take `$HOME` and fall back to /etc/passwd instead of `std::env::home_dir` (getpwuid_r). A user that only LDAP or sssd knows has no login shell or `~user` home from these, and the callers fall back as they already do when the entry is missing. Checks: `cargo build --release -p nanocode-cli` with `-Wl,--trace-symbol` on the five symbols: before, `nm -D` listed getaddrinfo, __res_init, getpwnam_r, getpwuid_r and getgrgid_r; after, none of them (std's rlib still references getaddrinfo, __res_init and getpwuid_r, and --gc-sections drops them). A live `nanocode exec -m claude-haiku-4-5 "Reply with exactly: ok"` under strace answered ok, opened /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf and no libnss, nsswitch.conf or passwd file, and resolved the egress proxy `pyramid-hand-egress.pyramid-hand-egress.svc` through the search list in glibc's order (as-is, tail388b2e.ts.net, then pyramid-hands.svc.cluster.local). Latency against getaddrinfo, output/dns-bench (interleaved, release, hosted Hand at load ~6, Tailscale MagicDNS 100.100.100.100), medians and p95: api.anthropic.com 81.5/135 ms against 87.0/147 ms (40 rounds), github.com 83.4/132 against 86.0/140, the proxy name through three search domains 336/468 against 333/458, localhost from /etc/hosts 92/114 µs against 97/123 µs (200 rounds). Both resolvers returned the same addresses in the same order for api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, github.com, localhost and pyramid.tehq.net. Simulator: `nanocode-sim --scenario dns` drives `dns::lookup` through a `Wire` that serves a seeded zone (CNAME chains, NXDOMAIN, NODATA, a hosts file, mixed case, compression) from 1 to 3 servers of which at least one is healthy and the others are silent or answer SERVFAIL or REFUSED, with garbage, duplicate, reordered and truncated replies, and judges the result against the zone, that TCP follows only a truncated reply, and that only configured servers are asked: 3,000 seeds pass with `--twice`. Mutations `cut_answer` (a server drops a record without setting TC) and `drop_search` (the resolver gets no search list) are caught by 1,634 and 961 of 3,000 seeds, and a resolver that ignores TC fails 524 of 3,000.
- perf(djs): JSON.parse and JSON.stringify keep their working vectors on the heap between calls (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane). A Code Mode tool call runs one `JSON.stringify` of its input and one `JSON.parse` of its result, mostly small values. Each `json::parse` made a `Parser` with five empty vectors (frames, keys, values, key units, per-depth shapes) and each `stringify_fast_at` a `Ser` with eight (output bytes at 256, pieces, frames, keys, deep offsets, clean prototypes, the key cache and its bytes), so a small call grew and freed them every time: about 1,700 of the 3,800 instructions of `JSON.parse('{"ok":true,"n":1}')` were `malloc`, `realloc` and `free`. `json::Scratch` and `json::StringifyScratch` hold them in `Heap::json_scratch` and `Heap::stringify_scratch`: a call takes them, clears them, and puts them back, and `restore_image` swaps them into the fresh heap like `compile_scratch`. They hold no value across calls (each is cleared on take), and a wide stringify buffer is not kept. Instructions per iteration (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, 20,000 iterations minus none, djsrun on 016205b06 -> this): `JSON.parse('{"ok":true,"n":1}')` 6,454 -> 5,692 (-11.8%), `JSON.stringify({ i })` 7,301 -> 6,073 (-16.8%) (QuickJS 2021-03-27: 4,723 and 7,792). Code Mode cells (output/cellbench on the code-mode-engine native host, instructions per cell from 1,200 minus 200 cells, best of 3): empty 80,837 -> 81,381 (+0.7%, the two swaps), tool1 190,552 -> 189,211, seq16 1,046,209 -> 1,017,876 (-2.7%), par16 1,163,175 -> 1,131,117 (-2.8%), agent 1,830,750 -> 1,819,988, sh 2,311,819 -> 2,309,165, seq 1,133,121 -> 1,113,671 (-1.7%), json 1,483,655 -> 1,465,948 (-1.2%), edit 1,133,685 -> 1,125,938. djs benches (base -> this): find 91.28M -> 91.28M, some 92.96M -> 92.97M, forEach 94.56M -> 94.56M, filter 146.23M -> 146.25M, map 160.49M -> 161.39M (+0.56%, previous entry), reduce 93.02M -> 93.02M, loop 301.40M -> 301.40M, gen 2,061.6M -> 2,061.6M, gennext 4,380.6M -> 4,380.6M, err 660.40M -> 660.40M. Checked: test262 subset 2,535 passing, identical pass set; the fuel harness (`Instance::step`, fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited, slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000) prints the same results, yields and `fuel_used` for the four edge scripts, loop, gen, err, the six callback benches and a JSON script (parse of a 1.5 KB text with escapes and 50 records, compact and indented stringify, a syntax error, `\u` escapes and a sparse map); `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Cell profile at 016205b06 (callgrind, 300 cells each, thousands of instructions per cell, sh/seq/json/edit/agent): compile 159/168/263/175/221; JSON.parse of tool results 85/330/313/147/0 (about 66k per 7 KB result); regexp split and its `pristine` check, exec and substrings 1,362 in sh (`l.split(/\s+/)` on 100 lines: 13.6k a line, `pristine` 2.7k a call, `exec_in` 950 a field, a 5-byte substring 423); string split by `'\n'` 241 in seq; per tool call about 57k (seq16 minus tool1 over 15), of which `new Promise(executor)` 7.0k, `JSON.stringify` of the input 7.3k, `JSON.parse` of the result 6.5k, the pump's `await nativeNext()` with its event object about 9k and the cell's own `await` 2.4k; arena zeroing (`zero_ahead`) about 110 per cell.
