- fix(djs): map reserves its result's dense store at the source's dense length, not its `length` (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, Code Mode cell lane). `each_call` (interp/run/each.rs) made map's result with `Heap::new_array_with_length_reserved(proto, len)`, which allocated a `ValueArray` of `len` slots: `[].length = 2 ** 30` then `.map(f)` asked for an 8 GiB store before it ran a callback. The function now takes the length and the reserve apart (`new_array_with_length_reserved(proto, len, reserve)`), and map passes the source's dense count capped at `len`, as filter does since 016205b06. A source whose dense store covers its length reserves the same as before. An element past the reserve takes the `append_element_reserved` refusal and the general store, as before. Check: `function main(){ const a = []; a[3] = 7; a.length = 1 << 30; const m = a.map((x) => x + 1); return m.length + m[3] }` gives 1,073,741,832 before and after (djsrun, 1 GiB heap: the base's reservation failed and fell back to the general loop, so both visit 2^30 holes in about 42 s with a 10 MB peak RSS); the map bench moves 160.5M -> 161.4M (+0.56%) for the extra `element_tail` read. Gates on the combined tree with the next entry: test262 subset 2,535 passing (identical pass set), fuel harness identical, clippy native and wasm32.
- test(sim): the `executor` scenario catches the two executor bugs fixed in 2981fa4e5 and dab3bab7b, with a mutation for each, and its `panics=63` was a miscount (2026-11-15, simexec lane). Two new shapes, drawn from the seed: `busy` (60% of seeds, `bin/nanocode-sim/src/drive.rs`), on a fresh current-thread runtime, readies a timer (a 1 µs sleep) or a socket (one byte already written) and then ping-pongs ordinary wakes between `block_on`'s future and a task; the event must be delivered within 1,024 rounds and 250 ms (both must pass before it fails, so a loaded host whose reactor thread is descheduled while holding the driver does not fail it). `threads` (60%) runs three runtimes at once on the one global reactor: a spinner (current-thread or one worker) that yields forever and so takes the driver for a zero-timeout turn every 61 polls, a receiver (current-thread or one worker) that waits for each of 8 to 47 messages, and a plain sender thread that wakes it from outside and waits for each to be received; a watchdog fails the seed when progress stops for 1 s (`a wake was lost`), and then, and while a stuck runtime shuts down, writes to a registered doorbell socket so the driver blocked in `epoll_wait` returns and the seed ends instead of hanging the process. Mutations live behind `nanocode_executor::sim` (doc-hidden): one global `AtomicU8` the sim sets, read with a relaxed load once per `run_queue` call and once per idle; and a pause (20, 50 or 100 µs, drawn per seed, zero otherwise) before an idle driver takes the reactor, which widens the window dab3bab7b closed. `uncounted_polls` zeroes the tick count at the start of every `run_queue` call (the pre-2981fa4e5 logic: neither `block_on`'s polls nor earlier calls count), caught by 40 of seeds 0..100; `unchecked_drive` makes `try_turn`'s `ready` always false (the pre-dab3bab7b logic: the driver blocks without looking at its queue again), caught by 53 of seeds 0..100 (a pause of 0 never caught it, 20 µs on 8 of 11 threaded seeds, 50 and 100 µs on all, so the pause list leaves 0 out). The `panics=N` line of sweep.sh counts lines matching `panicked`, and every `RESULT` line of this scenario carried `TasksStats { .. panicked: N }`, one per chunk (63 chunks for 0..2000 on 8 jobs); the field is now `unwound` and the sweep reports panics=0. A first run with the socket written through `UnixStream::try_write` panicked on WouldBlock (nanocode's `try_write` needs a readiness event first, as tokio's does), so the byte is written on the std socket before it is registered. Checks (hosted Hand, 5 cores, load 6 to 9 from other lanes): `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-executor --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean, `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 2000 4` passed=2000 panics=0, with `--scenario executor` 0..10000 passed=10000 panics=0 and `--twice` 0..2000 passed; existing mutations unchanged (skip_abort 39, leak_cancelled 72 of 100). Canary rows in cfo.sh: uncounted_polls on 100 seeds, unchecked_drive on 40 (each caught seed waits out the 1 s stall). Files: crates/core/executor/src/{lib.rs,runtime.rs,sim.rs}, bin/nanocode-sim/src/{drive.rs,tasks.rs,main.rs}, bin/nanocode-sim/cfo.sh.
- fix(claude): a steer that preempts a model call completes that call's step in the journal before the resend (2026-11-15). What: with steer_preempts_model under a durable execution policy (a turn log's effect gate), the preempted call's model step was begun and never settled, so the resend's admission advanced the operation past an unsettled effect and the turn failed with "cannot advance past an unsettled effect" instead of resending. The preempt branch now writes a Complete for the attempted step (with the retry scope it ran under) into the journal ahead of the deferred cursor's Advance, so both commit with the next step's admission; its output is a refusal, which a replay never reaches because the cursor already moved past that step. Found by a downstream server test holding a model call open over a durable turn log; without a policy nothing changes. Validation: cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude, native and wasm32-unknown-unknown.
- perf(djs): `each_leaf` (interp/run/each.rs) runs runs of int32 elements in `scan`, a loop monomorphized by mode class and operator, and takes a capture body (`x => { s += x }`) only in forEach (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, callback lane wave 2). What: before each element it evaluates, `each_leaf` calls `scan_any` when the class allows it: UNTIL (some, every, find, findIndex with a comparison), KEEP (filter with a comparison), MAP_TO (map with add, sub or mul), FOLD (reduce `(p, x) => p op x` and forEach's capture). `scan::<KIND, OP>` reads the source's dense store directly and goes on while the element is int32, the result is int32 (no overflow, no product of 0, which can be -0), the predicate does not decide the search, the next element is not a hole and the store fits the result's capacity. It stops one element before the last, before the fuel would reach 0 (at most `(fuel - 1) / cost` elements) and never runs with `gc_stress` or a pending collection. The element it stops at, and every element it does not take, goes through the wave 1 path unchanged, so fuel (the body's summed cost plus `CALL_FUEL` per element), yields, stores and frame state are the same. Stores go straight into the result's `ValueArray` after the first store proved its flags, then `Heap::set_element_count` writes the count and length and `Arena::wrote` notes the tracked range once. filter's result is allocated with the capacity of the source's dense store (at most its length) instead of growing from 0. Fix: a capture body (`get_cap_chk; get_arg0; op; put_cap_chk; return_undef`) returns undefined, but wave 1 stored the capture's new value as map's element and reduce's accumulator (`[1,2,3,4].map(x => { s += x })` gave [1,3,6,10]); `leaf` now takes it only in forEach. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, hosted Hand, djsrun on djs-embed, b29aaf7d2 -> this; QuickJS 2021-03-27 in brackets): find 265.8M -> 91.2M (-65.7%, QuickJS 748.4M: 8.20x faster), some 267.5M -> 92.9M (-65.3%, 1,048.4M: 11.3x), forEach 264.6M -> 94.5M (-64.3%, 1,114.7M: 11.8x), filter 492.4M -> 146.2M (-70.3%, 1,409.2M: 9.64x), map 507.4M -> 160.4M (-68.4%, 1,651.9M: 10.3x), reduce 246.2M -> 93.1M (-62.2%, 1,041.7M: 11.2x); loop 301.4M, gen 2,113.6M, gennext 4,440.6M, err 660.4M unchanged. wasm32 under V8 (node 24, wasmrun cdylib with `unsafe-heap`, instructions:u of 13 runs minus 3 runs over 10, best of 3): find 362.7M -> 102.9M, some 362.5M -> 101.6M, forEach 337.9M -> 111.6M, filter 542.7M -> 170.4M, map 547.1M -> 185.4M, reduce 330.3M -> 113.0M, loop 313.3M -> 322.4M, gen 2,480.6M -> 2,482.4M, gennext 4,816.7M -> 4,812.6M, err 733.4M -> 735.5M (V8 run-to-run noise on loop is about 3%: 358.5M to 368.4M on one build earlier in this lane); wasmrun.wasm 2,202,202 -> 2,211,120 bytes (+8.9 KB for the 18 `scan` instances). With the scan, the remaining cost per call (about 4,000 instructions in find: closure allocation, `each_call`, the leaf match, the first and last element in the general path, `each_done`) is larger than the 100 elements (about 6 instructions each). Checked: test262 subset (3,090 files) 2,535 passing with identical pass sets; the fuel harness (`Instance::step` with `Limits { fuel, slice }`) gives the same result, yield count and `fuel_used` as b29aaf7d2 at slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000 and fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited for the wave 1 edge script, fuse.js, loop.js, gen.js, err.js, the six callback benches and a new callback edge script (Numbers, -0, NaN, int32 overflow, strings, BigInts, null, holes, named properties, getters, a Proxy, a capture in its TDZ, field and `&&` predicates, reduce with and without an initial value, map and filter over 3,000 and 20,000 elements); the edge scripts print the same as b29aaf7d2; a filter and a map over an array of length 2^30 with three elements give the same result as before. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Any change to `run_hot` itself, even one argument of the yield call, moved loop and find natively by 2 to 4% through register allocation, so this change keeps `run_hot` untouched. Where gen goes now (callgrind, 200,000 iterations): about 1,050 instructions per iteration, of which resume about 313 and yield about 330 (each about 40 of them the frame copy and its memcpy), the rest the ten dispatched instructions of the two loop bodies. 2x QuickJS (gen <= 691M) needs about 345 per iteration in all, so the frame switch itself must go: the next step is a generator frame that runs in place in its own ValueArray (a per-frame value base in `run_hot` instead of `vals` of the one stack), which removes both copies and most header writes but touches every frame access, `safepoint_collect`'s stack scan and unwinding. - feat(exec): with `--attempt-pick verifier` (the default), `nanocode exec --attempts N` first compares the attempts' outputs and, when a strict majority of two or more attempts left the same output, applies the lowest-numbered of them without the verifier turn (2026-11-15, L7 best-of-N live lane: Terminal-Bench 2.1 with @cf/qwen/qwen3.8-27b, effort medium, 3 attempts). The output of an attempt is the type and bytes of each path that every attempt wrote or removed against base, so helper scripts with different names do not split a cluster. If no path is common to all attempts, the output is the trimmed final answer, and an empty answer joins no cluster. A tie between two clusters of the largest size leaves the pick to the verifier. Why: in run bo-q10v-1115-0319 (master 5124c7b9a, `--attempt-timeout 405`), task mteb-retrieve had attempts 2 and 3 write `result.txt` = "MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark" (the expected value) and attempt 1 a wrong title, but the verifier ran out its 810 s deadline, so nothing was applied and the trial scored 0 at $0.43; the plain arm passed the task at $0.09. The verifier re-runs the attempts' work, so it is the most likely step to reach the deadline, and agreement between independent attempts needs no model call. Reproducing check: `output/L7-bestofn-live/run-majority.sh BIN OUT CMD` (a chat-completions mock behind cfproxy, each attempt runs CMD once, the verifier answers `chosen: 1`). CMD `echo agreed > result.txt; echo $$-$RANDOM > scratch-$RANDOM.txt`: this change logs `attempts 1, 2, 3 left the same output, so attempt 1 was chosen without the verifier` and sends 6 model requests; master 5124c7b9a runs the verifier and sends 7. CMD `echo $$-$RANDOM > result.txt`: both run the verifier (7 requests). Checked: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode --no-deps -- -D warnings` (only the existing nanocode-executor `fetch_update` warning), `rustfmt --edition 2024 bin/nanocode/src/attempts.rs`, release build. The wasm32 target does not apply, because bin/nanocode is not built for it. Files: bin/nanocode/src/attempts.rs.
- perf(codex): a model step holds smaller transients: `ResponsesService::attempt` boxes the hedge race's `open` futures, the unhedged `open`, the WebSocket run and the WebSocket connect, `ResponseCreate::encode` writes the request into one buffer of its exact size, `ResponsesHttp::send` shares the encoded body with the HTTP client through `EncodedRequest::body` instead of copying it, and `Payload::write` sends head and body with one vectored write instead of a concatenated copy. psh's embedded `start` runs a command on one long-lived engine thread, and on a new thread only while that thread is busy (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, anonymous memory, wave 3). Why: each model step allocated four blocks of about 30 KB on the session worker (the attempt future in `Origin::scope`, the encoded body, its copy in `ResponsesHttp::send` and the head+body message in `Client::send`), and the request frame without input as a fifth. `-Zprint-type-sizes` (RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1 `cargo rustc --release -p nanocode-backend-codex-client --lib -- -Zprint-type-sizes`) showed why the attempt future was 29,928 bytes: `Hedging::race_when` keeps its `primary` argument as an upvar, a pinned copy and an awaitee (3 x 6,464 bytes of `open`) beside the 6,512-byte hedge block, and `run` holds the HTTPS and WebSocket paths side by side. With the boxes the attempt future is 7,008 bytes, the boxed `open` (6,464 bytes) lives only until the response head, and the hedge box exists only when a hedge fires. `encode` counts the frame with a writer that only adds lengths, serializes it once into a `Vec` of frame plus input length, and moves the tail with `copy_within` to splice the input pieces in, so the frame copy and its separate output buffer are gone. `EncodedRequest` keeps its JSON in an `Arc<String>` (`json` and `into_string` are unchanged), and `body` wraps it in `Bytes::from_owner`. `Connection::write_all_vectored` loops on `write_vectored` with `IoSlice::advance_slices`. The engine thread is a `OnceLock<mpsc::Sender>` and an `AtomicBool` busy flag: `start` swaps the flag, sends the run to the thread when it was free, and the thread clears the flag before it calls `ended`, so the next command of a turn finds it free. Engine thread locals stay valid across runs (rg's message state is scoped per invocation, `hash`'s last search is keyed by name, `PATH` and cwd, mktemp keeps its random state). Measured on the 5-core hosted Hand (load 1 to 6), `LLVM_BOLT=/usr/lib/llvm-23/bin/llvm-bolt CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1 scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode` of 9e70d5ce7 and of this change, bench/cli `suite.mjs --steps=10 --only=nc` under tools/netguard.sh, with the direct-tools lane (h=ncdirect, the shipped default) and the Code Mode lane; peak smaps sampled every 0.5 ms (output/peak.py, 20 processes per binary and lane): anonymous memory at the peak, median, direct 1,648 to 1,606 KB, Code Mode 2,670 to 2,506 KB (2,538 KB with BOLT run again on the same build); peak RSS direct 8,896 to 8,816 KB (8,786), Code Mode 12,092 to 12,236 KB (12,082). The file-backed part moves with each BOLT run: the same build laid out twice put 5,776 KB and 5,488 KB of the binary's text at the Code Mode peak, so peak RSS differences under about 0.3 MB between builds are layout noise. Suite medians of 4 interleaved passes of 5 rounds: tool turn direct 8.49 to 8.53 MB, Code Mode 11.65 to 11.89 MB (layout), one-shot CPU 5.12/5.43/5.65/5.80 to 5.17/5.34/5.65/5.47 ms, one-shot peak 7.48 to 7.33 MB, first-frame anonymous memory unchanged. Honest baseline of master 9e70d5ce7 dist+BOLT on this Hand: direct tool turn 8.4 to 8.9 MB (fx 0.0.16: 9.67 MB), of which 1.5 to 1.8 MB is anonymous and the rest file pages (binary text 4.2 to 4.6 MB, .rodata 1.4 MB, libc 1.0 MB), so the 4.8 MB target needs the file-page side. Checks: `cargo check --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-http --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-http -p nanocode-psh-embedded --no-deps` (no new warnings). Files: crates/backends/codex/client/{Cargo.toml,src/responses/request.rs,src/transport/wire.rs,src/transport/http.rs,src/tower/service.rs,src/tower/service/https/shared.rs}, crates/core/http/src/{wire.rs,client/mod.rs}, crates/patches/psh/crates/psh/src/embed.rs, Cargo.lock.
- perf(turnlog): `TurnLog::open` runs no garbage collection, and the snapshot trial in `Lease::commit` collects every state (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 gcfree lane). Before, open walked every `b3:` content key of every state (about 115K at 10K children), because a live durability session skips staging keys in its `committed_records` and live collection could leave a later checkpoint pointing at nothing. Now `Fold::collect` runs at each snapshot trial over all states. Unreached records of a state registered with `collect_unreachable` are dropped as before. Unreached records of every other state move from `stored` to a new `dead` map: `Fold::stored` still reads them, and `snapshot_records` leaves them out. At the top of `Lease::commit`, `Fold::revive` follows the references of the buffered checkpoints and `b3:` records through `EncodedPayload::assembled`, moves each dead record they reach back to `stored` and appends it to the row. So a session that skips a key it committed earlier still gets the record written again, and a snapshot never holds a record that no checkpoint reached at the trial. A log written by an older build keeps its garbage until the first snapshot trial after open, and a reopen drops dead records, as the open-time walk did. Numbers, box pyramid-prd-rootbytes-a3f1 (48 cores), `output/gcprof` with `MemoryLog`, pinned to one core, 3 interleaved rounds of 3 opens, base d55bd904b against the change: do10k (`do10k-rows.jsonl`) 394-568 ms against 283-411 ms. The same log after one snapshot commit (both builds write the identical row, md5 4dc646e3): 264-446 ms against 198-258 ms. A fresh native 10K log written by this change (scale-bench, 10,000 done, 0 children over two calls): 436-459 ms against 338-360 ms. Identity: on do10k both builds give `TurnLog::history` 70,566 events, 1de28722f2715485. The open fold differs only by what the base collects at open (50,434 records on do10k, 18 on the fresh log), and one snapshot commit on each log writes byte-identical rows from both builds (fresh md5 70f475b5). Cost: a snapshot trial now walks all states. Against a base whose harness registers no collectable state and so skips the walk, one snapshot commit takes 263-264 against 325-329 ms (do10k after migration) and 435-441 against 527-528 ms (fresh 10K). Sims: `--twice` 0..2000 2000/2000, `--twice --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` 1000/1000, `--calm --row-limit 1024` 1000/1000, `--twice --snapshot-ratio 1` 1000/1000, `--long 100` 200/200, 0 panics, the same on base, and `seal_skipped` caught 107/200 on both. The turnlog sim policy writes a `<scope>:gc` state whose checkpoint reaches a rotating chain of `b3:` contents, and pushes a content only when its own cache does not hold it, as `committed_records` does. It asserts that every content the checkpoint reaches reads back after each commit and after each restart. The new mutation `content_collected_live` registers that state as collectable, so its garbage is dropped instead of kept dead: caught 389/400 (`--twice`) and 377/400 (state-bytes). A build with `revive` disabled fails 186/400 and 318/400 on the restart read. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-turnlog -p nanocode-sim -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked -p nanocode-turnlog --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, rustfmt on the changed lines.

- perf(djs): the tier-0 loop fuses `i < n` with a local or argument bound, reads each instruction word without a bounds check in wasm, and stores `add_loc8`'s sum as an f64 directly when it is outside the int32 range (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs run_hot lane). What: (1) a third superinstruction head `inc_lt_loc` (`Op::wide` maps it to `inc_loc`, the general path runs it as `inc_loc`) heads `inc_lt_loc i; get_loc8 i; get_loc8 n | get_arg8 n; lt; jump_if_true8`; one `run_hot` arm serves both bound kinds and picks the slot base from the bound's opcode (`lp` or `bp + 2`), charges the group's summed cost (a const assertion keeps `get_arg8` and `get_loc8` the same cost and size), and runs the head as `inc_loc` when the bound is not an int32 or the branch is wide, so fuel totals, yields and stop points stay the same. The compiler emits it for unchecked locals and arguments below 256 (`loop_test` in compiler/resolve.rs). (2) Every `FuncTemplate` has at least `CODE_SLACK` (7) bytes of cell after its code (`alloc_template_in` pads `DATA`, `length_fits` in heap/walk.rs requires it), so the 8-byte instruction word at any `ip < end` is inside the cell and `word` reads it through `arena_read`: no check in the `unsafe-heap` wasm modules, the arena's one checked read natively, and no `Exit::General` at the arena's end. The padding is below 16 bytes, so `handlers` (floor of the rest over 16) finds no extra record. The unused `sp0` copy and its debug assertion go. (3) `add_loc8` stores `p + q` as raw f64 bits when `|p + q| > i32::MAX` (never NaN there) instead of `conv::number`'s int32 round trip. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, hosted Hand, ~/bench-djs, master 118dee1b3 -> this; native is djsrun on djs-embed, wasm is the wasmrun cdylib of djs-embed with `unsafe-heap` under node 24, 13 runs minus 3 runs over 10, best of 3; QuickJS 2021-03-27 in brackets): native loop 318.7M -> 301.4M (-5.4%, QuickJS 530.7M: 1.76x), gen 2,373.0M -> 2,113.6M (-10.9%, 1,382.9M), gennext 4,646.9M -> 4,440.6M (-4.4%, 4,475.9M), find 766.0M -> 782.3M (+2.1%, 748.4M), some 767.0M -> 783.5M (+2.1%, 1,048.4M), forEach 1,011.2M -> 1,011.5M (1,114.7M), filter 990.5M -> 997.8M (+0.7%, 1,409.2M), map 1,100.0M -> 1,110.3M (+0.9%, 1,651.9M), reduce 700.5M -> 703.0M (+0.3%, 1,041.7M), err 657.8M -> 660.4M (+0.4%, 1,984.4M); wasm loop 358.0M -> 319.3M (-10.8%), gen 2,887.2M -> 2,479.4M (-14.1%), gennext 5,204.9M -> 4,809.0M (-7.6%), find 856.3M -> 802.9M (-6.2%), some 857.2M -> 804.2M (-6.2%), forEach 1,155.8M -> 1,119.8M (-3.1%), filter 1,140.8M -> 1,086.8M (-4.7%), map 1,174.6M -> 1,151.8M (-1.9%), reduce 777.7M -> 732.2M (-5.9%), err 742.8M -> 738.2M (-0.6%). `let n = 2000000; for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) s += i` natively 598.7M -> 325.4M. By step (native / wasm loop): (3) alone 299.5M / 332.6M; (2) on top 297.5M / 315.8M and moves wasm find -5.8%, filter -10%, map -2.3% but native find and some +2.1% (LLVM's layout of `run_hot`, the native read keeps its check); (1) on top leaves the other benches within 0.3% natively and moves wasm filter +5.8%, err +2.1% against (2), still below master. The native +2.1% on find and some is the cost taken for the wasm gains. Measured and dropped: one backward-jump check `fuel <= lim` with `lim` = `i64::MAX` while a collection is wanted, else the fuel floor of `hot_backedges` jumps (replacing the collect, fuel and budget checks): wasm loop 315.8M -> 292.8M, but wasm filter +8.5%, forEach +3.7%, map +2.3%, gen +1.6% and native gen +1.7%, gennext +1.7%, err +1.6% (V8's and LLVM's code for `run_hot` again, D2441). loop stays above the 265M goal: per iteration natively about 150 instructions, of which about 60 are register moves and spills LLVM adds in the 5,000-instruction `run_hot`. Re-measured after rebasing onto each_leaf (e8cf87dd2 -> this, same method): native loop 318.7M -> 301.4M, gen 2,373.0M -> 2,113.6M, gennext 4,646.9M -> 4,440.6M, find 265.5M -> 265.8M, some 267.0M -> 267.5M, forEach 264.3M -> 264.6M, filter 492.1M -> 492.4M, map 507.1M -> 507.4M, reduce 245.8M -> 246.2M, err 657.8M -> 660.4M; wasm loop 352.8M -> 317.0M, gen 2,886.9M -> 2,481.1M, gennext 5,210.4M -> 4,812.3M, find 360.7M -> 360.3M, some 363.4M -> 363.2M, forEach 338.7M -> 338.7M, filter 546.8M -> 548.4M, map 545.0M -> 545.3M, reduce 328.4M -> 328.5M, err 746.7M -> 737.5M (each_leaf moves the callback benches out of the paths this change touches). Checked: test262 subset (output/t262 harness, 3,090 files) 2,535 passing with the identical pass set; the fuel harness (`Instance::step`, `Limits { fuel, slice }`) gives the same result, yield count and `fuel_used` as master for the edge-case script, a fusion script (Number sums across the int32 boundary, -0, NaN, Infinity, strings, null, objects with valueOf, local and argument bounds that are int32, float, string, object, NaN, undefined, BigInt and changed inside the loop, closures over the counter, labelled continue and break, a throw in the loop, a generator), loop.js, gen.js, find.js and err.js at fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited with slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000; both scripts print the same as master. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/bytecode/ops.rs, bytecode/template.rs, compiler/resolve.rs, heap/walk.rs, interp/run.rs, interp/run/hot.rs.
- perf(store-jsonl): `briefs::query` applies the caller's keep filter to the sorted candidates until it has `limit` of them, instead of to every row, so `--continue` (limit 1) calls it once instead of once per indexed session and runs about 0.5M fewer user instructions at 1,000 sessions (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: session store lane, wave 3). A row whose summary does not match its listing entry, or is unreadable, still sends the listing to the full path only when keep accepts it, as before. Checked on the hosted Hand with nc-lite `fast` builds of 524c2a6ca and of this change with the archive compaction change, bench/cli suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nclite --sessions=1000 --storerounds=10, three interleaved pairs, perf stat medians: store-resume user 21.93M/21.91M/21.89M -> 20.29M/20.25M/20.21M (20.8M with the compaction change alone), store-list 6.86M/6.86M/6.85M -> 6.91M/6.90M/6.90M, 0 errors, `nc-lite sessions` output byte-identical. `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-store-jsonl`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-store-jsonl --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- perf(store-jsonl): `Sessions::archive` compacts a session journal only when `Journal::superseded` finds more superseded bytes than live bytes, instead of on every archive, so `nc-lite exec --continue` on a 1,000-session store runs 21.9M -> 20.8M user instructions (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: session store lane, wave 3). What: compaction rewrote the whole journal into a temporary file, synced it and renamed it, and archive then read, compressed and synced it again. A resumed session's journal is mostly live, because each turn's Replace keeps the earlier content-addressed records: after 10 resumes of a bench session the compacted journal is 60,655 B and the uncompacted one 82,928 B. `superseded` estimates live bytes from the index: each state's entry once, each `Record::Entry` entry once, and for a value outside its state's entry the key, the value and the JSON frame `{"key":"","value":},`. Owner lines are not counted, so the estimate errs toward compacting. Compaction runs when the indexed length is more than twice that estimate, which bounds a journal at twice its live size and pays each rewrite with at least as many appended bytes as it rewrites. `JsonlStore::compact` still compacts every journal. A skipped compaction leaves the journal byte-identical, and archive still hardens, compresses, syncs and renames as before. Checked on the hosted Hand with nc-lite `fast` builds (symbols kept) of 524c2a6ca and of this change, bench/cli suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nclite --sessions=1000 --storerounds=10 on copies of one 1,000-session store, perf stat medians, interleaved: store-resume user 21.87M/21.92M -> 20.81M/20.79M, store-list unchanged (6.85M), 0 errors, request bodies identical round by round (25,855 to 34,610 B). 40 resumes of one session never compacted: the raw journal grew 14,939 -> 324,523 B, about 7 KB per resume of which about 1.8 KB is superseded, and its archive after 10 resumes is 5,471 B against 4,643 B compacted. Measured in the same pass and not shipped: the `.summaries-v2` base written zstd-compressed with the session dictionary (readers accept it since 3fbb728cd) takes a rebuilt 1,000-session base from 348,564 to 66,614 B and the store from 1,140 to 858 B per session, but the full summaries path (`nc-lite sessions` with `.index-v1` removed, the path `nanocode sessions` and every fallback read) rises 33.4M -> 40.4M user instructions, 7.1M of it in nanocode_zstd decoding (huff0 literals 3.0M, sequences 3.7M). SHA-256 of journal records is 3.7M of `--continue` under callgrind only because valgrind hides SHA-NI and the portable rounds run; natively, perf record over 20 resumes puts `nanocode_sys::sha256::x86::compress` at 1.6% of sampled user instructions (about 0.35M), so lazy verification was not worth weakening the read check. `cargo build --locked --profile fast -p nc-lite`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-store-jsonl`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-store-jsonl --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- perf(djs): an Array callback loop entered at the call (`each_call`, `EachNative`) whose callback body is one leaf expression runs in `each_leaf` (interp/run/each.rs) without dispatching the body: `get_arg0; get_arg1 | push0..3 | push_i8 | push_i32; add | sub | mul | lt | le | gt | ge | strict_eq | strict_ne; return` and `get_cap_chk c; get_arg0; add | sub | mul; put_cap_chk c; return_undef` (`x => x === 99`, `x => x > 49`, `x => x * 2`, `(p, x) => p + x`, `x => { s += x }`) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, callback lane). What: `fast_leaf_call` calls `each_leaf` after `each_call` entered the callback's frame for the first element and the call's fuel is charged (when fuel is left, as the run loop's check at that entry). It reads the frame's code once (as `builtins/array.rs` `comparator_of` reads a sort comparator's) and then, per element, evaluates the body on int32 or Number operands as run_hot's arms do (int32 first, then f64 through `conv::number`; `strict_eq` on int32, Numbers, identical bits, else a string or BigInt pair declines), decides the step as `hot_step` does (forEach, reduce, map, filter, some, every, find, findIndex), stores map's and filter's element, writes the capture's Box (with the tracked-page note), charges the body's summed cost (each instruction's `OPS` cost, `return` included) plus `CALL_FUEL`, and stops at each frame entry where run_hot stops: a wanted collection (`gc_stress`, `gc_pending` after a store) runs `safepoint()` there, and fuel <= 0 returns to the run loop. At any stop the frame and loop state are written as `hot_enter` writes them for that element (pc 0), so the general path or the next slice runs that element's bytecode as before; an element the kernel does not take (a non-number operand, the TDZ marker, a hole, a shorter array, a failed store, a non-boolean predicate result) is left to the bytecode with nothing changed. The element that ends the loop (the last one, or the one that decides some/every/find/findIndex) is completed in place as `each_leave` completes it (the store, the body's cost without `CALL_FUEL`, KVALUE and reduce's THIS, `pop_frame`, `each_done`), outside the per-element loop, which measured 17 instructions per element slower with that branch inside. A map entered at the call allocates its result's dense store at the source length (`Heap::new_array_with_length_reserved`) instead of growing it 8, 16, .., 128, and after one store through `create_element_fast` proves the result's flags (no user code runs in between) the next appends go through `Heap::append_element_reserved` (in-capacity append, filter's length set). Not done as a compiler head opcode (as `add_loc8`): the body would need two heads (`get_arg0`, `get_cap_chk`) mapped in `wide`, `implied`, `step` and the stack checker, `comparator_of` would no longer match `(a, b) => a - b`, and run_hot would get another arm (D2441); the match costs about 40 instructions per call. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, hosted Hand, output/djsrun on djs-embed, ~/bench-djs, bf4f96517 -> this; QuickJS 2021-03-27 in brackets): find 766.0M -> 265.4M (-65.3%, QuickJS 748.4M: 2.82x faster), some 767.0M -> 267.0M (-65.2%, 1,048.4M: 3.93x), forEach 1,011.2M -> 264.2M (-73.9%, 1,114.6M: 4.22x), filter 990.5M -> 492.0M (-50.3%, 1,409.1M: 2.86x), map 1,099.9M -> 507.0M (-53.9%, 1,651.9M: 3.26x), reduce 700.5M -> 245.7M (-64.9%, 1,041.7M: 4.24x); loop 318.7M, gen 2,373.0M, err 657.8M unchanged, gennext 4,646.9M -> 4,648.9M (+0.04%). In wasm32 under V8 (node 24, cdylib of djs-embed with `unsafe-heap`, `run` of main, instructions:u of 13 runs minus 3 runs over 10, best of 3): find 855.6M -> 359.3M (-58.0%), some 857.0M -> 365.6M (-57.3%), forEach 1,156.1M -> 345.4M (-70.1%), filter 1,145.8M -> 546.4M (-52.3%), map 1,280.6M -> 538.0M (-58.0%), reduce 777.5M -> 329.9M (-57.6%), loop 361.7M -> 356.6M, gen 2,886.0M -> 2,887.4M, gennext 5,202.8M -> 5,201.6M, err 748.2M -> 743.2M. Per element, find's kernel is about 112 instructions natively (callgrind) against 363 for the dispatched body, return arm, `hot_step` and `hot_enter`; the rest of each call (closure allocation, `each_call`, the match) is about 2,000. Checked: test262 subset (3,090 files) 2,535 passing with identical pass sets; the fuel harness (`Instance::step` with `Limits { fuel, slice }`) gives the same result, yield count and `fuel_used` as bf4f96517 at slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000 and fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited for a leaf edge script (every mode, Numbers, -0, NaN, int32 overflow of sums and products, strings, BigInts, null, undefined, holes, an array with a named property, a capture read in its TDZ, string concatenation through a capture, a reduce without an initial value, map and filter over 20,000 elements so collections fall inside the loop), the earlier edge and mixed workloads, loop.js, gen.js and the six callback benches; the edge script prints the same as bf4f96517. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/interp/run/each.rs, interp/run/fastpath.rs, interp/run/hot.rs (`object_slot` visibility), heap/object.rs.
- test(sim): the streams scenario checks five TLS rules on every seed (bin/nanocode-sim/src/streams/tls_rules.rs), each against an in-memory rustls client and server pair over the simulator's Ed25519 key and a pinned verifier, with random fragment sizes and confidentiality limits of 8 to 31 records: a TLS 1.2 handshake that signs with Ed25519 completes and carries data; after a flipped tag byte both sides' write, write_vectored and flush fail and the peer gets bad_record_mac; a client session cache resumes the servers it can hold and drops the one before them; a ChangeCipherSpec sealed inside an encrypted TLS 1.3 record is refused as IllegalMiddleboxChangeCipherSpec with unexpected_message; and no key encrypts more records than its suite's confidentiality limit. Five mutations replay the bugs e289207d6 fixed, four through a runtime switch in the patched rustls (`rustls::internal::mutation::set`, one relaxed atomic load at each hook, None unless the simulator sets it): tls12_without_ed25519 (caught by 1000 of 1000 seeds), tls_write_after_error (1000/1000), tls_cache_by_capacity (evicting by VecDeque capacity instead of max: 746/1000), tls_encrypted_ccs (1000/1000) and tls_late_key_update (refresh only at the exact limit, no stop for the KeyUpdate: 704/1000); each has a canary row in cfo.sh. A rule's writes loop over partial writes and settle the pair when rustls takes none, as a full send buffer or a pending KeyUpdate makes it do. The non-empty certificate_request_context fix (needs client auth) and the c1e78a172 blocked-write stall (in nanocode-tls's stream, needs a small transport buffer) have no mutation yet. Checked on the hosted Hand (5 cores shared, load 3 to 5): sweep 0..2000 passes, 5000 unmutated streams seeds pass, --tidy clean, workspace check clean; the wasm32 check of rustls fails on master's own `UnixTime::now` in time_provider.rs, which this change does not touch (2026-11-15, simtls lane).
- deps(djs): djs-core loses the code nothing in the workspace reaches: 1,780 lines net (83,199 to 81,419 lines of src/; 46 files, 22 lines added back as trimmed `use` lists) (2026-11-15, djs cut lane "djscut"). How: every `pub ` in djs-core became `pub(in crate) `, a loop put back `pub` wherever djs-embed, djs-prelude or djs-prelude's build script (which builds djs-core with no features) failed to compile, the items rustc then listed as dead were deleted with their imports, and every `pub(in crate)` went back to `pub`, so the diff is deletions only and visibility is as before. Gone: bytecode/disasm.rs's listing and vm/dump_runtime.rs's dump writer, heap/layout.rs's layout export for js/src/reader.ts, `Phase1Code::bytes`, `CodeBuf::finish`, regexp `exec`/`exec_at`/`resume`, `num::literal_value`, `NumStr::len`/`is_empty` and similar accessors. Kept: djs-embed's whole public API (a first cut that also narrowed it to what code-mode-engine calls removed `Instance::call`, `set_now` and `Builder::fuel`, which the equivalence harness and other embedders use, so it was reverted), trait impls with empty bodies, the regions compat_inputs.rs hashes, and macro-generated items (the `ops!` table's helpers, `imm` types, atom constants); the -15,000 target is not reachable by deleting dead code, this is all of it. RECORDS_HASH and BUILD_HASH change as with any djs-core edit. Equivalence: a harness on djs-embed (`Snapshot::build` of each test with assert.js, sta.js and its includes, fuel 200,000,000) over every 4th file of test262's test/built-ins, test/language and test/annexB (12,199 files) prints byte-identical results before and after (7,049 OK, 3,760 ERR with the same messages, 1,390 SKIP), and a 29-script smoke corpus (instantiate and run with a fixed clock, seed and time zone) is byte-identical too, both 4cff7ecb6 against the cut on it; the rebase onto 23cfbf6cd conflicted only where perf(djs) added `CodeBuf::exact` beside the removed `finish`. Checked: cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets and the wasm32-unknown-unknown check of djs-core, djs-prelude, djs-embed and nanocode-code-mode-engine, nanocode-sim release sweep 0..2000 with 4 jobs (2,000 passed, 0 panics) and --tidy clean.
- perf(alloc), measured and not shipped: a bump arena per turn (or per model step) for the turn's transient allocations does not lower tool-turn RSS, because a turn allocates several times its live peak and an arena cannot reuse memory before its reset (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: tool-turn peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, arena lane). Nothing in the build changes. Method: an experiment build of 23cfbf6cd (release, symbols kept; uprobes are not available on the hosted Hand's kernel 6.18, which has no tracefs) wrote one 40-byte record (thread id, operation, address, size, CLOCK_MONOTONIC time) to fd 9 from each `GlobalAlloc` call of `nanocode_sys::alloc::Heap`, and one 10-step tool turn of bench/cli (`suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc`, under tools/netguard.sh) ran on each row: the direct-tools row (h=ncdirect) and the Code Mode row (h=nc). Step boundaries are the request-body allocations of 28 to 40 KB. Results for the nanocode-worker thread, which makes 94% of the allocated bytes: the direct row allocates 19,164 blocks and 4,452 KB in the turn, with a live peak of 573 KB and 202 KB live at the end; steady steps allocate 340 to 360 KB each (the first steps 948 and 486 KB) and leave 17 to 21 KB alive past the step; 2,225 KB of the 4,452 KB live less than 0.1 ms and 1,365 KB less than 1 ms. The Code Mode row allocates 7,052 KB, live peak 2,048 KB (1,216 KB in large blocks from Code Mode), steady steps about 400 KB with 23 to 28 KB survivors, and one 2,953 KB step that compiles the cell. Models, from the same records: a turn arena needs the turn's volume, 4.45 and 7.05 MB, against live peaks of 0.57 and 2.05 MB; a per-step arena that is reset only when all its blocks are freed never resets, because every step leaves survivors (history items, tool results), so its peak is 5.0 and 7.1 MB; an oracle per-step arena that receives only the blocks freed in the same step, with the survivors on the heap, peaks at 985 KB (direct) and 2,134 KB (Code Mode), above the sum of the per-size-class live high-water marks of the size-class heap, 853 KB (direct; largest classes 32 KB 128 KB, 20 KB 100 KB, 10 KB 60 KB, 448 B 53 KB, 8 KB 48 KB) and 1,945 KB plus the large blocks (Code Mode). So no assignment of these allocations to an arena beats the size-class heap with full reuse, and the arena also adds a lifetime rule that every allocation site must keep. Where the gap is: the worker's segment holds about 1.6 MB resident at exit of the direct row (pagemap, agent lane of turn-boundary release) for 853 KB of per-class high water, so about 0.75 MB comes from page structure and purge policy (one touched page per class per heap, retained high-water pages, dirty slices), not from transient lifetimes; the other threads are small (durability-store 220 to 337 KB allocated, about 60 KB live peak; each psh engine thread about 81 KB allocated, 61 KB live peak).
- fix(process): a truncated command output drops the start or end of a secret form the window cut before it redacts, not after, so a JSON-escaped secret cut inside its escaping no longer leaves a stray backslash beside its placeholder; test(sim): the capture scenario finds the omission marker by its count, and gains the mutation `redact_then_trim` (2026-11-15, CFO capture failures, lane capbug). Why: `CapturedChunk::trim_truncated_secrets` redacted the head and tail first and then looked for a form's partial start at the head's end (and partial end at the tail's start). A secret `AFFBBCDECDF\\` (two backslashes) has the escaped form `AFFBBCDECDF\\\\` (four); a head cut after three backslashes held the whole plain form, which redaction replaced, leaving `[S0]\`, and a lone backslash is no form's prefix, so it stayed, while the full output redacts the escaped form whole. The partial cut also counted redacted bytes, not captured ones, in the omitted count. What: the trim now runs on the captured bytes, repeating until no suffix of the head is a proper prefix of a form (and no prefix of the tail a proper suffix of one), so cutting a partial form that begins inside a complete one also drops the rest of that one; `render` redacts once, over the whole output. The second CFO shape was the checker's: the filler alphabet holds `.`, space and newline, so the output itself could contain `\n... `, and the check took the first such text for the marker; it now takes the first `\n... <digits> bytes omitted ...\n`. `redact_then_trim` renders the old way in the sim; cfo.sh runs it as a canary over 4000 seeds. The old order failed about once in 10^5 seeds (a cut had to land between the third and fourth backslash of an escaped secret whose only escapes are its trailing pair), so half the generated secrets are now letters ending in two backslashes, and the mutation is caught by 3 of seeds 0..400, 21 of 0..4000 and 14 of 4000..8000; capture seeds 0..20000 pass, also with --twice.

- refactor(psh): rg's 103 flags are one table: crates/patches/psh/crates/psh-utils/src/rg/flags/defs.rs declares `const FLAGS: &[Flag]` of a `Flag` struct (long and short names, aliases, negation, value name, category, short and long docs and an `update` function) instead of 103 unit structs each implementing a 13-method `Flag` trait behind `&dyn Flag`, and the parser and the help writer read its fields (2026-11-15, swarm pshcut). psh-utils 102,730 to 100,673 lines of Rust (-2,057). No behavior change: every string literal of master's defs.rs is in the table byte for byte (output/rgflags-diff/lits.py; the literals of rg/flags/mod.rs, parse.rs, hiargs.rs and doc/help.rs are unchanged), `rg -h`, `rg --help`, `rg --type-list` and `rg --version` are byte-identical, and output/rgflags-diff runs every flag's long, short, alias and negated forms with valid and invalid values and 6,000 seeded combinations of 1 to 4 flags (6,607 cases) through master's and this release psh with equal stdout, stderr and status. It compares output as sorted lines and masks timings, because rg's parallel search orders lines differently from run to run; the 4 cases left differing were NUL-separated records the harness does not split and one `-q --trace` race, each equal over 8 reruns of both binaries once sorted.
- build(cli): BOLT also trains a Code Mode tool turn (`train-cli.py codemode`: the bench's ten steps three times with `--codex-orchestration code-mode`), and orders the functions only it reaches after the direct tool turn's, which lowers the bench's 10-step tool turn from 17.9 to 13.1 MB peak RSS on a full `build-cli.sh` build and leaves the direct tool turn, one-shot, first frame and `--version` unchanged (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, wave 2 of cold layout). Why: since e6abbf80d Codex models call their tools directly and Code Mode is opt-in, so training's tool turn, which answers with whatever tool the request offers, ran `exec_command` and never reached Code Mode, while the bench's nc tool lane (`harness/fakellm.mjs`, `h=nc`) still sends every step as an `exec` cell, which nanocode runs through Code Mode though it was not offered. The bench's instrumented tool turn reached 920 functions training never ran (djs's compiler and interpreter, `code_mode::EmbeddedHost::drive_cell`, the cell journals), all left in `.text.cold`: at `exit_group`, with `fault_around_bytes` briefly at 4096, the tool turn touched 2.4 MB of `.text.cold` across 108 64 KB windows (6.9 MB resident) and 1.1 MB of `.rodata` across 45 windows (2.85 MB resident), against 0.25 MB across 34 windows when the same build runs the steps directly. A full build at fac31b654 measured tool turn 17.8 to 18.0 MB in the bench as it stands, and 8.7 to 8.9 MB with the nc lane sending `exec_command` instead (a local copy of the harness with `h=ncdirect` for nc); one-shot 7.2 to 7.65, first frame 6.7 to 6.9 MB, `--version` 1.64 to 1.78 MB. With this change, in the same interleaved passes (3 passes of 4 rounds, hosted Hand shared with four other lanes): tool turn 13.08 to 13.12 MB (bench as it stands), 8.68 to 8.75 against 8.70 to 8.79 (direct); one-shot 7.26 to 7.40; first frame 6.5 to 6.7 MB; `--version` 1.73 to 1.86 against 1.64 to 1.86. Hot `.text` grows by 0.7 MB (`__hot_end` 0xcec72a to 0xd9fe90), all of it placed after the startup, one-shot and direct tool-turn groups, so the direct paths touch the same pages. User instructions are unchanged: one-shot 4.10M against 4.10M, first frame 4.69M against 4.70M (perf stat, median of 6). Measured and dropped: putting `.rodata` input sections of 16 KB or more (or 4 KB) after every profile's small ones in `rodata-cli.py` (tool turn 12.3 to 13.1 against 12.96 to 13.24 MB, one-shot and first frame within spread). Not done: ordering `.text.cold` fragments apart from their hot parts; BOLT 23 emits each function's cold fragment in the hot order and has no option to order them separately, and the cold pages the direct tool turn still touches (252 KB across 34 windows) come from about 320 branch points training reaches in some runs and not others (process output waits, `MemoryStore` acquire, `Execution::accepted_input`).
- perf(store-jsonl): `nc-lite sessions` and `--continue` (nc-lite and `nanocode --continue`) read a brief listing from an append-only binary index, `sessions/.index-v1`, instead of parsing `.summaries-v2` and every summary, so listing 1,000 sessions runs 44.5M -> 6.87M user instructions and continuing the latest runs 44.3M -> 21.9M (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: session store index lane). What: `StateStore::list_briefs(scope, limit, keep)` (default `Ok(None)`, forwarded by `RecordCache` and `SharedStore`) returns `BriefState { preview, scope, state_id, updated_at_ms }` newest first, and `SessionStore::brief_page(workspace, limit, origins)` returns `SessionBrief` from it, or from `newest_page` (a bounded page) or `list_page` when the store answers `None`. `JsonlStore` keeps one row per state: the key (16 bytes for a lowercase UUID), the listing slot and entry of its `.jsonl` and `.jsonl.zst` names, and the summary's file, length, revision, scope (interned per record), `updated_at_ms` and preview, as LEB128 varints. The header names the `.listing` and `.summaries-v2` identities, the offsets read in each and the directory stamp. A listing reads the index, then replays only the new tail of `.listing` (same slot rules as `Listing::entries`) and of `.summaries-v2` (`Remember` and `Moved` as `Summaries::refresh` applies them), checks the directory stamp, stats each unarchived `.jsonl` as `indexed` does, and appends the changed rows as one record (offset-checked, under `try_lock`); the whole index is rewritten through `Listing::change` when it is missing, when its appended records outgrow its base record, or when either source file was replaced. The store answers `None`, and the full path runs, whenever the full path could differ: a stale listing, a summary whose file or length does not match its listing entry, a summary that is neither packed nor a root record whose `session_id`, `workspace` and `updated_at_ms` match it, two present names for one key, or a colocated member that `keep` accepts. Checked on the hosted Hand with nc-lite `fast` builds of master d5c0200be and of this change: bench/cli suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nclite --sessions=1000 --storerounds=10 on copies of one 1,000-session store, perf stat through the PATH shim, medians: store-list user 44.54M -> 6.87M, kernel 11.91M -> 9.53M, wall 23.9 -> 20.4 ms; store-resume user 44.27M -> 21.91M, kernel 15.87M -> 14.87M, spawn to request 25.7 -> 23.4 ms; 0 errors in both. `nc-lite sessions` output is byte-identical to master's on the bench store after the run, after deleting a session file, with garbage appended to the index, with a bad magic, with the index missing, and with a foreign `.jsonl.zst` whose summary is unknown (that case falls back: 51.5M against master's 50.4M). The index costs about 95 bytes per session (93,374 bytes at 1,000 sessions). Under callgrind the listing's 7.3M splits into the dynamic loader 1.6M, index decode 1.3M, row scan and output 2.2M and printing 1.0M; steady `--continue` spends 1.9M in `list_briefs` and the rest in session open and hydrate, the Codex build, compaction at archive and SHA-256 of journal records (3.7M, `Record::located`, `Journal::stored`). `cargo build --locked --profile fast -p nc-lite`, `cargo clippy -p nanocode-store-jsonl -p nanocode-durability -p nanocode-durability-core -p nc-lite`, `cargo check --lib -p nanocode-durability-core -p nanocode-durability --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check -p nanocode-cli`.
- perf(djs-embed): a native snapshot build takes the setup VM's arena as the image (`Vm::take_heap`) instead of copying it with `to_vec`, so a tool turn's anonymous memory at exit falls about 324 KB and its peak RSS about 0.3 MB in the release build (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, anonymous memory, wave 2). Why: gdb at exit_group of a 10-step tool turn (segment and large-block headers read through /proc/pid/pagemap) showed Code Mode holding three large blocks: the instance arena (388 KB mapped, 340 KB resident), the snapshot image copied by `Builder::setup` (324 KB) and the setup VM's arena (836 KB mapped, 372 KB resident), freed but kept in the large-block cache. The cache reuses a block only for a request of at least half its size (`LARGE_CACHE_FIT`), and the instance asks for `Heap::image_capacity(image + IMAGE_ROOM)`, which is 384 KB for an image of 320 KB or less and 448 KB above it. So the setup arena's 372 KB stayed resident whenever the image was at most 320 KB (the release build here), and was reused as the instance arena only when it was larger (the BOLT dist build of fac31b654, with 384 KB and 332 KB blocks and no third). With the arena as the image, the setup arena is never freed, the 324 KB copy is gone, and Code Mode holds image plus instance (about 712 KB) on both sides of that cliff; the compile also skips one 324 KB memcpy and the transient of arena and copy together. wasm keeps the copy: its arena sits at the end of linear memory and the instance reuses the freed space there. Measured (bench/cli suite under tools/netguard.sh, release profile with symbols, base 3f730c21f8, interleaved A/B binaries on the hosted Hand at load 3): RssAnon at exit_group over 17 tool turns each, median 6004 KB before and 5680 KB after; VmHWM median 23280 KB before and 23000 KB after; suite medians of 3 rounds in 4 interleaved passes, tool turn 22.28/22.73/22.80/22.81 MB before and 22.56/22.60/21.97/22.70 MB after, one-shot CPU 11.16/10.55/10.81/10.58 ms before and 9.29/10.87/9.24/11.04 ms after, first-frame anonymous memory 4.82 MB on both. Not confirmed on a dist+BOLT build: there the image straddled the cliff on the large side, so the expected change is the removed transient, not the exit footprint. Measured and dropped in the same pass: growing the setup arena in smaller steps or committing lazily (Arena::zero_ahead already touches only 16 KB ahead, and the mapped 836 KB costs nothing untouched; its realloc copy and the to_vec copy are transients at Code Mode compile, about 1 MB below the tool turn's peak, which comes at the end of the turn with psh threads alive); sizing the 328 KB Vec from the source length (it is the image itself, already exact). Remaining anonymous memory at the peak of the dist build of fac31b654 (sampled every 0.3 ms from /proc/pid/smaps): the session worker's segment, 1.5 to 2.3 MB resident for about 0.25 MB of live blocks, the high-water marks of per-step transients in each size class (four about 30 KB blocks per model step: the boxed `ResponsesService::attempt` future in `Origin::scope`, the request body in `ResponseCreate::encode`, and two in `Client::send` and `ResponsesHttp::send`); 120 to 140 KB of heap per psh-engine thread, one per command; and the nanocode-durability-store thread's own heap, about 124 KB resident.
- perf(subagents): the registry's state mailbox erases each job's reply type before it reaches `nanocode_sync::Mailbox::call`, so `call`, its oneshot and its posted closure are compiled once instead of once per registry job (2026-11-15, bloat lane). `StateMailbox` in `runtime.rs` boxes the job as `FnOnce(&mut RegistryState) -> Box<dyn Any + Send>` and downcasts the reply to the caller's type; a mismatch is unreachable because each job's closure is wrapped next to its own downcast. Behavior is unchanged: jobs still run in order on the same mailbox. cargo llvm-lines on nanocode-subagents (release): 1,097,588 lines / 26,257 copies before, 1,017,417 / 24,330 after (-7.3%). Release rebuild of the crate alone, 3 interleaved rounds under ~/bench.lock on the shared 5-core hosted Hand at load 3.8-7.9 (other lanes building, so walls are noisy): user CPU 52.6/48.8/49.3 s before, 46.7/44.6/51.7 s after (mean -5%); wall 33.3/30.2/32.5 s vs 36.9/25.7/42.1 s, within the noise. Also measured, not shipped: splitting the Claude backend's 9,800-line agent.rs into seven child modules so its one oversized codegen unit (about 100k estimated size vs about 37k for the others) runs in parallel: release rebuild wall 33.4/27.0/26.7 s before, 25.3/25.0/25.0 s after (median -7%) with user CPU unchanged, at load 5.9-7.4; not landed because moving about 5,000 lines of a file several lanes edit daily costs more in conflicts than 2 s.
- perf(store-jsonl): the JSONL store starts its `nanocode-jsonl-sync` thread on the first batch that has files to sync, and answers a settled reply with nothing to sync inline while no sync thread exists, instead of starting the thread at open (2026-11-15, swarm lane startup). Why: read-only uses (`nanocode sessions`, its final `flush`) started and joined a thread that never synced a file. Ordering holds: a reply answered inline has no earlier unsynced file it could overtake, and once the thread runs every reply goes through it as before. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 12-16), release builds with and without this change, interleaved, `sessions --all` on a 52-session home, `perf stat -r 60`: task-clock 8.95 -> 7.10 ms, instructions:k 15.4M -> 11.2M, one thread fewer; p50 wall under `chrt -f 50` (200 runs) 6.85 -> 6.94 ms, within noise. Output byte-identical. Files: crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/lib.rs.
- perf(cli): `nanocode sessions` defaults `--telemetry` to off, as `nanocode hand` does; `--telemetry agent` or NANOCODE_TELEMETRY still turns it on (2026-11-15, swarm lane startup). Why: listing sessions runs no agent turn, model call or tool, yet every run created a new log/otel/<time>-<pid>/ directory with traces.jsonl and metrics.jsonl (233 such directories after a benchmark), started three exporter threads and wrote the startup span. The observability crate's `--telemetry` help still names only `nanocode hand` as off by default. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 12-16), release builds with and without this change (both non-PIE), interleaved, 150 runs under `chrt -f 50` and `perf stat -r 40`, `sessions --all` on a 52-session home: p50 wall 6.91 -> 6.33 ms, peak RSS 11.6 -> 11.1 MB, page faults 501 -> 429, instructions:u 2.07M -> 1.70M, task-clock 9.53 -> 8.31 ms. Output byte-identical. Files: bin/nanocode/src/lib.rs.
- perf(cli): bin/nanocode links its binary non-PIE (`-no-pie`) on Linux glibc from build.rs, so a plain `cargo build --release` or `cargo install` gets the same no-relocation start that scripts/build-cli.sh already gets from `-Crelocation-model=static` (2026-11-15, swarm lane startup). Why: the PIE release binary carried 156,774 R_X86_64_RELATIVE relocations (3.7 MB of .rela.dyn) that ld.so applied on every start, dirtying 2.9 MB of .data.rel.ro before `main`; `--version`, which prints from the C main, spent 2.3M of its 2.3M user instructions and 866 of its 964 page faults there. The main executable loses load-address randomization, as the shipped BOLT build already does. Measured on the hosted Hand (5 cores, load 12-16), release builds of master and this change, interleaved: spawnbench under `chrt -f 50` (150 runs, p50 wall, peak RSS) and `perf stat -r 40`: `--version` 7.05 -> 5.22 ms, 8.7 -> 2.1 MB, page faults 964 -> 98, instructions:u 2.29M -> 0.24M; `--help` 7.30 -> 5.24 ms, 9.5 -> 3.2 MB, faults 1,019 -> 158; `sessions --all` (52-session home) 8.76 -> 6.91 ms, 17.2 -> 11.6 MB, faults 1,344 -> 501. Output byte-identical. Files: bin/nanocode/build.rs.
- fix(sim): cfo.sh's triage reads the results with awk, not gawk, and the bisect was run end to end for the first time (2026-11-15, swarm lane cfo-fix). Why: triage is the only part of the CFO that had never run on a real failure; on a host without gawk (the hosted Hand has only mawk) its `gawk` pipe failed, `picked` came back empty and triage returned 0 having done nothing, silently. Its field extraction is POSIX awk (`summary` and `failures` already use `awk`); only upload's merge needs gawk's `asort`. Checked with a throwaway 10-commit git repository whose commits from the 7th on fail seed 7 (a per-commit nanocode-sim that prints a real FAIL line), the seed record written by `run_job` and `cfo.sh triage`: it reproduces, bisects in 6 runs and records first_bad = the 7th commit and last_good = the 6th; with a missing binary in the range it still finds both, and with every commit failing it records the oldest as first_bad with no last_good. Before, on mawk only, the same run recorded nothing.
- fix(sim): cfo.sh records a job only when its own timeout or the simulator ended it, and skips one killed from outside, as zempo's CFO does (2026-11-15, swarm lane cfo-fix). Why: `run_job` ran the simulator under `timeout --signal=KILL` and recorded every exit 137 as a failure ("killed: timeout after Ns or out of memory"), and a 143, so a `systemctl restart` of nanocode-cfo.service, a deploy or the OOM killer showed up on the results page as failing fuzzers and missed canaries on whichever commit was being fuzzed. What: `timeout --verbose` prints `timeout: sending signal KILL to command` into the job's log only when it fired, which sets `timed_out` (now in each record, and the only way a record gets the "killed: timeout" message); a job that died of SIGKILL, SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP without that line is not recorded, logs one "killed from outside ... not recorded" line to stderr, and its wall time is charged to its fuzzer without rescaling its batch. Checked with a fake simulator through `run_job` (pass, FAIL, a hang past the timeout, kill -KILL and kill -TERM of itself): before, the hang and the self-KILL both recorded "killed: timeout after 2s or out of memory" and the self-TERM "exit 143"; after, the hang records ok=false timed_out=true "killed: timeout after 2s", both outside kills record nothing, pass and FAIL are unchanged.
- perf(psh): psh-utils' stable sorts compile once: `order::sort_by`, `sort_by_key` and `sort` (crates/patches/psh/crates/psh-utils/src/order.rs) sort the positions `0..len` in one non-generic `positions` behind a `dyn FnMut(usize, usize) -> Ordering` and move the elements into that order by following each cycle, and 48 call sites across ls (dirs first), du, tree, cp, rm, chmod, find, fd, rg, grep, jq, tar, zip, diff, opts and git use them instead of `<[T]>::sort_by` (2026-11-15, swarm bloat-psh lane). Why: std's stable sort is instantiated whole (driftsort, quicksort, smallsort, merge: about 1,900 lines of LLVM IR) per element type and comparator closure, so the sorts were 115,399 of psh-utils' 2,030,698 IR lines. Each comparator at those sites is a total order (key comparisons with `Ord`), for which a stable sort's result is unique, so the output is the same; `sort`'s own line sorts and every `sort_unstable*` stay as they were (`ls -v`'s version comparison too, which need not be transitive). Numbers (cargo llvm-lines --release -p psh-utils, 5-core hosted Hand): 2,030,698 -> 1,967,459 lines (-3.1%), sort instantiations 115,399 -> 50,902; a smoke script (ls -la/-R/-v/-S/-r, find, du, tree, sort, jq sort/keys/to_entries/sort_by/group_by, grep -r, rg --sort/--sortr/--json, fd, tar, cp -r, chmod -R, zip/unzip, diff -r, git add/commit/status/diff/log/rm/stash/branch/checkout/blame) prints byte-identical output before and after.
- perf(build): djs-core and djs-libm compile once in a native release build instead of twice (2026-11-15, build speed lane "djs-twice"; thread's hosted Hand, 5 cores, load 12 to 19 from other lanes). Why: djs-prelude's build script makes the base image with djs-core as a build-dependency, and cargo builds a build-dependency with `build-override` (opt-level 0, 256 codegen units) as a separate unit from the opt-level 3 library, and its features differed too: djs-prelude's `unicode` enabled djs-core's two Unicode features but not the `unicode` umbrella that djs-embed enables (which BUILD_HASH leaves out, so the base image still matched). What: `[profile.release.package.djs-core]` and `.djs-libm` set release's opt-level 3 and 16 codegen units, which take precedence over build-override, so the host and target units are equal and cargo shares them; `fast`, `dist`, `lite` and `wasm` repeat their own values for the two packages so their builds are unchanged; djs-prelude's `unicode` adds `djs-core/unicode`. In a cross build (wasm32) the host djs-core now builds at the profile's opt-level instead of 0. Measured: cold `cargo build --locked --release -p djs-embed`, `RUSTC_WRAPPER=`, private target dir, interleaved under the bench lock: summed user CPU 49.6, 47.0 s before against 35.7, 33.9 s after (-13.5 s); wall 96, 90 s against 88, 74 s (the shared base image now waits on the opt-level 3 djs-core, which runs its build script faster); rustc runs of djs_core 2 against 1.
- perf(djs): the compiler emits two superinstruction heads, `add_loc8` (`s += i` on unchecked locals) and `inc_lt` (a `for` loop's `i++` followed by its test `i < constant` and the backward `jump_if_true`), and the tier-0 loop runs each whole group as one instruction (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track: fewer dispatched instructions per loop iteration). What: each head is a new opcode that, outside the tier-0 loop, is exactly its group's first instruction (`add_loc8` is `get_loc8`, `inc_lt` is `inc_loc`; `Op::wide` maps them, `step` runs them through those arms), and the rest of the group stays in the code after it in one fixed layout written by `CodeBuf::exact` without short forms: `add_loc8 a; get_loc8 b; add; put_loc8 c` (7 bytes, one instruction word) and `inc_lt i; get_loc8 i; push_i32 k; lt; jump_if_true`. So jumps into the middle of a group, the stack checker, the line table (each piece keeps its phase-1 position), disassembly and every general-path case (a non-number operand, an object's valueOf, int32 overflow, a wide branch) behave as the separate instructions did. `run_hot` runs the group when its operands are int32 or Numbers (`add_loc8`) or the local is int32 and the branch is `jump_if_true8` (`inc_lt`), charges the summed cost of the group's instructions (`group` over `OPS`) and keeps the backward jump's safepoint (collection, fuel, budget) at the same point; otherwise it runs the head as its plain instruction and the next ones follow as before, so fuel totals, yields and stop points do not change. Fusion happens in the resolution re-emit (`compiler/resolve.rs`, beside the `inc_loc` rule) for locals below 256. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, hosted Hand, output/djsrun on djs-embed, ~/bench-djs, master 1ff02df03 -> this; QuickJS 2021-03-27 in brackets): loop 766.7M -> 318.7M (-58.4%, QuickJS 530.7M: 1.67x faster), gen 2,549.0M -> 2,373.0M (-6.9%), err 686.6M -> 657.8M (-4.2%), filter 993.4M -> 990.5M (-0.3%), find 768.8M -> 766.0M (-0.4%), some 769.9M -> 767.0M (-0.4%), gennext 4,655.0M -> 4,646.9M (-0.2%), forEach 1,010.1M -> 1,011.2M (+0.1%), map 1,098.8M -> 1,100.0M (+0.1%), reduce 697.4M -> 700.5M (+0.45%). In wasm32 under V8 (node 24, output/wasmrun cdylib of djs-embed with `unsafe-heap`, `run` of the script's main, instructions:u of 13 runs minus 3 runs over 10, best of 3): loop 931.3M -> 367.8M (-60.5%), gen 3,092.6M -> 2,887.7M (-6.6%), err 781.9M -> 741.2M (-5.2%), filter 1,156.8M -> 1,145.1M (-1.0%), find 862.6M -> 855.4M (-0.8%), some 863.7M -> 861.5M, gennext 5,226.2M -> 5,204.9M, forEach 1,152.9M -> 1,155.7M (+0.2%), reduce 776.5M -> 778.1M (+0.2%), map 1,328.0M -> 1,337.5M (+0.7%). Measured and dropped in the same session: `inc_lt` with a local or argument bound (`i < n`, three heads or one head that reads the bound's opcode): native gen -16.6% and loop -59%, but in V8 every variant that loads the bound in the arm (inline, through an out-of-line helper, with or without `bp`) moved find, some, forEach, reduce and filter by +5.5 to +9.3% (find 861.7M -> 930.6M) and loop by up to +19%, while the constant-only arm left them within 0.8%; the cause is V8's code for the larger `run_hot` (as D2441), not the arm's own work. Checked: test262 subset (output/t262, 3,090 files) 2,535 passing with identical pass sets; a fuel harness on djs-embed (`Instance::step` with `Limits { fuel, slice }`) gives the same result, yield count and `fuel_used` as master for the edge-case script, a mixed workload, a fusion edge script (strings, objects with valueOf and toString, BigInt, NaN, -0, Symbols, int32 overflow of the sum and of the counter, float, string and object bounds, labelled continue and break, a body past a short jump, closures over the counter, a throw inside the loop, generators), loop.js and gen.js with slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000 and fuel limits 1,000, 33,333 and 100,000; the edge-case scripts print the same as master. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/bytecode/ops.rs, bytecode/code.rs, compiler/resolve.rs, interp/run.rs, interp/run/hot.rs.
- fix(claude): `scripts/claude-request-parity.py` compares Claude Code 2.1.318's requests with nanocode's on a local mock key by key (headers, parameters, metadata, system blocks, tools, every message of a scripted ten-step turn, and the WebFetch side request), with each intended difference and both sides' expected values or digests in `crates/backends/claude/upstream/request.json`, and exits 1 when a difference appears, changes or goes away; nanocode's direct Claude Code context now matches it on every message, and it sends Claude Code's built-in tools sorted by name ahead of the rest (2026-11-15, Claude parity lane). Why: the earlier check (an uncommitted predecessor of this one) compared only request bodies with intended keys dropped, so headers, metadata, the side request and the order of tool inputs could drift unseen. The script captures the pinned official executable (`--claude`, sha256 checked against `prompts/upstream.json`) for two models: glm-5.2, which neither client knows, so both run their direct tools through the whole turn (Bash, WebFetch over a local HTTPS page, Read, Edit after a read, Edit of an unread file, cd into and out of the workspace, a failing command, Write); and claude-opus-5-5, which nanocode runs in Code Mode by design, so only its first request's system prompt, parameters, headers and first messages are compared. Closed here: the git status context, the untrusted-download line, `<total_tokens>` only for the models Claude Code sends it to, the Opus 5.5 paragraph only for Opus 5.5, the /fast line in the direct context, `replace_all: false` filled into Edit inputs, environment updates joined with blank lines, and the tool order (Claude Code sorts its built-ins by name; nanocode sent WebSearch and WebFetch first). Already matching and now guarded: WebFetch's HTML to Markdown conversion and side prompt, `is_error: false` on successful Bash results, the working-directory change notices, and Edit refusing an unread file (e525ef1). Documented, 49 keys: Claude Code's Node SDK headers, billing header and `?beta=true` (nanocode is not a Claude Code build and sends only the betas its body uses), summarized and prefix-bound thinking, automatic caching, custom-model defaults for max_tokens and effort (set outside this backend; Opus matches), an empty `tools` list left out of the side request, Claude Code's deferred placeholder tool (not model-visible; adding it needs the mid-conversation tool changes beta and a Terminal-Bench A/B), and Code Mode's own context for Opus. Not compared: subagent and skill lists, since `--tools` leaves out Agent and Skill and nanocode offers no subagent tools to direct-tool models by default; adding them is a model-visible change that needs a Terminal-Bench A/B. Checked: the script passes against a fast build of this commit, and fails with the changed key when a documented value is edited.
- perf(sim): `scripts/rustc-parallel-frontend` leaves out `-Zshare-generics=y` for bin crates when `NANOCODE_SHARE_GENERICS=lib`, and `bin/nanocode-sim/cfo.sh` builds the fuzzed `nanocode-sim` with it, so the 26K-line sim crate instantiates and inlines its own copies of the std and workspace generics again (`BTreeMap` search and insert, `Atom::update`, `Tree::find`) instead of calling the upstream copies 2728472 linked (2026-11-15, sizeinl lane). Why: share-generics cost the sim 3% of its instructions, spread across hundreds of std and workspace generics with no hot one to mark `#[inline]` (most are std's own `BTreeMap` internals), and the cost lands in the one binary the CFO runs for hours per commit, while a developer's loop pays the build instead. Measured on the thread's hosted Hand (5 cores, load 6 to 9, under `flock -x ~/bench.lock`, the same target dir, sim crate rebuilt alternately three times each): `nanocode-sim --seeds 0..300` instructions 13.596G (share-generics) -> 13.140G with the bin crate unshared (-3.4%; 13.204G before 2728472), cycles 6.52G -> 6.07G mean (noisy at that load); `sweep.sh 0 2000 5` wall 5.40 -> 5.28 s mean of six alternated runs; sim bin crate release rebuild 35.6 -> 43.4 s and binary 45.1 -> 46.7 MB, which is why it is opt-in rather than the default. Without the variable nothing changes. Checks: cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets, nanocode-sim release build, sweep 0 2000 4 passed, --tidy clean.
- perf(turnlog): `Fold::garbage` indexes the first holder of each content in a `HashMap` and marks reached contents in a `Vec<bool>`, `drop_garbage` removes the unreached records in one `BTreeMap::retain` pass, and `Fold::load` moves a decoded `Stored` record into the fold instead of cloning its value (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 fastopen lane). Before, the walk built a `BTreeMap<&str, Vec<_>>` of holders, kept a `BTreeSet` of visited contents, looked up each reached value a second time and removed garbage keys one by one. On the 10K parent log (`do10k-rows.jsonl`, 128.3 MB snapshot plain, 105.2 MB of it `Stored` values) that walk was about 40% of `TurnLog::open`: 252 ms of 568 ms in one instrumented open, with the rest in base64 and inflate (about 145 ms) and in parsing and applying records (about 160 ms). The collected set does not change. After `TurnLog::open` of that log, both builds collect 50,434 records and give the same `Fold::snapshot(0)` (94,746,934 B, SipHash 325389d3d58db33d) and the same `TurnLog::history` (70,566 events, 1de28722f2715485). Measured with `output/openprof` on box pyramid-prd-rootbytes-a3f1 (48 cores, load 9), 3 interleaved rounds of 3 opens each, base 4cff7ecb6 against the change: pinned to one core 539-614 ms against 419-490 ms, unpinned 512-578 ms against 408-464 ms (about 20% less). `collect_in` before each snapshot commit runs the same code. Sims (base and change identical): `--twice` 0..2000 2000/2000, `--snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` 1000/1000, `--calm --row-limit 1024` 1000/1000, `--snapshot-ratio 1` 1000/1000, `--long 100` 200/200, 0 panics, and the `seal_skipped` mutation is still caught. A 50 ms open needs more than this: open still inflates and parses every `Stored` value, and the walk still visits every content key (about 60 ms for the index alone), so the next step is a snapshot that leaves values out of open and a garbage walk that does not enumerate all keys at open.

- perf(store-jsonl): `JsonlStore::open_home_async` opens the session directory deferred, as `open_home_in_background` (bin/nanocode) does, so a CLI that opens the store no longer reads every directory entry at open to look for abandoned temporary files; they are removed by the first full scan or the first write instead (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: nc-lite listing target of 1 ms for 1,000 sessions). What: `Sessions::open_home(home, false)` ran `clear_temporaries`, one readdir of the sessions directory plus a name check per entry, before every command, including `nc-lite sessions` and `--continue`, whose listing then reads `.listing` instead of the directory. Callers: nc-lite, agent-host's async open and the brain example. Checked on the hosted Hand with nc-lite `fast` builds of master 1ff02df03 and of this change, bench/cli suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nclite on copies of one 1,000-session store, 10 rounds each, perf stat: store-list user instructions 45.68M -> 44.52M, kernel 15.18M -> 13.57M; store-resume user 45.18M -> 44.26M, kernel 16.77M -> 15.83M; 0 errors. An abandoned `<session>.jsonl.compact-<dead pid>-*` file placed in that store was gone after one listing and one `--continue`. `cargo build --locked --profile fast -p nc-lite`.
- feat(sim): mutations for 58 more nanocode-sim invariants, which raises the share of invariants with a mutation that catches them from 76 of 181 (42%) to 134 of 181 (74%) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 durability swarm, dst-mutations lane). An invariant here is one class of check that a scenario reports: a variant of the turns `Invariant` enum, a named hands check, or a distinct failure message of a scenario's judge. The lane inventory (`logs/inv.py` in ~/w/lanes/dst-mutations) lists all 181 with a regex for each message. Each mutation ran through `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 N 4` with its cfo.sh canary flags, and its CAUGHT messages were matched to the inventory. Each new mutation models a product or host bug behind the scenario's existing mutation enum. Turns cells: `buffered_admission_written` (cell_rows, 66/400), `cell_before_checkpoint` (cell_model_once, 129/400), `open_drops_journals` (cell_lost, 143/400), `resume_redispatches_running` (cell_external_once, 45/400). Agents gets a `--mutation` flag with `cancel_ignored`, `shutdown_hangs`, `shutdown_keeps_harness` (harness_released, 144/200) and `turn_leaks` (turns_released, 200/200). Runtime `--store kv` takes the store scenario's KV mutations, and `drop-tool-result` (93/100), `rewrite-assistant` (93/100) and `drop-acked-answer` (63/100) change the request that the model server receives. Executor gets 6 more, mpp 8, sync 5, websocket 3, alloc 2, capture 1, streams 3, egress 6, http_server 2 and the store KV 5 (`cas_acks_unwritten`, `cas_reports_conflict`, `get_corrupts_value`, `list_phantom_key`, `list_skips_key`). `--mutations` lists 118 rows (66 before), and cfo.sh lists the new rows that need flags. Every new mutation is caught. With no mutation the sweeps on the same binary pass: store and `--records slots` 300/300, agents 300/300, turns 500/500, turns turnlog `--twice` 500/500, turnlog `--snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` 300/300, websocket, http_server, alloc, egress, mpp, sync, streams, hands, executor and capture `--twice` 300/300 each, runtime kv 60/60, kv remote 60/60, kv http `--twice` 40/40. 47 invariants still have no mutation: mostly store staging checks, http_server parse paths, egress resolver and time bounds, and runtime final_text, remote_completion_twice and effect_once.

- feat(exec): `--attempt-pick self-check` runs each attempt's own check command again in its copy and picks by that run's exit and counts, not by a reported `self-check: <passed>/<total>` line (2026-11-15, verified-pick lane, thread's hosted Hand; `--attempt-pick verifier` stays the default). On query-optimize an attempt ended with `self-check: 5/5` while the hidden tests failed, and the old pick applied it. Each attempt's note now asks it to end with `check: <command>`: one shell line that runs the task's checks from the copy's directory, exits 0 only when every check passes and prints its counts as a test runner's summary or as a last line `<passed>/<total>`. When an attempt ends, the orchestrator runs that command through the chosen shell in `<root>/<label>` (output in `<label>.check`, stopped with its process tree at the `--attempt-timeout` deadline) and reads the counts from the last output line that holds `N passed`, `N failed` or `N error(s)` (pytest, cargo test and jest summaries) or is exactly `P/T`.
