An attempt passes only when the command exits 0 and its counts show `passed == total > 0`, so a false claim, a check masked with `; true` that still prints a failure, and a command that prints no counts all lose. The first attempt that passes wins and the rest stop as before. An attempt with no `check:` line or a failing command is no candidate, and when none passes the run fails with the attempts kept instead of applying the copy with the best claim. Reproducing check: `output/verified/run.sh <nanocode>` against `output/verified/mock.py`, a scripted Responses mock with 2 attempts and `check.sh` that prints `5 passed` and exits 0 only when answer.txt holds 42. false (attempt 1 writes 41 and claims `self-check: 5/5` with `check: ./check.sh` at 1.1 s, attempt 2 writes 42 at 3.1 s): attempt 1's check exited 1 counting 4/5, attempt 2's exited 0 counting 5/5, and attempt 2 was applied (answer.txt=42); the previous binary on the same script applied attempt 1 (answer.txt=41, check fails) and stopped attempt 2. masked (`check: ./check.sh; true` on the wrong copy): exit 0 but 4/5, so attempt 2 was applied. early (attempt 1 correct at 1.1 s, attempt 2 would take 30 s): attempt 1 applied in 1.18 s and attempt 2 stopped. missing (the correct attempt names no command, the other's command fails): rc=1, nothing applied, attempts kept. Checked: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode --no-deps -- -D warnings`, rustfmt on both files; the `nanocode` binary has no wasm32 build (`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` reports E0601, no `main`, as on master). Files: bin/nanocode/src/attempts.rs, bin/nanocode/src/cli.rs.
Live (2026-11-15, thread's hosted Hand, Terminal-Bench 2.1 through ~/swarm/verified-pick/run-ds.sh on the best-of-n paced stack, @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 through nano-ai-proxy at one request start every 6 s, release build of 47e915f9a, 2 runs per task per arm, $0.15/M in and $0.50/M out): `--attempts 2 --attempt-pick self-check` passed 2 of 6 (query-optimize 1/2, mcmc-sampling-stan 1/2, circuit-fibsqrt 0/2) for $0.753, 2.7 passes per dollar; single passed 2 of 6 (0/2, 2/2, 0/2) for $0.497, 4.0 passes per dollar. Every applied pick came from a command the orchestrator ran again (`./check.sh` counting 9/9, 4/4, 13/13 and 6/6), so no claim without a passing run won, but two of those four picks still failed the hidden tests: the attempt wrote its own check.sh, weaker than the task's tests. On circuit-fibsqrt both attempts of both runs reached the 3060 s `--attempt-timeout` without a `check:` line, so nothing was applied. Three trials (bo2 mcmc x2, single mcmc x1) are left out and were run again: the relay's bearer mint failed when the turn's request token changed, the model calls got HTTP 500 and the attempts exited 1. Total model spend $1.54 including those.
- feat(exec): `nanocode exec --attempts N --attempt-pick self-check` picks the attempt by the attempts' own checks instead of a verifier turn (2026-11-15, best-of-n lane, thread's hosted Hand; `--attempt-pick verifier` stays the default). Each attempt's note also asks it to find the checks the task gives or implies (its tests, a checker, an example with expected output, each stated requirement), run them in its copy, fix what fails and end with `self-check: <passed>/<total>`. Attempts now report to the parent as they finish (an unbounded channel), and the first that exits 0 with `passed == total > 0` wins at once: a `watch` channel tells the others, each attempt's wait selects on its child, the `--attempt-timeout` deadline and that signal, and a stopped attempt's process tree is killed through the same `stop` the deadline uses (`Exit::Cancelled` names the winner), so the slower attempts stop spending tokens. When none passes, the winner is the one reporting the most passing checks, then one that exited 0, then the earliest to finish; an attempt that exited non-zero without a self-check line is no candidate, and when no candidate is left (every attempt failed, such as on a provider 403) the run fails with the attempts kept instead of applying an arbitrary copy. Applying the winner, the base check and the verifier path are unchanged (the verifier code moved into `verify`). Reproducing check: `output/bo3/run.sh <nanocode>` against `output/bo3/mock.py`, a scripted Responses mock whose attempt N runs one `exec_command` then answers with a fixed self-check line (1000 in / 100 out tokens per request). early (attempt 2 reports 1/1 after 2 s, attempt 3 would take 30 s): self-check applied attempt 2 (answer.txt=42, check PASS) in 2.13 s with 5 model requests, attempt 3 stopped after its first; the same script with `--attempt-pick verifier` applied attempt 2 in 30.17 s with 7 requests (3x2 plus the verifier), so 29% fewer requests and 14x less wall time. most (1/3, 2/3, 0/3): attempt 2 applied in 3.15 s. fail (every request HTTP 403): rc=1, nothing applied, attempts kept. Live: on GLM-5.3 Flash through the Workers AI proxy a toy check task picked the attempt that reported 1/1 and stopped the other two; the 5-task Terminal-Bench comparison (circuit-fibsqrt, chess-best-move, mcmc-sampling-stan, query-optimize, winning-avg-corewars, bo3 vs single) got HTTP 403 from the shared quota on every request and was stopped, so it measures nothing yet. Checked: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode --no-deps -- -D warnings`, rustfmt on both files, a release build in rust:1.97-bullseye (GLIBC_2.30). Files: bin/nanocode/src/attempts.rs, bin/nanocode/src/cli.rs.
- perf(nc-lite): `--continue` picks the newest session of the workspace with the store's newest page (scope and updated_at read from each summary's head, one summary decoded) instead of decoding and sorting every saved session, so resuming in a 1,000-session store runs 29% fewer user instructions (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: nc-lite --continue target of 2 ms). What: `Lite::session` called `workspace_sessions`, which listed every session through `SessionStore::list` (each summary's record parsed twice) and kept the first; it now calls `newest_page(cwd, 1, ..)`, the path bin/nanocode already uses. `nc-lite sessions` and the terminal's session picker keep the full listing: the same newest page with no limit measured slower there (60.9M against 45.7M user instructions), since it parses each head and then each record. Checked on the hosted Hand (shared, load 5 to 20) with nc-lite `fast` builds of master 3e574d49a and of this change, bench/cli suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nclite on copies of one 1,000-session store, 10 rounds each, instructions from perf stat: store-resume user instructions 61.10M -> 43.32M (median), kernel 22.5M -> 17.4M, spawn to request 94.5 -> 42.7 ms (wall is noisy on this host); store-list 45.72M -> 45.67M (unchanged); resume errors 0 in both. `cargo build --locked --profile fast -p nc-lite`.
- perf(alloc): an empty page is retired even when it heads its size class, and freed slices are purged once more than 4 are dirty (was 64), so a tool turn's peak RSS falls about 1.1 MB (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, anonymous memory). Why: at exit_group of the master binary (gdb, /proc/pid/pagemap, reading each 4 MB segment's header), a 10-step tool turn held 2.3 to 2.8 MB resident in allocator segments for 0.63 MB of live blocks: 0.2 to 0.45 MB sat in empty pages kept only because they were their class's head (classes of 5 KB to 64 KB blocks, such as a 64 KB-block page of 248 KB resident with no block in use), and 0.7 MB in free slices that were never purged, because 64 dirty slices (4 MB) is more than a 63-slice segment can hold, so the threshold was never reached. The large-block cache was not the cause: the only large blocks in a tool turn are two live ones from Code Mode (djs Heap arena growth via Arena::zero_ahead, 836 KB mapped and 384 KB touched, and a 328 KB Vec::with_capacity in code-mode-engine cell::compile), neither cached; a one-shot maps none. Measured (bench/cli suite under tools/netguard.sh, release profile, one binary with the policies switched by environment variables for the experiment, then the final build against the same binary with master's policy; interleaved passes of 2 rounds, hosted Hand at load 5 to 11): tool turn peak RSS 44.48/44.66/44.65/44.53 MB before and 43.41/43.63/43.49/43.40 after, one-shot 35.78/36.01/35.96/36.01 before and 35.57/35.11/35.62/35.30 after, anonymous RSS after the first frame 5.36 to 5.40 before and 5.23 to 5.27 MB after; one-shot and first-frame CPU unchanged within noise, minor faults +5% in a tool turn (4162 against 3959). Each policy alone moves the tool turn 0.1 to 0.2 MB; together 1.0 to 1.1 MB, because retiring the head page leaves its slices dirty and only the lower threshold returns them. Measured and dropped: preferring dirty free runs when placing a new page (no change on top), purging on every retire (threshold 0: same RSS as 4, +15% minor faults), threshold 16 (tool turn 44.0 MB, half the gain), and trimming the main loop's heap (collect every page and purge) whenever the TUI waits for input after the first frame (0.05 MB, inside noise: the post-frame anonymous memory is on other threads' heaps and in live data).
- perf(cli): BOLT trains offline on the benchmark's HTTP/1.1 chunked stream and a 10-step tool turn, and keeps functions whole when splitting saves under 256 bytes (`-split-threshold=256`), which lowers the 10-step tool turn's peak RSS from 13.65 to 12.83 MB and one-shot from 8.6 to 8.2 MB (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, wave 3, cold layout). Why: after the first frame most of the binary's resident text is fault-around neighbours of a few touched `.text.cold` pages. They are cold fragments of hot functions whose zero-count blocks ran in the benchmark but not in training, spread over the first 5 MB of `.text.cold` (32 pages across 26 64 KB windows in one-shot, 146 across 70 in the tool turn, read with `fault_around_bytes` at 4096 and pagemap at `exit_group`, put back to 65536 after). Training missed them for three reasons. (1) `scripts/train-cli.py`'s server answered HTTP/1.0, close-delimited, while providers and the benchmark answer HTTP/1.1 chunked on a kept-alive connection, so `http::wire::chunked`, `keeps_alive` and `BodyReader::next` stayed cold. It now sends `transfer-encoding: chunked` and `connection: keep-alive`. (2) Training ran with the network up, so whether the Tempo MCP connects (`mcp_tools::client::connect_session`, `tempo::Listing::load`) reached their failure paths depended on the build host. Training now runs in an unprivileged user and network namespace with only loopback (same uid; it trains online, as before, where the kernel refuses one), so the profile no longer depends on the build host's network. (3) The tool turn trained 3 steps; it now runs the benchmark's 10 steps three times, because whether the store groups a step's writes (`shared_store::drive_grouped`) depends on timing and one run reaches it about two times in three. Against the benchmark's own instrumented runs, the blocks training never reached fall from 595 to 86 (one-shot), 2495 to 606 (tool turn) and 167 to 62 (first frame). Better training alone does not lower RSS (tool turn 13.78 vs 13.49 MB in the same pass), because the few cold fragments still reached sit in different windows. `-split-threshold=256` keeps those small cold tails in hot text (+240 KB of `.text`). Measured (bench/cli under tools/netguard.sh, 6 interleaved passes of 4 rounds, BOLT rerun on 37b42b7f5's `linked` with the new profile; the hosted Hand at load 25 to 30): tool turn 13.48 to 13.79 MB on master vs 12.73 to 12.92 MB; one-shot 7.98 to 8.79 vs 7.83 to 8.26 MB; RSS after the first frame (6.0 to 6.6 vs 6.05 to 6.24) and `--version` (1.74 to 1.89 vs 1.83 to 1.95) within spread. User instructions are unchanged: one-shot 7.58M vs 7.55M, first frame 7.36M vs 7.35M (perf stat, median of 6). Measured and dropped: the threshold with the old profile (tool turn 13.48 to 13.68 MB, no change), thresholds of 128 (13.33) and 512 (13.03 to 13.06), and 2048 (13.36 to 13.45 MB; `.text` grows to 4.9 MB). Not measured end to end: a full build reruns `rodata-cli.py` with the new profiles, which reorders `.rodata` from them; these numbers keep 37b42b7f5's `.rodata` order.
- fix(codex): the turn metadata in `client_metadata["x-codex-turn-metadata"]` now matches codex-cli 0.166.0's default: it drops `tool_namespaces_info` and adds `model` and `reasoning_effort`, and the request parity check compares the turn metadata key by key and runs nanocode in Code Mode (2026-11-15, Codex parity lane v2). Why: `scripts/codex-request-parity.py` compared only the set of `client_metadata` keys, so the contents of the turn metadata could drift unseen, and since e6abbf80d made direct tools the default it compared nanocode's direct tools with codex-cli's Code Mode request. Comparing the metadata turned up 19 undocumented differences. codex-cli 0.166.0 sends `tool_namespaces_info` only when `turn_metadata_includes_tool_info` is set (core/src/session/session.rs, config default false), and the capture has none, so nanocode stops computing it: `RequestProfile` loses the inventory and its code-mode tool names, `with_code_mode_tool_names` is gone, and the codex backend ignores the tool summaries from `model_contract`. `model` (the wire model id) and `reasoning_effort` (the request's effort) come from the request's own policy. What: the check now runs `nanocode exec --ephemeral --codex-orchestration code-mode -m gpt-6-luna -t high "Say hi"` (the default tool mode is unchanged), and adds one `turn-metadata:<key>` fact per key, with ids and the start time compared by presence and objects by digest. Measured against the mock: undocumented differences 19 to 0 (40 differences in total, all documented in crates/backends/codex/upstream/request.json); the first request's body 61,143 to 58,269 bytes (-2,874, -4.7%), all of it the dropped inventory, sent on every request. Documented, not closed: `agent_name`, `thread_source`, `turn_trigger`, `history_initialization`, `root_turn_id`, `turn_started_at_unix_ms`, `window_id`, `window_number`, `context_window_id` and `installation_id` need session state (agent lineage, the compaction window counter, the host frontend, a persistent installation id) the request layer does not carry, and `sandbox`, `sandbox_mode`, `auto_review_enabled`, `node_repl_*` and `analytics_enabled` describe codex-cli's own policies, which nanocode does not have. Mutation check: removing the documentation of `turn-metadata:sandbox` and documenting `turn-metadata:model` makes the check report one undocumented and one stale difference and exit 1. Checks: `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-codex` (only the existing const-fn warning in retry.rs). Files: crates/backends/codex/client/src/responses/request.rs, crates/backends/codex/client/src/lib.rs, crates/backends/codex/src/model/run/{mod,responses}.rs, crates/backends/codex/upstream/request.json, scripts/codex-request-parity.py.
- perf(psh): the standalone psh links statically and not position independent, compiled loops run their native stretches synchronously with a fast path for counting-loop arithmetic, `for i in {a..b}` iterates the range without expanding it, `shopt` lookups are a table index, and a signal that is only ignored no longer counts as a trap (2026-11-15, psh lane wave 2: startup <=0.5 ms, loops >=100x bash). Why: callgrind of `psh -c :` was 1.27M instructions, half of it the dynamic loader relocating 24k relative relocations and binding libc symbols, and on this VM every mapping and page fault is dear (1.8 ms CPU against 0.76 ms for /bin/true); the flat loop's per-iteration cost was mostly the async run_with future (476 instructions per iteration of a 2-command loop) and eval's recursion with an undo log; `for i in {1..20000}` spent 45M instructions materializing and expanding 20000 words, 16M of them in `Options::shopt`, which searched SHOPTS by name on every call; and a shell started by Python (which ignores SIGXFSZ) got an "ignore" trap at start, so every loop ran interpreted: a 100k-iteration loop took 4.4 s instead of 5 ms. What: crates/patches/psh/.cargo/config.toml sets `-C target-feature=+crt-static -C relocation-model=static` for the linux-gnu targets of this workspace only (nanocode's own build does not read it); flat.rs `spin` runs Stmt/Item/jumps/LoopHead/BodyDone/nested loops/for(( )) clauses synchronously while native operations run and errexit is off, taking the scheduler budget per command as run_with does (`Sched::refund` gives it back when it hands a command to run_with) and returning to run_with on a pending signal, a spent budget or anything it does not run; `Ex::quick` evaluates `a OP b` over integer slots and numbers, `i++`/`--i` and `i = b`/`i += b` without recursion or undo, falling back to eval (which fails as before) otherwise; `expand::lazy_seq` recognises a for word list that is exactly one integer brace sequence without zero padding and at most the million words seq allows, and `flat::run_for_range` assigns each value straight into the loop variable's slot (the variable now always has one) when it holds an integer or is unset, else assigns it as before; `Shopt::INDEX` is computed at compile time; `Traps::live` (any trap but an ignored signal) replaces `!traps.map.is_empty()` in the hot checks (exec.rs, flat.rs, now.rs, eval.rs). Measured (CPU ms user+sys, median of 21, posix_spawn harness with SIGPIPE/SIGXFSZ default, 5-core host under load avg ~8; master 02b304a43 -> now; bash 5.2): `psh -c :` 2.42 -> 0.62 (bash 5.11; /bin/true 0.65-1.4 on this host); while [ ] 100k 5.47 -> 0.57 (bash 203, 356x); while (( )) 100k 5.07 -> 2.13 (bash 82, 39x); while [[ ]] 100k 5.76 -> 0.85 (bash 143, 168x); s+=i loop 100k 6.43 -> 3.00 (bash 284, 95x); for(( )) echo | grep -c 20k 5.61 -> 1.79 (bash 53, 29x); for i in {1..20000} echo | grep -c 9.73 -> 1.82 (bash 43, 23x); seq 20000 | grep -c 1 4.42 -> 1.78 (bash 10.5). Instructions (callgrind, deterministic): while (( )) 69.4M -> 46.1M, s+=i loop 104.8M -> 75.4M, brace loop 103.6M -> 18.4M. Not met: (( )) and s+=i loops at 100x, the echo pipeline at 100x, seq|grep <=1.1 ms (the per-iteration interpreter still costs ~450 instructions; next is superinstructions or induction-variable elimination for pure counting loops). psh-spec: oils 2495/2511, brush 3131/3171 (brush/compat/builtins/kill/17 failed once under load and passes on 3 reruns, the known flake), agent 727/727, utils 998/1001; a 31-case differential script of brace ranges, readonly/declare -i/local loop variables, set -u/-e, break/continue, traps and `$_` prints byte-identical output to bash. A statically linked psh-spec harness segfaulted in full runs (not psh), so the harness was run dynamically linked (RUSTFLAGS overrides the config). Upstream delta: crates/patches/psh/.cargo/config.toml, psh-engine/src/{flat,exec,expand,options,sched,now}.rs, builtins/{trap,eval}.rs.
- feat(codex): a headless Codex-harness turn (`nanocode exec`, or `CodexHarness::headless(true)` / `CodexBuilder::headless(true)` from a host) that ends with a final message admitting incomplete or unverified work is continued once with a `<persistence>` user nudge; the next final message ends the turn as before, and interactive sessions are unchanged (2026-11-15, Codex persistence-guard lane). Why: in Terminal-Bench 2.1 run 0d6c29c9 (GPT-6 Luna high), 12 of 25 failed nanox attempts ended on a message admitting the work was incomplete (circuit-fibsqrt 4 of 4 after 3-5 model calls, winning-avg-corewars 3, feal 2, mcmc-sampling-stan, query-optimize, install-windows-3.11 1 each) against 5 of 17 failed codex-cli attempts. `admits_incomplete` matches a lowercase phrase list (curly apostrophes folded) built from those final messages: it flags all 12, the 13 unflagged failed finals all report success, and on passed attempts it flags 4 of 53 (two say "I did not run tests", where the nudge asks for verification); the nudge fires at most once per turn, the policy the lane set. Replay (hosted Hand, replay/ harness outside the repo): each flagged attempt's final request was rebuilt from its trajectory (luna.md, the permissions developer message, the Code Mode `exec` tool, every call and output), followed by the admitting message and the nudge, and sent 3 times each to Workers AI kimi-k2.7-code and deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 (GPT goes only through subscriptions this lane could not reach): of 72 replies, 54 called a tool (continued), 6 ended with text (all kimi, 3 of them on query-optimize), 10 were still reasoning at the replay's 8,000-token cap (all circuit-fibsqrt) and 2 were transport errors, so 54 of 60 decided replies continued where the recorded runs stopped every time (deepseek 32 of 32, kimi 22 of 28; every flagged attempt continued in at least half its decided replies). An `<autonomy>` developer block saying the session is non-interactive and to keep working until every requirement is verified was also measured, on the 25 failed attempts' final requests without the admitting message, 2 samples each on kimi: 13 of 50 replies called a tool without it and 13 of 50 with it, so it was not shipped. Validation: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and wasm32, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, and `output/persistence-guard` (a Responses mock behind `NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` running `nanocode exec`): a final message admitting incomplete work then a clean one takes 2 model calls with the nudge as the last input item and returns the clean one, an admitting reply every time takes 2 calls and returns the second admission, and a clean reply takes 1 call with no nudge.
- fix(codex): a Chat Completions gateway (GLM, Kimi and other custom models on Workers AI or OpenRouter) repairs open-model tool calls instead of rejecting the response, and answers a call it cannot repair through the tool's own error instead of failing the turn (2026-11-15, tool-call-repair lane). Before, `normalize` turned any malformed call into a retryable `invalid Chat Completions stream: normalize_*` error, so the same request was resampled (30 times in the replay below) and the turn then failed. Now `transport/chat/repair.rs` parses arguments leniently once strict parsing fails: a ``` fence, trailing commas, single-quoted strings, unquoted keys, Python `True`/`False`/`None`, raw control characters and unknown escapes inside strings, closing brackets after the value, an empty string as `{}`, and a JSON string holding the object. A string value whose schema type is only integer, number, boolean, array or object and that parses as one is converted, and a missing property whose schema declares a `default` gets it (no Codex tool declares one today, so this applies to MCP and SDK tools). A returned name that is not a wire alias or original name is matched case-insensitively and without a `functions.` prefix or a Kimi `:N` index suffix, against the alias, the name, `ns.name`, `ns.alias`, `ns_name` and `ns__name`, and a name repeated by stream concatenation; a match must be unique. A custom tool takes `input`, a JSON string, or the one string field of an object. What still does not resolve passes through: an unknown name becomes a `function_call` the driver answers with `unsupported call: <name>`, and unparseable arguments reach the handler, which answers `failed to parse function arguments: ...`. Workers AI rejects a history whose assistant `tool_calls[].function.arguments` is not valid JSON (HTTP 400 `Assistant tool call function.arguments must be valid JSON`, checked on GLM-5.3 Flash and Kimi K2.7 Code), so the replayed history sends such arguments as `{"unparsed_arguments": "<raw>"}`; an undeclared `history_N` name in history is accepted. A forced `tool_choice` still rejects a call to another tool, and a stream's tool call without an ID or with a gap in its indexes gets an ID instead of failing. Harness `output/tool-call-repair`: `capture` runs a direct-tools Codex agent through `ChatGateway::workers_ai` against a local recorder on 10 small shell tasks (47 requests); 40 of them were sent to `@cf/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash` and `@cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code` through the Workers AI proxy and saved as fixtures (80 responses, 352k input tokens), and `replay.py` serves each response to builds before and after this change and records whether the turn continued or the request was resampled. Real responses: GLM 0/40 rejected before and after; Kimi 2/40 before and after, both empty streams (`finish_reason: stop`, 66-68 completion tokens, no content or tool call: the provider dropped the call), and 8/40 Kimi responses named the original tool (`exec_command`, `apply_patch`) instead of the wire alias, which `resolve` already accepted. Mutations of those calls (42 fixtures, 16 failure modes): 39/42 rejected before, 0/42 after (38 repaired, 4 answered with the tool error above; the 3 string-typed numbers were accepted before but reached the tool as strings). `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client`, also for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, passes.
- Correction to the Android entry of 2026-11-14 (797e0ea54, fix(android): build nanocode for aarch64-linux-android and run its smokes under qemu): it says qemu-aarch64-static was registered with binfmt_misc for output/tgt-smoke/smoke.sh "then unregistered". That was false when it was written: the binfmt_misc entry `tgt-qemu-aarch64` stayed registered on dev-georgios after the smokes, so every aarch64 ELF executed on that host went through qemu. It was removed on 2026-11-14 at about 18:15 PST (2026-11-15 02:15 UTC), and /proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc no longer lists it. The Android entry stays as written; this entry corrects it.
- feat(codex): Codex sessions get background jobs by default: `Tools::default()` now has `background_jobs: true`, and the executor-backed workspace that `CodexHarness` installs (`WorkspaceTools::with_process_executors`, the path `nanocode exec --harness codex` takes) carries job_start, job_wait and job_kill; Codex host instructions gain one line, "Write numeric answers in plain decimal (16.35, not 1.635e+01) unless the task asks for another format." (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 nanox on mcmc-sampling-stan and install-windows-3.11). Why: the background-jobs entry below shipped the tools behind a switch that nothing turned on, and even with the switch on, the CLI's Codex path never reached them, because `CodexHarness::build` sets its own workspace source (`ConfiguredWorkspaceFactory`, no jobs) before `tool_runtime` would build `WorkspaceTools::with_jobs`. So nanox followed long builds with exec_command and write_stdin polls: in the local copies of three failed nanox mcmc attempts it made 34, 172 and 21 write_stdin calls, and one attempt timed out at 1800 s polling an rstan compile. Separately, 4 of 6 failed nanox mcmc attempts wrote the posterior mean in scientific notation (`format(x, digits = 17, scientific = TRUE)`, so 1.6352291497083582e+01), which the verifier's `-?\d+\.?\d*` reads as 1.635. What: `background_jobs` defaults to true (only the Codex backend reads it; the Claude policy always hides JOB_TOOLS, so Claude sessions are unchanged), and `ConfiguredWorkspaceFactory::create` adds `with_job_tools()`. A host that wants codex-cli 0.166.0's exact tool list sets `with_background_jobs(false)`: the existing JobsHidden policy then hides the three tools in both direct and Code Mode exposures. The plain-decimal line goes after `<runtime_model_identity>` in `ModelConfig::host_instructions`, so built-in Codex models get it and custom models do not; the upstream base prompts are unchanged. Measured with output/long-command (mock.py serves `/v1/models` and streaming `/v1/responses` and scripts the model; run.sh runs the debug `nanocode exec --model gpt-6-luna --harness codex --thinking high --ephemeral --no-tempo-tools --no-subagents --codex-orchestration <mode>` against it with `NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL`; build.sh prints one 80-byte line every 0.5 s for 60 s). Catalog: the first request in direct mode now lists apply_patch, exec_command, job_kill, job_start, job_wait, update_plan, view_image and write_stdin, Code Mode's exec description names the three job tools, and both carry the plain-decimal line. 60 s build: polling as nanox did (exec_command with yield 10 s, then write_stdin with yield 1000 ms) took 12 model calls and 11,222 bytes of tool output in 60.6 s; job_start then job_wait (tail_lines 5) took 3 model calls and 582 bytes in 59.4 s; one Code Mode cell (job_start, then job_wait until exit_code) took 3 model calls (exec, wait, answer) and 992 bytes in 60.0 s. The plain-decimal line is not measured on GPT yet: an A/B prompt probe on Workers AI models (deepseek-v4.1-flash, kimi-k2.7-code, 12 samples per arm) wrote plain decimals in both arms (0 of 12 scientific without the line), so it cannot discriminate; the check is a nanox rerun of mcmc-sampling-stan. Checks: `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` (no new warnings), `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-tool-host --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, rustfmt. Files: crates/runtime/tool-host/src/selection.rs, crates/backends/codex/src/builtin_tools/workspace_runtime.rs, crates/backends/codex/client/src/openai/config.rs.
- fix(claude, codex): a model call waits for the response head as long as the stock client does, and only a stream that stalls after its head arrived counts toward the twice-in-a-row stall rule (2026-11-15). Before, `nanocode-http`'s `read_timeout` (300 s, `MESSAGES_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT`) also bounded `Client::response_head`, the host transport's `post_idle` used the same 300 s, and a head timeout counted as a stall, so a provider that queued a request for more than 300 s failed the call at about 600 s (live: a 682 s first byte behind a rate-limited provider). Stock Claude Code 2.1.300 waits `API_TIMEOUT_MS ?? 600000` ms for the head (the SDK `timeout`) and starts its 300 s idle watchdog only on the body. Its first-byte watchdog (`CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS`, 180 s plus 1 s per 32 KiB of body, 599 s on a retry) is armed only for first-party Anthropic, Anthropic AWS without a custom base URL, and Bedrock, so it does not apply behind `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and is not ported. Now `ClientBuilder::head_timeout` bounds the head when set, `MESSAGES_HEAD_TIMEOUT` is 600 s for the native client and the host transport, `x-stainless-timeout` derives from it, and `stall` requires `accepted`. A head timeout is retried like other transport errors, as the SDK retries its timeout. Codex CLI 0.162.1 sets no timeout on the `/responses` HTTP request (`Request::timeout` is `None`) and applies `stream_idle_timeout` only in `spawn_response_stream`, while nanocode's Responses HTTPS path wrapped the head in the 300 s idle bound and counted it as a stall. The three head waits in `transport/http.rs` (native, layered, host) now wait without that bound. The WebSocket path already matched Codex CLI (idle bound per message) and is unchanged. Validation, debug `nanocode exec` against a local aiohttp mock (`exec --harness claude|codex`, one sample each, this Hand): head delayed 400 s on every request, before claude rc=1 at 601.2 s after 2 POSTs ("operation timed out, twice in a row") and codex rc=1 at 601.5 s after 2 POSTs, after both rc=0 at 400.5 s and 400.4 s after 1 POST. Head sent and `message_start` then 400 s of silence, before and after claude rc=1 at 601.3 s and 601.2 s after 2 POSTs ("request or response body error: operation timed out, twice in a row"), unchanged. `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-http and the claude and codex backends native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo clippy --locked` with nanocode-cli, report no warnings in the changed files.
- fix(exec): when `--attempt-timeout` stops an attempt, the parent first stops the attempt's whole process tree with SIGSTOP (the attempt, then every process whose parent is in the tree, read from `/proc/*/stat` until a scan finds none), then kills each process group of the tree and the attempt with SIGKILL, so no tool command of a stopped attempt keeps running (2026-11-15, L7 best-of-N live lane: `nanocode exec --attempts 3` on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with @cf/qwen/qwen3.8-27b). Why: before, only the attempt process got SIGKILL. Each tool command runs in its own process group (`nanocode psh-shell -lc ...`), so it was reparented to init and kept running. In Terminal-Bench task adaptive-rejection-sampler, all three attempts were stopped at the 405 s deadline while each ran `apt-get install r-base`. Their orphans kept the dpkg lock, and the verifier's own `apt-get install curl` failed with "Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend", so the trial scored 0 whatever the attempts did. `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/children` is not used because kernels without CONFIG_PROC_CHILDREN (this Hand's 6.18.56) do not have it. Other platforms keep the old behavior. Reproducing check: `output/L7-bestofn-live/run.sh` (a chat-completions mock behind cfproxy: every attempt calls `exec_command` with `/usr/bin/sleep 299; echo late > late.txt`, the verifier answers `chosen: 1`; `--attempts 3 --attempt-timeout 4`). Leftover `sleep 299` processes after the run: master 35ba28283, 3 in every run; this change, 0 in 2 of 2 runs. Both runs took 4 s, rc 0, and attempt 1 was applied. Checked: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-cli`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode --no-deps -- -D warnings` (only the existing nanocode-executor `fetch_update` warning), `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check bin/nanocode/src/attempts.rs`. The wasm32 target does not apply, because bin/nanocode is not built for it. Files: bin/nanocode/src/attempts.rs.
- perf(cli): on Linux x86_64 the installed `nanocode` is an 8 KB static front (`bin/nanocode-front`: no libc, no allocator, its own `_start`) that answers `--version`/`-V` itself and otherwise execve's `nanocode-agent` beside it (the directory of `/proc/self/exe`) with the same argv and environment, so `argv[0]` (`nc`), `current_exe` helpers and `nanocode-python` beside the binary are unchanged (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, wave 3, front-entry lane). What: `scripts/release-cli.sh` builds it in the amd64 container (`cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path bin/nanocode-front/Cargo.toml`) and publishes `nanocode-front-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.gz` beside the unchanged `nanocode-<triple>` asset; `install` puts the full binary at `nanocode-agent` and the front at `nanocode` when the release lists a front for the target, keeps one `nanocode` otherwise, and moves an existing install either way (checked against local file:// releases: fresh install without and with a front, upgrade from one binary, a re-run that downloads nothing, and back to one binary). macOS, Windows and aarch64 Linux keep the single binary: there is no aarch64 machine here to run a front on, so none ships untested. The crate is outside the workspace (`exclude`) because a `no_std` binary cannot build under the workspace's `panic = "unwind"` dev and release profiles (rustc: "unwinding panics are not supported without std"; Cargo's `CARGO_CFG_PANIC` reports `unwind` even under `dist`, so a build script cannot switch); its build script reads the version from `[workspace.package]`. Why: `ru_maxrss` is the maximum over the images a process ran, so a front lowers a row only when the full binary is never mapped; of the bench rows only `--version` qualifies, and there the dynamic 48 MB binary pays ld.so, libc and fault-around before its own early `--version` return. Measured (bench/cli suite under tools/netguard.sh, `--only=nc`, 3 interleaved passes of 4 rounds, the master 37b42b7f5 binary both as the single binary and as `nanocode-agent`, hosted Hand at load 26 to 29, `fault_around_bytes` 65536): `--version` 1.71/1.78/1.88 MB to 0.27/0.29/0.30 MB (`/usr/bin/true` measures 1.17 MB under the same runstat); one-shot 8.06/8.80/8.76 to 8.52/8.81/8.72, RSS after the first frame 6.14/6.35/6.73 to 6.57/6.19/6.70 and the 10-step tool turn 13.92/14.07/14.19 to 13.88/14.20/14.02 MB, the same within spread since the agent's own image sets them; `--help` CPU 3.26/3.21 to 3.04/3.54 ms (noise) and 144 to 152 minor faults for the extra execve. Not done: serving the first frame or the one-shot from the front, which would need a second implementation of the welcome screen, terminal queries and config, or of the request path, and would put the agent's whole startup on the first keystroke; those rows need the agent's own layout and anonymous memory to shrink.
- perf(cli), measured and not shipped: a static glibc link of the Linux CLI (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, static-glibc lane). Nothing in the build changes. Built from the same objects, rodata order and BOLT profile as 37b42b7f5's binary: `-static -nostartfiles` with crt1.o, crti.o, crtbegin.o ... crtend.o, crtn.o (crtbegin.o, not crtbeginT.o, so libgcc_eh finds unwind tables through `dl_iterate_phdr` and never walks the 1.9 MB `.eh_frame`), an lld `--symbol-ordering-file` that puts the 384 libc functions the bench runs first in `.text` in first-call order (found with gdb breakpoints on all 1,558 libc functions through the startup, one-shot, first-frame and tool-turn parts; 186 KB of code in 313 KB, 6 windows of 64 KB instead of 12 or more), then BOLT `-lite` with the build's layout. bench/cli under tools/netguard.sh, three interleaved passes of 3 to 4 rounds, hosted Hand at load ~30, `fault_around_bytes` 65536, master binary first: `--version` 1.81 to 1.46 MB, one-shot 9.0 to 8.1 MB (CPU 8.3 to 5.0 ms), peak during the first frame 8.0 to 6.8 MB, but RSS after the first frame 6.66 to 7.09 MB (worse), tool turn 14.2 to 13.9 MB, and the tool turn's process tree 25.4 to 18.5 MB. Why it is not shipped: (1) DNS and the home directory go through NSS. std's `getaddrinfo` (every model connection) and `getpwuid_r` run in every bench run. The release links on rust:1.97-bullseye (glibc 2.31), where a static binary dlopens libnss_files and libnss_dns from the host at run time, so name lookups break on any host whose glibc is not 2.31. Even with glibc 2.34+ (files and dns built into libc.a), nsswitch modules such as myhostname, resolve, mdns4_minimal, systemd or sss are dlopened from the host's glibc into the static process. Keeping NSS out needs code (a resolver that reads /etc/hosts and resolv.conf itself, `$HOME` without getpwuid_r), not link flags. (2) Non-lite BOLT, which would put libc next to the hot text and should fix RSS after the first frame, is still blocked. Starting `__restore_rt`'s and `_dl_tlsdesc_undefweak`'s FDEs at their symbols (glibc's CFI starts 1 and 7 bytes early; libgcc unwinds a signal frame by `__restore_rt`'s code pattern anyway) gets BOLT 23 past "cannot be properly disassembled". It then segfaults on the PIC jump table it "fixes" in `__res_context_query` (Ubuntu's libc.a is built PIE). `-skip-funcs` does not stop it disassembling that function, and `-jump-tables=none` fails on handle_amd's PIC jump tables. Next, if static is wanted: take NSS off the CLI's paths first, then retry. With no resolver code linked, the BOLT crash goes away too.
- perf(djs): run_hot keeps only `code`, `end`, `bp`, `lp` and `vals` of the frame in locals: the header index is `lp - HEADER` (always, by the frame layout), the constant pool is read from `Exec::consts` (kept current by calls and returns already), and frame entry checks the new frame against the stack cell's end in bytes (`stack + Header::SIZE`) instead of a cached capacity (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 djs track: run_hot's per-instruction cost against QuickJS). Why: those three locals were assigned at every call, return and generator switch and live across the whole loop; natively `lp` was spilled and reloaded for every local access, and V8 spills what the loop keeps live (D2441). With them gone LLVM keeps `lp` in a register. The generator resume (`gen_resume_hot`) gets the capacity from the heap at its call. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, hosted Hand, output/djsrun on djs-embed, ~/bench-djs, the previous commit -> this): gennext 4,741.5M -> 4,653.8M (-1.9%), map 1,127.6M -> 1,098.4M (-2.6%), loop 784.5M -> 766.7M (-2.3%), find 786.2M -> 768.8M (-2.2%), some 787.3M -> 769.9M (-2.2%), filter 1,012.4M -> 993.2M (-1.9%), err 697.9M -> 686.3M (-1.7%), reduce 708.7M -> 697.4M (-1.6%), forEach 1,019.4M -> 1,010.1M (-0.9%), gen 2,566.7M -> 2,549.0M (-0.7%), empty 0.85M unchanged; against master 02b304a43 both commits together: loop 848.9M -> 766.7M (-9.7%, QuickJS 530.7M), reduce -7.2%, forEach -6.6%, find -6.1% (818.9M -> 768.8M), some -6.1%, map -5.5%, filter -5.2%, gennext -4.4%, gen -4.1%, err -3.3%. In wasm32 under V8 (as the previous entry, 13 runs minus 3 over 10, best of 3, two interleaved rounds, measured before the rebase on 767ba009c plus the previous commit): loop 939.7M/947.9M -> 891.9M/896.4M (-5%), find 1,286.2M/1,233.6M -> 1,169.2M/1,169.9M (-5 to -9%), gen 3,830.4M/3,829.7M -> 3,678.9M/3,671.3M (-4%), forEach 1,481.5M/1,482.7M -> 1,422.5M/1,414.2M (-4%). test262 subset (output/t262, 3,090 files) 2,535 passing with identical pass sets; the edge-case script prints the same as master, and the fuel harness gives the same results and total fuel for every slice size. Checked: `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (only the 3 pre-existing `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` errors). Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/interp/run/hot.rs.
- perf(djs): the tier-0 loop checks the fuel only at its safepoints (backward jumps, frame entry, returns and generator frame switches) and before an instruction it leaves to `step`, instead of `fuel <= 0 || ip >= end` before every instruction; the per-instruction charges are unchanged (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 djs track: run_hot's per-instruction cost against QuickJS). What: `run_hot` (interp/run/hot.rs) checks `fuel <= 0` and `ip >= end` once when it enters a frame from the run loop; inside the loop a taken backward jump, a frame entry (`call_closure!`, the `%EachDense` re-entry), a return and `switch_frame!` break out with fuel <= 0 (after the collection check, so collection points do not move), and a return into a native caller (or a switch to a frame with no bytecode left) leaves the loop instead of the next round's `ip >= end`. The `ip` check goes because bytecode cannot run off its end: the stack checker rejects such code at template creation (`StackError::FallsOffEnd`) and jumps outside it (`BadTarget`). Why: in `for (let i = 0; i < 2e6; i++) s += i` (9 instructions an iteration) the two compares and `end`'s reload were 5 of 47 native instructions per instruction, and V8 pays them in the same place. Fuel accounting: every instruction still charges its cost class, so a call's total fuel, its result and its collections are unchanged; a run that runs out of fuel now stops at the first safepoint or general-path instruction after that, not at the next instruction, so it can overshoot by the straight-line code before the next one, which the next run pays first as before (D1740). Stop points still depend only on the program and the fuel (deterministic), every loop has a backward jump and every recursion a frame entry, so an infinite loop or recursion still stops. With `hot_loop` off (tests only) the run loop still stops before the next instruction: results and fuel equal, slice ends may come earlier (run.rs's and hot.rs's docs say so). Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, hosted Hand, output/djsrun on djs-embed, ~/bench-djs, master 02b304a43 -> this): loop 848.9M -> 784.5M (-7.6%, QuickJS 530.7M), forEach 1,081.8M -> 1,019.4M (-5.8%), reduce 751.5M -> 708.7M (-5.7%), find 818.9M -> 786.2M (-4.0%), some 820.2M -> 787.3M (-4.0%), gen 2,657.2M -> 2,566.7M (-3.4%), filter 1,047.3M -> 1,012.4M (-3.3%), map 1,162.4M -> 1,127.6M (-3.0%), gennext 4,868.0M -> 4,741.5M (-2.6%), err 709.5M -> 697.9M (-1.6%), empty 0.85M unchanged. In wasm32 under V8 (node 24, djs-embed built for wasm32-unknown-unknown with `unsafe-heap`, `run` of the script's main, instructions:u of 7 runs minus 2 runs over 5, measured on master 767ba009c before the rebase): loop 1,051.6M -> 936.8M (-10.9%), find 1,300.2M -> 1,238.2M (-4.8%), gen 4,065.2M -> 3,892.1M (-4.3%). Checked with a fuel harness on djs-embed (`Instance::step` with `Limits { fuel, slice }`): an edge-case script (comparisons of mixed types, loops, recursion to RangeError, finally, exceptions and stacks from callbacks and generators, re-entrant valueOf) and a mixed workload give the same results and the same total fuel with slices of 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000; `for (;;)`, a float-counted `while` and an endless recursion caught in a loop still end with OutOfFuel (overshoot at most 13 units). Measured and dropped in the same session: fusing a comparison with the conditional jump after it in the hot loop (peeking the next instruction): native loop -5.2% and gen -2.1%, but under V8 loop +4.4%, find +4.7% and gen +4.0% (the extra code in run_hot, as D2441); reading the instruction word with a u64 bound and re-reading the opcode after the Box arms' page-tracking call: V8 within noise, the three per-instruction spills stayed. test262 subset (output/t262, 3,090 files) 2,535 passing with identical pass sets. Checked: `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (stable 1.100's new `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint reports 3 errors in bytecode/handlers.rs and bytecode/template.rs, the same on master; none in the changed files). Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/interp/run/hot.rs, interp/run.rs.
- feat(codex): `--working-state-budget TOKENS` (`NANOCODE_WORKING_STATE_BUDGET`, with `--working-state-retain`, default half the budget; `CodexBuilder::working_state`, `OpenAiBuilder::working_state`, `ModelConfig::working_state`) bounds how much old tool output a Codex-harness session replays (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 context-compaction lane: nanox spends 1.28M input tokens per pass on the Codex pair, and in its longest attempts tool results are 78% of the visible transcript, 102k of 131k tokens at the last call of make-mips-interpreter a00023). Off unless set. New module `nanocode-backend-codex-client::session::working_state`: before each mid-turn compaction check (`maybe_compact`), once the live (not yet elided) tool outputs pass the budget by `estimate_item_tokens`, the oldest outputs are replaced, oldest first, until at most the retain amount is left, with `[output elided by the working state budget: N tokens, exit C; see <working_state>]`, and each one's custom tool call input (an exec cell's source or an apply_patch body) with a stub naming the files it patched when the stub is shorter. One developer message `<working_state>` placed after the newest elided output, rebuilt at each elision and carrying the earlier block's lines forward, lists every file patched in the session and each elided call (first line, 160 characters) with its exit code. Assistant messages, function call arguments (update_plan, exec_command) and reasoning are kept, so the plan and the commands stay in the transcript. The history is replaced through `ManagedSessionState::replace_prepared_history`, so the next request is a full one; hysteresis (elide down to the retain amount, not to the budget) keeps the prefix stable between elisions so it caches. Measured offline on the 10 longest nanox attempts available on the hosted Hand (run 16e15f9a, gpt-6-luna, 596 calls; the report's other top-10 attempts live on dev-georgios, which this lane could not reach): the ATIF trajectories were rebuilt into `ResponseItem` sequences, the module replayed at every call boundary (`output/working-state`), and each call's reported prompt_tokens adjusted by the o200k tokens of what was elided, stubbed or added (`replay/rust_replay.py`; the reconstruction tracks reported prompt_tokens at slope 0.99 to 1.05 per visible token plus about 6.5k of prefix). Budget 16000: 58,198 to 32,048 input tokens per request (-44.9%), 4.01M to 2.14M per pass over the 8 passes; 311 of 586 tool outputs elided (287k unique tokens), 11 of them later quoted verbatim by the model (a line of 24+ characters reappearing in a later call or message), state block at most 6.7k tokens; uncached tokens rise from 0.73M to 1.14M since each elision resends the suffix, a net -28.9% in uncached + 0.1 x cached units. Budget 24000: -33.1% per request, 6 quoted later; 32000: -24.0%; 48000: -11.2%. `apply` takes at most 1.5 ms per call (release). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client` and the wasm32 check of it and `nanocode-backend-codex`, `cargo build -p nanocode-cli` (`--help` lists both flags), clippy on the changed crates.
- feat(cli): the psh shell that runs `exec_command` and `shell` commands answers `apply_patch` and `applypatch` as a utility (`bin/nanocode/src/patch.rs`, `Mode::PathFallback`: a real `apply_patch` on `PATH` still wins). It reads the patch from its one argument or from stdin, applies it relative to the shell's working directory with the codex backend's patch engine (`apply_patch::apply`, now `pub`), prints `Success. Updated the following files:` on stdout, and on failure prints the engine's error on stderr with exit 1, as Codex CLI 0.162.1's standalone `apply_patch` does (2026-11-15, lane L16). The pure-heredoc interception of a162ab6eb is unchanged and still answers first. The utility runs inside the nanocode process (the Harbor hand is `/installed-agent/nanocode/nc` in the task container), so it needs no writable directory, symlink or `PATH` change, and `bash script.sh` sees it because psh runs nested `bash`/`sh` itself. Stock Codex puts its arg0 `apply_patch` link under `$CODEX_HOME/tmp/arg0`, which Harbor trials do not have on `PATH`: in the cmp2 and glmmini GLM stock-codex trajectories every compound form (a heredoc followed by `\n python check.py`, `&& …`, after `cd … &&`) answered `/bin/bash: line 1: apply_patch: command not found`, after which GLM searched the file system or wrote files by hand. Mock (`output/L16`, `run14.py` + `mock14.py`, script `s_ap2.json`, 14 `exec_command` steps, stock Codex 0.162.1 run locally where its arg0 link is on `PATH`): before (b873e6913 build) 6 of 12 patch steps applied; after, 11 of 12, and all 13 non-shebang outputs equal stock's after masking chunk IDs, wall times and run directories: heredoc then a newline command, heredoc then `&& cmd`, `; echo rc=$?` on a missing file (`rc=1`, stock's text), `apply_patch "$(cat p.txt)"` inside `bash fix.sh`, and `printf … | apply_patch`. The pure-heredoc steps (add, `cd sub &&`, update, missing file, `workdir`) are byte-identical to before. Rebased on 88e95c06e, the two steps with commands after the closing delimiter take that commit's `exec_command` path first; their output differs from stock only in `Original token count` (2 against 13 and 14), where the utility alone matched stock byte for byte before the rebase. Not covered: an executable script with a `#!/bin/bash` shebang runs the real bash, which finds no `apply_patch` (stock passes it locally, fails it in Harbor). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-backend-codex --lib` and `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode --lib` (no new warnings), `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`.
- fix(claude): `Read` of an image keeps up to 2000 pixels a side and up to 3.75 MiB of bytes, as Claude Code 2.1.318 reads a file for Opus 5.5, instead of shrinking it to 1568 pixels a side and 1,150,000 pixels and recompressing anything over 500 KiB to JPEG down to quality 10 (2026-11-15, Claude-pair pass-loss lane). Claude Code 2.1.318 (the release nanoeval's `cc` arm runs; strings of `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64@2.1.318`) reads an image with `vd(model)`: the first-party cap of 2000 pixels a side, the model's `image_limits` (`maxWidth`/`maxHeight` 2576, `maxImageTokens` 4784 for claude-opus-5-5 and every 5.x model) and `targetRawSize` 3,932,160 bytes (`maxBase64Size` 5 MiB times 3/4); it sends the file's own bytes when they fit, otherwise resizes to fit 2000x2000 and the 4784 28-pixel-patch budget, and only past 3.75 MiB tries JPEG at 80, 60, 40 and 20. nanocode's brain already fits each tool image to the model (`ImageResolution::of`: 2576 pixels, 4784 patches for the 5.x models), but `image_block` on the hand cut it to the old 1568/1.15 MP limits first, so the brain never saw the detail. Now `image_block` fits within 2000x2000 (`fit_within`, Claude Code's `jOn` rounding), keeps the source bytes when they fit and are no larger than `TARGET_RAW_IMAGE` (`MAX_IMAGE / 4 * 3`), and past that tries JPEG at Claude Code's four qualities; the brain still applies the per-model patch budget, so on a 5.x model the image the model gets is Claude Code's size. Measured with `output/read-fidelity` (`ClaudeWorkspaceFiles::execute_output("Read", ...)` built at 138220ee0 and with this change), then each output fitted as the brain fits it for claude-opus-5-5 and compared with Claude Code's pipeline: a 1920x1080 frame reached the model at 1429x804 (1.15 MP, 1508 patches) before and 1920x1080 (2.07 MP, 2691 patches) after, Claude Code 1920x1080; a 2880x1800 screenshot 1356x847 before, 2000x1250 after and in Claude Code; a 3840x2160 contact sheet of 16 frames 1429x804 (as JPEG) before, 2000x1125 after and in Claude Code; a 960x540 video frame of video-processing's example (662 KB PNG) went out as JPEG at 39.5 dB PSNR before and as its own PNG bytes after, as in Claude Code; 640x640 chess-best-move-sized boards were unchanged. tesseract on 1920x1080 frames of 12 px monospace text read 97.0% of the characters before and 99.9% after (Claude Code 99.9%), 99.4% and 99.9% at 14 px. `Read` itself got faster on the images it no longer resamples: 1920x1080 PNG 74.9 to 10.0 ms, 2880x1800 155 to 116 ms, 3840x2160 437 to 300 ms (one run each). Cost: an image above 1.15 MP now spends up to 4784 input tokens in the request instead of about 1500, the same as Claude Code. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

- docs(decisions): a Claude turn whose response is refused once and then answered finishes, and every refused call counts in the turn's usage; nothing in the refusal path changes, and a plain resend of the identical request is not a lever for Terminal-Bench refusals, because the API refuses those requests deterministically (2026-11-15, refusal-handling lane, against Terminal-Bench 2.1 run 200a4c68's 27 nano refusal errors). Harness: output/refusal-mock (ignored): stub.py is a scripted streaming Messages endpoint whose responses end with stop_reason refusal (with or without a finished text block, and with `stop_details.category` cyber or bio) or end_turn; run.py runs a debug `nanocode exec --model claude-opus-5-5 --no-subagents` at 138220ee0 against it and records each request. Results: ok exits 0 after 1 request; refuse(no text),ok exits 0 after 2, the second identical to the first; refuse(text),ok exits 0 after 2, the second carrying [assistant text, Claude Code's recovery note]; refuse,refuse,ok exits 0 after 3, the third ending in REFUSAL_CONTINUATION; refuse,refuse,refuse,ok exits 1 after 3 with "provider refused the request (stop_reason=refusal); turn stopped"; refuse(bio),ok exits 0 after 2, the second sent unchanged to `claude-opus-5`; refuse(bio),refuse(bio),refuse,refuse exits 1 after 4. The turn's `agent.turn` span for refuse,ok carries usage.input_tokens 200 and usage.output_tokens 14 (two calls of 100 and 7), so refused calls count. The share of refuse-once-then-answer turns that end the attempt is 0 of 1 on this harness, already at master before this entry (the resend landed in 1c6dfe3ed, the fallback in f85fd5a04, the continuation in 15c87b4da); run 200a4c68 ran a build before the fallback. Replaying recorded first requests against the Messages API on the thread's Hand: Claude Code 2.1.318's and nanocode's first requests of break-filter-js-from-html, dna-assembly, protein-assembly and vulnerable-secret were refused on every one of 8 sends each, mostly at 0 output tokens, each with a category (cyber or bio) that `refusal_fallback` maps; crack-7z-hash's were refused 8 of 8 for Claude Code and 6 of 8 for nanocode. So an identical resend recovers nearly none of these, and the fallback model is what recovers them, as the refusal-fallback-check run d83ae647 showed (8 of 9 passed with 0 refusals on crack-7z-hash, dna-assembly and feal-differential-cryptanalysis). The resend stays, since it is what Claude Code does and costs one call only when the classifier stops a response.
- fix(codex): `exec_command` also applies an `apply_patch` heredoc that other commands follow, then runs those commands in the shell, with the patch summary first in their output (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1 lane L3-ds-codex-tokens). What: `apply_patch::heredoc` returns the text after the closing delimiter, and `ExecCommandHandler` applies the patch, then runs that text with the `cd` directory as `workdir`; a patch that fails returns `apply_patch verification failed: …` and the later commands do not run. A heredoc with nothing after it keeps codex-cli 0.162.1's intercepted text. Why: the models mostly append a check to the patch (`apply_patch <<'PATCH' … PATCH\nls -l ars.R`, `… PATCH\npython x.py`). Codex-cli also answers these, through the `apply_patch` alias that it puts on PATH, while nanocode returned `apply_patch: command not found` and the model wrote the file again. In 184 nc-codex last-request.json files (~/hill/harbor logs and jobs, cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0044; output/L3-ds-codex-tokens/replay.py), 70 calls returned that error (17 DeepSeek, 53 GLM): 8 were heredocs alone (the previous entry), 52 had commands after the delimiter (this entry), and 5 put a command before `apply_patch` (still unhandled). Estimated saving from replay: one model call and one rewrite of the file per hit, about 10k input tokens per DeepSeek trial and 74k per GLM trial over all trials. Cause of the lane's question: live DeepSeek adaptive-rejection-sampler nc-codex a0 sent 2.84M input tokens against stock's 1.33M (35 vs 23 calls) because it wrote the 33 KB ars.R three times (apply_patch as a function call, then `apply_patch <<'PATCH' … PATCH\nls -l ars.R`, then `cat >`). Request composition is otherwise the same as stock (reasoning replay, tool output sizes and the 3,000-token history budget match). Across 23 matched cmp2 DeepSeek tasks, m3-codex already used 0.82M input tokens per trial against stock's 1.54M (~/hill/analysis/cb_trials.json), and stock itself ranged 0.26M-2.0M on this task. Check: output/L3-ds-codex-tokens/run3.py shellpatch (mock Responses server, 6 apply_patch exec calls): 8efd8ecad 0 of 6 apply, stock codex-cli 0.162.1 6 of 6, this build 5 of 6 with the same text as stock (only `echo pre; apply_patch <<…` still fails). `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy` on it and `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` pass.

- check(codex): `python3 scripts/codex-request-parity.py` diffs nanocode's first Codex request against codex-cli 0.166.0's, both captured offline against a local Responses mock, and exits 1 when any difference appears that `crates/backends/codex/upstream/request.json` does not document or a documented one disappears (2026-11-15, Codex parity lane). The fixture holds codex-cli's request for `codex exec --json --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox --skip-git-repo-check -m gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort=high "Say hi"` (custom `responses` provider on the mock, fresh CODEX_HOME; paths, ids and authorization scrubbed), and `--codex PATH` recaptures it; the check runs `nanocode exec --ephemeral -m gpt-6-luna -t high "Say hi"` with NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL on the mock (`--nanocode`, default target/debug/nanocode). It compares the method and path, every header but host and content-length, every top-level body field (client_metadata by key, prompt_cache_key by presence), `service_tier`, each tool and namespace in `tools` or the `additional_tools` item by its exact JSON, and each input text part by tag and content. Baseline on 35ba28283: 24 differences, all now documented with their reason in the fixture, 0 undocumented: identity headers (originator, user-agent), accept-encoding, x-codex-beta-features remote_compaction_v2 (not implemented here), the x-codex-turn-metadata header and x-codex-window-id and client_metadata's installation, window and root-turn keys (no source for them in nanocode), skills_instructions (no CODEX_HOME skills), the permissions message's added runtime_model_identity, codex-cli's multi-agent v2 surface (collaboration_mode, multi_agent_role, multi_agent_mode, the collaboration namespace's six tools, which address agents by task path and mailbox where nanocode's subagent runtime uses numeric ids as nested exec tools), clock.sleep, request_user_input and request_user_input_async, and exec's description. What matches byte for byte: the base instructions message, environment_context, the prompt, `wait`, model, reasoning `{effort, context}` with no summary, text verbosity, include, store, stream, tool_choice, parallel_tool_calls, the Responses Lite header and the `functions` namespace placement. Service tier: codex-cli 0.166.0's `exec` sends no `service_tier` (none in the capture): models.json gives gpt-6-luna and gpt-6-sol `default_service_tier: "priority"`, but only the TUI reads it (tui/src/service_tier_resolution.rs); core's `get_service_tier` (core/src/session/mod.rs) uses only a configured tier. nanocode exec defaults to Standard and sends none either, so the tier matches and stays. Not changed: no tool was added, since clock.sleep and request_user_input change what the model sees and go through the Terminal-Bench A/B, and request_user_input has no user to answer in exec. Mutation check: setting the fixture's reasoning effort to medium and dropping clock.sleep's documentation makes the check report `param:reasoning` and `tool:clock.sleep` as undocumented and exit 1. Files: scripts/codex-request-parity.py, crates/backends/codex/upstream/request.json.

Why: nanoeval's two A/B runs on dev-georgios with gpt-6-luna at high effort on the ChatGPT plan, `16e15f9a` and `650d0782`, each carried nanox (Code Mode) and nanoxd (direct) on the same rows; on the 94 attempts matched across both arms over 22 hard tasks direct passed 50.0 % against Code Mode's 43.6 % (+6.4 points) with 15 % fewer tokens and 11 % fewer agent-seconds per pass, and led in both runs (nanoeval `report.py`, 16:59 PST Nov 14). The loss kept: circuit-fibsqrt, nanoxd 0/3 against nanox 2/3 in `650d0782` (the entry on it below finds the cause in the trajectory). On the full Codex pair nanox in Code Mode was at parity with codex-cli 0.166 (59.1 % against 59.9 %), and codex-cli itself gives gpt-6-luna only Code Mode, so the default now differs from codex-cli's request shape on purpose. Checked: `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` (thread's hosted Hand, on 138220ee0 plus this change), then `nanocode exec -m gpt-6-luna "say ok"` against a local mock of `/v1/models` and `/v1/responses` (`NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL`), reading the tools of the first request's `additional_tools` item: with no flag it offers `functions.apply_patch`, `exec_command`, `update_plan`, `view_image`, `write_stdin` and `tool_search`, and no `exec` or `wait`; with `--codex-orchestration code-mode` it offers `functions.exec` and `functions.wait` only, as the default did before; `--codex-orchestration direct` matches the default. - feat(djs): sloppy-mode block-level function declarations (Annex B.3.2, B.3.4) (2026-11-15, djs conformance lane "annexb"). A plain function declaration in a block, a `switch` case or an `if` body of sloppy code now also writes the enclosing function's (or the script's) var binding when it is evaluated, which `var` creates unless replacing the declaration with `var F` would be an early error: a lexical binding of the name in a scope between the block and the function, an enclosing block's function of that name, a parameter, or a catch parameter with a pattern. The parser records each declaration with the `name_put` reference it emits after it (`FuncState::annexb`), and `Parser::settle_annexb`, run when the function or unit ends (so lexical declarations after the block count), points the reference at the var scope or leaves it on the block binding, where it writes the binding to itself. `if (x) function f() {}` parses as a block around the declaration, and two function declarations of one name in a sloppy block share the binding. Sloppy is the absence of a "use strict" directive in the function or any enclosing one, outside classes and modules; the top level of a script now records its own directive. test262 (conformance mode): 29,400 to 29,902 of 36,835 run, no test that passed fails; annexB/language/global-code 30 to 144 of 153, function-code 33 to 158 of 159, eval-code 82 to 345 of 469 (the global eval tests; eval still binds top-level declarations as locals); sub.list 2808 (2808 frozen-off), 2535 with T262_FROZEN=1. Bench instructions:u against master: within 0.1% on every file (empty +0.10%, gtest +0.03%, the rest +-0.00%). Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings`.
- fix(tls): a TLS handshake whose write is blocked also reads, so two peers with small transport buffers no longer wait on each other forever (2026-11-15, HTTP/TLS bugs lane: the tiny-buffer handshake stall). Why: `Pass::handshake` in crates/core/tls/src/stream.rs read only while `session.wants_read()`, and rustls answers false during the handshake while it still has records to send (`sendable_tls` not empty, before it may send application data); tokio-rustls's handshake loop has the same shape. When both directions have only a few bytes of room, a TLS 1.3 client whose middlebox-compatibility ChangeCipherSpec (6 bytes) does not fit stops reading, while the server, blocked writing its flight into the client's full buffer, also has unsent records and does not read either: both `poll_handshaken` return Pending and nothing wakes them. Real sockets hide it (kernel buffers hold a whole flight), which is why nanocode-sim's streams scenario gives TLS pipes at least `SOCKET_BUFFER_MIN` (4,608) bytes. What: the read loop also runs when this pass's write was blocked (`wants_read() || write_blocked`); the read only fills rustls's deframer, `process_new_packets` consumes it, and the peer's handshake flight bounds it. Measured with output/tls-stall (nanocode-tls `connect`/`accept` over two in-memory pipes with seeded capacities, write piece sizes, TLS 1.2 or 1.3 and up to 40,000 bytes each way after the handshake, polled by a seeded single-thread scheduler that reports a stall when neither side is woken): capacities 1..64, seeds 0..200, master 18 of 200 stall, all TLS 1.3 with a client-to-server capacity of 1 to 5 bytes and neither side handshaken (seed 174: there 5, back 6); with this change seeds 0..10,000 at capacities 1..64, 10,000..20,000 at 1..512 and 20,000..25,000 at 1..20,000 all pass, 25,000 of 25,000, bytes checked both ways. Commands: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-tls` (nothing in nanocode-tls), `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tls --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. File: crates/core/tls/src/stream.rs.
- feat(claude): `ClaudeBuilder::steer_preempts_model(true)` cuts short the model call in flight when a steer arrives and sends the request again with the steer, instead of the steer waiting for the call to finish (2026-11-15, pyramid2 perf bet C: production Pyramid's steer-to-agent latency while the model runs is the in-flight call's remainder, 1.3 s p50 and 24 s max over 12 shadow steers, and pyramid2's bench mock showed 404 ms p50 for a 0.5 s hold). Default off, so hosts that do not opt in behave as before. How: `TurnSteering` gains a `watch::Sender<u64>` bumped by `accept_steer`; before each model step the run loop subscribes (marking it changed at once when a steer that missed this step's `consume_steering` is still pending), and `request_response` races that receiver against the stream's opening and every receive, beside the turn's cancellation. A preempted call returns `TurnCancelled` with no server recovery while the turn's own cancellation is live, and the run loop then treats it like the refusal fallback: the aborted response is dropped (nothing of it reaches the history), `model_step_offset` is set as a finished first call sets it, `cursor.index` moves to the next step and the cursor is deferred, so the next iteration's `consume_steering` binds the steer to the new boundary exactly as a steer consumed after a finished call is bound, and durable recovery resumes there (the abandoned `model-N` step began with `StepRecovery::Rerun`, so an open step is never replayed; a crash before the deferred cursor commits reruns `model-N` and consumes the steer after it, as without preemption). The call is never preempted once its stream showed a server tool call, an MCP tool call or a container, or after a code-only upgrade notice (`preemptible`), since server effects may already have run; nor on a replaying boundary. The aborted call's tokens are not counted in the turn's usage (the provider may bill its prefill; the resend reads the same prefix from the prompt cache). `ModelCallStarted` and `ModelCallFailed` ("turn cancelled") are emitted for the aborted call as for any failed call. Codex is unchanged. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Behaviour is measured end to end in tempoxyz/pyramid2's bench (crates/server/tests/bench, a mock Messages endpoint that holds the first request 0.5 s while the driver steers 0.1 s in). Files: crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent/side.rs.
- perf(cli), measured and not shipped: where nanocode's peak RSS comes from on Linux, and three layout changes that do not lower it (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: peak RSS against fx 0.0.16, wave 2). Nothing in the build changes. Why this is written down: the rows are set less by what nanocode touches than by the kernel's fault-around, which maps up to 16 cached pages (`/sys/kernel/debug/fault_around_bytes` = 65536) around every read fault on a file mapping, so one touched page in a 64 KB window costs 64 KB. With `fault_around_bytes` set to 4096 for the run, the bench/cli rows for the master binary (37b42b7f5) fall from `--version` 1.80 to 0.50 MB, one-shot 8.5 to 5.0 MB, RSS after the first frame 6.2 to 4.1 MB and the 10-step tool turn 13.8 to 8.8 MB (fx 0.0.16 then: 0.13, 3.1, 4.0 and 4.6 MB), so about 40% of every row is neighbours of touched pages. Per section at exit (gdb at `exit_group`, /proc/pid/pagemap), one-shot holds BOLT's hot `.text` 1.98 MB of 3.1, `.text.cold` 2.1 MB, the original `.rodata` 1.07 MB, libc.so.6 0.7 MB (524 KB of its text, faulted around for a few dozen functions) and 2.2 MB anonymous; the tool turn 3.0 MB hot text, 4.0 MB `.text.cold`, 1.74 MB rodata and 3.9 MB anonymous. Exactly, one-shot touches only 67 pages of `.text.cold` (cold fragments of hot functions whose blocks the training did not run), but they fall in 36 different 64 KB windows. `madvise(MADV_RANDOM)` does not turn fault-around off for a mapping (checked on kernel 6.18). Measured and dropped (bench/cli under tools/netguard.sh, three interleaved passes of 4 rounds, hosted Hand at load 25 to 40, BOLT rerun on the same `linked` binary and profile as 37b42b7f5's build): without `-split-all-cold` `--version` 1.80 to 1.83, one-shot 8.53 to 8.78, after first frame 6.50 to 6.55, tool turn 13.94 to 13.77 MB (all within spread); without `-split-functions` (whole functions in hot text) every row grows: `--version` 2.05, one-shot 10.2, after first frame 7.7, tool turn 15.8 MB. A fully static glibc link (relinked from the same object with `-static`): (1) crtbeginT.o's `frame_dummy` registers `.eh_frame` with libgcc_eh, whose GCC 13 registration walks every FDE at startup and faults the whole 1.9 MB `.eh_frame` (`--version` 3.7 MB); linking crtbegin.o instead (`-nostartfiles` with crt1.o, crti.o, crtbegin.o ... crtend.o, crtn.o) leaves unwinding to `dl_iterate_phdr` and removes it; (2) static glibc's own startup (IRELATIVE resolvers, cpu features, tunables) touches 62 pages spread over 12 windows of its 0.8 MB, so without ordering those functions `--version` stays at 1.6 MB unBOLTed and 1.89 MB after BOLT; (3) BOLT cannot process the static binary outside `-lite` (`__restore_rt`'s FDE starts one byte before the symbol: "function cannot be properly disassembled"), and lite leaves libc's functions where they are. The static binary also links getaddrinfo, getpwnam_r and dlopen from libc.a (NSS). Next, in order of expected effect: order the startup's libc functions next to the hot text (a static link with an lld `--symbol-ordering-file`, or BOLT with a profile of the static binary from `-instrumentation-sleep-time`), keep the cold fragments a run reaches in few windows (train the bench's streamed one-shot and tool turn, or put `.text.cold` in the order the training first reached each fragment), and the anonymous 2.2 to 3.9 MB (allocator `DIRTY_SLICES_MAX` 64 slices of 64 KB and the 8 MB large cache are kept dirty). Tools used: gdb with a Python script that reads /proc/pid/smaps and pagemap at `exit_group` as the bench's NC_BIN; `fault_around_bytes` was put back to 65536 after each run.
- feat(cli): `nanocode exec --escalate-model MODEL --escalate-after N` continues the prompt on MODEL once the session model makes N top-level tool calls in a row that write no file (2026-11-15, O3 cascade lane L8-cascade). What: `stream_turn` counts top-level `tool.call` events (no `parent_call_id`) whose tool is not Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, Write or apply_patch and whose arguments hold none of `> `, `>>`, `<<`, `tee `, `sed -i`, `apply_patch`, `write`, `mv `, `cp `, `rm `, `mkdir `, `touch `; at the next `model.call.started` after N such calls it cancels the turn, `Runtime::switch` carries the transcript to MODEL (same route and harness, else exec rejects the flag), and exec sends `Continue.` on the new agent. Without the flags exec is unchanged. Why: from 635 non-infra DS-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3-Flash TB2.1 trials (~/hill/harbor jobs and the cf-all-ds-glm-1115-0044 jobs, failure causes from ~/hill/analysis/fail-causes-2026-11-14.py, infra failures dropped), this exact rule at N=8 fires at least 20% of the task budget before the trial's end in 38 of 132 failed trials (29%: DS 33%, GLM 25%; timeouts 47%, wrong answers 14%) and in 81 of 503 passed trials (16%); N=6 gives 37%/21%, N=10 22%/13%, N=12 14%/10%. Repeated-command and repeated-error detectors caught at most 10% of failures, and an edit-tool-only write signal fired on 27% of passes at N=8. The script is output/L8-cascade/stall.py on the lane's Hand (`python3 stall.py --impl`). Check: a mock Messages server (output/L8-cascade/mock.py, run.sh) answers the weak model with `ls /` forever and the strong model with a Write, then text; before (no flags) the run made 21 weak calls and ended on the weak model's give-up; after (`--escalate-after 4`) it made 4 weak calls, cancelled the 5th before its request, and 2 calls on the strong model whose first request carried the prompt, the 4 tool calls and results and the interruption, then the Write ran. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-cli` native and wasm32, `cargo clippy -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` and `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` pass. Not measured: the pass rate or cost of a live escalation; the only Workers AI model stronger than DS is kimi-k2.7-code, whose cached input costs 0.19 $/M against DS's 0.006 $/M.
- perf(claude): a Claude request replaces the content of old tool results with Claude Code's `[Old tool result content cleared]` in batches (`agent/clearing.rs`, applied to the wire messages before image eviction, not to the stored history; off while a message thread holds the conversation) (2026-11-14, TB2.1 Claude pair tokens/pass, lane L4). Rule, from Claude Code 2.1.304's tool-result clearing (`Nn = {keepToolUses: 12, clearAtLeastTokens: 20000}`, results under 64 characters not counted): walking the results in order, once the results that left the 12 most recent add up to at least 20,000 estimated tokens, all of them are cleared together. The cleared set is a function of the history alone, so it only grows in steps of at least 20,000 tokens and the cached prefix breaks once per step. Stock Claude Code applies the same edit only after an idle gap of 65 minutes (behind a flag), so in an eval it never clears; this goes past parity for tokens. Each message caches its result sizes (`HistoryMessage::result_tokens`), so a request does not re-measure the history. Measured with output/claude-cache (mock Messages server that replays a scripted 40-call session through Code Mode, simulates prompt caching from the request's breakpoints with 20-block lookback, tokens = JSON bytes / 4), `nanocode exec -m claude-opus-5-5 -t high`, debug build, hosted Hand, 1 run per arm (deterministic): input tokens 2,842,543 (read 2,722,836, create 119,707) before, 1,964,765 (read 1,778,377, create 186,388) after, -30.9%; last request 119,707 -> 69,354 tokens; prefix breaks 0 -> 2 (the two batches); list-price-weighted cost (read 0.1x, 5-minute write 1.25x) 421.9k -> 410.8k units, -2.6%. Stock Claude Code 2.1.304 on the same mock: 2,573,253 (read 2,483,106, create 90,147), no prefix breaks, breakpoints on the last two system blocks and the last message. Other findings, not changed here: breakpoint placement (tools, system, tail) and `clear_thinking_20251015 keep:all` already match Claude Code; Claude Code keeps 30,000 characters of a Bash output inline and moves the rest to a file behind a 2 KB preview, and returns a stub for an unchanged re-Read, where nanocode keeps up to 12,000 tokens (`TOOL_RESULT_TOKEN_LIMIT`) of an exec result and has no Read dedup (unsafe in Code Mode, where a script may never have printed the first read).
- fix(mpp): a session top-up adds the largest of the configured top-up amount, the server's `suggestedDeposit` and what the channel has already spent (its cumulative amount), never less than the shortfall, so a busy channel's deposit at least doubles with each top-up and a run needs about log2(spend / first deposit) top-ups instead of one per fixed chunk (2026-11-15, same mainnet audit: 855 top-up transactions, most of them small fixed or shortfall-sized). Before, `required_top_up` took the shortfall or the configured amount, which overrode the suggestion, so nanocode's tool sessions topped up by 0.1 MACH even where a service suggested 1 MACH, and `top_up_ahead` always added the configured amount.
