On wasm32, with this and the two entries above it applied to the nanocode revision that nanocode-ts pins: the nanocode-ts host in Node drove a Codex session whose scripted `dispatch` answered the first request with (a) or (b): (a) the body cancelled and the attempt failed at 300.8 s, the second request at 301.7 s, the turn completed at 301.8 s; (b) the request aborted at 300.7 s, the second at 301.7 s, completed at 301.9 s; per request the host armed one 300,000 ms timer for the head and one for the body. On the released nanocode-ts build-f3aa94f both were still waiting at 330 s with no long host timer armed. What a second stall does is the entry "a model call whose stream stalled is asked again once". Not changed, reported: on wasm32 the host WebSocket's `connect` and `send` have no counterpart of the native `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` and `SEND_TIMEOUT`; a host does its own admission of the request inside them (nanocode-ts settles remote work and admits the effect there), and nothing measured here bounds that. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-claude-client` and `-p nanocode-backend-codex -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, pass. Files: crates/backends/codex/client/src/transport/{http.rs,chat.rs}.

- fix(claude): a 402 that outlasts its attempts fails the turn, instead of leaving it for a durable host to drive again (2026-11-14, nanoeval's lane "a key that is spent during the run" on nanocode-ts build-b8158fd). 9bebe258c made a 402 whose problem type is `/reference#description/payment-failed`, `https://paymentauth.org/problems/verification-failed` or `https://paymentauth.org/problems/session/delta-too-small` transient, so that it gets Claude Code's backoff "within the 11 attempts". `BackendFailure::retryable` of `ClaudeError` returned `is_transient()`, so the error that ends those attempts was retryable as well: a turn under an execution policy settled as `Settlement::FailAttempt` (crates/backends/claude/src/agent/durable.rs), `AgentRuntime::durable_outcome` answered `Interrupted`, and a durable host drove the turn again (nanocode-ts: `drive` answers `retry`, App.ts throws "runtime recovery required", marks the turn interrupted and its alarm runs it again), eleven more requests each time, with no end. The gateway answers `payment-failed` for every failure of a payment step, the ones that pass (its payment Durable Object overloaded, the cases of 9bebe258c) and the ones that do not: one answer serves them all, and it words an empty wallet ("The wallet … holds 0 of the 3 … its channel needs now"), a spending limit that is used up, an expired key and a revoked key under that one type, with no field that tells them from an overload; only its 429 for a busy channel carries `retry` and `Retry-After`. So a session on a key whose wallet was empty never ended its turn. In nanoeval's lane (a scripted gateway that answers every model request `payment-failed` after two responses; nanocode-ts build-b8158fd, this crate at 0bbcb64a0) 27 requests of the row that was running reached the gateway in 279 s: nanoeval's relay sent the first one 9 times during its wait of 15 s, the ten other attempts followed until 199 s, the turn was driven again 5 s later and had asked 8 more times when the 300 s agent timeout of the row ended it, and the row was scored 0; on build-f3aa94f (0e428f673, without 9bebe258c) the turn ended at the first 402 it was handed. Now `retryable` leaves out a 402 that no `x-should-retry` header decided. `is_transient` is unchanged, so such a 402 keeps its 11 attempts and their backoff, and the error after the last one fails the turn (`Settlement::Fail`, `durable_outcome` `Failed`). A 402 with `x-should-retry: true`, and 408, 409, 429, 5xx, transport and stream errors, are retryable at the end as before. What this does not change: an empty wallet still costs 11 requests and 184 s before the turn fails, because nothing in the body says that this `payment-failed` will not pass; the gateway is the place to say it (a `retry` field, as its 429 has, or a 503 for its own failures), and a host that knows may cancel the turn sooner, as nanoeval now does for its rows. Measured with output/claude-402 (a whole Claude session turn with a `MemoryStore` session store against a scripted TCP server that answers every Messages request, or the first N, with one status and body; it prints the posts, the error of the turn, `retryable()` of it and what `durable_outcome` answers), debug builds of 0bbcb64a0 and of 0bbcb64a0 with this change, one run each: `payment-failed` on every request, 11 posts and failed at 184.0 s, retryable and `Interrupted` before; 11 posts and failed at 183.9 s, not retryable and `Failed` after. `delta-too-small` on every request: 11 posts at 183.9 s, retryable and `Interrupted` before, not retryable and `Failed` after. `payment-failed` (overloaded) or `verification-failed` twice and then an answer: 3 posts, completed at 1.8 s before and 1.7 s after. `insufficient-balance`, a 402 with another body (nanoeval's `model_budget`), 401, 403, 404 and 422: 1 post, failed at 0.1 s, not retryable and `Failed`, before and after. 500 on every request: 11 posts at 184.0 s, retryable and `Interrupted`, before and after. Codex needs no change: output/codex-status (the Codex client's service against a scripted host transport that rejects every HTTPS request with one status, 0bbcb64a0) sent 6 posts in 6.2 s for each of 401, 402 `payment-failed`, 403, 404 and 422 (five reconnects, 0.2 s doubling) and failed with an error that is not retryable, and 30 posts in 98.5 s for 500 with a retryable one. On wasm32, in a Worker: the module of nanocode-ts b8158fd built against 0bbcb64a0 with this change (`cargo +1.97.1 build --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --profile wasm`, 15,426,621 bytes, not passed through wasm-opt) was put in place of the released module in nanoeval main 40e3fea: the lane passed in 218 s, the row ending as a `budget` error "Messages HTTP 402: …" 199.1 s after the first refusal and 19 requests (nanoeval's relay held the request for its wait of 15 s, then the 11 attempts), where the released module failed the lane in 318 s. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client --no-deps -- -D warnings` on both targets passed, on 0dff6b832 with this change; the harnesses and the module were built at 0bbcb64a0, the revision of build-b8158fd. Run again on c97e1a49f, after nanocode's own executor replaced tokio (c2ee03965) and hedged requests arrived (1d4463636, off unless a host asks): the same two cargo check commands and clippy with `-D warnings` on both targets pass, and both harnesses, moved from tokio to nanocode-executor, give the same answers, one run each, c97e1a49f against c97e1a49f with this change: `payment-failed` and `delta-too-small` on every request, 11 posts and failed at 184.6 and 184.5 s, retryable and `Interrupted` before; 184.4 and 184.5 s, not retryable and `Failed` after. The overloaded `payment-failed` or `verification-failed` twice and then an answer: 3 posts, completed at 1.9 and 1.8 s before, 1.7 and 1.8 s after. `insufficient-balance`, `model_budget`, 401, 403, 404 and 422: 1 post, failed within 0.2 s, not retryable and `Failed`, before and after. 500 on every request: 11 posts at 184.5 s, retryable and `Interrupted`, before and after. Codex on c97e1a49f: 6 posts in 6.2 to 6.4 s for 401, 402, 403, 404 and 422, not retryable, and 30 posts in 98.9 s for 500, retryable. Files: crates/backends/claude/client/src/lib.rs.

- fix(store-jsonl): the session listing's unique mtime stamp reads nanocode_platform::system_time() instead of SystemTime::now(), so simulated runs take the host's clock; nanocode-sim --tidy flagged listing.rs:71 after 38e547873 and is clean again (2026-11-14).
- fix(cli): /reload with a command running hands the command over as nc hand's SIGTERM path does instead of killing it (2026-11-14, nanocode CLI e2e item a). After flushing the session and the store, reload calls `nanocode_process::leave_reader`; when outputs are open it skips the runtime shutdown, which dropped the running call and stopped its process group, and execs the new nanocode, so the command runs to its end with its output read by the detached `read-outputs` process, and the resumed turn tells the model the call's outcome is unknown. Foreground Bash (`foreground::Capture`) registers its pipes as open outputs, which the hand path's hand-over also missed. Before, python3 crunch.py died at the reload; after, it ran its 60 s and the reader exited.
- fix(tui): a single newline in a reply or in reasoning breaks the line instead of joining as a CommonMark soft break: `render_from` renders with `breaks`, as chat messages already did (2026-11-14, nanocode CLI e2e item i). Both upstreams keep the break: codex-rs tui markdown_render.rs (openai/codex 9d11b38f) `soft_break` pushes a new line outside table cells and link labels, and Claude Code 2.1.325 shows a three-line reply on three lines (tmux, claude-haiku-5-5). A table cell still joins its soft breaks with a space.
- fix(cli): a Claude background Bash completion (`<task-notification>`) shows as a notice with its summary (`Background command "…" completed (exit code 0)`, a warning when it failed or was killed) instead of a raw user cell, live and when a session is replayed (2026-11-14, nanocode CLI e2e item b). `events::background_notices` reads status and summary from each notification, as `completion_agent` does for subagent completions; the model still gets the whole text.
- fix(tui): text cut at a pane edge ends in an ellipsis (`unicode::ellipsize`, the queue's truncation moved there): slash-command descriptions, F1 help actions and picker labels; and Esc in the picker `nanocode resume` opens exits (2026-11-14, nanocode CLI e2e items f, g). The resume picker already gave each session its age, model and id as the item's detail, but the label column took the widest first prompt, so one long prompt pushed every detail past the edge; `picker::fitted` caps the label column at what the widest detail leaves and ellipsizes longer labels. Esc with no session yet quits, as Esc in `claude --resume` exits (2.1.325, checked in tmux); from /resume inside a session it still only closes the picker.
- fix(cli): `nanocode exec` reads the prompt from stdin when stdin is not a terminal, as `claude -p` does, says when a failed exec session got no reply, and `nanocode models` prints the catalog when a custom endpoint's model listing fails (2026-11-14, nanocode CLI e2e items c, d, e). c: Claude Code 2.1.325's getInputPrompt joins the argument and piped stdin with one newline (`[prompt, stdin].filter(Boolean).join("\n")`), stops waiting after 3 s without data and refuses piped input over 10 MiB; `PIPED_PROMPT_WAIT` and `PIPED_PROMPT_LIMIT` are those values, so a harness that leaves stdin an open pipe still runs; an embedder with an `answer` hook keeps stdin for answers. d: a new exec session whose turn failed before any reply is kept, since it resumes with its prompt and Claude Code also keeps a failed -p session, but exec ends with `session <id> has only the prompt: the turn failed before any reply` instead of the plain session line; the store has no delete, and `abandon_created` left the session listed. e: `print_models` returned on `listed()`'s error before printing; it now prints every group, the listing error as the Codex note, and exits 1 with that error, and a 401 or 403 names the variable whose key was refused (NANOCODE_OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY) or says none was set.
- fix(python): C extensions get CPython 3.13's exception links, PyObject_VectorcallDict, tracebacks through PyErr_Fetch/Restore, keyword-only PyArg parameters, PyCMethod's defining class, number slots and a per-module PyModule_GetDef (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 bug-fix wave: confirm the C API's calls, errors and module state). How found: a check extension written for this (one C file, 25 checks: METH_NOARGS/O/VARARGS|KEYWORDS/FASTCALL(|KEYWORDS) with ints, floats, bytes, tuples, dicts, None and keywords; PyObject_Call, CallObject, CallFunction with 13 format strings, CallMethod(ObjArgs/NoArgs/OneArg), Vectorcall(Method/Dict) into Python; PyErr_SetString/Format/SetObject/SetNone with a PyErr_NewException class, chaining by cause and by context, PyErr_Fetch/Restore, Python errors seen in C through NULL and PyErr_Occurred, errors from tp_init, a getter, a setter, tp_richcompare, nb_add, tp_hash, mp_length, mp_subscript, tp_iternext, tp_call and tp_repr; multi-phase init with m_size > 0, two Py_mod_exec slots, PyType_FromModuleAndSpec, PyType_GetModuleState/GetModuleByDef, a second import and a reload) with a Python driver, first passing 25/25 against CPython 3.12 so the expectations are CPython's, then compiled under ext/ locally (not committed). On master the extension did not link: `rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: PyException_GetCause` (also GetContext, SetCause, SetContext, SetTraceback, GetArgs and PyObject_VectorcallDict); with those seven stubbed inside the check, master passed 17/25 natively and in python.wasm alike. What changed: (1) api.rs adds PyException_GetCause/GetContext/SetCause/SetContext (the setters steal their reference and SetCause sets __suppress_context__, as CPython's do), SetTraceback, GetArgs, SetArgs and PyObject_VectorcallDict. (2) PyErr_Fetch returned a NULL traceback and PyErr_Restore dropped the one it was given, so an error a C function fetched and restored arrived without the frames it was raised in; Fetch now returns the exception's __traceback__ and Restore puts the given one back. (3) PyErr_SetObject/SetString/Restore with a type that is not an exception class raised TypeError; now SystemError `_PyErr_SetObject: exception <class 'int'> is not a BaseException subclass`, CPython's. (4) c/varargs.c: PyArg_ParseTupleAndKeywords ignored `$`, so keyword-only parameters took positional arguments (`varkw(1, 2.0, b'x', (), None, True)` with `idy#|O!O$p` returned instead of raising); positional arguments now stop at `$` and extra ones raise `varkw() takes at most 5 positional arguments (6 given)`. (5) types.rs: METH_METHOD|METH_FASTCALL|METH_KEYWORDS raised `state() uses calling convention 0x282, which the C API does not run yet`; invoke now takes the defining class (the C type for its methods, PyCMethod_New's class, none for module functions, which refuse METH_METHOD with SystemError) and passes it as PyCMethod's second argument. (6) Only nb_bool of tp_as_number reached Python, so a C type's nb_add was unreachable from `+` (`TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'Box' and 'NoneType'` instead of the ZeroDivisionError its slot raised); abi.rs's NumberMethods now has CPython's full 36-field layout and every binary slot becomes __op__ and __rop__ (the reflected one calls the slot with the operands swapped, as CPython's wrap_binaryfunc_r does), plus the in-place, unary, __int__, __float__, __index__ and ternary __pow__/__rpow__/__ipow__ slots. (7) module.rs: PyModule_GetDef searched the def-to-module map, which keeps only the latest module of a def, so after a second import of a multi-phase module PyType_GetModuleByDef on the first module's types failed (`No superclass of 'capicheck.Box' has the given module`); a module-to-def map answers it per module. Check output (natively with the debug nanocode-python, and in python.wasm through nanocode-ts's Bash host): before 17/25, failing a/varargs_keywords, b/PyErr_SetObject, b/PyErr_Fetch_Restore, b/type_slot_errors, c/module_state, c/second_import, c/module_from_spec, c/module_free; after 23/25, both. The two that stay are not the C API's: c/module_from_spec, since importlib.util.module_from_spec on a builtin module returns the module already in sys.modules (rustpython-vm's _imp.create_builtin looks there first, where CPython creates a fresh multi-phase module); c/module_free, since m_traverse, m_clear and m_free never run: a module's proxy is pinned and a type from PyType_FromModuleAndSpec is immortal and holds its module, so module state lives as long as the interpreter (CPython frees it only through its cycle collector). Unchanged, natively, before and after: msgpack's test/ 154 passed and 7 skipped, ujson's tests/test_ujson.py 476 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfail and markupsafe's tests 79 passed and 1 skipped (pytest replaced by a small runner, as before, since RustPython lacks `email` for importlib.metadata; it counts parametrized cases itself), regex's test_regex 101/101 and pyyaml's legacy suite 2609 tests after; in python.wasm markupsafe, msgpack, pyyaml (CSafeLoader), regex and ujson import their C modules and round-trip. python.wasm with the check compiled in: 28,651,673 bytes on master with the stubs, 28,666,375 after. Commands: `cargo build -j2 -p nanocode-python-cli` and `target/debug/nanocode-python driver.py`; nanocode-ts `NANOCODE_CC=<wasi-sdk clang> NANOCODE_PYTHON_SOURCE=<this tree> node output/build-python.mjs` and the driver run through `Bash.create` with that python.wasm; `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-python-capi -p nanocode-python --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/core/python-capi/{c/varargs.c,src/{abi.rs,api.rs,module.rs,types.rs}}.
- fix(python): a run refused for memory reports how much it held and how much it asked for at once, and the native shell says the limit and what to do (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 bug-fix wave). `Ran` gains `held: Held { bytes, asked }`: `host::State::over` records the bytes the run held beyond its start and the size of the allocation it refused (0 when the refusal came from crossing the ceiling at a refuel rather than from `VirtualMachine::reserve`), so a host can tell the model what happened instead of a bare 126. The native `python3` (shell.rs) now prints `python3: it held 48.0 MiB, past this shell's 48.0 MiB memory limit for one run; read and process the data in chunks (a file line by line, a batch of rows at a time) and write results out as you go instead of holding them all` (with `and asked for N MiB more` when one allocation was refused) and, for steps, `python3: it ran N steps, this shell's limit for one run; split the work into shorter runs that save their progress to a file and continue from it`, where it printed `it held more memory than this shell allows` and `it ran more steps than this shell allows`. nanocode-ts's python.wasm passes `held` through its response to the JavaScript host, which words its own message with the host's knobs. Reproducing check (nanocode-ts `output/limits/check.ts`, `Bash.create` over a MemoryFileSystem, 48 MiB `maxMemoryBytes`, python.wasm built from this tree with `NANOCODE_PYTHON_SOURCE`): before, `s = 'a ' * 30000000; s.split()`, an endless `x.append(str(len(x)))` and `json.loads` of 5,000,000 floats all answered `python3: it held more memory than this shell allows` (126); after, `it asked for 57.2 MiB at once while holding 0.0 MiB, past the 48.0 MiB ...`, `it held 48.0 MiB, past the 48.0 MiB ...` and `it held 48.0 MiB ...`, in 4-6, 631-659 and 241-286 ms as before (4, 1,868 and 372 ms on the first run of the old module). Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-python` (native) and the wasm32 release build of python.wasm through nanocode-ts's scripts/python.mjs pass; `cargo clippy --no-deps -p nanocode-python -- -D warnings` passes.
- perf(cli): `nanocode --version` and `-V` print from the C `main` before anything else runs: no argument parsing, allocator, runtime or psh probe (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: startup RSS against fx 0.0.16, which `--version` measures). Why: `run_with` handled `--version` inside `Cli::parse`, after `nanocode_psh::serve_if_requested` and `read_outputs_if_requested` had collected `std::env::args` (the first allocation, which maps a 4 MiB allocator segment through an 8 MiB reservation) and after the parser walked the static command tables; `perf record -e page-faults -d` of `--version` counted 27 anonymous, 10 .rodata and 8 .text faults in the binary, and strace showed the segment's mmap and two munmaps. What: `nanocode_sys::main!` on linux-gnu now passes argc and argv to `entry::prepare`, which keeps them in two atomics; `entry::only_argument_in(&[c"--version", c"-V"])` answers whether argv holds exactly one argument and it is one of those, and `entry::print` writes the line to fd 1 with write(2), retrying EINTR, so the version path neither allocates nor initializes std's stdout buffer. `run_with` starts with that check and prints `nanocode <version>\n`, the line `Cli::parse` printed, ignoring a failed write as `arguments::Error::exit` does, and returns success; every other argument list, and every other platform, goes through `Cli::parse` as before. Checked against master's build: `--version` and `-V` print the same line and exit 0, `--version | head -c 3` exits 0, `--version >&-` exits 0, `--version extra` still prints the version through the parser, `--help` is unchanged; strace of `--version`: 52 syscalls against 56, no 8 MiB mmap. Measured on dev-georgios at load about 40, `taskset -c 24-27`: `perf stat -r 30` of `--version` against the previous commit's build-cli output: user instructions 338.2k to 313.7k, kernel 1.445M to 1.235M, page faults 112 to 87; `/usr/bin/time` peak RSS 2,816 KB in all runs to 2,304-2,560 KB (master before the read-only data ordering: 3,328 KB). bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=startup,firstframe,oneshot --only=nc --rounds=1` under tools/netguard.sh, 20 rounds rotating master's build, the previous commit's build and this one: startup peak RSS median 3.25, 2.75 and 2.50 MB, startup CPU 0.82, 0.88, 0.85 ms; first-frame and one-shot rows move only within the BOLT training spread (one-shot peak 12.50, 10.75, 11.25 MB; first-frame RSS 12.16, 10.04, 10.25 MB; their CPU 6.67, 6.44, 6.51 and 6.71, 6.41, 6.30 ms). Reproduce: `strace -c nanocode --version` (no `mmap(NULL, 8388608` line) and `perf stat -e page-faults nanocode --version`. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys` native, wasm32-unknown-unknown, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl and aarch64-apple-darwin, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-sys --lib` and `-p nanocode-cli` (only master's warnings). Files: crates/core/sys/src/{entry.rs,lib.rs}, bin/nanocode/src/lib.rs.
- fix(tls): nanocode-tls builds against crates.io rustls again: the vendored rustls keeps the provider-facing API a provider must fill, inert, so one provider source compiles against both (2026-11-14, tempoxyz/pyramid's nanocode bump). Why: 4e5ee70ca (QUIC, secret extraction, FIPS) and d86704732 (FFDHE, DHE) cut `Tls13AeadAlgorithm::extract_keys`, `Tls12AeadAlgorithm::extract_keys`, `Tls13CipherSuite::quic` and `Tls12CipherSuite::kx` from the vendored rustls and the matching impls and fields from nanocode-tls's graviola provider, but `[patch.crates-io]` only reaches nanocode's own workspace: downstream (tempoxyz/pyramid, which needs crates.io rustls with ring for sqlx, kube and reqwest) builds nanocode-tls against crates.io rustls 0.23.46, where those methods are required and those fields must be initialised, and got 13 errors (4 missing `extract_keys`, 6 missing `kx`, 3 missing `quic`). The cuts were right to drop the behaviour; the mistake was dropping what an implementer must write, which a subset fork cannot do while downstream keeps upstream, as serde_json's trim ("every remaining API item is upstream's") already holds. What: the vendored rustls gets back `extract_keys` on both AEAD traits (required, upstream's signatures), `UnsupportedOperationError` (with its `Display`, `Error` and `From` for `Error`), `ConnectionTrafficSecrets` (`Aes128Gcm`, `Aes256Gcm`, `Chacha20Poly1305`, re-exported at the root), `Tls12CipherSuite::kx` with `crypto::KeyExchangeAlgorithm` (only `ECDHE`, `non_exhaustive`, so DHE stays unrepresentable) and `Tls13CipherSuite::quic` as `Option<Infallible>` (only `None` fits, so no QUIC module comes back); nothing in it reads them, so every connection is unchanged. nanocode-tls gets back its four `extract_keys` impls, `quic: None` and its six `kx: ECDHE` lines (4e5ee70ca's and d86704732's hunks); `ffdhe_group` and `fips` stay out, since crates.io rustls defaults them (`FfdheGroup::from_named_group` answers `None` for X25519, P-256, P-384 and X25519MLKEM768, `fips` false, what the removed impls returned). Checked: output/tls-crates-io, its own workspace with nanocode-tls by path and rustls =0.23.46 with `ring` and no nanocode `[patch]` (graviola 0.4.5 from crates.io, as downstream gets it), builds, and handshakes nanocode-tls's provider as client against a ring server for each of its 9 suites (3 TLS 1.3, 6 TLS 1.2, ECDSA and RSA leaves under one CA), then compares `dangerous_extract_secrets` both ways: 9 of 9 suites agree with ring's keys and IVs, so the restored `extract_keys` are correct where they run. Control: the same harness against master's nanocode-tls fails with the 13 errors. Downstream: tempoxyz/pyramid at its bump (nanocode a5d401e0c) with every nanocode git package patched to this checkout and no nanocode-tls compat patch, `cargo +1.99.0 check --manifest-path backend/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets` passes (crates.io rustls 0.23.46 with ring beside nanocode-tls). Commands: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` (only master's two unused workspace dependency warnings); `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tls -p rustls`, and `-p nanocode-tls` for wasm32-unknown-unknown; `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-tls` (nothing in touched files); nanocode-sim release `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 300 2` with no scenario and with `--scenario egress` (the egress proxy serves TLS through the vendored rustls): SWEEP passed=300 failed=0, panics=0 each. Files: crates/patches/rustls/src/{crypto/cipher.rs,crypto/mod.rs,lib.rs,msgs/handshake.rs,suites.rs,tls12/mod.rs,tls13/mod.rs}, crates/core/tls/src/provider/{aead.rs,suites.rs}.
- fix(process): a PTY command's output drain waits for each chunk's delivery by parking its blocking thread (`nanocode_sync::block_on`, now public) instead of `nanocode_executor::Handle::current().block_on` (2026-11-14, tempoxyz/pyramid's nanocode bump). Why: `drain_blocking` took the current nanocode runtime's handle before spawning its blocking reader, so under a host that installs a `nanocode_platform::Host` and runs no nanocode runtime (tempoxyz/pyramid's Hand, whose Host is tokio) every tty `exec_command` panicked with "there is no reactor running, must be called from the context of a nanocode runtime"; it was the last "left for the executor steps" item of the platform refactor. The wait needs no runtime: `Sender::send` is `Actor::run`, an unbounded send to the capture's owning task (spawned through the platform `Handle`, so on the host) and a oneshot reply, so a thread-park waker is all it needs, and the owning task runs wherever the host runs it. Without a host nothing changes in effect: the reader is on a blocking-pool thread, where a multi-thread runtime's `block_on` already parked (`park_on`). What: crates/integrations/process/src/output.rs drops the handle and calls `nanocode_sync::block_on(chunks.send(..))`; nanocode-sync exports its existing `blocking::block_on` (native only, as `blocking_send` and `blocking_recv` that use it). Checked: output/process-host installs a Host that spawns onto a nanocode runtime it never enters, chooses /bin/bash as the shell, and drives `ShellSessions::execute` of 20 tty commands (`printf pty-N-ok`) from a plain thread with `nanocode_sync::block_on`: 20 of 20 return their output and exit 0; with master's output.rs the first command panics with the message above. Downstream, with the same patched checkout: tempoxyz/pyramid's `cargo +1.99.0 test --manifest-path hands/Cargo.toml control` (14 passed) and `--test transport` (12 passed). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-sync`, again for wasm32-unknown-unknown; `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-sync` (nothing in touched files); `nanocode-sim --tidy` reports the same 6 lines as master; `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 300 2 --scenario sync`: SWEEP passed=300 failed=0. Files: crates/integrations/process/src/output.rs, crates/core/sync/src/{lib.rs,blocking.rs}.
- fix(code-mode): a recovered exec observation is not preempted by steering, and the sub-agent resume note says a result the history shows is real (2026-11-14, forward-port of 4ced7cd74 from backport/recovered-exec-6cde8f5, which tempoxyz/pyramid pins). Why: as that commit's entry says, a host that moves a turn recovers the exec observing a cell, the sub-agent runtime steers the replayed turn with its resume note at once, and the steer cut the recovered observation after about 0.1 s with only "Script running with cell ID 1" while its cell still waited on a long command; the note then called that call's result unknown, and agents gave up on or repeated commands that finished minutes later. Master had since split `ObservationMode` into `Started(yield, Preemption)` and `YieldAfter(yield, quiet_until, Preemption)`, so the commit did not apply: `YieldAfter` now carries `Option<Preemption>`, `recover_with_updates` builds no `Preemption` and passes `None` (it waits until its cell ends or its yield time runs out; `quiet_until` equals the yield there, so no quiet hold), and `exec`'s wait path passes `Some`; `Started` is unchanged. A steer that arrives meanwhile is read at the next model step. The session notice (a background Bash job ending) still ends a recovered observation, as it ends any. durable.rs's `in_flight_evidence` and `RESUME_MESSAGE` take 4ced7cd74's wording unchanged. Checked from the host: tempoxyz/pyramid `subagent_cells_tests::a_steer_waits_for_the_recovered_cell_of_a_moved_subagent` passes against this checkout, and fails against it with master's code_mode/mod.rs ("the steer cut the recovered exec short: Script running with cell ID 1 / Wall time 0.1 seconds"). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-subagents`, again for wasm32-unknown-unknown; `cargo clippy --locked --lib` of both (nothing in touched files); `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 300 2 --scenario runtime` and `--scenario agents`: SWEEP passed=300 failed=0, panics=0 each. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/mod.rs, crates/runtime/subagents/src/durable.rs.
- fix(rustls): the vendored rustls is brought up to 0.23.46 (2026-11-14). What: the two 0.23.46 changes that touch code the trimmed copy still has. `Tls13ClientSessionValue`, `ClientSessionCommon` and `ServerSessionValue` get 0.23.46's hand-written `Debug` impls, which leave out the session secret and the master secret (the trimmed structs lack `max_early_data_size` and `freshness`, so those fields are left out of the impls too); the TLS 1.3 client carries the server's key-exchange group through its handshake states (`kx_group`) and calls `set_kx_hint` in `ExpectFinished`, after the server's Finished is verified, rather than on the ServerHello. 0.23.46's other changes are in code this copy no longer has (ECH, certificate decompression). Version set to 0.23.46 in crates/patches/rustls and Cargo.lock. Swapping in stock 0.23.46 is not an option: nanocode-tls builds against the trimmed API. Checks: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` (only master's two unused workspace dependency warnings); `cargo check --locked --lib -p rustls -p nanocode-tls` natively and for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (only master's nanocode-sys `getsockopt` warning) and aarch64-apple-darwin; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tls --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; nanocode-sim built in release, `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 300 2` gives SWEEP passed=300 failed=0, panics=0, and with `--scenario streams` passed=300 failed=0 (142 TLS runs, 70 of them TLS 1.2).
- perf(store-jsonl): `nanocode sessions` and `exec --continue` list a session store from a `.listing` index of its session files instead of reading the directory and stat-ing every file, for as long as the directory's mtime still equals the stamp the index ends with; and the summaries cache is dropped once the process reads or acquires a session (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: sessions at 14,600 against fx). Why: on the 14,600-session bench store (~/wave/stores/nc, 14,600 `.jsonl.zst` and 14,600 `.owner` files) `perf record -e instructions:k` of `nanocode sessions` put 39% of its kernel instructions in getdents64 (ext4's htree readdir hashes and sorts all 29,200 names), 30% in page faults and 20% in one statx per session file, which the listing needed only to check the `.summaries` cache (dev:ino and length) and order sessions by birth time; and `--continue` kept the 11 MB summaries base and its 14,600 entries alive through the whole turn. What: sessions/.listing holds one line per session file (birth time in ns, length, dev:ino, name) and ends with a stamp line (the directory's dev:ino and mtime in ns). A listing trusts it only when the file ends in a stamp equal to the directory's current dev:ino and mtime and its appended lines are no longer than its snapshot; it then stats only plain `.jsonl` files (appends never touch the directory) and, in `newest_summaries`, the sessions the page shows, and rescans when any of them differs. Otherwise it scans as before under an exclusive flock on the directory: before the scan it sets the directory's mtime to a fresh nanosecond value and reads it back (a filesystem that truncates it gets no index), after it checks the mtime is unchanged, writes the snapshot by rename and sets a second fresh mtime that the snapshot's stamp names. Each change this build makes to the directory (restoring, creating, compacting and archiving a session file, creating an owner file, rewriting `.summaries`) runs under the same lock and, only when the directory's mtime equalled the index's stamp right before, appends the changed files' lines and a new stamp and sets the mtime to it; under a held lock or a broken chain it only makes its change, and the next listing rescans. Why it holds: a create, rename or unlink by any other process (an older build, another tool) sets the directory's mtime to a kernel timestamp, which never equals a stamp this build chose, so the next listing rescans; `.jsonl.zst` files are only ever written by rename, so their identity and length change only with the directory; the one change it cannot see is a foreign create, rename or unlink that lands inside one of this build's locked changes (between its mtime check and its new stamp, the span of one archive or restore), and even then the shown sessions are stat-ed and a mismatch rescans. Older builds ignore `.listing` (neither a session nor a temporary name) and never read the directory's mtime. `clear` skips its temporaries pass when the index is current, since the scan that wrote it cleared them and every later change was recorded. `Summaries::forget` drops the cache on `read_record(s)` and `opened`, so `--continue` frees it as it loads the chosen session; a later listing reloads it. Reproducing check (run against master 090bb095f and this build, both BOLT builds of scripts/build-cli.sh, on copies of ~/wave/stores/nc): ~/wave/sess-tools/check.sh and check2.sh on dev-georgios print `nanocode sessions --limit 20000`, `sessions` and `sessions --all --limit 100000` of master and this build (age column cut) byte-identical on the fresh store, on the indexed store, after this build's `exec --continue`, after master's `exec --continue` on a store this build indexed, after a new session from each build, and after a session's `.zst` is replaced by another's with the directory's mtime then reset to the index's stamp (the shown-session check catches it); `strace -c` of an indexed listing shows 0 getdents64 and 117 statx (master: 62 getdents64, 14,610 statx). Measured on dev-georgios (32 threads, load about 55), taskset -c 28-29, A/B interleaved over 25 rounds (sess-tools/ab.mjs: perf stat and /usr/bin/time, each binary on its own store copy, `sessions` then `exec --continue` each round), medians [p25, p75], master -> this build: `sessions` kernel instructions 164.6M [159.4, 165.0] -> 42.6M [36.6, 43.0], user 372.1M -> 375.3M, task-clock 97.1 [95.3, 99.4] -> 67.2 [64.9, 68.2] ms, peak RSS 31.5 -> 32.3 MB; `exec --continue` kernel 183.6M [182.4, 184.9] -> 63.2M [62.2, 64.4], task-clock 120.2 [116.9, 123.2] -> 84.6 [83.5, 90.6] ms, peak RSS 42.0 [41.5, 42.3] -> 35.5 [35.5, 36.0] MB. bench/cli `BENCH_PERF=1 tools/netguard.sh taskset -c 28-29 node harness/suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nc,fx --sessions=14600 --storerounds=20` on fresh copies of ~/wave/stores, nc vs fx 0.0.16 (store-list / store-resume medians): master kernel 165.8M / 176.7M vs fx 98.4M / 103.9M, task-clock 108.4 / 122.9 vs 75.0 / 77.7 ms, wall 218.6 / 252.6 vs 153.3 / 191.1 ms, peak RSS 31.8 / 41.0 vs 33.2 / 34.6 MB; this build kernel 37.4M / 57.9M vs 98.1M / 103.9M, task-clock 72.0 / 86.4 vs 73.5 / 77.7 ms, wall 152.4 / 198.8 vs 155.1 / 181.0 ms, peak RSS 32.4 / 34.3 vs 33.2 / 34.6 MB. `exec --continue` still trails fx by about 9 ms of CPU: the rest is user time (407M instructions against fx's 507M at a lower IPC), most of it parsing the 11 MB summaries base, which this change does not touch. Validated with cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-store-jsonl and cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-store-jsonl, native and wasm32-unknown-unknown (where the crate is empty).
- perf(turnlog): `Lease::commit` moves the written row body into its stored rows instead of copying it (2026-11-14, Georgios: at most 2 KB of parent memory per finished child). `stored` built each row with `to_owned` or `format!` from a borrowed snapshot, boundary or records body, so a snapshot commit held the packed snapshot twice until the host's append returned. `stored` now takes the body: a body that fits one row becomes that row, and a body split into parts copies the later parts behind `PART` and truncates the body to its first part. A sampling heap profile of the wasm module (32 KB sampling allocator, stacks from the host, 2K in-object score run at 113.1 MB peak) showed the growth that set the peak during a snapshot append, with the 5.52 MB packed snapshot, a 5.52 MB `stored` copy and an 11.03 MB JSON encoding of the append live at once. Native, `output/memprobe` (counting allocator) on the 10K-child parent log, first snapshot commit after `TurnLog::open`, 2 interleaved rounds against 67319a5a7 with identical bytes each round: commit peak 30,077,487 -> 20,222,669 bytes (one 9,854,820 byte snapshot fewer), commit 713/730 -> 571/617 ms, same snapshot bytes and held memory. nanocode-sim turns/turnlog: --twice 0..2000 2000/2000, --calm --row-limit 1024 1000/1000, --twice --snapshot-ratio 1 1000/1000, --twice --row-limit 4096 --snapshot-rows 4 1000/1000, --long 100 200/200, seal_skipped caught 107/200.
- perf(turnlog): `SqlLog` moves the bodies out of the SQL host's answer instead of cloning them, in `load` and `scan` (2026-11-14, Georgios: at most 2 KB of parent memory per finished child). `row` cloned each body from the borrowed answer, so `TurnLog::open` held every loaded row twice until the answer was dropped: 42,140,106 bytes of bodies twice for the 5,414 rows of the 10K-child parent log in ~/w/lanes/restart2/data/do10k-rows.jsonl. `row` now takes the cells by value. Checked with cargo clippy -p nanocode-turnlog and the 10K turn scenario of durable-cloudflare scripts/hillclimb.mjs (see the memory lane's LAND.md).
- fix(turnlog): `Fold::garbage` follows chunk manifests, so `TurnLog::open` collects unreachable stored records in logs that hold chunked payloads (2026-11-14, Georgios: at most 2 KB of parent memory per finished child). A reached value that was not an inline payload (`=`) made `garbage` give up and collect nothing, and a nanocode-ts parent always holds a few chunk manifests (`%`, `^`), so open collected 0 of the 50,434 unreachable records of a 10K-child parent (superseded registry pages, deltas and session records, 29.2 MB of keys and values). The new `EncodedPayload::assembled` returns an inline payload's JSON or joins a manifest's chunks (looked up in the same state) and nested manifests, and returns None for any other or incomplete record, where `garbage` still gives up. The walk visits each content once and scans one holder's value, since every holder of a content key holds the same content (it walked every holder per reference: 16 s at 10K). Collection stays at open only: a live durable session skips staging records in its `committed_records`, so dropping one while it runs could leave a later checkpoint pointing at nothing. Measured with output/memprobe on ~/w/lanes/restart2/data/do10k-rows.jsonl (2 interleaved rounds against the previous commit, memory identical every round): held after open 129,807,235 -> 95,614,686 bytes, records collected 0 -> 50,434, next snapshot 128,206,759 -> 94,746,934 plain and 18,112,901 -> 9,854,820 packed bytes, its commit 1,352-1,537 -> 784-875 ms and commit peak 54,851,728 -> 30,077,487 bytes; open 866-873 -> 1,276-1,420 ms (the walk, on a host at load 10). Every checkpoint's references, read per state through `EncodedPayload::read`, resolve to the same 69,602 records (57,711,719 bytes) before and after, with the same 19 unresolved references the log already had.
- perf(turnlog): `codec::History` keeps at most one deflate window, and `Fold::load` applies each record as it decodes it (2026-11-14, Georgios: at most 2 KB of parent memory per finished child). `History::extend` appended the whole plain row and then drained it to `WINDOW`, so after `TurnLog::open` folded a snapshot row the history kept a capacity of the whole snapshot (128 MB for a 10K-child parent). It now drains and appends only the last `WINDOW` bytes of the row. `Fold::load` collected a row's records into a `Vec<Record>` before applying them (one more copy of the snapshot's records while it was folded); `record::each` streams them and `decode` uses it. Measured with output/memprobe (a counting allocator around `TurnLog::open` over a `MemoryLog` of ~/w/lanes/restart2/data/do10k-rows.jsonl, the parent log of a 10K-child turn run; 2 interleaved rounds against b605ff2bf, memory identical every round): held after open 257,901,855 -> 129,807,235 bytes, open peak 520,187,544 -> 263,998,304 bytes, open 1,014-1,020 -> 750-845 ms; the next snapshot is byte-identical (digest d8c0b7922047ca94, 18,112,901 packed bytes).

- perf(events): a coalesced text delta reaches `nc exec`'s printer and the terminal interface as a typed value beside its JSON payload, and the Responses client borrows a plain delta string instead of parsing it twice (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: bench/cli user-space cost per streamed token). Why: perf record -e instructions:u of `nc exec` at 10,000 tok/s (50,000 tokens, one published `assistant.delta` per token at that rate) put 13.7% of user instructions in the printer, 12.2% of them `serde_json::from_str::<Payload>` of the delta payload the publisher had just encoded, 16.6% in publishing (the payload encode) and 18.5% in `decode_wire_event`; output/tokbench (the same serde_json patches, fat LTO) measured 2,520 instructions to parse one 133-byte delta payload in the printer, 2,990 to encode it and 2,920 to decode the SSE event, about 17 to 22 per byte, so each token paid three JSON passes of about 2.5k to 3k instructions each. What: `TimedAgentEvent` (doc-hidden) gains `delta: Option<SharedTextDelta>`, set only by `EventChannel::publish_pending`, the one place a coalesced `assistant.delta`, `reasoning.summary.delta` or `tool.input.delta` is published; `SharedTextDelta` (doc-hidden) holds the same fields as the payload's `TextDeltaRef` with `Arc<str>` strings and `borrowed()` gives the `TextDeltaRef`, which `encode_payload` serializes as before, so the payload bytes and `AgentEvent` are unchanged and every other subscriber still reads JSON. `PendingDelta` keeps its item, call and tool ids as `Arc<str>`, so a published delta adds one allocation (the text) and reuses its pending buffer. `stream_turn` reads `Turn::events` through `try_recv_timed`/`recv_timed` and `Printer::event` takes the delta and only parses the payload when there is none; the TUI's `next_agent_event`, `next_buffered_event`, held event and `EventMapper::apply` carry it the same way (`text_payload` falls back to the payload), the focus and side views pass `None`, and `EventMapper::assistant` inserts a reply's call only when it changed instead of allocating its key on every delta. In crates/backends/codex/client/src/tower/stream.rs `required_text` returns the inside of a delta's `RawValue` when it is a JSON string with no backslash or control byte, which is exactly its decoded value, and otherwise parses it as before. Checked with a node script on bench/cli harness/fakellm.mjs (`nc exec --ephemeral`, master against this build): a 3,000-token stream with an escaped `\n\n` every 40 tokens, 500 tokens at 2,000 tok/s, a one-word reply and 50 blob chunks of 300 bytes gave byte-identical stdout (16,965, 2,403, 6 and 15,001 bytes) and stderr; the two-step tool turn's stderr differs only in the fixture's retry jitter (2.0 s against 2.1 s) on both sides; sweep.mjs --mode=tui showed every token (missing 0, max token 2,999 and 29,999) on both. Measured with scripts/build-cli.sh builds (dist, BOLT 21; master 778e5ad4a against a5d401e0c plus this change, whose base only drops the Codex developer block), bench/cli sweep.mjs under tools/netguard.sh, pinned to 4 CPUs at load 35 to 75, lanes interleaved per sample, each run under perf stat; medians [p25, p75]: --mode=cli at 10,000 tok/s (12 samples) user instructions 860.0M [850.6, 870.4] to 748.8M [744.8, 756.3] (fx 0.0.16 673.8M), user cycles 775M [756, 793] to 739M [699, 798] (fx 548M), task-clock 517.6 to 521.0 ms (fx 490.9, within the load's spread); at 1,000 tok/s (16 samples) user instructions 97.5M [97.0, 98.5] to 86.4M [85.7, 86.7] (fx 71.0M), user cycles 147.2M to 153.6M with IQRs [136, 161] and [140, 160], task-clock 100.9 to 107.4 ms (fx 95.5); the first variant of this change (an `Arc<TextDeltaRef<'static>>` with owned strings, three allocations per delta) gave 764.9M and 87.6M, and at 100 tok/s (20 samples) 17.4M to 16.4M (fx 11.1M). --mode=tui: at 1,000 tok/s (8 samples) user instructions 385.5M to 375.5M, tree CPU 204 [193, 217] to 189 [182, 200] ms (fx 317); at 10,000 tok/s (12 samples) 979.1M to 915.3M, user cycles 829M to 802M, tree CPU 541.7 [467, 646] to 535.8 [492, 629] ms, lag p50 5.50 to 6.29 ms with overlapping IQRs. Gates, suite.mjs --parts=firstframe,idle,oneshot --rounds=20: first frame 19.53 [17.46, 22.58] to 19.89 [17.50, 22.17] ms, its CPU 6.78 to 6.50 ms, RSS 12.09 to 11.93 MB; idle CPU 0 both; one-shot CPU 7.80 [7.27, 8.08] to 7.55 [6.90, 8.60] ms, peak RSS 12.50 MB both. Not reached: fx's user instructions; the payload is still encoded once per delta (about 3k instructions) because `AgentEvent::payload` is public, and the SSE event's own parse is about 2.6k. Commands: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-types` and `-p nanocode-backend-codex-client`, both again with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-types -p nanocode-cli -p nanocode-backend-codex-client` (only master's warnings), `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed hunks. Files: crates/core/types/src/events/stream.rs, crates/core/types/src/events/mod.rs, crates/backends/codex/client/src/tower/stream.rs, bin/nanocode/src/lib.rs, bin/nanocode/src/stream.rs, bin/nanocode/src/app.rs, bin/nanocode/src/events.rs, bin/nanocode/src/focus.rs, bin/nanocode/src/side.rs.
- fix(code-mode): a hand tool selection that admits every tool of the hand sends none, so it needs no hand support, and the Claude backend exports `HAND_TOOLS`, the Claude Code tools a hand runs (Bash, Edit, Read, TaskOutput, TaskStop, Write) (2026-11-14, Terminal-Bench 2.1 Codex parity, wave 4). A codex session on a nanocode hand saw the hand's Claude Code tools in its cell: in nanoeval's gateway e2e lane (nanocode-ts build-67dea25, hand nanocode-cli-0bbcb64) `ALL_TOOLS` of a codex cell was apply_patch, exec_command, view_image, write_stdin, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, TaskStop, hands, and a gpt-6-luna trace called `tools.Bash` 13 times, while codex-cli offers only its own tools. nanocode-ts now gives every session a hand tool selection whose `codex` entry, when the host names none, excludes `HAND_TOOLS`; `RemoteCodeModeHost::selected_tools` returns no selection when the selection keeps every tool of the hand (a Claude session), so such a session neither sends a selection nor fails on a hand that cannot select tools (one with dynamic providers), and only a selection that drops a tool requires hand support. `ClaudeToolPolicy` routes files by the same constant. The hand is unchanged: the CLI hand has taken per-session selections since cd09093fb, so nanocode-cli-0bbcb64 runs it. Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings` for both; nanoeval's gateway e2e lane, which now asserts a codex cell's `ALL_TOOLS`, fails before and passes after (see nanocode-ts and nanoeval DECISIONS). Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/remote/mod.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/{code_mode_policy,lib}.rs.
- fix(python): the Python files of the packages whose C modules are compiled in are frozen into python3, so `import markupsafe`, `import msgpack`, `import yaml` (and the legacy `_yaml`) and `import regex` work in python.wasm and natively with no files on disk (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 bug-fix wave). Before, only the C modules (`markupsafe._speedups`, `msgpack._cmsgpack`, `yaml._yaml`, `regex._regex`) were built in: their packages' Python wrappers were never shipped, every earlier check copied them from the wheels onto sys.path, and a plain `import markupsafe` failed with `No module named 'markupsafe'`, which the import scan (`_missing` in boot.py) reports as a missing package, so nanocode-ts's host sent the run to Pyodide or failed. crates/core/python/site holds each package's Python files as released (markupsafe 3.0.4 `src/markupsafe/{__init__,_native}.py`, msgpack 1.2.4 `msgpack/*.py`, pyyaml 6.0.3 `lib/yaml/*.py` and `lib/_yaml/__init__.py`, regex 2026.11.9 `regex/*.py`, from the PyPI sdists with their published SHA-256 checked), each with its license file (BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, MIT, Apache-2.0 with CNRI-Python; byte-identical to the ones beside the C sources in python-capi/ext); `Python::new` adds them with `rustpython_vm::py_freeze!(dir = "../site")` after the frozen stdlib, the same way rustpython-pylib freezes Lib, so the FrozenImporter answers them before the path finder, the scan counts them as present, and they stay in sys.modules across runs as the stdlib does. build.rs reruns on changes under site, since the proc macro reads files that rustc's dep-info does not list. ujson ships no Python files. kiwisolver's `_cext` is not compiled in, so nothing is added for it. Reproducing check, nanocode-ts's Bash API with WebAssembly compilation disabled as in a Worker (`WORKER=1 node output/markupsafe.ts <python.wasm>`) on `python3 -c 'import markupsafe; print(markupsafe.escape("<a>"), markupsafe._speedups)'`: master (e525ef15f) `python3: markupsafe: No module named 'markupsafe' (this simulated shell has no Python packages, only the standard library)`, exit 127 (and the same for msgpack, yaml, regex, _yaml); this tree `&lt;a&gt; <module 'markupsafe._speedups' (built-in)>`, exit 0, `markupsafe._escape_inner is markupsafe._speedups._escape_inner` True, msgpack packs with `msgpack._cmsgpack`, `yaml.__with_libyaml__` True with CSafeLoader, `regex.findall(r"\p{L}+", ...)` through `regex._regex`; the native debug nanocode-python prints the same. python.wasm (nanocode-ts build, wasm-opt -Oz, baked) 28,636,681 to 28,937,636 bytes (+300,955). Interleaved, 15 rounds each on this shared 5-core Hand at load 4.8, master then this tree, ms: compile minimum 10.0 and 10.1, median 18.9 and 20.1; first `print(1)` run with instantiation minimum 14.2 and 14.7, median 23.5 and 50.3; a json, re and Counter script minimum 2.7 and 2.7, median 3.4 and 10.1 (the medians move with the machine's load between rounds; the minima are equal). First import in a fresh instance: markupsafe 20 ms, msgpack 15 ms, yaml 100 ms, regex 56 ms, then under 3 ms. Commands: `cargo build -j2 --offline -p nanocode-python-cli`, `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-python --no-deps -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/core/python/{build.rs,src/lib.rs,site/**}.
- fix(claude): a successful Bash result carries `"is_error": false` on the wire, as Claude Code 2.1.300 sends it, and every other tool still omits the key on success (2026-11-14, Claude harness tool parity). Stock request bodies from output/b6-tools (mock.py scenario `cwd`: seven Bash calls, one `exit 3`) show `is_error: false` on the six successful Bash results and `true` on the failure, while Read, Edit, Write, WebFetch and TaskStop results omit the key unless they fail. What: `ContentBlock::ToolResult::is_error` is `Option<bool>`, serialized only when `Some`, so a stored `false` survives the durable history and tool receipts; `tool_result`, `tool_result_content` and `tool_result_blocks` keep their `bool` parameter and store `Some(true)` or `None`; `call_tool` stores `Some(is_error)` for Bash and for any failure, and `None` otherwise; the ToolSearch discovery and companion separation in agent.rs read `Some(true)` as the error. Measured with output/b6-tools (`run.py cwd` on vercel/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, last request's tool_result blocks against stock with the run directory masked): master e525ef15f 1/7 equal (only the failure), this build 7/7; `run.py unread` keeps the key off the 10 Read, Edit and Write results and sends `false` on its first Bash. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client -p nanocode-backend-claude` (no warnings), `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` for the mock runs. Files: crates/backends/claude/client/src/lib.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent.rs.
- feat(sim): `--scenario streams` (bin/nanocode-sim/src/streams.rs) drives today's nanocode-io, nanocode-executor and nanocode-tls code under the deterministic executor, with seeded pipes that take short reads and writes, fill to a capacity, return spurious Pending (self-woken) and close (2026-11-14). Workloads per seed: `nanocode_io::copy` from a producer (write_all, write, write_vectored, flush, shutdown) through an optional BufReader into one of nine consumers (read_to_end with a prefix, BufReader read_until, read_line, lines, read_exact then EOF, take, fill_buf/consume, read_buf, read_to_string); an echo through `nanocode_io::split` halves (with `is_pair_of`) and an optional BufReader; `copy_bidirectional` as a proxy with both sides half-closing; a JoinSet of 1 to 12 tasks spawned through `nanocode_platform::spawn_joined`, `spawn_task` + `push` on the installed simulated host (executor `spawn_with`), with platform sleeps, `timeout`, panics (`resume_unwind`, so no hook output), aborts at planned times and a dropped set; and, unix only, `nanocode_tls::connect`/`accept` (TLS 1.3, or 1.2 ECDHE-ECDSA) over the egress self-signed CA, both sides split and exchanging up to 40 kB each with close_notify. Invariants: progress (the run finishes), copy_exact, echo_exact, proxy_exact (bytes and returned counts), joined_once, join_len, joined_output (cancelled exactly when the abort came before the task returned, else its value or panic payload), abort_drops (a dropped set's unfinished futures are dropped within one settle), timeout_verdict (elapsed exactly when the inner sleep is longer than the limit), tls_exact. Mutations, each in the fuzzer table as a canary, caught over seeds 0..2000: drop_pipe_byte 1998, early_eof 1992, skip_wake (lost reader wake) 1999, drop_spawned (host drops a JoinSet task) 1450, corrupt_tls_byte 913 (TLS runs in half the seeds). TLS pipes hold at least 4608 bytes (Linux SOCK_MIN_SNDBUF): with both directions smaller than a few bytes, rustls' `wants_read()` (false while TLS bytes wait to be sent during the handshake) deadlocks both handshakes, which happened in 8 of the first 1000 seeds and is upstream rustls/tokio-rustls behaviour no real socket reaches. The digest covers only verified outcomes, and TLS runs on its own executor after the plain run, since its handshake bytes come from graviola's real random source. Found the FillBuf panic fixed above. Sweeps (sweep.sh, 3 jobs, every pass row of cfo.sh's table): store_content, store_slots, agents, the five turns rows, websocket, http_server, egress, mpp, sync and their `--twice` rows 5000 seeds each; runtime memory/kv/kv-calm/kv-http/memory-http 2000 each and the three runtime `--twice` rows 1000 each (all failing on master before the subagents clock fix); streams and streams `--twice` 10000 each; alloc and alloc `--twice` 1000 each: every row failed=0, panics=0. Checks: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-sim` (only the two existing alloc.rs warnings), `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean.
- fix(sim): tidy's allowance for `nanocode_executor::Handle` in crates/runtime/durability/src/shared_store.rs counts the 2 uses ec5bfb41f left (the `OnceLock<Option<Handle>>` and `Handle::try_current()`), both on the path without a host after `spawn_driver` has handed its driver to an installed one (2026-11-14). `nanocode-sim --tidy` failed on master with "2 uses of nanocode_executor::Handle where the allowance counts 1"; with this and the subagents and hedge clock fixes it prints `TIDY determinism: clean`.
- fix(agent): hedged first-byte requests (`Hedging::race`, crates/core/agent/src/hedge.rs) time the primary's and the hedge's first bytes with `nanocode_platform::now()` instead of `Instant::now()` and `elapsed()` (2026-11-14, `nanocode-sim --tidy`). Why: 1d4463636 timed them on the wall clock while sleeping the hedge deadline on the platform host; the recorded first-byte times set later hedge deadlines, so a host with its own clock (the simulator) mixed wall time into its runs. `--tidy` flagged hedge.rs:170 and 198. Checks: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-agent-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-agent-core` (no warnings).
- fix(subagents): the root's completion batching window (`completion_deadline`, `record_completion_wake` and `continue_root` in crates/runtime/subagents/src/runtime.rs) reads `nanocode_platform::now()` instead of `std::time::Instant::now()` (2026-11-14, nanocode-sim runtime `--twice`). Why: a2662527d measured the window on the wall clock but sleeps it through the platform host, so a host with its own clock (the simulator, any embedder) slept `host deadline - wall now`: under the simulator a sub-millisecond, wall-time-dependent delay that made every runtime `--twice` configuration nondeterministic. `nanocode-sim --tidy` flagged runtime.rs:6754, 6759 and 9679. Before (master 778e5ad4a): `--scenario runtime --store memory --twice` failed on 7 of seeds 0..20, kv and kv/http on 3 of the first 10, e.g. seed 3 diverging at `57225910569 model r0 steps 2` vs `58167569431`. After: memory and kv `--twice` 40/40, and the sweeps in the sim commit. Checks: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-subagents --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-subagents` (no warnings).
- fix(io): `FillBuf` (crates/core/io/src/ext.rs) returns an empty first fill as the end of the stream instead of polling the reader a second time (2026-11-14, nanocode-sim streams scenario). Why: to hand out a slice with the reader's lifetime without unsafe, FillBuf polls `poll_fill_buf` twice and called a Pending second poll unreachable; when the first poll is empty (end of stream), BufReader's second poll goes back to the inner reader, which may return Pending (legal for any AsyncRead) or fresh bytes, so `fill_buf().await` panicked with "a filled buffer stays filled" at the end of a stream whose reader does not repeat its EOF on the very next poll. A non-empty first fill still takes the second poll, which BufReader and Take answer from their buffer. Found by the streams scenario's FillBuf consumer: 9 of seeds 0..200 panicked before (41, 46, 54, 65, 66, 95, 99, 108, 122), none after. Checks: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`, `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-io --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-io` (no warnings), `nanocode-sim --scenario streams` over 10000 seeds (sweep.sh, passed).
- feat(cli): `python3` and `python` in nanocode's shell run nanocode-python on Windows, from nanocode-python.exe beside nanocode.exe (2026-11-14, Windows release lane). Why: f4a02a256 left the utility out on Windows (`SHELL_UTILITIES` empty there) because bin/nanocode/src/python.rs used Unix-only std APIs, so the nanocode-python.exe the Windows zip ships was unreachable from a session. What: python.rs builds on every native target: arguments and environment go from psh's bytes to an OsString (as they are on Unix, lossily as UTF-8 on Windows, where psh keeps UTF-8), argv[0] is set only on Unix (`CommandExt::arg0` is Unix-only), a status without a code is 128 plus the signal on Unix and 1 on Windows, and the executable bit is set only on Unix; the program found beside nanocode and the downloaded one carry `EXE_SUFFIX`. nanocode-compression (the xz decoder for the download) moves from nanocode-cli's Unix dependencies to its native ones; Cargo.lock is unchanged. Unix behavior is the same code. Checked: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` (master's warnings), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-cli` (master's one needless_borrow), `cargo check --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p nanocode-cli -p nanocode-python-cli --bins` and the aarch64-pc-windows-msvc dist build of the release commit, which includes this change. Not run on Windows here: output/winrelease-probe.yml runs `psh-shell -c "python3 -c 'print(6*7)'"` as a non-blocking step.
- build(release): Windows is a release target: scripts/release-cli.sh builds x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-pc-windows-msvc and publishes `nanocode-<triple>.zip` (nanocode.exe and nanocode-python.exe) in SHA256SUMS beside the macOS and Linux files, and install.ps1 installs them as install does on Unix (2026-11-14, Windows release lane). Why: since f4a02a256 and 579a6a2ba nanocode and nanocode-python build and run on Windows, but the release had no Windows files and no installer. What: build-cli.sh gains a `*-windows-msvc` arm that builds nanocode-python.exe and then the binary with the same remapped paths as the macOS arm (no BOLT, no digest: the Windows nanocode finds nanocode-python.exe beside itself, it never downloads it) and prints the `.exe` path; on a Windows host rustc and clang find MSVC themselves, off Windows it needs `NANOCODE_XWIN`, a directory from `xwin splat`, and links with `LLD_LINK` (default lld-link), exporting INCLUDE for the C compiler and passing the CRT and SDK library directories with -Lnative; paths go through cygpath -m when it exists, so remapping works under Git Bash. release-cli.sh stages each triple under target/release-cli/windows, zips it after the gzip and xz loop (so the zips are not compressed again) and adds the zips and install.ps1 to SHA256SUMS and to --publish. The zip holds no nc.exe, as the release holds no nc: install.ps1 (`irm .../install.ps1 | iex`) picks the triple from the OS architecture, verifies the zip against SHA256SUMS, skips the download when .nanocode.sha256 matches, moves the running files aside (Windows can rename an executable that runs but not overwrite it), hard-links nc.exe to nanocode.exe (a copy where links fail) and adds the bin directory to the user PATH unless NANOCODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH is set; NANOCODE_RELEASE and NANOCODE_BIN work as in install. ARM64: nanocode-cli and nanocode-python-cli build for aarch64-pc-windows-msvc with no source change: graviola's aarch64 assembly never names x18 (Windows' TEB register) and its `adrp`/`:lo12:` relocations assemble for COFF, the Win32 declarations in nanocode-sys have no pointer-width-dependent layout between x86_64 and aarch64, and the stack bounds come from GetCurrentThreadStackLimits on both. Checked: `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` on Linux with NANOCODE_XWIN (xwin 0.6.5 splat, SDK 10.0.22621), NANOCODE_CC=clang-22 and LLD_LINK=lld-link-22 (dist profile, 7m11s at 2 jobs): ARM64 PE files, nanocode.exe 37,445,120 bytes, nanocode-python.exe 15,737,344 bytes with its 8 MiB stack reserve; release-cli.sh's zip and SHA256SUMS steps on staged files, then install.ps1 under pwsh 7.4.6 against a local HTTP release: first install, a second run that downloads nothing, an update to a new zip (old files moved aside, nc.exe linked again) and a checksum mismatch that stops before installing. output/winrelease-probe.yml builds both triples with build-cli.sh on windows-latest and windows-11-arm, installs through install.ps1 and runs the binaries; it has not run yet. `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` (master's warnings), `cargo check --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `--target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc -p nanocode-cli -p nanocode-python-cli --bins` (master's warnings).
- fix(cli): a steer the agent accepted but never delivered to the model, because the turn was cancelled or failed first, goes back into the prompt with the notice `steer not delivered before the turn ended · restored to the prompt`, instead of staying in the transcript as if sent while no request ever carried it (2026-11-14, e2e in tmux). Why: both harnesses publish `InputAccepted` with kind `steer` when a steer is queued on the running turn and `RunSteered` only when a model call takes it; the TUI dropped the steer from its own queue at `InputAccepted`, so esc esc between the two lost it, and its restore on interrupt only covered steers not yet accepted. `EventMapper` now keeps accepted steers until their `RunSteered` (cleared at `RunStarted`), and `settle_turn` restores what is left, ahead of the draft. Repro with a local Responses mock (output/e2e/mock_responses.py, `NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL`): `SLOW stream please`, after 3 s type `steer: hello again` + Enter, esc esc, then a new prompt: before, the next request's input had no `steer: hello again` and the prompt was empty; after, the prompt holds it. A steer typed while a cell runs is still delivered (the next request carries it) and nothing is restored.
- fix(cli): a confirmation prompt (`press ctrl+c again to quit`, `press esc again to interrupt`, the side pane's esc and ctrl+c prompts) stays on the status line only for `QUIT_CONFIRMATION` (2 s), the window in which the second press acts, instead of `STATUS_VISIBLE` (4 s), and every flash keeps the instant it expires rather than the instant it was shown (2026-11-14, e2e in tmux). Why: a second ctrl+c 2 to 4 s after the first, while the status line still said to press it again, only re-armed the prompt, so nanocode stayed open and showed the hint again. Repro before: in tmux, send-keys C-c, sleep 2.5, send-keys C-c: still running. After: the hint is gone at 2.5 s (capture-pane counts it 1 at 1 s, 0 at 2.5 s), and two presses 0.5 s apart exit 0 with the resume line.
- fix(hedge): Codex hedges reach turns 2 and 3 of a CLI session and their first byte comes sooner: the hedge cap counts against the whole window (`ceil(window * cap / 100)` hedges per window, 10 of 100 by default) instead of the requests seen so far, the quantile deadline applies only once the window holds `ceil(100 / (100 - quantile))` samples (10 for p90, the fewest where p90 is not the maximum) and is the floor before that, the WebSocket hedge sends on a spare connection opened when the primary request is sent (kept for the next request when unused) instead of connecting at the deadline, reasoning output items without content no longer count as the first output, the hedge carries no `x-codex-turn-state` and the connection takes the hedge's turn state when it wins, and Codex hedges run through `Hedging::race_when` with `x-nanocode-hedge: 1` in `client_metadata` on both the WebSocket and HTTPS hedge (the Codex client has no admission window, so a hedge is never throttled there); the cap and deadline rules are shared with the Claude hedge (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 latency SLA: GPT p99 turns 2-3 against codex-cli 0.166). Not the cause: prompt cache and reasoning settings. 12 traced gpt-6-luna sessions of 9275ee377 on dev-georgios read 12,416 of 12,677 input tokens from cache on turn 2 and 12,544 of 12,713 on turn 3, as codex-cli's rollouts do (190 luna sessions: median 15,872 of 16,016 on turns 2 and 3); both send effort medium with no reasoning summary, and codex-cli's turn 2 reasoned in 135 of 189 sessions against 2 of 12 for nanocode. Causes, from the same traces: (1) the cap admitted one hedge in a process's first 10 requests, so a CLI session whose turn 1 hedged could not hedge turns 2 and 3; (2) with 1 or 2 samples the p90 deadline was the slowest sample, so one slow turn 1 (2,926 ms observed) set the turn-2 wait to 2.9 s; (3) the hedge connected at the deadline and spent 0.1 to 1.0 s (about 0.5 s typical) on TLS and the WebSocket upgrade before sending, and hedges dispatched at 1.5 s lost to primaries at 2.2 to 2.7 s; (4) a turn-2 response with a reasoning item at 1,205 ms and text at 3,347 ms counted 1,205 ms as first output, so no hedge fired. codex-cli sends `x-codex-turn-state` on every request of a turn, including reconnects, and has no hedge; a hedge is a full replay on a new connection, so the turn state would only pin it to the backend of the slow primary. Measured with `bench/sla/run.ts --live --lanes=live-nc-codex@t3,live-codex,live-nc-codex@old --samples=20 --turns=3 --settle=3000` (nanocode-ts), interleaved, 20 sessions per lane, e2e TTFT p50/p99 ms, t3 = this change on 9275ee377, old = 9275ee377: gpt-6-luna t1 1,218/2,064 vs codex 1,824/3,221 (old 1,321/3,207), t2 1,106/3,072 vs 1,661/3,124 (old 1,229/2,599), t3 1,208/2,550 vs 1,464/2,573 (old 1,205/2,291); gpt-6.1-sol t1 1,807/8,556 vs 2,441/4,755 (old 2,022/5,381), t2 1,661/4,512 vs 1,900/6,779 (old 1,889/5,158), t3 1,597/4,129 vs 2,074/7,241 (old 1,864/5,653); gpt-6-astra (this change against codex-cli 0.166 only, 20 sessions per lane) t1 1,604/2,798 vs 2,717/4,419, t2 1,827/4,000 vs 1,928/4,580, t3 1,698/4,360 vs 1,877/3,655. The sol t1 p99 is one 8,556 ms sample (the next is 2,305 ms) with the spare connected 0.6 s after the request. Load average was 60 to 86 on 32 cores from concurrent evaluation runs in all lanes. `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 1000 5 --scenario runtime`: 1,000 passed, 0 failed.
- fix(hedge): a hedged model request is one logical call: the hedge carries `x-nanocode-hedge: 1` (`HEDGE_HEADER`), takes an admission slot only when one is free and never queues for one, so it is not sent while the Claude client's admission is cooling down after a 429 or its window is full (`HedgeOutcome::Throttled`); the hedge deadline starts after admission and hedge timing reads `nanocode_platform::now()` (2026-11-14, durability crash gate). Cause: the race wrapped `stream_prepared`, so time a request spent waiting in `Admission::admit` behind a retry-after counted as "no first byte"; the hedge then queued in the same admission and both requests were released together, about 36 ms apart, as two accepted provider calls for one logical call. The journal, events and child turns already took only the winner, but the 2K crash gate counted the second request as a repeated child turn. On the hosted Hand at nanocode-ts ddca280 (nanocode a5d401e0c), `node scripts/hillclimb.mjs --scenario score --agents 2000 --rate 200` in durable-cloudflare made 4,001 child calls (1 repeated child, 1 identical request body 36 ms after the first, 1,662 rejected). With this change built into nanocode-ts (`npm run build`, clang-22) the same run made exactly 4,000 child calls, 0 hedges, 0 repeats (1,692 rejected), and the `twice` crash scenario passed with 0 lost and 0 repeated. Simulator: the runtime scenario now enables `HedgePolicy::DEFAULT` and the model network fails `model_call_duplicated` when a request without the hedge marker repeats a request body that is still open; mutation `hedge-unmarked` drops the marker. `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 2000 5 --scenario runtime`: before (SDK at 090bb095f) 536 passed, 1,464 failed, all `model_call_duplicated`; after 2,000 passed with 3,723 hedges. After: `--children remote` 0..1000 and `--wire http` 0..500 pass; `--mutation hedge-unmarked` 0..500 fails 365 seeds. `--twice` fails about 31% of seeds with or without hedging enabled (94/300 with hedging off, 95/300 on), so that nondeterminism predates this change. `cargo check --locked --lib` native and wasm32 and `cargo clippy` add no warnings.
- fix(claude): Edit and Write refuse a file the session has not read with `File has not been read yet. Read it first before writing to it.` for the models Claude Code 2.1.300 guards, and only those (2026-11-14, Claude harness tool parity). Stock behavior read from its bundled cli (~/hill/stock/rt/claude-glibc/claude): Edit's `validateInput` returns `Vin` (errorCode 6) when `readFileState` has no entry or a partial view for an existing file, after the identical-strings, missing-file, `Cannot create new file` and notebook checks and before the match search, unless the guard is skipped; Write does the same (errorCode 2) for an existing file. The guard is skipped when `!pnn(model) && Lpe(...)`: `Lpe` holds whenever Read is offered and reading the path is allowed (always under bypassPermissions, as nanocode runs), and `pnn` is true for the canonical model names in `ae` = claude-opus-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5, claude-opus-4-5, claude-opus-4-1, claude-opus-4-0, claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-0, claude-3-7-sonnet, claude-3-5-sonnet, claude-3-5-haiku, after `DL` canonicalizes the id by substring (claude-opus-4 and claude-sonnet-4 not followed by `-<one digit>` map to the -4-0 names). So stock refuses for those models and allows unread edits for the rest (claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, non-Claude models), which is why the parity runs on DeepSeek saw both allow. What: `text_files::reads_first(model)` applies that canonicalization in stock's order; `ClaudeWorkspaceFiles::with_model` sets `read_first`, and claude_files.rs passes `context.model()`; with it, `edit` returns `NOT_READ` for an existing file with no view or a token-truncated view when the edit changes text and is not a creation, and `write` returns it for an existing file with no view (a truncated view already refused). Measured with output/b6-tools (mock.py scenario `unread`/`unreadx`: make three files, Edit unread, Edit unread with a missing string, Write unread, an identical-strings Edit, Read, Edit, Write new, Edit-create, Edit, Write again; stock through direct tools, nanocode through its Code Mode exec cell as it runs Claude models): stock claude-haiku-4-5 refuses steps 2-4 and then matches; nanocode before 8/11 outcomes equal to stock on claude-haiku-4-5 (it applied the three unread changes), after 11/11; claude-opus-5-5 11/11 before and after (no refusal, as stock). Not changed: nanocode-ts host file tools (`FileHost`), which see no reads. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-backend-claude` (no warnings), `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Files: crates/backends/claude/tools/src/tools/{text_files,workspace_files}.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/claude_files.rs.
- fix(claude): WebFetch converts HTML to markdown as Claude Code 2.1.300 does, with its limits (2026-11-14, Claude harness tool parity). Stock behavior read from its bundled cli (~/hill/stock/rt/claude-glibc/claude): `p8t` runs turndown 7.2 with default options (setext headings, `*   ` bullets, indented code blocks, `_`/`**`, inlined links, `* * *`) and `remove(["style","script","noscript","iframe"])` over `e.slice(0, 1048576)`, appending `\n\n[Content truncated due to length...]` past that, and only when the content type includes `text/html`; turndown parses with the domino HTML5 parser it bundles (`<x-turndown id="turndown-root">` + page + `</x-turndown>`, no doctype, so quirks mode, scripting on); `JCt` then cuts the markdown at 100,000 UTF-16 units with the same `\n\n[Content truncated due to length...]` suffix. nanocode's own tag stripper wrote ATX headings, `- ` bullets, fenced `pre`, ` | ` table cells, decoded 6 entities, escaped nothing and cut at 100,000 chars with `...[content truncated]`. What: `tools::turndown` (crates/backends/claude/tools) holds a port of domino's tokenizer and tree construction (`tools/html.rs`: character references against domino's 2,231-entry table, generated into `tools/entities.rs` by output/b6-tools/gen-entities.mjs from the bundled chunk, the Windows-1252 remap of `&#128;`..`&#159;`, RCDATA/RAWTEXT/PLAINTEXT, in-body, table, row, cell, caption, column group, select and template modes, foster parenting, the adoption agency and formatting reconstruction, SVG and MathML with breakout and integration points) and of turndown (`tools/turndown.rs`: collapse-whitespace, blank and flanking-whitespace rules, the escapes, every commonmark rule, the join of newlines); agent/web.rs calls `turndown::markdown(page, 1_048_576)` for `text/html` and `turndown::bound(markdown, 100_000)`, and drops its own converter. Measured with output/b6-tools (td.mjs runs the turndown+domino chunk extracted from the 2.1.300 binary under node as the oracle; md-harness runs the old converter and the new module; compare.sh): byte-identical output on 73 inputs (41 live pages from wikipedia, rfc-editor, doc.rust-lang.org, docs.python.org, MDN, github, go.dev, sqlite (2 MB, past the 1 MiB cut), the WHATWG parsing spec, bbc, lwn, HN and others, plus 32 synthetic cases for misnested formatting, foster parenting, entities in text and attributes, `<ol start>` values, inline code fences, foreign content), old 9/73, new 73/73; end to end with the parity mock (run.py fetch: six live WebFetch calls, the side request's page text compared with stock 2.1.300's from a run at the same minute) old 1/6, new 6/6. The oracle matched stock's own side requests on the six pages before the port. Time on the 2 MB sqlite page: 36 ms (old 15 ms, node turndown 368 ms). Not done: stock's `[WebFetch note: ...offset: 100000.]` suffix and `offset` paging, and its preapproved-domain prompt. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-backend-claude` (no warnings), `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`.
