Files: crates/backends/claude/tools/src/tools/{mod,html,entities,turndown}.rs, crates/backends/claude/src/agent/web.rs.
- fix(retry): a Workers AI error that the gateway passes on with the upstream's own 4xx status ends the model call at once on both harnesses, instead of being retried like a server error (2026-11-14, ~/hill/analysis/glm-backlog.md items 2 and 3, HILLCLIMB.md open sub-finding of item 2). The Tempo gateway answers a Workers AI rejection with HTTP 502 and the problem body `{"type":"/reference#description/upstream-failed","code":"upstream_failed","detail":"8007: {\"object\":\"error\",\"message\":\"Image count 10 exceeds limit 8 per request.\",\"type\":\"BadRequestError\",\"param\":null,\"code\":400}"}`, and in a stream as a `response.failed` (Responses) or `error` event (Messages) whose message is the same `<code>: <json>` text. In cmp2 every `<code>: {...}` detail was the 8007 BadRequestError (250 occurrences across the stock and nanocode logs); 3046 "Request timeout" (502) and 3021 rate limiting (429) carry plain text. The 502 made the request patient (9a695d182: up to ten minutes) and then reconnectable (322de32b7), and the Claude client counted the 502 and the `api_error` event as transient, so a request that can never succeed was sent again for minutes and then failed the run with exit 1 anyway, as the 8 stock-claude video-processing trials and the stock-codex trial did. Now a `detail` (problem body) or error `message` of the form `<digits>: <json>` whose JSON `code` is a 4xx that `retry::retryable_status` does not retry (so not 408, 409 or 429) makes the error final: in the Codex client `ApiErrorEnvelope::is_terminal` (crates/backends/codex/client/src/transport/api_error.rs) returns true, so `retry_advice`, the patient wait and `reconnectable` all stop; in the Claude client `ClaudeError::is_transient` (crates/backends/claude/client/src/lib.rs) returns false for such an `Http` body or `StreamError` message, and an `x-should-retry` header still decides first. A detail without an inner status (3046, 3021) or with a 5xx inner status stays retryable, so capacity and timeout errors keep their retries. A run whose final answer arrived is unaffected: the CLI sends no request after the answer (1 post in both builds with the mock failing every later request). Mock (output/retry-mock: mock.py from ~/hill/retrymock with `cf8007` (the 502 above), `cf8007ev` (the in-stream form), `cf3046` and `<action>x<count>` plans; `run.sh <binary> <codex|claude> <plan> <tag>`, `batch.sh <binary> <label>`), before ~/hill/bin/nanocode-4421fca (retry code identical to 090bb095f) against this build: codex cf8007x2000 timed out at 300 s after 22 posts, after 1 post and exit 1 in 0.3 s; codex cf8007evx2000 30 posts and exit 1 after 88.9 s, after 1 post in 0.3 s; claude cf8007x2000 timed out at 300 s after 14 posts (patient wait), after 1 post in 0.1 s; claude cf8007evx2000 11 posts and exit 1 after 184.0 s, after 1 post in 0.1 s. Unchanged in both builds: cf3046x3 then success 4 posts and DONE (codex 7.2/7.4 s, claude 4.3 s); ok then cf8007x50 1 post and DONE; a verification-failed 402 then success 2 posts and DONE (codex and claude); codex 500x29 then success 30 posts and DONE; codex nine 502s then a 402 11 posts and DONE. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client` and `-p nanocode-backend-claude-client`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib` on both (only master's retry.rs missing_const_for_fn); `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`.
- fix(claude): direct sessions answer each later user prompt with a `system` message `<total_tokens>15000000 tokens left</total_tokens>` and count the tool rounds' tokens left from the context at that prompt, as Claude Code 2.1.300 does (2026-11-14, Claude turn context parity: tokens-left, environment and attribution reminders, agent and skill listings). Stock behavior read from its bundled cli (~/hill/stock/rt/claude-glibc/claude): the `total_tokens_reminder` attachment runs after each tool result and, when `totalTokensReminderAfterUserTurn` holds (the `tengu_lapis_anchor_user_turn` flag, default true), after each regular user prompt; its default mode is `padded-countdown`, where `reanchorTaskBudget` sets the anchor to the context tokens at that prompt and `remaining` is 15,000,000 less the context tokens past the anchor. The first prompt's anchor is 0, which nanocode already matched. What: `Conversation::tokens_anchor` (serde default 0, so stored sessions keep their counts) takes `active_context_tokens` when a prompt that is not the first arrives in an `upstream_context` session, which pushes that system message after the prompt, and the per-round message subtracts the anchor from the last response's input, cache and output tokens. Checked with output/turnctx (mock.py, a scripted Messages server that answers each prompt with one Bash call and then text; run.py runs two prompts, the second with `--continue`, for stock 2.1.300 and for `nanocode exec`; cmp.py compares every request's messages with the attribution, environment and compaction texts masked): stock against ~/hill/bin/nanocode-4421fca (master before this change) 2 of 4 requests identical (no message after `Second prompt.`, then 14996610 where stock sends 14998899), against this build 4 of 4; with a 200,000-token window and a 180,000-token response in the second turn (`WIN=200000 BIGV=180000 BIG=3`), which makes both compact before the tool result, 2 of 5 to 4 of 5, and the post-compaction round now sends stock's 14819206 instead of 14816917. Left in that last request: stock resends the date, the attribution reminder and its agent-type and skill listings after a compaction. Already on master and not changed here: the attribution reminder, the environment message and the per-round tokens left (af6c01493), `# Environment update` when Bash leaves the working directory (ec1028f51). Not done: the agent-type and skill listings, which stock renders only beside its Agent and Skill tools (`Available agent types for the Agent tool:` and `The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:`); direct sessions offer neither tool, so listing them would name tools the model cannot call. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` for the mock runs. - fix(release): scripts/build-cli.sh runs `cargo fetch --locked` before it builds, and every build in it runs `--offline`, so a pinned hand rebuilds from an empty `CARGO_HOME` (2026-11-14, Georgios's TB2.1 Codex gate: hand release path). The pinned hand nanocode-cli-0bbcb64 was built by hand on dev-georgios with `cargo zigbuild --locked --offline --profile dist --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.31 -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, and after `~/.cargo/registry` was removed that command fails: 0bbcb64's Cargo.lock still has 11 crates.io packages (tokio, libc, windows-sys, bytes and others; master has none since d8b376fb4), and an offline build cannot download them. The script had the same failure under the `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true` that 2026-11-14's release-hygiene entry tells a builder to set. The fetch runs with `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE` removed from its environment, so it downloads only what the registry cache lacks and touches no network when the cache is complete (`cargo fetch --locked` with a full cache and `CARGO_HTTP_PROXY` pointed at a closed port exits 0); the builds after it are offline, so a build never reaches the network. release-cli.sh goes through build-cli.sh for every target, so it gets the same. A pinned hand is built with `scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.2.31` (zig 0.13.0 and cargo-zigbuild on PATH), not the bare command. Before and after on dev-georgios, at 0bbcb64a0 with this script change applied, each with its own empty `CARGO_HOME`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8`: the bare command and the old script (with `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`) both exit 101 with `error: no matching package named `tokio` found`; the new script with `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true` downloads the 41 MB the lockfile names, builds nanocode-python (3 m 49 s) and nanocode (8 m 55 s), and the binary prints `nanocode 0.7.0`, 50,591,928 bytes, 0 strings with `/home/` or `/Users/`. At master the fetch downloads nothing (no registry packages) and `cargo build --locked --offline -p nanocode-cli` from an empty `CARGO_HOME` already passes.
- fix(codex): Codex sessions in the WebAssembly brain (nanocode-ts, which runs the eval's nanox arm) describe `exec` with the full codex-cli-shaped description instead of the embedded runtime's compact one, and Codex `exec` and `wait` results default to codex-cli's 10,000-token budget (2026-11-14, Terminal-Bench 2.1 Codex parity: request diff against codex-cli 0.166.0). Why: the earlier request diffs captured the native CLI, whose `ToolRuntime::model_specs` passes `compact: false`; the brain builds tools with `EmbeddedToolRuntime`, which since a068afe4d passes `compact: true` for hosts with cells, so every nanox request opened `exec` with "Run JavaScript to orchestrate tool calls. Each call evaluates the code as a fresh async module." and a one-paragraph globals list, not codex-cli's template. codex-cli also truncates each `exec` and `wait` result to `resolve_max_tokens(None)` = `DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` = 10,000 tokens (`truncate_code_mode_result`, codex-rs/core/src/tools/code_mode/mod.rs and unified_exec/mod.rs at rust-v0.166.0) and says "Defaults to 10000 tokens." for both; nanocode had no budget (only the 12,000-token history cut). What: `Tools` gains `with_full_exec_description` (the embedded runtime then passes `compact: false` and keeps the "Runs raw JavaScript" line) and `with_output_budget`; the Codex harness's `tool_runtime` sets both, with 10,000. The budget reaches cells the way `with_exec_yield` does: the brain writes `max_output_tokens` into the `// @exec:` pragma and `max_tokens` into the `wait` input when the call gives none (`source_budgeted`, `wait_budgeted`), in the embedded runtime for hosts with cells and in the native runtime for local and hand-routed cells, so a hand applies its existing truncation (code_mode/output.rs, codex-cli's "Warning: truncated output" format) and needs no new release; `exec_spec_budgeted` and `wait_spec_with` then say "Defaults to 10000 tokens.". `wait`'s schema lists its properties in codex-cli's order (cell_id, max_tokens, terminate, yield_time_ms), the exec example names `exec_command` when it is a nested tool, and the deferred-tools guidance ends with codex-cli's "Tool availability can change between calls.". Claude sessions set neither flag, so they keep the compact embedded description and no budget. Checked: output/codex-embedded-spec (an `EmbeddedToolRuntime` over a mock cells host serving the native codex `apply_patch`, `exec_command`, `view_image` and `write_stdin` definitions, with the Codex 30 s exec yield) gives a 6,802-byte compact `exec` before and an 8,661-byte one after whose nested tool sections are byte-equal to codex-cli 0.166.0's (capcx2/001.json) and whose header differs only in the lines the Code Mode conformance track made accurate (fresh JavaScript context, cell lifetime, `exit`, `image`/`audio`/`generatedImage`, `notify`) and the Nanocode extension lines; `wait` is byte-equal to codex-cli's; the cell it dispatches changes from `// @exec: {"yield_time_ms":30000}` to `// @exec: {"max_output_tokens":10000,"yield_time_ms":30000}` and `wait` from `{"cell_id":"1"}` to `{"cell_id":"1","max_tokens":10000}`. The native mock capture (capnx-a7 against capnx-wave3) changes only the exec example, the max_output_tokens line and the availability line, and its `wait` is byte-equal to codex-cli's. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-tool-host -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-codex`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and clippy on them report nothing in the changed files. Left as is: codex-cli's goals, MCP resource and clock tools are features nanocode lacks; the brain's own `hands` tool (nanoeval's `hands: 'always'`) stays in the eval's list; and a hand still lists its Claude-shaped Read, Edit, Write, Bash and TaskStop in `ALL_TOOLS` (96314dec0 hid them only from the description), so nanox called `tools.Bash` 13 times across the 38 finished nanox attempts of 0d6c29c9, 16e15f9a and a763f96d; hiding them there needs nanocode-ts to give its `RemoteHost` a `HandToolSelection`, which nothing sets today. extract-moves-from-video is not a harness gap: its traced attempts (e5581bd1 a00009 nanox, a00010 cx) both hit the 1800 s agent timeout while OCRing frames with tesseract in the krun guest, where one 1280x720 frame took 5.7 s and eight parallel tesseracts ran at about 7% CPU each in both arms; and the 65 `view_image` calls on .ppm frames and 3 on .jpg in recent nanox attempts all returned images. Needs a nanocode-ts release and Worker redeploy to reach the eval; the hand CLI is unchanged.
- fix(codex): Responses Lite requests (the gpt-6 catalog models) nest their function and custom tools in a `functions` namespace in `additional_tools`, as codex-cli 0.166.0 does, instead of listing them flat (2026-11-14, Terminal-Bench 2.1 Codex parity: request diff against codex-cli 0.166.0). codex-cli builds the item with `create_tools_json_for_responses_lite` (codex-rs/tools/src/tool_spec.rs at rust-v0.166.0): every `Function` and `Freeform` spec, and the children of any `functions` namespace, go into one `{"type":"namespace","name":"functions","description":""}` placed where the first of them stood, and other namespaces stay as they are. nanocode now does the same when it serializes an `AdditionalTools` item for the wire (`functions_namespace` in crates/backends/codex/client/src/responses/request.rs), so its stored prefix, history and the top-level `tools` of non-Lite models are unchanged. A call that names the `functions` namespace is the default namespace, as codex-cli's `ToolName` reads it: `CodeCall` and `qualified_tool_name` (tower/stream.rs) drop it, and the Chat Completions registry (transport/chat.rs) registers that namespace's tools unqualified, so a Lite body sent through a Chat gateway keeps its tool names. The model does not echo the namespace: three requests with codex-cli's captured body (~/nc-live/a6/capcx2/001.json, its namespaced tools) to chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses on gpt-6-luna returned `custom_tool_call` items for `exec` with no `namespace` field (~/a7/probe/ns.py on dev-georgios). Checked with the mock capture (~/nc-live/a6/capnc.sh, `nanocode exec --no-subagents -m gpt-6-luna -t high`): before (capnx-wave3) `exec` and `wait` sat at the top of `additional_tools`; after (capnx-a7) they sit in a `functions` namespace with an empty description, as in capcx2/001.json, and every other request field and input item matched capnx-wave3 apart from ids and client_metadata (`tool_namespaces_info` unchanged). `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-codex`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and clippy on them report nothing in the changed files.
- fix(psh): bash 5.3 details in declare, `local -`, set, hash, trap, printf -v, nameref and indirect expansion (2026-11-14, psh conformance). Declaration expansion applies only to an unquoted literal builtin name that is not disabled (`"declare" y=$v` splits, as in bash 5.3). `declare -aA` reports `-a: invalid option` and returns 2 after it creates the variable. `local -` stores the set option bits in the call's Frame and restores them on return. `set +` followed by an invalid letter applies the options before it and returns 1. `set` quotes `~` only at the start or after `=`/`:` and `#` only at the start. `hash NAME` needs an executable file and drops a stale entry, and `hash -l` single-quotes paths. A trap action restores PIPESTATUS. A process substitution drops inactive (inherited, not running) traps, so `trap -p` there lists none. `declare -n x=x` is refused before the variable is created. A chain of 8 namerefs resolves (bash 5.3: the 9th fails). `printf -v` matches a subscript's closing bracket through nesting, quotes, backslashes, backquotes and `$( )`/`${ }`. `export +x` is an operand, so an invalid identifier, as `+` is not an export option. `${!ref:=word}` assigns to the variable or element `ref` names, and `${!ref:?msg}` reports `!ref`. psh-spec (in-process, Linux): brush 3013 -> 3033, oils 2418 -> 2419, no new failures. Upstream delta: crates/patches/psh/crates/psh-engine/src/{builtins/declare.rs,builtins/hash.rs,builtins/printf.rs,builtins/set.rs,builtins/trap.rs,exec.rs,expand.rs,options.rs,state.rs}.
- feat(psh): psh takes bash's `--verbose` (as `-v`), `--debug`, `--rcfile FILE` and `--init-file FILE` at invocation, and `-o`, `+o`, `-O` or `+O` as the last word lists the options before the script runs (2026-11-14, psh conformance). `--help` and `--version` now apply after the whole command line parses, so `--version --bogus` is an invalid option as in bash 5.3. The listing runs the `set`/`shopt` builtins in the spawned main future, with `emacs` shown on as bash shows it at that point. A `-v` echo of the last chunk without a final newline ends with one. psh-spec (in-process, Linux): brush 3005 -> 3013 of 3171, oils 2418 of 2511, agent 727, utils 999, no new failures. Not done: `-i`, `-r`, `-D` and `-m` job messages. Upstream delta: crates/patches/psh/crates/psh-engine/src/{invocation.rs,lib.rs,builtins/mod.rs,builtins/set.rs}.
- perf(cli): build-cli.sh orders the hot read-only data of the shipped binary together, and BOLT lays out the functions a tool turn runs in their own run after the one-shot's (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: process memory against fx 0.0.16). Why: file-backed pages are most of every process's RSS and the kernel maps them in 64 KiB fault-around windows. BOLT already orders .text by the training profile, but .rodata kept the link order of the one fat-LTO object: valgrind lackey of a one-shot (master 778e5ad4a, `--tool=lackey --trace-mem=yes` under bench/cli's fixture) touched 304 pages of the 6.4 MB .rodata spread over 47 windows (3.0 MB of RSS), while the input sections it touched sum to about 150 KB (947 anonymous constants, 97.7 KB; 301 functions' own tables, 54.9 KB; the merged `.rodata.cst*`/`.rodata.str*` blobs are 310 KB together). What: (1) the final crate is built with `cargo rustc ... -- -C save-temps -C link-arg=-Wl,-Map=<out>/<bin>.map --print link-args`, so its LTO object, link map and link line are kept (`<out>/<bin>.link` is replaced only when rustc ran, so a fresh cargo keeps the previous link's files); (2) new scripts/rodata-cli.py reads the `--emit-relocs` relocations of the built binary: every .rodata input section a function in the startup, one-shot or tool-turn training profile references, then everything those sections reference through `.rela.rodata`, in that order, and relinks the same object with an `INSERT BEFORE .eh_frame` script that places the merged constant blobs, then those sections, then the rest of `.rodata`; only `.rodata` moves, so the training profile of the original binary still applies, and the BOLT steps lay out the relinked binary; (3) train-cli.py gains a `tools` mode (`exec --ephemeral "List the files steps=3"`, a code-mode exec cell running `exec_command ls` three times), build-cli.sh keeps its profiles in `tools/` and order-cli.py places functions only it ran after the one-shot's (they were spread through the full training's cdsort order). The static hot set is about 0.9 MB and holds 1,217 of the 1,249 input sections the lackey run touched. Lackey of a one-shot of this build: 173 .rodata pages in 27 windows (from 304 in 47). Cost: the bin crate's rustc keeps its temporaries in deps (about 0.8 GB of bitcode beside the 99 MB object) and the relink takes seconds. Measured with bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=startup,firstframe,oneshot,tools,fleet --only=nc --rounds=1 --steps=10 --toolrounds=1 --fleetrounds=1 --fleet=8` under tools/netguard.sh, `taskset -c 24-27`, dev-georgios at load about 40, 20 rounds rotating six binaries: master's build-cli output and its pre-BOLT binary laid out twice more with master's BOLT steps, against this pipeline's build-cli output twice and once with BOLT retrained on the relinked binary (these three were built from a tree that also held a store-jsonl change only `--continue` and `nanocode sessions` reach, which no measured row runs); medians [p25, p75] per binary: one-shot peak RSS 12.50 [12.25, 12.75], 12.75, 13.00 to 11.50 [11.25, 11.75], 11.00 [10.75, 11.25], 11.00 MB; first-frame RSS one second after the frame 12.34, 12.12, 12.18 to 10.45, 10.12, 10.25 MB (anonymous memory 2.00 to 1.99 in all, so all of it is file pages); tool turn (10 steps) peak 18.00, 18.25, 18.50 to 16.50, 16.50, 15.75 MB; fleet of 8 per agent 12.41, 12.50, 12.81 to 11.31, 10.97, 10.78 MB; one-shot CPU 7.18, 7.28, 7.23 to 6.67, 6.84, 6.69 ms, first-frame CPU 7.19, 7.42, 7.41 to 6.90, 6.87, 6.64 ms, first frame 19.2, 19.6, 19.3 to 19.1, 17.8, 18.6 ms (load-bound); `--version` peak 3.25, 3.00, 3.00 to 2.75, 2.75, 1.25 MB. The tool group alone (same pre-BOLT binary laid out three times each way, own probe sampling smaps at the peak, 10 rounds): tool-turn peak 18.50, 18.75, 18.25 to 18.25, 18.25, 18.00 MB with text at the peak 7.82, 8.13, 7.45 to 7.12, 7.31, 7.42 MB. Reproduce: `valgrind -q --tool=lackey --trace-mem=yes` of `nanocode exec --ephemeral` against the fixture and count distinct 4 KiB pages and 64 KiB windows of addresses inside .rodata (readelf -SW for its range). Files: scripts/build-cli.sh, scripts/rodata-cli.py, scripts/train-cli.py, scripts/order-cli.py.
- feat(codex): `builtin_tools::served` gives hosts its pieces: `ServedDirectories::resolve` is public, `ReadFile::new(directories, definition, chunk)` is a standalone `Tool` sharing an `Arc<ServedDirectories>` (what `ServedTools` installs), `read_file` answers the file's permission bits as `mode` (`st_mode & 0o7777`) beside `size`, `modified_ns`, `offset` and `data`, and `served::redact(output, &Redactor)` is public over nanocode-process-contracts' `Redactor`, with `ServedTools::redacting` building a raw `Redactor` from its `Redactions` (2026-11-14, tempoxyz/pyramid dropping its copies). Why: tempoxyz/pyramid's `hands/src/machine.rs` kept its own `Served` (directories file with a `RwLock` and `Mutex`), `ReadFile` and `redact_proxy_credentials`, about 300 lines, because upstream's were private: it installs its own shell tools (Codex and Claude, with secrets) rather than `ServedTools`, its `write_file` resolves workdirs through the same directories, a copy gives the file it writes the permission bits `read_file` reports, and it redacts with a `Redactor` it builds from secrets and proxy forms. The private `scrub` and `scrub_json` went: `Redactor::text` and `Redactor::json` are the same loops. `Redactor::raw(0)` keeps what was redacted before: no JSON-escaped forms, and no length floor beyond the 8-byte password minimum `proxy_forms` already applies. Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and for wasm32-unknown-unknown (`served` builds on unix only, as before), clippy clean for the crate.
- feat(claude-client): `ClaudeWorkloadIdentity::cached_auth(http, base_url, cache)` keeps federated tokens in a host's `ClaudeTokenCache` (`load(identity_token)`, `store(identity_token, access_token, expires_at)`); `auth` is unchanged and caches nothing (2026-11-14, tempoxyz/pyramid dropping its copy). A refresh asks the cache for the current identity token first and uses its token only while it outlives the 30 s mandatory refresh margin; an exchange stores what it got; `refresh_rejected` never reads the cache, since the server just refused the token it would return. Why: Anthropic accepts a projected JWT once, so tempoxyz/pyramid's backend keeps the last token in a 0600 file keyed by the JWT's SHA-256 for a restarted process in the same Pod, and for that it kept its own copy of the whole exchange (`backend/crates/engine/src/claude_federation.rs`, about 300 lines). The host owns the storage and the key (it gets the identity token itself), upstream the margin and the bypass on rejection. `ClaudeWorkloadIdentity` keeps its fields, so struct literals still build. Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-client` native and for wasm32-unknown-unknown (federation builds off wasm only, as before), clippy clean for the crate.
- feat(types-core): `pricing::estimate_tokens(input, cached_input, cache_write_input, output, model, tier)` is public and a `const fn` (2026-11-14, tempoxyz/pyramid dropping its rate table). Why: it was `#[doc(hidden)]` in a private module, so tempoxyz/pyramid's `backend/crates/utility/src/models.rs` hard-coded each model's standard-tier input and output rate in a `const` table that drifts from these; as a `const fn` that table can be built from it (`estimate_tokens(1, 0, 0, 0, model, ServiceTier::Standard).input()`). The two `min` calls became `if`s, since `Ord::min` is not const. Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-types-core` native and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, clippy clean for the crate.
- feat(sandbox): `run::Call` takes `private_hosts`, passed to the egress `Allowlist` that `Runner::run` built with none (2026-11-14, tempoxyz/pyramid dropping its copy). Why: tempoxyz/pyramid's organization tools (`backend/crates/tools`, `Tools::run`) run their own copy of `Runner::run` because a test backend lets its fixtures on localhost through (`PYRAMID_TOOL_PRIVATE_HOSTS`), which `Call` could not say. Nothing in nanocode builds a `Call`; a caller that does adds `private_hosts: &[]` for today's behavior. The proxy's address rules are unchanged. Checked: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sandbox` native and for wasm32-unknown-unknown (an empty library there), clippy clean for the crate.
- feat(computer): `Engine::diffs(false)` and `Native::diffs(false)` make every step return the app's whole state, and `capabilities().diffs` reports the choice; the default stays diffs on (2026-11-14, Pyramid: drop the Hand's own copy of the engine). Why: `Engine::capabilities` set `diffs = true` and `run` always read with the last snapshot, so a host whose `computer` tool promises the whole new state after each action (Pyramid's hands/src/desktop.rs) could not use the engine. With it off, `run` reads with no earlier snapshot (fresh indexes, `Change::Whole`) and the description's "the app's whole new state" branch applies; embedded.rs's `observe` keeps choosing per call. Also fixes `numbered`'s fresh numbering, which computed `then_some(next - 1)` for every line and so overflowed in debug builds whenever the first line was not actionable (any window line, on the first `get_app_state` of a session and on every step with diffs off); it is now `then(|| next - 1)`. Linux: zbus and zvariant left with the hand-written D-Bus client on 2026-11-13 (its entry below), nothing in Cargo.lock names them, so no gate is needed and none is added (AGENTS.md: no Cargo features). Checked with output/engine-diffs (a fake `Backend` with a window, a "Count N" button that increments and a "Reset" button; `cargo run --offline`): master's code panicked "attempt to subtract with overflow" at engine.rs `numbered` on the first `get_app_state`; with this change the default engine reports `diffs = true` and the click returns the "Since its last state" header with only `~ [0] Button "Count 1"`, and `diffs(false)` reports `diffs = false` and returns the whole state with both buttons at the same indexes. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-computer` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-computer` (no warnings). nanocode-sim does not cover this crate. Files: crates/integrations/computer/src/engine.rs, tool.rs.
- feat(chatgpt-extension): `ExtensionLink::serve_ranked(path, rank)` lets a connection on a higher-ranked socket take the link over from the live one; `serve(path)` is `serve_ranked(path, 0)`, so one socket keeps first-come-wins (2026-11-14, Pyramid: drop hands/src/browser.rs's `BrowserLink`). Why: Pyramid serves two sockets on one link, its own extension's and the ChatGPT extension relay's, and its extension must take the browser over from the relay but never the reverse; `BrowserLink` copied `ExtensionLink` with a tokio Mutex only for that, and its monitor loop (hands/src/main.rs) copies `Watch`, which needs an `ExtensionLink`. What: `Live` carries its rank and a `Signal`; the claim replaces a held connection only when its rank is lower (same or higher answers `other_browser` as before) and fires the replaced one's signal, whose read loop then ends as a disconnect: its writer stops, the relay sees EOF, and its pending steps fail as disconnected when `pending` is cleared. Checked with output/link-takeover (`cargo run --offline`, two sockets ranked 0 and 1 on one link): rank 0 gets hello, rank 1 gets hello and rank 0 reads EOF, a new rank 0 and a second rank 1 each get `other_browser`, and once rank 1 closes, rank 0 connects again and a second rank 0 is refused. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-chatgpt-extension` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-chatgpt-extension` (no warnings). nanocode-sim does not cover this crate. File: crates/integrations/chatgpt-extension/src/link.rs.
- docs(decisions): the Codex wait and poll path leaves no harness-side cause on Terminal-Bench 2.1 make-mips-interpreter, fix-ocaml-gc and query-optimize: nanox (codex:gpt-6-luna:high, Code Mode) and codex-cli 0.166 (cx) spend the same model time, requests and input tokens there (2026-11-14, runs 650d0782 and bec3e408 and wave-3 run 0d6c29c9, Worker a6416bd0 with nanocode a5d401e0c). (a) make-mips-interpreter is 0 of 3 on both arms, with one agent_timeout each (nanox a00019, cx a00093). Model generation is 1,628 s of nanox a00019's 1,772 s (100 calls; tools did 95 s of work), against 1,323 s of cx a00021's 1,445 s over 152 calls. Over the three pairs nanox generated 137.6k output tokens in 3,098 s of model time and cx 137.2k in 3,213 s, 42 to 46 tok/s on both. nanox makes fewer, longer calls because one cell batches apply_patch with a run of `node vm.js`; its write_stdin polls of those runs (11, 0 and 11 per attempt) took 5 s each. The one harness-side loss: at 11:10:23 UTC the session's Durable Object pump restarted on a Worker-wide event (a00019 and a00022 logged `retrying`, kind detached, `hand slot is not attached`, in the same second) and dropped a model call 53 s into generation. 5 of the nanox attempts in 650d0782 and bec3e408 carry such a retry, two of them in the same second, and none of 0d6c29c9's do: the pump restarting under a running attempt, which no client change prevents. (b) fix-ocaml-gc is 5 of 5 on both arms. No nanox attempt calls `wait` any more (0 calls in the 18 nanox attempts pulled from the three runs), since a5d401e0c removed the orchestration block that told the model to hold a cell, so 5237db845's empty-wait hold has nothing to hold. The model polls with write_stdin cells naming `yield_time_ms: 1000`, which the empty-poll floor (codex-cli's MIN_EMPTY_YIELD_TIME_MS, 5,000 ms) stretches to 5 s, and almost every poll returns build output (bec3e408 a00156 55 of 57, a00298 59 of 60; 650d0782 a00013 62 of 63, a00085 83 of 83). Five pairs, nanox against cx: 377 against 414 requests, 22.8 M against 23.3 M input tokens, 588 to 842 s against 562 to 726 s of wall time; cx's requests that carry no visible item, its polls, number 50 to 67 per attempt against nanox's 18 to 83 polls. Requests are already incremental: nanox runs on the Responses WebSocket with `previous_response_id` on one connection (connection_generation 1 throughout, no reconnects), while cx posts the whole input over HTTP through nanoeval's proxy on every request. input_tokens counts the whole context either way, so an empty poll gets cheaper only by polling less, which only a floor longer than codex-cli's would buy. (c) query-optimize: every failure on both arms (nanox 0 of 4, cx 2 of 4) is the verifier's runtime gate, the solution's median at 1.20 to 1.46 times the golden query's against the 1.05 allowed; the other five tests pass. No nanox cell used setTimeout (0 of the 18 trajectories); its 30 s polls are write_stdin on a running sqlite3 comparison of the original query. codex-cli refuses no sleep in Code Mode (Claude Code's refusal of a 25 s Bash sleep has no Codex counterpart, and codex-cli's clock.sleep is a top-level tool that ends when new input arrives), and nanocode's Codex backend refuses none either, so nothing changes there. Left as is: nanoeval's Worker sets CELL_YIELD_MS 120000, which as `cell_yield` sets both exec's and wait's default yield for Codex sessions, where codex-cli's are 30 s and 10 s; no cell in these runs outlived 30.2 s, so it changed nothing measured here. The block tells the model to keep calling `write_stdin` in one cell until the process exits and to wait on a yielded cell instead of polling across turns; in the tb21 losers' traces that held cells polling for minutes, which codex-cli's model, never told so, does not do. `developer_context` now joins only the permissions and host instructions, so Code Mode and direct-tools sessions send the same developer message, and it and `task_input` no longer take the tool set. Every failure in that run, in all three arms (nanoxd a00002/a00038/a00074, nanox a00037, cx a00075), takes the same path: two `sed` reads of sim.c, a third call probing for yosys/abc, then a final answer at call 4 (3.0-4.5 k reasoning tokens) that says no circuit fits 32,000 signals and leaves gates.txt alone. The passes skip the probe and write a generator at call 3; a00001 passes with a partial lookup for isqrt 0-255 because the tests use small N. At call 4 (after the probe), the history decides and the request shape does not: with nanoxd a00038's history, give-up was 12/28 on nanocode direct with `reasoning.summary: auto`, 15/28 without summary, 6/16 with the tools in a `functions` namespace, 10/16 with both, and 6/16 on codex-cli's Code Mode request with the same calls rewritten as exec cells. With nanox a00037's history (the same probe, exit code 0), give-up was 1/16 on nanocode direct and 0/14 on codex-cli Code Mode. So dropping `reasoning.summary` (96dfd92c5) is parity and not a fix for this task: without it, reasoning ran 30-45% longer at call 3 and give-ups did not drop. The gap between arms is 3 attempts per arm on a task where the per-attempt give-up rate is about 1/3 in every arm. - perf(executor): the durability store's runtime no longer drives the shared reactor, a read shorter than its buffer clears the source's read readiness, and exec's printer records a reply key's model call once (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: bench/cli headless CPU per token). Why: every runtime thread that idles takes the process-wide reactor (`Reactor::try_turn`) and `Reactor::release` wakes every thread parked waiting for it, so the nanocode-durability-store thread (a current-thread runtime that only waits in `block_on(pending())`) and the session's worker traded the reactor on every event: the store thread sat in epoll_wait, woke for each SSE chunk, woke the worker through its task and took the reactor back before the worker idled again. strace -f of `nc exec` at 1,000 tok/s (5,000 tokens): the store thread made 4,873 futex and 4,808 epoll_wait calls, the worker 4,877 futex and 9,623 recvfrom (one returning EAGAIN per chunk); perf record put 17.7% of the process's samples on the store thread, nearly all scheduler and futex. What: `Builder::drive_reactor(false)` (default true) builds a runtime whose threads park instead of turning the reactor and do not count as drivers (`Driving` holds an `Option`), so with no other driver the reactor's fallback thread runs it as before; its tasks are woken through their slots as before, and its timers and I/O are delivered by whichever runtime drives. `spawn_driver` builds the store runtime with it. `poll_read_with` (TCP, Unix streams, pipes) clears the read readiness it read with when a read returns fewer bytes than the buffer holds, as tokio does on epoll and kqueue: both are edge-triggered here, and readiness is cleared only if no event arrived since it was read (the tick in `Io::clear`'s compare-exchange), so the next read waits for the next edge instead of making a syscall that returns EAGAIN; Windows keeps its retry path. `Printer` inserted the reply key and its model call index into a map on every delta; it now inserts only when the key is new (a retry removes the dead call's keys, so the retry's first delta inserts again). Measured with scripts/build-cli.sh builds (dist, BOLT 21) of c97e1a49f plus the streaming change above, with and without this, bench/cli sweep.mjs --mode=cli --rates=100,1000,10000 --samples=20 under tools/netguard.sh, pinned to 4 CPUs at load 35 to 70, lanes interleaved per sample, each run under perf stat; medians [p25, p75]: at 100 tok/s task-clock 34.6 [32.6, 39.9] to 28.4 [26.4, 31.4] ms (fx 0.0.16 27.9), kernel instructions 40.1M to 28.4M (fx 30.5M), context switches 1,645 to 932 (fx 1,436), user instructions 17.96M to 17.59M (fx 10.68M); at 1,000 tok/s task-clock 134.8 [125.9, 139.5] to 104.2 [96.5, 108.1] ms (fx 85.9), kernel instructions 279.7M to 177.6M (fx 173.6M), context switches 14,358 to 7,838 (fx 8,421), user 101.3M to 98.5M (fx 70.5M); at 10,000 tok/s task-clock 686.6 [641.6, 757.4] to 480.9 [443.4, 515.9] ms (fx 401.9), kernel instructions 2,183M to 1,352M (fx 1,403M), context switches 101,902 to 58,826 (fx 58,696), user 913M to 878M (fx 675M); the harness's tree CPU 49.5 to 41.8 ms (fx 42.8), 167 to 129 ms (fx 113) and 785 to 544 ms (fx 463). A third build with only the short-read and printer parts gave kernel instructions 275.6M at 1,000 and 2,146M at 10,000 tok/s (-1.5%, -1.7%) and user -0.4% and -0.8%; the rest is the reactor. The terminal interface has the same two threads: sweep.mjs --mode=tui (8 samples of 3 s, master against this build) tree CPU 334 [303, 350] to 117 [108, 119] ms at 1,000 tok/s and 787 [747, 857] to 446 [418, 458] ms at 10,000, token lag p50 5.28 to 5.12 and 5.10 to 4.97 ms, every token shown. Gates, suite.mjs --parts=firstframe,oneshot,fleet --rounds=20, master against this build: first frame 16.5 [14.9, 18.8] to 15.1 [13.7, 20.2] ms, its CPU 6.55 to 5.41 ms, RSS 12.04 to 12.02 MB; one-shot CPU 5.04 [4.77, 5.38] to 5.23 [4.76, 5.38] ms and peak RSS 12.63 to 12.50 MB, and under perf stat (30 rounds) user instructions 8.53M both, kernel 9.31M to 9.19M, context switches 40 to 33.5; fleet CPU per agent 20.5 to 19.6 ms. Checked: piped output byte-identical to the streaming build on the bench fixture (3,000 and 500 streamed tokens, a one-word reply, a two-step tool turn); a saved `nc exec` session, `--continue` and `nc sessions` work; a mid-reply retry prints as described above. nanocode-sim does not run this executor. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-executor` and `-p nanocode-durability` native and wasm32, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-executor --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` (only master's nanocode-sys getsockopt warning), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-executor -p nanocode-durability -- -D warnings`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Files: crates/core/executor/src/runtime.rs, crates/core/executor/src/net.rs, crates/runtime/durability/src/shared_store.rs, bin/nanocode/src/stream.rs.
- perf(cli): `nc exec` writes each reply delta to a pipe or file as it arrives instead of holding the reply until its message completes (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: bench/cli headless lane). Since the retry fix of 2026-11-14 (f908fadb7), `stream::Printer` held every `assistant.delta` when stdout was not a terminal and printed the message at `assistant.message`, so a single-message reply reached a pipe only at the end of the stream: in bench/cli harness/sweep.mjs --mode=cli (5 s of scripted tokens) nc gave 1 update at 100 and 1,000 tok/s and 6 at 10,000, a token lag p50 of 2.5 s and p99 of 4.9 s and a time-to-first-token overhead of 5.0 s, where fx 0.0.16 streams every token. Now the printer treats a pipe as it treats a terminal: deltas are written as they arrive and flushed once per batch of ready events (`stream_turn` already drains `try_next` before each flush), and the `live` flag and the held buffer go. Output without a retry is byte-identical: runs of master and this build against the bench fixture (bench/cli harness/fakellm.mjs) (3,000 tokens unpaced, 500 tokens at 2,000 tok/s, a one-word reply and a two-step tool turn) gave identical stdout (16,965, 2,403, 6 and 19 bytes) and stderr, in 34 and 387 pipe reads instead of 1. What changes: a request retried after part of its reply was printed now leaves that partial line in the pipe, then a newline and the retry's reply, with "the partial reply above is discarded" on stderr, exactly as on a terminal (a mock Responses server that cuts the first stream after three deltas: master printed "Reply 2 alpha beta gamma", this prints "Reply 1 alpha " and that line); a mid-reply retry is rare, a consumer that needs only a finished reply can wait for exit status, and every lane bench/cli compares streams to a pipe. Measured with scripts/build-cli.sh builds (dist, BOLT 21) of c97e1a49f with and without this, bench/cli sweep.mjs --mode=cli --rates=100,1000,10000 --samples=20 under tools/netguard.sh, pinned to 4 CPUs at load 35 to 70, lanes interleaved per sample, medians [p25, p75]: at 100 tok/s lag p50 2,490 to 0.152 [0.110, 0.172] ms (fx 0.132), p99 4,940 to 1.58 ms (fx 0.70), first-token overhead 4,991 to 0.157 ms (fx 0.180), updates 1 to 500, tree CPU 32.5 [28.7, 36.2] to 33.2 [27.8, 36.9] ms (fx 28.0); at 1,000 tok/s lag p50 2,500 to 0.057 ms (fx 0.031), p99 4,950 to 2.99 ms (fx 2.97), overhead 5,000 to 2.17 ms (fx 2.27), updates 1 to 4,678 (fx 4,740), CPU 103 [89, 113] to 130 [115, 140] ms (fx 76); at 10,000 tok/s lag p50 2,518 to 0.030 ms (fx 0.023), p99 4,958 to 4.02 ms (fx 3.85), overhead 5,008 to 0.084 ms (fx 0.103), updates 6 to 36,027 (fx 40,245), CPU 546 [501, 581] to 617 [600, 670] ms (fx 417). The CPU added is the write and the reader's wake per batch; the next entry takes it back. Commands: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-cli --no-deps` (only master's needless_borrow at lib.rs `hedge_policy(&args)`). Files: bin/nanocode/src/stream.rs, bin/nanocode/src/lib.rs.

In one interleaved window on dev-georgios with `NANOCODE_HEDGE_CAP_PERCENT=0` (bench/sla/run.ts --live, --samples=20 --turns=3 --settle=3000), turn-2 p50/p99 was 2,035/5,182 ms on 00c215b02, 1,200/4,596 ms on 1d4463636 and 1,535/2,977 ms on Codex CLI 0.166. - deps: djs loses the features no nanocode build turns on: djs-core's `dump`, `lazy`, `compile-cache` and `prelude` and djs-prelude's `packed`, `names` and `registry`, with djs-lzrc, `vm::registry` and `compiler::prelude_function_names`: 25,907 lines of Rust and a package (2026-11-14, DEPENDENCIES.md rank 1). Why: djs-embed, nanocode's only way in, takes djs-core with `full` and `embed` (and `unsafe-heap` on wasm32) and djs-prelude with `raw`, `full` and `embed`; the rest served djs-wasm's modules and djs's own tools, which are not vendored. What: output/cfgstrip resolved every `cfg`, `cfg_attr` and `cfg!` naming those seven features as off (27 files, 23 module files only they reached: `Vm::dump` with vm/dump*.rs and call_site.rs, the lazy compiler and interpreter, the compile cache, smap_codec.rs, djs-prelude's registry.rs), leaving every other feature open; djs-core's build.rs sets `djs_prelude` on every non-wasm target as before (the `prelude` feature only added it on wasm) and no longer filters the removed names out of its feature hash, compat_inputs.rs drops them from its image-neutral list, djs-prelude's build.rs no longer writes the registry offsets, base names or coded image, and djs-lzrc (the coder only `packed` used) goes from the tree and Cargo.lock. Then what only those reached: `vm::registry` (801 lines, read by djs-prelude's build script for `registry` and `names`) with `compiler::prelude_function_names`, the `PRELUDE` source on wasm32 (gated on `djs_prelude` like its one remaining reader, `Vm::install_prelude`), and `Unit`'s `base`, `line` and `col`, which only lazy units set (`Unit::base` is 0 and `line_col` the line table's, as they always were with `lazy` off). Runs of blank lines the deletions left were collapsed outside literals. Proof: `-Zunpretty=expanded` of djs-core, djs-prelude and djs-embed with nanocode's features on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, wasm32-unknown-unknown, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-apple-darwin, before and after: djs-embed equal; djs-core differs only in the removed items, the `Unit` fields and the two bodies above, `SOURCE_HASH` and `RECORDS_HASH`; djs-prelude only in `BUILT_BY` and the base image, whose 195,824 bytes differ only at offsets 92 to 95, its build hash. `RECORDS_HASH` changes because interp/run/lazy.rs leaves a region directory (output/rh computes it with each changed file put back: only that file restores it), so a Code Mode snapshot a host stored under the previous build fails to load once and is rebuilt (code-mode-engine's `cached_snapshot` path warns and compiles it), as after any djs change to those regions.
- deps: the vendored djs, psh, pymath and RustPython crates lose their tests: 99,810 lines of Rust and 11,659 of snapshots and manifests (2026-11-14, DEPENDENCIES.md rank 1). Why: no build compiles them (each library sets `test = false`, AGENTS.md allows no tests outside nanocode-sim, and dev-dependencies of path dependencies outside the workspace are never resolved, so libm, proptest, pyo3, insta and datatest-stable were never even fetched), and they were a fifth of the vendored Rust. What: output/cfgstrip resolved every `cfg` and `cfg_attr` with `test` off in crates/patches/djs, psh, pymath and rustpython-* and deleted what they drop, with the doc comments and attributes in front of it (285 files); the module files only those items reached went (djs's compiler snapshots and vm/dump_size_tests.rs, psh-utils' tests.rs, tests_text.rs and tests_misc.rs, and the rest), and so did the ungated `#[test]` functions in psh-utils' fd/patterns.rs and the ruff parser's token_set.rs, pymath's `pyo3_proptest!` macro and its four calls (it expanded to tests only), the 246 insta and disassembly snapshots, every `[dev-dependencies]` table and the `[[test]]` tables that named missing tests/ files. djs-core's `full`, `embed`, `regexp-unicode-props` and `unicode-normalization` named `djs-prelude/<feature>`, which only its dev-dependency on djs-prelude made valid, so they now name nothing; djs-prelude's own features still turn on djs-core's. rustpython-stdlib's tkinter.rs and re.rs, which no `mod` declared, went too. Trailing blank lines the deletions left at the ends of files were trimmed. Proof: `cargo rustc -p <crate> --lib --profile check --target <t> -- -Zunpretty=expanded` for the 30 touched library crates on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, wasm32-unknown-unknown, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-apple-darwin, master against this change, compared with comments and blank lines dropped: 96 of 120 equal; djs-core differs only in `SOURCE_HASH` and djs-prelude only in `BUILT_BY` (djs-core's build.rs hashes its source text, so any edit changes them; images are keyed on their dependency descriptor, not on it), pymath only in the deleted `pyo3_proptest!` definition, rustpython-pylib only in its frozen modules' order, and rustpython-vm and rustpython-stdlib are equal as multisets of lines except the `-dirty` git identifier and the frozen modules (their derive output and frozen order change between two builds of the same source). rustpython-doc lost only a trailing `cfg(test)` block; cargo cannot expand it or rustpython-derive-impl (untouched) alone, being build-only.
- deps: DEPENDENCIES.md ranks what is left after today's cuts (2026-11-14, its table was empty). Why: every ranked row went today (registry packages to 0, psh's deflate, inflate and SHA, rustls' QUIC, ECH, unbuffered, kTLS, FFDHE, certificate compression, 0-RTT and raw keys, pymath's libm on wasm, RustPython's threading and dead features), so the next cuts needed new numbers. What: one `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-cli --timings` (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3, 3m58s, 659.9 s of unit time over 97 units, a 73,886,048-byte `nanocode`), `cargo bloat --crates` on the same build, `cargo tree -p nanocode-cli` for what links what, and line counts of crates/patches and of the ports outside it (crates/tui, nanocode-compression). Dead code was found with a cfg resolver (output/cfgstrip: `cfg` and `cfg_attr` evaluated with given features on and off and `test` off, the items they drop deleted, and module files no `mod` reaches listed) checked by expanding the crates before and after with `-Zunpretty=expanded`: 99,810 lines of tests in djs, psh, pymath and RustPython that no build compiles (rank 1), djs's `dump`, `lazy`, `compile-cache` and `prelude` features and djs-prelude's `packed`, `names` and `registry`, which nanocode never turns on (rank 2), and rustpython-stdlib's tkinter.rs and re.rs, which no `mod` reaches. The same resolver finds little left in serde, serde_core, serde_json, rustls, rustls-webpki and rustls-pki-types (under 100 lines, arms for `alloc` without `std` and other features nanocode never turns on), and graviola exports nothing nanocode does not call. psh-wasm (1,490 lines) stays: nanocode-ts builds dist/psh.wasm from the psh workspace.
- perf(store-jsonl): replaying the summaries journal indexes only the files its `moved` lines move from, and session file names are decoded and checked in one pass (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: sessions at 14,600). At its first `moved` line the replay built a map from every entry's file to its state ids (14,600 cloned files and ids, 3 MB, on every listing of a store where `archive` ran since the last rewrite); `refresh` now parses the journal's lines first, collects the files `moved` lines move from, and indexes and keeps tracking only entries in those files, which are the only ones a later move looks up, so moves apply as before. `key_of` decoded a name and then re-encoded the key with `file_name` to compare; it now checks while decoding that each literal byte is one `file_name` keeps at that position and each `%XX` is uppercase hex of a byte it escapes (`plain`, shared with `file_name`), which accepts exactly the same names. Checked on store copies: after three new sessions left 8 `moved` and 3 `remember` lines behind the base, master and this build print the same `sessions --all --limit 100000`, and the summaries rewritten by `exec --continue` match master's. Measured as above against the change below it: `nanocode sessions` instructions:u 394.5M -> 370.9M [370.6M, 372.5M], instructions:k 168.5M -> 159.7M [158.4M, 162.7M], page faults 7,366 -> 6,287, peak RSS 33.1 -> 31.3 MB, task-clock 72.7 -> 71.8 ms; `exec --continue` instructions:u 469.3M -> 442.3M, instructions:k 190.1M -> 184.0M, page faults 8,549 -> 7,455, peak RSS 43.6 -> 41.8 MB. Against fx 0.0.16 with bench/cli `BENCH_PERF=1 suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nc,fx --sessions=14600 --storerounds=20 --storehome=<copies of ~/wave/stores>` under tools/netguard.sh and `taskset -c 20-23` (rounds 1-19, median; master in the same harness in brackets): list peak RSS 31.5 MB [47.8] against fx 33.3, instructions:u 370.6M [469.9M] against 500.8M, instructions:k 160.0M [210.7M] against 97.9M, cpu 82.8 ms [99.4] against 71.5; `--continue` peak RSS 40.8 MB [46.0] against 34.7, instructions:k 175.9M [200.8M] against 104.1M, cpu 92.2 ms [101.4] against 74.1. What still trails is kernel time: getdents over 29,200 names (each session's `.owner` file doubles them) and one statx per session file, about 38M instructions each, which fx does not pay because it lists from its index alone. firstframe and oneshot (`suite.mjs --parts=firstframe,oneshot --only=nc`, 3 x 10 rounds interleaved): first-frame RSS 12.04 MB (master), 12.29 MB (master rebuilt: BOLT's training runs move it by about 0.25 MB between builds of the same source) and 11.85 MB (this build), oneshot peak RSS 12.50 / 12.75 / 12.25 MB and cpu 5.88 / 5.51 / 5.03 ms. Checks as above. Files: crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/{summaries.rs,sessions.rs}.
- perf(store-jsonl): the session summaries keep the base they read as one shared string and each entry's summary as a range of it, entries are boxed, and the directory scan keeps only what listing reads (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: sessions at 14,600). What: `Summaries::refresh` parsed the 10.9 MB base into 14,600 owned `Box<RawValue>` copies (8.2 MB) while still holding the bytes it read, so both were resident at once; `base` now turns the frame it read into an `Arc<String>` without copying (the length prefix is dropped in place and the journal behind it split off), parses it with a borrowing `DeserializeSeed`, and stores each summary as `Raw::Base(base, range)`. Summaries remembered later, read from journal lines or from a legacy `.summaries.json` stay `Raw::Owned`; a base entry serializes by reading its text back as a `&RawValue` (a rewrite or a remembered copy), so the bytes written are unchanged. The entries map holds `Box<Summary>`: 14,600 entries need 32,768 buckets, which were 152 bytes each with the summary inline and are 32 now, and every growth rehashed and moved them. `files` returns per session file its key, creation time, `dev:ino` identity, length and path instead of the whole `Metadata` (about 180 bytes) and computes the identity once. On-disk format and behavior are unchanged: on store copies, master and this build list the same sessions in the same order (`sessions`, `sessions --all --limit 100000`), rewrite the same summaries after a forced append failure (an unterminated byte appended to `.summaries`, then `exec --continue`), and read a legacy `.summaries.json` home to the same listing and the same rewritten summaries (compared as parsed JSON with file identities removed). Measured as in the entry below it, against that change, median [p25, p75]: `nanocode sessions` instructions:u 409.8M -> 394.5M [392.8M, 394.8M], instructions:k 183.3M -> 168.5M [164.5M, 170.0M], page faults 10,519 -> 7,366, peak RSS 43.8 -> 33.1 MB, task-clock 77.9 -> 72.7 ms; `exec --continue` instructions:u 492.9M -> 469.3M, instructions:k 211.0M -> 190.1M, page faults 11,799 -> 8,549, peak RSS 47.0 -> 43.6 MB. `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-store-jsonl -- -D warnings` passes natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown. Files: crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/{summaries.rs,sessions.rs}.
- perf(cli): `nanocode sessions` reads a workspace's page through `SessionStore::newest_page`, as `--continue` does, instead of `list_page`, which decoded every cached session summary into a `StateSummary` on every core only to keep the page (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: sessions at 14,600). `--all` still lists through `list_page(None, ..)`. On the same copy of the 14,600-session bench store (~/wave/stores/nc) master and this build print byte-identical `nanocode sessions` and `nanocode sessions --all --limit 100000`. Measured on dev-georgios (32 threads, load about 45) with BOLT shipped builds of master c97e1a49f and of this change, each on its own copy of the store, interleaved run by run, 20 rounds after a warm-up: `perf stat -e instructions:u,instructions:k,page-faults,task-clock` and `/usr/bin/time -f %M` under `taskset -c 20-23`, `nanocode sessions --home` from the bench workspace, median [p25, p75]: instructions:u 469.2M [469.1M, 470.7M] -> 409.8M [409.6M, 411.2M], instructions:k 208.7M [207.3M, 210.7M] -> 183.3M [182.9M, 185.6M], page faults 14,910 -> 10,519, peak RSS 47.8 -> 43.8 MB, task-clock 83.5 -> 77.9 ms; `exec --continue` against bench/cli's fake model is unchanged (instructions:u 495.0M against 492.9M). `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli` passes. Files: bin/nanocode/src/lib.rs.
- perf(cli): on Linux glibc `nanocode` enters through its own C `main` (`nanocode_sys::main!`), so the process skips the Rust runtime start-up work the CLI never needed (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: startup and one-shot per-process cost against fx). Why: `strace` and callgrind of `nanocode --version` showed std's `lang_start` probing the main thread's stack guard with glibc's `pthread_getattr_np`, which opens and scanf-parses /proc/self/maps (most of the 87k of 431k user instructions this commit removes, plus the kernel's rendering of the maps), calls sched_getaffinity, first-touches glibc's malloc (getrandom, brk), and installs SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handlers with a 12 KiB alternate signal stack; once that handler is installed, every thread std spawns repeats pthread_getattr_np, sched_getaffinity, mmap, mprotect, two sigaltstack calls and an munmap (a one-shot spawns 7 threads). A toy with 7 threads (`rustc -O -C panic=abort`) measured 332k against 249k user instructions, 2.05M against 1.67M kernel and 206 against 123 syscalls. What: crates/core/sys/src/entry.rs `prepare` keeps what std's `sys::init` did that the CLI relies on: a closed descriptor 0 to 2 is reopened on /dev/null (fcntl F_GETFD failing with EBADF, as std does where it cannot poll) and SIGPIPE is ignored; `exit` leaves through `std::process::exit`, which runs std's `rt::cleanup` (stdout flush), with the `ExitCode`'s status, found by comparing it with `ExitCode::from(0..=255)` since `ExitCode` has no stable getter. std still reads the arguments from its glibc `.init_array` hook. `nanocode_sys::main!(nanocode_cli::run)` expands to that `extern "C" fn main` on linux-gnu and to the plain `fn main() -> ExitCode` elsewhere, and bin/nanocode is `no_main` only on linux-gnu, so its unsafe code stays in nanocode-sys. Given up: std's `thread 'main' has overflowed its stack` message (an overflow still faults on the kernel's stack guard gap and glibc's guard pages) and the name `main` for the main thread in panic messages. Same behavior checked against master's build: `--bogus` exits 1, `psh-shell -c 'echo hi; exit 7'` prints hi and exits 7, `kill -PIPE $$` exits 141, `--help | head -1` and `yes | psh-shell -c 'head -c 1'` exit 0, and `--version` with fds 0, 1 and 2 closed exits 0. Measured on dev-georgios (load 40 to 56), pinned to CPUs 24-27, interleaved: master c97e1a49f and this commit each built with scripts/build-cli.sh (BOLT 21) and each pre-BOLT binary laid out twice more with build-cli.sh's BOLT steps, since layouts differ by training. `perf stat` of 20 rounds per binary under tools/netguard.sh: `--version` user instructions 430.6k, 430.6k, 430.6k to 343.8k, 344.0k, 344.1k, kernel 1.755M, 1.747M, 1.759M to 1.492M, 1.491M, 1.499M, page faults 124 to 118-119, task clock 0.60-0.66 to 0.54-0.55 ms; one-shot user 8.53M to 8.43M, kernel 9.35-9.43M to 8.97-9.05M, page faults 734-737 against 735-742. bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=startup,oneshot,firstframe --only=nc --rounds=1` under netguard, 20 rounds rotating the two master layouts and two of this commit's: startup CPU 1.147 [1.00-1.24] and 1.139 ms to 0.924 [0.83-1.07] and 1.069 ms, startup max RSS 3.50 to 3.25 MB in all four; one-shot CPU 6.50 and 6.60 to 6.37 and 6.29 ms (load inflates every CPU figure about 2.5 times), one-shot max RSS 12.5 and 12.0 against 12.62 and 12.5 MB and first-frame RSS 11.93 and 11.94 against 12.17 and 11.70 MB (anonymous memory 2.01 against 2.00 MB in all), inside the layout spread. `cargo check --locked` of nanocode-cli's `nanocode` for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and aarch64-apple-darwin and of nanocode-sys for x86_64 glibc and musl, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and wasm32-unknown-unknown pass with master's warnings only; clippy of nanocode-sys and of the bin adds none.
- fix(claude): Write and Edit refuse a path whose last component is a symbolic link with `Refusing to write <path>: it is a symbolic link. Write to the link's target path instead: <target>.`, Write after a token-truncated Read answers `File has not been read yet. Read it first before writing to it.`, and Write names a directory or a non-regular file by the given `file_path` in Claude Code 2.1.300's texts (2026-11-14, the two items the claude-read entry below left). Stock behavior read from its bundled cli (~/hill/stock/rt/claude-glibc/claude): `Npe` runs in the `checkPermissions` of Write, Edit and NotebookEdit, after `validateInput`, and denies when `wi(fw(file_path)).leafIsSymlink`, printing the lexically resolved absolute path and the link's landing; a denial reaches the model as plain error text, not `<tool_use_error>`. Read stores `isPartialView` only when it cut a page to the token cap (`In`, the `showing lines 1-N of M total` or `showing the first N of M characters` banner, which needs no offset past 1 and no limit); Write's `validateInput` answers `Vin` for such a view whatever the mtime, before its stale check, and Edit keeps `isPartialView` on an existing file (`Wt&&In?.isPartialView`), so a later Write still refuses; Edit itself is allowed. What: `View::Truncated` is the view of a Read with no paging whose result is not whole; `ClaudeWorkspaceFiles::write` returns `NOT_READ` (new beside `MODIFIED_SINCE_READ`) for it and `edit` keeps it. `link` resolves `file_path` lexically (`lexical`), and for a symbolic link `landing` follows it to the canonical target, or, for a dangling link, the hops' last path (stock prints `…/nothere.txt` and `…/nodir/x.txt`); an unresolvable link (a loop) is not refused and keeps the path error. Write refuses a dangling link before `write_target`, which created the link's missing parent directories and the target, and an existing one after the not-read and stale checks; Edit refuses after its string checks, in both the existing and the creating path. Write, Edit and `execute_sync` return `ToolOutput`, so the refusal is `ToolOutput::error` and the other errors keep `<tool_use_error>`. `write_target` answers `<file_path> is a directory, not a file. To create a file inside it, include the file name in file_path.` and `<file_path> exists but is not a regular file (a device, FIFO or socket). Write only creates or overwrites regular files.` instead of `target is not a regular file`. The host file tools (`FileHost`) see no symbolic links or reads and are unchanged. Measured on a copy of the claude-read parity mock (~/wt/cwe-par: mock3.py with count_tokens answering a quarter of the messages' JSON length, so stock cuts pages to its token cap, and a new scenario `wedge`, 36 tool calls: token-truncated Reads followed by Write, Edit then Write, a paged Read then Write, a removed file; Write through relative, absolute, chained, dangling, parent-missing and looping links, through a symlinked directory and in it, a link to a directory, a directory by relative and absolute path, a FIFO; Edit through a link with a present and a missing string and a dangling link with an empty old_string), identical tool_result texts after masking the run directory (rdiff.py), stock 2.1.300 against the claude-read build and this one: wedge 7 -> 30 of 36 (left: the four truncated Read pages, whose line counts follow stock's count_tokens; the loop's ELOOP text; a final `ls` whose bytes shift with the run directory's length), reads 28 -> 30 of 43, edit 15, texts 45 and read 15 of 18 unchanged. Not done: stock 2.1.300 sends the truncation banner as a separate `system` role message after the tool result, with the allow_large hint, where nanocode appends it to the result in `<system-reminder>`. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude-tools` (no warnings), `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` for the parity runs. Files: crates/backends/claude/tools/src/tools/{text_files,workspace_files}.rs.
- perf(cli): `Host::start` and `Host::open` wait for a custom endpoint's model list only when no context window is given (`--context-window` or `NANOCODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW`), since the list is read at agent start only for a listed custom model's window, which an explicit window replaces (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 latency track: Ready 174 to 178 ms on Messages with 37f0aeb in ~/hill/tmp/ttft2 against 51 to 53 ms with 77765bb in SLA.md, target 30 / 60 ms). No commit between 77765bb and master adds the time. The ttft2 Messages lane also exports `NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` (the morning lane did not: 0 `/v1/models` GETs from it in ~/hill/tmp/ttft-proxy.jsonl), so a `--harness claude` session lists the OpenAI endpoint's models (54 GETs in ttft2's proxy.jsonl, 90 to 120 ms p50 through the meter proxy) and the session's agent waits for them. The bench's live lanes time spawn to "new session", which is drawn when the agent starts, not when the composer opens. With the same environment, 77765bb, 37f0aeb and master c97e1a49f take the same time to "new session" (a mock that answers `/v1/models` after 120 ms: 136 to 139 ms p50 each), and since eda8a6007 the composer opens in 12 to 14 ms. Without `NANOCODE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` all three draw "new session" in 11 to 19 ms. The first Enter and the first request of `nanocode exec` waited for the list in the same way. Now an explicit window skips the wait: a list that fails then shows only in the /model and /harness pickers and `nanocode models`, and no longer ends a session that cannot use it. Without an explicit window the wait, the listed window and the failure at session start are unchanged. Measured with release builds of master c97e1a49f and this change, a local mock (~/wt/rr/mock.py: `/v1/models` after 120 ms, 404 for the rest, Anthropic base `/ant/v1`, OpenAI base `/oai/v1`) and a PTY harness that times spawn to "Ask anything" and to "new session" (~/wt/rr/bench.py, the ttft2 environment and `--thinking low --no-tempo-tools -m vercel/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 --ephemeral`, 120x40, builds interleaved), 12 sessions per build and route: "new session" p50 139.0 to 16.9 ms on Messages and 137.6 to 15.5 ms on Responses, "Ask anything" 14.0 and 14.3 ms on both builds. With `NANOCODE_CONTEXT_WINDOW` unset (6 sessions each) both builds draw "new session" at 136 to 140 ms. `nanocode exec --harness claude` (~/wt/rr/execbench.py, 8 runs each), spawn to the request at the mock: 141.1 to 19.6 ms p50, and 141.6 against 141.7 ms with the window unset. With the OpenAI base on a closed port, master exits with `failed to list models from …` before any request with and without the window, and this change sends the request with the window and exits as master does without it. File: bin/nanocode/src/host.rs.
- docs(sla): the live TTFT matrix at 30 sessions x 3 turns per cell with hedged first-byte requests (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 latency gate). Lanes interleaved, prompts unique, Enter to the first reply token drawn: master 1d4463636 as shipped (hedge) and with `NANOCODE_HEDGE_CAP_PERCENT=0` (cap 0) against Claude Code 2.1.318 (hosted Hand, API key, egress proxy; haiku from the hedged-requests lane's run of the same lanes) and Codex CLI 0.166.0 (dev-georgios, ChatGPT login). Result: nanocode wins all 18 Claude p50 cells and 20 of 24 GPT p50 cells (losses gpt-6-luna turn 2 in both lanes, gpt-6.1-sol turn 3 hedged, gpt-6-astra turn 2 cap 0), and loses p99 in 3/9 (hedge) and 2/9 (cap 0) Claude cells and 5/12 (hedge) and 9/12 (cap 0) GPT cells. Hedging cuts GPT tails (gpt-6-luna turn 1 p99 7,379 to 3,166 ms, gpt-6-astra turn 3 8,129 to 3,833) but not gpt-6-luna turns 2 and 3 or gpt-6.1-sol turns 1 and 2. Commands: `node bench/sla/run.ts --live --rejected --key --lanes=rejected-nc-claude@hedge,rejected-nc-claude@nohedge,rejected-claude --claude-model=<m> --samples=30 --turns=3 --settle=3000 --timeout=30000` and `--live --lanes=live-nc-codex@hedge,live-nc-codex@nohedge,live-codex --codex-model=<m> --samples=30 --turns=3 --settle=3000 --timeout=60000`; SLA.md has the tables.
- deps(rustls): the vendored rustls loses RFC 7250 raw public keys, 347 of its 24,249 lines, and rustls-webpki its `RawPublicKeyEntity`, 53 of its 5,670 (2026-11-14, cutting vendored code: DEPENDENCIES.md rank 1). Why: no nanocode config uses raw keys (no resolver returns `only_raw_public_keys`, no verifier `requires_raw_public_keys`: nanocode-tls, the platform verifier, store-sql's verifiers and the mpp and egress servers all keep the defaults), so the client never offered a certificate type and the server always sent X.509. What: `CertificateType`, `AlwaysResolvesClientRawPublicKeys` and `AlwaysResolvesServerRawPublicKeys`, `ResolvesClientCert::only_raw_public_keys`, `ResolvesServerCert::only_raw_public_keys`, `ServerCertVerifier::requires_raw_public_keys` and `ClientCertVerifier::requires_raw_public_keys`, `ClientHello::server_cert_types` and `client_cert_types`, `verify_tls13_signature_with_raw_key`, the client's offer and its checks of the server's answer, the server's negotiation and echo, the client_certificate_type and server_certificate_type fields of `ClientExtensions` and `ServerExtensions` (both now read as unknown extensions) and PeerIncompatible's `IncorrectCertificateTypeExtension` and `UnsolicitedCertificateTypeExtension`; the `ExtensionType` names stay. Wire: every connection nanocode makes or serves is unchanged; toward a client that offers the extensions, this server now answers as a server that never implemented RFC 7250: master's server echoed X.509 (in EncryptedExtensions for TLS 1.3, in ServerHello for TLS 1.2) when the offered list held X.509, and now echoes nothing; it aborted with handshake_failure when the list held no X.509 (raw keys only, say), and now sends its X.509 chain, which a client requiring raw keys then refuses itself (master's TLS 1.3 client with handshake_failure after EncryptedExtensions; its TLS 1.2 client never checks and completes); a list with neither was already ignored. A malformed offer (an empty or truncated list) was a decode_error and is now ignored, and a duplicated one is still refused. As a client: rustls never offered, so a server's certificate-type extension was and stays an unsolicited extension (unsupported_extension), except that a malformed body was a decode_error first. output/rustls-equality checks it against a reference built for it, master's rustls with only its two server certificate-type checks (`validate_server_cert_type_extension`, `validate_client_cert_type_extension`) taken out, which answers a well-formed offer as a server without RFC 7250 does, with 0 differences: all four OLD/NEW pairings on 30,000 deterministic cases (828 MB of wire bytes per pairing) and 3,000 real-crypto cases; `offerraw`, master's client offering certificate types either itself (a verifier requiring raw keys and a client resolver with only raw keys, so it sends server_certificate_type and client_certificate_type of [RawPublicKey]) or through a ClientHello rewritten in flight to carry one or both extensions with one to three of X.509, OpenPGP, RawPublicKey, 1609Dot2 and an unassigned type (254,877 ClientHellos rewritten), against this server and the reference (100,000 deterministic cases, 662 MB, and 5,000 real-crypto cases); `offer`, the same offers mixed with the previous cut's 0-RTT offers, also against master's server for the 0-RTT-only cases (100,000 deterministic cases, 1.25 GB, and 5,000 real-crypto cases); `serve`, master's server resolving only raw keys in one case of four (and accepting 0-RTT otherwise) against master's client and this client (100,000 deterministic cases, 2.62 GB, and 5,000 real-crypto cases). Control: master's server answers the certificate-type offers with other bytes than this server in 60,020 of 100,000 `offerraw` cases (2,588 of 5,000 real-crypto), so they reach the removed code. - deps(rustls): the vendored rustls loses TLS 1.3 early data (0-RTT), the client's sending and the server's accepting, 830 of its 25,079 lines (2026-11-14, cutting vendored code: DEPENDENCIES.md rank 1). Why: no nanocode client turns early data on and no nanocode server accepts it: every `ClientConfig` (nanocode-tls's native and webpki configs, nanocode-http's HTTP/1 copy, store-sql's Postgres configs, the sandbox egress upstream and nanocode-sim's) keeps `enable_early_data` false, and every `ServerConfig` (the mpp proxy's and the egress proxy's minted ones) keeps `max_early_data_size` 0, so the client never offered early_data and the server declined every offer. What: the client loses `ClientConfig::enable_early_data`, its `EarlyData` state, `WriteEarlyData`, `ClientConnection::early_data` and `is_early_data_accepted`, the client early traffic secret, EndOfEarlyData, `CommonState::early_traffic` and `send_early_plaintext`, and `Tls13ClientSessionValue`'s `max_early_data_size` with the NewSessionTicket early_data extension it came from (`NewSessionTicketExtensions` goes: the ticket's extensions are read, checked for duplicates and dropped, as a rustls that never knew one reads any unknown); the server loses `ServerConfig::max_early_data_size`, `ServerConnection::early_data` and `reject_early_data`, `ReadEarlyData`, its `EarlyDataState`, the accept decision with ticket freshness (`ServerSessionValue::set_freshness`, `is_fresh` and `MAX_FRESHNESS_SKEW_MS`), `ExpectEarlyData`, the early_data ack in EncryptedExtensions and in NewSessionTicket, and the client_early_traffic_secret it derived on every resumption only to replace it before any record was read; `HandshakePayload::EndOfEarlyData`, `SecretKind::ClientEarlyTrafficSecret`, `KeyScheduleTrafficWithClientFinishedPending::update_decrypter` and PeerMisbehaved's `EarlyDataExtensionWithoutResumption`, `EarlyDataOfferedWithVariedCipherSuite`, `InvalidMaxEarlyDataSize`, `OfferedEarlyDataWithOldProtocolVersion` and `TooMuchEarlyDataReceived` go too. Kept: the server still reads a client's early_data request and declines it as RFC 8446 4.2.10 asks, skipping 0-RTT records it cannot decrypt up to one maximum-size record (16,384 bytes, the old default for a server with max_early_data_size 0, now `MAX_FRAGMENT_LEN`), also after a HelloRetryRequest, and still refuses early_data in a second ClientHello; the early_data names in `ExtensionType` and `HandshakeType` stay. Wire: every connection nanocode makes or serves is unchanged, and so is the answer to a client offering 0-RTT with a stale ticket. Differences only toward malformed peers: a NewSessionTicket whose early_data body is not 4 bytes was a decode_error and is now ignored (a duplicated one is still refused); an EndOfEarlyData with a body was a decode_error and is now an unexpected_message (it was unexpected in every state already); an early_data ack in EncryptedExtensions was and stays an unsolicited extension (unsupported_extension), since the client never offers it. Off the wire: a server no longer reads its clock when it receives a PSK offer, so one whose time provider fails no longer refuses the offer with `FailedToGetCurrentTime` (it could not have issued a ticket), and a key log no longer gets CLIENT_EARLY_TRAFFIC_SECRET lines (nanocode sets no key log). output/rustls-equality now builds three rustls side by side: master's, a reference (master without its two RFC 7250 server checks, for the next cut) and this one, with 0 differences: all four OLD/NEW pairings on 30,000 deterministic cases (828 MB of wire bytes per pairing) and 3,000 real-crypto cases; `offer0rtt`, where master's client turns early data on behind a session store that stamps every ticket's max_early_data_size with 1, 100, 1,000, 16,384, 16,385, 20,000, 65,536 or a random size up to 100,000 (the ticket a server that once allowed 0-RTT left behind) and writes 0 to 40,000 bytes of early data into the resumed connection, against this server, the reference and master's server as nanocode configures it (100,000 deterministic cases, 3.35 GB, 109,548 early-data writes, and 5,000 real-crypto cases); `serve`, where master's server sets max_early_data_size to the same sizes (so its tickets carry early_data and it accepts 0-RTT), or in one case of four only resolves raw public keys, against master's client and this client as nanocode configures them (100,000 deterministic cases, 2.62 GB, and 5,000 real-crypto cases). Controls: master's server accepting early data gives other bytes than this server in 41,039 of 100,000 `offer0rtt` cases (407 of 5,000 real-crypto), and master's client offering 0-RTT gives other bytes than the nanocode client in 24,585 of 74,904 `serve` cases with an accepting server (1,049 of 3,762 real-crypto), so the offers reach the removed code.
