- fix(codex): a custom model's tool output enters the history cut to 12,000 bytes (a 3,000-token budget, head and tail around `…N tokens truncated…`), as Codex 0.162.1 records it, instead of the 12,000 tokens (about 48 KB) every model had (2026-11-14). Stock: `record_prepared_conversation_items` (codex-rs/core/src/session/mod.rs at rust-v0.162.1) stamps each function and custom tool output with `history_truncation_token_limit = with_serialization_allowance(model_info.truncation_policy).token_budget()`, and `ContextManager::record_item_with_metadata` (core/src/context_manager/history.rs) truncates the output with `TruncationPolicy::Tokens` of that limit. The unknown-model policy `{mode: bytes, limit: 10000}` times 1.2 is `Bytes(12000)`, whose token budget is 3,000, so the marker counts tokens, not characters; OpenAI models' `{mode: tokens, limit: 10000}` give 12,000, which `TOOL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT` already was. What: `ContextManager` keeps `tool_output_token_limit` (default `TOOL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT`) and `truncate_tool_output` takes it; `ManagedSessionState::set_tool_output_token_limit` sets it; `ModelRun::execute_model_tools` sets it before it appends a batch's outputs, from `history_tool_output_tokens(model)`: `with_serialization_allowance(model.tool_output_token_budget())` (2,500 -> 3,000) for a model that `truncates_tool_output_by_bytes`, else `TOOL_OUTPUT_TOKEN_LIMIT`. `with_serialization_allowance` (upstream's `policy * 1.2` rounded up, `tokens + tokens.div_ceil(5)`) is exported beside the limit. The ToolResult event's `visible_output` uses the same limit, so a logged result is what the model received. A history replayed by `ManagedSessionState::new`/`resume` keeps the default bound, which leaves outputs already cut to 3,000 tokens unchanged. Built-in models (Sol, Terra, Luna, Astra, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, Daybreak Blue) keep 12,000 tokens. exec_command and write_stdin outputs already fit (their response budget reserves the header), so this binds on other outputs over 12,000 bytes, such as view_image and unsupported-call errors that echo a long path or name, and Code Mode results. Measured with a debug build of this tree against ~/hill/stock codex 0.162.1 on ~/wt/codex-histtrunc-par/mock3.py scenario `hist` (ds/low, 14 tool calls: view_image of a 20,000-byte and a 9,000 x `é` path, unsupported calls of 20,000, 11,982, 11,983, 60,000 and 5,000 x `€` name bytes, two long-workdir exec_command errors, `seq 1 100000` with and without `max_output_tokens`, a write_stdin poll of `seq 1 30000`, a real image), last request's function_call_output items with chunk IDs, wall times and session IDs masked: master (13f3502) matches stock on 6 of 14 (20,132-, 20,018-, 18,132-, 12,001- and 15,018-byte outputs went in whole, the 60,018-byte one as 48,027 bytes), this build on 10 of 14 with the same bytes and markers (`…2033…`, `…2005…`, `…1533…`, `…1…`, `…12005…`, `…755 tokens truncated…`); the other 4 differ only in the run directory in the echoed path and the C library's ENAMETOOLONG text (stock's musl `Filename too long`, glibc `File name too long`), and each equals stock's algorithm (3,000 tokens, floor and ceil char boundaries) applied to nanocode's own message. `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-backend-codex-client and nanocode-backend-codex natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown and `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode` pass without warnings. Files: crates/backends/codex/client/src/session/{context,mod,state}.rs, crates/backends/codex/src/model/run/tool_calls.rs.
- fix(claude): Write answers `File has been modified since read, either by the user or by a linter. Read it again before attempting to write it.` when the file changed on disk after the model read it, and Write and Edit results name the file by the `file_path` the model sent, as Claude Code 2.1.300 does (2026-11-14, parity findings L6/M2 and the open issues of the claude-texts entry below). Stock behavior read from its bundled cli (~/hill/stock/rt/claude-glibc/claude: Write's `validateInput` refuses with `Y1n()` when `mtime > readFileState.timestamp` and the bytes differ from a whole view (`DC`, `X1n`), or on any mtime change after a view that started past line 1; the Write and Edit result mappers print `filePath`, which is the input `file_path`) and measured with a new parity scenario `reads` (43 tool calls, ~/wt/claude-read-par/reads_scen.py on mock3.py, stock 2.1.300 beside the old and the new nanocode). What: `ClaudeWorkspaceFiles::write` runs the check `edit` already runs for its error path: with a recorded view, a newer mtime, and bytes that are not the digest of a `Whole` or `Current` view (a `Part` view never matches), it returns `MODIFIED_SINCE_READ`, which reaches the model as `<tool_use_error>…</tool_use_error>`; a touch that leaves the bytes alone, a file never read, and a new file still write. Write and Edit, in the workspace and the host file tools, print the given path (`sub/rel2.txt`, `./sub/rel3.txt`, `/w/sub/../sub/rel4.txt`) instead of the canonical absolute one. Measured (identical tool_result texts after masking the run directory, rdiff.py): reads 22 -> 29 of 43, edit 14 -> 15 of 15, texts 45 and read 15 unchanged; Write and Edit results in `reads` 1,974 -> 1,867 characters (stock 1,889) with the run directory masked, and each relative call saves the length of the working directory. Not taken: Read dedupe (`Wasted call — file unchanged since your last Read. Refer to that earlier tool_result instead.`, keyed by path, offset and limit with an unchanged mtime) fired 0 times in 412 stock-claude Reads of 191 cmp2 trials, with 0 identical re-reads, and stock clears that state on compaction while nanocode's file tools see neither compaction nor whether a Code Mode or subagent call put the earlier result in the model's context, so a wrong `Wasted call` would cost a turn; offset 0, which stock numbers from `0`, saves nothing and shifts every shown line number by one from the line the model must pass back as `offset`. Left: stock refuses Write through a symbolic link (`Refusing to write <path>: it is a symbolic link. Write to the link's target path instead: <target>.`) and Write after a token-truncated Read (`File has not been read yet. Read it first before writing to it.`). - fix(claude): once the response after a max_tokens continuation finishes, the thinking of the cut replies leaves the history; a cut reply that held only thinking is removed and its continuation text joins the user message before it, as Claude Code 2.1.300 sends it (2026-11-14, ~/hill/analysis/glm-runaway.md "Not done"). The continuation request itself is unchanged: it still carries the cut thinking, which is what lets GLM-5.3-Flash finish (6 of 6 live replays in the glm-runaway lane, against Claude Code's recovery without it, which ran to the cap). After it, the dead thinking was billed on every later call: in cmp2 GLM nc-claude, 3 of 4 cuts were followed by more calls (circuit-fibsqrt-a2-t0 29, regex-chess-a1-t0 18, winning-avg-corewars-a2-t1 4), each carrying the 65,536-token cut, 3.34M input tokens over 51 calls (~/wt/claude-cutthink-p3/carry.py); regex-chess-a1-t0's last request held a 225,579-character cut thinking block. `drop_cut_thinking` runs when a response is not a text-only max_tokens stop (a stop with a tool call counts as answered): it walks back over the trailing pairs of an assistant message followed by a user message that holds only `OUTPUT_LIMIT_CONTINUATION` (the nudge text, now a constant), drops Thinking and RedactedThinking blocks from the assistant message, and when nothing is left removes it and appends the nudge's blocks to the nearest earlier non-System message if that is a user message (System notices sit after tool results, and `wire_messages` moves them past user messages anyway); text of a cut reply stays. Mock (~/wt/claude-cutthink-p3: mock.py adds signed thinking blocks and logs per request its bytes and violations: a thinking block whose text no longer matches its signature, two consecutive same-role messages, or a final tool_use turn not led by thinking), stock Claude Code 2.1.300 against nanocode f4a02a256 and this tree, debug builds: cutthink (call, a 288,889-character thinking-only cut, a continuation with a call, 5 more calls) sends requests identical to f4a02a256 up to and including the continuation (requests 1 to 3, messages compared after normalizing paths, tool ids and the token budget), then 23.6 to 27.1 KB per request instead of 312.7 to 316.1 KB (all 6 later requests, 0 violations; stock 71.8 to 75.2 KB, whose system prompt is 48 KB larger); cutthink2 (two cuts in a row) 23.9 to 27.3 KB instead of 662.0 to 665.4 KB, ending in `[tool_result, nudge, nudge]` as stock; cutthinktext (thinking and text cut) keeps the text and drops the thinking, 23.8 to 27.2 KB instead of 312.8 to 316.2 (stock keeps both: 360.9 to 364.3 KB); cutthinkfirst (cut on the first call) merges the nudge into the prompt message as stock; cutthinktool (the continuation is itself cut inside a tool_use) also drops it; cutthinkend (the continuation ends the turn) unchanged. The parity scenarios maxtok, maxtok3, maxtok4 and maxtok5 send identical requests and exit codes before and after. Not measured: Anthropic's first-party `block_binding` (`prefix_mismatch_behavior: drop_block`) might drop the continuation's own thinking server-side if its binding covers the removed block; no live call was made (gateway wallet empty).
