- nanocode-sim's `cell_rows` expects 3 rows (plus the admission row of a durable submit) for a clean turn whose cell makes one External call (2026-11-14). 97866818c commits the cell journal once the External result is buffered and the cell waits or finishes, so a restart replays the result instead of an unknown outcome, and `turns` failed 331 of 2,000 seeds on master since, every one on `cell_rows` (an External turn wrote 4 rows, not 3, or 3 buffered, not 2). With the new count `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 2000 5 --scenario turns --policy turnlog --twice` passes 2,000 of 2,000, also with `--retain 0`, `--snapshot-rows 4` and both.
- `nanocode-turnlog` keeps a session's tail in one row: with `snapshot_rows` set, a plain commit extends the last `r` row instead of inserting a row, through the new `LogHost::extend` (2026-11-14, Georgios: a cold open reads a constant number of rows, ideally under 20). Why: a cold open read the last snapshot and every row after it (`k + 2` rows for a tail of k rows), so with `snapshot_rows` 64 the log statement read 1 to 66 rows and the whole cold turn 22 to 80, depending on where the session was in the snapshot cycle. A snapshot every few rows would bound that but writes the whole state each time, and on Durable Objects a written row bills as 1,000 read rows. What changed: (1) `Stream::pack` pads each row's deflate output to a multiple of 3 bytes with empty stored blocks (`00 00 00 ff ff`, at most two) before the final empty block, so the base64 text of two rows concatenates into the base64 of one stream; consecutive rows of one segment already form one deflate stream (sync flush, the previous plain as dictionary), so `rows` decodes an extended row with the dictionary of its first part. Old readers decode the padded rows. A commit that may extend the tail packs its records with a leading newline, so an extended row stays one record per line for readers that split on newlines (durable-cloudflare scripts/measure-faults.mjs does; `decode` streams JSON values and reads both). Without it the fault harness failed every scenario with a JSON parse error. (2) `LogHost::extend(scope, Extension { cut, row, seq, tail })` moves row `row` to key `seq`, drops its last `cut` characters (the final block, `SEAL` = 3) and appends `tail`. It returns `None` by default, and the writer then appends as before, so other hosts are unchanged. `SqlLog` runs one `UPDATE nanocode_log SET seq = ?3, body = substr(body, 1, length(body) - ?4) || ?5 WHERE scope = ?1 AND seq = ?2 RETURNING CAST(seq AS TEXT)` and answers `Fenced` when no row moved (the seq comes back as text because the nanocode-ts SQL bridge rejects any cell that is not text or null; with `RETURNING 1` the update committed and its reply failed); a key that another writer already took fails on the primary key. That keeps the fencing of `INSERT`: two writers that share `next` cannot both move the row or both take the key. `MemoryLog` does the same in its `Atom`. (3) The writer extends only when the commit writes one plain `r` row (no snapshot, no boundary, no parts), `snapshot_rows` is set, the result fits `row_limit`, and neither the commit nor the tail row holds a `Recovery` record. `Recovery { at: None }` takes the row's key as `at` on load, so a recovery row is never moved. `open` takes the last stored row as the tail when it is an aligned `r` row without parts and without `Recovery`. Since the row moves to the commit's seq, `next`, `Fold::seq`, `recovering` and `next_attempt` reload as before. `tail_rows` at open is now `next - 1 - snapshot seq` (seqs, not stored rows), the same number for every log written before, so the snapshot cadence is unchanged. Cost: the `UPDATE` reads 2 rows and writes 1 (an `INSERT` writes 1, measured in miniflare), and SQLite rewrites the tail row, which grows to at most `snapshot_rows` commits, at each commit; parameter bytes per commit grow by about 3 B. Measured with durable-cloudflare output/cold.mjs (a copy of output/turns.mjs that also runs a 200-turn session and counts the cold turn alone: restart, one turn, metrics), local workerd, the build-8f204d2 dry-run bundle with nanocode_wasm.wasm built from nanocode-ts e94cf80 against this SDK (base: master 36faa48f2; `cargo build --profile wasm`, `wasm-opt -O3 --one-caller-inline-max-function-size=100 -Oz` as scripts/build.mjs does), 2 interleaved rounds, 3 cold opens each, both rounds identical in rows. Cold turn rows read after 43 turns: 58/61/64 -> 15/15/15 (log statement 44/47/50 -> 1); after 200 turns: 22/25/28 -> 17/17/17 (log 8/11/14 -> 3). Rows written by the cold turn: 3 -> 3. Warm turns (5 each, statements/rows written/rows read): reply 1/1/0 -> 1/1/2, cell 1/1/0 -> 1/1/2, timer 2/2/0 -> 2/2/4, charge 2/2/0 -> 2/2/4. Cold turn ms on the quiet round: 274/202/181 -> 221/188/186 at 43 turns, 177/199/192 -> 206/229/187 at 200 (noise). nanocode-sim: `SimHost` and `CellHost` implement `extend` (the sim's staged insert plus a staged drop of the old row, so a crash drops both), the cells scenario passes `snapshot_rows`, and the commit path applies a tick's compactions before it decodes the committed rows (it decoded the old and the moved row together). New invariant: after a commit that stored one more row, that row is not one the writer could have merged into the row before it (both aligned `r` rows, no `Recovery`, within `row_limit`). Mutation `tail_rows_appended` (the host answers `extend` with `None`) is caught on 1,986 of 2,000 seeds (`sweep.sh 0 2000 5 --scenario turns --policy turnlog --twice --snapshot-rows 4 --mutation tail_rows_appended`). Second new invariant: with `snapshot_rows` set, after every commit a `TurnLog::open` of the stored rows agrees with the live writer on `recovering()` and on `next_attempt` for every unfinished turn. A source mutation that drops the `Recovery` guard (extends into and from rows holding `Recovery`) passes every other check but fails this one on 1,849 of 2,000 seeds with `--twice --snapshot-rows 4` and 1,517 of 2,000 with `--twice --snapshot-rows 2 --retain 0` (the reload reads `recovering` true and attempt 2 where the writer holds false and 1). Checks (seeds 0..2000, 5 jobs): `--twice`, `--twice --retain 0`, `--twice --snapshot-rows 4`, `--twice --retain 0 --snapshot-rows 4`, `--twice --snapshot-rows 3 --row-limit 1024`, `--twice --calm --snapshot-rows 2` and `--twice --snapshot-rows 4 --state-bytes 131072` pass 2,000 of 2,000 with 0 panics. A MemoryLog harness (60 commits, `snapshot_rows` 4, reopen every 1, 2, 3, 5 or no commits, every stored row decoded after each commit) decodes every row. durable-cloudflare with the build-8f204d2 bundle and this wasm: `node scripts/drill.mjs` completes charge, waiting and deploys with no failures, and `node scripts/measure-faults.mjs --seed 1` runs 1,340 checks with no findings once its `admission`, `finish` and `call` plans also arm a `BEFORE UPDATE ON nanocode_log` trigger (a refused commit is now an `INSERT` or an `UPDATE`; durable-cloudflare change). durable-vercel `npm run drill` with this wasm passes 8 of 8 (its SQL log shows 5 `turn_log_extend` against 3 `turn_log_append` per drill). `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-turnlog -p nanocode-agent`, the same for `nanocode-turnlog` and for `nanocode-agent -p nanocode-code-mode --features nanocode-code-mode/local-cells` with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo +1.97.1 clippy --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-turnlog -- -D warnings -A clippy::useless_conversion` on both targets pass; clippy on nanocode-sim reports only the two lints in src/alloc.rs that master already has. Files: crates/core/turnlog/src/{codec,host,lib,writer}.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/src/{cells,turnlog,turns}.rs.
- perf(subagents): the root receives subagent completions in one batched prompt per wake, and while its direct children run each wake waits as long as the time since the first wake (2026-11-14, swarm hill-climb lane root). Before, `continue_root` drained only the completions already queued, so the root woke about once per finished concurrency slot (309 model calls for 10,000 children) and each wake appended one full continuation prompt per child (about 400 bytes with its instructions and marker). Every root call sends the whole context, so the root's request bytes grew with calls times context: about 62 KB per child at 10,000 children. Now, after a wake, the loop keeps collecting completions until `last + (last - first)` of the root's wake times, and it also waits until a steered batch reaches the running turn (`SteerWatch.injected`) before it routes the next one. The wake times reset when the root has no active direct child, and then a batch goes out at once, so the last results arrive without delay. The number of wakes grows with the logarithm of the swarm's duration. A batch of two or more completions is one prompt: one line per child (`Subagent N completed: <output>`, `failed: <error>`, or interrupted), the continuation instructions once, and one `<subagent_completion>` marker for the last child, which is what `parse_completion_prompt` returned for the joined prompts before. A single completion keeps its prompt. The root reads the same ids, statuses and outputs, later. Measured with durable-cloudflare `scripts/hillclimb.mjs` (mock provider, `--agents 10000 --batch 100 --rate 200 --scenarios score`, in-object with `maxConcurrentSubagents: 64`, nanocode-ts bc9a923 built on its pinned SDK 36faa48f2 with this change cherry-picked; this commit's parent adds 87df9f7f4 and 38f05b9fb to crates/runtime/subagents, which these runs do not include; 5-core Hand shared with four other benchmark lanes, interleaved master, change, master, change): root bytes per child 62,359 / 62,512 -> 142 / 148, root calls 309 / 309 -> 15 / 15, wall 559.7 / 572.0 -> 595.9 / 608.8 s, saturation 0.185 / 0.181 -> 0.170 / 0.166, parent peak wasm 1,696 / 1,672 -> 1,123 / 1,125 MB, parent rows written per child 1.11 / 1.11 -> 1.16 / 1.16 (`s6-master-10k`, `s6-after-10k`, `s6-master-10k-2`, `s6-after-10k-2`). Parent bytes per child fell from 169,581 / 167,169 to 112,283 / 112,512. Wall rose by 6.4% in both pairs, and the mean child active time rose from 2.10 / 2.22 s to 2.30 / 2.38 s, on a Hand with load average 2 to 4 from the other lanes. The mock provider answers a root call at once, so these runs do not include the time a real provider takes for 309 root calls whose request bytes add up to 624 MB. The crash gate at 2,000 children (`--agents 2000 --gate-agents 2000 --scenarios spawn,turn,done,twice`, `s6-gate-after-2k`) passes: lost 0, repeated after done 0, repeated outside in flight 0 in every scenario; restart ready 1,045 ms, first call 2,445 ms, list 1,451 ms. `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-subagents -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked -p nanocode-subagents --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check crates/runtime/subagents/src/runtime.rs` pass.
- perf(code-mode): a OneLog restart parses each tool catalog once and restores every session's cell journals in one CellJournals update (2026-11-14, restart lane). At 10K in-object children (nanocode-ts DO, durable-cloudflare hillclimb turn scenario saved at its kill point, 5004 cells: the root's spawn cell and 5003 finished child exec cells), `OneLog::journals` took 4.5 to 5.9 s of the restart natively: every cell header carries the same `$nanocode_tools` mark, and `OneLog::cells` parsed the 27 KB catalog again for each of them, `CellJournal::fold` deep-copied it (`header.tools.to_vec()`), and `OneLog::journals` inserted each session into `CellJournals.restored` with its own `Atom::update`, which clones the whole map each time (O(N^2) in sessions). Now `OneLog::cells` keeps the parsed catalogs of one call by digest, `CellJournal.tools` is `Arc<[Value]>` like `CellJournalHeader.tools` and `CellRecord.tools` so fold, `CellRecord::snapshot` and `CodeModeRuntime` share it, and `CellJournals::restore_sessions` inserts all sessions in one update. Measured with output/restart-bench (native, 4 workers) restarting a copy of the DO's SQLite log (5414 rows, last snapshot 18 MB packed / 128 MB plain) through `nanocode::turnlog` with the wasm host's policy (`snapshot_rows: Some(64)`), `--mode restart --store onelog --scope owner --session <root> --agents 10000 --latency 50 --calls 50`, 3 interleaved rounds on the shared 5-core Hand: first model request after restart base 6588 / 6132 / 6977 ms, change 1634 / 1634 / 1919 ms; `OneLog::journals` base 4.5 to 5.0 s, change 0.11 to 0.17 s; `TurnLog::open` unchanged at 0.9 to 1.1 s. In the nanocode-ts Durable Object (durable-cloudflare scripts/hillclimb.mjs turn scenario at 10K agents, state saved at its kill point and restarted from copies of it: output/restart-snap.mjs with SNAP_SAVE, then SNAP_LOAD, interleaved, bundles built from nanocode 22f8297d9 with and without this change on nanocode-ts 177b460), first model request after restart base 7389 / 6235 / 7163 ms, change 4662 / 4025 / 4300 ms; `sdk.open` base 3709 / 3344 / 3837 ms, change 1411 / 1158 / 1217 ms; longest wasm.enter base 3660 / 3316 / 3805 ms, change 1857 / 1786 / 1739 ms; parent wasm memory 1605 MB to 957 MB. Crash gate with the change, `hillclimb.mjs --agents 2000 --scenarios spawn,turn,done,twice`: all pass, 0 lost, 0 repeated after done, 0 repeated outside in-flight. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-agent --features nanocode-code-mode/local-cells -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked -p nanocode-code-mode -p nanocode-agent --features nanocode-code-mode/local-cells --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-sim`.

- deps(sys): nanocode-sys declares the Win32 API itself (`nanocode_sys::windows_sys`), nanocode-sys stops depending on windows-sys, and psh-os, the vendored rustls-platform-verifier and rustpython-host_env take windows-sys's paths from nanocode-windows-sys (2026-11-14, Georgios: third-party packages to 0). What: crates/core/sys/src/windows_sys.rs (Windows only) holds the 955 items those crates use, in windows-sys 0.61.2's own module tree (`core`, `Win32::Foundation`, `Win32::Storage::FileSystem`, `Win32::System::Threading` and the rest), each windows-sys's definition taken from its macro-expanded source for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-pc-windows-msvc (identical on the three): 212 functions, each in its own `#[link(name = "<dll>", kind = "raw-dylib", modifiers = "+verbatim")]` block as windows-link 0.2.1 expands them for non-x86 Windows, plus types, structs and unions with their derives and impls, constants, and windows-sys's `decode_utf8_char` and `utf16_len`, which its `w!`-built constants call. `windows_sys::` paths become `crate::windows_sys::` and `super::` paths stay, since the tree keeps windows-sys's shape. crates/core/windows-sys (package nanocode-windows-sys) re-exports that tree and carries windows-sys's `s!` and `w!` macros, copied unchanged; psh-os, rustls-platform-verifier and rustpython-host_env name it as `windows-sys` (`package = "nanocode-windows-sys"`), so their sources are unchanged and their feature lists go. certificate_store.rs and junction.rs import `crate::windows_sys`. The libc declarations also cover aarch64-pc-windows-msvc now (the Windows group's cfg; its items equal the x86_64 MSVC ones), which rustpython-host_env needs there. The item list came from the callers' `windows_sys::` paths and use trees (654 paths) and then from compiling `nanocode-python` (with `--keep-going`, past nanocode-python-capi's C build) and the psh workspace's psh-os for the three Windows targets until nothing was missing. That loop also reads E0408 and `unused variable` on uppercase names: a match arm naming a missing constant compiles as a binding, so rustpython-host_env's error tables (90 `ERROR_*` names) were found that way; a final build has none left. Not supported: 32-bit x86 Windows, where windows-link adds `import_name_type = "undecorated"`. Why: windows-sys is 334,283 lines and windows-link comes with it; after this only tokio, mio, socket2 and errno name them, all of which leave with tokio. Equal: output/libc-sys/wharness, which depends on windows-sys =0.61.2 with the workspace's features and on this nanocode-sys, checks at compile time for the three targets 1,828 assertions (every struct's and union's size and alignment, every field's offset and size, every type alias's layout, every integer constant's value, the size of the 13 pointer constants such as INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE and the HKEY roots, which const evaluation cannot compare by value, and of the GUID constants) and coerces each of the 212 functions and windows-sys's to one function pointer type written in each crate's names (424 coercions); a separate script checks that every function's DLL name equals windows-sys's expansion for all three targets (212 functions, 0 differences). The vendored verifier was compiled for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu through output/libc-sys/verifier-win, since nothing in the workspace builds it for Windows. Nothing here runs on Windows; Windows stays check-only. Packages: 136 before, 137 after (nanocode-windows-sys), 11 third-party before and after (windows-sys and windows-link stay for tokio, mio, socket2 and errno); the psh workspace's lock loses windows-sys and windows-link. Commands: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`; `cargo check --locked --target T -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-windows-sys -p nanocode-libc` and `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-python --keep-going --target T` for the three Windows targets; in crates/patches/psh `cargo check --locked -p psh-os` for the three and x86_64 Linux; `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-windows-sys` for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu (no warnings before or after) and natively; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-sys -p nanocode-windows-sys --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; the harness's `cargo check --target T`. Files: crates/core/sys/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs,src/windows_sys.rs,src/certificate_store.rs,src/junction.rs,src/libc/mod.rs}, crates/core/windows-sys/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}, Cargo.toml (member), crates/patches/{psh/crates/psh-os,rustls-platform-verifier,rustpython-host_env}/Cargo.toml, both Cargo.lock files.
- deps(python): the vendored RustPython crates and pymath take the C library from nanocode-sys through nanocode-libc, a crate that re-exports `nanocode_sys::libc` under the name the vendored code already uses, and libc's last users outside the async stack go (2026-11-14, Georgios: third-party packages to 0). What: crates/core/libc (package nanocode-libc) is one line, `pub use nanocode_sys::libc::*;`, and rustpython-host_env, rustpython-vm, rustpython-stdlib, rustpython-common and pymath name it as their `libc` dependency (`package = "nanocode-libc"`), so their sources, written against the libc crate (`libc::X` paths, `use libc::{...}` lists, `use libc::*` globs in crt_fd.rs, errno.rs and os.rs, `use libc as c` in socket.rs and `libc::$name` inside _stat.rs's macro), are unchanged. The generated declarations grow to the 728 names nanocode, psh-os and RustPython use: 724 items on Linux glibc, 717 on musl, 646 on macOS, 638 on iOS, 610 on Android, 180 on Windows GNU and 177 on MSVC (RustPython's C runtime calls), and `c_void` on wasm32. The names were found by scanning the vendored sources (qualified paths, use lists, every libc name in the files that glob-import libc) and then by compiling `nanocode-python` and `nanocode-python-cli` for every supported target until no name was missing (S_IFBLK, S_IFIFO and S_IFSOCK came only from the macro). A glob that previously resolved a name through libc and now could resolve it through another glob would have been ambiguous before, so no name changes meaning silently. Why: after this, libc's users are tokio, mio, socket2, signal-hook-registry and errno only, all of which leave with tokio. Equal: output/libc-sys/harness against libc =0.2.191 at compile time: x86_64 and aarch64 glibc 87 types, 169 fields, 443 constants, 159 functions and statics; musl 87, 173, 439, 158; macOS 82, 167, 390, 160; iOS 81, 165, 389, 154; Windows GNU 27, 26, 117, 36 and MSVC 27, 26, 114, 36; all pass. At run time on x86_64 glibc 197 address and value checks, 1,132 comparisons of libc's Rust functions over sample arguments (panics included, in debug and release builds) and 49 smoke calls; x86_64 musl and aarch64 musl (qemu-aarch64) 194, 1,132 and 47; 0 failures. Behavior: nanocode-python-cli built from the previous commit and from this one runs output/libc-sys/py/check2.py (errno codes and names, os, stat, signal, time and locale constants, open, write, lseek, fstat, ftruncate, dup, chmod, access, scandir, umask, times, clocks, gmtime, localtime and mktime under TZ=UTC, strftime, strptime, strerror, OSError mapping, setlocale, isatty, cpu_count, urandom, and the calls its sandbox refuses, such as symlink, pipe and fork): the 88 lines of output are identical but for one modification time the sandbox sets to the current time, twice over. Not checked: Android, where nanocode-sys does not build on master (alloc/os.rs's `mremap`); RustPython on iOS, where libc 0.2.191 has no `system` and rustpython-host_env's call to it fails on master too; cross targets of nanocode-python itself, whose C API build script needs a C compiler for the target, so RustPython was compiled there with `cargo check -p nanocode-python --keep-going`. Packages: 135 before, 136 after (nanocode-libc), 11 third-party before and after. Commands: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`; `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-python -p nanocode-python-cli` (x86_64 glibc) and `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-python --keep-going --target T` for aarch64 glibc, both musl, both macOS, iOS, Windows GNU and MSVC and wasm32; `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-libc -p nanocode-sys --all-targets` (nanocode-sys's 3 warnings from before, none new); `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-libc --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; the harness's checks and runs as above. Files: crates/core/libc/{Cargo.toml,src/lib.rs}, Cargo.toml (member), crates/core/sys/src/libc/*.rs, crates/patches/{rustpython-host_env,rustpython-vm,rustpython-stdlib,rustpython-common,pymath}/Cargo.toml.

- deps(sys): nanocode-sys declares the C library itself (`nanocode_sys::libc`), and nanocode's own crates take libc's types, constants and functions from it instead of the libc crate (2026-11-14, Georgios: third-party packages to 0). What: crates/core/sys/src/libc/ holds the declarations the workspace's own crates use (nanocode-sys, nanocode-process, nanocode-sandbox, nanocode-home, nanocode-backend-claude, nanocode-backend-claude-tools, nanocode-backend-codex, nanocode-chatgpt-extension, nanocode-computer, nanocode-store-jsonl and the facade's runner example): 192 names and the items they name, 218 items on Linux, 210 on macOS, 208 on iOS, 211 on Android and 45 on Windows (C runtime names libc also declares there), as extern "C" functions and statics, `repr(C)` structs and unions with libc's derives and `Default` impls, type aliases, constants and libc's Rust functions (`CMSG_*`). Each item is libc 0.2.191's own definition for that target, taken from its macro-expanded source (`cargo rustc -p libc --target T -- -Zunpretty=expanded` with RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1), with `crate::` paths flattened, doc and deprecation attributes dropped, libc-private items and fields made `pub(super)`, the bodies of its `unsafe fn`s in an `unsafe` block (nanocode-sys denies unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn), its `debug_assert!`s, which the expansion (a debug build) turned into `if true`, back to `if cfg!(debug_assertions)`, and its `assert!` panics as `panic!`; `Padding`, libc's private padding wrapper, and its cast helpers are written out by hand. Items equal on several targets are written once: unix.rs (every supported Unix), linux.rs, linux_gnu.rs, linux_musl.rs, apple.rs, macos.rs, windows.rs, and one file per target for the rest; mod.rs selects them by cfg. Targets: x86_64 and aarch64 Linux with glibc (the CLI's) and musl (Pyramid's Hand), aarch64 Android, x86_64 and aarch64 macOS, aarch64 iOS and the iOS simulator, x86_64 Windows GNU and MSVC (check-only), and wasm32-unknown-unknown (empty, as libc is there); any other target gets no declarations, where libc covered every platform it knows. Callers name `nanocode_sys::libc::X`, or `use nanocode_sys::libc;` where a file names several, so their code is otherwise unchanged. The generator (syn over the expanded source, the closure of the names asked for, grouping by identical tokens) and the harness are in output/libc-sys, not committed. Why: libc is 133,106 lines with a build script, of which nanocode uses a few hundred items; this is the first step of taking it out of the graph, and once psh-os and the vendored RustPython move too, only tokio, mio, socket2, signal-hook-registry and errno (the async lane's) still name it. Equal, checked against libc =0.2.191 by output/libc-sys/harness, a binary that depends on both and is generated from the same item lists: at compile time, for every target, every type alias that is a primitive is the same type as libc's (a `Same<T>` bound), every struct, union and opaque type has libc's size and alignment, every public field libc's offset (`offset_of!`) and size, every integer or float constant libc's value (`assert!(ns::X == libc::X)` in a const, which also needs the same type), and every function and static libc's signature (both coerced to one function pointer type written in each crate's names); at run time, every extern function and static has libc's address (the same symbol, link names included), pointer and struct constants are byte-equal, and libc's Rust functions with integer arguments give libc's results, a panic counting as a result, over 32 sample values per argument (18 small ones for the `extern "C"` ones such as `CMSG_LEN`, where a debug build's overflow would abort), in debug and release builds. Counts on x86_64 glibc: 49 types, 72 fields, 109 constants at compile time and 1 at run time, 56 functions and statics; macOS 51 types, 82 fields, 90 constants, 57 functions; Windows 15, 13, 22, 8. Run on x86_64 glibc: 101 address and value checks, 36 value comparisons and 49 smoke calls (open, read, write, fcntl, dup2, poll, mmap, madvise, munmap, mremap, getrandom, pthread keys and attributes, posix_openpt, grantpt, unlockpt, tcgetattr, tcsetattr, uname, statvfs, getpwuid_r, gethostname, sendmsg and recvmsg passing a descriptor through CMSG_*, dlopen, dlsym, dlerror, signal, fork and waitpid, kill, killpg, fsync, syscall), each compared with the libc crate's call or result, 0 failures; x86_64 musl (static, natively) and aarch64 musl (under qemu-aarch64) 98 checks, 36 comparisons and 47 calls (a static binary cannot dlopen), 0 failures; aarch64 glibc, macOS, iOS, Windows and wasm32 compile-time checks only, all passing. Android: nanocode-sys does not build for aarch64-linux-android on master either (alloc/os.rs calls `libc::mremap`, which libc does not declare for Android), so the harness cannot build there; the Android declarations are generated and compiled but not compared. Packages: 135 before and after, 11 third-party before and after (libc stays for tokio, mio, socket2, signal-hook-registry, errno, psh-os and RustPython); the workspace's `libc` dependency entry goes, and crates/patches/psh/Cargo.lock follows nanocode-sys. Commands: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets`; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets` of the eleven changed crates (12 warnings before and after, the same ones); `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` of the same crates; `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-sys --lib` for every target above; the harness's `cargo check --release --target T` for every target and `cargo run --release` on the three it runs on; nanocode-sim `--tidy` and bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 2000 2 --scenario runtime with --store kv, --store memory, --store kv --twice and --store kv --wire http. - feat(platform): spawn_task and spawn_joined run on an installed host, so a JoinHandle works where a host drives the futures (2026-11-14, tokio replacement, after step 9). What: nanocode_executor::spawn_with(future, spawn) wraps the future in a driver that writes its output, a panic or a cancellation into a JoinHandle's cell and hands the boxed driver to spawn; abort marks the cell and wakes the driver, and a driver dropped unfinished (its host stopped) completes the handle as cancelled. nanocode-platform's spawn_task and spawn_joined use it when a Host is installed (JoinSet::push takes such a handle), and the executor otherwise, as before. Why: with tokio gone, an embedder that runs nanocode inside its own runtime (pyramid-core under tokio) installs a Host whose spawn is its runtime's spawn; spawn_task and spawn_joined bypassed the host and needed a nanocode runtime, which such an embedder does not run, while spawn already went through the host. The simulator installs a host too, so these two calls now run under its deterministic executor instead of failing. Equal: output/remote-spawn drives spawn_with from tokio 1.52.3's runtime: a value (42), a panic (is_panic and its message), abort of a pending future (cancelled), is_finished before a 20 ms sleep ends (false) and its output after, a JoinSet of five pushed handles completing in sleep order (4, 3, 2, 1, 0), and a handle whose host runtime was dropped answering cancelled when awaited on a nanocode runtime. Packages: unchanged (third-party 3). Files: crates/core/executor/src/{remote.rs,join_set.rs,lib.rs}, crates/core/platform/src/native.rs.
- feat(executor): nanocode's executor replaces tokio's runtime, and tokio leaves the workspace with mio, socket2, signal-hook-registry, errno, wasi, bytes and pin-project-lite (2026-11-14, tokio replacement, step 9 of plan-22). What: nanocode-platform's spawn, spawn_task, spawn_on, spawn_joined, spawn_blocking, sleep, sleep_until, timeout, timeout_at, Sleep and Handle run on nanocode-executor when no host is installed; every tokio::task, tokio::runtime, tokio::time and tokio::spawn use (JoinHandle, AbortHandle, JoinSet, JoinError, yield_now, the coop budget, task ids, Builder, Runtime, Handle) names nanocode-executor's; nanocode-io's bridge from tokio's IO traits goes; nanocode-sim's tidy bans nanocode_executor::{spawn, sleep, timeout, Builder, Handle} in simulated crates where it banned tokio::{spawn, time, runtime}, with SharedStore's one current_thread runtime still allowed. The executor: a runtime has N worker slots and one MPSC run queue (nanocode-sys's), whose consumer a one-worker runtime keeps for its life and a larger one takes per pop; an idle worker takes the reactor's driver and waits in epoll_wait (a runtime thread drives instead of the nanocode-reactor thread, which parks while one is present), and a task pushed while every worker is parked or driving unparks one or wakes the poller; current_thread block_on drives on its own thread the same way; a worker runs at most EVENT_INTERVAL (61, tokio's) tasks before it polls the reactor without waiting; a task's state is one atomic (idle, scheduled, running, notified, done) and its future lives in an AtomicPinBox while it is not being polled; a panic becomes JoinError::Panic with tokio's Display and Debug, whose payload sits in nanocode-sys's new Exclusive so JoinError stays Sync as tokio's is; yield_now defers its wake to the end of the batch and deferred wakers run last-first, as tokio's Defer does; runtime drop cancels every task still alive through a weak list compacted when it doubles past the live count, and waits for blocking tasks as tokio's does, shutdown_timeout and shutdown_background bound that wait; the blocking pool starts a thread per job up to 512 and keeps idle threads 10 s. Fixed while switching: a current_thread block_on whose future panicked dropped the run queue's consumer, so the runtime never ran a task again; a one-worker runtime dropped the consumer when its worker exited, so shutdown spun; the weak task list counted finished tasks whose JoinHandles were still held as live and compacted on every spawn (quadratic in a 200,000-task fan-out). Why: DEPENDENCIES.md's goal of nothing outside the async baseline; tokio was the last of it. Equal: output/executor-equality runs one set of programs on tokio 1.52.3 and on nanocode-executor and compares: try_current outside a runtime; spawn and await; a panic's JoinError (Display, Debug, is_panic) for a str, a String and a u8 payload; abort before and after completion; spawn_blocking and its panic; is_finished; JoinError into io::Error; block_on inside block_on panics; 300 consume_budget calls take 3 polls of the task and the budget is full at a task's start and unconstrained outside; a JoinSet of 20 tasks that yield 0 to 6 times completes in the same order, abort_all cancels 2 of 2 and an empty set answers None; dropping a runtime drops a pending task; shutdown_timeout returns before a 400 ms blocking task; 1,000 tasks that yield and sleep on a 3-worker runtime: 8 groups, 0 differences (before the yield and consumer fixes, 2 and a hang). The earlier harnesses' native columns, now the shipped configuration, pass as well: net-equality 106 cases, process-equality 36, fs-equality 36,000, 0 differences. Cost, interleaved with tokio on the same programs at load 3 to 4: spawn and await from block_on (200,000) 6.1 to 7.0 µs against tokio's 6.1 to 6.6 on one worker and 5.9 to 7.3 against 6.3 to 13.6 on four; a fan-out of 200,000 spawns then awaits 543 to 964 ns per task against 304 to 319 on one worker (an Arc, a boxed future and a weak-list node per task where tokio allocates once) and 349 to 384 against 347 to 431 on four; spawn_blocking (20,000) 7.5 to 14.4 µs against 10.4 to 11.4; 64-byte loopback round trips p50 on one worker 6.9 to 10.4 µs against tokio's 7.2 to 8.2, on current_thread 4.41 to 4.49 against 4.64 to 4.66. End to end, debug builds of nanocode against a mock Messages server (output: e2e/run.sh, run2.sh), 5 interleaved runs of master's tokio build and this one: a one-turn exec 85 to 119 ms against 88 to 107, a turn that calls a tool 142 to 192 against 133 to 163, a Code Mode cell that runs Bash (echo, sleep 0.2, a redirect) and Write, 3 runs, 364 to 419 against 361 to 394 ms, with the same output, file contents and exit status 0; before the shutdown fix every exec of this build printed its reply and then spun until killed. The TUI in a 120x40 tmux pane, same builds: it starts, answers a prompt, redraws after a resize to 90x30, and Ctrl-C, Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D exits with status 0, for both. Not measured: the bench/cli first frame and the nanocode-ts SLA mock, which are not in this repository. Checks: cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets clean at each commit of the series; clippy of the 31 crates the series touches adds no warning in a touched file; wasm32 cargo check --lib of nanocode-io, -sys, -sync, -http, -websocket, -tls, -backend-codex, -backend-codex-client, -backend-claude, -backend-claude-client, -mcp-http, -platform, -durability, -code-mode-engine, -tool-runtime, -executor, -mcp-tools and nanocode clean; rustfmt clean on new files and on each touched file that was clean before; nanocode-sim --tidy clean and sweeps on the series tip (next entry). Downstream (pyramid, pyramid-core): nanocode_platform::spawn_on takes nanocode_executor::Handle, spawn_task and spawn_joined return nanocode-executor's JoinHandle and AbortHandle, nanocode_sync::splice takes nanocode-executor TcpStreams, nanocode_sync::Duplex no longer covers types that only implement tokio's traits, and nanocode's sockets, timers and processes need no tokio context: under a foreign executor the nanocode-reactor thread drives them. Packages: cargo metadata 135 to 129 (third-party 11 to 3: libc, windows-link and windows-sys stay); DEPENDENCIES.md's Removed list updated. Files: crates/core/executor/src/{runtime.rs,task.rs,queue.rs,blocking.rs}, crates/core/sys/src/{exclusive.rs,lib.rs}, crates/core/platform/src/native.rs, crates/core/io/src/lib.rs, bin/nanocode-sim/src/tidy.rs and 41 call sites and manifests.
- feat(executor): child processes, signals and files: nanocode-executor gains process, signal and fs, and every tokio::process, tokio::signal, tokio::fs and tokio::io stdio user moves onto them (2026-11-14, tokio replacement, steps 7 and 8 of plan-22). What: nanocode-sys gains unix::signal: a sigaction handler (SA_RESTART, errno saved and restored) that marks the signal pending and writes one byte to a nonblocking close-on-exec self-pipe, then calls the handler it replaced, as signal-hook-registry chains; it refuses SIGILL, SIGFPE, SIGKILL, SIGSEGV and SIGSTOP as tokio does; and pidfd_open (Linux). nanocode-executor gains signal::unix::{signal, Signal, SignalKind} and signal::ctrl_c: the self-pipe is a reactor source whose own waker drains it and wakes every listener of a signal that arrived, and a listener sees the signals delivered after it was created; process::{Command, Child, ChildStdin, ChildStdout, ChildStderr} over std::process::Command: nonblocking pipes, a child's exit seen through a pidfd registered with the reactor on Linux and through a SIGCHLD listener created before the first try_wait elsewhere or when pidfd_open fails, kill_on_drop, children dropped before they exit kept and reaped on the next spawn and drop as tokio's orphan queue does, wait closing stdin first, output and wait_with_output reading both pipes while waiting, start_kill after exit answering Ok as tokio's does; fs: std::fs calls on the blocking pool (on a pool of its own when no nanocode runtime is current, so they also work under another executor), File with a read buffer of at most MAX_BUFFER (2 MiB, tokio's DEFAULT_MAX_BUF_SIZE), seek and sync, OpenOptions, DirBuilder, read_dir, and stdin, stdout and stderr on the same blocking machinery. Windows (check-only): a child's exit is polled every EXIT_POLL (1 ms), its pipes block in place, and ctrl_c never completes, so Ctrl-C keeps the console's default of ending the process. Why: tokio's runtime can't leave while these need it. Deliberately different: a File write waits for its blocking write to finish instead of returning before it as tokio's write-behind does, so a write error surfaces from that write rather than the next call. Equal: output/process-equality runs one script set through tokio's process and signal, through these under tokio's runtime and under nanocode's multi_thread(1) runtime: exit codes 0, 1, 7 and 255, death by SIGKILL, a missing program's error kind, output() of 0 B to 100 MiB on stdout with half on stderr, a 0 B to 100 MiB round trip through cat, writing to a child that closed stdin (BrokenPipe), kill, try_wait, id and start_kill after exit, SIGTERM to a process group, 1,000 kill_on_drop children dropped (0 left running, 0 zombies at the end), two SIGUSR1 listeners each seeing one signal and a second one, and SIGKILL refused: 36 cases, 0 differences. output/fs-equality runs 300 seeded scripts of 60 operations (write, read, read_to_string, metadata, remove_file, create_dir_all, read_dir, canonicalize, rename, a File created, written, flushed, sought, synced and measured, a File read, sought from the current position and read to the end, an append, a DirBuilder with mode 0o700, remove_dir_all) through tokio::fs and through these under both runtimes: 36,000 comparisons, 0 differences; a mutation that writes 0.1% short gives 4,088. Cost, 5 interleaved rounds at load 4, spawn and wait of true (1,000 sequential) p50/p99 in µs: tokio 4,166/33,896, 3,334/34,029, 3,342/31,277, 3,823/35,909, 3,454/16,399; these on tokio's runtime 3,688/33,940, 3,403/31,313, 3,764/32,486, 4,020/34,054, 3,248/15,690; on nanocode's runtime 3,613/33,977, 3,404/32,129, 3,749/34,047, 3,851/33,837, 3,126/15,498; 100 MiB through cat in MB/s: tokio 1,839, 3,352, 1,136, 1,366, 2,490; on tokio's runtime 1,394, 1,664, 1,533, 2,558, 3,069; on nanocode's 3,118, 2,221, 2,987, 2,090, 2,511, all within the spread. Packages: unchanged (third-party 11). Files: crates/core/executor/src/{process.rs,signal.rs,fs.rs,blocking.rs,lib.rs}, crates/core/sys/src/unix/{signal.rs,mod.rs} and 30 call sites and manifests.
- feat(executor): new crate nanocode-executor, nanocode's own runtime: a reactor over epoll and kqueue, timers, a task executor with a blocking pool, and nonblocking TCP and Unix sockets that work under any executor; every tokio::net user and the TUI's AsyncFd move onto it (2026-11-14, tokio replacement, steps 5 and 6 of plan-22). What: nanocode-sys gains unix::poll (one edge-triggered epoll registration per descriptor for reading and writing with EPOLLRDHUP, an eventfd wake; on macOS EV_CLEAR kqueue filters and an EVFILT_USER wake; a nonblocking connect and SO_ERROR) and AtomicPinBox (an AtomicBox whose value stays pinned, so a task's future can move between threads without unsafe outside nanocode-sys). nanocode-executor holds: the reactor, one per process, whose driver state (the event buffer, the token map, the timer map keyed by (deadline, id)) passes between threads as an AtomicBox, so whichever thread takes it waits in epoll_wait and the others park; readiness is a word with a tick, tokio's ScheduledIo scheme, so a WouldBlock clears only the readiness that operation saw, and read or write closed stays set; registrations and timers reach the driver through nanocode-sys's MPSC queue, drained after every wait before events are dispatched, so an event can't outrun its registration; a nanocode-reactor thread drives it while no runtime thread does (always, in this commit, since tokio still runs every task), and parks while one does; net: TcpStream (connect over every resolved address, set_nodelay, into_split with tcp::OwnedReadHalf/OwnedWriteHalf and reunite, peek, readable, writable, try_read, try_write), TcpListener (bind, from_std, accept), UnixStream, UnixListener, UnixDatagram, unix::Pipe for a pipe descriptor (the sandbox's stdin pipe), Source<T> in place of AsyncFd, and lookup_host on its own thread through getaddrinfo, as tokio does on its blocking pool; and the runtime the later commits switch to (Builder current_thread and multi_thread, block_on, spawn, a blocking pool of at most 512 threads kept 10 s, tokio's two defaults, JoinHandle, AbortHandle and JoinError with tokio's messages, JoinSet in completion order, a coop budget of 128 polls as tokio's, yield_now and task ids), unused by the workspace until then. Windows (check-only): the poller is a wake channel with timers, a socket retries a WouldBlock every POLL_RETRY (1 ms) and connect runs on a thread. Why: DEPENDENCIES.md's goal; mio, socket2 and tokio's net leave once the runtime follows. Deliberately different: sockets are registered for both directions at once (mio registers what the caller asks); EPOLLPRI is not requested (mio does not either); nanocode_sync::splice takes nanocode-executor TcpStreams, so pyramid-core's two callers convert a tokio stream with into_std and from_std; while tokio still runs the tasks, a readiness event is seen by the nanocode-reactor thread and reaches the tokio worker as a cross-thread wake. Equal: output/net-equality runs the same scripts (an echo of up to 2 MB written in random chunks over into_split halves, a Unix stream and 20 datagrams, a refused connect, a reset, a connect timeout, lookup of localhost, a literal, a missing port and an unknown name, an accept of 2,000 connections, 20 sleeps and two timeouts) through tokio's net, through these sockets under tokio's runtime, and through them under nanocode's multi_thread(1) and current_thread runtimes: 196 cases over 20 seeds, 0 differences, and the process's descriptor count back to where it started. Cost, loopback, one runtime per process, 64-byte round trips (20,000) p50 and p99 in µs, 3 runs at load 6: tokio's net on tokio's multi_thread(1) 8.2/23.6, 7.3/23.0, 7.2/14.8; this commit's sockets on tokio's runtime 14.2/146, 12.0/78.7, 14.2/73.0 (the cross-thread wake, which the runtime commit removes); nanocode's multi_thread(1) 10.4/28.8, 9.3/18.5, 6.9/29.5; current_thread, tokio then nanocode, 4.65/6.56 and 4.41/6.35, 4.66/5.16 and 4.49/5.06, 4.64/8.59 and 4.41/4.89. 256 MiB through loopback: 2.1 to 8.2 GB/s for every side, within the run-to-run spread. One gap stays: 100 connections opened at once on a current_thread runtime are accepted at 1.6k to 5.2k/s against tokio's 40k to 47k/s (multi_thread is equal, 1.9k to 3.7k/s against 2.2k to 3.1k/s); instrumented, one accept or connect syscall in the burst takes 10 to 30 ms in the kernel, which this Hand did not explain. - feat(io): new crate nanocode-io carries `AsyncRead`, `AsyncWrite`, `AsyncBufRead` and `AsyncSeek`, a `ReadBuf`, the extension traits (`read`, `read_exact`, `read_to_end`, `read_to_string`, `read_buf`, `take`, `read_u8/u16/u32/u64/i32`, `write`, `write_all`, `write_vectored`, `write_u8/u32/i32`, `flush`, `shutdown`, `read_until`, `read_line`, `fill_buf`, `consume`, `lines`, `seek`, `rewind`, `stream_position`), `BufReader`, `Lines`, `Take`, `split` (`ReadHalf`, `WriteHalf`), `copy`, `copy_bidirectional`, `sink` and `empty`, and every user of tokio's IO traits and utilities moves onto it (2026-11-14, tokio replacement steps 3 and 4 of plan-22). Two deviations from the plan. (1) The traits keep tokio's shape, including a `ReadBuf` (over initialised memory only, so no unsafe), not futures-io's `&mut [u8]`, so the 13 types implementing the traits (TLS stream, websocket and HTTP connections, the deflate stream, the embedded process reader, the simulator's sockets) move by an import swap. (2) Instead of a `compat::Tokio<T>` wrapper at every socket, pipe and file, nanocode-io has a native-only blanket impl of its traits for any `T` that implements tokio's, so tokio's TcpStream, UnixStream, ChildStdout and File keep working until steps 5 to 8 replace them, and the bridge leaves with tokio in step 9. Coherence still allows our own impls for local types and for `Box<dyn Duplex>` and `Box<dyn AsyncRead/AsyncWrite + Send + Unpin>`, which those call sites need. Two smaller signature changes: `take` borrows its reader (`Take<'a, R>`), so `(&mut *reader).take(n)` keeps working without an `impl for &mut T` that would overlap the bridge, and `claude_bash`'s head and the sandbox's `read_all` declare their reader `mut`. `split` shares the stream through a new nanocode-sys `BiLock` (an `AtomicBool` plus one `AtomicWaker` per half; the guard wakes the other half when it drops), since a lock-free shared `&mut` needs `UnsafeCell`. nanocode-tls's `TlsStream` now implements nanocode-io's traits, which finishes step 4: tokio-rustls left on 2026-11-14 (agent 27). Behaviour matches tokio by construction: `copy` follows tokio's `CopyBuffer` (fill while there is room, read more while the writer is pending, flush only when the reader is pending), `read_to_end` uses tokio's 32-byte probe read and `reserve(32)` growth, `read_to_string` reads into the string's own buffer and restores it on invalid UTF-8, and EOF and write-zero errors carry tokio's kinds and messages. Equality: output/io-equality drives one scripted reader and writer (random chunk sizes, injected `Pending`, an injected error at a random offset, EOF, zero-length writes) through tokio 1.52.3's io-util and through nanocode-io, comparing results, error kinds and messages, bytes, flush and shutdown counts, poll counts and how far the reader was consumed, for read, read_exact, read_to_end, read_to_string, BufReader read_line and lines, read_until, read_u32, write_all, copy, copy_bidirectional and take: 0 differences over 5 seeds x 100,000 scripts. A mutation that stops `write_all` one byte early gives 67 differences in 5,000. Throughput, `io-equality bench`, in memory, median of 5 interleaved rounds: copy 256 MiB 19,443 vs 20,202 MB/s (0.96); BufReader lines over 64 MiB 736 vs 982 MB/s (0.75); read_to_end 256 MiB 1,484 vs 2,709 MB/s (0.55). That last gap is the zeroing of each newly reserved region: tokio reads into uninitialised capacity, which needs unsafe, and the call sites read pipes and sockets whose syscalls cost far more than the memset. An initialised watermark keeps zeroing to once per reallocation, not once per read (88 MB/s before it). Checks: `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` reports nothing new in the touched files and `cargo clippy -p nanocode-io -p nanocode-sys --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` nothing in nanocode-io; after rebasing onto a3f421924, `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` clean and wasm32 `cargo check --lib` of nanocode-io, nanocode-sys, nanocode-sync, nanocode-http, nanocode-websocket and nanocode-tls clean; release nanocode-sim seeds 1..150 `--scenario runtime --twice` 149/149 identical, `--wire http` 149/149, `--store kv` 149/149, `--scenario websocket` 149/149; `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean. Rebased again onto d8bbf7921 and re-checked there: `cargo check --locked --workspace --all-targets` clean, clippy of the 23 touched crates adds no warning in a touched file, wasm32 `cargo check --lib` of nanocode-io, -sys, -sync, -http, -websocket, -tls, -backend-codex, -backend-codex-client, -backend-claude, -backend-claude-client and -mcp-http clean, `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean, and `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 2000 2 --scenario runtime` with `--store kv`, `--store memory`, `--store kv --twice` and `--wire http` 2000/2000 each with 0 panics; then onto b5a918613 with the workspace check clean. Simulator wall time, `--scenario runtime` seeds 1..150, 4 interleaved runs at load 6: master 11.51, 10.85, 10.96, 10.67 s, this change 11.08, 10.80, 10.72, 11.01 s (median 10.91 s both). The CLI's first frame and one-shot were not re-measured: every CLI call site still drives the same tokio types, now through the bridge's generic impls, which monomorphize to the same calls. Downstream: tempoxyz/pyramid-core's `nanocode_sync::pipe` and `splice` callers (gateway and mac-gateway hands.rs, with tokio's `TcpStream`) and its `Box<dyn Duplex>` (hosted process.rs) compile unchanged through the bridge; a type there that implements tokio's traits by hand also gets nanocode-io's; code that names `nanocode_sync::Duplex`'s supertraits must import them from `nanocode_io`. - fix(claude): in Code Mode, Bash's description says that the end of a `run_in_background` command, or of one moved to the background at its timeout, makes the waiting exec or wait call return, even one whose script sleeps on a timer, and that a command put in the background with `&` or `nohup` is not followed (2026-11-14, Terminal-Bench 2.1 claude-full run 200a4c68 on Worker d2473f9dd: train-fasttext passed on both arms, nano a00167 in 2138 s, Claude Code 2.1.318 a00168 in 1065 s). Nano started each of its six training batches with `nohup sh -c '…' > logN.txt 2>&1 &` through Bash in a cell, then waited in eight cells of `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 120000 to 295000))` that each read the log afterwards: 1955 s of the 2138. The log files' modification times in the attempt's own `ls` show each batch ended 20 to 150 s before the cell that checked it, about 400 to 700 s in all. The rest of the gap is the model training more and larger runs (twice the data, single-threaded on one CPU). Claude Code's model ran the same kind of runs as foreground Bash calls with `timeout` 600000 to 1200000 that returned the moment training ended. Nanocode already follows a background job started with `run_in_background` or moved at its timeout: since f351a1b60 its end preempts the exec or wait call that is waiting. A shell job is invisible to it, and Claude Code's refusal of a leading `sleep` of 25 s or more (a81ec4e87) has no counterpart for a cell's timer. The upstream sentence ("re-invokes you when it exits") does not say how that reaches a cell. In the same run's other 14 nano attempts no cell waited on a timer of 25 s or more. Change: with `code_mode`, `NESTED_BACKGROUND` follows upstream's "No `&` needed.", the way `NESTED_TIMEOUT` follows its timeout sentence, and a missing sentence fails as the timeout one does. Without Code Mode the description is upstream's unchanged: both additions are empty strings between the parts that the split takes apart. Checked: output/bash-desc prints the Bash description that `nanocode_backend_claude::hand_tools` serves, with the sentence after "No `&` needed."; `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude`, natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and its clippy pass report nothing; `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 200` passed=200 failed=0, panics=0. Not verified: a model. Hands serve this description, so it reaches an eval slot with the next nanocode-cli release that nanoeval pins. Files: crates/backends/claude/src/claude_bash.rs.

Upstream codex-cli 0.166.0 evicts no images from its history (codex-rs core/src/context_manager has no image window; it only resizes each image to fit `MAX_DIMENSION`), and OpenAI documents up to 500 image inputs per request (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/images-vision). On run bec3e408 (rest-codex-plan2, tb21 financial-document-processor, attempt a00022, gpt-6-luna high, 2026-11-14 08:02 UTC) nanox passed in 480 s against codex-cli's 136 s: 67 model calls against 19 and 448 s of model time against 115 s, with tool time only 31 s. 45 of the 67 calls viewed an invoice image; it viewed 11 images 76 times (6 to 8 each), because with 11 images in a window of 8 the batch eviction (4 at a time) never let one request hold all of them, and the prompt fell by about 4,500 tokens every few views (48,445, 49,910, 51,373, 47,505...). - fix(codex): a Responses stream emits one `assistant.message` per output item, with the item's complete `output_text` (2026-11-14, codex-multipart lane, follow-up to 1d7cbd4bc). Before, 1d7cbd4bc emitted the message at every `response.output_text.done`, so a message item with two `output_text` parts produced a partial message and then a complete one. `nanocode exec` keys messages by item id and prints only the first one when the deltas were not printed, so it lost the second part. Now `output_text.done` holds the message (`DoneMessage`, with the text of the item's done parts), and the next decoded event decides: `response.content_part.added` for the same output index returns the text to `done_texts` and the item grows, `StreamEvent::Other` (such as `content_part.done`) and `StreamEvent::Failure` keep the message held, and every other event emits it before that event is published. `output_item.done` then emits nothing when its text and phase match, as before. The message now follows the decode of `content_part.done` and `output_item.done`, but precedes the `api.event` of `output_item.done` and the `ResponseItem` normalization. Reproduced with a local Responses mock (one message item, parts `First part. ` and `Second part.`, without `output_text.delta` frames) and `nanocode exec --gateway vercel -m luna`: stdout was `First part. ` with 1d7cbd4bc and is `First part. Second part.` with this change. With delta frames, and with one part, stdout is unchanged. The other consumers (bin/nanocode events.rs, app.rs, side.rs, actions.rs and stream.rs, runtime/agent turn_inbox.rs, runtime/subagents) read one message per item id. Not measured: the latency SLA bench against 1d7cbd4bc. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client`, again with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client` (nothing in stream.rs), `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check`, `cargo build --release --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Files: crates/backends/codex/client/src/tower/stream.rs.
- perf(codex): a Responses stream emits `assistant.message` at `response.output_text.done` instead of after `response.output_item.done` (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 latency SLA: rendered tok/s equal to provider tok/s). `receive` in crates/backends/codex/client/src/tower/stream.rs ignored `output_text.done`, so the message that ends the streamed text (and, since 77a3bff00, the TUI's immediate frame) came only after the client parsed `content_part.done` and the whole `output_item.done` item, both of which repeat the reply. Now `output_text.done` decodes to `StreamEvent::TextDone` with the text kept as a `RawValue`, so the held display deltas flush (bbf2b0c73) before the text is unescaped. The arm then emits `assistant.message` with the item id and phase that `output_item.added` or the first delta recorded, and the text of the item's `output_text` parts that are done so far. `output_item.done` (and an item that only `response.completed` lists) emits the message as before only when its phase or `output_text` differs from what was emitted, so a one-part reply has one `assistant.message` with the same content and the event order is unchanged. A reply with several `output_text` parts first gets the partial message and then the complete one, which the TUI appends as a prefix extension. Checked: `nanocode exec` against the bench fixture (300 tokens) writes byte-identical stdout with the base and fixed builds. Measured with nanocode-ts `bench/sla/run.ts` (mock, `--lanes=nc@base,nc@fix --tokens=20000 --samples=20 --turns=2`, interleaved, under ~/sla-live.lock on the hosted Hand, 5 cores; base 4e7737e64), 40 turns per lane, p50 / p99 of tail (provider's last write to last token drawn, ms) and rendered/provider ratio p50 / p1: tail 7.62 / 18.36 -> 5.88 / 23.68, ratio 0.833 / 0.620 -> 0.888 / 0.555 (turn 1 tail 5.99 -> 4.48, turn 2 10.65 -> 6.29; provider 588k and 536k tok/s). The p99 and p1 values are the single worst of 40 turns and move with the shared machine's load in both directions. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client`, again with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client` (nothing in stream.rs), `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check`, `cargo build --release --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. Files: crates/backends/codex/client/src/tower/stream.rs.
- feat(python): pyyaml's C module (pyyaml 6.0.3, `yaml._yaml`) and libyaml 0.2.5 are compiled into python3, and pyyaml's legacy test suite passes, 2609 tests with no failures or errors, in python.wasm and natively (2026-11-14, Georgios: run the top compiled Python packages in plain wasm32 with a C API layer written in Rust, no Pyodide). `_yaml.c` is generated from the sdist's `yaml/_yaml.pyx` by Cython 3.3.0 (`cython -3 --module-name yaml._yaml -I yaml yaml/_yaml.pyx`), since the sdist ships only the .pyx, and lives with libyaml's eight C files and two headers in ext/yaml._yaml, with libyaml's version macros in its defines file; both licenses are kept beside them. libyaml is the first C source to call the C allocator and strdup, so src/libc.rs (wasm32 only) gives malloc, calloc, realloc and free over the PyMem_Raw allocator and strdup over malloc, and fread, fwrite and ferror for libyaml's FILE reader and writer, which no caller can reach in wasm32, where no FILE exists (they move nothing and report an error); include/libc declares them. Before, python.wasm would have imported `env.malloc`, so its imports are checked to be only `python.host_*`. One C API fix: Cython's limited API shares one `cython_function_or_method` type across every Cython module in the process and checks a cached type's `__basicsize__` against its spec, and `type.__basicsize__` reported RustPython's layout size for a type made from a C spec, so importing a second Cython module (msgpack._cmsgpack and then yaml._yaml) failed with `Shared Cython type cython_function_or_method has the wrong size`. `type.__basicsize__` is now a property (as `__dictoffset__` already is) that answers the C type's own tp_basicsize for a class built from a C type (in C_TYPES, not a proxy type, a CObject subclass) and the original member for every other class; the VM's own slots.basicsize, which its layout checks use, is unchanged. Benchmark (1,000 records, best of 5 after a warm-up, ms, python.wasm then Pyodide 314.0.7 with its pyyaml wheel): CDumper 275 to 300 vs 69.2, CLoader 369 to 394 vs 96.0; pure-Python Dumper about 790 vs 322 and Loader about 2,700 vs 726, so the C module is 2.7x (dump) and 7x (load) faster than pure Python here and the gap to Pyodide is mostly the interpreter. nanocode-ts bench/python/score.ts: packages 4/18 to 5/18, compiled modules 4/274 to 5/274, C API symbols 354/538, external crates 5, limits 4/4; python.wasm 28,429,332 to 28,642,152 bytes (+212,820). Unchanged: ujson 454 passed and 4 skipped, msgpack 154 passed and 7 skipped, regex 101/101, markupsafe's checks, natively and in python.wasm. Commands: `cargo clippy --offline -p nanocode-python-capi -p nanocode-python --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown, `node scripts/check-dependency-boundaries.mjs`. Files: crates/core/python-capi/{ext/yaml._yaml/*,include/libc/{stdio.h,string.h},src/{bridge.rs,libc.rs}}.
- fix(subagents): a remote child's turn is admitted only after the child holds its input, `RemoteBackend` repeats `child_run` with the same request id after a transport error, a restored child's `child_pending` read repeats, and spawn startup cleanup defers to a running `close_all` (2026-11-14, dst lane). What: `ChildHost::run` returns `BackendFuture<Result<ChildTurn>>` (`ChildTurn` is `BackendFuture<Result<TurnResult>>`, exported from nanocode-agent and nanocode): the outer future resolves once the child stored the request's input or answered it, and the inner one with the turn's result. `RemoteBackend::submit` and `route` await the outer future, so `Harness` admits a message as Started only after the child has it. Before, `submit` returned at once, and a parent that died before `child_run` reached the child lost every message of that turn: on restart `child_pending` named the child's previous request (f2358b20c's open item 1, seed 231). An outer `NanocodeError::Backend` (a request that was not sent or an answer that was lost) repeats `run` with the same request id while the child is open, after `completion_retry_delay(attempt)` (now public in nanocode-subagents), with a warn trace per attempt. The child answers a known request id with its running or finished turn, so a repeat starts no second turn. Other errors still end the turn with that error. Before, a lost answer failed the child in the parent while its object ran the turn, and the agent listing changed after a restart. `Registry::pending_turn` repeats a failed pending-turn resolver with the same delay, and `RemoteChildren` re-inserts its restored marker when `child_pending` fails. Before, one failed read rejected the restart notice and left the child interrupted until the next restart while its object still ran the turn (open item 2, seed 560). `close_batch` returns at once while the scope is closing. `validate_insert` refuses inserts then, so `close_all` already closes every session of the scope. Before, a spawn whose start overlapped `close_all` found the journal frozen in `BatchStartup::commit`, and its rollback waited for the closing lock that `close_all` held while `close_all` waited for the spawning turn: both stopped for `AGENT_STOP_TIMEOUT` (30 s), in 7 of 5000 seeds once the start waited for the child. nanocode-sim: `Host::run` resolves after the child stored the input; mutation child-acks-early (the outer future resolves before the request reaches the child, the previous contract) is caught by 6 of seeds 0..1000 and 39 of 0..5000 (41 before the rebase onto 77a3bff00) (remote_turn_lost). Measurements (release nanocode-sim, this Hand, `bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 5000 3 --scenario runtime --children remote`): f2358b20c 62 of 5000 fail (36 remote_turn_lost, 24 remote_list_changed, 2 not settled); with the admission order and the `child_pending` retry 14 fail (the sweep lists 13: 7 close_all timeouts and 6 remote_list_changed from lost answers); those 13 seeds rerun with the `close_batch` change: 7 pass; with the `child_run` retry as well 0 of 5000 fail. Local children: `sweep.sh 0 2000 3 --scenario runtime` 2000/2000. Not covered: a parent that dies after the child stored the input and before the admission row is written redelivers the message after the restart, and the child receives it twice; the simulator has no duplicate-delivery check yet. A `child_run` that never succeeds blocks the harness in `start_turn`, so close and interrupt of that agent wait for `AGENT_STOP_TIMEOUT`. Hosts: nanocode-ts needs the matching `child_run`/`child_wait` change in src/wasm/children.rs. Other mutations with this change, seeds 0..1000: child-adopts-turn 42, child-forgets-notice 694 and child-settles-lazily 868 caught. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-subagents -p nanocode-agent -- -D warnings` is clean (nanocode-sim has two clippy errors in bin/nanocode-sim/src/alloc.rs, which this change does not touch); `cargo +1.97.1 check --locked -p nanocode-subagents -p nanocode-agent -p nanocode --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes; rustfmt --edition 2024 on the changed files.
- fix(subagents): `Harness` consumes the restart notice (`durable::RESUME_MESSAGE` from the root) when the recovered turn it was meant for already finished, and requeues every other message; remote.rs drops its `RemoteChildren::recovering` steer override; nanocode-sim gains `--children remote`, a simulated `ChildHost` (2026-11-14, dst lane). What: `start_turn` returns `Started::Prompt` or `Started::RecoveryOnly`. RecoveryOnly means the restored turn was resumed but its recovery steer answered `TurnNotSteerable` or `TurnStopped` (a remote child finished that turn while the parent was away; `child_pending` returns the last finished request, as nanocode-ts's Durable Object does). The message that started the turn and any batch go back to the front of the queue and start the next turn, except a `resumes()` message, which is admitted as Started because the turn it describes is over. Before, remote.rs turned that steer failure into `Ok(())` for the recovering request, so a peer message that happened to start the recovery turn was admitted and never reached the child (lost work). The previous lane's first version requeued the notice too, and the child ran one extra model turn per restored finished child (duplicated work). The simulator: bin/nanocode-sim/src/children.rs models child Durable Objects with their own disk (inputs, notices, running turn, steer ids, received prompts), a fault link (unsent, lost and duplicated requests and child_done notices, latency), child crashes that abort the worker and notifier and recover after 5 s, and a plan per child (spawn and wait on grandchildren, message peers, submit_result) driven through `RemoteChildren::call_tool`. `--store log` runs the parent on the turn log (`settle_durably` for remote seeds). After the roots settle, a remote seed kills the parent without shutdown, restarts it and checks: `remote_list_changed` (the agent listing is the same, not for Stop::Close), `remote_restart_reran` (no child turn runs, not for Stop::Close), `remote_turn_lost` (a completed child received every message whose send was accepted, only for Stop::Never without a cancelled root turn: an interruption fails queued messages by design) and `remote_completion_twice` (one parent incarnation sees a child turn complete once). Mutations: child-adopts-turn (a new request adopts the running turn) is caught by 52 of 0..1000 against 10 baseline failures, child-forgets-notice by 689, child-settles-lazily (the turn log settles lazily) by 871; a child-drops-steer mutation of the first version failed exactly the baseline's 62 of 0..5000 seeds and is removed. Measurements (`bin/nanocode-sim/sweep.sh 0 5000 4 --scenario runtime --children remote`, one build, this Hand): before the fix 314 of 5000 failed (174 remote_restart_reran under Close, 115 remote_turn_lost, 23 remote_list_changed, 2 not settled); 75 of the lost were interruption-cancelled messages and 174 reruns were the closed tree's journal not recording the close, so those checks are scoped as above; with the fix 62 of 5000 fail. Local children are unchanged: `sweep.sh 0 3000 4 --scenario runtime` 3000/3000 and `--wire http` 0..1000 1000/1000. Open, not fixed here: (1) 36 remote_turn_lost under Stop::Never (seed 231): the parent admits a message as Started and dies before `child_run` reaches the child, and on restart `child_pending` names the child's last finished request, so the in-flight request and its message vanish; the parent keeps no copy of a remote turn's prompt (by design, for its row count), so the fix is a durable in-flight request in the parent or a `child_run` the child acknowledges before the message is admitted. (2) 24 remote_list_changed (seed 560): one failed `child_pending` during resume makes `fail_unresumable` leave the child interrupted until the next restart; `pending` is a read and could be retried, which needs a retry policy. (3) Closing a root does not record its children's closed state durably before the scope freezes its journal, so a restart after Close resumes them (local and remote). Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-subagents -p nanocode-agent -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo check --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` for both.

- fix(code-mode): a session's `store()` values outlive the session's `LocalCells` runtime, so a `Cancel` ends the session's cells but not its stored values, and a hand that stays up while the brain retires keeps them (2026-11-14, nanocode 1.0 Code Mode conformance track: ts-hand store). A restart without a crash on the ts-hand host retires the brain runtime as Cloudflare does: on shutdown both backends cancel the tool runtime (claude_tools.rs, codex model/run), which sends the remote `Cancel { session_id }` to the hand, and the hand's `LocalCells::cancel` removed the session together with its `CodeModeRuntime` and that runtime's `stored` map. The next brain opened the same session on the same hand, which started a fresh runtime, so `load` read `undefined` (durability/store-persists-across-restart: `after restart: undefined`; the frames show `Cancel` after the first turn, then a close with code 1000 and a new connection). A hand with a cell journal sink lost the values the same way, since `CellJournals::load` reads a session's stored map only once per process. `LocalCells` now keeps each session's map in an `Arc<Atom<…>>` of its own and gives it to every runtime it starts for that session (`CodeModeRuntime::with_stored`), so the map outlives a cancelled runtime, and writes of cells that the cancel terminates land in it. `cancel` drops the entry only when its map is empty and no runtime holds it. Kept as it was: `Cancel` still terminates every cell of the session, a sink still restores keys the runtime does not hold, and a host that drops its `LocalCells` (a process restart, a disposed nanocode-ts module) still depends on its sink. The brain-side alternative (the brain keeps the stored map in its journal sink and seeds each new hand connection) was not taken: the remote protocol carries no stored values today, so it needs a new frame for every write and a seed on every open, whereas native hands already keep Code Mode state, cells and stored values, on the hand. A process that serves many sessions now keeps the stored map of each cancelled session that wrote one for as long as its `LocalCells` lives, which is what an open session already cost. Conformance, output/cm-conf over origin/master and over this change, durability cases and every case that names or calls `store`/`load` (74 cases, both backends): ts-hand 144 to 146 of 148 (store-persists-across-restart fail to pass on Claude and Codex), native-host 146 and 146, native-remote 144 and 144, native-remote-brain 144 and 144, ts-node 143 and 143 (the remaining failures are skips and the ts-node yielded-cell-wait-after-restart and Codex notify-not-resent-on-replay failures that fail on origin/master too), 0 pass to fail. The ts-hand host ran nanocode-ts origin/master built against this checkout with harness-gaps 0002 (ts-hand expect_on entries) applied to the suite. Commands: `cargo check --offline --locked --lib -p nanocode-code-mode` and `cargo clippy --offline --locked --no-deps --lib -p nanocode-code-mode -- -D warnings`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, nanocode-ts `cargo build --offline --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --profile wasm`. Files: crates/runtime/code-mode/src/code_mode/{local.rs,mod.rs}.

Unpaced: Responses 0.900 (0.535) to 0.921 (0.563), tail 7.07 / 23.37 to 5.73 / 23.77; Claude 0.933 (0.447) to 0.909 (0.529), tail 7.54 / 25.83 to 9.28 / 26.53. The 0.13 to 1.8 ms that the trace removed per turn is below the spread of these samples: unpaced, both arms draw 430k to 500k tok/s p50 against 510k to 580k from the mock, and the p99 tails of 17 to 27 ms on Claude come from single slow samples in both arms. The change stays, since the traces show the held event applied after the frame in 11 of 12 turns and event order unchanged. - The JSONL store replays a `moved` line of its `.summaries` journal through an index from file identity to state ids, built once on the first `moved` line of a refresh, and takes a `remember` line's summaries by value, instead of scanning every summary for each `moved` line and cloning each remembered one (`Change::replay`, crates/integrations/store-jsonl/src/summaries.rs; `Change::apply` stays for the single change `record` applies) (2026-11-14, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: every POST.md row ahead of fx). A 14,600-session store saved by bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=store --sessions=14600 --storejobs=12` leaves 267 `moved` and 131 `remember` lines after the 10.1 MB base frame, and `perf record` of `nanocode sessions` put 24% of its samples in `Change::apply`, 267 scans of 14,600 entries; the journal can grow to the base frame's size before a rewrite, so a long-lived store replays more. Built by scripts/build-cli.sh (dist, BOLT 21) at master 4e7737e64 with and without the change on an m4-metal-small box, 20 interleaved runs of `nanocode sessions --home <store>` under `perf stat`: user instructions 583.6M to 439.1M (-24.8%), kernel instructions 267.3M to 266.9M, page faults 13,840 to 13,690, task clock 80.8 to 55.7 ms, wall 81 to 57 ms, peak RSS 48.3 to 46.8 MB; `suite.mjs --parts=store --only=nc --storerounds=8` under BENCH_PERF=1: listing 93.7 to 67.7 ms wall (CPU 91.2 to 64.8 ms), continuing the latest session 100.4 to 73.6 ms wall (CPU 98.9 to 73.3 ms), all exits 0; fx 0.0.16 on the same store lists in 45.6 ms and continues in 67.5 ms, so listing still trails, now on the 14,606 statx calls of `Sessions::files` (kernel instructions 2.8x fx's) and the base frame's parse. `nanocode sessions --all` and `--all --limit 100000` print the same bytes with either build.
- fix(codex): a reply cut at max_output_tokens that holds only reasoning is still sent back on the retry, as Codex 0.162.1 does, but is no longer kept in the history once the step succeeds (2026-11-14, ~/hill/analysis/glm-backlog.md item 3; report ~/hill/analysis/glm-runaway.md). Runaway thinking in cmp2 GLM-5.3-Flash at effort high (calls of at least 60,000 output tokens or cut by max_output_tokens, tiny image incompletes left out; ~/hill/analysis/runaway_quant.py): stock-codex 3 calls in 3 of 61 trials (785 s), nc-codex (old build 4c2c2ca) 11 in 6 of 54 (4,641 s), stock-claude 19 in 10 of 65 (11,209 s), nc-claude 4 in 4 of 58 (2,274 s); each costs about $0.033 and 190 to 1,130 s. All three stock-codex cuts held one reasoning item and nothing else (227,046, 226,374 and 247,010 characters in the last requests of make-mips-interpreter-a1-t0, regex-chess-a1-t0 and circuit-fibsqrt-a1-t0). On the gateway's Responses route a trailing reasoning item is dropped from the prompt, but one followed by a function_call is kept: a 10,239-character reasoning item added 0 input tokens as the last item (163 against 163) or before a final assistant message (167 with the message), and 1,920 before a function_call (2,100 against 180), two of them 3,840. So Codex's retry, which appends the cut reasoning, reaches the model as the unchanged request, and once the retry answers with a call the dead reasoning sits before it and is billed on every later call: the input after the retry rose by 71,327, 65,923 and 54,921 tokens and stayed for the rest of those trials (22, 152 and 20 calls, 12.7M input tokens, $0.38 at the fitted $0.03/M cached rate; ~/hill/analysis/runaway_carry.py). This tree records the step as before (the cut items still go into each retry, so a provider that reads reasoning items can resume from them) but leaves out of the step's output, and so the session history and the durable step record, every cut batch that holds only reasoning; a cut that holds a message keeps all its items as before. Live, through a private meter proxy on port 18097 ($0.6 in all): replaying the three cut requests at effort high 13 times answered every time with a call in 47 to 2,707 output tokens, so a plain retry is what recovers on this route and a lower effort is not needed for it (effort is honored: on a number-theory prompt with a 12,000-token cap, low finished in 1,048 to 6,076 tokens 7 of 7, medium and high hit the cap 17 of 17, on both routes); replaying the request after each retry with and without the cut reasoning (2 each) took 259,193 against 193,657, 82,947 against 28,419 and 293,416 against 227,880 input tokens, and all 12 answered with a sensible exec_command call of 69 to 960 tokens. The mock (~/wt/glm-runaway-mock, mode rcall: a reasoning-only incomplete, then a call, then DONE; `python3 run.py stock:rcall:1 base:rcall:1 new:rcall:1`): stock Codex 0.162.1, nanocode 0020940 and this tree send the same retry ([user, reasoning]); the request after the call carries [user, reasoning, function_call, function_call_output] in stock and 0020940 and [user, function_call, function_call_output] here; rcall:2 likewise (8 items against 6); zinc:1, zinc:6 and zinccall:1, whose cuts hold a message, send the same requests as 0020940. The Claude harness is unchanged: its continuation after a max_tokens cut keeps the cut thinking, which the Messages route does pass to GLM (the next input rose by 65,580 tokens in nc-claude regex-chess-a1-t0), and replaying that continuation with Claude Code's "Output token limit hit" text answered 6 of 6 times in 73 to 5,123 tokens at effort high or low, while Claude Code's own recovery, which drops the cut thinking and appends the same text, ran to the 40,000-token probe cap in 3 replays (318 to 373 s) and was still thinking in the other 3 when the upstream cut the stream after 190 to 273 s and in cmp2 stock-claude cut again right after 4 of 15 cuts. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`, `cargo build --locked -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`.
