A naked function's CFA at entry is `rsp+8` whatever its caller's frame, so this holds with frame pointers forced too, which annotating the `asm!` blocks in place would not: the enclosing function's CFA is then rbp-based and X25519 overwrites rbp. Windows gets no CFI (`Cfi!` expands to nothing there, as it unwinds with `.pdata`). The other 46 x86_64 routines leave rsp alone and stay `asm!`. aarch64's assembly also moves sp without CFI (576 bytes in `mlkem_rej_uniform_vartime`) and is unchanged. Checked with output/graviola-cfi, built for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu in an arm64 container and run under `qemu-x86_64 -cpu max` (Rosetta has no ADX, which graviola requires): `transform.py` made the change and fails on a jump, call or return whose stack depth disagrees with where it lands; `verify_cfi.py` walks every reachable instruction of the 39 linked functions from their entry (jumps, calls into their subroutines, `ret`) and found the CFA rule equal to the stack at all of them; `unwind` runs X25519, ML-KEM-768, P-256 and P-384 ECDH and ECDSA, Ed25519 with key decoding and RSA-4096 signing in a loop, checking every agreement, decapsulation and signature, under a 1 kHz `ITIMER_PROF` handler that unwinds with `backtrace::trace_unsynchronized`, pprof-rs's path. On master's graviola (`unwind-before`) and on crates.io graviola 0.4.1 it died with SIGSEGV within seconds in each of 6 runs, at that libgcc instruction, sampled in `curve25519_x25519` or `curve25519_x25519base`. With the change, 31 runs (5 of 60 s, 26 of 10 to 30 s) took 565,878 samples inside graviola, from 28 of the 39 routines in a 20 s run, and every one unwound to `main`. Four earlier runs of the harness died without reaching its fault reporter right after its binary was rebuilt; 31 later runs, 6 of them from the same source, did not, and running a copy while rebuilding it did not reproduce it. graviola 0.4.1's own tests (157 unit and CAVP, 18 Wycheproof, 11 zeroing, with the vectors of its v/0.4.1 tag) pass with the 39 files swapped in, as they do with the original assembly. Under qemu no operation got slower (µs per operation, three interleaved runs each, after against before): X25519 253 to 254 against 254 to 272, ML-KEM-768 320 to 323 against 324 to 332, P-256 ECDH 299 to 300 against 339 to 368, P-384 ECDH 2,775 to 2,805 against 4,323 to 4,404, P-256 ECDSA 344 to 345 against 382 to 414, P-384 ECDSA 4,134 to 4,141 against 6,698 to 6,810, Ed25519 174 to 176 against 174 to 189, RSA-4096 signing 20,495 to 20,641 against 20,567 to 21,030. qemu's timing is not a CPU's, so this shows the extra call per routine costs nothing measurable there, not what an x86_64 machine gains. `cargo check --locked --lib` of graviola, nanocode-tls, nanocode-sandbox and nanocode-mpp natively, for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and for x86_64-apple-darwin, of the last three for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and release builds of graviola for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, x86_64-unknown-linux-musl and aarch64-apple-darwin passed. Files: `crates/patches/graviola/src/low/macros.rs` and 39 files in `crates/patches/graviola/src/low/x86_64/`.
- The codex `apply_patch` handlers accept a JSON function call whose arguments carry the patch text in `input` (or `patch`), and apply it as the freeform form (2026-11-15). DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on the codex harness sometimes sends `{"input": "*** Begin Patch..."}` as a `function_call`, and `ToolInput::into_freeform` answered `expected freeform tool input`, so the model rewrote the whole file through `exec_command` and spent about 2x input tokens on the chain. A scan of every codex trajectory under ~/hill/harbor/jobs and ~/hill/cf/runs (last-request.json for nc, rollout-*.jsonl for stock, 2026-11-15) found function-style `apply_patch` calls only from DeepSeek: nc 3 of 88 trials (cf 2 of 3, vercel 1 of 85, every one answered `expected freeform tool input`), stock 1 of 128 trials. GLM 5.3 Flash made none in 232 nc and 87 stock trials. Codex CLI 0.162.1 goes no further: `ApplyPatchHandler::matches_kind` accepts only `ToolPayload::Custom`, and its one DeepSeek call got `unsupported call: apply_patch`, so this acceptance goes past stock. Arguments without a string `input` or `patch` field return `failed to parse function arguments: ...`. Checked with `output/ap-fn` (a scripted Responses mock that emits one `apply_patch` call, then `DONE`, run through `nanocode exec --harness codex --model @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, debug builds before and after on master 1d9243eb1): before, `{"input"}` and `{"patch"}` returned `expected freeform tool input` and wrote no file; after, both returned `Success. Updated the following files:\nA hello.txt\n` and wrote `hello from patch`, byte for byte the freeform call's output.
- perf(djs): three run_hot changes for the tier-0 `loop` bench measured and not shipped, and the wasm `loop` count varies by up to 6% between identical runs (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs loop lane wave 3). Base: b29aaf7d2. Method: output/djsloop3-style harness (djsrun, fuelrun, t262 and the wasmrun cdylib of djs-embed with `unsafe-heap` under node 24, `perf stat -e instructions:u` best of 3, wasm as 13 runs minus 3 runs over 10) on the hosted Hand, with `valgrind --tool=callgrind --dump-instr=yes` per-instruction counts of `run_hot` on loop.js divided by its 2,000,000 iterations. Profile at the base: 150.3 instructions per iteration, all in `run_hot`: two dispatch heads of 13 (bounds check of the word, `cmp 0xd8` range check, jump table), `add_loc8` 22 to decode both operands, 34 on its f64 path (`s` passes int32 after about 65,000 iterations, so 97% of iterations add an f64 and an int32), 10 for the store, `inc_lt` about 47, and the backward-jump checks 8. Results (native loop, native gen, native others): (1) one frame pointer `lpv = vals + 8 * lp` (a `loc!` macro for every local slot, `self.lp` where the index is needed): loop 301.4M -> 304.9M (+1.2%), gennext +2.0%, err +1.3%. The local accesses lose one add each, but LLVM's register assignment for the rest of `run_hot` adds more moves than that saves. (3) `add_loc8` reads the next word and runs `inc_lt` or `inc_lt_loc` in place (both arms as macros that decline with their own opcode): loop 301.4M -> 308.5M (+2.4%), gen +2.9%. The dispatch head goes, but the inlined copies add about 20 register moves and spills per iteration (for example `mov %r11,%r12; mov %r15,%r11; mov %rsi,%r15` on the `add_loc8` path). (1) and (3) together: loop 302.6M (+0.4%), gen +1.9%. An `add_loc8` f64 path through `Value::is_number` and one decode per operand: loop 334.3M (+10.9%), since LLVM lowers the two tests to `sete`/`setne` pairs with reloaded 64-bit masks (48 instructions against 34). An explicit `OP_COUNT..=u8::MAX` arm to remove the dispatch range check: identical native code (rustc merges the arm with the default). The other native benches moved within 0.2% in every variant. Wasm: two runs of the same base module gave loop 313.6M and 333.7M (forEach 335.7M and 341.6M), so V8's tier-up timing, not the code, decides the wasm `loop` count at this sample size, and a 1% wasm gate on `loop` needs a larger sample (best of 10 or more) before it can separate changes. Not tried: bet (2), moving rarely run arms out of `run_hot`, which is the remaining lever on the register pressure that defeats (1) and (3). Checked on the base: test262 subset 2,535 passing, fuel harness output recorded. No source change.
- A released reactor driver wakes one of the workers waiting for it, not all of them (2026-11-15). `Reactor::release` (after every `try_turn`, so after each reactor turn and each worker's emptied run queue) unparked every worker in `park_for_driver`; only one can take the driver, so the rest woke, failed `try_turn` and parked again, and with 32 workers that herd was most of the process's CPU. A perf profile of tempoxyz/pyramid2's server on a 32-core host, idle after its work with two turns stuck, put 93% of its samples under `Shared::work` in `park`, `futex_wake` and `notify_waiting`, burning 2 to 8 cores with nothing to run. One wake is enough: the woken worker takes the driver when it idles, and a worker with tasks reaches `try_turn` within `EVENT_INTERVAL` polls or when its queue empties, as before. Measured on that host with pyramid2's bench conc phase (50 concurrent turns, 1,560 jobs; base pyramid2 8f4de91 on nanocode d5498e78, interleaved, load 15 to 20): server CPU per phase 43.1 and 45.3 core-seconds before, 10.0 and 8.8 after; replayed-turn overhead p50 82 and 102 ms before, 62 and 66 after; idle CPU with stuck turns 2.94 cores before, 0.00 after. Two earlier pairs at load 21 to 24 measured CPU 40.6 to 15.0 and 12.7, with overhead p50 worse (77 and 102 to 133 and 204 ms), so it is not a latency win on a saturated host. Also tried, and not kept: waking a parked worker from `Shared::notify` even while one runs (hung one run and spun 3.9 cores idle), and waking one only while the run queue outgrows the running workers (one of two runs had 8 timeouts). `nanocode-sim --scenario executor` passes seeds 0..200 and still catches all ten executor mutations.

The tool definitions and `prompts/compact.md` are byte-identical to 2.1.318. 2.1.325 builds the compaction prompt's first section from a `CRITICAL: Respond with TEXT ONLY` constant and `${...}` placeholders, so the extractor now finds that template by its `. - fix(codex): pin codex-cli 0.169.0 (rust-v0.169.0, d32063f96c2d) in place of 0.166.0. The pinned tool sources (shell, apply_patch, plan, view_image specs, the lark grammar, responses_api, tool_spec, json_schema types) are byte-identical at 0.169.0. `models.json` adds gpt-6.1-terra at index 2, whose instructions template is astra's (nanocode already sends astra.md for Terra), so luna.md moves to `/models/4` with unchanged bytes. - The codex agent driver and the CLI `exec` future hold their large state on the heap only while it lives (2026-11-15). `AgentDriver::run` takes `self: Box<Self>`: an async fn keeps its by-value argument twice (the upvar and the moved local), so the 4,240-byte driver sat in the future three times with the spawn block's own copy. `ModelRun` (3,856 bytes) lives in a `Box`, and the awaits of `accept_execution_command`, `accept_idle_route`, `Execution::persist` and `Execution::cancel_operation` (2.3 to 3.6 KB each) are boxed. `Command::Spawn` carries `Option<Box<ChildState>>`, so `Command` drops from 976 to 256 bytes in every driver local and channel slot. In `nanocode_cli::exec`, `SessionArgs` is boxed and the `prepare`, `Host::start`, `app::open_session`, `attempts::run`, `latest_session`, `unanswered` and `host::archive` awaits are boxed. Layouts from `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1 cargo rustc --release -p nanocode-backend-codex --lib -- -Zprint-type-sizes` (and `-p nanocode-cli`): the spawned driver block went from 28,016 to 6,608 bytes, `AgentDriver::run` from 23,736 to 6,560 and the `exec` future from 15,168 to 4,728. Measured on 47e915f9a with `~/sw/heapprof/tracer.patch` and `run.sh` (one direct 10-step tool turn, bench/cli tools part, h=ncdirect): the global live heap peak went from 646,262 to 622,609 bytes and the worker thread's share from 474,649 to 460,594. The `spawn_agent_driver` allocation site holds 11,208 bytes in 8 blocks instead of 28,376 in 7, plus 6,280 bytes boxed under `run`, and the `exec` task 4,728 bytes instead of 15,168. Peak RSS of untraced release builds, 3 interleaved runs each, was 30.16, 31.13 and 31.08 MB before and 30.11, 30.66 and 31.05 MB after, which is within noise. Both builds sent 11 requests of 28,999 to 32,532 bytes. `execute_task` (10,592 bytes) stays as it is: its 7,360-byte `drive_session` await is the state that is live during a turn, so boxing it moves those bytes without a reduction. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex`, also for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo clippy -p nanocode-backend-codex -p nanocode-cli` passed.
- `RoutedTool::definition` clones the local tool's parameters schema only when it adds `workdir` (a `cua` tool, or a route snapshot that is not empty) or changes `required` (a `cua` tool). Otherwise the routed definition shares the local `JsonSchema` `Arc<Value>`. Before this change, every routed tool deep-cloned its schema `Value` and then stored the unchanged copy. In the direct tool turn, `routing.rs:526` allocated nothing, so every clone was equal to its source. Measured on 47e915f9a with `~/sw/heapprof/tracer.patch` and `run.sh` (one direct 10-step tool turn, bench/cli tools part, h=ncdirect), analysed with `tr.py`: the global live heap peak went from 646,252 bytes in 3,348 blocks to 629,980 bytes in 3,066 blocks, and the worker thread's share from 474,651 to 458,383. The tool definition theme went from 93,896 bytes in 983 blocks to 77,648 bytes in 703 blocks, and its total allocation from 179,299 to 148,675 bytes. The clone site held 30,598 bytes in 424 blocks and now holds none. The net is smaller than the clone because `JobTool::definition` builds a new `Value` on each call: that value (13,702 bytes) was freed after the clone and is now the stored one. Both builds sent 11 requests of 29,013 to 32,546 bytes, 338,561 bytes in all, identical except for message UUIDs and the tool output's chunk ID and wall time. Peak RSS of untraced release builds (`max_rss_mb` of the suite, 5 interleaved runs each) was 30.53, 31.26, 31.27, 30.97 and 30.75 MB before and 30.53, 31.00, 31.18, 31.00 and 31.05 MB after, which is within noise. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-tool-runtime`, also for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, passed.
- The codex request prefix keeps the instructions text once as text and once as JSON, and the durable prefix log shares the request encoder's JSON (2026-11-15). A heap trace of one 10-step direct tool turn (`bench/cli` tools part, h=ncdirect, the tracer of ~/sw/heapprof on master 9c49d6f98) held the 18 KB instructions five times at the peak: `PrefixDigest.instructions` in `prompt_cache` (18.0 KB), `RequestPrefix.instructions` in `shared_request_prefix` (18.0 KB), the developer message item (18.0 KB), the request encoder's `encoded_prefix` RawValues (26.5 KB with the tools item) and `ContinuationCache::sync_prefix`'s `EncodedPayload`s (26.5 KB), 111.5 KB in all. Now `prefix_digest` compares a SHA-256 of the instructions, `shared_request_prefix` compares the instructions against the text in its cached developer item, and `SharedPrefix` keeps one lazily filled `Arc<str>` of each prefix item's plain JSON. `RequestInput::encode_prefix` reuses that `Arc<str>` for every item that `RequestResponseItem::rewritten` leaves unchanged (the developer item) and encodes the rewritten ones (the `functions` namespace of the tools item) itself, and `sync_prefix` takes the same `Arc<str>`s through `shared_prefix_json` before its own encoder. `shared_prefix` no longer stores an empty prefix as the last one: `ModelRun::preconnect` builds a profile over `Arc::from([])`, which replaced the turn's prefix there and made `shared_prefix_json` miss. Measured on the hosted Hand with `run.sh` and `tr.py` of ~/sw/heapprof, a release build with line tables and the tracer: the prefix theme at the peak went from 111,531 B to 56,421 B (developer item 18,043, shared JSON 26,504, rewritten tools item 8,176), the global peak from 646,250 B to 564,335 B and the worker's from 474,725 B to 392,706 B (the second run on master ba3deec20, so other changes contribute to the totals, not to the theme). The 11 request bodies of the turn (`DUMP` of `harness/fakellm.mjs`, 29,013 to 32,546 bytes) are byte-identical to the base build's after the item ids, `Chunk ID` and `Wall time` are masked. Peak RSS of release builds, 8 interleaved runs each with `peak.py`: Anonymous RSS at the peak 1,792 KB to 1,754 KB median (minimum 1,712 to 1,684), total RSS 31,622 KB to 31,644 KB (file-backed text of a non-BOLT build moves it by more than the heap change), allocator segments resident 946 KB to 960 KB; an earlier 8-pair run of the same change without the empty-prefix rule gave Anonymous 1,790 to 1,732 KB and segments 1,138 to 1,064 KB, so the RSS effect is about 40 to 60 KB of anonymous memory and inside the noise of total RSS. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex-client -p nanocode-backend-codex`, also for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo clippy` of both passed. Files: `crates/backends/codex/client/src/responses/{mod,request}.rs`, `crates/backends/codex/client/src/session/context.rs`, `crates/backends/codex/src/prompt_cache.rs`, `crates/backends/codex/src/durability/context.rs`.
- perf(subagents): `Registry::release_all` skips the release of a scope whose task tree never reserved an agent ID when no subagent store, journal or journal reservation is installed, and marks that scope `Released` in the same mailbox call (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track, shutdown-path lane). Why: the tool turn's peak RSS falls at process exit, and `release_scope` touched cold code (restoration wait, scope locks, message pause, close request, change notification) in fresh 64 KB fault-around windows even when no subagent ever ran. A scope with `next_id == 0` has no topology, sessions or cold leaves, and without a store or journal there is nothing to save, so skipping it drops no dispatched work. A scope that ever reserved an ID, or any registry with a store or journal, takes the full release as before. Measured: bench/cli tools part (`--parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc`, direct lane) under tools/netguard.sh on the hosted Hand, dist + BOLT binaries from scripts/build-cli.sh at d9d958224 with and without the change, three interleaved passes of 4 rounds (`m.sh 4 3 base new`): max RSS median base 8.52, 8.54, 8.55 MB, change 8.17, 8.10, 8.14 MB (-0.40 MB, -4.7%), cpu/step unchanged (2.0 ms). After the runs no nanocode process remained. Not shipped from the same lane: an exit that skips drop glue after `services.shutdown` (it needs child process groups terminated outside `Drop` first), and a BOLT training change (train-cli.py tools mode already runs the ephemeral exec through exit, so the shutdown path is already in the profile). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-subagents` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-subagents`.

- perf(djs): `run_tier1` translates a hot loop body into a register form at entry and runs that instead of the bytecode (interp/run/tier1.rs only, `run_hot` unchanged) (loop 262.15M -> 238.31M instructions natively, -9.1%) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs tier-1 register lane). What: `translate` walks the body from the loop head to its backward jump once per entry with an abstract operand stack. Locals, arguments, stack slots and constants become registers in a 256-entry `Value` array loaded at entry (a register index is a u8, so its reads have no bounds check); `GET_LOC`/`GET_ARG`/push instructions emit nothing, a binary op writes the temp of its stack depth, `PUT_LOC` retargets the previous op's destination, a compare followed by a conditional jump becomes one `Branch`, and an int step of the counter followed by that branch against an int constant becomes one `Latch` (`i++ < n`), or `StepBranch` against a register. Every op records the exit state of the first bytecode instruction it covers (pc and the abstract stack), so a decline, a jump out, the fall-through at the body end, the fuel check at the head and the backedge budget write back the written locals and the live stack slots and leave at a bytecode boundary with exactly the fuel `run_hot` would have left: each op charges the summed fuel of the instructions it covers, and the pass guard (`fuel > pass`) is unchanged. Forward jumps inside the body are labels: the abstract stack is materialized into its canonical temps before a jump and at a label, and a write to a local first materializes stack entries that still name it. The typed `I` form is lowered to a flat `Op` struct (kind byte plus fixed fields) for the run loop: a `#[repr(u8)]` data enum made LLVM decode every variant's fields in the dispatch. New ops beyond 8b3968951: `PUSH_CONST`/`PUSH_CONST8`, `STRICT_EQ`/`STRICT_NE` (numbers and identical bits, declining for two strings or two BigInts), `NOT`, `IS_UNDEFINED`, `IS_NULLISH`, dense `GET_ELEM` (`Heap::get_element_fast`, int32 key >= 0) and `PUT_ELEM` (`set_element_fast`, and with a collection wanted after it the pass leaves at the next instruction, so `run_hot` reaches the same safepoint). Float results above |i32::MAX| skip `conv::number`'s int probe (same bits). Steps measured on loop: first register form with a niche-packed enum 333.1M (166/iteration, worse), `repr(u8)` and compare masks 291.6M, `Latch` and the add overflow and float paths 260.0M, flat `Op` 238.3M (~119/iteration). The raised target (loop <= 106M, 5x QuickJS 530.7M) is not met: per iteration the two dispatches cost ~15 instructions each (bounds check, eager field loads, jump table), the float `s += i` ~35 and the latch ~25, so reaching ~53 needs either one dispatch per iteration (a loop-latch suffix on the preceding op) or unboxed int/float registers specialized from the entry values. Not done: field loads through the IC (`field_hit` is private to hot.rs) and calls to leaf functions. Code Mode cells do not change: their loops run under 16,384 backedges or contain calls and field ops, so `run_tier1` is not reached. Measured on the hosted Hand, base 8b3968951 against this change (output/djsrun, output/fuelrun, output/t262, output/cellbench, ~/sw/tier1x/{bench,fuel,cb}.sh). `perf stat -e instructions:u` best of 5: loop 262,153,694 -> 238,306,225 (-9.10%), gen 2,061.645M -> 2,061.645M, gennext 4,380.672M -> 4,380.672M, find 91.278M -> 91.278M, forEach 94.558M -> 94.559M, some 92.965M -> 92.966M, filter 146.251M -> 146.251M, map 161.390M -> 161.391M, reduce 93.023M -> 93.023M, err 660.399M -> 660.399M (all others within +0.001%). Cellbench (instructions per cell, best of 3, 1,200 minus 200 cells, loop 60 minus 10): empty 81,358 -> 81,311, tool1 189,092 -> 188,994, seq16 1,016,433 -> 1,015,749, par16 1,129,545 -> 1,128,838, loop 173,195,428 -> 173,195,653, agent 1,819,383 -> 1,819,387, sh 2,309,031 -> 2,309,008, seq 1,113,310 -> 1,112,766, json 1,465,659 -> 1,465,557 (noise). Checks: test262 subset (~/t262.list) 2,535 passing, output identical to base; the fuel harness (`Instance::step`, fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited, slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000) prints identical results, yields and `fuel_used` for the four edge scripts, the ten benches and two tier-1 scripts (~/sw/tier1x/js/check.js: dense element loads and appends, if/else and ternary branches, break, `===` on strings, null and undefined, `!`, int overflow into doubles, shifts, modulo and NaN compares, all past 16,384 iterations; loop2.js), 360 lines each; `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Wasm instruction counts were not measured in this change.
- A foreground Bash command whose shell exits while processes it started still run names them in its stderr: "The command exited, and these processes it started are still running in the background. Nothing reports when they end:" and one line per process, such as `PID 766 (fasttext supervised ...)` (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1, bg-survivors lane). In train-fasttext a00345 the model ran `prep && shuf && nohup fasttext ... &`, Bash returned no output in 0 s while the chain kept running, and the model started a second training on a 1-vCPU slot; eight Nano attempts started work with `&` or `nohup` instead of `run_in_background`. `run_bash` exports `NANOCODE_COMMAND_ID` (the hand's pid and a counter; a warm shell receives it on stdin with the session variables, so its pool lane does not change). After the shell exits, `nanocode_executor::process::survivors` lists the live processes that are in the shell's process group, or lead a session and carry that mark: psh keeps externals and forked `&` jobs in its own group (`Placement::Inherit`) and starts `nohup` and `setsid` externals in a session of their own (D1067). Linux and Android read /proc. macOS uses `proc_listallpids`, `getpgid`, `getsid` and `KERN_PROCARGS2` through new nanocode-sys bindings, since `ps -axwwE` took a 95 ms median on gak-9. Other platforms list nothing. A forked copy of psh is named "psh, running part of the command". The caller's `max_stderr` (the Bash tool's stream bytes) bounds the note: a line falls back to the PID alone, then to "and N more", and the command's own stderr is cut to make room, as for the memory-kill line. The text without survivors is unchanged. Harness: output/bg-survivors-agent (a Claude agent with `install_default_tools`, so Code Mode with nested Bash, against a local Messages SSE mock; `run.sh` prints each tool result). On Linux (rust:slim-trixie arm64 container on gak-9), `sleep 30 &`, `true && (sleep 30) &`, `nohup sleep 31 > /dev/null 2>&1 &`, `true && sleep 32 &`, `true && nohup sleep 33 > /dev/null 2>&1 &` and `for i in 1 2 3; do sleep 4$i & done` name their survivors (the fifth case: `PID 18828 (psh, running part of the command)` and `PID 18831 (sleep 33)`), `echo hi` returns `hi` with no note, and a python3 survivor with 40,000 arguments is listed by PID alone under the 128 KiB nested limit. On macOS psh runs a `&` job that is not one program on a thread (`fork_jobs` is Linux-only), so `sleep 30 &`, `true && (sleep 30) &` and `true && sleep 32 &` leave nothing running and get no note, and `nohup sleep 31 > /dev/null 2>&1 &` is named. Scan cost (`output/bg-survivors-agent/src/bin/scan.rs`, debug build, three runs): Linux with 25 processes, median 110 to 114 us and p95 125 to 133 us over 200 rounds; macOS with 790 processes, median 2.09 to 2.14 ms and p95 2.39 to 2.44 ms over 50 rounds. Checks: `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-executor -p nanocode-process -- -D warnings` for the host, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and aarch64-apple-ios, `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-sys -- -D warnings` on macOS, `cargo check --locked --lib --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -p nanocode-executor -p nanocode-process`, and `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- The one-shot `exec` exit that skips agent and host drop glue and `runtime.shutdown_background` was measured and not shipped, and neither was a contiguous shutdown-only group in `scripts/order-cli.py` (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track, shutdown-path lane, wave 2). The variant on 3f184c786 kept a process-wide registry of armed `ProcessGroupGuard` groups (`nanocode_process::terminate_groups`, SIGSTOP and SIGKILL per group) and of live `kill_on_drop` children (`nanocode_executor::process::kill_live`), and on unix `exec` called `std::mem::forget` on the agent and host after `host.runtime.shutdown()` and `host::archive`, then `main` ran `tempo::close`, both kills, dropped the telemetry guard and called `std::process::exit`. The registry is process-wide, so it belongs at process exit, not in `HostServices::shutdown`: an SDK host can run several runtimes in one process. Correctness held: a turn whose `exec_command` left `sleep 300` running (yield 250 ms) left no such process in both builds, the JSONL session resumed with `--continue`, stdout ended with the full reply, and with `NANOCODE_TELEMETRY=agent` and a local OTLP collector under a loopback-only namespace both builds exported the same span names (146,250 and 146,227 OTLP bytes). With network, the variant omitted the `mcp.initialize`, `mcp.server_start` and `mcp.transport_connect` spans of MCP connections still in flight at exit, which the base build closes only by dropping their tasks. A child that `sh -c 'sleep 301 &'` puts in the background of a finished command survives in both builds: `ProcessChild::new` disarms the guard once the leader is reaped. Why it is not shipped: the shutdown path is not where the exit peak comes from. A gdb probe (`pg.py`: pagemap and `/proc/<pid>/status` at the write of `session ` to stderr and at `exit_group`, 9 direct 10-step tool turns of `train-cli.py tools` per build, interleaved) found that after the cut the base build faults a median 44 pages of `nanocode-agent` text (28 to 90) in a median 3 new 64 KB windows, and the variant 32 pages (16 to 32) in 2. Both builds also fault 37 pages of `ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` and 0 to 139 pages of `libc.so.6` text in `exit` (`_dl_fini` and atexit). The base build frees 29 to 64 anonymous pages (`madvise`) during drop glue before those faults, and the variant frees none, so VmHWM minus VmRSS at the cut was a median 168 KB for the base build and 276 KB for the variant. On dist + BOLT binaries from `scripts/build-cli.sh` (base 3f184c786, variant the same plus the change), 3 interleaved passes of 4 rounds each: the direct tool turn (`--parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc` in benchd) had max RSS pass medians 8.51, 8.35, 8.53 MB base and 8.59, 8.69, 8.72 MB variant, the Code Mode tool turn (bench/cli) 11.54, 11.17, 11.81 and 11.55, 12.05, 11.80 MB, one-shot 6.84, 7.12, 7.30 and 6.75, 7.34, 7.41 MB, and first frame, which never runs the changed code, 6.18, 6.17, 6.44 and 6.53, 6.66, 6.55 MB, so the BOLT layout of each build moves peak RSS by about 0.3 MB on its own. Instruction counts are not available on the hosted Hand (no perf). From the `session ` write to `exit_group`, strace showed 1.5 ms and 13 `madvise` calls for the base build and 0.7 ms with none for the variant. The shutdown-only group of `order-cli.py` has no room to act: 44 pages already sit in 3 windows, the minimum for 44 pages. An exit through `_exit` after flushing stdout would skip the `ld.so` and libc faults, but it also skips the BOLT instrumentation dump that `DT_FINI` runs, so `train-cli.py` would lose every exec profile. Commands: `~/sw/buildq.sh ./build.sh base|new` (`scripts/build-cli.sh nanocode-cli nanocode`, `LLVM_BOLT=/usr/lib/llvm-23/bin/llvm-bolt`), `m.sh 3`, `bg.py` and `pg.py` of ~/sw/shutdown2, and `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-process -p nanocode-executor` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` plus `cargo clippy` of the variant passed.
- perf(djs): `run_tier1` runs the loop latch as a suffix of the op before it, dispatches from a fixed 256-entry op array, tests the latch bound as one wrapping range compare, and runs a loop to its end instead of returning every 16,384 backedges (loop 238.27M -> 148.73M instructions natively, -37.6%) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs tier-1 wave 3). What: after lowering, a `Latch` that jumps to the loop head and is no label target is copied into the op before it when that op only writes a register (`Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, `Mod`, the bitwise ops, `Mov`, `Step`, `GetElem`, `Not`, `IsUndefined`, `IsNullish`): that op then steps the counter, charges the latch's fuel, and goes to the head or past the latch, so `s += i; i++ < n` is one dispatch per iteration. A failed counter step leaves at the latch's own exit state with the first op's fuel charged, which is what the separate `Latch` op did. The program is copied into a `[Op; 256]` indexed by a `u8` (a program over 256 ops declines, as a register index is already a `u8`) and read through a reference, so the dispatch has no bounds check and no longer loads and spills all 16 `Op` fields before the jump table (31 to 14 instructions). `Latch` stores the int range of counter values that take the jump (`lo` and `span`, from the compare mask and the bound) and tests `i.wrapping_sub(lo) as u32 <= span`; a bound whose range is empty (`i < i32::MIN`) becomes a `StepBranch` instead. The backedge budget in `run_tier1` is removed and `run_tier1` returns nothing: the run loop called it again at once after a budget exit (`while self.fuel > 0 && self.run_tier1() {}`), so the budget only re-translated the loop every 16,384 iterations; the head still leaves when the fuel reaches the pass guard. Steps on loop (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 5): latch suffix 204.76M, fixed array 169.14M, range latch 153.32M, no budget 148.73M (~74 per iteration: dispatch 14, float add ~30, latch and fuel ~25). Base 6ecd42e3e against this change, hosted Hand: loop 238,274,153 -> 148,725,556, gen 1,985.643M -> 1,985.645M, gennext 4,306.682M -> 4,306.684M, find 90.817M -> 90.819M, forEach 94.097M -> 94.100M, some 92.504M -> 92.507M, filter 145.811M -> 145.814M, map 160.951M -> 160.954M, reduce 92.562M -> 92.564M, err 653.201M -> 653.203M (others within +0.003%, the larger code). The loop target (<= 106M, 5x QuickJS) is not met: the rest is the generic float add (`s` leaves int32 after ~65,536 iterations) and the per-op fuel and tag checks, which need registers specialized by type. Checks: test262 subset (~/t262.list) 2,535 passing, identical to base; the fuel harness (fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited, slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000) prints identical results, yields and `fuel_used` for the four edge scripts, the ten benches, gennext, jsonfuel and a tier-1 script with 17 loops past 16,384 iterations (add, sub and mul overflow into doubles, modulo, dense element loads and stores, `Mov`, `!`, xor with a down-counting latch, step 2, float accumulators, a counter that overflows int32 at the latch, a float bound, `/`, if/else, `=== undefined`, a string concat that declines), 384 lines each; `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32 reports nothing in the changed files (its other errors, in bytecode/handlers.rs, bytecode/template.rs, compiler/parser.rs, heap/arena.rs and regexp/exec.rs, are on master with this toolchain; the one in tier1.rs, an `as u32` on a `u32`, is fixed here).
- docs(decisions): f09d89ceb measured in wasm, and what tier 1 for generators needs (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs tier-1 wave 3). Wasm (wasmrun cdylib for wasm32-unknown-unknown, release, run by Node 24, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, steady state per run as (13 runs - 3 runs) / 10, best of 3, base 6ecd42e3e): loop 334,442,800 -> 219,397,983 (-34.4%), gen 2,166.7M -> 2,171.2M (+0.2%, gen does not reach `run_tier1`). Generators are not changed. A callgrind profile of gen (two for-of loops over a 100,000-yield generator, f09d89ceb, 198.6M instructions) puts ~990 instructions on each iteration: `run_hot` ~365 (the dispatch alone ~42), `gen_resume_hot` ~305 (about 100 of them in heap layout accessors: `object_slots`, the saved array's length and capacity, `template_of`, `template_head`, plus the realm check of `GENERATOR_NEXT`) and `gen_yield_hot` ~285. QuickJS spends ~690 per iteration. The target (<= 691M, ~345 per iteration) is below QuickJS, so trimming these two calls is not enough: the generator's loop body and the for-of body have to run as one register program, with the yield and the resume as register moves and an exit that writes back both frames in the suspended state `gen_yield_hot` leaves (pc, `hp_off`, state, the caller's `iter_next_loc` result). `body` declines both loops today (`YIELD` and `ITER_NEXT_LOC` are not in its list).
- fix(claude): the headless finish check names stale test output and the time left, and the last deadline reminder names stale test output (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1, finish-text lane). Why: of 33 failed nano rows in runs 1fbd4a11 and 5f48d05d, 7 (3 that ended, 4 capped by the time limit) failed only because a /tmp/frame.bmp from the agent's own test runs was still there: the make-mips-interpreter and make-doom-for-mips checkers wait for that file, sleep 1 s and stop the VM, and never delete an old one, while Claude Code's passing rows end with `rm -f /tmp/frame.bmp`. video-processing ended after 141 to 340 s of 3600 s and was wrong in 6 of 6, while Claude Code's passes ran 319 s or more and tested variants. `finish_check::NOTICE` becomes `finish_check::notice(Option<&Reminders>)`: it adds one point, "Files your own test runs wrote where the task's program or its checks write output or wait for it, such as a file in /tmp, are deleted, and processes you started are stopped.", and with a deadline it says after "nobody will reply." how much time remains, as `Reminders::remain` ("54 min 59 s of this task's 60 min remain."), the same `spoken` text the reminders use (`Deadline::remain`, shared with `Reminders::notice`). A capped row never reaches the finish check (it does not fire once `Reminders::last_passed`), so the reminder at the last of `REMINDER_PERCENTS` adds `LAST_REMINDER`: "Before the time is up, delete files your own test runs wrote where the task's program or its checks write output or wait for it, such as a file in /tmp, and stop processes you started." Earlier reminders and the text without a deadline are otherwise unchanged, and no task is named. Checked with output/finish-text-agent (the finish-check-agent harness: a `Claude::builder` against a local Messages SSE mock that answers a prompt with one `Bash` call and anything else with `end_turn` text, run.sh, gak-9, 2026-11-15), model calls and finish notices in the final request: interactive 2 and 0; headless 3 and 1 with the new point and no time; deadline 3,300 s of 3,600 s left 3 and 1 with "54 min 59 s of this task's 60 min remain."; 50% elapsed 3 and 1 with "4 min 59 s of this task's 10 min remain." in both the reminder and the notice; 80% elapsed 3 and 1, reminder without the last point; 95% elapsed 2 and 0, reminder "29 s of this task's 10 min remain." with the last point. Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (the existing `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT` dead-code warning on wasm), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`.
- fix(claude): the deadline reminders before the last one tell the agent to keep working until the time is up, and only the last one tells it to finish (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1, deadline-wording lane). Why: in run 3d8f01a9 (wave 7 build) every row that passed 50% of its limit reacted to the reminders, but they made the agent stop early. All three nano make-doom-for-mips rows ended on their own at 629 to 652 s of 900 s (70 to 72%) and failed, one of them after it skipped a check to wrap up, and a direct-tools row ended at 578 s of 900 s with "I'm out of time, so I'll report honestly what I found rather than claim a fix", with 322 s unused. Every reminder said "Make sure every output the task asks for exists in its final location now, before you spend time improving it. Do not start a command or a wait that cannot finish in the time that remains." The reminders at 50% and 75% (`EARLY_REMINDER`) now say, after the time left and "only what is on disk then counts.": "Keep working until then. First put every output the task asks for in its final location, then use the time that remains to improve and test it." The reminder at the last of `REMINDER_PERCENTS` (`LAST_REMINDER`) says: "Finish now. Make sure every output the task asks for is in its final location, delete files your own test runs wrote where the task's program or its checks write output or wait for it, such as a file in /tmp, and stop processes you started. Do not start a command or a wait that cannot finish in the time that remains." The headless finish check and the text without a deadline do not change, and no task is named. Checked with output/deadline-wording-agent (a copy of output/finish-text-agent with a 75% label: a `Claude::builder` against a local Messages SSE mock, run.sh, gak-9, 2026-11-15): 50% elapsed "Time limit: 4 min 59 s of this task's 10 min remain." with the keep-working text, 75.8% ("2 min 24 s") and 80% ("1 min 59 s") with the keep-working text, 95% ("29 s") with the finish text, and model calls and finish notices as in the finish-text lane (interactive 2 and 0, headless 3 and 1, 95% 2 and 0). Commands: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (the existing `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT` dead-code warning on wasm), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`.
- fix(executor, sim): `dns::Wire` is a public trait again, with `receive`, `send` and `stream` returning futures, and `dns::lookup` takes `&mut impl Wire` again (2026-11-15). f1cc5300c made the wire a private struct on the reactor and `lookup` build its own, which stopped nanocode-sim building: its dns scenario drives the resolver through `FakeWire`. The reactor wire is now the private `Sockets`, which `resolve` passes to `lookup`; its sockets, its one nanocode-lookup thread and `M_ARENA_MAX` are unchanged, and only the call path is generic. `FakeWire`'s calls are `async` and never wait, so the sim polls `lookup` once with a no-op waker and fails the seed if it is not ready. Checked: workspace `cargo check --locked --all-targets`, the wasm32 check of nanocode-executor, `nanocode-sim --tidy` clean, `sweep.sh 0 2000 4` passed=2000 failed=0, `--scenario dns --seeds 0..2000 --twice` passed=2000, and both dns mutations still caught (cut_answer by 1094 seeds, drop_search by 636).
- feat(claude): after the first deadline reminder every tool round states the time left, and every note nanocode adds to the conversation is published as a `context.notice` event (2026-11-15, Terminal-Bench 2.1, deadline-audit lane). Why: in run 3d8f01a9 the reminders fired once each at 50%, 75% and 90%, so between them the agent guessed the time: extract-moves a00049 judged 6 to 8 min left at 1,236 to 1,250 s of 1,800 s when about 9 to 10 min remained, and ended at 1,276 s. "Time limit:" appeared in 0 of the 98 attempts' artifacts, because the system message after tool results was written to no event, so the notes could not be audited. `Reminders::notice` now returns, once the first of `REMINDER_PERCENTS` has passed, "Time limit: <Deadline::remain>" (such as "Time limit: 4 min 49 s of this task's 10 min remain.") on every tool round where no reminder is due; the three full reminders keep the wording of 30e4b80b2. The line goes in the same `Role::System` message after the tool results as the reminders, not into a tool result, so tool text stays as the tool returned it. New `AgentEventKind::ContextNotice` (`context.notice`, `ContextEvent::Notice(ContextNotice)`), payload `after_model_call_index`, `role` and `text`: Claude publishes it with the exact text of the `Role::System` message it appends after a tool round (the deadline line or reminder, and with upstream context also the round notices, working-directory update and `<total_tokens>`) and of the headless finish check (`role` `user`). Before this, neither the finish check nor the deadline reminders were in any event; the capped-call notice and the expired-call text are in the tool result already. Hosts that log every event (nanoeval's `agent/events.jsonl`) now hold the notes; nanoeval's ATIF trajectory still ignores the kind. Checked with output/deadline-audit-agent (a copy of output/deadline-wording-agent: a headless `Claude::builder` with one `Bash` tool against a local Messages SSE mock that answers N requests with a `Bash` call and then `end_turn` text, the event stream written as JSON lines, run.sh, gak-9, 2026-11-15): 5% elapsed, 4 rounds: no time note, 1 `context.notice` (the finish check, "54 min 59 s of this task's 60 min remain."); 51.7% elapsed, 4 rounds: the 50% reminder after round 1, "Time limit: 4 min 49 s of this task's 10 min remain." after rounds 2 to 4, then the finish check, 5 events; 95% elapsed, 4 rounds: the last reminder then 3 short lines, no finish check, 4 events; 52.5% of 20 s elapsed with 1.5 s per response, 7 rounds: 50% reminder (7 s), line (6 s), 75% reminder (4 s), line (3 s), 90% reminder (1 s), lines (0 s, 0 s), 7 events. In every case each note in the final request equals the `text` of one `context.notice` event. Commands: `cargo check --locked --workspace` (the existing `nanocode-sim` `Dns` dead-code warning), `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-types-core -p nanocode-backend-claude --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (the existing `GIT_STATUS_LIMIT` dead-code warning), `cargo clippy --locked --no-deps --all-targets -p nanocode-types-core -p nanocode-backend-claude -- -D warnings`.
- perf(djs): `run_tier1` specializes an add by the types it sees and runs a one-op loop body in place (loop 148.72M -> 96.30M instructions natively, -35.2%, under the 106M target) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs tier-1 wave 4). What: `Op::k` is a `Cell<K>` that an op rewrites as it runs. `K::Add` that adds an int32 to a Number in f64 form becomes `K::AddF`, which tests only "the left operand is an f64 and the right an int32" (one mask compare and one tag compare) and adds them, with the result range test of `number` kept so a result inside int32 still becomes the int form. A miss of that guard turns the op back into `K::Add` on the general path, so a register that changes type costs one generic add, never an exit. An `Add` or `AddF` whose latch suffix jumps back to itself (a one-op loop such as `s += i; i++ < n`) loops inside its own match arm (`spin!`), so the dispatch (13 instructions: index, four field loads, jump table) runs once per entry instead of once per iteration, and the operands, counter, bound and fuel stay in machine registers. The latch suffix charges the op's fuel and the latch's fuel as one precomputed sum, and a failed counter step charges only the op's own fuel, as before. The run loop is labeled `'run` so the macros leave it from the inner loop. Steps on loop (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3): `AddF` and the one fuel subtraction 114.10M (56/iteration: dispatch 13, add 20, latch 20), `spin!` 96.30M (~47/iteration). Base 690c37b3b against this change, hosted Hand, best of 3 interleaved: empty 857,536 -> 857,856, loop 148,723,294 -> 96,299,954, gen 1,985.643M -> 1,985.643M, gennext 4,306.594M -> 4,306.595M, err, find, some, forEach, filter, map and reduce within 0.001%. Checks: test262 subset (~/t262.list) 2,535 passing, identical to base; the fuel harness (fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited, slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000) prints identical results, yields and `fuel_used` on 17 scripts (the four edge scripts, loop, gen, gennext, err, find, some, forEach, filter, map, reduce, jsonfuel, a float-accumulator script of 10 functions: an int sum that overflows into a double, sums from 0.5, 1e308, -Infinity and NaN, a double step, a double sum that comes back into int32 and leaves it again, a string concat that declines, a counter that overflows at the latch, a sum over a mixed int and double array, an accumulator replaced by an object with `valueOf`, and -0; and a generator script), 408 lines each; `scripts/base.sh --check` passes; `cargo check --locked --lib -p djs-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes; `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32 reports nothing in tier1.rs.
- perf(djs): `run_tier1` runs a for-of loop over a plain generator and the generator's loop body as one register program (gen 1,985.6M -> 593.7M instructions natively, -70.1%, under the 691M target and 2.3x below QuickJS's 1,383M) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs tier-1 wave 4). What: `body` accepts one `iter_next_loc` whose jump is the loop's backedge. `gen_site` checks, once per translation, that its iterator local holds a plain generator suspended at a yield (`suspend::suspended_frame`: GENERATOR kind, SUSPENDED state, the original %GeneratorPrototype%.next), that its saved frame is above the arena's tracked end, and that the resume pc is the `jump_if_false8` and `drop` after that yield. Register sources are arena addresses now (`Frame::slot`), so one register file covers the caller's stack slots and the generator's saved frame array in place, without a frame switch. At `iter_next_loc` the translator emits `Resume` (charges `iter_next_loc`, the resumption's `jump_if_false8` and `drop` and `len / 8`, and saves the fuel), copies each generator register the trace writes into a shadow register (found by a first translation pass on a clone of the plan), then traces the generator from the resume pc: straight-line register ops, at most one backward jump, and conditional jumps as side exits, until the same `yield`, whose value register the caller's stack takes and whose fuel (`yield` plus `len / 8`) is charged on the trace's last op. Every exit inside the trace is a rollback: it restores the fuel saved by `Resume` and writes the shadow values to the generator's frame, so tier 0 runs `iter_next_loc` again from the state before it (the generator stays SUSPENDED and nothing else changed: a trace has no `put_elem`). Exits after the yield write the current generator registers to the saved frame, which is the suspended state `gen_yield_hot` leaves (state, pc, `hp - bp` and the frame header do not change between iterations). The caller's loop head is the `iter_next_loc` target with the yielded value on the stack, so a loop head may now hold `depth` stack values (`Frame::depth`, from `sp - lp - locals`). A translation is refused when the caller's loop writes the iterator or `next` locals. Tier-up: the generator's own backedge was the only counted backward jump, so the budget always ended inside the generator, where `body` declines on `yield`. Now a hot `yield` that returns to a bytecode caller counts against the budget too (`run_hot`, after `switch_frame!`), and a decline on `yield` sets `hot_backedges` to 1 for the next `run_hot` (restored at the next `run_tier1`, `Exec::tier1_nudge`), so the next counted event is the yield back into the caller's loop head. Refuted on the way: setting the budget through a new `run_hot` prologue branch instead of `opts.hot_backedges` cost 0.1 to 0.3% on every tier-0 bench (find +81k, err +2.0M: `run_hot` register allocation), and making `gen_yield_hot` decline under the nudge so the general yield path ends `run_hot` regressed gen by 28% (the general path does not count against the budget, so the program re-entered the generator frame every time). Base 34d94bbdc against this change, hosted Hand, best of 3 interleaved: gen 1,985,644,404 -> 593,694,914, gennext 4,306.68M -> 4,318.63M (+0.28%: it counts one more budget event per iteration and is not fused, as `.next()` allocates an iterator result per step), loop 96.30M -> 96.50M (+0.2%, the 16,384-iteration tier-0 warm-up), empty, err, find, some, forEach, filter, map and reduce within 0.02%. Checks: test262 subset 2,535 passing, identical; the fuel harness prints identical results, yields and `fuel_used` on the 17 scripts of the entry above (a generator edge script among them: for-of over generators with int, float and mixed yields, a generator that throws mid-loop, `break` then `next()`, exhaustion then `next()`, nested loops creating new generators, `next()` loops, and an accumulator that changes type mid-loop); `scripts/base.sh --check`; `cargo check --locked --lib -p djs-core --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; clippy reports nothing in the changed files.
- perf(alloc): `segment::acquire` skips the reset of the 64 page records for a segment it maps fresh, and resets them only for a segment taken from `SEGMENT_CACHE` (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: anonymous memory at the tool-turn peak). Why: `Segment` is 56 bytes of header and 64 `Page` records of 88 bytes (5,688 bytes), so the reset loop wrote the second 4 KB page of every segment header, although a fresh anonymous mapping is already zero and the records past byte 4,096 (slices 46 to 63) are written only when a page is made there. Expected cut: one 4 KB page per segment, 8 segments at the peak. Method: release build of origin/master 0a36b56c5 with and without the change, bench/cli `suite.mjs --parts=tools --steps=10 --only=nc --toolrounds=1` (direct tool turn, h=ncdirect) under tools/netguard.sh, a sampler that polls /proc/pid/smaps_rollup every 0.3 ms and at each new `Anonymous` maximum reads /proc/pid/smaps, the segment headers through /proc/pid/mem, every live page's free list and /proc/pid/pagemap, and each thread's stack pointer from /proc/pid/task/tid/syscall. `Anonymous` at the peak, 5 interleaved passes: 1,632/1,612/1,640/1,600/1,528 KB before (median 1,612) and 1,584/1,596/1,572/1,448/1,604 KB after (median 1,584). Breakdown of the 1.53-1.64 MB peak before the change (8 threads alive: main, worker, durability, lookup, blocking, mpp-forward-proxy, psh-engine, psh-ready): allocator segments 1,040-1,170 KB in 8 segments, of which the worker's is 612-672 KB resident for 363-452 KB of live blocks, the main thread's 104 KB for 39 KB live, and the six other threads' 12-104 KB each for 0-20 KB live (each holds 8 KB of header and at least one 4 KB page per size class it used, 4 to 21 classes); free dirty slices 0-32 KB; no large blocks and no glibc thread arenas at the peak; thread stacks worker 136-140 KB, main 68 KB, psh-engine 40-44 KB, durability and lookup 20 KB, blocking, mpp-forward-proxy and psh-ready 12 KB each; private copies of file pages (relocated data of the PIE binary, libc and ld.so) 104 KB; glibc `[heap]` 16 KB; TLS and other small anonymous mappings about 40 KB. So freed memory kept by the allocator is not the gap: whole 4 KB pages covered only by free blocks inside live pages are 64-72 KB of the worker segment (20480-byte, 7168-byte, 3584-byte and 12288-byte classes), and free dirty slices are at most 32 KB, so a purge at turn boundaries or on each freed block (MADV_DONTNEED of whole free pages) recovers at most about 0.1 MB, and was not built. The rest is live heap (about 0.5 MB), one page per size class per thread, and stack depth. Measured and dropped: smaller thread stack sizes (residency is the touched depth, not the reserved size, and every stack but the worker's and main's is 12-44 KB touched); `M_ARENA_MAX` (no thread arena is resident). Harness: ~/sw/anonpeak (peak2.py, an2.py, run.sh), removed after this entry.
- perf(process): `Capture::read` and `Capture::rest` in foreground.rs read command output into an 8 KB heap buffer instead of an 8 KB stack array (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: anonymous memory at the tool-turn peak). Why: the two arrays sit in the state of the two `Capture::read` futures that `collect` joins, and the compiler copies that state through the stack frames of the functions that build and poll it. Frame sizes from objdump of the release build with line tables (the `sub $N,%r11` of each stack probe loop, or the sum of `sub $N,%rsp`): the poll of `run_bash_with_environment::{closure#0}` 167,936 bytes, and `run_bash`, `run_bash_with_environment` and `nanocode_platform::timeout::<run_bash_with_environment::{closure#0}::{closure#2}>` 65,536 bytes each; after the change none of these four reaches 4 KB. Every page of a probed frame is written when the function runs, so each bash tool call touched up to about 160 KB of the worker stack. Measured with the harness of the entry above (release build of 0a36b56c5, direct 10-step tool turn, 6 interleaved passes, this change together with the segment header change): `Anonymous` at the peak 1,612/1,616/1,600/1,576/1,624/1,528 KB before (median 1,606) and 1,580/1,528/1,604/1,528/1,504/1,568 KB after (median 1,548), so about 30 KB of the 58 KB is this change. The worker stack still has 136-140 KB resident at the peak, because the model request path has a chain of large poll frames of its own (`CodexHarness::build::{closure#3}` 36,864 bytes, `AgentDriver::run::{closure#0}` 29,352, `http::connect::stream::{closure#0}` 23,584, `RunnerPool::connect_detected::{closure#0}` 23,504, `Response::chunk::{closure#0}` 22,688, `X25519MLKEM768::start` 22,368, `http::connect::tcp::{closure#0}` 18,200). Other large frames in the binary: `psh_utils::WITHOUT_GIT::wrap` 197,120 bytes and `psh_engine::exec::run_external_with::{closure#0}` 52,264 on the psh-engine thread, `Inflate::new` 40,960. Next: boxing or shrinking those futures lowers the worker stack, and fewer resident threads lowers the per-thread segment floor of 24-104 KB each.
- perf(djs): `each_fused` keeps what it derives at a call site in `Heap::each_site` (the child template, its leaf, the builtin's mode, the pushed constant, the fuel of the fixed instructions), FOLD (forEach and reduce over `+` and `-`) sums 8 biased words per step, and MAP_TO (map over `+`, `-`, `*` a constant) tests 8 elements against one range of the biased word and writes 8 results (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, callback lane wave 3). What: (1) `each_site` keys the entry on the arena offset of the `fclosure` and the callee's offset. A collection empties it with the other offset caches (`after_collect`, `compact_for_image`), so an offset cannot name another cell. A hit still reads the callee's and the child's template flags, since `fastpath` and `native` add flags after a template is made. One entry: a second fused site in the same loop takes the derivation each time, as before. (2) FOLD: `v = w ^ (INT_HI << 32 | 2^31)` is `p + 2^31` for an int32 and has a nonzero high word otherwise, so the OR of 8 `v` finds a non-int and their wrapping sum minus `8 * 2^31` is the exact chunk sum. The step takes the chunk when the new accumulator fits int32. A prefix that leaves int32 inside the chunk is not observable: the general path then adds in f64, which is exact below 2^53, and `conv::number` returns the int32 form, so the result is the same Value. (3) MAP_TO with a constant `q` (and `q > 0` for `*`): the passing elements are `[MIN - q, MAX - q]` for `+`, `[MIN + q, MAX + q]` for `-` and `[MIN / q, MAX / q]` for `*` (clamped to int32), one range of the biased word. The result is the low 32 bits of the wrapping operation with the int tag. A `* q` of `p = 0` gives `+0`, which the general path also stores as int 0. (4) `test_range` gives UNTIL its `(key, lo, c)` with `c` computed once. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3, hosted Hand, djsrun on djs-embed, 08e583813 -> this; QuickJS 2021-03-27 in brackets): find 37.26M -> 32.74M (-12.1%, 748.4M: 22.9x), some 38.56M -> 34.04M (-11.7%, 1,048.4M: 30.8x), forEach 66.88M -> 35.16M (-47.4%, 1,114.6M: 31.7x), filter 75.03M -> 71.56M (-4.6%, 1,409.1M: 19.7x), map 101.47M -> 68.50M (-32.5%, 1,651.9M: 24.1x), reduce 67.54M -> 36.38M (-46.1%, 1,041.7M: 28.6x); loop 148.72M, gen 1,985.6M and err 653.2M unchanged. Under V8 (node 24, wasmrun, best of 5, wall time on a loaded Hand): find 2.15 -> 1.80 ms, forEach 2.19 -> 2.02 ms, map 5.89 -> 3.70 ms, loop 6.91 -> 6.90 ms, gen 87.2 -> 82.8 ms, err 31.8 -> 32.1 ms. Where find's 32.7M goes (callgrind, per call of 100 elements): the folded UNTIL scan about 600 (about 4.4 per element, 35 SSE2 instructions per 8, plus about 130 of setup), `each_fused` about 290 (it was about 600 with `leaf_of`, `template::child` and the checks), the outer loop in run_hot about 490, `get_method`'s prototype hit about 70 (`data_at`, `get_prototype_of`, `object_class`) and the decline through `decline_fast` into `decline_plain`. Refuted: (a) a run_hot arm for `fclosure` that calls `each_fused` (find 32.98M, but gen +0.7% and err +1.0% from the larger loop), and the same check at the top of `decline_fast` (err +0.7%); the call stays in `decline_plain`. (b) A branch-free KEEP for filter against a constant (the same range test, every element stored and the count advanced by the test, also with the store index masked to the chunk) took filter from 71.3M to 80.6M; filter keeps the per-chunk mask and the branchy copy. Not done: map's and filter's result arrays still pay the arena's zeroing (`zero_ahead`, memset) and the minor collections of 20,000 short-lived arrays (about 1,400 per call together on map), which the scan cannot remove without allocating uncleared memory against the zeroed-allocation rule. The 50x targets (find 15M, filter 28.2M, map 33.0M) need the outer loop, `get_method` and the allocator to shrink, outside each.rs. Checked: test262 subset (3,090 files) 2,535 passing with identical pass sets; the fuel harness (fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited at slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000; the core, each, generator and regexp edge scripts, loop.js, gen.js, err.js, the six callback benches and a new FOLD/MAP_TO/KEEP edge script over ints near both int32 ends, -0, doubles, strings, holes and lengths 0 to 1,000) gives the same result, yield count and `fuel_used` as 08e583813 (336 runs, no differences); the edge script prints the same as 08e583813 and as node 24. `cargo clippy --locked --lib --no-deps -p djs-core -- -D warnings`, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, reports nothing in the changed code (clippy 1.100 reports 8 findings in bytecode/, compiler/parser.rs, heap/arena.rs and regexp/exec.rs that this change does not touch). Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/interp/run/each.rs, heap/mod.rs, heap/gc.rs, heap/compact.rs, djs-prelude/base.
- `Reactor::exit_driver` starts the `nanocode-reactor` fallback thread only when the driver still holds a source or a timer (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track, one-shot kernel lane, wave 5). When the last driver left `block_on`, `exit_driver` always spawned the fallback thread, so every `nanocode exec` cloned a thread with a 2 MB stack just before `exit_group`. `exit_driver` now takes the idle driver, drains the command queue and spawns the thread only if a source or timer is registered. `register` and `arm` check the driver count after they push their command (`Reactor::driven`), so a registration that races with the last driver's exit either finds no driver and starts the fallback itself or is drained by the exiting driver. `reactor::reactor()` is gone and `arm` returns `io::Result<Armed>`. Bench one-shot (static dist on 08a782ec0, `~/sw/k3/ab.sh`-style perf stat wrapper, 8 interleaved passes of 12): kernel instructions 2.98M to 2.87M (medians per pass 2.98-3.01M against 2.86-2.88M), page faults 368 to 362, user instructions 3.44M to 3.43M, and strace shows no `clone3` or `MAP_STACK` mapping before `exit_group`. The bench harness host now reads 2.98M for the same 08a782ec0 build that read 2.18M in wave 4, so absolute numbers moved with the host and only the interleaved difference is the result. The TUI first-frame part (4 passes of 4) reads 3.82M kernel and 4.45M user on both builds, within its noise, because the interactive runtime keeps its worker thread.
- `blocking::Pool::add_thread` uses `AtomicUsize::try_update` instead of `fetch_update` (2026-11-15), because `cargo clippy -D warnings` on rustc 1.100 rejects the deprecated name. Behavior is identical.
- Measured and not shipped for the one-shot (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track, one-shot kernel lane, wave 5, static dist on 08a782ec0 plus the fallback change, 8 interleaved passes of 12). (1) A UTC `/etc/localtime` link (`Etc/UTC` or `UTC`) giving `Zone::utc()` without opening the file, and (2) the first `dns::System::load` taking its stamps from the opened `/etc/hosts` and `/etc/resolv.conf` instead of two path `statx` calls. Together they remove one open, read and fstat of `/etc/localtime` and two path lookups, but they add a second `readlink` and an EOF read per file, and the stacked build measured 2.86-2.88M to 2.92-2.95M kernel instructions and 362 to 365 page faults, so neither shipped. (3) The +0.11M user instructions of 34a3ba226 are not in the DNS path: 12 sampled runs of the unstripped BOLT output attribute about 5% of samples to `dns::from_hosts` and `dns::encode`, but those run on an 8-line hosts file four times per one-shot, and BOLT's split fragments put samples on neighbouring symbols, so the difference is attributed to the per-build BOLT layout. (4) The `/.git` probe on the filesystem root stays, because `ProjectHome::discover` must find a repository at any ancestor. Findings handed to other lanes: the one-shot with `--gateway vercel` and a local base URL still resolves gateway.tempo-dev.workers.dev (twice), api.inference.boundless.network and mercator.sh on the main thread from `tempo::apply` (8 path `statx`, 8 UDP sockets), and `release_file_pages` at model call 1 drops 45.7 MB of read-only PT_LOAD mappings, so every text page after the request refaults. Next: those two items, then the per-fault cost (about 360 faults is most of the 2.9M kernel instructions).
- chore(djs): `cargo clippy -D warnings` on rustc 1.100 is clean again for the djs workspace (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, callback lane wave 5). What: `write_handlers` and `alloc_template_in` write through `as_chunks_mut` instead of `chunks_exact_mut` and `copy_from_slice`, `park::hash_words` reads through `as_chunks` instead of `chunks_exact`, `HandlerTable`, `Arena`, `regexp::Input` and `regexp::Caps` add the `is_empty` that `len_without_is_empty` asks for, and `ClassSpanKind` keeps its public variant names under an `#[expect(clippy::enum_variant_names)]`. Checked: `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` in crates/patches/djs, natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (without djs-base), reports nothing; `scripts/base.sh --check` passes. Files: djs-core bytecode/handlers.rs, bytecode/template.rs, compiler/parser.rs, heap/arena.rs, regexp/exec.rs, djs-embed/src/park.rs, djs-prelude/base/base.rs.
- perf(djs): `until_run` scans 16 elements per step, and a `===` search that stops at a match compares the low and high 32-bit halves of each word separately (find -11.4%, some -10.9%) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, callback lane wave 5, from the wave 4 handoff patch). What: for `STRICT_EQ` with `stop`, a chunk of 16 words passes when no low half equals `q as u32` and every high half equals the int tag `INT_HI`. Both tests are one 32-bit compare per lane, which SSE2 does with `pcmpeqd`, and the first word that fails either test ends the chunk loop. The scalar `bad` test then finds the exact index, so a double, a string, a hole or the match itself stops the scan where the 8-word range test did. The other comparisons keep the range test of `test_range` with 16 words per step. Prototype (standalone crate, 100 int32 elements with the match last, 20,000 searches, `instructions:u` per search): 8-word range fold 460, 16-word range fold 427, 16-word split-half test 338, and a u64 OR/AND variant (`d = w ^ t`, OR of `d` for the tag and AND of `(d - 1) | d` for the match) 717, which is refuted because the 64-bit compare has no SSE2 form. Instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3 interleaved, hosted Hand, djsrun on djs-embed, 098cc51c6 -> this): find 32.74M -> 29.02M (-11.36%), some 34.04M -> 30.32M (-10.93%); forEach 35.16M, filter 71.54M, map 68.48M, reduce 36.38M, loop 96.50M, gen 593.7M, gennext 4,318.6M and err 580.0M within 0.02%. Refuted from the same handoff patch: a `Heap::species_at` cache of the entry indexes of `Array.prototype.constructor` and `Array[@@species]` for map and filter measured map 68.48M -> 71.45M (+4.3%) and filter 71.54M -> 74.51M (+4.1%), because `plain_species` already returns at the frozen-builtins test (D2304) before any property lookup, so the cache only adds its own checks. `plain_species` stays as it is. Checked: test262 subset 2,535 passing with an identical pass set; the fuel harness (fuel 1,000, 33,333, 100,000 and unlimited at slices 1, 2, 3, 7, 100 and 5,000 over the core, each, generator and regexp edge scripts, the bench scripts and a new find/some/findIndex/every edge script over lengths 0 to 257, both int32 ends, -0, doubles, strings, holes and species overrides) gives the same output as 098cc51c6 in all 384 runs; clippy -D warnings natively and for wasm32 and `scripts/base.sh --check` pass. Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/interp/run/each.rs, djs-prelude/base.
- Measured and not shipped: MAP_TO as u64 lane arithmetic (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, callback lane wave 5). The wave 4 handoff estimated MAP_TO at about 11 instructions per element and proposed `((w & 0xFFFF_FFFF) * q & 0xFFFF_FFFF) | INT_HI << 32` so that LLVM uses `pmuludq` and `paddq`. Prototype (standalone crate, 100 int32 elements, 20,000 maps, `instructions:u` for the run): the 8-word fold with a u32 store 27.36M, the same with the u64 masked store 27.36M (LLVM narrows the masked product back to a 32-bit `imul`, since only the low half is used and x86-64 SSE2 has no `pmulld`), explicit `[u64; 8]` arrays for the range test 21.40M for `*`, and a biased store (`(w ^ BIAS) + q ^ BIAS`, exact because the range test keeps `p + q` in int32) 15.52M for `+`. A product of biased words (`(w ^ BIAS) * q + 2^31 - q * 2^31`) gets `pmuludq` only in a separate `#[inline(never)]` function and is no faster. In djs-core the result is the reverse: `scan_any` already compiles the existing loop with the range test in SSE2 and the store as load, `imul` or `add`, `or` and store from memory (about 67 instructions per 8 elements, not 11 per element), and both candidates measured worse than 0704cb701 (best of 3 interleaved): the array form map 68.48M -> 70.42M (+2.8%), and the biased store for `+` and `-` with the old `*` path map(x => x + 1) 68.16M -> 70.16M (+2.9%) and map(x => x - 3) 72.76M -> 74.52M (+2.4%), map(x => x * 2) unchanged, because the scalar biased store is one instruction more per element and LLVM keeps it scalar. The store stays as it is. What remains of map's 68.5M is outside the scan: about 8.3M is `scan_any`, and run_hot, `decline_plain`, `mark_old` and the result array allocation take the rest (sampled with `perf record -c 5000`).
- perf(process): `CapturedChunk::limit` streams a take through lossy UTF-8 decoding, the redaction forms and the new `OutputCut` in 8 KB pieces, so a take allocates O(limit) instead of three copies of the 1 MiB capture window (2026-11-15, Nanocode 1.0 CLI track: stream tool output). Why: `take_output` built `with_omission_marker` (window-sized Vec), `String::from_utf8_lossy(..).into_owned()` (second window-sized copy) and then cut 40 KB out of it, while the chunk still held the window. What: `OutputCut` (nanocode-process-contracts) keeps the first `limit / 2 + 1` bytes and the last `limit - limit / 2` bytes at char boundaries plus the length, char, newline and last-byte counts, and reproduces `redact_and_limit_in` and `limit_omitted_in` exactly; when nothing was trimmed it calls those functions on the whole text. `Redaction` holds the decoder carry (an incomplete UTF-8 sequence) and, per redaction form in `Redactor::forms` order, a pending buffer that holds back `form.len() - 1` bytes, which reproduces the sequential `str::replace` of `Redactor::text`. Exactness: a differential harness (output/stream-diff) compares `render` + the old limit functions against `limit` on 300,000 seeds (599,896 takes, 251,916 truncated) with invalid and truncated UTF-8, multibyte chars, up to 3 self-overlapping secrets in raw and named forms, windows of 1 to 1 MiB, limits 0 to usize::MAX and both units: identical output. Measured (fast profile + line tables, allocation tracer, bench/cli direct 10-step tool turn with NC_TOOL_CMD, 3 interleaved rounds, base origin/master 9452a7af3): `ls` live heap peak 442,7xx B both, max RSS 31.1/31.2/31.1 to 30.7/31.1/31.2 MB; `seq 1 150000` (1.0 MB per call, no omission) 4,659 KB to 3,090 KB live peak, max RSS 35.6-36.1 to 32.8-32.9 MB; `seq 1 1200000` (8.3 MB per call) 4,871-4,874 KB to 3,149-3,211 KB, max RSS 36.5-36.7 to 33.5-33.6 MB. Model-visible request bytes unchanged (last request 504,642 and 501,122 B before and after). Remaining gap to the large-output target (+0.5 MB over `ls`): the 1 MiB head and tail window that `CapturedOutput` keeps per take and the ten 40 KB results in history and request bodies.
- perf(djs): `run_tier1` fuses a `while(!(v=it.next()).done)` loop over a plain generator with the generator's loop body and keeps the iterator result in registers (gennext 4,318.6M -> 921.8M instructions natively, -78.7%, under the 1,000M target) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs tier-1 wave 5). What: `body` accepts one `get_method` + `call0` site on `next` after a local read, and `get_field` anywhere in a loop that has that site. `gen_site` resolves `it.next` through the `get_method` IC and requires %GeneratorPrototype%.next on a suspended plain generator. `translate` traces the generator as for for-of, requires a put or set of a local right after `call0`, and replaces the result object with a value register and a flag register: `v.done` reads as false and `v.value` reads the value register. The loop is compiled rotated (body first, test last), so the body reads `v.value` before the site; `run_tier1` then requires the entry object in `v` to have the cached iterator-result shape with `done` false (`Heap::iter_result_fields`) and seeds the value register from it. A spare iterator result is allocated before the run (decline if a collection is pending); an exit after a yield writes the value register into it and stores it into `v` and any stack slot that held the virtual object. The yield flag is a register written by a `Mov` rather than a dispatcher-local boolean: the first version with a `K::Yielded` op and a `boxed` local in the dispatch loop made gen +4.3% (593.7M -> 619.4M) from the loop's code generation; with the register flag gen is 591.9M (-0.3%). Other benches: loop, err, find, some, forEach and reduce within +0.07%, filter +0.41% and map +0.43% (the longer `body` scan of loops with `get_field`), empty +10K instructions. Checked: test262 subset 2,535 passing with identical pass sets; the fuel harness (408 runs over the core, each, generator and regexp edge scripts, the djs benches, jsonfuel and the tier-1 and generator edge scripts) identical to the base; `scripts/base.sh --check` clean; `cargo check --lib -p djs-core` natively and for wasm32. Files: crates/patches/djs/crates/djs-core/src/interp/run/tier1.rs, heap/object.rs.
- Measured, not adopted (2026-11-15): sharing one encoded `Arc<str>` record per Codex history item (`HistorySegment::records`, `ResponseHistory::records_from`) between the request prefix cache and the durable context. Direct 10-step tool turns of the dist build through the bench harness with the allocation tracer (`meas.sh LABEL BIN CMD`, `NC_TOOL_CMD` `ls` and `seq 1 1200000`), anonymous RSS at exit in KB, base against the change: `ls` 1192, 1252, 1256 against 1228, 1232; 8 MB output 3632, 3620, 3628 against 4828, 3460, 3608. The 8 MB turn stays about 2.4 MB above the `ls` turn either way, so the change does not close the gap to the 0.5 MB target. The 8 MB peak of live heap was 3.15 MB on the base trace. The remaining excess is in the capture and the request body of the large output, not in history encoding.
- perf(djs): `run_tier1` lowers a counted loop whose only body op adds the counter into an accumulator (`s += i` under a fused latch) to one `K::Accumulate` op that runs the loop out of line in `accumulate` with the accumulator and counter in locals, and `body` stops its scan at a `get_field` whose key is not `value` or `done` (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs tier-1 wave 7). What: the latch fusion marks op 0 as `K::Accumulate` when it is an `Add` with `d == a`, `c` equal to the latch register and `a != c`; at run time it checks that the counter is an int and the accumulator an int or a double, then repeats add, counter step, fuel charge, range test and pass test in registers exactly as the fused `Add` + latch did, and writes both registers back on every exit (overflow side exit, range exit, fuel pass). Any other operand type sets the op back to `K::Add`. `body` returned `Err(get_field)` only after a full scan when no `next()` site was found; only `value` and `done` reads can belong to the iterator-result fusion, so other keys end the scan at once. Why: callgrind showed 44 instructions per iteration in the AddF spin with r[] loads and stores and Op fields reloaded each time. A guard on the `Add` arm instead of a lowered op cost gen +10.4% and gennext +6.4% from code layout of the dispatch loop, and an out-of-line guard still cost +4.5% and +2.4%. Measured with `perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3 interleaved, 759f81902 against the change, hosted Hand x86_64: loop 96,509,068 -> 52,378,213 (-45.7%), gen 591,882,621 -> 584,596,143 (-1.2%), gennext 921,848,188 -> 911,247,431 (-1.2%), err +0.000%, find -0.07%, some -0.07%, forEach -0.001%, filter -0.03%, map -0.03%, reduce -0.11%, empty +0.005%. Not shipped: re-entering tier 1 at the first backedge of a loop head whose last tier-1 run finished the loop (an `again == Some(ip)` test at the run_hot backedges) cost gen +3.5%, gennext +2.4% and +0.2 to +0.3% on the array benches. Validation: test262 subset 2,535 pass, identical; fuel harness 408 runs, 0 diff; `scripts/base.sh --check` clean; `cargo check -p djs-core` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean; `cargo clippy -p djs-core` adds no warning.
- perf(djs): `run_tier1` folds a register `Mov` into the fall-through of the op before it (gen -6.6%, gennext -3.9%) (2026-11-15, nanocode 1.0 djs track, djs tier-1 wave 7). What: after lowering, a `Mov` at index s is fused into op s-1 when s is no jump target (no `to` of a `Branch`, `Jump`, `JumpIf`, `Latch` or `StepBranch` and no forward label), op s-1 carries no fused latch and is not a `Jump` or `Leave`; fused pairs do not chain (s advances by 2). The op stores `m`, `ma`, `md` and `mfuel` (its own fuel plus the Mov's); `next!` and the fall-through branch of `latch!` copy `r[ma]` to `r[md]`, charge `mfuel` and step `k` by 2. Taken branches and exits never run the Mov, as before, and fuel is charged at the same point with the same sum, since a `Mov` neither exits nor tests fuel. Why: callgrind on gen after the accumulate change showed about 6 dispatches per fused generator iteration, 3 of them `Mov` (the yielded value and the resume shadows), each with the full dispatch (`prog[k]` load, operand decode, jump table, fuel and `k` update). Measured with `perf stat -e instructions:u`, best of 3 interleaved, against 398439b90's tier-1 code, hosted Hand x86_64: gen 584,595,744 -> 545,871,599 (-6.6%), gennext 911,246,613 -> 875,570,231 (-3.9%), loop +0.006%, empty -0.02%, err, find, some, forEach, filter, map and reduce within 0.001%. Validation: test262 subset 2,535 pass, identical; fuel harness 408 runs, 0 diff; `scripts/base.sh --check` clean; `cargo check -p djs-core` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` clean; `cargo clippy -p djs-core` adds no warning.
- Measured (2026-11-15, bigout lane): live heap at the peak of the direct 10-step tool turn (bench harness, fast profile with line tables, allocation tracer, `NC_TOOL_CMD`), base d97214984: `ls` 620,668 B, `seq 1 1200000` (8.3 MB per call) 3,200,464 B, a gap of 2.58 MB. Top live sites at the 8 MB peak: `CapturedOutput::push` head and tail window 1,052,608 B in 2 blocks; the durable history encoding (`ContinuationCache::sync_history` through `paged.rs`) 428,120 B; the Codex request build over `ResponseHistoryIter` 426,632 B; `truncate_middle_with_token_budget` history items 362,034 B in 9 blocks; the embedded process reader buffers 262,144 B in 4 blocks. The window cannot shrink without a change of model-visible output: `limit_omitted_in` reports `…N tokens truncated…` from the redacted window length and the take limit is known only at take time. A summarized window stays exact if the caller passes the largest take limit at spawn (the Codex tools cap it at `output_token_budget`): raw bytes only within half that limit of each window end, pure ASCII interior chunks kept as length and newline counts, raw fallback for non-ASCII bytes and for any redaction form. The three history copies (about 1.2 MB) remain above the 0.5 MB target after that.
