- fix(python-capi): numpy's string scalars and C code that calls builtin type slots directly (2026-11-16, Georgios: numpy in python.wasm through the C API). A C type deriving from str (numpy's str_, with its own larger tp_basicsize) is now a str subclass in RustPython, and its C objects use CPython's non-compact unicode layout (the code points live in a separate buffer whose pointer follows the PyCompactUnicodeObject header), so the subclass's extra fields after the header are not overwritten by text; PyType_Ready sets the LONG/LIST/TUPLE/BYTES/UNICODE/DICT/BASE_EXC/TYPE subclass flags from the class's real ancestry, as CPython's inherit_special does, so PyUnicode_Check and friends hold for C subclasses with several bases; PyUnicode_Type and PyBytes_Type get tp_repr, tp_str and tp_dealloc and PyBaseObject_Type gets an identity tp_hash (numpy delegates to them as PyUnicode_Type.tp_repr(obj)); every C extension object converted back to RustPython, not only CObject instances, can be passed as self to a C slot; PyNumber_Float calls float(x), so it parses strings as CPython does (it used to accept only numbers). Checked natively with numpy's ext directories in place (still local): np.str_ construction, repr and methods, string array indexing, str(np.array([...])), np.char/np.strings ufuncs and np.array(['1', '2']).astype(float) now match CPython numpy 2.5.5, and the earlier smoke script still matches. `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-python-capi --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown.
- fix(python-capi): python.wasm links again: src/libc.rs (wasm32 only) defines `__errno_location` over a thread-local `c_int` (2026-11-16, pillow lane). numpy's C API surface (b60a62e59) reads errno in PyErr_SetFromErrno through `__errno_location`, which nothing defined on wasm32-unknown-unknown, so `cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` of nanocode-ts's python crate failed with `undefined symbol: __errno_location`. include/libc/errno.h already declared it. python.wasm after wasm-opt -Oz: 29,150,542 bytes. Check: `NANOCODE_CC=clang-22 cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-python-capi --no-deps --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings`. Files: crates/core/python-capi/src/libc.rs.
- feat(python-capi): C++ extensions. An extension directory may hold .cpp, .cc or .cxx files (found by the default glob or listed in its `sources` file) and an optional `flags` file of raw compiler flags, one per line, appended after its defines (2026-11-16, Georgios: numpy, matplotlib, contourpy and pillow must build into python.wasm through nanocode's C API, and their sorting, umath, Agg, tri, qhull, ft2font and contour cores are C++, most of it pybind11). On wasm32 a C++ file compiles as C++17 against the libc++ 22.1.8 headers vendored under include/c++/v1 (from llvmorg-22.1.8, the clang-22 the build uses; no `__cxx03`), with `-fwasm-exceptions` and RTTI, so pybind11's throw/catch and `dynamic_cast` work as upstream instead of a -fno-exceptions fork of every package. Our `__config_site` turns on localization with a C-locale-only runtime (iostream and sstream compile; setlocale, newlocale and the `*_l` functions accept only "C", "POSIX", "C.UTF-8" or "" and the `*_l` calls forward to the plain C functions), threads through libc++'s external thread API as a single-threaded implementation in include/c++/v1/__external_threading (mutexes lock and report EDEADLK on relock, call_once runs once, `std::thread` construction fails with EAGAIN, so a package that starts threads gets std::system_error rather than a hang), the monotonic clock, no wide characters, filesystem, random_device or time-zone database. The runtime the headers need is compiled into the archive only when some extension has a C++ file: the libc++ sources it uses (algorithm, chrono, exception, ios, iostream, locale, memory, mutex, new handlers, stdexcept, string, system_error, thread, typeinfo, vector, ryu and the rest listed in crates/core/python-capi/cxx/sources), libc++abi (exceptions, personality, typeinfo, demangler, guards, new/delete over malloc and free, which are the Rust allocator) and libunwind's Unwind-wasm.c, vendored under crates/core/python-capi/cxx with only the private headers they include (1.6 MB, found with `clang -MM`), plus cxx/runtime.c for the `__cpp_exception` tag, `__dso_handle`, `__cxa_atexit` (a no-op: python.wasm never runs static destructors) and the C-locale functions. C files on wasm32 now compile with `-fwasm-exceptions -mllvm -wasm-enable-sjlj`, so a C library that calls setjmp (qhull, libpng, FreeType) lowers it to wasm exception handling; functions without setjmp compile to the same code. The arity table wrapper of a C++ source is emitted as assembly naming the symbols, because a C++ wrapper that includes the source cannot name static functions of anonymous namespaces' mangled names, and it is skipped when a source takes no function's address. pybind11 3.1.0's headers are vendored once under include/pybind11 for every extension. abort (a Rust panic), aligned_alloc (alignment up to 16, the heap's alignment, else NULL), memchr, PyCapsule_SetDestructor (accepts and drops the destructor, as PyCapsule_New already does), PyDict_SetDefault, PyWeakref_NewRef, _PyType_Lookup and PyUnicode_DecodeUTF32 are new, with c/state.c holding the single thread state pybind11 reads (PyThreadState_Get/GetUnchecked/New, PyGILState_GetThisThreadState with gilstate_counter 1 and interp set, the TSS API over one heap slot per key, PyInterpreterState_GetDict/Main, frames reported as absent, Py_GetVersion, PyDict_GetItemStringRef, managed-dict visit and clear through tp_dictoffset, and PyInstanceMethod). The heap's alignment is 16 on every target, since wasm32's max_align_t is 16 and libc++abi allocates exceptions with that alignment. Exception handling encoding: clang-22's default legacy form (try/catch/delegate); a two-module probe (one function with legacy try/catch_all, one with exnref try_table) validates and runs in Node 24.22.3 and Bun, and validates in workerd 2026-11-16, so both encodings load in the runtimes nanocode-ts hosts; legacy also loads in browsers that shipped wasm exceptions before exnref. Measured: `import example` of pybind11's own example compiled in, linked into python.wasm with every runtime symbol resolved but the printf family the libc work provides, throws and catches C++ exceptions inside PyInit, then stops at the C API's lack of pybind11's handmade heap types (a `property` subclass and a `type` subclass built through PyType_Type.tp_alloc), which is the next change; so no extension uses C++ yet and python.wasm links as before. Checked with `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-python-capi --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown (NANOCODE_CC=clang-22), `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-python --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and a release python.wasm build importing yaml, markupsafe, msgpack and ujson.
- fix(python-capi): pybind11 modules import. pybind11 3 builds its classes by hand from `PyType_Type.tp_alloc` and calls `PyType_Type`'s and `PyProperty_Type`'s own slots from its metaclass and static-property type, so the C API now fills those builtin slots at startup (tp_basicsize as PyHeapTypeObject, tp_alloc, tp_getattro, tp_setattro, tp_call and a no-op tp_dealloc for `type`; tp_descr_get and tp_descr_set for `property`), each forwarding to the builtin's own method. A C type whose base is any builtin that accepts subclasses (`property`, `type`) is created on that base, its tp_descr_set, tp_getattro and tp_setattro become `__set__`/`__delete__`, `__getattribute__` and `__setattr__`/`__delattr__` (when they are not the generic ones), Py_TPFLAGS_MANAGED_DICT gives instances a `__dict__`, and PyType_Ready inherits tp_basicsize and tp_itemsize from the base when the type leaves them 0. Multi-phase init sets the module's `__spec__` before its exec slots, as importlib does, since pybind11 caches the module under `__spec__.name`. PyThreadState_Get returned the interpreter state; it now returns the one thread state in c/state.c, whose `interp` and `gilstate_counter` pybind11 reads, and the duplicate PyDict_GetItemStringRef and PyInterpreterState_Main that be6232f and b60a62e both defined (master stopped linking python.wasm) are defined once, in extra.rs. Measured 2026-11-16 with pybind11's own example (`m.def("add", &add, py::arg("i") = 1, py::arg("j") = 2)` and a function throwing `std::runtime_error`) compiled in as ext/example with a temporary printf shim until the libc printf family lands: `example.add(2, 3)` is 5, `example.add()` is 3, `example.__doc__` is "pybind11 example plugin", and the C++ exception arrives as RuntimeError("boom"); `example.add.__doc__` is still None. Checked with `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-python-capi --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown and a release python.wasm build (NANOCODE_CC=clang-22) importing yaml, markupsafe, msgpack and ujson.
- docs(python-capi): size cost of C++ in python.wasm. A release python.wasm (nanocode-ts python/, cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown, NANOCODE_CC=clang-22, before wasm-opt) at 314d30d is 21,844,586 bytes (8,258,567 gzip -9) with no C++ extension, so no libc++ runtime; with pybind11's example compiled in as ext/example plus a temporary printf shim it is 22,123,980 bytes (8,329,075 gzip -9), +279,394 bytes (+70,508 gzip) for the libc++/libc++abi/libunwind runtime the linker keeps (exceptions, typeinfo, demangler, strings, iostream-free paths) together with one pybind11 module. Measured 2026-11-16 on the hosted Hand; each later C++ extension's delta excludes this one-time runtime cost.
- feat(python-capi): a musl 1.2.5 subset (MIT, crates/core/python-capi/lib/libc with its COPYRIGHT) compiled into the extension archive on wasm32, so C and C++ extensions link against a real C library (2026-11-16, Georgios: numpy and matplotlib in python.wasm through the C API). It provides the printf and scanf families, strtod/strtof/strtold and the strto*/ato* integers (floatscan/intscan), qsort/qsort_r/bsearch/div/rand, the string.h extras (strcpy, strncpy, strcat, strcspn, strspn, strpbrk, strtok, strerror/strerror_r, memchr, memrchr, memmem, strnlen, stpcpy...), UTF-8 multibyte conversions, wcslen and wmemchr/wmemcmp/wmemcpy/wmemmove/wmemset (numpy's string ufuncs), time (gmtime/localtime as UTC, mktime, timegm, strftime), and project-owned nanocode/ files: FILE stdio whose stdin/stdout/stderr and fopen'd files go through Python's io (pyio.c), exit/atexit, getenv with no environment, nl_langinfo for the C locale and the setjmp/longjmp runtime for -mllvm -wasm-enable-sjlj. Native builds keep the host libc. The math.h fast paths for copysign/fabs/floor/ceil/sqrt/trunc are function-like macros, so C that takes their address (numpy's generated ufunc tables store (void *)npy_fabs) gets the real function. The tree was written by the libc lane and ported onto current master with the C++ support; checked by linking python.wasm with numpy's ext directories (next entry) and `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-python-capi -p nanocode-python --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown with NANOCODE_CC=clang-22.
- feat(python-capi): numpy 2.5.5 compiled into python3 (2026-11-16, Georgios: numpy in python.wasm through the C API, no Pyodide). ext/ holds numpy._core._multiarray_umath (numpy's common/, multiarray/, umath/, npymath/, npysort/ and highway headers in their upstream layout plus the sources numpy's meson build generates: the .c.src/.h.src expansions, __umath_generated.c, __multiarray_api.h/__ufunc_api.h, funcs.inc and the dispatch headers; generated once with numpy's own meson configured with -Dcpu-baseline=none -Dcpu-dispatch=none -Dblas=none -Dlapack=none -Ddisable-optimization=true, so every ufunc loop is numpy's portable baseline C/C++ and highway's scalar target), numpy.linalg.lapack_lite and numpy.linalg._umath_linalg on numpy's bundled f2c LAPACK/BLAS (lapack_lite's f2c library lives only in numpy.linalg.lapack_lite, so no symbol is defined twice in the one binary), numpy.fft._pocketfft_umath (pocketfft, C++), and numpy.random's Cython modules (_common, bit_generator, _mt19937, _pcg64, _philox, _sfc64, _generator, mtrand, _bounded_integers, with the npyrandom distributions library in one of them). config.h and _numpyconfig.h are written for the target from compiler macros instead of meson's host probes (long double is IEEE quad on wasm32, 80-bit on x86_64). numpy's pure-Python package (176 files, without tests/, f2py/ and _pyinstaller/) is frozen from crates/core/python/site/numpy like yaml and msgpack, so `import numpy` needs no files on disk. The extensions' templates, meson files and Cython sources are not kept: the generated C is what compiles. Measured: a release python.wasm built from this tree through nanocode-ts' scripts/python.mjs (before wasm-opt) is 29,278,891 bytes against 21,847,695 bytes for a build of master without numpy (about +7.4 MB). Through nanocode-ts' Bash/python.wasm, linspace, sin, sum/mean/max/cumsum, broadcasting, astype, linalg.solve/det/inv/eig, random.default_rng(0).normal, fft.fft, array printing, sort/unique/where, str_/bytes_ scalars, string arrays and np.char/np.strings give output byte-identical to CPython 3.12 with numpy 2.5.5; the import and that script take 1.6 s. numpy's own test suite (124 modules of numpy/_core, linalg, fft, random, lib, ma and polynomial, run under a native nanocode-python build by a pytest-compatible runner kept in the ignored output/ directory, because pytest itself needs subprocess, which nanocode-python refuses): 25,900 tests collected, 22,705 passed, 1,559 failed, 31 errors, 839 skipped, 181 crashed (object and structured dtypes, subclassed scalars), and 20 modules fail at import (mmap, asyncio and the C test helpers, which are not shipped). The largest failure groups are warnings raised from C not reaching the warnings module, bytes_/str_ subclasses where an exact bytes/str is expected, missing PyArg format codes for pickling, and __text_signature__. Checked with `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-python-capi -p nanocode-python --no-deps -- -D warnings` natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown (NANOCODE_CC=clang-22).
- feat(python-capi): nan, nanf and nanl in the wasm32 libc (musl 1.2.5's src/math/nan*.c), and the libc is checked against glibc (2026-11-16, libc lane). matplotlib's and contourpy's C++ link needs `nan`, the one symbol of the matplotlib lane's list (clock_gettime, exit, the FILE functions and stdin/stdout/stderr, getenv, localtime, nanosleep, printf/snprintf/sprintf/vsnprintf/vfprintf/vasprintf, qsort, sscanf, strcat/strcpy/strncat/strncpy/strpbrk, strerror_r, strftime, strtod/strtof/strtold/strtol/strtoll/strtoul/strtoull, time, ungetc, __wasm_setjmp/__wasm_setjmp_test/__wasm_longjmp/__c_longjmp) that the archive did not define; the C++ runtime's list (vsnprintf, snprintf, vfprintf, fprintf, strerror_r) was already covered, so its local shim can go. Checked with a local, uncommitted extension that formats 3,810 printf cases (every conversion, flag, width and precision over integers at their limits, doubles from subnormals to infinities and NaN, strings and chars) and runs strtod over 8,985 random doubles, the strtod/strtof/strtol edge cases, sscanf, qsort/bsearch, fopen/fgets/fseek/ftell/ungetc over Python's io, strerror_r, asprintf, the multibyte conversions, time/gmtime/localtime/mktime/timegm/strftime at six instants, and setjmp/longjmp through five frames, against the same C compiled natively with gcc and glibc 2.39: in python.wasm 3,767 printf cases are byte-identical and strtod round-trips all 8,985; the 43 that differ are the test's own (long is 32 bits on wasm32, so `%ld` of a 64-bit value; long double is IEEE quad on wasm32 against x87 on x86_64, so `%La`; one case that passes no format) except `%a` of subnormals, where musl prints 0x1p-1074 and glibc 0x0.0000000000001p-1022, both valid C. strftime matches glibc's gmtime output at every instant except `%Z`, UTC against glibc's GMT; the setjmp test returns 45301, as natively. Build note: lib/libc/nanocode/setjmp.c defines the __c_longjmp tag in top-level assembly beside __builtin_wasm_throw, which clang 22 (the NANOCODE_CC the build uses) needs, while Ubuntu's clang 18 crashes on it ("symbol __c_longjmp is already defined") and without it ("undefined tag symbol cannot be weak"), so the wasm32 C build needs clang 22. Size: 0 bytes in python.wasm today (nothing referenced nan yet, so the archive member is not linked; 13, 9 and 27 bytes of code when it is); python.wasm with numpy and this change 27,179,279 bytes after wasm-opt (31,309,607 raw), and yaml (CSafeLoader), markupsafe, msgpack, ujson and numpy import and round-trip in it. Commands: nanocode-ts `NANOCODE_CC=clang-22 NANOCODE_PYTHON_SOURCE=<this tree> node output/build-python.mjs`, `cargo check -p nanocode-python-capi` natively and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. Files: crates/core/python-capi/lib/libc/{sources,src/math/nan.c,src/math/nanf.c,src/math/nanl.c}.
- fix(python-capi): numpy no longer prints add_newdoc UserWarnings on import (2026-11-16, Georgios: numpy in python.wasm). A C type created from a static PyTypeObject (no Py_TPFLAGS_HEAPTYPE in its tp_flags) reports __flags__ without HEAPTYPE, through a static_extension flag on the patched RustPython's PyTypeSlots; RustPython still treats it as a heap class internally, which its layout and attribute code need. C getsets and members are now getset_descriptor objects whose __objclass__ is the C type, as in CPython, rather than property objects. numpy's add_newdoc treats types with HEAPTYPE and property objects as pure Python and warned 141 times on the first import. Measured with a native nanocode-python: the first import prints no warnings, and the smoke script (linspace, sin, reductions, broadcasting, casts, linalg, random, fft, printing) still matches CPython numpy 2.5.5 byte for byte. Known gap: docstrings numpy attaches to C getsets with add_docstring are not visible (ndarray.shape.__doc__ is None). np.linalg.eigvals returning complex for a real symmetric matrix is not a bug: CPython numpy 2.5 does the same. `cargo clippy --locked -p nanocode-python-capi -p nanocode-python --no-deps -- -D warnings` passes natively and for wasm32-unknown-unknown.
- fix(python): an import a host restart interrupted resumes in place, and stdlib names never come from the filesystem (2026-11-17, Georgios: numpy on async filesystems). A host without a synchronous filesystem (nanocode-ts `RustPython.layered` over a Durable Object or Vercel `SqlFileSystem`) stops a run at the first path it lacks, fetches it and reruns in the same interpreter. `_start` then dropped every module still `_initializing`, so a rerun made a new `numpy` while finished submodules (`numpy._core.arrayprint`, single-init C extensions such as `_multiarray_umath`) still held the abandoned one: printing an array raised `AttributeError: partially initialized module 'numpy' has no attribute 'isfinite'`, linalg recursed and dropping finished modules too broke `numpy.dtypes`, which only `_multiarray_umath`'s one init fills. Now `_start` keeps each interrupted module object, and a `_Resumer` first on `sys.meta_path` re-executes it in that same object when it is imported again, so every reference stays valid; modules loaded from the filesystem are still dropped and re-found as before. `np.random.default_rng` raised a bare `NameError` because `numpy.random.bit_generator` (a built-in Cython module) imports `secrets` -> `hmac` -> `_hmac`, which RustPython lacks, so `_Finder` probed cwd and site-packages for it in the middle of a C module's init, and no rerun can recover that. `_Finder` now returns nothing for a top-level stdlib name: frozen and built-in finders already come first, so a stdlib name was never satisfied from the filesystem when present. The name set is `sys.stdlib_module_names` plus what CPython 3.14 lists and RustPython's lacks (`_ast_unparse _hmac _py_warnings _remote_debugging _types _zstd annotationlib compression`, from diffing `uvx --python 3.14` against python.wasm). It is built at runtime because the boot snapshot cannot hold a frozenset constant (`PyObjBag::make_constant` panics). Measured 2026-11-17 in Node 24 with nanocode-ts `bench/python/asyncfs.ts` (a MemoryFileSystem behind a Proxy without `sync`, a fresh interpreter per cold probe, python.wasm baked by scripts/python.mjs without wasm-opt) and that host's cache unchanged (build-67bdee0's `layered`): build-67bdee0's python.wasm fails 3 of 7 (array AttributeError, default_rng NameError, linalg RecursionError); this commit passes 7 of 7 (numpy array, default_rng, linalg solve and det, matplotlib and scipy through Pyodide, a missing module), with `default_rng` dropping from 32 to 13 host stats and running 146 ms cold. Sync MemoryFileSystem results are unchanged.
- fix(python-capi): matplotlib 3.11.2 renders with Agg in python.wasm, pixel-identical to native (2026-11-17, mpl2 lane; Georgios: numpy and matplotlib in python.wasm through the C API). Pushed as d8b877c, 6a74b10..d35a171 (zlib 1.3.1 with Pillow 13.0.0's _imaging, _imagingmath and _imagingmorph; contourpy 1.4.0; kiwisolver 1.5.1; matplotlib's _path with Agg, _image, _tri, _qhull, backends._backend_agg, ft2font with HarfBuzz) and 2530903. Bugs found on the way, each one capi-wide rather than matplotlib's: (1) nothing called `__wasm_call_ctors`, so wasm-ld used its command model and wrapped all 432 exports to rerun every C/C++ static constructor (and destructor) on each call, which reset C++ globals between calls (ft2font's enum table emptied after module init); `module_defs` now calls it once, which makes wasm-ld drop the wrappers; (2) `_Py_Dealloc` ran a type's tp_dealloc on a proxy, so the bridge queue freed it again (heap corruption in wasm on pybind11 static properties); (3) C heap types bridged to classes held no reference for their class, so freeing a tuple naming one ran pybind11's metaclass dealloc and unregistered it; (4) `Py_tss_t` stored a pointer in a 32-bit `pthread_key_t` (native segfault); (5) `PyCFunction_GET_*`, `PyMethod_GET_*` and `PyMemoryView_GET_BUFFER` read CPython structs (now `_PyMemoryView_GetBuffer` returns the exporter's own C view, and a memoryview of a C exporter keeps its shape and format); (6) bridged C types had no tp_mro, which pybind11's getbuffer walks; (7) builtin types lacked nb_bool/nb_int/nb_float/nb_index for C callers; (8) FreeType was built with FT_CONFIG_OPTION_DISABLE_STREAM_SUPPORT, which removes FT_OPEN_STREAM that matplotlib opens fonts through; (9) ft2font's enum placeholders now build their Python objects at module init instead of in static constructors. socket.py from CPython 3.14 joins the bundled Lib (matplotlib's backend_bases imports it; its selectors import is lazy). Measured: `plt.plot(sin)` + `savefig` of a 600x400 figure at 100 dpi in python.wasm through nanocode-ts `python3` gives a PNG whose decoded pixels match native matplotlib 3.11.2 exactly (0 of 240,000 differ); import of matplotlib.pyplot 3.3 s and plot+savefig 0.2 s more on the hosted Hand, first run including the font cache. Size: the release python.wasm with these extensions is 35,757,294 bytes (12,999,518 gzip -9) against 31,291,617 (11,737,795) for the numpy lane's build without them, +4.47 MB raw, +1.26 MB gzip. Checks: `cargo check --locked -p nanocode-python-capi` native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` (NANOCODE_CC=clang-22) at each commit; release python.wasm built from this tree imports numpy, yaml, kiwisolver, contourpy and PIL.Image. Not yet done: matplotlib and Pillow test subsets, nanocode-ts bench/python/score.ts entries; `_PyMemoryView_GetBuffer` keeps a built view (and its memoryview) for the run when the exporter is not a C type.
- fix(python-capi): numpy.float64 and numpy.complex128 work where float and complex do (2026-11-17, mpltest lane; Georgios: matplotlib's own tests in nanocode-python). A C object whose type subclasses float with float's layout (numpy.float64) now bridges to a Python object with a PyFloat payload, and a complex subclass with complex's layout (numpy.complex128) to one with a PyComplex payload, attached to the C object as a proxy is, instead of a CObject wrapper; float's own methods, math.ceil/floor/trunc, hashing and set membership read that payload, where before they raised TypeError "Expected type 'float' but 'float64' found" or "cannot use 'float64' as a set element". PyLong_Type, PyFloat_Type, PyComplex_Type and PyBool_Type also get their number slots (nb_add through nb_matrix_multiply, nb_negative/positive/absolute/invert, nb_power) forwarding to PyNumber_*, since numpy's float64.as_integer_ratio calls PyLong_Type.tp_as_number->nb_lshift directly (it segfaulted on a null slot). Natively, matplotlib 3.11.2's test_ticker goes from 501 passed, 47 failed, 1 error to 547 passed, 1 failed, 1 error (CPython 3.13: 549 passed, 2 skipped); test_path 103 passed, 1 failed, 5 skipped. numpy 2.5.5's scalar test modules (test_abc 4/5, test_numerictypes 136/138, test_scalarprint 32/34, test_longdouble 12/15 passed) give the same counts before and after; numpy, yaml, kiwisolver, PIL.Image, contourpy and matplotlib import; wasm32 and native cargo check pass.
- fix(python-capi): _PyMemoryView_GetBuffer frees the views it builds (2026-11-17, mpltest lane). For a memoryview whose exporter isn't a C type, the C view it builds was kept for the whole run, and since the table held the memoryview the bridge parked the memoryview's proxy forever too: 300 np.asarray(memoryview(...)) calls left 150 views. It now drops a built view once the memoryview's C object has no C references (the table's own reference keeps the C object from being freed, so its count stays readable), and the same loop holds at most 2. A loop comparing np.asarray(memoryview) with memoryview.tolist() over 2,000 bytearray views, 1-D and cast to 2-D, matches in every case. Corrections and checks for d8b877c ("pybind11 classes, static properties and enums work"): its message lists PyInstanceMethod_* among what it added, but the commit adds no PyInstanceMethod function; that line is wrong and stays in history. Pillow's PNG encoder, built against zlib only, writes byte-identical PNGs in python.wasm and native CPython: nanocode-ts bench/python/score.ts hashes a 64x64 RGB gradient PNG Pillow 13.0.0 saves, sha256 prefix 0e578415339aecf5 in both.
- fix(python-capi): a C type's tp_dealloc can call the C API when Rust drops the last reference (2026-11-17, mpltest lane). The bridge only set its machine inside a C call, so when Rust dropped a C object's last reference outside one, tp_dealloc ran without it and every C API call in it failed silently: numpy's array_dealloc clears a structured array with an object field through PyDict_GetItem(dtype.fields, name), got NULL and crashed in PyArg_ParseTuple. _Py_Dealloc now borrows the thread's current VM for tp_dealloc when no C call is active, without sweeping the release queue inside a drop (the next C call sweeps it). `np.zeros(3, [('x','f4'),('y','O')]); del a` segfaulted and now runs; matplotlib's test_colors under native nanocode-python went from crashing at test_colorizer_bivar_cmap (312 of 325 run) to 321 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped (CPython 324 passed, 1 skipped). wasm32 cargo check passes.
- fix(python-capi): a C type with mp_subscript but no sq_item isn't iterable (2026-11-17, mpltest lane). update_slot fills the sequence item slot from __getitem__ too, so iter() fell back to indexing on every numpy scalar and returned an empty iterator where CPython raises TypeError; matplotlib's Normalize.process_value took np.longdouble scalars for sequences and lost them. c_type now clears the sequence item slot when the C type has no sq_item. matplotlib test_colors native 321 -> 322 passed of 325 (CPython 324), test_ticker unchanged at 547; numpy scalar test modules keep their counts (test_abc 4/5, test_numerictypes 136/138, test_scalarprint 32/34, test_longdouble 12/15), and test_scalar_methods, which crashed at test_object_field before the tp_dealloc fix, now completes with 146 passed, 96 failed (mostly inspect.signature of builtin methods).
- fix(python-capi): build matplotlib's C++ exts with its Agg bug-fix defines (2026-11-17, mpltest lane). Upstream's meson.build adds -DMPL_FIX_AGG_IMAGE_FILTER_LUT_BUGS and -DMPL_FIX_AGG_INTERPOLATION_ENDPOINT_BUG to every C++ file; our ext/ builds left them out, so bilinear and other filtered resampling (imshow, LightSource shading) came out shifted by about 0.001 against CPython and failed image comparisons. Each matplotlib ext's defines file now lists both. A probe of imshow (nearest, bilinear, antialiased, hanning), pcolor, contour, contourf and _image.resample is now pixel-identical to CPython's matplotlib 3.11.2 wheel, and native test_colors went from 322 to 324 passed of 325 (CPython: 324 passed, 1 skipped).
- 2026-11-17: **Every built-in base prompt now leaves out "# Apps (Connectors)" and "# Plugins", and "# Using skills" unless the host's instructions carry a skill catalog ("### Available skills"); the 2026-11-13 GLM-family rule now covers Sol, Astra, Luna and Terra too.** nanocode serves no codex_apps MCP, loads no plugins and lists no skills to the model, so those sections describe tools a session never has (tool_search, codex_apps, skills.list). The cost dive on the Terminal-Bench traps equal-options runs (EQ1 gpt-6.1-sol traps-ni 1252c5cb, EQ2 gpt-6-astra traps 3231e157, nanox vs pi with thinking on, per scored attempt) found nanox's first request at 6,052 input tokens against pi's 1,350, and that prefix, resent on every call (8.0 calls per attempt against pi's 6.1), was 55% of the $0.0120 gap on Sol and 40% of the $0.0521 gap on Astra; the rest was the post-final loop. Visible output (1,719 vs 1,610 tokens), reasoning (301 vs 388), uncached new input and retries were not a gap, and nanox's cache hit rate was higher (87.7% vs 76.6%). o200k_base counts, prompt files at 76a97ad63: sol.md 4,212 to 3,315 tokens (21,779 to 17,329 bytes), astra.md 4,148 to 3,251, luna.md 3,520 to 2,658. A caller's own `system_prompt` is never edited, and the pinned prompt files are unchanged.
- fix(python-capi): Python classes get tp_mro and tp_bases on their C type objects (2026-11-17, mpltest lane). type_pointer made the C view of a Python class with both NULL, and C code reads them on any type it is handed: numpy's _descr_from_subtype takes tp_mro[1] of a Python subclass of a numpy scalar, so np.array(MyFloat(1.0), dtype=object) segfaulted. Both tuples are filled once the type is registered, since they name the class itself. numpy's test_ufunc under native nanocode-python went from a crash at test_unary_PyUFunc_O_O_method_full to 809 passed, 50 failed of 874.
- feat(python-capi): compile numpy's test extensions (2026-11-17, mpltest lane). numpy._core._multiarray_tests, _umath_tests, _rational_tests, _struct_ufunc_tests, _operand_flag_tests and _simd are in ext/, built like _multiarray_umath with the same includes and defines. numpy's own test suites import them (test_ufunc, test_multiarray, test_simd*), and score.ts counts numpy's 19 compiled modules, of which 13 were built. _simd.dispatch.c is numpy 2.5.5's generated baseline file with its NPY_SIMD branches removed: no target nanocode builds enables a numpy SIMD backend (NPY_DISABLE_OPTIMIZATION natively, no wasm backend), so those 520 KB were dead code. All six import natively and in python.wasm, and _rational_tests.rational and _umath_tests.inner1d give CPython's results.

- fix(codex): an empty reply to the finish check ends a headless turn with the final message the check followed, and a headless turn that ran no tool call gets no finish check (2026-11-16, nanocode 1.0 not-worse sprint). Why: on Terminal-Bench and the trap evals with GPT-6.1 Sol, the model often answered the finish-check reminder with an empty message; the empty-response nudge then fired and the model repeated its final, two extra model calls per attempt, read as 10 to 13% of the nanox arm's spend. `ModelRun` in crates/backends/codex/src/model/run/turn.rs now keeps the finish check as one enum, `FinishCheck` (`Due`, `Asked(final)`, `Settled`): the reply to the check settles it, an empty reply returns the kept final with no nudge and no further call, a reply with tool calls or text goes on as before, and a reply cut for continuation (`end_turn: false` with no calls) keeps it asked. A turn with no tool call has no result for the check to run, so it is not asked. Checked with a harness in output/empty-final: a mock Responses server that answers by script and the CLI with the codex deadline set from `HARNESS_DEADLINE_SECS` (a harness-only patch to bin/nanocode/src/host.rs, both builds), on master 76a97ad63 and on this change. Script exec, final, empty: master 4 requests (finish check, empty, `<empty_response>` nudge, repeated final), this change 3 and the first final. Script final, empty, with no tool call: master 3 requests, this change 1. A text reply to the check, a tool call after it, and no deadline: the same requests and final on both. `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex`, again with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `cargo clippy` on it pass.
- fix(python-capi): PySequence_Check asks for the sequence item slot, as CPython does (2026-11-17, mpltest lane). It returned true for anything whose class had __getitem__, so a numpy scalar counted as a sequence; Pillow's putdata checks each item with PySequence_Check and refused a flattened uint8 array ("sequence must be flattened", matplotlib test_jpeg_2d). It now checks the type's sequence item slot (dicts excluded, as before), which C types fill from sq_item and Python classes from __getitem__. numpy scalar test modules natively: test_numerictypes 136 -> 137 passed, test_scalarinherit 4 passed (crashed before the tp_mro fix), test_scalarmath 1478 passed of 1583, none fewer; Pillow putdata with lists, tuples, ranges and RGB tuples gives CPython's results.
- 2026-11-17: **A headless Codex session (`headless`, as nanoeval and every non-interactive host sets it) sends a shorter base prompt and tool list: the prompt leaves out "# When to ask the user for permission", "# Personality" with its writing-style subsections, "## Intermediate commentary", "## Final answer", every paragraph of "# Working with the user" but the two on compaction, and the two rules about PR descriptions and product user flows; the tools leave out `update_plan` and `exec_command`'s `justification`, `login`, `prefix_rule`, `sandbox_permissions` and `shell` parameters.** Why: equal-cost parity with pi at launch. After the 457b0d9 prompt cut and the end of the post-final loop, nanox on the traps equal-options runs was still projected at about 1.19x pi's cost per attempt on gpt-6.1-sol and 1.10x on gpt-6-astra, and the prefix nanox resends on every call was the one remaining cause (first request 6,052 input tokens against pi's 1,350). Everything cut addresses a person who is not there in a headless run: permission requests, tone, progress updates, final-message formatting and the plan widget, and the approval parameters (`justification`, `prefix_rule`, `sandbox_permissions`), which exec_command reads and ignores; `shell` and `login` keep their defaults, which every traps and Terminal-Bench run used. What stays is the core coding guidance: the opening, "# Autonomy and persistence", the compaction paragraphs and "# Rules for getting work done". o200k_base counts: sol.md 3,315 to 966 tokens headless, astra.md 3,251 to 966, luna.md 2,658 to 837; the direct tool list 1,207 to 808. With 457b0d9 that is about 3,650 fewer input tokens on every Sol or Astra request, a first request near 2,400. An interactive session's prompt and tools are unchanged, and a caller's own `system_prompt` is never edited.
- fix(python-capi): python.wasm's pow is djs-libm's, for C extensions and Python's math alike (2026-11-17, mpltest lane). wasm32 has no libm: C's pow (numpy's np.power, float ** in C extensions) resolved to compiler-builtins' weak FreeBSD routine, and pymath's wasm path kept its own port of the same routine, while every other math function already took djs-libm's. That routine isn't correctly rounded: pow(10.0, -5.0) gave 9.999999999999999e-06 and 2 ** -0.5 was off by an ulp, so matplotlib's ScalarFormatter picked offset 0.0007199999999999999 where CPython picks 0.00072 (test_offset_value). python-capi now exports pow from djs-libm on wasm32, and pymath's pow calls djs-libm and drops its port. djs-libm's pow (musl's, from Arm) matched glibc on 1,000,000 random inputs; in python.wasm the probe of 21 pow expressions now matches CPython, and test_ticker went from 547 to 548 passed of 549 (CPython 549). wasm32 clippy is clean for the changed crates.
- fix(python): threading.Condition, time.get_clock_info and socket objects work in python.wasm (2026-11-17, stdlib lane; Georgios: python3 in nanocode runs only on python.wasm, so the common stdlib must import there). The wasm _thread shim's RLock gains `_is_owned` (held means owned, with one thread): threading.Condition's fallback probes ownership with acquire(False), which always succeeds on that lock, so `Condition.wait` and everything on it (queue.Queue.get with a timeout, concurrent.futures) raised 'cannot wait on un-acquired lock'. time.get_clock_info exists on wasm32-unknown-unknown (it was wasi-only), since asyncio's event loop reads it at construction. The socket stub's socket() accepts the usual (family, type, proto, fileno) arguments before raising OSError, instead of a TypeError for passing any, so code that catches OSError around socket creation (asyncio's self-pipe, http.client) falls back. The same stub now serves native nanocode-python too, which had no _socket at all, so `import socket` (and http.client, urllib.request, email.utils, xmlrpc) works there and only opening a connection fails.
- feat(pylib): python.wasm freezes the stdlib packages agent scripts and the scoreboard's packages import (2026-11-17, stdlib lane). Added to crates/patches/rustpython-pylib/Lib from rustpython-pylib 0.6.0's Lib (CPython 3.14's): concurrent.futures (without process.py: no processes), email, http (client, server, cookies, cookiejar), asyncio (without the Windows modules), wsgiref, xmlrpc, selectors, socketserver, bdb, pdb, doctest, pydoc, profile, pstats, trace, rlcompleter and the four _pyrepl modules pdb and pydoc import (utils, types, trace, pager). Two shims for a host with no threads or descriptors: concurrent.futures.thread runs each submitted call inline in submit() when `_thread` is the frozen single-thread shim (its Thread.start runs the target to the end, so a worker would block forever on its queue), and asyncio's selector loop goes on without a self-pipe when socket.socketpair() raises OSError, so asyncio.run with coroutines, gather, Queue and timeout works (asyncio.sleep(d > 0) waits for real and the host may refuse it). select.py provides select() for no descriptors only (sleeps for its timeout, ENOSYS otherwise), as a callable object so selectors' class attribute doesn't bind it as a method. ctypes is a pure-Python stand-in without FFI: the C types with sizeof/alignment, Structure, Union, arrays, POINTER, cast, CFUNCTYPE and create_string_buffer work, CDLL raises OSError and calling a foreign function raises NotImplementedError; scipy (stats, io.arff, _ccallback), pandas.errors and numpy._core._internal import it at module level for types alone. Size, built with nanocode-ts scripts/python.mjs build() then wasm-opt -Oz and bake({image: true}) against this commit's parent: python.wasm 20,078,800 to 20,080,997 bytes (+2,197, the Rust changes above), python.data 19,002,326 to 20,097,561 (+1,095,235; it is already compressed, gzip -9 saves nothing). By source gzip -9: asyncio 108 KB, email 95 KB, http 60 KB, doctest 28 KB, pdb 35 KB, pydoc 27 KB, xmlrpc 22 KB, wsgiref 17 KB, bdb 11 KB, concurrent 9 KB, the rest under 8 KB each. Left out: sqlite3 (needs _sqlite3), ssl, multiprocessing, curses, readline, dbm, mmap and the tty modules (no C module or no host for them), and smtplib, imaplib, ftplib, mailbox, webbrowser (need sockets or processes to do anything). On native nanocode-python, asyncio, unittest.mock, pdb and doctest still fail to import because its subprocess raises ImportError on a host that cannot spawn; python.wasm's subprocess runs through psh and they import there.
- fix(python): frozen numpy modules have a site-packages __file__, as matplotlib's do (2026-11-17, stdlib lane). numpy.testing's private utils compute NUMPY_ROOT from np.__file__ at import, so `import numpy.testing` failed with AttributeError once concurrent.futures was frozen; np.get_include() needs it too. With this the scoreboard (nanocode-ts bench/python/score.ts, CAPI wheels from the mpltest lane) moves from 7/18 packages and numpy 13/19 extension modules to 8/18 and 19/19, with the numpy and plot checks unchanged (14/14, matplotlib 6/6, pillow 6/6, contourpy 2/2, kiwisolver 1/1).
- 2026-11-17: **The Codex backend's headless finish check is off by default; `CodexBuilder::finish_check(true)` turns it back on.** With it off, a headless root turn that ends with a final message ends there: no `<system-reminder>` finish notice and no extra model call. The 2026-11-16 handling of an empty reply (the empty-response reprompt, and an empty reply to a finish check keeping the final before it) is unchanged. Why: equal-cost parity with pi at launch (Georgios, 2026-11-17). In the traps equal-options reruns on build-3ad0361 (FRONTIER EQ-COST, runs 4c58f660 on gpt-6.1-sol and a1a5dc91 on gpt-6-astra, 75 nanox attempts each, all passing), every nanox attempt made exactly one call after its final answer, the finish check, and that call was the whole of nanox's remaining cost gap to pi: +$0.0023 of +$0.0018 an attempt on Sol and +$0.0094 of +$0.0049 on Astra, while nanox was cheaper than pi up to the final answer. On those runs it changed no verdict: 150 of 150 attempts passed with it. The Claude backend's finish check, which the 2026-11-15 Terminal-Bench entries justify, is separate and unchanged. Check: the mock Responses server in output/empty-final (five scripted scenarios, with and without a 600 s deadline) gives 2 requests for exec then a final (3 with the finish check in nanocode-fixd), 1 for a final with no tool call, and still 3 for exec, then an empty reply, then the reprompted final.
- 2026-11-17: **A headless Claude session (`headless`, as nanoeval sets it) sends a shorter system prompt and Bash description.** The pinned Claude Code text stays authentic in interactive sessions; headless leaves out only lines that address a person watching a terminal: the markdown-in-a-terminal, permission-mode, hooks and clickable `file_path:line_number` lines, the Claude Code surfaces line, the pronoun paragraph and the "confirm first" sentence (the rest of that paragraph, on looking before deleting and reporting outcomes faithfully, stays). From the Bash tool it drops the `gh`, `@name` notification and commit-attribution lines and the rendered guidance on writing the `description` parameter (the parameter and its first sentence stay). Kept: every line on doing the task, verification, persistence and reporting. Why: cost per pass on Claude Opus 5.5 traps was 1.13x pi's (run dd6ab7c8) and the gap is cached input from the prefix; this follows the Codex headless trims of 2026-11-17. Measured on the eval path (nanocode-ts wasm host, headless hands session with one attached hand, first `/v1/messages` body captured by a mock dispatch, counted with Anthropic `count_tokens`): with nanocode-ts's headless tool filter alone 10,737 input tokens, with this as well 10,042 (system and messages 2,342 to 1,980; the exec tool 8,395 to 8,062). Interactive requests are byte-identical (12,974 before and after).
- 2026-11-17: **A subagent whose submit_result is accepted and durable ends as completed, and model retries never pass max_attempts.** (1) Once a child's result is accepted and persisted durably, its harness gives the turn's trailing reply SUBMITTED_GRACE (15 s) to finish on its own; if the turn is still running then and still in its submitted stage, the harness stops it, and a stopped or failed turn that holds a submitted result settles as completed with that result instead of interrupted or failed. Why: in production (nanocode-ts build 9254e52, Codex backend over Responses SSE) a child's result was durable at 7.8 s, but the trailing model call after acceptance kept getting HTTP 429 and retried until 133 s, so the child never reached completed and its parent's wait never returned it. 15 s covers a normal trailing reply (a few seconds) and is far below the throttled retry window that held it open. (2) Patient statuses (429, 502, 503, 504, 529) no longer add attempts past max_attempts ("attempt 8/5"): in the Codex client and the Claude backend each patient retry instead waits at least half of what remains of PATIENCE divided by 2 for every further retry left (`retry::patient_delay`), so the attempts that are allowed are spread over the patience window, and a retry is still refused when it would end past PATIENCE. Check: `cargo check --locked --lib` and `cargo clippy --locked --lib` of nanocode-subagents, nanocode-backend-codex-client, nanocode-backend-claude and nanocode-http, native and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- 2026-11-17: **nanocode-python builds for iOS and runs numpy on Apple platforms.** (1) `heap::is_static` on Apple took the image as `_mh_execute_header` up to `get_end()`, but `get_end()` returns the unslid link-time address, so with ASLR the range was empty and every static C object (numpy's builtin `PyArray_Descr`s, extension type objects) counted as heap memory: `import numpy` crashed in `heap::header` reading a header that is not there (EXC_BAD_ACCESS from `PyDict_SetItemString` in numpy's `set_typeinfo`). The range now comes from the Mach-O image that holds this code (`dladdr` on `image`), from its lowest to its highest segment end without `__PAGEZERO` and `__LINKEDIT`, slid by the image's load address, so it is also right when the crate is linked into an app's executable or a dynamic library rather than a command-line binary. (2) The extension build passes clang an iOS triple with the deployment target rustc uses (`rustc --print deployment-target`, `arm64-apple-ios10.0` for aarch64-apple-ios, with `-simulator` for aarch64-apple-ios-sim) and the SDK from `xcrun --sdk iphoneos|iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path`; with cc's bare `--target=aarch64-apple-ios` clang found no iOS headers. (3) `os.system` is left out on iOS, whose SDK marks `system` unavailable. Measured on an M-series Mac (macOS, `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-python-cli --target aarch64-apple-darwin`, 48.8 MB binary): before, `nanocode-python -c "import numpy"` exited with SIGSEGV; after, it takes 0.37 s (three runs 0.39/0.37/0.37 s), a matplotlib Agg plot saved to PNG 0.77 s (0.89/0.77/0.77 s), `-c pass` 0.01 s, and numpy 2.5.5, Pillow 13.0.0, yaml, regex, msgpack, ujson, markupsafe, contourpy and kiwisolver import. `cargo build --locked --release -p nanocode-python` now succeeds for aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim and x86_64-apple-darwin.
- 2026-11-17: **The C extensions of nanocode-python take an explicit Apple triple on macOS too.** Building nanocode-swift's staticlib for aarch64-apple-darwin compiled the extensions with plain `cc` and no `--target`, and with both `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=12.3` and `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=16.0` in the environment (nanocode-swift's `.cargo/config.toml` sets both) Apple's clang picked iOS: 437 of the archive's 4,477 objects carried `LC_BUILD_VERSION` platform 2 (iOS, minos 16.0), and `xcodebuild -create-xcframework` refused the macOS library ("binaries with multiple platforms are not supported"). Every Apple target now passes `--target=<arch>-apple-macosx<version>` (or `-apple-ios<version>[-simulator]`) with the deployment target from `rustc --print deployment-target` and `-isysroot` from `xcrun --sdk macosx|iphoneos|iphonesimulator --show-sdk-path`; after it the same objects carry platform 1, minos 12.3, and the xcframework builds.
- 2026-11-17: **Native `time.sleep` in nanocode-python wakes when the run is stopped.** It called `std::thread::sleep` for the whole duration and never looked at `Run::stop`, so an embedder that runs Python on one thread (nanocode-swift's simulated shell, where numpy's C state is process-wide) could not stop a sleeping script: `python3 -c "import time; time.sleep(30)" & sleep 1; kill %1; wait; python3 -c "print('after kill')"` in nanocode-swift's Console took 32.3 s, the next `python3` waiting out the sleep. It now sleeps in slices of at most 20 ms, checks `stop` before each, and ends the run as cancelled when it returns true; the same script takes 1.3 s, and `time.sleep(0.3)` still takes 0.32 s. WebAssembly builds keep refusing sleep as before.

## Headless Codex requests drop exec text for interactive-only features (2026-11-16)

Headless Codex sessions already drop `update_plan` and the approval and shell fields of `exec_command` from the direct tool list; the Code Mode `exec` description still carried them as nested declarations, together with the `audio`, `generatedImage`, `notify` and `yield_control` globals and the hand-routing and image-file notes. Headless requests now drop those lines from the `exec` description too: 2841 to 2143 tokens (o200k) for the stock Sol eval tool set, about 700 tokens off every request's prefix. A request without an `exec` tool (direct orchestration) also drops the two prompt lines that tell the model to batch through `functions.exec`, a tool it does not have.

Measured on the stock build (code_mode, hedge 10, headless) against the earlier direct build on traps-ni Sol, 75 scored attempts each: $0.0286 to $0.0448 per attempt. Of the +$0.0162: +$0.0098 is the build change in direct mode alone (requests 5.65 to 6.73, mostly extra verification commands after the edit), +$0.0030 is Code Mode over direct on the same build (first request 2568 to 4411 input tokens; visible output +12% from JavaScript-wrapped commands; 1.4 fewer requests), and +$0.0034 is run-to-run spread. Hedging dispatched no request on traps; on TB it billed 5% more on the 78 of 267 attempts it touched, and the hedge won 14 of 172 dispatches.

## Responses Lite requests keep parallel tool calls off, also in direct orchestration (2026-11-16)

Responses Lite models (Sol, Astra) send `parallel_tool_calls: false`, matching codex-rs, where Code Mode's `exec` batches independent calls. With direct orchestration there is no `exec`, so each response carries one tool call: on traps-ni Sol, direct nanocode made 1.00 tool calls per response while another client on the same model made 1.24. Sending `true` for direct requests was tried and reverted: the Responses Lite endpoint rejects it with a 400 (`requires parallel_tool_calls to be false`). Direct requests instead drop the two prompt lines that tell the model to batch through `functions.exec`, a tool they do not have.

## Headless Claude requests drop exec text for interactive-only features (2026-11-17)

Headless Claude sessions already drop the GitHub lines and the interactive shell parameter from the Bash text inside the Code Mode `exec` description, but the description still carried the `audio`, `generatedImage`, `notify` and `yield_control` globals and the two Nanocode extension notes (hand routing for names missing from `ALL_TOOLS`, image files shown after a cell), which headless Codex requests already drop. Headless Claude requests now drop the same items: the two lines are removed, and the four globals are removed from the one-line `- Globals:` list (Claude renders the compact form, so the items are `; `-separated rather than lines). Interactive sessions keep the text unchanged. The Codex helper is not shared: the two backends render different description forms, and the Codex trim also edits nested declarations Claude does not have. Measured with Anthropic `count_tokens` on a captured stock headless first request (claude-opus-5-5; its model, system, messages and tools): 10,042 to 9,636 input tokens (-406, about 4% of every request's prefix); the exec description goes from 19,216 to 17,995 characters. Not dropped: the subagent tools (`spawn_agent`, `wait_agent`, `submit_result`, about 6.2k characters), WebSearch and TaskStop, which headless sessions can call. Cache layout checked on the same capture's first two requests: tools and system are byte-identical between calls, and the breakpoints sit on the system blocks and the last message, so each call writes only the new suffix. Hedging stays as it was for Claude requests (default policy: p90 of recent first-byte times, at least 1.5 s, at most 10% of requests, after 10 samples per model). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` native and with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, `cargo clippy --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-claude` (no warnings in the changed file), rustfmt, and a local test (not committed) that renders the stock exec description through `upstream_tool` headless and interactive.

## Headless exec defers the session start's sync to the first tool step (2026-11-17)

Before its first model request a headless `nanocode exec` waited on three fsyncs: the session create record, the first prompt's admission, and the pool prefix written as files under `records/` (each a file and a directory fsync). Headless sessions now write the root session's create record and its first admission with `Settle::Ordered` (`SessionStore::with_deferred_start`, via `StateStore::acquire_with_settle`), and the JSONL store opened for them (`JsonlStore::open_home_in_background_inline`) writes new records inline in the session journal instead of as shared files. Every later write is unchanged: a tool step's admission is still `Settle::Durable`, and a durable write syncs the journal, which holds the create record, the prompt and the prefix, so all three are on disk before the first tool call is dispatched or any file is written. Effects keep exactly-once: nothing a tool does can run before its step is durable. What is given up: a crash or power loss before the first tool step may lose the session and its prompt entirely (`exec` then exits non-zero and nothing ran); headless runs are one-shot and the caller reruns them. Interactive and server sessions keep `open_store` and today's policy, and child sessions are never deferred. Measured on an M-series Mac under load (another eval run; load average 17-27) with interleaved cold and warm runs, N=14 each, Sol through a local relay, time from process start to the first model request: warm median 44.8 ms vs 58.2 ms on the parent master (ratio of means 0.749, 95% bootstrap [0.599, 0.921]) and vs 63.2 ms on c3bed90f7 (0.797 [0.641, 0.976]); cold 0.945 [0.909, 0.984] vs the parent master. A local stub trace shows no sync wait before `model.call` (three before). Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib` of nanocode-durability-core and nanocode-durability native and wasm32, clippy with no new warnings in the changed files, and `nanocode-sim --scenario runtime` with the new `--deferred-start` flag (seeds 0..2400 on kv and log stores, 0..400 on memory and with remote children: all pass; mutations acks-unflushed, drop-acked-answer, tool-result-twice and drop-tool-result are still caught with it). The core default `acquire_with_settle` commits ordered updates through `commit` so the simulator's stores exercise the ordered path.

## Headless Codex sessions take the compact exec header (2026-11-17)

Headless Codex sessions in Code Mode described `exec` with codex-cli's full header, which repeats what the nested declarations and the `wait` tool already say. They now take the compact header that other embedders use (same rules: pragma, awaiting, strict-mode engine, globals, `ALL_TOOLS`), and headless requests also drop from `exec`'s text the comments and the `chunk_id` and `original_token_count` fields of nested result types, the MCP and WebAssembly mentions when no nested tool is an MCP tool, and the four `wait` lines that repeat its parameter descriptions. Every nested tool and argument stays. Interactive sessions keep codex-cli's text. Measured on the eval's headless hands session (nanocode-ts `bench/handbench.ts` with a native hand, Sol, mock dispatch, o200k): `exec` 1760 to 1146 tokens, `wait` 343 to 259, first request about 3979 to 3283 input tokens. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and wasm32, clippy with no new warnings in the changed files.
## Headless Codex sessions may ask for a single verification run (2026-11-17)

`ResponsesServiceConfig::single_verification` (builder `single_verification`) swaps the `<headless_task>` block for a narrower one: the same failure modes (packages the check may lack, state left in place, the task's paths, names and units, edits limited to what was asked), but one verification run of the deliverable as the check would run it, rerun only when it fails, instead of separate fresh-process, diff and independent checks. Off by default. It exists to A/B the request count of headless sessions: on traps-ni Sol the current block took 6.7 requests per attempt against 5.65 before it, mostly extra verification commands after the edit. Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` native and wasm32, clippy with no new warnings in the changed files.

## Code Mode system prompt caches through its static blocks (2026-11-17)

Under `code_only`, `default_system_blocks` appended the Code Mode rules (`prompts/code_mode.md`, 2,614 characters) and, for models with a bash-first bypass note, that note (493 characters for Opus 5.5) after the upstream blocks, but the system breakpoint stayed on the upstream main block. Those blocks are the same for every session of a model, yet a new session wrote them to the cache on its first request instead of reading them, about 650 to 780 tokens (characters / 4) per session. The breakpoint now moves to the last static block (the bypass note, else the Code Mode block), ahead of the environment and project instructions `build_system` appends. It moves rather than adds, so a request still carries two explicit system breakpoints, one on its last tool and the automatic conversation breakpoint: four in all. No prompt text changes. `code_mode_marks_the_last_static_system_block` and `code_mode_request_stays_within_four_breakpoints` in `instructions.rs` check the placement and the count (`cargo test -p nanocode-backend-claude --lib instructions`).

## GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, and Codex's ultra effort (2026-11-17)

OpenAI released `gpt-6.2-astra` and `gpt-6.2-sol` on 2026-11-17, with the same Responses shape as `gpt-6-astra` and `gpt-6.1-sol`. `Model::Astra62` and `Model::Sol62` are new variants. The short aliases `astra` and `sol`, the default model (`Astra62`) and the default subagent model (`Sol62`) move to them. The versioned IDs keep the older models, and the persisted serde names `astra` and `sol` still decode to them, so saved sessions and checkpoints keep their model. Both use the Astra/Sol prompts pinned at openai/codex d32063f9: codex HEAD c08843a5 has the same bundled `models.json` (sha256 match) and doesn't list 6.2 yet. Codex gets 6.2 from the remote `/models` catalog, which hadn't reached ChatGPT accounts at 10:10 PST (`model_not_found` from `/backend-api/codex/responses`). Pricing comes from the OpenAI model pages. Astra 6.2 costs $8 input, $0.40 cached input, $10 cache write and $40 output per million tokens. Priority is twice that. Long context (prompts over 272K tokens) is $16 input and $60 output, and ultrafast is 6x standard, matching Astra 6's multipliers. Sol 6.2 costs the same as Sol 6.1.

Changes that match codex-rs (`models-manager/models.json` and `protocol/src/openai_models/reasoning_effort.rs` at c08843a5):
- `Thinking::Ultra` is new. Astra, Sol, Terra and Daybreak Blue list `ultra`; Luna and custom models don't. Codex's `resolve_reasoning_effort` never sends ultra on the wire. Instead it sends the model's `multi_agent_reasoning_effort` (xhigh for Astra, Sol and 6.1 Terra), else max, else the highest supported level. `Model::wire_thinking` does the same for `reasoning.effort` and for `configuration_update` items. Subagents that inherit an ultra parent's effort run at `Model::multi_agent_thinking`. Claude maps ultra to max.
- Sol's default effort is now low, codex's `default_reasoning_level` for `gpt-6.1-sol`. It was medium.

Not yet done: under ultra, codex also adds a proactive `<multi_agent_mode>` developer message (`core/src/session/multi_agents.rs`). nanocode sends no multi-agent mode message at all today.

Checks: `cargo check --locked --lib` native and wasm32 for types-core, agent-types, subagents, agent, backend-codex-client, backend-codex and backend-claude, plus `cargo check -p nanocode-cli --bin nanocode`. `output/gpt-6-2` prints the alias, serde, effort and pricing table for every Codex model.

## Codex upstream pin moves to bc2c3284 (2026-11-17)

Since d32063f9, openai/codex (330 commits, up to bc2c3284 at 18:24 UTC) has left `models.json` and every base prompt byte-identical. Among the pinned tool sources, only `shell_spec.rs` changed: `exec_command`'s `login` description is now "Request login-shell startup. Omit to inherit." (openai/codex#61744; PowerShell gets its own text, and nanocode doesn't expose it). `standard.rs` and the `upstream/request.json` snapshot copy that text. Checks: `python3 scripts/verify-codex-upstream.py` passes, and `cargo check --locked --lib -p nanocode-backend-codex` passes native and wasm32.

## GPT-6.2 Ultrafast launch pricing (2026-11-17)

The [Astra 6.2](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.2-astra) and [Sol 6.2](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.2-sol) model pages specify Ultrafast at 3x Standard through February 28, 2027, then 6x starting March 1, 2027 (Pacific time). The initial model addition used 6x immediately. Astra62's short- and long-context Ultrafast rates are now halved, and Sol62 has its own 3x rates instead of sharing Sol 6.1's 6x rates. Older models and the other service tiers keep their rates. These are the current static list-price estimates, as elsewhere in this table; update the 6.2 Ultrafast rates when the launch discount ends.

Validation: native and wasm32 checks of nanocode-types-core, plus arithmetic verification of all four rate components against 3x Standard for both context lengths and both 6.2 models.
